yelp:train:63653.para:
While it's undeniable that we're at Hooters, and their Vegas location is significantly more disappointing than one could fathom, the importance of customer service in today's economic climate cannot be overstated for a business's success. The valet who merely drove our car and ignored us completely, without offering any help with our bags, made it clear that a tip was not expected. Their silence, likely due to a smoke break, was deafening. 

The pool, open around the clock throughout the year, is exclusively male, and the thought of the sperm count there is unsettling. The only females present are the Hooters girls, whose job is to engage in flirtatious behavior. Their attempts at humor fall flat. From my vantage point, I observed waitresses actively avoiding them after being provoked for a fifth photo and subjected to derogatory language. 

Expecting violent vomiting from neighbors, with the door ajar, is a common occurrence in Vegas at a place like this. If you have the means, consider visiting elsewhere. If not, it's wiser to stay home, conserve your funds, and perhaps invest in a new pair of shoes. 

On a brighter note, the staff did exhibit commendable behavior. It's crucial to maintain respect towards them.

yelp:train:63729.orig: Great for the price. Nice and cozy. Was expecting much less. Cheap and not too far from anything
yelp:train:63729.para: Excellent value for money. Comfortably snug. Surpassed my expectations. Economical and conveniently located.

yelp:train:63850.orig:
So I found this place from Yelp and it was the closest Barber shop to my location.  I was able to walk in without an appointment on Saturday at 11:30am and was seated immediately.  That was awesome because the place was busy I just got lucky I guess.

I was told over the phone a haircut was $11 but found out the Fohawk cut I was getting was $13.  Still a bargain though because the guy did a great job.  Love the classic Barber shop style where they use a proper razor.

When the Barber finished up I was surprised to learn that he was Nelson!  Definitely will be coming back next month.
yelp:train:63850.para: I stumbled upon this Barber shop on Yelp, which was the nearest to me. On a Saturday at 11:30am, I walked in and was promptly seated, a fortunate occurrence given its popularity. The cost of my Fohawk cut was $13, slightly higher than the $11 advertised, but the quality of work justified the price. I appreciate the traditional Barber shop ambiance with its use of a proper razor. To my delight, the Barber turned out to be Nelson, and I'm planning to return next month.

yelp:train:63993.orig: Food is mediocre but the fact is its so damn cold to eat here. Would maybe be 3 stars, if they cared at all about the temp. \nThe four groups eating here are complaining and huddled in one small area where it's all the way up to 50 degrees.
yelp:train:63993.para: The cuisine lacks quality, yet the issue is its excessively chilly temperature for consumption. It could be rated 3 stars if there was any concern for the warmth. The four distinct groups dining here are expressing dissatisfaction and congregating in a confined space where the temperature reaches a frigid 50 degrees.

yelp:train:64075.orig:
This place is just ""okay"". My dad loves this place.. Or used to love it. Honestly, the only reason why I go to this place is because of their shrimp and mussels. Oh! And their free refills of Thai Iced Tea. That's it. It's good. But everything else is.. Pure nasty-ness. Unless, of course, you're into the taste of shit.

Anyway, I hate their servers here with a passion. Especially the hostess. The last and final time my family and I were there, we brought in fam members from New York. So in total there were around NINE of us. The hostess wanted us to fit in ONE booth. ONE freaking booth. How do you expect all nine of us to fit into ONE BOOTH!? When we kindly asked if we could have at least two, she rolled her eyes at us, gave us attitude and finally gave in after arguing with my dad. My dad, of course, went to go complain at the front. She started arguing with my dad and finally my dad gave in and yelled, ""SHUT UP! I'M THE CUSTOMER AND YOU'RE NOT!"" Dumb hoe finally shut her mouth. 

There are plenty of events like this in the past. I swear, I've never came across such rude and disrespectful people in my whole entire life. 

They're also pretty slow on refills. Just a F
yelp:train:64075.para:
This location is merely satisfactory. My father has a fondness for this spot, or at least he did in the past. To be honest, the sole motivation for my visits is their shrimp and mussels. Plus, the complimentary Thai Iced Tea refills are a bonus. It's decent, but the rest is downright unpleasant. Unless you enjoy the flavor of something unpalatable.

Regarding the staff, I detest their service, particularly the hostess. The last time my family and I visited, we had about nine people. The hostess insisted we could all squeeze into a single booth. A single booth for nine people! How could she expect us to fit? When we politely suggested at least two booths, she dismissed us, displayed a negative attitude, and eventually relented after my father intervened. My father, as always, went to lodge a complaint at the front. She engaged in a dispute with my father and, after some back and forth, my father asserted his position as the customer, which finally silenced her.

I've encountered numerous such incidents in the past. I can't recall ever encountering such impolite and disrespectful individuals in my entire life.

Additionally, they tend to be slow with refills. Just a F

yelp:train:64479.orig: just went in today to get new tires and 1 of the new tire they gave me was 10 PSI lower than the recommended air pressure. I later find out there is  slow leak on the new tire. \n\nupdated: Had to get it fixed next morning before work. They were quick to fix the problem. i was told there was a leak on the sensor probably from the tire change.  they apologized and cleaned my tires so i moved it from 1 star to 4 stars.
yelp:train:64479.para:
Today, I visited to purchase new tires and discovered that one of them had a tire pressure of 10 PSI below the suggested level. Subsequently, I learned there was a gradual leak in the new tire. The following morning, before work, I had the issue resolved promptly. The technicians identified a leak in the sensor, likely due to the recent tire swap. They expressed regret and thoroughly cleaned my tires, prompting me to upgrade my rating from 1 star to 4 stars.

yelp:train:64704.orig: I was very disappointed with my recent service. I realized it was busy and was told it would take 40 minutes, no worries, but when I noticed they 'mark' your car with a white marker - it is to tell the workers what level of service you paid for which determines your place in line.  After waiting 1 hour, 20 minutes and seeing  many others who came after me had come and gone, I was not happy.  I mentioned to the service person what happened and he did not deny it and said he was sorry. I will not longer spend my lunch hour at this place!
yelp:train:64704.para: I felt quite disheartened with the service I received lately. I understood it was a busy time and was informed it would take about 40 minutes, which I didn't mind, but when I saw they were using a white marker to indicate the service level you chose, which dictates your queue position, it was disconcerting. After waiting for an hour and 20 minutes, observing numerous others who arrived after me had left, my dissatisfaction grew. I brought this to the attention of the attendant, who neither refuted nor dismissed it, expressing regret instead. Henceforth, I will not utilize my lunch break at this establishment.

yelp:train:64762.orig: After years of passing by this place we finally decided to stop and try it, and i'm glad to say it did not let us down. The chicken wings and ribs were delicious and freshly grilled. The mac&cheese was good but the mash potatoes were salty, the corn is out of a can but i don't care since i didn't go for the corn. The cucumber salad is really good too. The place was very clean and has good customer service. All in all we will be back soon.  loved the outdoor seating!
yelp:train:64762.para: Following numerous visits without stopping, we chose to dine here and I'm pleased to report it exceeded our expectations. The succulent chicken wings and ribs were delightfully grilled. While the mac&cheese was satisfactory, the mashed potatoes were excessively salty, but I didn't mind as I didn't order the corn, which was canned. The cucumber salad was also excellent. The establishment maintained a pristine environment and provided commendable customer service. In summary, we're eager to return, especially appreciating the outdoor dining area.

yelp:train:64877.orig: Great food and big portions. Make sure u try the breakfast burrito. Staff is friendly and fast. They have like a million tv's so if your looking for some sports playoff action, go visit the lodge.
yelp:train:64877.para: Enjoy delicious meals and generous servings. Don't miss out on the breakfast burrito. The team is welcoming and efficient. With numerous televisions available, if you're seeking sports playoff excitement, consider visiting the lodge.

yelp:train:65233.orig: great food. one of the most unique locations i have been to. beer is above average. the whole experience is amazing. I will always be coming back to this place, unless they turn it into a church again.....
yelp:train:65233.para: Exceptional cuisine and a distinctive venue make this place unforgettable. The beer quality is commendable, contributing to an overall fantastic experience. I'm committed to revisiting this spot, barring any unforeseen conversion to a religious site.

yelp:train:65257.orig:
Don't waste your time.

The pros:  Very pretty, beer is good, relatively inexpensive.

The cons:  Food is absolutely terrible.  In two trips, they served tasteless philly cheese steak (how is that even possible), and a quesadilla that was cold.  When I returned it to the waiter, they brought it back two minutes later, they had evidently just thrown it into the microwave.  Also the food took  more than an hour to arrive.

I will only go here if a group of friends forces me to go, and even then I will only drink.  Please don't bother taking anyone here for dinner.
yelp:train:65257.para:
Avoid spending your time here.

Advantages: The ambiance is attractive, the beer selection is commendable, and it's quite affordable.

Drawbacks: The culinary experience is abysmal. During two visits, I was served a bland Philly cheese steak and a chilled quesadilla. Upon requesting a replacement, it was quickly reheated in the microwave. Additionally, the wait for food was excessively long, exceeding an hour.

I'll only consider visiting with a group of friends who insist, and even then, I'll limit myself to consuming beverages. Do not recommend this place for a dining experience.

yelp:train:65725.orig: Color printer was down for maintenance; could not provide me with a concrete turnaround time.  No problem, I understand that this happens.  What irked me was that they refused to recommend any other printing service in the Pittsburgh area, citing \""conflict of interest.\""  \n\nBe professional!  If you can't do the job for me, help me find someone that can. Will never use.
yelp:train:65725.para: The color printer was undergoing maintenance and couldn't give me a specific timeframe for its return. I get that maintenance is necessary. However, I was frustrated that they wouldn't suggest alternative printing services nearby, due to a declared \"conflict of interest.\"\n\nMaintain professionalism! If you're unable to assist me, please guide me to a reliable service provider. I will not consider using this service again.

yelp:train:66422.orig: Best strawberry bubble drinks (smoothies or teas) I've ever had, hands down, no question. (And I've had a lot!) Other than that, the dishes are delish, the portions are huge, and the menu has a great variety. Yes, the food is a little greasy (but thus very tasty), and the service is hit or miss... Still, for those of us who were/are students in the Oakland area, Lulu's is a beloved staple.
yelp:train:66422.para: I've sampled countless strawberry bubble beverages, and I can confidently say they're the best I've ever experienced, without a doubt. Apart from these, the cuisine is scrumptious, the serving sizes are generous, and the menu boasts an impressive assortment. While the food might be slightly oily, it's undeniably flavorful. The service quality varies, but for Oakland's student community, Lulu's holds a cherished place.

yelp:train:66620.orig: Got moussaka. Instead of bechamel, they put american cheese on top...interesting, cheap and not a tasty choice. So much lamb on the menu, it's hard to avoid. Just because it has lamb in it, doesn't mean its Mediterranean. Friend had beef platter. Beef too dry, too well done. For this price, you could get a lot better. Would not recommend
yelp:train:66620.para:
Received moussaka with a layer of American cheese instead of traditional bechamel. It's intriguing but inexpensive and lacks flavor. The prevalence of lamb dishes makes it challenging to resist. Despite the presence of lamb, it doesn't qualify as Mediterranean cuisine. A friend opted for a beef platter, which was unfortunately overcooked and lacked moisture. Given the cost, there are certainly more satisfying options available. I would not suggest this.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original meaning, topic, sentiment, emotion, and intent while using different wording and sentence structure. The length is also roughly the same.)

yelp:train:67228.orig: Being a sushi snob, I had always considered Umi to be the city's gold standard.  While it still is, Chaya is very solid as well.  My sashimi was as fresh as possible, which is the most critical requirement (in the East End, one must carefully avoid some other sushi stops).  My son ordered the basic sushi platter, so we didn't give Chaya the chance to show off it's creativity, but his sushi was fresh and well prepared. The dining area is very comfortable as well.\n\nPS - it is BYOB.  We stopped at East End Brewing first for a growler of beer, and the crisp waitstaff at Chaya had beer glasses on our table within seconds after we were seated!
yelp:train:67228.para: As a connoisseur of sushi, I've always viewed Umi as the epitome of excellence in the city. Although it maintains its status, Chaya is equally commendable. The sashimi served was as fresh as it gets, a paramount necessity in the East End, where one must be cautious of certain sushi establishments. My son opted for the standard sushi platter, thus not allowing Chaya to demonstrate its inventive flair, but the sushi was fresh and expertly crafted. The ambiance of the dining space is also quite cozy.\n\nP.S. - Chaya follows a BYOB policy. We first stopped at East End Brewing for a growler of beer, and the prompt and courteous waitstaff at Chaya promptly provided us with beer glasses soon after we were seated!

yelp:train:67670.orig: I ate here with my girlfriend and 2 other friends a couple of Fridays ago.  We had reservations for a Friday night and whenever we arrived there was only one other table in the club.  Since the dining room is fairly cavernous, it was almost awkward.  As you would expect at a finer dining establishment the tables were covered in white tablecloths and there was silverware on the table for a number of courses.  We were sat near the windows which overlooked the Monogahela River and I imagine that the view would have been pretty great but since we were visiting at night in winter, there was not much to be seen.\n\nOur table decided to start off by splitting zucchini and ricotta fritters and the caprese kabobs while I also ordered the beer & 3 cheese soup since I thought that it sounded good.  The fritters were not completely what I expected but were really good and lived up to their name of fritters.  Meanwhile the caprese kabobs left a little to be desired as they were just some tomatoes and cheese on a kabob with a little balsalmic drizzle.  Finally my cheese soup was an interesting mixture.  I could taste the beer but it also tasted strongly of American cheese, you know the singles k
yelp:train:67670.para: A few weeks back, I dined with my partner and two pals at this upscale venue. We had a reservation for a Friday evening, and upon arrival, we found only one other group occupying the space. Given the spacious dining area, it felt slightly uncomfortable. The tables were elegantly draped in white linens, and silverware was set for various courses. We were seated by the windows with a view of the Monogahela River, but the nighttime winter scene offered little to admire.\n\nOur group began with zucchini and ricotta fritters, and I also opted for the beer and three-cheese soup, as it seemed appealing. The fritters exceeded my expectations, despite not being exactly as I imagined. The caprese kabobs, however, were somewhat underwhelming, consisting merely of tomatoes and cheese on a skewer with a hint of balsamic. Lastly, my cheese soup presented a unique blend, with a noticeable beer flavor and a strong American cheese essence.

yelp:train:67857.orig: Honestly, I'm not sure what everyone is raving about.  It was a lovely way to see the city but the driver spend the entire time making duck jokes, and yes I get that duck jokes are the gimmick but I thought there would be a little bit more information on the city.  He would point out a building or statue and mention the name but that was about all the info you got before he started quacking again. It also only takes a quick route through downtown then spins up by the stadiums on water.  I thought we would see more.\nOur seats were REALLY uncomfortable.  We were in the back and the space was not long enough for our legs. We shared the duck mobile with a large (Somewhat pushy) elderly group who were not interested in sharing with us or the nice young couple who were there with their toddler.  They cut in line, tried to sit in all the window seats and It was a battle just to get them to move around so we could sit together. \nAll in all I wouldn't recommend it for grow ups. Fun if you have kids (or are pushy spoiled old folks who act like kids!).
yelp:train:67857.para: Truthfully, I'm uncertain about the hype surrounding this experience. The tour offered a charming glimpse of the city, yet the guide was preoccupied with duck puns, despite their novelty. The information provided was minimal, with only building or statue names mentioned before he resumed his humorous quips. The route was a swift dash through the city center, then a detour by the waterfront stadiums. I expected a more comprehensive exploration. Additionally, the backseat was extremely cramped, with insufficient legroom. We had to contend with an intrusive elderly group and a demanding young family with a child, who disregarded our attempts to find a peaceful spot. In summary, I wouldn't suggest this for adults, though it might entertain children or those with a childlike demeanor.

yelp:train:68073.orig: I had a German meal and it was very good.  The beer choices were limited to 5 draft brews and some bottled beer.  The beer was okay not outstanding.  They need to create small experimental beers to bring some excitement to an otherwise un-interesting beer selection.  No Oktoberfest or pumpkin beers.  The service was unequal.  Prompt attention upon arrival on a slow Thursday night.  The waiter disappeared when I wanted to pay.  He mumbled something about having to run some cases.  Other waiters ignored me even though I was standing right by the bar and register. I will not return to this place, there are too many other better restaurants in the area.
yelp:train:68073.para: I enjoyed a German dining experience, which was quite pleasing. The beer options were restricted to five draft selections and a few bottled varieties. The beer quality was decent but not exceptional. It would benefit from the introduction of small-scale experimental brews to add some thrill to the otherwise dull beer assortment. There was a noticeable absence of Oktoberfest or pumpkin-themed beers. The service was inconsistent. I received immediate service upon my arrival on a leisurely Thursday evening. However, the waiter vanished when I was ready to settle the bill, muttering about running some deliveries. Other staff members overlooked me despite my proximity to the bar and cashier. I've decided not to revisit this establishment, as there are numerous superior dining options nearby.

yelp:train:68581.orig: Tried it and they were out of everything we tried to order. Gave them another try and same thing. We gave up and wont be going back
yelp:train:68581.para: Experienced a lack of stock for our requested items, attempted again with no success. Consequently, we've decided not to return.

yelp:train:68688.orig: I ordered a fajita quesadilla and why I got was a fajita burrito swimming in a pool of fluid which caused the bottom to be mushy and pasty...quite gross!  Don't think I'll be back!!!
yelp:train:68688.para: I procured a fajita quesadilla, but what I received was a fajita burrito drenched in excess liquid, resulting in a soggy and unappetizing base...definitely not worth returning to!

yelp:train:68722.orig: Best vets office ever!  These folks love pets more than any other vets I have ever been to. Fancy place in a very convenient location. Highly recommend.
yelp:train:68722.para: The most exceptional veterinary clinic I've encountered! The staff here has an unparalleled affection for animals, surpassing any other veterinarians I've met. It's a luxurious facility situated in an extremely accessible spot. I wholeheartedly endorse it.

yelp:train:68932.orig:
Lately I've noticed two things.

First, the friendliness of the staff at Chick-Fil-A has gone up exponentially.  I don't think it's just one store in particular, because it seems to be at all locations (or at least all of them we visit).  Second, the fries are tasting better.  It's not that the fries themselves are different, because they look or even really taste new, but they seem to be letting them cook longer, which leads to crispier fries, instead of those nasty limp waffle things that they used to put out.

Now I just need to make sure to remember to ask for ""well done"" fries just in case, and I think I can actually grow to like these Chick-Fil-A fries... I still don't really care for the spicy chicken, however.  I can let them slide on that as long as they offer hot sauce on the condiment bar and free chicken once a year, however.
yelp:train:68932.para:
Recently, I've observed two developments.

Initially, the warmth of the Chick-Fil-A team has significantly increased across all the places we frequent. It's not confined to a single outlet, as the improvement is noticeable in every location we visit. Secondly, the quality of the fries has improved. The fries themselves haven't changed in appearance or flavor, but they appear to be cooked for a longer duration, resulting in a crisper texture rather than the previously subpar, waffle-like fries. 

To ensure I get the best, I'll remember to request "well done" fries. I'm starting to appreciate these Chick-Fil-A fries, despite my ongoing indifference towards the spicy chicken. I'll tolerate it as long as they provide hot sauce on the condiment bar and offer free chicken occasionally.

yelp:train:69211.orig: My wife and I went with another couple for a birthday celebration. We asked for outdoor seating and had a nice table on the balcony. The hostess was friendly enough. The first person at our table didn't say a word while he poured our water. The server showed up several minutes later, but dismissed our questions quickly refocusing us to explain a menu item that was unavailable and it's alternate. Starters took a while. The mussel app was good until the 5th which was so fishy and rank I had to spit it out (so it was my last). After another 45 minutes, 3 of 4 entrees arrived. After a wait and finally asking the hostess to track down our last entree, it finally was delivered. My salmon and shrimp (the special/alternate) were overcooked but pasta underneath was good. Lasagna had been sitting so long under a heat lamp that a few layers were too hard to eat, meatloaf was ok. Lamb chops were good, but cold by the time meatloaf arrived and we could all start to eat. Very disappointed with the service and food; wine was reasonably priced. Robert Bruce Pinot was very good. No desire to return.
yelp:train:69211.para: My spouse and I joined another pair for a birthday gathering. We requested an outdoor table and were accommodated on the balcony. The hostess greeted us amiably. The first guest at our table remained silent as he served our drinks. The waiter appeared after a few minutes and promptly shifted our attention to discussing a dish that wasn't available, suggesting an alternative instead. The appetizers took some time. The mussel starter was enjoyable until the fifth, which tasted excessively fishy and unpleasant, leading me to spit it out (thus it was my final course). Following another 45 minutes, three out of four main courses were served. After some delay and a request to the hostess to locate our final dish, it was finally brought to us. The salmon and shrimp (our chosen/alternative) were overdone, though the pasta beneath was satisfactory. The lasagna had been exposed to heat for too long, making some layers too tough to consume, while the meatloaf was acceptable. The lamb chops were decent but became cold in comparison to the meatloaf's arrival, delaying our meal. Overall, we were quite disenchanted with both the service and the food, though the wine was fairly priced. The Robert Bruce Pinot was commendable. We have no intention of revisiting.

yelp:train:69421.orig: Chuck is beyond amazing. There aren't enough words to describe how caring he is. I've seen how hard he works and cares for each one of his patients. Not too long ago I had something that presented as a pinched nerve in my right hand. My thumb, index finger and middle finger were numb, felt like they were on fire and slowly swelling. It was to the point where I couldn't even move my fingers, write or even put my clothes on. I remember it was the middle of the night and I went to the ER and what a waste of time! I immediately called Chuck the next morning and in a matter of four-five treatments I was able to see a tremendous difference. I was able to write, feel, and move my fingers. I highly recommend his practice to anyone.
yelp:train:69421.para: Chuck is exceptionally wonderful. It's impossible to encapsulate the level of his compassion. I've witnessed his dedication to each patient he attends to. Recently, I suffered from a pinched nerve in my right hand, causing numbness and swelling in my thumb, index, and middle fingers. I was unable to move my fingers, write, or dress myself. It happened during the night, and my visit to the ER felt futile. However, after contacting Chuck the following day, within four to five treatments, I observed a significant improvement. I regained the ability to write, feel, and move my fingers. I wholeheartedly endorse his medical practice for anyone in need.

yelp:train:69671.orig:
I love Kabob Grill. I'm definitely a creature of habit when it comes to what I order, but have ventured from the norm a few times. My favorite combination is the chicken kabob with two sides. With that I normally get the Omar's salad, which has a light flavored dressing. I also get the potatoes harra. These are potato cubes with lots of garlic.

If you like garlic, definitely order a side of their garlic sauce. It is great for dipping the chicken, potatoes, and bread that is served with the meal.

I've also tried the veggie plate and it provided a lot of variety with just as much flavor. 

Kabob Grill also has a location in Stonecrest at Piper Glen if you end up in South Charlotte and this location has all of the same menu items.
yelp:train:69671.para:
I have a strong preference for Kabob Grill, often sticking to my usual order, but occasionally trying new things. My go-to is the chicken kabob served with two sides. Typically, I opt for the Omar's salad, which features a subtly flavored dressing. I also enjoy the garlic-infused potatoes, which are simply potato cubes seasoned with garlic. 

For those who appreciate garlic, I recommend adding a side of their garlic sauce. It's delicious for dipping the chicken, potatoes, and bread that accompanies the meal. I've also sampled the veggie plate, which offers a diverse range of flavors. 

Kabob Grill is also available at the Stonecrest Piper Glen location in South Charlotte, where you can find the same menu items.

yelp:train:69719.orig: Pike's is right behind my office and when I don't feel like driving somewhere or just want some good comfort food for lunch, this is the best option.  The grilled cheese is really pretty awesome!  It's got two kinds of oozy, gooey super melted cheese on it.  And when I ask for it to be well done, it comes out perfect, yay!  The pecan fried chicken is another good one.  Its sweet and savory, and all kinds of bad for you but hey sometimes you gotta splurge!  It comes with a broccoli casserole which is also delicious, and the mashed potatoes, which I do not love.  But that's okay you can sub a different side for $1!  Desserts are very tempting.  So far though I have resisted, except I was given a slice of the mousse cake for my bday fro my boss, how could I say no to the boss??  Its a cheesecake with layers of the chocolate mousse, it was really silky and smooth tasting, very decadent and very delicious.  Luckily I had co-workers help me eat it.\n\nThe prices are very reasonable here.  Service is hit or miss.  I feel like they just drop you check right after you get your food, which is odd because I eat lunch at off peak times so its not like they need the table.  No matter, I sit and
yelp:train:69719.para: Situated conveniently behind my workspace, Pike's serves as an ideal choice for a hassle-free lunch with delectable comfort food. The grilled cheese sandwich here is exceptional, boasting two varieties of richly melted cheese. When I request it to be thoroughly cooked, it consistently delivers perfection. Another commendable dish is the pecan fried chicken, a delightful blend of sweet and savory flavors, albeit not the healthiest option. Accompanied by a broccoli casserole and mashed potatoes (which I'm not particularly fond of), the option to swap sides for a nominal fee is appreciated. Desserts are undeniably alluring, and while I've managed to resist, I couldn't refuse a slice of the mousse cake on my boss's birthday, thanks to the support of my colleagues. The cake, a layered cheesecake with chocolate mousse, is incredibly smooth and indulgent. Prices at Pike's are quite fair, though the service quality can be unpredictable. It's peculiar that they tend to hand over the check immediately after serving the food, especially during off-peak hours when a table isn't necessary. Nonetheless, I find myself seated and...

yelp:train:69895.orig: I am very much a fan of Carraba's, but this one dropped the ball.  My sausage and lentil soup was great, as usual.  But my mom ordered spaghetti and had to send it back twice before telling them to take it off the bill completely.  For some reason whoever was cooking yesterday thought that spaghetti sauce should be like water.  It's spaghetti and you're an Italian restaurant.  Spaghetti should be a no brainer.
yelp:train:69895.para: I hold Carraba's in high regard, yet this instance fell short. The sausage and lentil soup maintained its usual excellence. However, my mother's request for spaghetti was disappointing, necessitating its return twice before it was entirely removed from the charge. The culinary team yesterday seemed to misconstrue the essence of spaghetti, treating it as if it were water. Given that it's a dish deeply rooted in Italian cuisine, it should be straightforward.

yelp:train:70041.orig: Love NODA, Love the atmosphere and everything but with that said Cabo was just bleh. I mean i just didnt see how it was special or anything. The queso we ordered came out cold and i didnt LOVE my meal soo 2 stars it is for me.
yelp:train:70041.para: I adore NODA and appreciate the ambiance, however, my experience at Cabo left me unimpressed. The queso served was disappointingly cold, leading me to rate it a mere 2 stars.

yelp:train:70099.orig: Had lunch here today. The tuna tacos were fantastic and the chips and salsa were some of the best I've ever had. Had the cabo toll appetizer and it was good but honestly not needed with the free chips and salsa.
yelp:train:70099.para: Enjoyed a meal at this place today. The tuna tacos were exceptional and the chips and salsa were among the finest I've tasted. I also tried the cabo toll starter, which was satisfactory but not essential given the complimentary chips and salsa.

yelp:train:70277.orig: Fun atmosphere with a solid selection of brews. Staff has always been helpful in giving recommendations.
yelp:train:70277.para: Lively vibe paired with a robust variety of beverages. The team consistently provides guidance for suggestions.

yelp:train:70453.orig: Excellent independent coffee shop.  Hometown feel with NoDa culture.  Staff is friendly and the locals are interesting.  Good place to relax or have laid back business meeting.  Free Wifi and rocking chairs don't hurt either.
yelp:train:70453.para: Exceptional autonomous coffee establishment. Offers a local charm with NoDa's vibe. The team is amiable, and the community members are engaging. Ideal for unwinding or conducting a casual business discussion. Benefits include complimentary internet access and comfortable rocking chairs.

yelp:train:71202.orig: I am usually very positive about reviews  and complementary about employees. Unfortunately, I made the decision of visiting this establishment tonight. If the business wishes to flourish, make some changes very soon.
yelp:train:71202.para: Generally, I maintain a positive outlook on feedback and commend staff members. Regrettably, I chose to experience this venue this evening. For the business to thrive, it's imperative to implement alterations promptly.

yelp:train:71208.orig: I just realized I have never reviewed this restaurant but have been coming here since we moved to Charlotte a little over two years ago.  LOVE this place! They make their own dough and sauce daily and pizzas are baked in a REAL wood-fired oven.  This is thin crust pizza at it's finest!  The antipasto is fresh, cold, and huge..will easily feed four.  The Wine list is small but good selection and very reasonably priced.  Service is friendly and efficient.  Most nights you will find Jeff, the affable owner seating tables.  (The story goes Luisa brought the oven from Italy, opened the  restaurant and  then Jeff bought it)  Tuesdays is KIDS NIGHT, so be warned.  Although, I must admit that even though I don't like kids much, I have braved the masses to feed my Luisa's craving on several Tuesdays...it's that good!  Oh, and save room for desert, both the Tiramisu and the Cannoli are house-made, fresh, and outstanding!
yelp:train:71208.para: I've just come to the realization that I've never given this Charlotte eatery a review, yet I've frequented it for over two years. I adore this spot! They craft their own dough and sauce every day, and their pizzas are cooked in an authentic wood-fired oven. This establishment offers the best thin crust pizza imaginable. The antipasto is not only fresh and large but can easily serve a party of four. The wine list is modest but boasts a commendable range at affordable prices. The service is both amiable and prompt. Most evenings, you'll see Jeff, the welcoming proprietor, attending to guests. (The tale tells of Luisa who imported the oven from Italy, initiated the restaurant, and then Jeff acquired it.) Beware of Tuesdays, as it's KIDS NIGHT. Despite my general dislike for children, I've ventured into the crowds on several occasions to satisfy Luisa's desires, and it's undeniably worth it. Don't forget to leave room for dessert; both the Tiramisu and the Cannoli are homemade, fresh, and exceptional!

yelp:train:71252.orig:
This is one of the worst Verizon stores out there and poss the worst in Charlotte. Save yourself time and stress and head up to Northlake Commons or Sharon Corners at Southpark. This one is always busy and when it's not, it is still slow.  I have had 3 bad experiences here, so I don't know if it is a poor hiring/training issue or what, since the rest of the organization seems to offer fantastic service (via phone or other store).

I went in to upgrade my phone and they didn't ask any questions about what I typically use my phone for, but seemed to just push the iPhone as the phone du jour, so after I got it home and was working with it I realized it was so poorly suited for me that I returned it within 14 hours (and lost some $$ on it).  I was so unimpressed he didn't take the time to understand my needs and match me up to the right phone. 

So I gave up for a few months and when my blackberry was really dying and my hubby and I were trying to figure out if we wanted to switch to T-mobile which was cheaper or stay with VZW we were trying to compare plans, phones, etc. The guy who helped us was a total d!ck and basically said ""Sure, switch."" Huh?  I've been with you for year
yelp:train:71252.para:
This Verizon location in Charlotte is notably subpar, and it's always crowded or sluggishly operational. To avoid wasting time and causing unnecessary anxiety, consider visiting Northlake Commons or Sharon Corners at Southpark instead. I've encountered three unsatisfactory experiences here, leaving me uncertain whether it's due to inadequate staff recruitment or training. Despite this, other parts of the company deliver excellent customer service through various channels.

When I attempted to upgrade my phone, the staff didn't inquire about my usage habits but instead aggressively promoted the iPhone as the current trend. Upon using it at home, I discovered it was ill-fitted for my needs, leading me to return it within a week, resulting in a financial loss. The lack of effort to understand my requirements and provide a suitable device left me disenchanted.

For a period, I refrained from engaging with Verizon. However, when my Blackberry's performance declined, and my partner and I contemplated switching to T-mobile for cost savings, we sought assistance. The individual we interacted with was dismissive and simply endorsed the switch without proper consideration.

I've been loyal to Verizon for a year, but this experience has left me questioning my commitment.

yelp:train:71560.orig:
Picked up takeout here this past week and was really impressed, not only with the establishment and service, but also how busy the place was on a Tuesday night. This made me more excited for the meal! Located right behind Fresh Market on Providence/Sardis area, the place is small, but cozy. I called in ahead, so I just walked up to the counter and gave them my name. The food came out right away. There is no bar area, so don't plan on getting a drink while you wait for your order. 

Ordered Pad Thai, Pad Woon Sen & Fresh Rolls (spring rolls on steroids). All this for $28. Not bad, as I've paid more and less for the same order at other restaurants. Surprisingly, I got a side of white rice too? Not sure if this is typical or a mistake? 

Got home and dove right in as I was starving. Food was really good and the portions were huge. Made for great lunch the next day. Ordered both dishes ""medium spicy"" and the Pad Thai came with a little more heat than the Pad Woon Sen, which was fine as the Pad Thai was for the lady. 

I'm a fan and will be back again!
yelp:train:71560.para:
This week, I opted for takeout from a nearby eatery and was genuinely pleased, not just with the venue and customer service, but also the bustling atmosphere on a Tuesday evening. The spot is compact yet inviting, situated just behind Fresh Market in the Providence/Sardis region. I placed my order in advance, so I simply approached the counter and provided my name. The food was promptly served. There's no bar section, so you won't be able to sip a drink while waiting for your meal. 

I chose Pad Thai, Pad Woon Sen, and large Fresh Rolls (enhanced spring rolls). The total cost was $28, which I found reasonable compared to other places. I was also pleasantly surprised to receive a side of white rice, though I'm uncertain if it's a common practice or an error. 

Upon returning home, I immediately started eating due to my hunger. The meal was delicious and the portions were substantial. It was perfect for a satisfying lunch the following day. I requested both dishes with a medium spice level. The Pad Thai had a bit more heat than the Pad Woon Sen, but it was acceptable as it was intended for the woman. 

I'm a regular and will definitely return!

yelp:train:71775.orig: Must be a good place at night. The espresso was collecting a social security check.
yelp:train:71775.para: It appears to be a pleasant spot during evening hours. The espresso was earning its modest income.

yelp:train:72226.orig: This was my first foray into \""real\"" North Carolina Style BBQ.  Simple menu and simple food that is delicious.  We arrived at 2:45 PM (note that they close at 3:00 PM) and we were greated with smiles and warmth - the waitress couldn't have been nicer.  Loved the vinegar-based sauce and the brunswick stew was incredible.  We left with full bellies and two pulled pork sandwiches and a bottle of their homemade sauce for the road.  \n\nWe were stranded in Charlotte en-route to Boston and Bill Spoons warmed our cold, yankee hearts to the core.  Thanks :)
yelp:train:72226.para:
My initial experience with authentic North Carolina BBQ was delightful. A straightforward menu paired with tasty dishes made it enjoyable. We got there at 2:45 PM, just in time as they shut at 3 PM, and were welcomed with cheerful smiles and hospitality. The tangy sauce and the exceptional Brunswick stew were standouts. We departed satiated, with two pulled pork sandwiches and a bottle of their homemade sauce to take with us. 

Stranded in Charlotte on our way to Boston, Bill's Spoons managed to thaw our chilly, northern spirits. Appreciation is due.

yelp:train:72508.orig: K&W can be a lot of fun if you're looking for comfort food. They cook like my mom and grandma...everything is southern, mushy, and well-seasoned. I love to get a sample of every vegetable on the line.\n\nIt's kind of reminiscent of elementary school cafeteria lines, which is always fun. The staff is very friendly and syrupy-sweet, which can be pretty nice. I think this is a great place to go if you're in the right mood for it. It can be a disaster if it's too busy or if you're not looking for a revisiting of your childhood days...especially when the place is really busy. Sometimes on Sunday afternoons, the church crowds can be overwhelming...but overall, it's a good, safe place for no-atmosphere and great food.
yelp:train:72508.para: K&W offers a delightful experience for those seeking heartwarming comfort dishes, reminiscent of my family's southern cooking style - soft, flavorful, and well-seasoned. I enjoy sampling all the vegetable options available. The ambiance brings back fond memories of school cafeterias, with the staff's warm and sugary demeanor adding to the charm. This spot is perfect for those in the mood, but it may not be ideal if it's overly crowded or if you're not reminiscing about your youth. On busy Sundays, the influx of churchgoers can be intense, yet it remains a reliable destination for unpretentious dining with delicious fare.

yelp:train:72727.orig: Walmart is always the best. Set up a little different then most I've been too but easy to find your way around and get lost just looking. Parking is the worst during the day heads up.
yelp:train:72727.para: Walmart consistently stands out as superior. Although my experience was slightly unique, navigating the space was straightforward, albeit the risk of getting disoriented while searching. Be mindful of parking challenges during daytime hours.

yelp:train:72756.orig:
It is a weirdly configured McDonalds, no question about it; but I don't believe that is really a factor here.  Just be mindful that if you are going in, the doors are located on the sides and if you take drive-thru you have to circle the building at least once then exit by taking at least one u-trun back onto South Boulevard.

The location is relatively clean in the dining area and drink station; I don't know about the kid area though.  The speed of service is somewhat slower than the average McDonalds (both front and drive-thru); the front associate automatically will assume people are on-the-go, so typically no trays.  

However, what makes this a one-star is the food quality.  Typically anything fried at this location is going to be both burnt and greasy (this includes hash browns, fries, apple pies, McNuggets, etc.).  The burgers are also surprisingly greasy as well.  And the levels of salt are surprising as well.  Probably the only bright spot is that the McCafe drinks were on par.

Overall, this is not a McDonalds location to go to, just go down the next exit.
yelp:train:72756.para:
This McDonald's has an unconventional layout, but it's not a significant issue in this context. Remember, when entering, the doors are on the sides, and if you opt for the drive-thru, you'll need to circle the building at least once before exiting via a u-turn onto South Boulevard. 

The dining area and drink station are fairly tidy, but there's uncertainty about the kid zone. The service speed is somewhat slower than usual McDonald's, with the front staff often assuming customers are in a hurry, hence no trays. 

The main reason for this one-star rating is the subpar food quality. Here, fried items like hash browns, fries, apple pies, and McNuggets are often overcooked and oily. The burgers are also unexpectedly greasy. The salt content is also surprisingly high. The only redeeming factor is that the McCafe drinks are average.

In summary, this McDonald's location is not recommended, and it's better to choose the next exit.

yelp:train:72972.orig:
Lets face it....when it comes to your furry family members, you HAVE to have a great vet with great employees and a nice facility that you feel comfortable going to---this is IT!

After going to another vet for a while, I started to realize that I really didn't like them, so I started asking around to other pet owners, and Piper Glen kept coming up with rave reviews from everyone I spoke with.  So finally I took my sweet angel here.....and this is now the ONLY place I will take her!

The staff is very welcoming and friendly, which sets you at ease right away. The waiting area is very well stocked, comfortable, and above all----clean!!

The vet assistants and the doctors are always so wonderful and professional, but they make you feel at ease, and take the time to explain things and answer questions.

Our girl had an issue with her gums/lips that we had learned to live with since our former vet said it was normal.  When we showed it to our doctor here, they quickly gave us a treatment for it and within just a week or two was cleared up and our girl is happier and eating 100% better than before because of it!

They do have a boarding facility that is beautiful and clean and
yelp:train:72972.para:
Admit it, when it comes to your beloved pets, you must have an exceptional veterinarian with commendable staff and a reassuring environment that makes you feel at home---this is essential!

After experiencing dissatisfaction with another vet, I began seeking recommendations from fellow pet owners, and Piper Glen consistently emerged with glowing testimonials. Consequently, I decided to bring my cherished pet here, and now, it's the sole destination for her care.

The team is incredibly warm and approachable, instantly putting you at ease. The waiting area is well-equipped, cozy, and most importantly, spotlessly clean!

The veterinary assistants and doctors are consistently outstanding and courteous, making you feel comfortable while taking the time to clarify and address your concerns.

Our pet had a gum/lip issue that we had resigned ourselves to, as per our previous vet's advice. However, upon presenting it to our current doctor, they promptly provided a remedy, and within a week or two, the problem was resolved. Our pet is now more joyful and has significantly improved her eating habits, thanks to the treatment.

They also offer a stunning and immaculate boarding facility.

yelp:train:73014.orig: Far overpriced for the quality of food you receive. Many other great options just a few miles away.\n\nThat being said, it is more \""authentic\"" than some Mexican restaurants, and the margaritas weren't half bad.
yelp:train:73014.para: The cost is excessively high relative to the food's quality, with numerous superior alternatives within a short distance. However, it offers a more genuine Mexican experience compared to some establishments, and the margaritas are quite enjoyable.

yelp:train:73035.orig: This church is close to our home but the community is just to large compared to what I am used to.  The parish community is friendly and welcoming but due to its large size just overwelming.  The mass and music are not traditional to what I am accustom to, but are instead more contempary.  I have been to Catholic churches in various states and countries.
yelp:train:73035.para: The church near our residence is quite expansive, making it feel overwhelming compared to the smaller communities I'm familiar with. The parish community exudes friendliness and openness, yet its vastness can be a bit daunting. The style of mass and music here diverges from my usual experiences, leaning towards a more contemporary approach. Having visited Catholic churches across different states and countries, this is a unique experience for me.

yelp:train:73305.orig: The entire property is run down, kinda creepy and pretty yucky.  I had rented some inline skates thad had moldy inserts.  I think they may be the only roller rink in Madison so you don't have too  many options.\n\nObviously this place is popular with kids and they don't seem to notice all the blight so we would just grin and bear it.
yelp:train:73305.para: The property appears dilapidated, somewhat eerie, and quite unappealing. I rented inline skates that featured moldy inserts. Given that it might be the sole roller rink in Madison, there aren't many alternatives. Clearly, this location is favored by children, who appear oblivious to the surrounding decay, leading us to simply endure it with a smile.

yelp:train:73455.orig: As someone who uses a bicycle daily for commuting purposes and running the occasional errand, I have greatly appreciated the service people at Williamson Street Bikes. Whether it's changing a flat, or a major overhaul of gears, brakes, derailleur, etc., the guys working there have always been polite, informative and helpful.  Although there have been times where I spent a boatload of money on new gear, there have also been plenty of times when they made a quick fix for me at no charge.\n\nIn all, I'm pleased to have such a great resource so close to where I live (and nicely situated on the bike path!)
yelp:train:73455.para: I regularly commute on my bike and occasionally run errands, and I've found immense value in the assistance provided by the staff at Williamson Street Bikes. Their politeness, knowledge, and willingness to help have been consistent, whether it's repairing a punctured tire or conducting a comprehensive bike component upgrade. Despite some instances where I invested heavily in new parts, they've also offered free, swift repairs. Overall, I'm satisfied with this excellent resource conveniently located near my residence and strategically positioned along the bike path.

yelp:train:74203.orig: Fun place to go if you need to get off state street for a while- hasn't been updated since the 50's and it shows. It's only a half block each off of the capitol square and state street. \n\nIt does get busy on weekends, so be ready for that. Shuffleboard and pitchers are the prime attraction. Can't be missed on a pub crawl.
yelp:train:74203.para: A delightful spot to escape the hustle of state street, this location hasn't seen renovations since the 1950s, reflecting its age. Situated just a short distance from the capitol square and state street, it's a half-block away. \n\nWeekends bring a lively crowd, so prepare for the bustle. The main draws are shuffleboard and pitchers, making it an essential stop for a pub crawl.

yelp:train:75068.orig:
After a day of sitting in meetings- a great seafood dinner within walking distance of my hotel seemed like a perfect way to end my day. So after debating between a couple of choices- we chose to go to the Ocean Grill- a sleek contemporary restaurant that was voted the best seafood restaurant in Madison in 2006.

Too bad the weather didn't cooperate as I would have liked to have sit outside on their patio area.  Oh well- we did get a nice table by the windows to enjoy our dinner.

This restaurant prides itself on its 26 varieties of sparking wine which makes them Madison's premiere champagne bar.  Not in the mood for champagne?  They have a great wine list with over 25 wines available by the glass.

We started with fresh oysters (2 varieties), fried calamari with a peanut sauce and an interesting goat cheese coated with nuts and honey and served with fruit. All were delicious- a perfect way to start our evening.

The entrees were where it fell apart a little for me.  While the grouper sounded wonderful- coated with horseradish and served with wasabi mashed potatoes and stir fried vegetables- in reality, the fish was bland and over cooked and the vegetables were almost greasy
yelp:train:75068.para: Following a day filled with meetings, a nearby seafood dinner within walking distance of my hotel appeared as an ideal way to conclude the day. After considering a few options, we decided on Ocean Grill, a modern, contemporary eatery that was recognized as the top seafood restaurant in Madison in 2006. Unfortunately, the weather didn't permit us to dine outdoors on their patio. However, we managed to secure a lovely window-side table for our meal. This establishment boasts 26 different sparkling wines, establishing it as Madison's leading champagne bar. If champagne wasn't your preference, they offer an extensive wine list featuring over 25 selections by the glass. Our meal commenced with two varieties of fresh oysters, fried calamari with a peanut sauce, and a unique goat cheese topped with nuts and honey, accompanied by fruit. All these dishes were delightful, setting a fantastic tone for our night. However, the entrees didn't quite meet my expectations. Despite the grouper's appealing description of being coated with horseradish and served with wasabi mashed potatoes and stir-fried vegetables, the fish turned out to be tasteless and overdone, and the vegetables were almost greasy.

yelp:train:75531.orig:
I was visiting Wisconsin and craving Korean food towards the end of my trip, which lead me to this restaurant. My impression of the decor was that it was very minimal, but there were some historic Korean knick-knacks. There was only 1 person working trying to seat, take orders, serve, and ring up the bill. He was super nice and greeted us immediately. 

As for the food...we got ddukbokki (spicy rice cakes), kimchi fried rice, and yukgaeyang (a spicy beef soup). There was a lack of side dishes that Korean restaurants are known for and the ones that came out were unimpressive (kimchi, fried sweet potatoes, and pickled radish). The ddukbokki was too mushy/overcooked and lacked the spicy taste that I was craving. I enjoyed the kimchi fried rice and the portion size was big. The yukgaeyang was decent. However, the food came out fast and the service was great. 

Compared to other Korean restaurants I've been to back home this place ranks low but seeing how this is one of two Korean restaurants in Madison it does the job if you're in the mood for Korean.
yelp:train:75531.para: During my stay in Wisconsin, my desire for Korean cuisine towards the trip's conclusion guided me to this eatery. The interior design was quite sparse, yet it featured some antique Korean memorabilia. A single staff member was managing seating, order taking, service, and payment processing, and he was exceptionally welcoming. \n\nRegarding the meal, we were served ddukbokki (spicy rice cakes), kimchi fried rice, and yukgaeyang (a spicy beef broth). There was a noticeable absence of the usual Korean side dishes, and the ones provided were underwhelming (kimchi, fried sweet potatoes, and radish pickles). The ddukbokki was overly soft and lacked the desired spiciness. However, I found the kimchi fried rice to be enjoyable and the portion size generous. The yukgaeyang was satisfactory. Despite the rapid service and excellent service, when compared to other Korean restaurants I've frequented, this establishment falls short. Nevertheless, it fulfills its role as one of the two Korean dining options in Madison for those seeking Korean food.

yelp:train:75702.orig: I haven't been all that impressed with Bluephies.  The food was fine, but overpriced for what we received.  I think I paid about $14 for a salad with grilled chicken.  The decor was interesting but I wasn't really feeling the ambiance.  I stopped by another time for their famous desserts and was again somewhat disappointed.  The cookie dough egg roll, Oreo ravioli, and Butterfinger wontons didn't live up to expectations.  You can get an edible meal here, but the price-value equation is a little off.
yelp:train:75702.para: Bluephies left me somewhat underwhelmed. The cuisine was acceptable, yet the cost seemed excessive for the portion size. I recall spending roughly $14 on a salad with grilled chicken. The interior design was intriguing, but it didn't quite set the right mood. On a subsequent visit, I was let down by their renowned sweets. The cookie dough egg roll, Oreo ravioli, and Butterfinger wontons failed to meet my anticipations. While edible options are available, the balance between cost and quality isn't quite right.

yelp:train:75799.orig: I went to Cinema as a new customer for the first time a few weeks ago. My perm was falling out, I hadn't had a cut in awhile and I described myself as the \""before\"" girl in shampoo commercials. I just let Nicole do her thing, whatever she thought would make me look better. She gave me a fantastic cut that brought out my curls, taught me how to style my hair, and recommended a few awesome products. It has made ALL the difference! I look and feel like a rockstar again and as for my curls - I have people asking me all the time if I got it repermed!  Hehehe. She will definitely be my new go to girl. \n\nThe shop itself is fabulous - it smells great, the staff is friendly, and it has a calm, relaxing environment.  And the prices are very reasonable for the level of service you get. I would recommend Cinema to anyone.
yelp:train:75799.para: A few weeks back, I became a Cinema regular as a fresh patron. My hair was untamed, I hadn't visited a salon in some time, and I saw myself as the "pre-styled" version in ads for hair products. I entrusted Nicole with my hair transformation, and she delivered a stunning cut that accentuated my natural curls, instructed me in hair styling techniques, and suggested some excellent products. This change has been transformative! I now exude confidence and my curls are the talk of the town. Nicole has earned her spot as my preferred stylist. \n\nThe salon's ambiance is delightful - it's fragrant, the team is welcoming, and it offers a serene atmosphere. The cost is also quite fair considering the quality of service provided. I wholeheartedly endorse Cinema to everyone.

yelp:train:76126.orig:
I'm going to give this place the benefit of the doubt and say that we went on a bad night. Business was slow with only 2 lone diners in the entire restaurant not including by boyfriend and I. This would have been fine I guess except that there was no music playing through the speakers whatsoever. The only sound in the diner was the quiet clinking of silverware and the distant reminder that we all die alone. Existential crises aside, it's safe to say that the ambiance (or lack thereof) was nothing short of fucking awkward. 

I am sorry to say that the food did not make up for it. Mozzarella sticks were good but it mostly went downhill from there, both my grilled chicken sandwich and my boyfriends quesadilla had this weird sweet taste to them and both meals were left half finished. 

The service was good, if quiet.

All in all the Parkway did the job and we both left unhungry but that is the extent of the praise I can give it. Probably not a place for date night, unless awkward silences are your thing.
yelp:train:76126.para:
I'll assume this location deserves a chance and acknowledge that our visit coincided with a poor night. The establishment was underwhelmingly quiet, hosting just two patrons, excluding my boyfriend and I. While this could have been acceptable, the absence of any background music was glaring. The only audible elements were the soft tinkling of cutlery and a subtle reminder of our solitary existence. Despite these existential thoughts, it's clear that the atmosphere was uncomfortably awkward. 

Regrettably, the cuisine failed to compensate for the experience. The mozzarella sticks were decent, but subsequent dishes, including my boyfriend's quesadilla and my grilled chicken sandwich, had an unusual sweet undertone. Both meals were abandoned halfway. 

The service was commendable for its silence. 

In summary, the Parkway fulfilled its purpose, and we departed without hunger. However, this is the sole commendation I can muster. It seems unlikely to be a suitable venue for a romantic evening, unless you find awkward pauses appealing.

yelp:train:76161.orig: They announced today they are closing. As you can see due to my previous review I am not surprised. Sad but not suprised.
yelp:train:76161.para: They declared today their shutdown. Given my earlier critique, it's understandable that I'm not taken aback. Regretful yet expected.

yelp:train:76742.orig: The restaurant is a reconverted barn so it's a very cool restaurant space! I ordered the battered beer cod (only offered on fish fry nights which is Wednesday and Friday) and it was good. My coworker ordered the chicken salad which he liked. He said the chicken tasted crispy and wasn't greasy either. Overall had a nice meal there
yelp:train:76742.para: The eatery, transformed from a barn, offers a unique dining atmosphere! I opted for the battered beer cod, exclusively available on fish fry nights (Wednesday and Friday), and found it enjoyable. My colleague chose the chicken salad and expressed his approval, noting the chicken was crispy and not oily. In summary, we both had a pleasant dining experience.

yelp:train:77697.orig:
Stayed three nights for an on site conference.  Service is what you would expect.  Room is slightly less than what you would expect.  Food is fine.

Here is what I did not expect: as an SPG gold level member to be put in one of the rooms farthest from everything with a view of the parking lot.  To be charged almost $300/night AND THEN an additional $13/day for wired, yes wired, internet access in my room.  Insult to injury $8 for a beer.  And the ""authentic"" Native American decor - cheesy.  Almost to the point of insulting.  Burning sage in the lobby?  Really?

In summary, I felt they took advantage of a group bringing them several hundred customers for four days.

Fail.
yelp:train:77697.para:
Remained for three nights attending a conference on-site. The service met standard expectations. The room was marginally below expectations. The food quality was acceptable.

Here's what surprised me: despite being a Gold level SPG member, I was allocated a room distant from amenities with a parking lot view. I was charged nearly $300 per night plus an extra $13 daily for wired internet in my room. The added $8 for a beer felt like a slight. The so-called "authentic" Native American decor seemed cheesy and bordered on disrespectful. The practice of burning sage in the lobby seemed unnecessary.

In conclusion, I felt exploited as a group bringing them several hundred customers for four days.

Result: Fail.

yelp:train:78269.orig:
Yummy food, open till midnight, walking distance from Sidebar, fantastic pianist... HOW HAVE I NEVER BEEN HERE BEFORE?!? 

We walked in at 1045 on a Saturday night, ever-so-slightly depressed, sober (hence the depression); the three of us.  We were seated right away, and the kind host offered us a lunch menu in addition to the three dinner menus, which I thought a bit odd, the only snafu, if you can call it that, of the evening.  

I ate the cup of squash soup ($5, including a brulee'd ginger marshmallow that will blow your mind) and split the bruschetta plate ($12) and tasted the creme brulee ($7?) and thought everything was delicious.  The bruschetta, in particular, was standout and made for a great snack.  The kitchen, according to our accommodating server, closed at 1130, so I'll bear that in mind when i next get the late-night munchies.  The pianist shut down at about five, maybe ten till midnight.  We didn't leave till about 10 after midnight, quite satisfied and with spirits much lifted.  I suppose that last part may have had a little something to do with the fact the two TVs over the bar were playing Spaceballs, but also the food was delectable, so who knows.  i'll be b
yelp:train:78269.para:
Delicious cuisine, open until the stroke of midnight, conveniently located near Sidebar, accompanied by an exceptional pianist. HOW HAVE I NEVER BEEN HERE BEFORE?!? 

On a Saturday night at 10:45, slightly downcast and sober, we entered, and were immediately seated. The hospitable host presented us with a lunch option along with the three dinner choices, which seemed unusual, the only minor hiccup of the night. 

I savored the squash soup ($5, with a ginger marshmallow topping that will astonish you) and shared the bruschetta platter ($12), relishing the creme brulee (approximately $7?) and found everything to be scrumptious. The bruschetta, especially, stood out and served as an excellent snack. Our accommodating server informed us that the kitchen closed at 11:30, a detail I'll remember for future late-night cravings. The pianist ceased playing around five or ten past midnight. We lingered until approximately 10 after midnight, feeling content and our mood significantly improved. The combination of the two TVs over the bar showing Spaceballs and the mouthwatering food might have contributed to this, but it's hard to say for certain. I'll be back.

yelp:train:78585.para: They are absolutely terrible, extremely poor business owners, and I am now officially boycotting them for the following reasons...a companion of mine, her one-year-old child, and I visited their store some time ago and bought numerous items, amounting to over $250. Move your vehicles off my property!" At that moment, I informed him that his sign clearly stated "Parking for Easley's customers only" and that I was indeed a customer, presenting him with my receipt. After spending $250 on this particular visit, I was not willing to move my car even 18 feet. Furthermore, there were no other customers present.
