yelp:train:104137.orig: A visit to Aloha Specialties has been a tradition on all my trips to Vegas.  The reason is the great food.  I guess you can categorize the place as \""fast casual\"".  You order at the counter, take a number and food is brought out to you.  Service was quick.  This past weekend, my boys and I tried the Kim Chee Saimen, Korean Chicken , and Tripe Stew.  Everything was hot and delicious.  The Saimen had a nice kick from the spicy kim chee and it included large blocks of tofu.   That bowl of soup was huge.  The Korean Chicken was also well flavored, moist and has a nice grilled crust.  We all agreed that the Tripe Stew was amazing.  Tender pieces of tripe in a not-so-thick tomato based sauce.  That was comfort food at it's best.  I would order that again.  Overall, it was a great visit to the hawaiian restaurant.
yelp:train:104137.para: Regularly, I make it a point to dine at Aloha Specialties during my visits to Las Vegas, drawn by their exceptional cuisine. Recently, my sons and I sampled the Kim Chee Saimen, Korean Chicken, and Tripe Stew. All dishes were served piping hot and tasted fantastic. The Saimen was spicy due to the kim chee and came with generous tofu chunks. The soup portion was quite substantial. The Korean Chicken was flavorful, moist, and had a delightful grilled crust. We all concurred that the Tripe Stew was outstanding, featuring tender tripe in a light tomato sauce. It was the epitome of comfort food. I would certainly revisit and rate this Hawaiian restaurant highly.

I love Downtown Las Vegas also known as the 9th island. I'm a Hawaii girl living in Los Angeles, so when I go to Vegas, I always stop at the Cal for a slice of home. The local style food at Market Street Cafe (they have bomb Butterfish) and the plate lunch style grinds at Aloha Specialties are ONO! 

If you're not from Hawaii, you probably won't understand why a 30-something would want to hang at the Cal, the place is like a Hawaiian version of the movie Cocoon. But I love seeing the old Japanese and local people from Hawaii gambling with their wheel chairs and sometimes even oxygen tanks. They go! 

I've been staying at the Cal since small kid time, so its very nostalgic for me, lots of memories there. I love seeing the mixed faces and pidgin accents :) Also I've been brainwashed since childhood (they mail regulars a magazine with pictures of all the Hawaii winners) that I will win if play at a Sam Boyd hotel. Sure enough, I won 1000 quarters on Wheel of Fortune on my last visit, must be because I rubbed the shaka buddha's belly :) 

See you in March 2014, yay :)

The authentic local cuisine at Market Street Cafe, particularly their exceptional Butterfish, and the traditional plate lunches at Aloha Specialties are simply irresistible.

However, I find joy in observing the elderly Japanese and local Hawaiians engaging in gambling, sometimes even with their wheelchairs and oxygen tanks. They are undeterred. 

My connection to Cal dates back to my childhood, making it a place filled with nostalgia and countless memories. I relish the sight of diverse faces and pidgin accents. I would have given them five stars
yelp:train:107300.para:

We started with the antipasti appetizer, a delightful mix of cheeses, olives, pickled artichokes, prosciutto, and spicy ham. Although I'm not usually fond of olives, the red ones here were surprisingly enjoyable. Paired with the table bread, it felt like a complete meal. However, it's wise to save room for the main course, as their pasta dishes are a must-try. I opted for the seafood spaghetti, which was delicious but slightly overwhelming with its seafood content. My partner enjoyed the Sea Bass, which was cooked to perfection and melted in their mouth.

I would have given this place a perfect five-star rating.

The vegetables were not drowned in oil and the roll was not soaked through. The tri-tip was cooked to a medium/medium-well. I normally prefer medium rare, so next time I will request it and see if they offer that option. The green salad was standard. My friend got the hobo omelet and you have to be starving to finish it. It is a gigantic monster stuffed and topped with bacon, sausage, ham, spinach, onion, and cheese. The red potato chunks are tender, not too salty, but not crispy. It comes with a bread as well. He got the biscuit. They are big, not dense and light.  Both entrees cost around nine dollars. We were shocked by how generous the portions were for the price and that it tasted good too. I could not finish the meal
yelp:train:107744.para: I have a fondness for breakfast, but if I had the option to select any meal throughout the day, it would be a triumph. You watch the table and drop the order for the rest of the meal to approximately coincide with the customer finishing soup &/or salad. (And they weren't busy.) The waitress brought the check before bringing the dessert that is included in the 4-course meal. I had to ask for a refill of tea. The scallops in the linguine were the size of mini-marshmallows and poor quality. Sorry, but the cheddar biscuits aren't enough to bring me back. yelp:train:109511.para: Besides the tasty cheddar biscuits, I perceive the service as appalling and the pricing of the food excessive. I opted for a 4-course meal. The soup & salad arrived promptly and were satisfactory, neither exceptional nor disappointing. However, I was barely halfway through when the main course arrived, which is unacceptable, especially from someone with my background in service. It's crucial to time the remaining meal components to match the customer's completion of the soup & salad, particularly when the establishment isn't crowded. The waitress prematurely presented the bill before the dessert, which is part of the 4-course meal. I had to request a tea refill. The scallops in the linguine were disappointingly small and of inferior quality. Regrettably, the cheddar biscuits alone won't entice me to return. Compared to the plethora of superior seafood options in Las Vegas, Red Lobster falls short.

I'm not sure what this sauce is called, but it's the one that scorches your tongue. For my main dish, I opted for the usual Chicken Vindaloo. This dish features chicken simmered in a hot, spicy sauce with diced potatoes, and you can adjust the spice level. I chose the "hot" option, and it was absolutely delicious! The heat was intense enough to make me sweat while eating it. That's some fantastic food! I devoured it with garlic naan and cheese naan, leaving me quite satiated. I didn't have space for dessert, which is quite impressive.

yelp:train:118033.orig: I knew I wanted to look at rings before I walked in.  I was not greeted.  As soon as I got someone's attention.  I asked if the gold ring came without stones.  He said no, and turned his attention to other customers.  I had more questions and wanted to find the right gift for my brother.  I was turned off he made no suggestions and did not care to help me.  I waited minutes longer to at least try them on and see them outside of the case.  A lady finally came, she was pleasant and answered my questions.  Ultimately I wasn't interested in making a purchase from the experience I had.
yelp:train:118033.para: Before entering, I was certain I'd inspect the rings. Regrettably, I wasn't acknowledged. Once I managed to get someone's focus, I inquired about a gold ring without gemstones. The response was negative, and he shifted his focus to other patrons. I had additional queries and aimed to select an appropriate present for my sibling. His lack of advice and unwillingness to assist left me disenchanted. I decided to delay further to personally examine the rings outside their display. Eventually, a friendly woman approached, she was accommodating and addressed my inquiries. Nonetheless, the experience didn't sway me to buy anything.

yelp:train:118605.orig:
Service is awful and management is even worse. this place is not worth the price point. A complete tourist trap. I've lived in Las Vegas for 8 years and have never received such appalling service. That is probably why I have never eaten at Rainforest before. I should have stuck with my intuition. 

On a Friday night around closing time with a small rush from the club next door my friends and I ordered a few drinks and an appetizer. The drinks came slowly as the bartenders were more focused on closing the bar and the appetizer almost never came. We waited 45 minutes for an appetizer and if we hadn't made three unsuccessful attempts to alert management before finally getting their attention a fourth time then we probably would have never received it. 

Management was not only unresponsive but upon contact with management (Erika) they seemed to have lack of concern and offered absolutely no resolution. This is just food and beverage. Making me happy is as simple as showing some sympathy and throwing me a concession for my time and satisfaction for which you have frivolously wasted. 

The lifetime value of this customer was never valuable to the management of this place.
yelp:train:118605.para:
The service at this establishment is dreadful, with management being even more disappointing. It's not justified by its cost, essentially a tourist scam. Despite residing in Las Vegas for eight years, I've never encountered such poor service, which is why I've never tried Rainforest. Trusting my gut was the wiser choice. 

On a Friday evening, amidst the bar's closing rush and a slight influx from the adjacent club, my companions and I placed an order for drinks and a starter. The drinks were delivered at a snail's pace, with the staff preoccupied with winding down the bar. The appetizer was almost never served, and we endured a 45-minute wait. Had we not made three failed attempts to get management's attention before finally succeeding a fourth time, we might not have received it at all. 

The management was not just unresponsive, but also seemed to lack empathy and offered no solution. In the food and beverage industry, making a customer happy is as straightforward as showing some understanding and offering a token of appreciation for their time and satisfaction, which they have squandered. 

The value of this customer's lifetime was never considered important by the management of this place.

yelp:train:118816.orig:
My lovely gfs took me here for the big night of my bachelorette party weekend.  I'm such a lucky girl!!! :)

Yum I love Lawry's....it's almost as good as House of Prime Rib in SF.  Minus one star....b/c the salad at House of Prime Rib is better and the creamed spinach costs extra here.  The prime rib tastes just as good as HOPR and the customer service was excellent....so I'm giving it 4 stars.

I would definitely come back here again!  I'm drooling just thinking about it.
yelp:train:118816.para:
My adorable girlfriend brought me here for the significant celebration of my single woman's party weekend. I feel incredibly fortunate! 😊

Delicious! I adore Lawry's, it's nearly on par with the House of Prime Rib in SF. However, I'm deducting one star because the salad at House of Prime Rib is superior and the creamed spinach here is an additional charge. The prime rib's flavor matches that of HOPR and the service was outstanding, hence a 4-star rating. 

I am certain to return, I'm salivating at the mere thought of it.

yelp:train:119337.orig: To synopsize: \n  This is five star- but not 100% perfection (I have yet to find that anywhere).  Food was a 9/10, view was a 10/10, service was a 9/10, location was 10/10, drinks (Fall in Paris or something) was an 11/10, and I had a great time.  Portions were not as small as in fancy restaurants and for the price ($300 for two with two cocktails, two appetizers, and two entrees), the experience cannot be beat in Las Vegas.  Ask for a seat overlooking the fountain, it was seriously breathtaking!
yelp:train:119337.para: In summary: \n The establishment received a stellar 5-star rating, albeit not flawless (perfection eludes me in all places). The culinary experience scored a 9/10, the scenery a perfect 10/10, service was commendable at 9/10, the venue's location was impeccable with a 10/10 rating. The beverage selection, particularly the Fall in Paris, was exceptional at 11/10. The overall enjoyment was immense. Despite larger portion sizes compared to high-end dining, the value for money at $300 for two, including two cocktails, two appetizers, and two entrees, made it unparalleled in Las Vegas. For an unforgettable view, request a table with a fountain view, it's truly awe-inspiring.

yelp:train:119479.orig: My family and I visited this place yesterday to celebrate a birthday.  Let me tell you that it was the worst experience I've ever had at a restaurant.  The fish was horrible and the shrimp taste like it came straight from the freezer section of the local grocery store...actually that's giving them too much credit, because I've had frozen food from the market and it taste 110% better. Not only was the food inedible, but the entire restaurant had a strange smell...that should have been our first clue.  A couple of people in our group had the Gumbo and I wouldn't recommend that dish either.  My son had something as simple as a hamburger, and that was just barely edible. Everyone had stomach issues immediately after leaving the restaurant.  We are all from Los Angeles and have had our share of good fried fish all over LA, so we know good food. All I can say is don't do it, unless you like giving your money away. Let me make one thing clear, they are only receiving 1 star, because I don't believe have any other choice to select lower than 1.
yelp:train:119479.para: Yesterday, my family and I went to this location to commemorate a birthday, but it turned out to be the most disappointing dining experience I've ever encountered. The seafood was dreadful, with the shrimp tasting suspiciously like it was taken from the frozen aisle of a nearby supermarket - a comparison I find unfair, as I've sampled frozen market items that are noticeably superior in flavor. The food was unpalatable, and the restaurant was permeated with an odd odor, which should have been a warning sign. Even the Gumbo, tried by some in our group, was not recommended. My son's simple hamburger was barely tolerable. Post-meal, everyone suffered from stomach discomfort. Given our familiarity with high-quality fried fish in Los Angeles, this was a letdown. I'm leaving them with a stark 1-star rating, as I see no other option but to express my utmost dissatisfaction.

yelp:train:119702.orig: 1 cashier on the day after Thanksgiving- one of the busiest movie days of the year.  Line a mile long as you might expect.  No worries- we go to the \""Express Kiosk\"" inside the lobby.  Except that it isn't really \""Express\"", and there's a long line here as well (and only 1 kiosk).  Then the scanner to read your \""Club Card\"" doesn't work- so the holds people up even longer trying to get their 100 points so some year they an get a free Pepsie. Then buying popcorn the scanner doesn't work again.  Then the attendant ignores a request for \""extra butter\"" and puts on almost no butter.  It really gets a bit comical at some point and I almost start looking for cameras to see if I'm on candid camera.  Save the stress and rent a DVD- or go to a chain that's cares enough about it's customers to hire enough human beings on busy days.
yelp:train:119702.para: After Thanksgiving, a single cashier manages the influx of customers on the busiest movie day of the year, resulting in a mile-long queue. To avoid the wait, patrons head to the "Express Kiosk" within the lobby, but it's not a true express service and also has a lengthy line with just one kiosk. The kiosk's Club Card scanner malfunctions, causing further delays for customers trying to accumulate 100 points for a free Pepsi. The popcorn scanner also fails to function. The attendant's negligence in adding butter to the popcorn adds to the humor, almost prompting the customer to look for hidden cameras. To avoid the hassle, it's recommended to rent a DVD or choose a well-staffed chain outlet on peak days.

yelp:train:119840.para:

yelp:train:120039.para:
We appreciate it, and fortunately our mailbox remains intact unlike others. We secured our place just before the renovations concluded, securing a favorable rate at present (though rates have since increased). There was a minor conflict with the management, but it appears they've brought in fresh personnel.

Maintenance is commendable, and when our air conditioner malfunctioned during the summer, it was repaired within a day. The second incident took two days. You may need to liaise a few times.

Drawbacks:

- W/S/G incurs a high cost: We contribute an additional $55 monthly for this. (Update: It seems they've introduced more charges, making our WSG exceed $80 last month, which seems excessive for two individuals).

- The contracted company for renovation skimped on quality. The renovated apartment lacked a drawer handle, the new laminate floor developed bubbles, the bathroom towel rod collapsed after a few months, the blinds were not replaced with the updated models, the ceiling fan was unstable, and they substituted granite countertops with laminate (unclear reasoning). Moreover, the new refrigerator malfunctioned within months. I hope we won't be held accountable for these issues when we vacate, as others have expressed concerns.

Advice: This area is reliable and offers an excellent location.

yelp:train:121643.orig: Love this place. Best BBQ in Vegas. What's even better is that the food and service are consistently great. Our favorites: ribs, brisket, the king, burnt ends, cream corn, sticky Vegas style chicken wings and the best BBQ nachos you've ever imagined. If you haven't tried Memphis yet, run don't walk.
yelp:train:121643.para: This spot is fantastic, boasting the top-notch BBQ scene in Vegas. The standout factor is the unwavering quality of both the cuisine and customer service. Our top picks include succulent ribs, tender brisket, the king's special, smoky burnt ends, creamy corn, uniquely flavored chicken wings, and the ultimate BBQ nachos. If you haven't experienced Memphis yet, it's highly recommended to visit without delay.

yelp:train:121721.orig:
Poor quality, too expensive, dirty.

I give up on this place for their all-you-can-eat salad and pizza buffet which costs way too much (about $10). Consistently poor quality pizza, stained carpet, unmotivated staff. I've eaten here for lunch for almost three years now, and every time I go back I keep asking myself ""Why do I bother coming back to this place?"" Today, tables were unclean, and the salad bar had cottage cheese that tasted spoiled and the pizza was really poor quality. I know how hard it is to run a pizza establishment, and I feel for anyone who tries, really I do, but if you have time to lean, you have time to clean. Somebody needs to learn how to pick up a rag instead of texting on their cell phone.

Hint: take down the tip jar. We all know you expect a tip for nothing. It shows.
yelp:train:121721.para:
Substandard service, overpriced, unclean.\n\nI've lost interest in this venue due to their all-you-can-eat salad and pizza buffet, which is roughly $10. The pizza quality is consistently subpar, the carpet is stained, and the staff lacks motivation. I've visited for lunch almost three years, and each time I question my decision to return. Today, the tables were dirty, the cottage cheese in the salad bar smelled off, and the pizza quality was disappointing. I understand the challenges of managing a pizza place, and I empathize with those who do, but if you have spare time, it's better spent on cleaning rather than on your phone. Consider removing the tip jar; it's clear you anticipate a tip for no service.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the same meaning, topic, sentiment, emotion, and intent as the original text, but uses different wording and sentence structure. The length is also roughly the same.)

yelp:train:122052.para: Summarizing my experience in a single term would be 'disappointed.' yelp:train:122632.orig: This place is cheap , but for a few dollars more you can have MUCH better quality. This place is NOT good. If youre eating rolls, you can't tell what is inside, so youre fine. I only eat nigiri so I see the fish all too well. The first time I went here the tuna, which is usually a nice red color, was almost BROWN. I went another time to give them another chance, disappointed again. This is far from real Japanese food.
yelp:train:122632.para: This location offers affordability, yet by investing a few extra dollars, you can acquire significantly superior quality. However, it falls short of expectations. When it comes to rolls, the contents remain a mystery, which is acceptable for those who don't mind. As a nigiri enthusiast, I can clearly discern the fish, which is not ideal. The initial visit revealed tuna that was nearly brown instead of its usual vibrant red, leading to disappointment. On a subsequent visit, the same lackluster experience was repeated. It does not meet the standards of authentic Japanese cuisine.

yelp:train:123517.para: No proof of purchase, incorrect amount returned, and the meal was extremely disappointing. In my chicken burrito, I discovered tendons, excessive fat, and dark meat intertwined with brown fatty tissues. I genuinely wish to regurgitate it, but I'm reluctant to consume it again.

yelp:train:123548.orig: I really like this english pub. It's one of the few ones that serve a raspberry cider around town. They also have an traditional english item called a chip bunty (or butty) which basically is french fries (chips) served inside of a buttered roll. It's hard to look at without laughing but it's an awesome idea. They have a huge selection of draft beers on tap. This place actually has a better menu than the one on Spring Mtn.
yelp:train:123548.para: I genuinely appreciate this English pub. It stands out as one of the limited establishments in the area offering raspberry cider. They also offer a classic English dish known as a chip bunty (or butty), which consists of french fries (chips) nestled within a buttered roll. It's quite amusing to observe, yet it's a brilliant concept. They boast an extensive range of draft beers available on tap. In fact, this venue surpasses the menu options at Spring Mtn.

The french toast is just melt-in-your-mouth, pure bliss.  Can't get enough of it.  Wish you guys would come here to California!!!
yelp:train:124763.para: Each time I visit Las Vegas, I ensure to dine at Blueberry Hill. I adore the service, the pricing, the ambiance, and particularly the French toast. The French toast is incredibly delightful, melting in your mouth. I'm craving for you to visit us in California!

yelp:train:124805.orig:
Dan Dee is the best. They've been around forever and have been my family's go to dry cleaning service for many years. 

The owners are a couple and they are very nice. You always walk away feeling happy after dropping off your dry cleaning! 

I also dry clean my husband's Air Force uniform here, so, honestly it's a place where you can trust your clothes won't go missing.

In this fast paced world it's nice to find a simple place like this where you trust the owners and enjoy every experience you have. It may just be dry cleaning, but hey, it's important!
yelp:train:124805.para:
Dan Dee stands out as the top choice. This establishment has been a longstanding favorite for my family's laundry needs for quite some time. 

The proprietors, a devoted couple, exude warmth and friendliness. Leaving their premises always leaves you with a sense of joy. 

I also entrust my husband's military attire to them, making it a reliable spot where you can confidently leave your garments. 

In today's swift world, it's comforting to discover a straightforward establishment like this, where you can rely on the proprietors and savor each encounter. Even though it's just about laundry, it holds significant value!

yelp:train:125201.orig:
We went on the Friday night underwear night.. egads..

I drank beer for free cause I was not afraid to be in my undies then I asked what the beer was?  ICE HOUSE....  I didn't even know they had Ice house on draft ..  Hell I didn't know they stll made Ice house in a can or bottle.  I asked for a lime and I was refused.  

Partner was drinking ""Cape Cod""  Vodka cranberry woth a lime  He was rerefused a lime I was dumbfound.  WHen I asked if I were able to get more limes we were then refused service.

Sooooooooooo  The Eagle chain  is know aws a Levi Leather bar, this place smelled like it and looked like it however...  Swing and MISS

I have been there before and everytime I go I say I would not go back.  Last time I was there the Bartender was soo fcuking spun he was falling all over the place.  

 I will not go back and I love to support the gay community

Horrible attitudes.. drunk and or durgged out bartenders 

REALLY SERIOUSLY  This place totally sucked!
yelp:train:125201.para:
On a Friday evening, we attended a night dedicated to wearing underwear, quite astonishing...

I consumed beer without cost, as I wasn't intimidated by the prospect of being in my undergarments, then inquired about the beer's origin. To my surprise, I discovered it was Ice House, a brand I was unaware they still produced in cans or bottles. When I requested a lime, my request was denied. 

My companion was enjoying "Cape Cod" - a vodka cranberry mixed with lime. Similarly, I was denied a lime, leaving me bewildered. 

Thus, the Eagle chain, known for its Levi Leather bar aesthetic, fell short of expectations. I've visited before, and each time, I vow not to return. The last visit was particularly unpleasant due to the bartender's disheveled state. 

I will not revisit this place, but I am committed to supporting the LGBTQ+ community. 

The experience was marred by the unprofessional behavior of the inebriated and disheveled bartenders. 

In my opinion, this establishment was utterly disappointing.

yelp:train:125215.orig:
I have to give Deseret Industries credit for presenting a thrift store in a bright, clean, department store fashion. Kudos to them for knowing how important merchandising is! The store is exceptionally well organized, well lit, wide isles with an abundance of sales personnel who are dressed up in a tie and vest (!) All this in a thrift store! amazing.

But I am not overly impressed with the pricing here as it is a hit or miss. For some reason thrift stores tend to price Ralph Lauren at top dollar and this place is no exception. True it is an expensive brand, but Marshall's and TJ Maxx sell RL polos for $20, so I'm not gonna pay $20 for a used one. 

They sell better merchandise in a locked glass case and of course the price tags are hidden so you have to call over an employee just to get a price (annoying). Anything that is higher quality (which is often in the eye of the beholder) is priced accordingly. I once asked a clerk if he can open the case and he said he didn't have a key. He then rudely told me to ""find someone else"" to open it then walked away. What a jerk!

Out back is a covered patio with furniture and other larger items. Sometimes it is chock full of stuff,
yelp:train:125215.para:
I must acknowledge Deseret Industries for their innovative approach in transforming a thrift store into a vibrant, spotless department store aesthetic. Applause is due to them for recognizing the significance of merchandising! The store boasts remarkable organization, ample lighting, and expansive aisles, complemented by a generous number of sales staff donning ties and vests (!) All this, within the context of a thrift store, is truly impressive.

However, I am not particularly impressed with the pricing strategy here, as it seems inconsistent. Thrift stores often price Ralph Lauren at premium rates, and this establishment is no exception. While Ralph Lauren is indeed a high-end brand, Marshall's and TJ Maxx offer similar polos for $20, making it unreasonable for me to pay $20 for a second-hand item. 

They display superior merchandise in a locked glass case, with price tags concealed, necessitating a request for an employee's assistance to obtain a price (irritating). Items perceived as higher quality, which can be subjective, are priced accordingly. I once inquired a clerk if he could unlock the case, to which he replied he lacked a key. He then dismissively suggested I find someone else to open it, before departing. Such behavior is unacceptable!

In the rear is a

yelp:train:126449.orig: I still consider myself a sushi noob, but with the AYCE at Sushimon I'll be a pro in no time! Half-rolls so you can try new ones, chef specials with awesome names, very tasty fish, and the dessert was yum (tempura ice cream woohoo!). There cooked sides were kinda blah, but that might be because I was mesmerized by the sushi feast. Order as you go so you don't over-order and pay extra for what you don't eat. They're open super late (like 2am I believe) so, if like me, you crave your sushi at midnight this is the place to get your fix.
yelp:train:126449.para: Despite being a novice when it comes to sushi, I'm confident that frequenting Sushimon's all-you-can-eat (AYCE) option will quickly elevate my skills. They offer half-rolls for sampling various types, chef specials with catchy titles, and delicious seafood. The dessert, particularly the tempura ice cream, was delightful. The cooked side dishes were somewhat unremarkable, possibly due to my sushi-centric focus. To avoid unnecessary charges for unconsumed items, order incrementally. Sushimon's late hours, potentially until around 2am, make it an ideal spot for those of us who crave sushi at the stroke of midnight.

yelp:train:126489.orig: Place is our favorite....the fish is great and the people are cool. Place gets packed in the evenings which is always a good sign.\n\nWe have been going weekly for several years and can't say anything bad.   Hiro and Eddie are the best!!!!
yelp:train:126489.para: The location holds a special place in our hearts, with its excellent fish and amiable community. The evening crowds are a positive indicator. We've frequented this spot weekly for years, and we have nothing but praise, especially for Hiro and Eddie.

yelp:train:126559.orig: This review like a number of my other reviews is long overdue. For 4 years now Sushi Mon has been my quick, neighborhood go to spot when I'm in need of my fix. I'm literally down the street. With the exception of one incredibly gross, gut-wenching moment a few years back where me and some co-workers found a roach scrambling on our table as our waitress handed our bill, its been smooth sailing.. I'm glad because its said if you find just one of those mofos then its fairly certain theres an infestation. In this case I'm gonna chalk it up to a momentary lapse in unsanitary food practices and thankfully theres been no sight of those suckas ever since.\n\n It still gets busy during their peak times, prices are on par with the rest of them AYCE but I still fu*k with this place and the rest of the spots belonging to the Mon group.
yelp:train:126559.para: This critique, similar to my previous ones, is overdue. Sushi Mon has been my nearby, convenient choice for over four years whenever I crave it. I'm literally just a block away. Except for a single extremely unpleasant incident a few years ago when a co-worker and I encountered a roach on our table as our server delivered our bill, things have been consistently smooth. I'm relieved because it's rumored that finding one such pest indicates a larger problem. I attribute this isolated incident to a temporary lapse in maintaining proper hygiene standards, and I'm thankful that there hasn't been any recurrence since. Despite occasional busyness during peak hours and average pricing compared to other AYCE establishments under the Mon brand, I continue to support this place and its affiliated spots.

yelp:train:126959.para: Extremely impolite and lacking in professionalism.

yelp:train:127132.orig: I have been getting my hair done here at Salon Indigo, by Sara, for over 3 years and can not say enough about what a wonderful job she does.  I get stopped (yes literally) and complimented on my hair.  I have a very short spikey hair cut and Sara cuts it better than anyone ever has!   Highly recommend this salon!
yelp:train:127132.para: For more than three years, I've been visiting Salon Indigo for hair treatments under the skilled hands of Sara, who consistently delivers exceptional results. I frequently receive genuine praise for my distinctive, short, spiky hairstyle, which Sara expertly crafts. I wholeheartedly endorse this salon!

yelp:train:127444.orig:
I would have given this place four stars given that the food is pretty good, they deliver, and are close to us. However, my latest encounter, which was last then 10 minutes ago, was what brought the star level down. 
I placed a phone order for delivery (I usually do it online but I wanted a boba drink so I called it in instead because they dont have the drinks online). Let me replay the part of the conversation that made me angry...
Me:""Can I have a boba drink too?""
Person on the phone:""Yeah, you can have one. What do you want. "" (in a serious/annoyed voice)
Um. Wait. What?  That's not how you talk to a customer. I should've cancelled my order at that moment. But whatever, I guess my boyfriend and I will find other places close by. I actually liked this place but never again.
yelp:train:127444.para:
I would have rated this establishment four stars if not for the recent incident that occurred just ten minutes prior. Normally, I place my orders online, but for a boba beverage, I opted for a phone call as it wasn't available online. Here's the part of the dialogue that upset me:
Me: "Can I also get a boba drink?"
Person on the phone: "Sure, you can. What would you like?" (in a tone that was serious and irritating)
I should have stopped the order immediately, but I suppose I'll have to look for other nearby alternatives. Although I generally enjoyed this place, I won't be returning anytime soon.

yelp:train:127804.orig: shame on your deceptive business practices . You sold an extended warranty and then stated it was up. I purchased a 3 year extended that should extend from manufactures which is 1 year. My tv is just over 3 years old . I should have 6 months left. I am going to make sure that everyone knows about your terrible faulty business practices . I wish I could give you no star !!
yelp:train:127804.para: Expressing disappointment, I condemn your misleading commercial strategies. I bought a three-year extension, which should cover the manufacturer's one-year guarantee. With my television surpassing three years, I'm entitled to an additional six months. I intend to inform others about your unreliable and dishonest business operations. I regretfully wish I could assign you the lowest possible rating.

yelp:train:127850.orig: Great baguettes! Really, truly, great baguettes!\n\nSal at the checkout line is awesome too, and I always make sure to stop and say hi!
yelp:train:127850.para: Fantastic baguettes! Absolutely, undeniably fantastic baguettes!\n\nSal at the checkout counter is wonderful, and I always take a moment to greet her!

yelp:train:127867.orig: Disgusting is an under statement!! Doesn't even deserve a star. What a waste of money.  Be warned the food is nasty, we ordered general tso's and sesame chicken... neither were even close to what they should taste like.. the food was burnt and chewy. The lo mein is awful. Nothing good to say about the incompetent dtaff who told me twice that the forks and soy sauce was in the bag I checked and it wasn't.  I want my $30 back!!
yelp:train:127867.para: The quality of the food is far from satisfactory and doesn't warrant a single star. It's a regrettable expenditure. Caution is advised as the dishes, including General Tso's and Sesame Chicken, were disappointingly burnt and tough. The lo mein was particularly unpalatable. The staff's dtaff was inept, assuring me twice that essential items like forks and soy sauce were in a bag I verified to be empty. I demand a full refund of $30.

yelp:train:128403.orig: Nothing bad to say. Have your group ready to be seated when you get there. Food choices are outstanding. Quality is superior, service quick and friendly. Portions great, hot, fresh. Priced RIGHT!!! Many regulars there each visit & they know all the friendly staff. Won't go anywhere else now for breakfast! Hostess Devyn is the best!\nHated The Griddle :-(
yelp:train:128403.para: No negative comments to share. Ensure your party is prepared to take their seats upon arrival. The variety of food options is exceptional, with superior quality, prompt and amiable service. The portion sizes are generous, served hot and fresh. The pricing is perfectly balanced. Frequent patrons return, recognizing the welcoming staff. This place is now my go-to for breakfast, and I highly commend Hostess Devyn! I regret my previous experience at The Griddle.

yelp:train:128543.orig:
Terrible service! The waitress was extremely slow even slower after we mentioned we were catching a movie.  We had to practically jump up and down waving our arms to call her over.  It honestly looked as if she would serve other tables and avoid eye contact at our table and pretend we weren't calling her just so she could go to the kitchen. 

As for the food most everything tasted pretty salty especially the double pan-fried noodles...YUCK!  BUT, if you're into ALL that SALT  I guess go.

P.s.  We were harassed by a homeless person from the parking lot all the way to the front door walkway.
yelp:train:128543.para:
The service was dreadful! The server moved at a snail's pace, barely improving even after we indicated we were heading to a film. We had to almost leap and wave our limbs to get her attention. It seemed as though she would prioritize other tables, ignore our presence, and feign non-existence just to leave us for the kitchen. 

Regarding the cuisine, most dishes had an overwhelming saltiness, particularly the double pan-fried noodles, which was quite unpleasant. However, for those who enjoy an excess of salt, it might be suitable. 

Additionally, we were persistently bothered by a homeless individual from the parking area all the way to the entrance pathway.

yelp:train:128963.orig: Sexy!!! Sat outside in front of an outdoor firepit while enjoying a bottle of wine and crabcakes! Very classy! Waitress was sweet as pie and everybody there seemed to be happy and enjoying themselves.\nSuch a romantic place to gaze in your loved one's eye and let the ambience take you away!
yelp:train:128963.para: Enjoying a glass of wine and savoring crabcakes in the open-air setting of a firepit, exuding a sophisticated vibe! The attentive waitress added to the delightful atmosphere, with all patrons radiating joy and contentment. This idyllic spot is perfect for intimate moments with your partner, immersed in the enchanting surroundings.

yelp:train:129154.orig: More than party of 4 are force to pay 18% tips! Not that I am too cheap to pay for it, is I felt the food was not fresh, felt sick after we ate, service was terrible, no matter how many times we ask them to take the order. They never stay long enough to actually finish take your order. We have to order more than 8 times to finish our first decision of ordering 2 sashimi combo, 5 different type sushi order, and 4 appetizers. \n\nPlease don't go, it is waste of time, waste of money and it affect your health.  And most important: u will spend a quality time in bathroom typing a review on yelp. It is only 4 hours after we ate there and I already spend an hour in and out of the bathroom.  Alright, is enough of that. Please go if u want to want to experience what I did. Good luck!
yelp:train:129154.para: Over four people are compelled to contribute 18% in tips, despite not being stingy about payment. However, the food lacked freshness, leading to discomfort post-consumption, and the service was abysmal, with the staff failing to take orders promptly. It took us over eight attempts to complete our initial order of two sashimi combos, five sushi varieties, and four appetizers. \n\nAvoid this place, as it's a futile use of time and funds, and it could potentially harm your health. Moreover, you'll likely end up spending quality time in the restroom, penning a Yelp review within four hours of dining. I've already spent an hour there. That's enough. If you're curious about my experience, proceed with caution. Good luck!

yelp:train:129346.orig: Wow I am really disappointed. Food was very bland and tasteless. I have three kids and they all ordered from the kids menu. The two \""funny face\"" pancakes were awful. The design on them was pitiful and it was caked with so much whip cream I wasn't sure there was a pancake under it. My daughters Mac and cheese was chewy and gummy. Apparently the drink isn't included with a kids meal so each drink my small children drank was $1.30 a piece! Talk about nickel and diming. I had good memories as a kid but as an adult ihop was a huge let down.
yelp:train:129346.para: I'm genuinely disheartened. The meal lacked flavor and was unappetizing. My three children chose dishes from the kids' section. The "funny face" pancakes were disappointing, with a poor design and excessive whipped cream, making it hard to discern the actual pancake. My daughters' mac and cheese was overly chewy and gummy. It seems the drinks are extra charges for kids' meals, costing $1.30 each, which feels like excessive nickel and dime tactics. Despite fond childhood memories, my experience at ihop as an adult was a significant letdown.

yelp:train:129500.orig: We stood in 3 lines to pay a bill. We got up to the SELF-SERVICE MACHINE and it doesn't take plastic - only cash or check. WHUUUUTTTTT????!!!!!! What is this, 1970? Hey, Nevada Power.... in case you people have been on Mars for the last 35 years, this is the 21rst century. GET WITH THE FREAKING PROGRAM !!!!!!!!!!!!!! i want to swipe and go. we had to go back out to the car, ride around looking for a Wells Fargo, i had to withdraw cash, we drove back to the FREAKING POWER COMPANY, stood in line some more, and paid our bill. you know, they'll drag you through the mud before they turn your power on, but they won't forget to switch it off. Have a nice day, Nevada Power..... well, not really.
yelp:train:129500.para: We queued up in three rows to settle a payment. Approaching the self-service terminal, we discovered it only accepts cash or checks, not plastic. WHUUUUTTTTT????!!!!!! It felt like a throwback to the 1970s. Nevada Power, get with the times! I was eager to swipe and leave. We had to return to our vehicle, search for a Wells Fargo to withdraw cash, and then return to the outdated Power Company. Despite their tendency to make things difficult before activating your service, they certainly don't forget to deactivate it. A pleasant day, Nevada Power, but not quite.

yelp:train:129501.para: The level of customer support provided is extremely poor.

yelp:train:129759.orig: Stopped here never reading reviews or anything about the place... It looked nice and classy so I figured it would be awesome. Our waitress, Sharon just wasn't pleasant at all... She slammed our drinks and plates down. Then we asked for more bread and she said \""well I'll have to charge you\"" so that is fine but when she gave us the basket it only had two small pieces in it, which before each basket had about 4, so that was kinda crappy. Then one of us ordered another beer and she poured it and just let it over flow all onto the table and didn't even say a word.  The crab in the stuffed mushroom app and the stuffed shrimp dinner has mostly imitation crab in it, which for the price is just unacceptable. I had just plain fettuccine Alfredo and it was great I ate the whole thing....  The lighting is just so bright and it's around dinner so I don't want to be under a heat lamp during dinner... I'm not sure if I'd go back ....
yelp:train:129759.para: Never perused any comments or information about the venue... The place appeared stylish and upscale, leading me to expect a great experience. Our server, Sharon, was far from enjoyable; she forcefully delivered our beverages and dishes. When we requested additional bread, she stated, "I'll have to charge you," which I accepted, but the bread basket contained only two tiny pieces, a stark contrast to the usual four, leaving us feeling disappointed. Furthermore, when one of us ordered another beer, she carelessly allowed it to spill over onto the table without uttering a single word. The predominant use of imitation crab in the crab-filled mushroom appetizer and the shrimp dinner was deemed unacceptable for the cost. However, I thoroughly enjoyed the entire portion of plain fettuccine Alfredo. The excessive brightness of the lighting during dinner hours was another concern, making me hesitate about revisiting.

yelp:train:130074.orig:
This is the most overrated establishment in the Madison area. If I hear one person talk about the food and the PIE, how GREAT the pie is, I will scream. Yup.

My friend and I got there and we are waiting to be seated. We were acknowledged and asked to just step aside because a person with a walker was coming through. No problem. Then another party of two walks in and they are seated immediately. WHAT?!  We had been waiting and did a nice thing and were skipped over.

So we waited more and more. The place was cold and it was raining so the wait was even worse. Finally we are seated. Our server took over ten minutes to get to our table. When she got there, there was no greeting. She just asked us what we wanted. Wow. So much for service.

So then, we order. My order: coffee and a cobb salad. Coffee does not take too long. It took almost another ten minutes to get coffee. I am not kidding. This was probably the WORST service I have ever received. 

I get my coffee and shortly after my salad comes. Here is the thing, I never saw my server again until I was done with my salad. thank goodness the salad was fresh and delicious. If I had needed anything, I would have been SOL. Yeah
yelp:train:130074.para:
This establishment in Madison is widely considered excessively praised. Whenever someone extols the food and the exceptional quality of the pie, I'll express my frustration. Indeed.

My companion and I arrived and were left waiting for a table. We were recognized and asked to move aside for a person using a walker. No issue. Then, a duo entered and were immediately seated. Unbelievable. We endured the wait longer. The venue was chilly, and the rain made it even more unpleasant. Eventually, we were seated. Our server took over ten minutes to approach our table. Upon arrival, there was no welcome. She simply inquired about our order. Unimpressive. The service was far from satisfactory.

We placed our order. I chose coffee and a cobb salad. The coffee preparation was relatively quick. However, it took almost another ten minutes for the coffee to arrive. I'm serious. This was possibly the poorest service I've ever encountered. 

I received my coffee shortly after, and shortly after, my salad arrived. Here's the catch, I didn't see my server again until I finished my salad. Fortunately, the salad was fresh and tasty. If I had required assistance, I would have been in a dire situation. Absolutely.

yelp:train:130260.orig: Every student at U of I knows that Gumby's is the place to go for Pokey Sticks..I don't even think I can count how many times I ate these late at night! They are basically bread sticks with cheese on them and marinara sauce to dip them in...soooo good!
yelp:train:130260.para: Every individual enrolled at the University of Illinois is aware that Gumby's serves the best Pokey Sticks. I can't even tally the number of times I indulged in these late-night snacks! They essentially consist of bread sticks topped with cheese and served with marinara sauce for dipping, and they're incredibly delicious!

yelp:train:130308.orig: Over priced vodka and gin drinks in martini glasses. I thought for the price you would get a really good martini but they didnt even make it correctly.  A little pretentious but the servers are nice, just too expensive for poorly made cocktails.
yelp:train:130308.para: Exorbitant prices for vodka and gin mixed drinks served in martini glasses. I anticipated a high-quality martini for the cost, but the preparation fell short of expectations. While the staff is amiable, the steep prices for subpar cocktails are unjustifiable.

yelp:train:130559.orig: Very long wait for a mediocre pizza. \nNot worth the hype. Definitely had better pizzas elsewhere including Phoenix. Grimaldi's in Scottsdale have way better Margarita pizzas.
yelp:train:130559.para: Extended delay for an average-quality pizza. \nNot justifying the buzz. I found superior pizza options elsewhere, such as Phoenix. Compared to Scottsdale's Grimaldi's, their Margarita pizzas are significantly superior.

yelp:train:130622.orig: I've been wanting to go there for years. Finally had the opportunity. I was so excited like I was going to Disney. What a let down. I really didn't think that it had any flavor.
yelp:train:130622.para:
For a long time, I've yearned to visit that place. I got the chance recently. I felt as thrilled as if I were heading to Disneyland. Sadly, it was a disappointment. I genuinely didn't expect it to be anything special.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original sentiment of anticipation and disappointment, the topic of visiting a place, and the emotion of excitement turning into letdown. The length is roughly the same as the original text.)

yelp:train:130783.orig:
I have only been to Durant's a couple of times for drinks and dessert, but it was just such a cool place that now I have to go back for dinner. 

The beginning: Even though I know it's commonplace, I still felt weird entering through the kitchen.  

The atmosphere: If the cast of Mad Men were on location in Phoenix, they'd totally be at Durant's inhaling scotch. 

The lowdown: Our server was professional and helpful-suggesting wines for us as well as dessert options. We went with the strawberry shortcake and received a gynormous plate heaped with enough delectable amazing-ness to feed six people easily! The moist, spongy shortcake was topped with fresh berries, lots of whipped cream and then sprinkled with chocolate flakes. DEEEElicious!   

The verdict: Two thumbs up! 
To do list: Eat dinner here.
yelp:train:130783.para:
I've only visited Durant's a few times for cocktails and sweets, but it felt so unique that I must return for a meal. 

The intro: Despite it being a usual scene, I felt a bit out of place walking in through the kitchen. 

The vibe: If the characters from Mad Men were in Phoenix, they'd surely be at Durant's, savoring their scotch. 

The review: Our waiter was courteous and efficient, recommending wines and dessert choices. We opted for the strawberry shortcake, which came on a massive plate brimming with mouthwatering delights that could easily satisfy six diners. The moist, fluffy shortcake was adorned with fresh berries, generous whipped cream, and a dusting of chocolate shavings. Absolutely scrumptious! 

The conclusion: A solid two thumbs up! 
Next on my list: Dine at Durant's.

yelp:train:131308.orig:
This place has been here for a long time now. It has a lot of reviews, it does not need another. But, I will just put my 2 cents in.
It is a lovely place right on Central. My daughter lives within walking distance to it.
So she is the one that had me go there first.
Breakfast ,lunch, and dinner ,coffee and even the drink!
I have to say my favorite is the Breakfast.
Nice little place to go, I do not like it when it is packed and too many people here.
 
But, on off times it is better. Parking is limited.
Very worth a try. I really love downtown Phoenix, even though it is much different than most major cities. They are growing and developing ever so slowly.
yelp:train:131308.para:
This location has stood the test of time and boasts numerous reviews, making additional ones unnecessary. Nonetheless, I'll share my modest opinion.
Located conveniently on Central, my daughter resides nearby, prompting my initial visit.
The establishment offers a variety of meals, beverages, and coffee.
Among them, breakfast stands out as my preferred choice.
I appreciate the ambiance of this cozy spot, but it becomes less enjoyable when overcrowded and overly populated.

During quieter periods, it's more enjoyable. However, parking can be a challenge.
I highly recommend giving it a shot. Despite its unique character, I have a deep affection for downtown Phoenix and its gradual growth.

yelp:train:131350.orig: Went to Lux on a Saturday morning for the first time. It was packed and the line was from the counter to the door. Lucky for me, I was in line in front of John a frequent customer who told me that during the week there is not usually a line and he is usually in and out. I ordered the Egg sandwich and a caramel latte both were very good and the prices were not bad. I was very happy that they offer both almond and soy milk as an option. I look forward to returning during the week  or on a weekend night and having a more relaxed experience.
yelp:train:131350.para: On a Saturday morning, I visited Lux for the initial time and found it bustling with activity. The queue stretched from the counter to the entrance. Fortunately, I was ahead of John, a regular patron who informed me that on weekdays, the place is usually less crowded and he can quickly finish his visit. I opted for the Egg sandwich and a caramel latte, both of which were delicious and reasonably priced. I appreciated the availability of almond and soy milk options. I'm eager to return, either on a weekday for a more tranquil visit or on a weekend evening.

yelp:train:131512.orig:
Back in the mid-Nineties, studio-apartment-dwelling, student-loan-burdened me would come here and get great deals on things like Ecco shoes, Kenneth Cole shirts, fashionable jeans, and other things I never could have afforded new from Nordstrom's. Sometimes the condition was questionable, but the price always reflected that. I wore out several pairs of high-line shoes purchased here for $11-$12. 

Those days are long gone. Now, can't find a pair of shoes here for less than $30. The clothes are picked over. And mainly, going there is an opportunity for me to  bump into the future ex-Mrs. Bill B., or perhaps the exit strategy from the current prospective Mrs. Bill B. 

Because If you're looking for young or not-quite-so-young-anymore shoppers in 5-inch heels, miniskirts and too much make-up, this is a great place to find them.

Just don't offer to buy them shoes. Anymore. These days.
yelp:train:131512.para:
In the 1990s, as a financially strained university student living in a studio apartment, I frequented this place to snag affordable deals on items like Ecco footwear, Kenneth Cole tops, stylish denim, and other luxury goods I couldn't otherwise afford from Nordstrom. Occasionally, the quality was dubious, but the cost always mirrored that. I managed to wear out multiple pairs of high-end footwear bought here for $11-$12. 

Those times have passed. Now, it's nearly impossible to find shoes here for under $30. The merchandise is mostly sold out. Moreover, visiting this place gives me a chance to encounter the future Mrs. Bill B., or maybe the departure plan for the current Mrs. Bill B. 

If you're searching for younger or aging shoppers sporting 5-inch heels, mini skirts, and excessive makeup, this is an ideal spot to spot them. However, don't try to buy their shoes anymore. This is the current scenario.

yelp:train:131698.orig: I have been a regular at Via for over 20 years. The food was always great but the service often lagged. They fixed that over the recent years but the food quality is now sagging and the portions are shrinking. Went there the other night...ordered chicken tacos. When they came we found they were rancid...stunk so bad we almost got ill right there. The server they told us they make them in the morning...yuck. That does it for us...moving on.
yelp:train:131698.para: For more than two decades, I've frequented Via, where the cuisine consistently impressed, yet service frequently fell short. Recent improvements in service have been noted, however, the food's quality has declined and portion sizes have diminished. During my last visit, I ordered chicken tacos which, upon arrival, were noticeably spoiled and emitted a foul odor, nearly causing sickness. The server informed us of their morning preparation, which was unappetizing. This experience has led us to seek dining elsewhere.

yelp:train:131918.orig:
All I have to say is......W.....T......F?

yelp:train:132230.orig: Horrible service. Our waiter forgot one of our dishes and was rude. The food was mediocre. Do not come here!! Worse experience ever.
yelp:train:132230.para: Terrible customer service encountered. The waiter neglected an order and behaved inappropriately. The meal quality was average. Avoid this place at all costs! An extremely poor experience.

yelp:train:132477.orig:
Don't make early reservation on those online deals from credit cards, rewards, etc
By the time u get to the hotel u will not be in their priority list. The best room could probably give u is a 2 beds facing a parking lot or back area of the hotel ughhh.. yelp:train:132726.orig: i don't get why everyone seems to love this place. service is pretty slow and the food is just ok. the emphasis seems to be on volume over quality.
yelp:train:132726.para: I struggle to understand why this location is so popular. The service pace is sluggish and the cuisine is merely satisfactory, with a focus on quantity rather than excellence.

yelp:train:132776.orig: Amazing fresh, authentic food... wish I'd thought to ask for more guidance before ordering... It would be great to go with a big group in order to be able to sample more...
yelp:train:132776.para: Authentic and recently prepared cuisine... regret for not seeking additional advice prior to placing an order... Ideally, joining a larger party would allow for a broader range of tastes to be experienced...

yelp:train:132822.orig:

yelp:train:132822.para: The sole error of Siam's Lotus was its unfortunate timing and location. yelp:train:132904.orig: We were told to arrive early so we arrived before they opened. The outside of the restaurant is a little seedy but the inside is completely different with very efficient and friendly wait staff.\nThe yellow curry was the best I've ever had outside of Thailand. The tom yum soup was divine. I wish we had this kind of Thai food in the east coast!
yelp:train:132904.para: We were instructed to come ahead of time, so we got there before the restaurant's doors were unlocked. The exterior gives off a somewhat shabby vibe, but once inside, the atmosphere transforms with highly competent and amiable waiters. The yellow curry surpassed all previous Thai dishes I've tasted outside of Thailand, and the tom yum soup was nothing short of exquisite. I long for the opportunity to savor this exceptional Thai cuisine on the east coast.

yelp:train:132914.orig:
Best Thai food in Las Vegas?  Hell, you could put it up as best Thai food anywhere.  Some of the best Thai food I've ever had.

Came here for a lunch, since my old roommate works in Las Vegas now.  I must say that it was a bit of a pain in the ass to find this place, given that it's in the part of Vegas that I'd classify as the middle of absolutely nowhere.  But at least there's a lot of parking.  Additionally, the interior is really nothing to go crazy over...it's good for one thing, and that's stuffing a lot of people in it.

Anyways, I'm just glad that Yelp reviews has all those tips for what to eat.  Because my god, this menu is MASSIVE.  I could literally spend like 15 minutes trying to parse down the 25 things I want to eat, but can't because I don't want to be a massive fatass.  So I settle on the soft shell crab pad kee mao because I've never seen it before on any Thai menu (and under my cardinal rule, ALWAYS get something you've never gotten before if you're somewhere new).  Did not disappoint at all.  Good amount of spice and minty flavor, and the soft shell crab was fantastic.  Excellent choice, good work Yelpers!

Little more expensive than I'd prefer, but pretty
yelp:train:132914.para:
Las Vegas boasts the finest Thai cuisine, as per my personal experience. I stumbled upon this gem during a lunch break, as my former roommate is now based in the city. The location is somewhat remote, but it offers ample parking. The interior is functional rather than visually stunning, but it's efficient for accommodating a large number of patrons. 

I'm grateful for Yelp's guidance, as the extensive menu was overwhelming. I opted for the soft shell crab pad kee mao, a unique choice on a Thai menu, and it exceeded my expectations with its spicy and minty flavor profile. The crab was exceptional. Despite the higher price point, it was a worthwhile decision, thanks to the helpful Yelpers.

yelp:train:133232.orig: Food is not anything special and hibachi is way overpriced. While dining an ant crawled off my sisters plate and when we told them about it they made it seem like we were making it up, however later on in the night more ants appeared on our table and when we told the sever she wiped the table down with a dish rag and went on with no care. For a meal that was over $150 I expected better service and a much cleaner atmosphere. If you're thinking of coming here maybe try Ohjah instead; cleaner atmosphere, tastier food, fresher sushi, and much better customer service.
yelp:train:133232.para: Food at this place doesn't stand out and the hibachi dishes are excessively costly. During our meal, an ant incident occurred on my sister's plate, which they dismissed as a fabrication, but as the evening progressed, additional ants surfaced on our table. The server's response was to merely wipe the table with a cloth and continue without concern. Given the $150 price tag, I anticipated superior service and a cleaner environment. If you're considering dining here, you might want to opt for Ohjah, which offers a cleaner setting, more flavorful cuisine, fresher sushi, and superior customer service.

yelp:train:133307.para: The club is fantastic! The interior is incredibly stylish, with a gothic vibe, but it's definitely not for the typical crowd. yelp:train:133657.orig: Food poisoning alert. My husband and I dined at Emerils on 03/8/13. 3 hours after dining there he was violently ill with food poisoning. My guess was either the salmon or the banana crime pie. This had all the ear marks of staph poisoning . My shrimp was over cooked and cold,his salmon was undercooked and blah. The wine was ordered incorrectly and the staff became surly and indifferent when it was brought to their attention. It was restaurant week in Vegas and the menu was there but concealed behind other menu pages. Stay away from this restaurant it is hazardous to your health.
yelp:train:133657.para: On March 8, 2013, my spouse and I experienced food poisoning after eating at Emerils. Three hours post-meal, he suffered severely from food poisoning, likely due to the salmon or banana crime pie. The situation resembled staph contamination, with my shrimp being improperly cooked and cold, and his salmon undercooked. The wine was served incorrectly, and the staff responded rudely and apathetically upon realizing the mistake. During restaurant week in Las Vegas, the menu was hidden among other pages. Avoid this establishment as it poses a significant health risk.

yelp:train:133851.orig:
I love this place!  Yes, it's pricey, but if you want to complain, go to Mickey Ds, ok?  What I will tell you is that you don't need to upgrade to the Kobe beef, go with the Angus beef and you'll get a great burger.  

They have composed burger offerings and they have the any way you want it option, which is the way I roll at The Burger Bar.  Great fries, the pass the Mickey D's test.  Don't be shy about calling an audible and going to the onion rings, they are tasty!  The selection of beers is fantastic.  The staff is awesome, they will take good care of you while you're there.

Just go there and I promise you'll have a great burger.
yelp:train:133851.para: This spot is fantastic! While it may come with a higher price tag, it's worth it compared to fast food joints like McDonald's. Instead of splurging on Kobe beef, opt for the Angus beef for a delicious burger. The Burger Bar offers a variety of burger combinations, including the customizable option that I prefer. The fries are top-notch, surpassing the standard at McDonald's. Feel free to switch to the onion rings for a flavorful treat. The beer selection is impressive, and the staff is exceptional, ensuring a pleasant experience for you. I assure you, you'll enjoy a top-notch burger here.

yelp:train:133959.orig:

Sweet potato fries were just ok.  I've had way better.  They were a little cold and seemed like they were about 1-2 hours old

Good selection of beers if you aren't spoiled by the Northwest like I am
yelp:train:133959.para:
American Kobe Burger - Medium-rare as requested, received medium. The burger is fairly large, but the flavor doesn't quite hit the mark. It's satisfactory. The tomato component was quite small. 

Sweet potato fries were average, falling short of my past experiences. They appeared slightly chilled and seemed to have been stored for about 1-2 hours. 

A commendable variety of beers is available, especially for those not accustomed to the Northwest's offerings, like myself.

yelp:train:134087.orig: The food here is always pretty good. It's also pretty decent for a vegetarian as well. The best part about this place is the beer. The hard part is deciding between Hussong's or Burger Bar for food, which are both very amazing restaurants that are located right next to each other.
yelp:train:134087.para: The cuisine at this location consistently delivers a satisfying taste. It's commendable for vegetarians too. The highlight of this spot is its selection of beer, particularly the rare Dogfish Head varieties. I make it a point to visit this place whenever I'm in Las Vegas. The challenge lies in choosing between Hussong's and Burger Bar, both exceptional dining establishments situated side by side.

yelp:train:134109.orig: great sliders! great restrooms! great servers! Not so great casino-hotel, the hotel or mandalay bay are horrible.
yelp:train:134109.para: Excellent sliders and commendable restrooms, along with outstanding service! However, the casino-hotel experience, specifically the hotel or Mandalay Bay, is disappointing.

yelp:train:134336.orig: Wasn't sure what to expect but it was not cheesy, which I really appreciated. There's audience interaction throughout the show. Afterwards, Penn and Teller meet and greet people as they exit until every last person gets a chance for a photo or autograph, which I think is really, really nice.
yelp:train:134336.para: I wasn't certain of the outcome, but it turned out to be far from corny, a fact I found quite gratifying. The performers are humorous, with a touch of political satire, and they execute impressive magic tricks. Following the event, Penn and Teller personally interact with departing guests, ensuring each individual has the opportunity for a photo or signature, an act I consider exceptionally considerate.

yelp:train:134370.orig: I had a great time at the show. Not to surprising some of their tricks will blow you away. Tickets are a little pricey but they're less then some of the other shows on the strip.
yelp:train:134370.para:
The performance was thoroughly enjoyable, and it's no shock that some of their illusions will leave you astonished. I wholeheartedly endorse the event and suggest that if you're willing to wait, you can arrange for a photo with Penn and Teller post-show. While the tickets come at a premium, they're still more affordable compared to other attractions on the strip.

yelp:train:135819.orig: I almost feel sad to write a bad review but this place used to be my favorite Chinese restaurant of all time up until recently. If anyone from the restaurant is reading this, please work on the sanitation so life long customers will return for the food we love so much.
yelp:train:135819.para: It's almost heartbreaking to pen a negative critique, yet this former top-tier Chinese eatery held a special place in my heart until lately. Since that incident in the previous autumn, we've refrained from returning. Once a beloved spot, it has sadly lost its charm. To the restaurant's management, I implore you to prioritize cleanliness to regain the loyalty of long-standing patrons who cherish the cuisine.

yelp:train:136263.para:

yelp:train:136760.orig: Service out weighs food. Food is decent, but I'd rather give my business to a place with better service.
yelp:train:136760.para: Better service is more valuable than the quality of food. Although the food is satisfactory, I would choose a venue that prioritizes superior customer service.

yelp:train:136776.orig:
Here I go again, singing the praises of Chicago food.

As someone who was spoiled by having every type of food at her fingertips for eight glorious years, I really missed good Thai when I moved to Madison. I had a beef Pad Si Ew hankering from hell one day, so we ordered Sa-Bai Thong. 

Thai food should be cheap (under $10) and delicious. This was mediocre and more pricy. The sauce was thick, bland and jelly like, and there was barely any beef. 

I have given this place another shot, ordering Pad Thai the second time, and it was no better. What kind of a Thai place can't make decent Pad Thai?!
yelp:train:136776.para:
Here I am once more extolling the virtues of Chicago cuisine.

Being accustomed to having an array of culinary options within reach for a prosperous eight-year period, I found myself longing for superior Thai fare upon relocating to Madison. One day, I craved a beef Pad Si Ew, so we placed an order for Sa-Bai Thong.

Thai dishes should be affordable (under $10) and delectable. This dish fell short, being mediocre and costly. The sauce was dense, tasteless, and gelatinous, with minimal beef content. 

I revisited this establishment, opting for Pad Thai on a subsequent occasion, but the quality remained unimproved. How can a Thai restaurant fail to serve a decent Pad Thai?!

yelp:train:136919.orig:
