yelp:train:136954.orig:
Went here for dinner with girlfriends on Tues. Wasn't blown away.

It was difficult for me to find as there is no signage. I finally had to ask someone after wandering around for 15 mins. 

The service was lackluster. Our server gave us the impression we were inconveniencing her more than anything. Not warm or friendly at all.

The menu was mostly sandwiches and salads all of which I wasn't particularly in the mood for. I was expecting more choices. I ended up ordering the Burger Au Poivre II...for $14.50, I was expecting WAY better quality.

I will give them credit for their very extensive cocktail list and the bar is well stocked with every type of quality liquor you can imagine. I had the celebration champagne which was tasty.

Beautiful atmosphere. I'd probably return for drinks at the bar but not the food or service.
yelp:train:136954.para:
Had dinner with friends on a Tuesday and the experience didn't impress me.

Locating the place was a challenge due to the absence of clear signs, leading me to seek assistance after 15 minutes of aimless wandering.

The service left much to be desired, with the server seeming unenthusiastic and unfriendly. The menu, dominated by sandwiches and salads, didn't align with my cravings, prompting me to settle for the Burger Au Poivre II at $14.50, which fell short of my expectations in terms of quality.

I commend them for their comprehensive cocktail selection and the well-stocked bar featuring a variety of high-quality spirits. I enjoyed the celebration champagne, which was flavorful.

The ambiance was pleasing, but I'm inclined to return for drinks at the bar rather than dining or experiencing the service.

yelp:train:137355.orig: It's over rated. Thought my daughter would get a kick out of the place but she was over it as fast as we got there.
yelp:train:137355.para: The place is excessively hyped, I anticipated my daughter would enjoy it, but she lost interest immediately upon arrival.

yelp:train:137423.orig: Got a free room for two nights here after gambling for probably only an hour! This place is great, but I still prefer the Gold Coast for gambling. Very friendly patrons and dealers here, with a wide selection of things to do here.
yelp:train:137423.para: Secured a complimentary two-night stay at this location post a brief gambling session, which lasted probably just an hour. The venue is commendable, yet my top choice for gambling remains the Gold Coast, where the atmosphere is warm with welcoming patrons and dealers, and a diverse array of activities is available.

yelp:train:137516.orig:
The rooms are nice for off strip hotel and not very expensive.
The service though is consistent with the price.I guess that's why they are understaffed.
There are no signs when you drive up for check-in and was very confusing. The rude valet admonished us for being so dumb and had us drive around again.
If you want a taxi you are on your own as well as cocktail service in the casino bars. I guess alcohol is not a profit center.
yelp:train:137516.para: The accommodations offer a pleasant experience at an affordable cost, aligning with the pricing. It seems the staffing levels are low, possibly due to the cost. Upon arrival, the lack of signage caused confusion, and the impolite valet criticized us for our apparent lack of awareness, necessitating another round of driving. For taxi services, one must arrange independently, and the provision of cocktails in casino bars is not prioritized, suggesting alcohol may not be a lucrative source of revenue.

yelp:train:138336.orig: This is by far my favorite place on the strip. The energy at the Bellagio is radiant and I always feel happy and relaxed whenever I'm spending time here. The casino is huge and there are a nice variety of games. It's also very clean and well kept. \n  My favorite thing is the interior design with this hotel. There's a indoor botanical garden that is absolutely magnificent and they change it every season. There's also floral blown glass on the lobby ceiling. It's breathtaking. Outside they have a huge water design with fountains and lights. Every night they do a water show where there's music, fountains shooting up and lights to go along with the show. LOVE this place. It's gorgeous. :)
yelp:train:138336.para: This is undoubtedly my preferred spot along the strip. The vibrant atmosphere at the Bellagio fills me with joy and tranquility every time I visit. The casino's expansive size offers a diverse selection of games. It maintains an immaculate and orderly appearance. \n  The interior design of this hotel is my absolute favorite. There's an impressive indoor botanical garden that they update seasonally. The lobby ceiling features stunning floral blown glass. It's truly awe-inspiring. Outside, a grand water feature with fountains and illuminations is present. Each evening, a spectacular water display with music, ascending fountains, and lights accompanies the show. I adore this place. It's absolutely stunning. :)

yelp:train:138597.orig: Very dirty seriously needs updated. Stains on chairs in room, horrible shower will not stay here again. To top it off a homeless bum urinated in middle of casino and guest services did nothing to remove him or even care. He was allowed to wander around casino. Dont stay there.
yelp:train:138597.para: The place is extremely unclean and urgently requires renovation. There are noticeable stains on the seating in the room, and the shower facilities are substandard. Additionally, a homeless individual defecated in the center of the casino, and the guest services were completely indifferent, neither addressing the issue nor showing any concern. The individual was permitted to roam freely within the casino. It's strongly advised not to linger there.

yelp:train:139053.orig: This was my third time staying at the LVH. With my company,I travel to numerous trade shows, many of which are held in Las Vegas. This hotel is very dated but always seemed to be the best option for location and proximity to the convention center. Well, this particular trip turned ugly when on the second morning of my stay I woke up, went to the restroom and when I returned to bed, there were bed bugs crawling on the pillow. I had never seen one before but a quick search on my phone confirmed their identity. I called house keeping right away and they sent up a security guard that collected the bugs in little baggies. They sent up a bell hop to carry my things to my new room in the old unrenovated tower (downgrade). The security guard said you need to wash those clothes as soon as possible in hot water. I happened to agree. I had one more night to stay at the LVH and I in NO WAY wanted to transport those nasty creatures back to my home in FL. When I got to my new room and I made a call to find out about laundry services. I was passed around to about 4 different people before someone was able to tell me if my clothes could be laundered. House keeping passed me to the Bell hop, bell h
yelp:train:139053.para: During my third visit to the LVH, as part of my company's frequent trade show trips to Las Vegas, I found the hotel's outdated charm to be advantageous for its location and closeness to the convention center. However, my stay took a negative turn on the second day when I discovered bed bugs on my pillow after waking up. After quickly identifying them with a phone search, I immediately alerted housekeeping, who dispatched a security guard to collect the pests in small bags. They also arranged for a bellhop to transfer my belongings to a less renovated tower room (downgrade). The security guard advised me to wash the infested clothes in hot water as soon as possible. I had one more night left at the LVH and was determined not to bring those unwelcome pests back to my home in Florida. Upon reaching my new room, I inquired about laundry services and was transferred between approximately four individuals before finally being informed about the laundering options for my clothes. Housekeeping then directed me to the Bellhop.

yelp:train:139304.orig: Upgraded to the red room premier and was glad I did.  The room was super cute, very clean and the bathroom was huge.  The view was the best feature - looked right over the Bellagio fountains and the pool.  However...don't go to this hotel if you want a nice pool.  The pool is very boring by Las Vegas standards.  And it closes really early - 6PM.  Other than that, a very nice, reasonably priced hotel on the strip.
yelp:train:139304.para: Transitioned to the red room's exclusive event and felt fortunate for the choice. The room exuded charm, maintained impeccable cleanliness, and boasted an expansive bathroom. The most impressive aspect was the breathtaking vista, offering a direct sightline to the Bellagio fountains and pool. However, it's not recommended for those seeking a vibrant pool experience, as it falls short of Las Vegas's standards and shuts down at 6PM. Aside from that, it stands out as a pleasant, cost-effective accommodation on the strip.

yelp:train:139305.orig:
We won't stay here again.  We only booked this place because Caesars, where we normally stay, was hosting an event and so the rooms were 4x the normal rates.  And now that we've seen the new Cosmopolitan hotel, I doubt we'll stay anywhere else!

We booked a king non-smoking, but when we arrived, there were no king N/S rooms available, so they put us in a room with 2 double beds.  They agreed to move us the next day for a room with a king bed and a view (you can get a great view of the Bellagio fountains from Paris) for our troubles, and when we finally re-packed and got moved, we had no view of the fountains, instead we were one floor above the pool.  I don't really care to stare at sunbathers all day, and being only one floor up made for very loud mornings, when people started partying at the pool and music was thumping.

The beds are horrible.  There are no comforters, just a blanket with sheets on either side of it (a fake ""duvet""?), the mattresses are hard and the pillows are bad.  The rooms are also so dated, with old furnishings, old school tvs, etc, and our shower had giant cracks in the floor (the tiles)... I was a little concerned about where that water was going!
yelp:train:139305.para:
We won't return to this location. Our reservation was made due to Caesars hosting an event, causing a significant price hike. After experiencing the newly opened Cosmopolitan hotel, we're unlikely to choose any other accommodations.

We reserved a non-smoking king room, but upon arrival, no such rooms were available, so we were given a room with two double beds. They promised to relocate us the following day to a room with a king bed and a view of the Bellagio fountains (which can be seen from Paris). However, when we were finally moved, we were situated one floor above the pool, missing the fountain view and subjected to loud mornings with pool parties and music.

The bed quality is subpar. Instead of a comforter, we only had a blanket with sheets on either side, resembling a counterfeit "duvet". The mattresses were firm and the pillows were uncomfortable. The rooms felt outdated with antiquated furnishings and old-school TVs. Our shower had noticeable cracks in the floor (tiles), raising concerns about water leakage.

yelp:train:139320.orig:
(+)
- Cheaper rooms
- Very nice front desk people
- good location

(-)
- food options slightly limited
- not as many mirrors in hotel room

First time staying here my past Vegas trip. I was expecting something like Treasure Island but their room was much better lit and didn't look old at all. We took an early flight in, got to check in early and even got the adjoining rooms we wanted woot! Quick tip, if you want adjoining rooms that actually connect by a door, then your rooms will have to be one King bed and the other with 2 queens. The lady at the front desk who helped us was wonderful and talked us through our options.

We got our rooms for a really great price from hotels dot com, Paris isn't the cheapest option out there for hotels but it has great rates without sacrificing location and too much quality. It is within walking distance of cosmopolitan and a quick cab ride to Wynn.

There aren't that many food options. A couple nicer places and a few ""10 dollars for a sandwich/salad"" places. No food court for those on a budget but you can always walk to nearby Planet Hollywood and get a cheap 6 dollar sandwich at the much hyped over Earl of Sandwich

Oh and the
yelp:train:139320.para:
(+)
- Affordable accommodations
- Friendly staff at the reception
- Ideal location

(-)
- Limited dining choices
- Fewer mirrors in the hotel rooms

During my initial visit to this place, after previous trips to Las Vegas, I anticipated a stay similar to that at Treasure Island. However, the illumination in the rooms was superior and they appeared modern. We checked in early and secured the adjacent rooms we desired. A helpful tip: for rooms that are truly connected, one must have a King-sized bed and the other with two queen beds. The receptionist who assisted us was exceptional and guided us through our choices.

We secured our rooms at a fantastic price from hotels dot com, Paris may not be the most economical choice for accommodations, but it offers competitive rates without compromising on location or quality. The hotel is a short walk from the city's vibrant atmosphere and a quick taxi ride to Wynn.

Food variety is somewhat scarce. There are a few upscale eateries and a few budget-friendly options offering sandwiches or salads for under ten dollars. There's no food court for budget-conscious travelers, but nearby Planet Hollywood offers a reasonably priced six-dollar sandwich at the popular Earl of Sandwich.

yelp:train:139436.orig:
The worst hotel on the strip unless you enjoy poor service, an extremely slow check Ballys gaming company, who operates the hotel.. It took 48 minutes to check in. 

I would stay at an MGM or WYNN property before ever staying here. 

I have a laundry list of issues from starting up the iron to iron my clothes and it not working. 45 minutes later getting a replacement to getting water from the hall way vending machine for $3.00 and it not dispensing water. I called the front desk and they state, sorry, we can't help you. 

Worst hotel on the strip bar none.
yelp:train:139436.para:
The least desirable accommodation on the strip, characterized by subpar service, a notably delayed Ballys gaming company check-in process, which lasted 48 minutes. 

I would opt for an MGM or WYNN establishment over this one. 

I've compiled numerous complaints, from an iron that fails to function upon initial use, requiring a 45-minute wait for a replacement, to a hallway vending machine that dispenses water for $3.00 but doesn't, and the front desk's inability to assist. 

This establishment is unparalleled in its poor quality on the strip.

yelp:train:139764.orig:
Truly disappointing on several levels.  The quality of the fish was simply not that good.  I'm not even comparing it to Sugarfish (highly recommended), but merely to local LA places like Brothers Sushi in Woodland HIlls.  When I'm paying Nobu prices, I expect better than Woodland Hills sushi, know what I mean?

The portion sizes were, frankly, skimpy.  I will credit them for serving a real Salmon Roll, whereas many sushi places use pieces of meat that has been broiled/burnt, this was real salmon skin, just like the good places do it.

The prices are really astronomical...and given that they all buy their fish from the same place(s), pretty ridiculous.  Hey, I've had sushi in Japan with businesses, and even paid for it one time -- a vertiginous buying experience that will affirm to you that Amex truly does have no credit limit on your card -- so I do know good and even great sushi.  This is not it.

The service was, and I'm not sure if this makes sense, but obsessively and (worse) aggressively obsequious.  This guy would continually hover over us explaining to us how (and exactly) whatever we wanted would be taken care of by him of the sushi chef.  Very intrusive, and I realiz
yelp:train:139764.para:
It was genuinely underwhelming in multiple aspects. The fish's quality was far from satisfactory, not even in comparison to Sugarfish, which is highly recommended. When paying Nobu prices, I anticipated superior quality, akin to that of local LA establishments like Brothers Sushi in Woodland Hills. The portion sizes were disappointingly small, but I must acknowledge their authentic Salmon Roll, unlike many places that use overcooked meat, this was genuine salmon skin, akin to what reputable places offer.

The prices were exorbitantly high, especially considering they all source their fish from the same suppliers, which seems unjustifiable. I've experienced sushi in Japan, even paying for it once, which was a nerve-wracking transaction that confirmed that American Express indeed has no spending limit on your card. This experience has taught me what genuine and even exceptional sushi tastes like, and this was not it.

The service was excessively and intrusively attentive. The staff member would persistently hover over us, detailing how they would personally ensure our sushi order was handled by the chef. This was excessively invasive and made me question the appropriateness of such behavior.

yelp:train:139846.orig: I really enjoyed staying here. The staff is awesome. They have a wave pool and their own brewery!  You can't go wrong with a place that's making the beer!  The rooms are comfy and the beds are super soft, which suits me just perfectly.  \n\nThe staff here really went out of their way for us and were so very helpful, I do have to remove 1 star though because of one particular blackjack dealer who seemed to be having a bad day and was a little rude - but, even with that I still recommend this hotel/casino to everyone!
yelp:train:139846.para: I genuinely relished my time here. The team is exceptional. They boast a wave pool and their own brewery, ensuring a top-notch experience. The accommodations are cozy, and the mattresses are incredibly plush, aligning perfectly with my preferences. \n\nThe team here demonstrated remarkable dedication and assistance, which I must note with a single-star deduction due to an unfortunate incident involving a blackjack dealer who appeared to be in a rough mood and was somewhat impolite. Despite this, I wholeheartedly endorse this hotel/casino to all.

yelp:train:140125.orig:
Boy where do I begin. I booked a strip view room at this hotel about two months in advance. I was a late check in and called the hotel earlier in the day around noon to inform them that I would be checking in around 11PM. As expected, I arrived on the property around 10:30pm and saw that there was a HUGE line for check in. had to wait in line for about 45 minutes until I finally saw a front desk agent.

The agent told me that the strip view room I had booked was no longer available, whatever that means. I told the agent that I had fully paid for a strip view room and anything else was unacceptable. In short, the agent told me there was NOTHING he could do except put me up in a non-strip view room, then give me a call the next day around 3PM so I could move to a strip view room.

My temporary room was small, bland, utterly boring with a view of the 15 freeway. I waited until 4PM the next day and was not given a call on my room line, nor my cell, as promised by the agent from the night before. I ended up having to call the front desk and after being transferred to 4 different people, I was finally given a room to transfer to with a strip view. I asked that the difference in price
yelp:train:140125.para: I started my journey with a reservation for a room with a cityscape view at this establishment, made roughly eight weeks prior. Upon arriving late, I contacted the hotel around midday to notify them of my expected check-in time at 11PM. To my dismay, I encountered a lengthy queue upon arrival at 10:30PM and had to wait approximately 45 minutes to reach the reception. The receptionist informed me that the specific room I had reserved was no longer available, leaving me perplexed.\n\nI expressed my dissatisfaction, emphasizing that I had paid in full for a cityscape view room and any alternative was unacceptable. The receptionist, however, could only offer a room without a cityscape view, promising to call me the following day at 3PM to facilitate the transfer. The temporary room I was provided was cramped, dull, and monotonous, offering a view of the 15 freeway. Despite waiting until 4PM the next day, I received no call as promised. I had to contact the front desk, going through 4 different representatives before being allocated a room with a cityscape view. I requested that the price difference be addressed.

yelp:train:140251.orig: I'm only giving this two stars because of the the gentleman that checked us in, he was extremely nice and helpful, I wish I could remember his name but I don't. \n\nRegardless, this hotel sucks ass. Everything about it sucks ass. It is old, the beds are stiff and suck, the rooms look filthy because they are so old. The ac claims its at a temperature (for example 60) and it's not even remotely close to 60. The bathroom is still from the 80s, the shower head seems like they bought it at the dollar tree. The casino sucks. The drinks are expensive. The only reason we stayed here is because we waited too long to book for SEMA, and we immediately regretted it. If you want an enjoyable hotel experience don't stay here.
yelp:train:140251.para: I'm rating this establishment two stars due to the courteous and supportive individual who assisted us upon arrival, though I regret not being able to recall his name. \n\nDespite this, the hotel is disappointingly lacking in quality. It appears aged, with uncomfortable beds and a grimy appearance due to its age. The temperature control is inaccurate, failing to reach the stated 60 degrees. The bathroom's design harks back to the 80s, with a showerhead that seems like a bargain purchase from a dollar store. The casino is subpar, and the beverages come at a high cost. Our decision to stay was influenced by a delayed SEMA booking, but we soon wished we hadn't. For a pleasurable hotel stay, this place is not recommended.

yelp:train:140282.orig: Incredibly artistic and visually stimulating from the lesbian water contortionists to the midget and tall blond aerial silk combo. There was definitely an act for every type of sexual deviant out there no matter your flavor. For me, I fell in love with Cirque du Soleil for the amazing feats and distinguishing acts that set these people apart from those of us who cannot walk on our pinkies while twisted into a pretzel and I didn't really find that much of an ooh aah factor in this show.
yelp:train:140282.para:
The spectacle was remarkably creative and visually captivating, featuring a diverse array of performers from lesbian water contortionists to mixed-height blond aerial silk duos. It catered to every kind of unconventional sexual preference, ensuring there was something for everyone. I was particularly enamored with Cirque du Soleil for its extraordinary performances and unique acts that distinguished these artists from the average crowd, unable to perform complex contortions. However, I didn't find myself overwhelmed with a sense of awe in this particular show.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original meaning, sentiment, emotion, and intent, but uses different wording and sentence structure. The length is also roughly the same.)

yelp:train:141107.para:
I'm composing this message from the 12th-floor Venetian tower. The space is stunning, spotless, and expansive. I truly desire to remain here and enjoy a blissful end to my holiday, but I've only been here a short while and am quite disappointed with the hotel's customer service. My initial indication of this should have been when I contacted them a few days prior to our journey to inquire about special arrangements for a health concern I have. The person who answered was not apologetically helpful. My spouse then reached out to the concierge, assuming that their customer service-focused nature would result in better assistance. However, she was unable to assist without imposing a $70 daily charge, which I would have been fine with, but she remained unapologetic and dismissive.

Today, after navigating what I consider a tacky queue to check in, we were informed of a $28 daily resort fee. RESORT FEE! This charge is for the use of the pool and fitness room. I don't require the fitness room and I've never had to pay to use a hotel's pool. This vacation was a gift from a friend, along with a stipend that I had intended to use for spa services. However, now I'm obliged to pay (with no option to opt out) this resort fee.

yelp:train:141156.orig: Booo on getting rid of the tiger habitat (the one across from the gift shop).  Now the only way to see the white tigers is to pay to get into the Secret Garden.  Don't get me wrong.  The Secret Garden is absolutely worth the price, but I miss seeing the white tiger on my way into the casino.  Instead, there is a BLT Burger in the space.
yelp:train:141156.para: Criticize the decision to eliminate the tiger enclosure adjacent to the gift store. Presently, the sole method to witness the white tigers is through a paid entry to the Secret Garden. I acknowledge that the Secret Garden is indeed valuable for its price, yet I lament the loss of viewing the white tiger on my path to the casino. In its place, a BLT Burger stand occupies the area.

yelp:train:141555.orig:

yelp:train:141756.orig: I had the bone-in rib-eye, which is the best steak I've had in my life. Deliciously juicy, tender, full of beef flavor, with just the right amount of bite, the thought of this steak is making me salivate while writing this review.\n\nMy friend had his with the foie gras. If you like foie gras at all, DO THIS. It might seem a bit odd to pair these two together, but when I tried it, it set off little fireworks off my taste buds.
yelp:train:141756.para: I savored the bone-in rib-eye, the most exceptional steak I've ever tasted. It was incredibly succulent, tender, and bursting with beefy taste, accompanied by a perfect level of chewiness. The mere idea of this steak is causing my mouth to water as I pen this review.\n\nMy companion opted for the foie gras. If you have a liking for foie gras, I highly recommend it. Although it might appear unusual to combine these two, the experience ignited a delightful sensation on my taste buds.

yelp:train:141775.orig:
So this review is going to be two sided since we had mixed experiences. Let me start out by saying this is my 3rd Emeril's restaurant in Vegas. The other two places Fish House and Table 10 are always on the half priced ticket booth so a discount is always possible but given this is a steakhouse in The Venetian no discount. We came here on Dec 30th before our Marroon 5 concert. Securing a reservation over the phone a few days ahead of time was easy. We had wine, appetizers,2 main entrees,2 side dishes and a dessert. 
The service and customer service here is exceptional. 

We tried the lobster bisque, pasta special appetizer, BBQ shrimp, Cajun Ribeye, Filet Mignon, Gratin potatoes, Mushrooms and the Choc cake. 
Most of the food was delicious but a few fell short like the Ribeye and choc cake. the ribeye was overcooked, not that tender and lacking seasoning. The choc cake was dry and previously frozen. The special pasta appetizer was good but not excellent or anything I would mention ordering again.

yelp:train:141775.para:
This review will present a balanced perspective as our experiences were varied. I'll begin by noting that this is my third visit to Emeril's in Las Vegas, with previous visits to Fish House and Table 10, which often offer half-price tickets. However, as a steakhouse located in The Venetian, no discounts are available here. We dined at this establishment on December 30th, prior to our Maroon 5 concert. Making a reservation by phone a few days in advance was straightforward. We enjoyed wine, appetizers, two main courses, two side dishes, and a dessert. 

The level of service and customer care at this place is outstanding. 

We sampled the lobster bisque, a special pasta appetizer, BBQ shrimp, Cajun Ribeye, Filet Mignon, Gratin potatoes, Mushrooms, and the Chocolate cake. While most of the dishes were enjoyable, a few were less impressive, such as the Ribeye, which was overdone, lacked tenderness, and was under-seasoned. The Chocolate cake was dry and had been previously frozen. The special pasta appetizer was satisfactory but not remarkable enough to warrant a repeat order. The Filet Mignon was exceptional, with the demi glaze sauce being a standout. The BBQ shrimp

yelp:train:142069.orig: I have always put the MGM in the top division of Vegas Hotels. I fear they are now playing to attract second division clientel. Low rates but the service and quality of the stay was poor. FAIL.
yelp:train:142069.para: I've consistently regarded the MGM as a premier choice among Vegas accommodations. However, I'm concerned they're now targeting a less discerning clientele with their low prices, at the expense of service and quality, which I deem a failure.

yelp:train:142149.orig:
When we first started planning a group vacation in Vegas for about 60 people flying in from all across the continent, I thought the whole thing would be a gong-show, and an expensive one at that. The bulk of the crew were staying at the Flamingo with a group rate but my roomie and I managed to stumble across amazing deals at the MGM that completely won us over. $69/night for a double occupancy room (for two of the four nights)? That's better than I can get in my hometown.

The rooms were impeccably clean, offered enough furniture for us to feel like home rather than just two beds and a television, and staff seemed to be at our beck and call. yelp:train:142149.para:

The majority of our group secured accommodations at the Flamingo through a group discount, but my roommate and I serendipitously discovered exceptional bargains at the MGM, which ultimately swayed us. yelp:train:142343.orig: Casino review.  Disgusting smell.  I had a horrible head cold, could barely smell or taste a thing and even I was nauseated by the smell.  What IS that smell?  We couldn't get out of there fast enough.  We considered dining at one of their many restaurants and based on the smell decided against that.
yelp:train:142343.para: Casino critique. An offensive odor. Despite suffering from a severe cold that impaired my sense of smell and taste, I was still repulsed by the scent. The nature of the smell was baffling. The urgency to leave was palpable. The decision to avoid their numerous dining establishments was influenced by the overpowering stench.

yelp:train:142479.orig: There are only two good things about staying at the MGM Grand hotel in Vegas. The location and the bed. First of all the super gay employee who checked us in had an attitude when he told us there was a $200 fee to check in and we only had cash. I had no idea of the fee to begin with. Then we were never able to log in with their WiFi connection. Super complicated and it never worked not even offline my phone couldnt connect. I dont know if they have a signal jammer or what. The walk to the room was half a mile. I guess we made the mistake of staying when that loser miley cyrus was booked so the hotel and the parking lot was jam packed with the fall of americas future clogging up the hallways, elevators and parking garage. Spent over $500 for a 3 night stay which was really worth maybe $200. Im Definitely choosing a better place next year.
yelp:train:142479.para:
The MGM Grand in Vegas offers just two positive aspects: its prime location and comfortable beds. Initially, the enthusiastic employee who welcomed us was unpleasantly brusque when he informed us of a $200 check-in charge, which we were unaware of. Additionally, their WiFi proved to be a headache, with constant connectivity issues even when offline. The journey to our room spanned half a mile, and our stay coincided with a packed hotel due to a popular booking, leading to congested hallways and parking areas. Despite spending over $500 for a three-night stay, I'd say the value was closer to $200. Next year, I'll opt for a superior accommodation.

yelp:train:142731.orig:
The Happiest Place On Earth!

Best punk bar in Vegas!

I loves me the Double Down. Reminds me of the old Comet Tavern in Seattle (maybe a mix between ages compared to this), or Zeitgeist in SF (smaller than that, no amazing burgers), only a lot, lot dirtier. As punk rock bars goes, this one has it all. A great jukebox with real punk on it, graffitied walls, dirty bathrooms, regular men and women (you know, with ink and piercings, etc), friendly atmosphere, gambling, cocktails, and sometimes a band or two. I meet the friendliest people here: tourists and locals. 

On this trip I was proud to purchase an ""I Love Double Down Pussy"" t-shirt, which I can now proudly wear in cities where people will have no idea what the fuck it means (I'll try to post a pic when I can). 

There's a great metal sculpture over the bar (centipede) and a metal cockroach sculpture on the wall near the men's room. Pool, video poker and slots at the bar, and a small stage for bands.

I never miss the DD when in Vegas and you shouldn't either.
yelp:train:142731.para:
The epitome of joyful destinations!

Top punk bar in Las Vegas!

I adore the Double Down. It brings back memories of the vintage Comet Tavern in Seattle (a blend of eras compared to this), or Zeitgeist in San Francisco (smaller, no exceptional burgers), but significantly more grimy. In terms of punk bars, this establishment checks all the boxes. It boasts an authentic punk-themed jukebox, walls adorned with graffiti, unkempt restrooms, and a mix of inked individuals and those with piercings, all contributing to a welcoming vibe. Here, I've encountered the most amiable people, both tourists and locals. 

During my visit, I was thrilled to buy an "I Love Double Down Pussy" t-shirt, which I can now confidently display in cities where its meaning might be misunderstood (I'll share a picture when I get one). 

There's an impressive metal centipede sculpture above the bar and a metal cockroach sculpture on the wall near the men's room. The bar offers pool, video poker, and slot machines, along with a modest stage for live bands. 

I always make it a point to visit the DD when I'm in Vegas, and you should too.

yelp:train:142985.orig: I would go with 3 stars but they have animal attractions that can be great for kids so i bumped it up. We went to see the dolphins but the line was huge and I had just seen the documentary \""The Cove\"" a couple weeks ago so i was feeling like a jerk for wanting to see dolphins. Anyway nice place and really cool pirate ships and gift shop. My little boy loves pirates so he was blown away and he loaded up on pirate booty at the gift shop. I hear the pirate show is cool at night but that it shows to much of the lady pirates booties in skimpy clothes so we couldn't go by with our 5 year old. but we drove by and the fire and volcano and show looked great from the car.
yelp:train:142985.para:
I'd typically rate it 3 stars, but the presence of kid-friendly animal exhibits prompted me to increase it. We visited the dolphin exhibit, but the queue was extensive, and I felt guilty for wanting to see them after watching "The Cove" recently. Nonetheless, it's a fantastic spot with impressive pirate ships and a delightful gift shop. My young son adores pirates, and he was thrilled, collecting pirate memorabilia at the shop. The pirate performance at night is enjoyable, though it's not suitable for our 5-year-old due to the revealing attire of the female characters. However, from our vehicle, the fireworks and volcano display were spectacular.

yelp:train:143138.para:

Upon arrival, we attempted to secure our non-smoking room (2 Queens), but were informed by the reception that it was double-booked and the only option was a smoking 1-bedroom room. Our experience deteriorated further. We began gambling at TI, and fortunately, luck was on our side as my companion experienced a winning streak. yelp:train:143256.orig:
Since my first trip in July 2008, I've been to Vegas 11 different times now.  TI will always be one of my favorites, mainly because this is the first hotel I stayed at while in Vegas.

CHECK-IN/FRONT DESK - 4 Stars
Overall the front desk staff is very friendly and the check-in process is quite quick.  They have one large queue line that zig zags throughout the check-in/lobby area, which I like better than the individual lines for each front desk clerk that some hotels have.  For some reason it makes things go quicker, and you won't see someone further back in the line next to you check-in before you.

HOTEL ROOM - 4 Stars
The rooms I've stayed in before seemed very clean, modern, warm and welcoming.  The standard rooms also come with a decent sized LCD (plasma?) TV, safe, ironing board, desk, and a nice sitting chair by the window.

CASINO - 3 Stars
I do like to gamble at TI now and then, but for some reason the theme/decor of the casino itself does not call out to me.  I preferably would like to play next door at The Mirage or down the street at Harrah's or Bally's.  The casino staff is nice and friendly though, and always willing to help you brush up on your skills at th
yelp:train:143256.para:
From my initial journey in July 2008, I've visited Las Vegas a total of 11 times. TI will forever be among my preferred choices, primarily because it was the first hotel I stayed at during my Vegas visits.

RECEPTION/FRONT DESK - 4 Stars
The reception team is exceptionally amiable and the check-in procedure is relatively swift. They utilize a single, winding queue line that traverses the check-in/lobby space, which I find more efficient than the separate lines for each receptionist at other hotels. This arrangement seems to expedite the process and ensures you won't encounter someone further down the line completing their check-in before you.

HOTEL ROOM - 4 Stars
The accommodations I've experienced previously were consistently clean, contemporary, cozy, and inviting. The standard rooms also feature a substantial LCD (or plasma) TV, safe, ironing board, desk, and a comfortable chair by the window.

CASINO - 3 Stars
While I occasionally enjoy gambling at TI, the casino's theme/decor doesn't particularly appeal to me. I would rather play at The Mirage, Harrah's, or Bally's nearby. However, the casino staff is amiable and always ready to assist in improving your gaming skills.

yelp:train:143294.orig: I would gladly tell visitors to stay ANYWHERE else in Vegas.  There is nothing good about this hotel except location and the rooms were nice.  The customer service is non-existent.   Rude workers at check in. Waiting for 15 minutes at most food places before even being acknowledged. (there was NO line) Then another 20 minutes before any service.  Pool is small and SUPER crowded.  By 2:00, you cant even move if your in the water.  Not fun, not relaxing.  There are many more reasons NOT stay at this hotel.  The prices arent even great.  Definitely consider staying at one of the MANY other hotels on the strip.  I even emailed a complaint to the the hotel direct and havent heard a thing back.  Again, horrible customer service.
yelp:train:143294.para: I'd enthusiastically recommend exploring other accommodations in Vegas. The hotel's appeal lies solely in its prime location and the rooms' pleasantness. However, the customer service is utterly lacking. The check-in staff was impolite, and one had to wait for a minimum of 15 minutes at eateries without any queue, followed by another 20 minutes for service. The pool is tiny and excessively packed, making movement by 2:00 nearly impossible if submerged. It's far from enjoyable or soothing. There are numerous additional reasons to avoid this hotel. The pricing is not commendable. I urge you to consider staying at one of the numerous alternative hotels along the strip. I sent a complaint via email to the hotel's management, but received no response, highlighting the poor customer service.

yelp:train:143411.orig:
This Hotel is ghetto! 

I'm here on a conference and we booked at the Imperial Palace because all the flamingos were booked or so. First thing first, when you check your bags, the bell hop practically begs you for a tip, he will not stop bothering you about how he ""checked 23 bags"" til you tip him and tip him right! 
The rooms yell cheap motel quality all over! Their TV looks like its straight up out of the 80s yes I am talking about the 1980s. Square and fat, with the words MAGNAVOX. The beds were like bam, uneven parts hard parts soft. and sheets that dont even get you warm. 

But that's all forgivable until the next day, when I went out, they changed the locks on the door, on all the doors in the hotel.without prior notice! I mean it would've been at least courtious of them to tell you they would be doing that  especially if you just checked in the day before! Instead of going all around just to get new keys, talk about lost time!
yelp:train:143411.para:
The hotel appears to be a run-down place! 

I'm attending a conference and we reserved a room at the Imperial Palace due to a lack of available flamingos. Upon arrival, the bellboy aggressively solicits a gratuity, relentlessly reminding you of the 23 bags he "checked," until you comply and give him a tip. 
The rooms exude a sense of low-budget motel standards, with a TV that seems to have been manufactured in the 1980s, complete with bulky, square design and the MAGNAVOX branding. The beds are uneven, with hard and soft sections, and the sheets fail to provide warmth. 

However, this is all overlooked until the following day, when the hotel staff unexpectedly changes the locks on all doors without any prior warning. It would have been considerate of them to inform you of this action, particularly if you had just checked in the previous day. Instead of simply providing new keys, this results in wasted time.

yelp:train:143790.orig:
Huge disappointment - after reading all the great reviews on Yelp, I decided to have my family's Christmas dinner at Mon Ami Gabi.  Perhaps it was Christmas and the chef wasn't around or there was no delivery of fresh steak on Christmas day or whatever, but the steaks were the worst we've ever had at a restaurant that claimed to be a steakhouse of any sort.        

We had the following: 

- French onion soup - standard, decent, not spectacular
- Frisee & bacon salad - tasty
- Steak au poivre
- Steak roquefort
- Filet mignon with merlot butter  and red wine reduction

I think the problem is with quality of the steaks, the sauces were fine, but my mom's steak roquefort had the texture of cotton, my sister's steak au poivre had the texture of cotton with lots of veins and fat lumps, my filet mignon had a stringy texture like a inferior cut of meat and was not at all firm.  It was so bad that we left much of the entree untouched and left right after the main course, we didn't even have dessert on Christmas!!  This was a very disappointing meal and ruined our Christmas.  

On the other hand, the service was fine and the  prices were definitely cheaper than traditional steak
yelp:train:143790.para:
Deeply dismayed - despite numerous positive Yelp ratings, I opted for Mon Ami Gabi for our family's Christmas feast. It's possible that Christmas coincided with the chef's absence or a lack of fresh steak delivery, but the steaks were the most subpar we've ever encountered at a purported steakhouse. 

Our order included:

- French onion soup - average, satisfactory, not exceptional
- Frisee & bacon salad - enjoyable
- Steak au poivre
- Steak roquefort
- Filet mignon with merlot butter and red wine reduction

I believe the issue lies in the steak quality, as the sauces were acceptable. However, my mother's steak roquefort resembled cotton, my sister's steak au poivre was cotton-like with visible veins and fat, and my filet mignon had a stringy, inferior texture and lacked firmness. The meal was so unsatisfactory that we left much of the main course uneaten and departed immediately after the main course, skipping dessert on Christmas. This experience significantly marred our Christmas celebration. 

Conversely, the service was acceptable and the prices were notably lower than those of traditional steakhouses.

yelp:train:144614.orig:
I had one of the best French dinners here!
It was outstanding and we were really quite surprised at how wonderful the food was.

Escargot was buttery but not too greasy and had a parsley mixture which added to its unique flavor.

The bone in ribeye is a must u have to order it medium rare and it will melt in your mouth with the perfect combination of herbs for the rich beefy flavor.

The goat cheese in tomato sauce appetizer was magnificently seasoned as it burst in your mouth and filled your tastebuds with a tantalizing taste of balanced goat cheese and fresh tomatoes.
I'm returning!
yelp:train:144614.para:
I experienced an exceptional French meal at this place!
The food was astonishingly delicious, leaving us genuinely impressed.

The escargot was creamy yet not overly oily, complemented by a parsley blend that enhanced its distinct taste.

Ordering the bone-in ribeye medium rare is essential, as it dissolves in your mouth, harmonizing with the ideal mix of herbs to deliver a sumptuous beefy flavor.

The goat cheese-infused tomato sauce starter was splendidly seasoned, exploding in your mouth and saturating your taste buds with a captivating mix of well-balanced goat cheese and ripe tomatoes.
I'm planning to return!

yelp:train:144651.orig: The food was very good. I had the skate wig and beet salad and i was very happy with both. The tables were a little to close for comfort.
yelp:train:144651.para: The meal was exceptionally delightful. I savored the skate wig and beet salad, and I was thoroughly pleased with both. However, the proximity of the tables slightly compromised my comfort.

yelp:train:144795.orig: Beautiful place. Steak is great! Outside sitting and amazing views of the Bellagio fountains. Service is top notch and the vibe is perfect for a romantic outing.
yelp:train:144795.para: A stunning location. The steak here is exceptional! Enjoy the outdoor ambiance and breathtaking sights of the Bellagio fountains. The service is impeccable and it's ideal for a romantic getaway.

yelp:train:144980.orig: Husband and I celebrated his birthday over a long weekend in Vegas.  The restaurant was small but elegant and intimate with just 15 tables or less.  We had initially decided on the 5 course tasting but after speaking with our server, we were immediately sold on ordering from the a la carte.  For the first course, husband had pan-seared foie gras which paired perfectly with caramelized apple.  My escargots were juicy, flavorful and the sauce was great for dipping.  We both ordered the lobster thermidor for entree - 2 lbs of lobster cooked in a brandy cream sauce with asparagus and mushrooms.  The service was impeccable, food was well-prepared and I highly recommend it.
yelp:train:144980.para: My spouse and I commemorated his birthday during a weekend getaway in Las Vegas. The eatery was modest yet sophisticated and cozy, accommodating no more than 15 diners. We initially opted for a 5-course tasting menu, but after a conversation with our waiter, we chose to order from the a la carte menu instead. For the starter, my spouse enjoyed pan-seared foie gras, which complemented the caramelized apple beautifully. I relished juicy, flavorful escargots with a delicious dipping sauce. We both indulged in the lobster thermidor for our main course, savoring 2 pounds of lobster cooked in a brandy cream sauce with asparagus and mushrooms. The service was flawless, the meals were expertly prepared, and I wholeheartedly endorse it.

yelp:train:145130.orig:
The word dump doesnt cover it.

The place smelled of carpet deodorizer and lysol.  No fridge, broken knob on the thermostat, all night leaking shower.  Really?  $120?

Lower budget shouldn't mean run down - it was like a vagrant hotel.

There is no reason to stay in this place.
yelp:train:145130.para:
The term 'dump' doesn't encapsulate the entirety.

The atmosphere was permeated with the scent of carpet freshener and lysol. A lack of refrigerator, a malfunctioning thermostat knob, and a persistently dripping shower throughout the night. Truly astonishing that it costs $120.

A reduced budget shouldn't equate to a dilapidated accommodation - it resembled a transient shelter for the homeless.

There's absolutely no justification for residing in this establishment.

yelp:train:145538.orig:
My sister swears that she saw a cockroach strolling across her bedspread when we stayed here last.  I never saw it, so I cannot confirm nor deny the sighting.  But regardless, that's still pretty sick.  It happens to the best of hotels, and I am sure it's an isolated incident.

Now that I think about it, we should have complained. Oh well.  I like the central location of this places and its OG status as one of the oldest casinos on the Strip.  Go Flamingo!

The Flamingo habitat and the crab leg buffet are highlights.  Haven't stayed here in a while, but wouldn't mind it if I got a good deal.
yelp:train:145538.para: My sibling insists she observed a roach meandering on her bedding during our previous visit. I didn't witness it, hence I can neither validate nor refute her claim. Nevertheless, it's still quite distressing. Such occurrences can happen even in top-notch accommodations, and I'm confident it's a one-off event.\n\nReflecting on it, we might have voiced our concerns. Alas, it's not a lost cause. I appreciate the prime positioning of this establishment and its recognition as one of the earliest casinos on the Strip. I'm inclined to return if the price is right. The Flamingo's environment and the crab leg buffet are standout features.

yelp:train:145656.orig: Nice hotel and cool pool party, beautiful garden with (real flamingos!). Starting to cater to a lot of young folks. We got a non renovated room, the furniture was old and the bathroom was not appealing at all. Really thin walls, because we know when our neighbors are in. The good part was that we had a nice view of the strip.
yelp:train:145656.para: Enchanting accommodation and enjoyable pool gathering, stunning garden featuring authentic flamingos. The establishment is increasingly attracting younger guests. We stayed in a room that hasn't been updated, with outdated furnishings and an unattractive bathroom. The thin walls were a concession to our awareness of our neighbors' presence. However, the positive aspect was the pleasing sight of the strip from our vantage point.

yelp:train:146142.orig:
We def had to wait in line a good while to check in.  The line wrapped around the lobby at least three times. 

I read reviews about TVs in the bathroom mirror...but we did not have that. The room was pretty basic and it was supposed to be a deluxe king (we had two queens instead). 

The pillows feel short and kept slipping off the bed. The closet and bathroom were small but adequate. My room was $56 on week nights and over $100 on weekends. The resort fee was $25 for one day...which was nearly half of the room cost. 

They were working on the casino so whole sections had machines pulled out And caution tape roping it off. We spent all of our time in nicer casinos like Paris, Caesars, and others.
yelp:train:146142.para:
We had to wait quite a bit in the queue to complete check-in, with the line extending around the lobby at least three times. 

Despite reading about bathroom mirror TVs in reviews, we didn't experience that. The room was fairly simple and was advertised as a deluxe king, but we ended up with two queens. 

The pillows felt short and kept sliding off the bed. The closet and bathroom were compact but sufficient. My room cost $56 on weekdays and over $100 on weekends. The resort fee was $25 for a day, almost half of the room's price. 

The casino was under renovation, with sections cordoned off by caution tape and machines removed. We spent our time in more upscale casinos like Paris, Caesars, and similar establishments.

yelp:train:146463.orig:
I filled out a survey for this hotel for my stay. (Yes I was still pissed).

The manager or whatever did offer us a 1 night comp stay..

But I dont think I will be coming back.

Sorry Luxor I'm staying with your sister hotel. The Mgm.
yelp:train:146463.para:
During my visit, I completed a feedback form for the accommodation. (Indeed, I was still annoyed).

The hotel's representative or equivalent provided us with a complimentary one-night stay.

However, I am not planning to return.

Apologies Luxor, I'll be choosing your sister establishment, the MGM.

yelp:train:146531.orig: The bathtub and separate showers are nice, granite and tile, but the shower head and the towels are low rent. Other than this the tower deluxe room wasnt anythig special nothong particularly bad, just decent. If i wasnt hwre for work I would absolutely stay at least at the mandalay bay or nicer more mid-strip.  I had multiple problems with my keycard not working in the door, and an issue with my reservation thatr I called ahead to avoid and once there nothing was done and I was misinformed/lied too.  I will go out of my way not to stay here and make sure nobody else has to deal with their incompetence.  Too many bettere options to stay at on the strip to stay at the \""Sux\""ur.
yelp:train:146531.para: The bathtub and individual showers, crafted from granite and tile, offer a decent experience, yet the showerhead and towels fall short of expectations. The tower deluxe room itself doesn't stand out as exceptional or notably poor, merely average. Despite this, I would hesitate to recommend this place, especially if I had the choice, preferring options like Mandalay Bay or other mid-strip accommodations. I encountered several issues, including a faulty keycard and a reservation problem that wasn't resolved despite prior notification. I'm determined to avoid this establishment and advise others to do the same due to the staff's apparent incompetence. There are numerous superior alternatives available on the strip, making this option less than ideal.

yelp:train:146988.orig:
We stayed here for five days while visiting family in town.

I have no complaints at all, it was a great stay!

I did book online at hotels.com, and that was cheaper than the front desk price, but I assume everyone can find a price they are comfortable with one way or another.

We got a room with two queen beds, on the 28th floor of the main pyramid. The room was super spacious, which is always nice. The bathroom had a nice big shower, but no tub. I'm not sure if other rooms have tubs or all of them only have showers.

The wi-fi is free with the resort fee, but only in public areas, not your room...I guess I do have one complaint, but it didn't cause any issues, just not convenient.

All the staff we interacted with was friendly and helpful.

I would definitely stay here again!
yelp:train:146988.para:
During a five-day visit to see family, we chose this place and had a fantastic experience.

I made my reservation through hotels.com, which offered a more economical option than the counter price, though I believe people can find a suitable cost for their stay. 

Our accommodation featured a double queen bedroom on the 28th level of the central pyramid, providing ample space, a desirable trait. The bathroom boasted a generous shower, though it lacked a bathtub. It's uncertain if other rooms have bathtubs or if all have only showers. 

The complimentary wi-fi, included with the resort fee, is accessible in public spaces only, not within the room. This minor inconvenience didn't cause any problems, but it wasn't as convenient as I would have liked. 

Every staff member we came into contact with was amiable and supportive. 

I would certainly consider returning to this establishment.

Lots and lots of slots to choose from. The bell hops were really nice though, the only good customer service you will receive. yelp:train:147100.para:
Advantages: The hotel's exterior is visually appealing and boasts a well-designed structure. Inside, it's equally attractive, featuring three Starbucks, a pleasant lobby, and a substantial casino with numerous slot machines. The bell staff's friendliness stands out as the sole positive aspect of customer service. These factors contribute to the hotel's modest 1-star rating.

Disadvantages: The rooms are outdated, with everything appearing old-fashioned. There's no refrigerator, and the bed comforter is merely a sheet and a brown blanket, lacking comfort. The deluxe tower room on the 14th floor, which is supposedly "updated," fails to meet cleanliness standards, with dirty bathroom floors and a subpar shower head that causes discomfort. The valet service is consistently overcrowded, and a persistent lady knocked persistently on my room door on the first day, disturbing my sleep during a long drive.

yelp:train:147943.orig:
Being a big carnivore myself, i enjoy a big piece of red meat from time-to-time.   I was told by friends this place might fit the bill.
 
We were promptly greeted upon our arrival and were seated along the back booths.  The decor and the lighting was 'fitting' for the place and as well as the menu.   After several minutes pondering the menu, we had the shrimp cocktail to start which was nothing special and I should have expected that this being a steak place.  

We shared the 32 oz Porterhouse for two with assortment of mushrooms, fingerling potatoes and roasted corn.  And yes the porterhouse was delicious - juicy, perfectly seasoned and the fillet was outrageous.  The side dishes were somewhat ordinary BUT the surprise of the dinner was the roasted corn.  We just had to ask the waiter for the recipe which he was more than happy to share.  Just delicious.
The service was impeccable as well as the ambiance.  Was it the best steak I have ever had?  Perhaps if it wasn't for the roasted corn, it might have been......


Cheers,
yelp:train:147943.para:
As a substantial meat-eater, I occasionally relish a generous portion of red meat. A recommendation from acquaintances led us to this establishment. Upon our arrival, we were quickly welcomed and assigned seats at the rear booths. The interior design and illumination were aptly suited to the venue and its menu offerings. After contemplating the menu for a while, we opted for the shrimp cocktail as our starter, which was rather unremarkable, especially considering the steak-centric theme of the restaurant. 

We then shared a 32 oz Porterhouse steak for two, accompanied by a variety of mushrooms, fingerling potatoes, and roasted corn. The steak was exceptional - succulent, expertly seasoned, and the fillet was extraordinary. The accompanying side dishes were fairly standard, but the highlight of the meal was the roasted corn. We inquired about the recipe from the waiter, who was delighted to provide it. It was simply scrumptious. The service and atmosphere were flawless. While it might not have been the ultimate steak I've tasted, it could have been, especially if not for the delightful roasted corn. 

Cheers,

yelp:train:147971.orig:
Is it still considered a martini if it's just straight up gin?  Would I be considered an alcoholic because these are the kinds of questions that I ponder?

I'm only asking, because I was batting around ideas on what to order at the bar here while waiting for our showing of Kà to kick off, and none of the specialty drinks really called to me.  Instead, I just asked for a simple martini.  Um.  Extra dry.  Like... the gin, shaken, with a twist kinda dry.

And it was delicious.

It better have been, considering the price.  Although, admittedly, there was enough booze in my giant martini glass to account for the cost.  Still, when we're talking a Colicchio restaurant in one of the higher end megahotels on The Strip... with a gorgeous interior, personable bartender, and a generous pour...

Ain't got no complaints here.
yelp:train:147971.para: Is a martini still valid if it's merely gin without any mixers? I find myself contemplating such queries, as I deliberated over my drink choice at the bar while anticipating our K\u00e0 movie night. The specialty cocktails didn't appeal to me, so I opted for a classic, extra dry martini - gin shaken, with a hint of dryness. It tasted fantastic.\n\nThe price was justified, given the substantial amount of alcohol in my large martini glass. However, considering the upscale Colicchio restaurant in a luxurious megahotel on The Strip, complete with an attractive interior and a friendly bartender, I have no grievances.

yelp:train:148287.orig:
I must first start off and say I've never had steak before. I was advised by my friend if you're gonna have steak, you might as well have the best. So we decided Tom Colicchio might know a thing or two about steak. Therefore if you are a steak connoisseur, look at someone else's review! 

Pros:
Very nice casual atmosphere

My water glass was always filled... always... like if I just think about my water I see a water person waiting in the corner ready to refill my glass

Very little noise,  not like creepy deserted quietness, more like a nice low murmur. 

Waiter and all the staff we met were very kind and courteous about everything

Cons:

I don't know if it'll be too memorable. The food was good, the service was good but when I come back to Vegas again I'm not going to be like ""I have GOT to go to Craftsteak, like OMG gurl.""

4 stars
yelp:train:148287.para:
I've never tasted steak before, but my companion suggested that if I'm going to try it, I should opt for the finest. Thus, we chose Tom Colicchio as our guide. If you're a steak aficionado, consider exploring other reviews. 

Advantages:
The ambiance is pleasantly casual

My glass of water was consistently replenished, even when I merely contemplated it, with a person ready to refill it in the corner.

The noise level was low, not eerily silent but rather a gentle hum.

The waiter and the entire staff we encountered were exceptionally polite and attentive.

Drawbacks:

It might not leave a lasting impression. The meal and service were commendable, but I doubt I'll be compelled to return to Vegas and rave about Craftsteak.

4 stars

yelp:train:148347.orig: The hostess are very obviously not hired for the size of their brains, but hey, its vegas. The food is subpar, even for the prices it;s a ripoff. I got a sangria and it was bad news. Didn't even drink it. I bet the margaritas are better. I will give it another shot I guess but honestly, I would rather go to firefly down the street.
yelp:train:148347.para: The lady staff are clearly not selected for their intellectual capacity, but in Vegas, you know. The cuisine is disappointingly low-quality, especially considering the cost, making it a waste of money. I tried a sangria and it was unpleasant, so I didn't consume it. I suspect the margaritas might be superior. Despite this, I might revisit, although I'd prefer Firefly, which is just around the corner.

yelp:train:148554.orig: Ate here Feb 13.  If you are at the Venetian for a trade show and you need convenience, this is an all around winner.\nThat night was very windy so unfortunately the terrace was closed, but it looked like the terrace would be a lovely place to eat.  Someone said it was noisy, it might depend where you sit.  I thought it was quiet.  The service was excellent.  Like another Yelper here on the same night, we  enjoyed the trout. The side of garlic spinach was delicious.  Prices are high but typical for the location, so we didn't think it was over-priced.
yelp:train:148554.para: Dined at this establishment on February 13th. For those attending a trade show at the Venetian and seeking convenience, this place stands out as a top choice. The evening was gusty, leading to the terrace's closure, yet it appeared to be a charming spot for dining. Noise levels were reported to vary by seating area, but I found it to be relatively serene. The service provided was outstanding. Similar to another Yelper's experience on the same evening, we relished the trout and found the garlic spinach side to be exceptionally tasty. While the prices are elevated, they are standard for the area, so it wasn't considered excessive.

yelp:train:148563.orig:

yelp:train:148563.para:
Nestled on the 10th or 11th floor of the Venetian, there's an amusing character donning ersatz military attire, standing guard near the restrooms. Despite the grandeur, Bouchon maintains a relaxed and enjoyable atmosphere. I arrived barefoot in sandals after wearing high heels the previous evening and felt completely at ease.

When dining here, be sure to order the foie gras. It's an exquisite delight. It's like savoring it and thinking, "This is incredibly tasty....it's a rich, salty, indulgent treat....it's high in calories and cholesterol....it's illegal in some regions.....mmmmm......" It comes in the same jar you can find at Bouchon Bakery in Yountville, but in Vegas, it's served with endless warm toast. It's absolutely delicious.

I opted for the pork shoulder, which was a massive portion and I couldn't finish more than half. It was incredibly tender and tasty. My partner chose the monkfish and he enjoyed it. I appreciate the fact that they use All-Clad at T. Keller restaurants. It's a thoughtful detail. We ended our meal with beignets for dessert, as after indulging in foie gras and pork shoulder, it's only fitting

yelp:train:149184.orig: Our friends have been raving about this place, every time they come to Vegas they have brunch here.  So they wanted us to experience this place and me, being a green horned foodie in training, was looking forward to the experience.  It was what I expected with impeccable service and a place to live in the moment and enjoy each bite.  We order the pastry basket, American breakfast, chicken and waffles and shared them all and the gravy for the chicken had bits of bacon and chives - among the four of us which was plenty for a light breakfast.  Tip for the brunch, come early as we came at 9 AM and there was no waiting.  But by the time we left, long waits.  So enjoy the experience, come early!  All were delightful and I normally don't eat a big breakfast so sampling these dishes was just perfect for my small appetite.  I can't wait to come here for dinner to try the mussels!
yelp:train:149184.para: Our pals have been singing praises about this spot, every time they visit Las Vegas, they make it a point to have brunch here. Consequently, they urged us to check it out, and as a budding culinary enthusiast, I was eager for the experience. It lived up to my expectations with flawless service and a space to savor each morsel. We indulged in the pastry selection, American breakfast, chicken and waffles, and shared them, with the chicken gravy featuring bits of bacon and chives - enough for our light breakfast. A tip for the brunch: arrive early as we got there at 9 AM and didn't have to wait. However, by the time we departed, we encountered lengthy waits. So, relish the experience and remember to come early! All the dishes were pleasing, and as someone who doesn't typically have a large breakfast, sampling these dishes was ideal for my modest appetite. I'm looking forward to coming here for dinner to try the mussels!

yelp:train:149189.orig:
The best brunch on the strip!!!

Since they don't take reservations for brunch but recommend coming in earlier to avoid longer wait, I along with my friends got there around 9:30 and were seated within a few mins.

From the first moment you step on you can feel the cheerful/bright ambiance. Service, decor, and creativity all are bound to win your heart.

The food is definitely authentic french and hence even the French toast aren't the traditional ones you get at the American brunch restaurants. Not to say it was anything short of delicious.

Overall I had a great time and can't wait to get back for round 2 the next time I'm in that city.
yelp:train:149189.para:
Exciting brunch experience on the strip!

To bypass the no reservation policy for brunch, I and my pals arrived at 9:30 and quickly found a table.

Right from the entrance, the lively and cheerful atmosphere immediately captivates you. The combination of service, decor, and creativity is sure to charm you.

The French-inspired cuisine, including the French toast, is distinctly different from typical American brunch offerings, yet it's incredibly tasty.

In summary, I thoroughly enjoyed myself and am eagerly anticipating my return for another visit the next time I visit the city.

yelp:train:149195.orig: Didn't live up to its Yelp rating. It's so hard to find. Casino direction was not clear. We went there for Brunch. We had the famous Croque Madame and French Toast. The Croque Madame was good, but not worth the price tag. French Toast was too moist and lack flavors. The wait was an hour, if it was not for the Roulette Table that kept me busy, I would not have waited.
yelp:train:149195.para: The establishment didn't meet its Yelp score. Locating it proved challenging. The casino's guidance was unclear. We visited for breakfast, opting for the renowned Croque Madame and French Toast. While the Croque Madame was satisfactory, its cost was excessive. The French Toast was overly soggy and tasted bland. The wait time was an hour, but the Roulette Table kept me occupied, preventing me from leaving.

yelp:train:149402.orig:
I always look forward to come to Olives when I come to Vegas. It is somewhere you definitely need to make reservations or else you prob gonna have to wait. I never tried it for dinner but lunch is good and inexpensive. 

Service is usually good. They usually have lunch specials and I usually get that but i guess it depends on what pasta lunch special they have. Their pastas are really good because it's hand toss/house made. I also really recommend sharing a beef capraccio with a friend which is SUPER GOOD. There are like stuffing inside the middle of the plate and kind of a salad. I don't really like the stuffing but besides that It is super good. 

I recommend anybody coming here for lunch(never tried dinner) when they're in vegas.
yelp:train:149402.para: Whenever I visit Vegas, I eagerly anticipate dining at Olives. It's essential to book in advance, as waiting is likely otherwise. I haven't had dinner there, but I find their lunch offerings both tasty and affordable. \n\nGenerally, the service is commendable. I often opt for their lunch specials, particularly the pasta ones, which are notably excellent due to their handmade, house-tossed quality. I also highly suggest sharing a beef capraccio with a companion, as it's incredibly delightful. Despite not being a fan of the stuffing, the overall experience is exceptional. I advise anyone visiting Vegas for lunch to consider Olives, even though I haven't tried their dinner menu.

yelp:train:149520.orig: Tourist trap! The decor and ambience of the club is pretty cool but other than that this place is nothing special.
yelp:train:149520.para: The club's aesthetic and atmosphere are quite impressive, yet beyond that, it fails to stand out as anything exceptional.

yelp:train:149780.orig: I recently found my new favorite Ted Baker dress here for an unbeatable price.  I can easily see myself making this a regular stop on my LV trips!  Aside from the parking fiasco (we ended up driving over a curb and parking in some dirt, which apparently is OK!), this place is great  :)\n\nPlenty of shops, great deals, nice outdoor feel.  Maybe it's just that folks are nicer in LV than they are in LA, but I was super impressed by how calm and chill the shoppers are here -- It was the day after Christmas and nobody was yelling or pushing or being a general nuisance!  Way to go, civilized peeps!
yelp:train:149780.para:
I stumbled upon my latest go-to Ted Baker outfit at this location for an exceptional deal. I'm confident it will become a frequent part of my LV excursions! Despite the initial parking mishap (we accidentally drove over a curb and parked on some dirt, but it seems acceptable!), the venue is fantastic :) 

There's a wide array of shops offering great bargains, and a pleasant outdoor ambiance. Perhaps it's the friendliness of the locals, especially in LV compared to LA, but I was genuinely taken aback by the serene and relaxed demeanor of the shoppers on a post-Christmas day – no shouting, pushing, or general annoyance! Kudos to the well-mannered folks!

yelp:train:149794.orig:

yelp:train:149881.orig: Get the 7.77 deal, you won't regret it. That is, if they haven't stopped serving it. I first saw it on Rachael Ray's 40 Dollars A Day and had to try it. Steak, shrimp, baked potato and salad? And it was all pretty good, and just the right amount of food. And I think you even get a vegetable with that...
yelp:train:149881.para: Secure the enticing offer of 7.77, and you'll be pleased with your choice. This is true, provided they continue to offer it. I initially encountered it on Rachael Ray's 40 Dollars A Day and felt compelled to give it a go. A combination of steak, shrimp, a baked potato, and salad? It tasted delightful and satisfied my hunger perfectly. Plus, I believe a vegetable accompanies the meal...

yelp:train:150349.orig: This bar STINKS!! - LITERALLY!\n\nThis is the stinkiest, slimiest, stickiest bar I've ever been to. If you are drunk enough to not use any of your sense, KAMs is your place.
yelp:train:150349.para: This establishment emits an overpowering, literal stench!\n\nIt's the most pungent, slimy, and adhesive bar I've ever visited. For those who are inebriated to the point of sensory deprivation, this is the ideal spot.

yelp:train:150625.orig:
Translates to ""night play"" or ""after party"" in Norwegian -- as you can imagine, this place is open late in the night all week.

I'd like to think of this Madison's hidden gem of a bar (no sign outside, no phone)! 

Good drinks; Great ambiance  - Intimate; Asian influenced- one of the owners spent a lot of time in China. 

Their wood-burning oven roasted pizzas are very good. Love their three-cup tofu - an amazing blend of flavors served with rice and pickled veggies. I usually have them go a little easy on the soy and it is perfect for me. Their hummus plate is also delicious and a good value for the money.

Seating -- if it is winter, find a seat further inside - the door opening can get pretty drafty.  If there is a DJ, the back of the place can get loud. The best, most intimate space is at the furthest back wall on the left -- there is a little alcove with about 4 tables! If it is summer, their front windows open out, so you can sit either up front or outside and it is quite nice.

Note: Small food menu and No credit cards accepted (ATM on site though)
yelp:train:150625.para:
Translates to "nighttime revelry" or "post-event gathering" in Norwegian -- it's clear this establishment remains open late throughout the week. 

I envision this Madison's as a well-kept secret among bars (no outward signage, no phone number). 

Excellent libations and a cozy atmosphere - intimate, with a touch of Asian influence (one proprietor spent considerable time in China). 

Their oven-baked pizzas are commendable. I'm fond of their three-cup tofu - a delightful mix of tastes served with rice and pickled vegetables. I prefer them to reduce the soy, and it suits me just right. Their hummus platter is also tasty and offers good value for the cost. 

Seating -- during winter, opt for a spot further inside to avoid the drafty door. If there's a DJ, the rear area can get noisy. The most secluded and intimate area is at the farthest back wall on the left - a small alcove with roughly 4 tables. In summer, the front windows are open, allowing you to sit either up front or outside, which is quite pleasant. 

Reminder: Limited food selection and no credit cards accepted (ATM available on site).

yelp:train:150672.orig: There's really no way to describe the place without experiencing it. It's definitely one of the coolest clubs I've ever been to. The drinks are definitely pricey, but the eye candy, mouth candy, or whatever floats your boat makes it worthwhile. They really should change the name of this place to PURE DEBAUCHERY. Thanks to Harrahs MBA poker tournament, we got to go in early, and they had an open bar for 2 hours.  Of course, when you ask for water, you will get a 9 dollar plutonium container, called Voss. So I had 9 bottles of water along with all my drinks.  Pretty much every time you walk to the bar, you will be out 20 bucks. That said, the views of the strip are amazing and it remains one of favorite places in Vegas..
yelp:train:150672.para: Experiencing this location firsthand is the only way to truly grasp its essence. It's undeniably one of the most exhilarating clubs I've visited. While the beverages come with a hefty price tag, the visual and gustatory delights justify the expense. It might be aptly renamed PURE DEBAUCHERY. Thanks to the Harrahs MBA poker tournament, we were granted early access, and they offered an open bar for two hours. Naturally, when requesting water, you'll receive a 9-dollar plutonium container, known as Voss. Consequently, I ended up with nine bottles of water along with my other drinks. Every time you make your way to the bar, you're likely to spend around 20 dollars. Despite this, the strip views are breathtaking and it continues to be a top choice in Vegas.
