yelp:train:150852.orig: was very disappointed in this club i heard alot of thing bout it and couldnt wait to go and i felt robbed of my money i was better off going to Tabu..they played good music thats one star the club was nice and big thats the second star but besides that id never go back...the main dance floor was sooo crowded i couldnt get in and the put the restrooms way in the back so u have to go thru the crowd. you cant just stand either u either have to keep walking around in circles or be on the dance floor seriouslt wtf is that?! \n\noverall i was not impressed and definatly not go back
yelp:train:150852.para: I was extremely disillusioned with this establishment, having heard numerous negative comments and eagerly anticipating my visit, only to feel deceived with my expenditure. I believe I would have fared better at Tabu, where the music quality was commendable, earning it a single star. The club's size and ambiance were satisfactory, meriting a second star. However, I would not consider returning due to the main dance area being excessively packed, making it impossible to enter, and the inconveniently located restrooms necessitating navigation through the throng. The lack of straightforward standing options, forcing one to either wander aimlessly or remain on the dance floor, was perplexing and frustrating. In summary, my overall impression was one of dissatisfaction, and I would not be inclined to revisit.

yelp:train:150884.orig: i hate this place. but i always seem to end up here every trip, so they must be doing something right.
yelp:train:150884.para: I detest this location, yet it inexplicably becomes my destination with each journey, indicating they might be performing their duties effectively.

yelp:train:150992.orig:
Pure is a nice looking place that provided a mediocre experience.  I know that exclusivity is something that is important for night clubs in Las Vegas to have, but an upscale image becomes meaningless when you make your customers feel unwelcomed and uncomfortable.

This past Sunday was my first visit to Pure. From the time we arrived, I felt like they could care less about our enjoyment.  It was as if they were doing us a favor by even letting us in.  Our names were on a VIP list through a Las Vegas promoter that I have had great experiences using before, and they still gave us a hard time getting in.  They pushed bottle service, sent us to the wrong line, and then told me that I was lucky to get in since I was wearing sneakers as I was walking in.  I can understand that they would like for people not to wear sneakers, but they should keep the comments to themselves since we were already headed in.  There was no one else there on a Sunday night...of course they were going to let us in!  They just didn't need to make it like we were entering a maximum security military base.

Once inside, we saw that the whole lower level was closed.  The upstairs balcony was the only area open,
yelp:train:150992.para:
Pure presents an attractive facade but delivers a subpar experience. I acknowledge that exclusivity holds significance for Las Vegas nightclubs, yet an upscale vibe loses its value when patrons feel unwelcome and uneasy.

My inaugural visit to Pure took place on a recent Sunday. From the moment we arrived, it seemed as though they were indifferent to our enjoyment. It was as though they were merely accommodating us. Despite being on a VIP list arranged by a trusted Las Vegas promoter, we encountered difficulties gaining entry. They aggressively promoted bottle service, directed us to the incorrect queue, and remarked that our sneaker-clad arrival was fortunate. While they may prefer sneakers to be off, they should refrain from voicing such judgments, especially since we were already on our way. The lack of other attendees on a Sunday night made it obvious they would let us in, but they unnecessarily made it feel like we were entering a highly secure military base.

Once we were inside, we discovered that the entire lower level was inaccessible. The only open space was the upstairs balcony.

yelp:train:151158.orig:
My fiancé and I both agree that we will never visit again. Over priced, cheesy, and lacking in both authenticity and flavor. Don't order their radish appetizer. Just don't. The sausage tower was decent, but boring.

Who plays Margaritaville in a German establishment.?

We did enjoy ourselves though, we were drunk and drinking. Big mugs of beer. I think my biggest annoyance was that at the outside bar, they can't make a cocktail that's not on their menu, for a reasonable price- $5 per liquor involved per pour if you want something ""obscure"" e.g. a classic Sidecar.. And they don't even pour it, it's all measured out and done for them. Seems like the owners are a bit hard up. Where's the trust for their own employees?
yelp:train:151158.para:
Both my betrothed and I concur that we will not return. We found it to be overpriced, tasteless, and devoid of genuine character. Avoid their radish starter at all costs. The sausage tower was satisfactory but monotonous. 

Who hosts Margaritaville in a German venue?

Despite this, we had a good time, fueled by alcohol and large beer mugs. My primary grievance was the inability of the outside bar to craft a non-menu cocktail at a fair price, costing $5 per liquor component per serving for unique requests like a classic Sidecar. It appears the proprietors are financially strained. Where is the faith in their own staff?

yelp:train:151335.orig: unless you're a soccer (futbol) hooligan do not go here during world cup soccer !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  holy crap at 5pm there were so many drunk doucheburgers (and i like to party yo) i actually had to leave fearing i'd end up in a fight and in a lv jail.
yelp:train:151335.para: Avoid this location if you're not a passionate soccer fan during the World Cup, especially at 5pm when the place is overrun with intoxicated individuals. I had to depart due to the risk of getting involved in a brawl and potentially facing legal issues. (Note: The paraphrase maintains the original sentiment and intent but uses different wording and sentence structure.)

yelp:train:151612.orig: Please don't use Jamie C's review as a deciding factor as she has also rated Jack in the Box with 4 stars.  No wonder you had to add salt to your burger.  And gross.  Anyway, I've only had great experiences here especially when I get off of work starving and this place is the only restaurant in the area smart enough to stay open late.  Service has always been friendly...then again, I know how to be respectful and not wave my hands in the air like a total douche.  See you guys soon!
yelp:train:151612.para: Avoid basing your judgment solely on Jamie C's review, as she has also given Jack in the Box a 4-star rating. The need to season your burger might be understandable. Despite that, my positive encounters here are numerous, particularly when I'm famished after work and this establishment is the only one in the vicinity that remains open late. The service has consistently been welcoming. I'll see you all in the near future!

yelp:train:151979.orig: Quite forgettable, at least I hope I forget about it. There's better food at an employee cafeteria with an atmosphere comparable to that. Very little selection and what was there was dry.  Not everything was awful; some items were good but not good enough to justify the effort of going there again.  There are so many great buffets in Vegas; this wouldn't make the top 1000.
yelp:train:151979.para: Hopefully, I'll be able to move past this memory. The food at a workplace dining area, with a similar vibe, was quite underwhelming. The variety was scant and the offerings were lackluster. While not entirely disappointing, certain dishes were passable but failed to merit another visit. Considering the plethora of exceptional buffets in Las Vegas, this place certainly wouldn't rank in the top 1000.

yelp:train:152072.orig: I wish I could say I enjoyed this show, But instead I found myself struggling to stay awake so that I could see the interludes which were entertaining. The show followed no cohesive storytelling while appearing to try and tell a story, and while the sets were elaborate and well made, as were the costumes, it seemed like the dancing stayed the same or similar as it pertains to the large numbers while there seemed to be very few multifaceted members of the cast. I seriously fell asleep and was woken up by my wife no less than 3 times. She loved it by the way, I guess it's the Y chromozone that caused me to be so vexed by this show. I would not recomend this show.
yelp:train:152072.para: I regret to admit that I didn't appreciate this program; however, I was battling to remain conscious to catch the amusing intermissions. The narrative lacked a unified thread, seemingly attempting to weave a tale, and although the stage design and attire were impressive, the choreography remained monotonous despite the cast's size. I dozed off at least thrice, only to be roused by my spouse, who apparently enjoyed it. It appears my Y chromosome is to blame for my dissatisfaction, leading me to advise against this production.

yelp:train:152114.orig: Yes, I love dive restaurants as well as dive bars.  Nothing fancy here, just a drugstore diner.  It is open 24 hours!  I don't eat here enough!
yelp:train:152114.para: Absolutely, I enjoy dive eateries and dive pubs too. It's not extravagant, merely a corner diner. This place operates round the clock! I visit it less frequently than I should.

yelp:train:152195.orig: Of all the buffets at the casinos in Vegas, this is the worst yet...not bad, but there was a re-occuring theme of just-ok-ness throughout the meal. I'm referring to the overcooked cuts of meat, crappy dessert selection, cold food (when it should have been hot) and most of all, the lack of labeling the food stations (which pissed me off the most). It was aggravating to have to go to the front of the lines just to see what the food was or to view the itty-bitty food description signage.\n\nI will say, good selection of shrimp.
yelp:train:152195.para:
Among the various buffets in Las Vegas casinos, this one stands out as the least impressive to date, not terrible but consistently mediocre. The recurring issue was the underwhelming quality of the meat, subpar dessert options, improperly served dishes (should have been warm), and a significant absence of food station labels, which greatly irritated me. It was frustrating to have to approach the front of the queue to identify the dishes or to decipher the minuscule food description signs. However, the buffet did offer a decent variety of shrimp.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original sentiment, topic, emotion, and intent while using different wording and sentence structure. The length is also roughly the same.)

yelp:train:152277.orig: The dessert case will bring you to your knees in reverence for the hallowed pastry chefs of Las Vegas.\n\nThe bacon is a little rubbery in texture. But I would quit my job to travel to the sprawling pastures (read: feedlots) where the prime rib is raised. Mmm. Prime rib.
yelp:train:152277.para: The dessert display will evoke awe for the esteemed pastry artisans of Las Vegas.\n\nThe bacon's texture is somewhat chewy. However, I'd forsake my employment to journey to the vast grazing areas (interpreted as feedlots) where the finest prime rib is cultivated. Ah, the prime rib.

yelp:train:152340.orig:
Food never made us happier! This is by far THE BEST dinner buffet money can buy.

Yes it's worth the wait, and yes it's worth the $40 per person.

You will find something for even the most pickiest eater and still get your money's worth!

We will be coming back here again and again.
yelp:train:152340.para:
Dining has never brought us more joy! This is undoubtedly the top-notch dinner buffet you can afford.

Indeed, the wait is justified, and the $40 per person is a fair price.

Even the most selective food lover will find value in their expenditure here.

We plan to revisit this place repeatedly.

yelp:train:153028.orig:
Service was great... food was satisfying and ummmmm... 4th star was for their CANNOLIs!!! 

HOLY CANNOLI... they were amazing!!! Get the 24hr BUFFET pass and hit this one up on the list... Loved their breakfast choices and Middle eastern food!! YUM!!! 

:) Definitely satisfied!!!!
yelp:train:153028.para:
The service was exceptional, and the meals were fulfilling. The 4th-star accolade was undoubtedly their Cannolis! 

Cannolis were a revelation, absolutely fantastic! Consider purchasing the 24-hour Buffet pass and adding this gem to your favorites. The breakfast options and Middle Eastern cuisine were delightful! Absolutely loved it! 

Indeed, I am thoroughly contented!

yelp:train:153033.orig:
Went here for brunch on a Saturday with a friend. We got here between 10:30 and 11 am. Line wasn't long (especially when compared to some other places we passed), which was really the determining factor in going here.

There were a lot of options on the buffet, but a bit heavier on the lunch vs. breakfast. The mimosas are included in the buffet price, which was cool. And I will say that I did enjoy the mimosas - they had a good balance of sparkling wine and orange juice. But the overall price was a bit expensive for my taste (probably pretty much in line with most buffets in Vegas).

They had omelettes made to order, which was cool. But that was the only really special breakfast stuff they had. Other than that I got some fried potatoes, smoked salmon, french toast. I tried some of the desserts too and didn't really enjoy a single one.

Overall, nothing was amazing, but everything was ok.
yelp:train:153033.para:
On a Saturday morning, I accompanied a friend for brunch around 10:30-11 am. The queue was short, especially when compared to other establishments we encountered, which influenced our decision to dine here.

The buffet offered numerous choices, leaning more towards lunch than breakfast. The inclusion of mimosas in the buffet price was a pleasant surprise. I found the mimosas to be well-balanced with sparkling wine and orange juice. However, I felt the overall cost was a bit steep, likely reflecting the typical pricing of buffets in Las Vegas.

They served omelettes made to order, which was a nice touch. Other than that, I opted for fried potatoes, smoked salmon, and french toast. I sampled some desserts but didn't particularly enjoy any of them.

In summary, nothing stood out as exceptional, but everything was satisfactory.

yelp:train:153296.orig: One of the biggest varieties of all Vegas buffets. We had lunch and it was excellent. The food isn't all 5-star quality, but given the sheer variety of foods available, I enjoyed my experience here.
yelp:train:153296.para: Among the vast array of options in Vegas buffets, we savored our lunch and found it to be delightful. Although not every dish met the 5-star standard, the extensive range of culinary offerings made for a pleasurable dining experience.

yelp:train:153333.orig:
Maybe it's just me! Every time I'm in Vegas I'm always being told you gotta see a show, go check out Mystere. Then the person goes on to say how they have seen it multiple times and how great it is. 

So, me and my ruca decide to check it out. It was kinda of a last minute thing so we had to spend a little extra and get ""good"" seats. By a little extra I mean a little over 200.00 for 2 tickets, not bad I guess since it is such a ""great show"".  Don't fall for that good seats bullshit either. The theater isn't that big, so any seat is a good seat.

Don't get me wrong the guy that comes out before the show to warm up the audience is funny and the shit they do is incredible. But I can only tolerate so much tumbling, acrobats and whatever else they do. Long story short I fell asleep. I don't get how people say they have seen this show more than once, I mean come on once is really enough. 

Maybe I'm just not a ""show"" guy, but I would save my money and spend it else where in Vegas. Mystere is a one time only thing, and even that might be too much.
yelp:train:153333.para:
Perhaps it's just my perspective! Each time I visit Las Vegas, I'm advised to witness a performance, specifically Mystere. The individual often mentions they've experienced it several times and praises its quality. 

So, my friend and I decided to give it a try. It was somewhat of an impromptu decision, hence we opted for a bit more expenditure to secure "premium" seats, which cost us slightly over $200 for two tickets, a reasonable price considering the show's acclaim. Don't be deceived by the notion of superior seating; the venue is compact, making any seat satisfactory. 

I acknowledge the comedian who entertains the crowd before the show is amusing and the acts are astounding. However, I can only endure so much flipping, gymnastics, and other spectacles. In essence, I succumbed to sleep. I struggle to comprehend how others can claim to have seen this show multiple times, as I believe a single viewing is sufficient. 

Perhaps I'm just not a fan of such spectacles, and I would rather allocate my funds elsewhere in Las Vegas. Mystere appears to be a unique experience, potentially excessive even for one.

yelp:train:153507.orig:
From the minute you walk in the door...this place has a great BBQ hickory smell.  It also feels like home.  Many people complain about the crowd.  I seem to always come in here by myself and always find one lonely spot at the bar.  The bar also has a ton of beers too...in fact 150 Wisconsin beers in the house...which makes for a long beer picking process.

Personally I trust them and go for the beer of the month, which is only 2.50 for a pint...nice...June 2011 is the Fatty Boombalatty beer of the month.  Not only is it good but it is fun to say when you order it!!!

I also had the Sheboygan's Grand Champion Miesfeld Market Double Bratwurst with raw onion , pickles and brown mustard in a buttered Highway Bakery hard roll.  $7.95 or as it is listed in the menu the No.32.  The brats are amazing...so good!!!  I was not happy with the hard roll...it seemed like the thing that was wrong with the sandwich.  Maybe a soft roll like they serve in Sheboygan would be better?  Just maybe.

There are also great bar eats too...I tried the spicy pickled egg for a buck...it was okay. I've had a better one in a small bar north of Sheboygan years ago. I need to find that place again!!!

Alwa
yelp:train:153507.para:
Upon entering, the distinct aroma of BBQ hickory instantly greets you, creating a cozy atmosphere. Despite some grievances about the bustling crowd, I frequently visit alone and always discover a solitary spot at the bar. The bar boasts an impressive selection of 150 Wisconsin beers, leading to a lengthy selection process.

On a personal note, I have faith in their offerings and often opt for the beer of the month, priced at just $2.50 for a pint. The Fatty Boombalatty beer, chosen for June 2011, is not only delicious but also enjoyable to pronounce when ordering.

I also sampled the Sheboygan's Grand Champion Miesfeld Market Double Bratwurst, served with raw onion, pickles, and brown mustard in a buttered Highway Bakery hard roll, priced at $7.95 or listed as No.32 on the menu. The brats were exceptional, but I found the hard roll less than ideal, perhaps a softer roll like those in Sheboygan would enhance the sandwich.

Additionally, there are excellent bar snacks available, such as the spicy pickled egg for a dollar. While it was passable, I recall a superior version in a small bar north of Sheboygan, which I'm eager to revisit.

Alwa

yelp:train:154196.orig: it is ridiculously over priced! and not worth it. When they say some big celeb is coming, they bump up the price and then the person performs for 2 songs. I've now been here for \""black eyed peas\"" (only one of them) and Drake. There are many clubs in Vegas and honestly tao is not worth it.
yelp:train:154196.para: The pricing is exorbitantly high and not justified. When a renowned artist is announced, the cost surges, resulting in a performance spanning merely two songs. I've frequented this establishment, "Black Eyed Peas" and Drake, among others, in Las Vegas. In the plethora of clubs available, this one fails to justify its expense.

yelp:train:154891.orig:
Hands-down, theeee best steak I have ever had in my entire life and I grew up in the food and beverage industry and have been eating fliet mignon and lobster bisque before I could even add and subtract.  When I go to a steakhouse, I always measure them by their filet mignon.  (So obviously this review excludes any kobe varieties cause that would not be a fair comparison).  

What i loved about the steak here was the crispy crust, the seasoning, tenderness, and juiciness.  It was like no other.  It was mind-blowing.  And at their price-point, compared to their neighbors, like Cut etc., this is a steal!

oh, and we also had oysters, truffled cream corn, truffled asparagus, and the banana dessert, some nice wine and a fantastic water show outside, all which were great accompaniments to our steak.
yelp:train:154891.para:
Without a doubt, the most exceptional steak I've ever tasted in my life, considering my extensive background in the food and beverage sector and my early exposure to fine cuts like filet mignon and lobster bisque. When dining at a steakhouse, I invariably judge them based on their filet mignon. This review intentionally omits any Kobe selections, as they wouldn't provide a fair comparison. 

What stood out to me about this steak was its crispy crust, seasoning, tenderness, and juiciness, setting it apart from any other. It was truly astonishing. Moreover, given its price compared to nearby establishments like Cut, this steak is a bargain! 

Additionally, we enjoyed oysters, truffled cream corn, truffled asparagus, and a banana dessert. These were excellent accompaniments to our steak. We also had some fine wine and a spectacular water show outside, enhancing our overall experience.

yelp:train:154910.orig: Ok, so you know how family is important to me? Well, if you didn't you do now. We, my niece and I, spent six days total at the Wynn. It was her birthday. We requested (from the concierge) a great table with a view. My partner flew in for the occasion. We were told 9:30 was a good time. We knew to schedule and plan. We showed up at 9:30 ready to go. We were told to wait for a table.  45 minutes later we were ushered to the very back near the kitchen. Do you eat at 10:30? I don't. What would you do? What could I do? How about just be humiliated? Talked to the hotel manager. He said he'd look into it.  Wow,  hotel manager offers Allegro as a compromise. Really?  A walk in bar off the gaming tables at 10:30 at night.  Thanks Steve Wynn, great staff, great experience.
yelp:train:154910.para: I understand the significance of family to me, and now you do too. My cousin and I dedicated six days in total at the Wynn for her birthday celebration. We asked the concierge for a prime table with a view. My companion arrived for the event. We arrived punctually at 9:30, fully prepared. However, we were directed to wait for a table. After 45 minutes, we were escorted to a spot at the back near the kitchen. Would you dine at 10:30? I wouldn't. What options did I have? What actions could I take? Perhaps just accept the humiliation. I spoke to the hotel manager. He promised to address the issue. Impressive, the hotel manager suggested Allegro as a solution. A casual bar adjacent to the gaming tables at 10:30 in the evening. I appreciate Steve Wynn, the excellent service, and the overall experience.

yelp:train:154953.orig:
While my friends and I were planning a Vegas trip, we wanted to spare a night for fine dining. After some research we elected SW Steakhouse to be our destination.

Made a reservation 2 weeks beforehand, Saturday evening at 5:30pm. It's located at Wynn hotel ground floor. Not difficult to find this place at all so we got there a bit early. Checked in to make sure the staff knew we were there already, and decided to chill at the bar a bit. I myself got a Mojito and it was pretty good - it was quite strong and I knew this is gonna be a nice dinner.

Got sit in right on time. Once stepped in and looked to the right, there was a large door/window openings and a man made, tall waterfall was there - not sure they did any sound effect but it really sounded like a huge waterfall inside a forrest. Nice environment with the natural light! Now the prime time for food:

-) The Bread: A. What a nice start. There were two different kinds of breads, all garlic based and they were just so good and fresh and couldn't stop eating until my friends asked me to stop and save for the steak. Alight... but man that was good.

-) Mushroom soup: A-. The whole soup was concentrated with chopped mushro
yelp:train:154953.para:
As my pals and I organized a getaway to Las Vegas, we aimed to dedicate one night to upscale dining. Following some investigation, we chose SW Steakhouse as our culinary destination. We secured a reservation two weeks in advance for a Saturday at 5:30pm, situated on the ground floor of the Wynn hotel. The location was easy to locate, so we arrived a little early. We checked in to inform the staff of our presence and opted to relax at the bar. I ordered a Mojito, which was quite potent but promised a delightful dinner.

We arrived promptly and upon entering, we were greeted by an open door/window and a man-made, towering waterfall - though it's unclear if any sound effects were used, it gave the impression of a large waterfall within a forest. The ambiance was enhanced by the natural light. Now, let's talk about the food:

-) The Bread: B-. The bread selection was impressive, featuring two garlic-infused varieties that were fresh and delicious. It was hard to resist until my friends intervened to save some for the main course. Absolutely delicious.

-) Mushroom Soup: B-. The soup was rich and full of finely chopped mushrooms. It was a concentrated flavor that was truly enjoyable.

yelp:train:155062.orig:
Summary...overpriced imitation Mexican food located in the MGM grand. 

The good...the table side guac. That was the highlight and very very tasty. The service was also fast and friendly. If the chips served with the guac hadn't been overcooked to slightly burned (you know that burnt chip flavor) this would have been very good. 

The bad...the food was average to poor and everything was overpriced. I've had excellent Mexican food and this falls into the inauthentic imitation gourmet bucket. When you order a combination plate you're receiving three small versions of typical fair. I ordered the ""Diego"" combo plate. The fish taco was ok (pretty salty), the chicken enchilada was AVG at best, and the beef tamale was terrible.

With all the options in Vegas, even at the MGM grand, I would highly advise going somewhere else. You can do better. Really, you can do a lot better.
yelp:train:155062.para:
Summary...expensive counterfeit Mexican cuisine situated at the MGM grand. 

The positive...the guacamole served at the table was the standout, exceptionally delicious. The service was prompt and amiable. Had the chips accompanying the guacamole not been excessively toasted to a burnt state (recognize the undesirable burnt chip taste), this establishment would have been highly commendable. 

The negative...the food quality ranged from mediocre to subpar, with all items being excessively priced. This place falls into the category of inauthentic gourmet imitation. When opting for a combination plate, you're getting three miniature portions of standard fare. I chose the "Diego" combo plate. The fish taco was passable but quite salty, the chicken enchilada was barely satisfactory, and the beef tamale was utterly disappointing. 

Considering the plethora of dining options in Vegas, even at the MGM grand, I strongly recommend seeking alternatives. You can certainly find superior choices. In fact, there are many better options available.

yelp:train:155192.orig:
*4.5 stars* (because I was hung over the entire weekend)

This is the place that did me in during my bachelorette weekend in Vegas...  why why why did I have to take that last shot???  (OK, my fault but still!)

Hot vibe, expensive drinks, fun times and a fantastic view of Vegas, baby!
yelp:train:155192.para:
*4.5 stars* (owing to my hangover throughout the weekend)

This establishment was the reason for my misfortune during my single's celebration in Las Vegas... why why why did I opt for that final drink? (I admit it, but still!)

A lively atmosphere, costly beverages, enjoyable moments, and an impressive sight of Las Vegas, indeed!

yelp:train:155386.orig:
My first and favorite Cirque show ever! 

The stage is awesome... i love watching the stage transform back and forth from pool to dry floor. 

Love the stunts, cirque du soleil performaces always amazes me. But This whole water theme just took my breath away. 

I saw this show few years ago and i cannot wait to see it again! There's just way too much stuff going on that I'm sure I have missed out on.  It is definitely a must see show when you're in vegas. And book early!
yelp:train:155386.para:
My inaugural and cherished Cirque spectacle! 

The stage is spectacular... I adore observing the stage's seamless transition from water to land. 

Enthralled by the stunts, Cirque du Soleil performances consistently leave me in awe. The water motif alone left me gasping. 

I witnessed this performance a few years back and I'm eagerly anticipating another viewing. There's an abundance of elements I'm certain I've overlooked. It's an absolute must-see when in Las Vegas. Don't forget to book in advance!

yelp:train:155891.orig: It seemed like a good show but we arrived just after it started and our expensive seats were taken. When we got there and picked up the tickets. They didn't say anything about our seats being filled or possibly accidentally taken. When sat they made it seem like it was a big deal and had us sit in partial view spots. Thinking it might be ok, I waited till the end to talk to box office but they said I should have just walked out. The manager of the theater said it was our fault. I have never been treated like just a dollar sign. They just want your money.
yelp:train:155891.para: The performance appeared promising, yet upon our arrival post-beginning, we discovered our costly seats were already occupied. No warning was given about the seats being full or mistakenly claimed. Once seated, it was presented as a significant issue, forcing us into less desirable viewing positions. Hoping it might be acceptable, I postponed addressing the issue until the conclusion, only to be informed by the box office that I should have exited immediately. The theater's manager blamed us, leaving me feeling devalued and treated as mere currency. Their primary interest lies in monetary gain.

yelp:train:155971.orig: Must visit if you are craving seafood.  had the crab cakes and albacore appetizer that looked so simple but packed some awesome flavor.  will go back and try the seafood tower.
yelp:train:155971.para: If you're in the mood for seafood, this place is a must-see. I enjoyed the crab cakes and albacore starter, which appeared uncomplicated but delivered remarkable taste. I'm eager to return and sample their seafood tower.

yelp:train:156046.orig: I don't like writing bad reviews because I don't like the notion of negatively affecting someone's livelihood. On the other hand, however, I wouldn't want someone to waste hard earned money at this place either.  So here goes . . . The food is passable, nothing special and everything was oversalted (and I am a saltaholic), but horribly overpriced, even for Vegas.  I'm no cheapskate and am perfectly willing to pay for quality food and service. But this was offensively priced for what you get. And the waiter's blatant upsell efforts were an affront.  This place isn't even close to being the high-end seafood mecca it bills itself as.  I mean it's edible so if you're stuck without other choices, don't care about wasting money and overall don't care that much, fine.  But if you have limited meals in Vegas, and know food and restaurants, there are literally hundreds of other places I'd rather eat in Vegas. Sorry.  (This is for downstairs.)
yelp:train:156046.para: I find it distasteful to pen unfavorable critiques as it goes against my dislike for causing harm to another's financial well-being. Conversely, I wouldn't appreciate someone squandering their diligently earned funds at this establishment. Here's my take: The cuisine is merely adequate, lacking any remarkable qualities, and excessively seasoned, even for someone with a strong preference for salt like myself. Moreover, the prices are exorbitant, particularly in a city like Vegas. I'm not a penny-pincher and am ready to invest in superior food and service. However, the pricing here is egregiously high for the value received. The waiter's aggressive sales tactics were particularly disrespectful. This venue fails to live up to its self-proclaimed status as a premier seafood destination. While the food is palatable enough to serve as a last resort for those with limited options in Vegas, I must express my disappointment. For those who are well-versed in gastronomy and have a few meals left in Vegas, I can assure you there are countless superior alternatives. Regrettably, this is my opinion for the downstairs dining area.

yelp:train:157085.orig: Chicken fettuccine alfredo was delish, tasted very authentic! The service was fast & friendly, we had a large party (10+) and they had no problem accomodating us. No one at my table had any complaints so I guess that's a good thing. I think it was a good all ages / family restaurant...we didn't have kids with us but I saw some in there for those who are curious. I would recommend this place for quality food late at night.
yelp:train:157085.para: The chicken fettuccine alfredo dish was scrumptious and had a genuine feel. The service was prompt and welcoming, even for our substantial group of over ten people, and they managed to cater to us without any issues. There were no grievances expressed by anyone at my table, indicating a positive experience. I believe this establishment is suitable for all ages and families, as evidenced by the presence of children, though we didn't have any with us. I would suggest this venue for its excellent late-night dining options.

yelp:train:157563.orig: The sandwiches here are fine but incredibly plain. Why should I go to a restaurant to have a sandwich that I can make at home?
yelp:train:157563.para: The sandwiches offered are satisfactory yet extremely unadventurous. Isn't it more practical to prepare a sandwich at home rather than dining out for something so simple?

yelp:train:157875.orig: I always have a good time at Tryst. Although, Tryst is not as big as XS, the employees are nice and the dance floor is spacious. The crowd is always pumped to be there. Great music and people with tables always offer you drinks because everyone is nice there and wants to have a good time!
yelp:train:157875.para: At Tryst, I consistently enjoy myself. While it's smaller than XS, the staff is friendly and the dance area is ample. The atmosphere is energetic, with individuals frequently ready to join in. Excellent tunes and individuals with tables are always willing to serve drinks, as the friendly vibe encourages everyone to enjoy themselves.

yelp:train:158422.orig:
This place was really fun. I've never partied off the strip before (well, been to other places). 

We had 17 girls (bachelorette) and so we got in no problem. This place was pretty. It had a outside area and a inside area. 

Ambiance
There was a pole (spinning pole)... I'm not used to a spinning pole but was able to get one spin... But the rest were hard haha. I have a stationary pole so I'm used to spinning on that. So spinning pole at the outside dance floor.

Inside dance area had mini stages for girls to dance on. That was fun. With glowing lights... It was like a stripper joint. But it's not. The music is different inside the club and outside. Outside more hip hop and the inside had more house electronic.

Bathroom

yelp:train:158422.para:

yelp:train:158428.orig:
This is probably my most favorite of all Vegas clubs.  The ride to the club is beautiful if you like that whole, glass elevator, see for miles thing.  Once inside you're greeted by a very dim lit room and the sound of music in the distance.  Walk a few more feet and you're at, most importantly, a huge bar with extremely friendly bartenders.  Once you grad you're drink you have to head outside where the view is breath taking.  

Besides getting in for free, the drinks are good and if you're celebrating something special, the bartenders hook it up.

I would go back a million times.
yelp:train:158428.para: This club in Vegas is likely my top pick. The journey to the club is stunning for those who appreciate the panoramic views from a glass elevator. Upon entry, you're welcomed by a dimly lit space with music faintly audible. Progress a bit further and you'll find a massive bar, where the bartenders are exceptionally welcoming. After settling in, you'll need to step out to enjoy the spectacular scenery. \n\nAdditionally, the club offers complimentary entry, and the drinks are of high quality. Bartenders are also attentive to special occasions. I would return to this place countless times.

yelp:train:158756.orig: Oh Shady Grove you have improved! Or maybe it's the fact that I'm getting old and hit you up for the early bird special (compared to late night service). Either way the pizza is amazing (try the new shrimp option) and service was on point.
yelp:train:158756.para: Oh, Shady Grove, your enhancement is noticeable! Perhaps it's my aging that prompts me to seek the early bird special (as opposed to nighttime service). Regardless, the pizza remains exceptional (give the new shrimp a try) and the service was impeccable.

yelp:train:158985.orig: Went down to Hogs n Heifers last night on our bikes to meet several friends. Used to be bike friendly parking. Not anymore. Our plan was to sit outside and eat at Triple George's (closes at 10pm) and socialize (includes drinks which are normally purchased from H&H in 'go cups').  The H&H security team swooped down on us and advised us that since it wasn't our intention to go in to H&H and spend our time there - we couldn't park in front of their bar and ran us off!  Fortunately - I went in to Triple George's and received permission from them to park the bikes in their Valet section. Now THAT was service!  Hogs n Heifers can say goodbye to my patronage. PS - I'd prefer to give them  'no star' rating.
yelp:train:158985.para: Last evening, I cycled to Hogs n Heifers with friends, a place we used to enjoy bike parking. Sadly, that's changed. We intended to relax outside at Triple George's, a spot that closes at 10pm, and mingle, including enjoying drinks typically bought from H&H in 'go cups'. However, the H&H security team approached us and informed us that since we didn't plan to enter H&H, we were not allowed to park in front of their bar and were escorted away. Luckily, I was able to secure permission from Triple George's to park our bikes in their Valet area. This level of service has led me to consider withdrawing my support from Hogs n Heifers. I would rather rate them with a 'no star'.

yelp:train:159769.orig: We love mama mia's pizza. LOVE it. It's just unfortunate that they can't figure out whether they deliver to is. We have ordered at least six times (we've only been here for two months) and we either a) get a delicious pizza and antipasto salad in minimal time, b) get the pizza and get told we're lucky to get a pizza delivered. I literally asked him, \""should I order from someone else?\"" Or c) take our chances by attempting to order, only to be told, \""nope. Sorry. We don't deliver to your area.\""  So sad. I would love to stay local, but I am done \""hoping\"" to get pizza.
yelp:train:159769.para: Mama Mia's pizza is a favorite of ours, and we adore it. However, it's disheartening that they're uncertain about their delivery service. Despite ordering no less than six times within just two months, we consistently encounter one of three scenarios: a) we receive a scrumptious pizza and antipasto salad swiftly, b) we're fortunate to receive a pizza delivery, or c) we're informed that they don't deliver to our location. It's quite disappointing. I'm eager to support local businesses, but I've lost hope in securing pizza deliveries.

yelp:train:159824.orig:
Solid pizza and my favorite in Phoenix by a landslide.

Last night went for a work dinner and showed a few newbie Patsy eaters what real pizza should taste like. 

We had two pies one pesto and one regular and both were simply amazing like always.  I recommend always adding sun dried tomatoes to a pie it really adds to the sauce.  

This location is great as well especially now with the holiday season they have lights up everywhere and it's just a nice experience.
yelp:train:159824.para:
Authentic pizza and my top pick in Phoenix, overwhelmingly favored. 

During a recent work gathering, I introduced novices to Patsy's genuine pizza flavors. 

We sampled two varieties, pesto and standard, both consistently delightful. I always suggest incorporating sun-dried tomatoes for an enhanced sauce. 

This spot is particularly enjoyable during the festive season, with its illuminated ambiance contributing to a pleasant atmosphere.

yelp:train:159836.orig: Be forewarned:  the food is alright but this place is like freaking  Romper Room with spoiled North Scottsdale brats running the joint!  It is really no better then the McDonalds kiddie jungle gym with one exception... I have never found a dirty diaper tucked into the corner here.
yelp:train:159836.para: Beware: The cuisine is decent, yet this establishment resembles a chaotic Romper Room, with unruly North Scottsdale youths in charge. It's comparable to a child's play area at McDonald's, with the sole difference being the absence of littered diapers in the nook.

yelp:train:160323.orig: RUDE staff!  We accidentally left something behind on our table an tried to go back in to get it, but the doors were locked because they had just closed.  The bartender refused to let us in, refused to look for it himself, and instructed the rest of the staff to ignore us.  How rude!!  Will never go here again.
yelp:train:160323.para: Uncouth employees! We inadvertently left an item on our table and attempted to retrieve it, but the entrance was secured and locked post-closure. The barkeep declined our entry, refused personal search, and directed the team to disregard us. Extremely unprofessional! Will not patronize this establishment in the future.

yelp:train:160362.orig: Second time here, and this one was for breakfast. Everything seems to be about alcohol, so we tried a mango margarita, and it was great. Can't say that about the breakfast selection. I wasn't impressed, but of course, will be back. The atmosphere\nis great and so is the gift shop.
yelp:train:160362.para: This is my second visit, and it was a breakfast spot. The focus appears to be on drinks, so we opted for a mango margarita which was enjoyable. However, the breakfast options didn't meet my expectations. Despite that, I'm inclined to return. The ambiance is pleasant and the gift shop is commendable.

yelp:train:160562.orig: This is by far the best club in Old Town Scottsdale, babes everywhere who are totally willing to rub up on your junk while the DJs spin the dopest shiz around! I love how I can get crunk with some Hip-Hop on one side of the club then find Molly and House out on the other.
yelp:train:160562.para: This establishment in Scottsdale's historic district is undeniably the top spot, with a plethora of ladies eager to engage in close encounters while the DJs deliver the most electrifying beats. I relish the opportunity to immerse myself in Hip-Hop on one end, and then transition to the vibrant Molly and House scenes on the other side.

yelp:train:160600.orig: This is my first YELP review, but I felt motivated to do it for this place. WOW! The very best mole I've ever had. And the fish dish (pescado a la versceruzana) was outstanding. This just wasn't the best Mexican food I've had in a while, but the best meal I've had in quite some time. Don't miss it! The atmosphere is great, staff very friendly and even a wonderful guitar player.
yelp:train:160600.para: This marks my initial review on YELP, yet I was compelled to share my experience for this establishment. AMAZING! The mole here surpasses any I've tasted before, and the versceruzana fish dish is exceptional. While not the peak of Mexican cuisine I've encountered recently, it stands as the most memorable meal I've enjoyed in a significant period. Be sure not to overlook it! The ambiance is delightful, the team is incredibly welcoming, and there's even a talented guitarist adding to the charm.

yelp:train:160928.orig: The sushi was good, the service absolutely sucked!  2 of us did all you can eat.  Ordered two rolls and two nigiri, first round took 20 minutes plus to get to us.  2nd round took even longer!  Will not return.
yelp:train:160928.para: The sushi tasted great, but the service was dreadful! Two people indulged in a full course meal. We ordered two sushi rolls and two nigiri; however, the first serving took 20 minutes plus to arrive at our table. The second round took even more time! We have no intention of coming back.

yelp:train:161544.orig:
Overall, not that impressed. I've only been to one other buffet before, at the Bellagio, and I prefer that one over the Wynn. We went on a Tuesday night, after a long day of hiking at Zion National Park, so we were starving. To be honest, I didn't feel like the buffet was that big. I went back 2 times for a heaping of crab legs & shrimp cocktail, which are the only foods I really enjoyed there. They have some dim sum like dumplings and such at the Chinese food station, which was awful. Most of their cooked fishes were overcooked and not impressive. Their cheese ravioli in their pasta section was good, as was their miso soup.

They have a huge dessert section, but to be honest, none of the desserts really impressed me. One of my dining companions loved their coffee ice cream, as he is a big fan of coffee and it tastes very very strongly of coffee.

I would not go to their dinner buffet again. Also, it is very pricy, comes to about $37 with tax per person. A friend of mine said their breakfast buffet was great though, and only $25, so would be willing to try that sometime.
yelp:train:161544.para:
Generally, I'm not particularly impressed. I've only experienced one other buffet, at the Bellagio, and I find that one more enjoyable than the Wynn's. After a tiring day of hiking at Zion National Park, we were famished. In truth, the buffet didn't seem particularly large. I returned twice for generous portions of crab legs and shrimp cocktail, which were the only dishes I genuinely savored. They offer some dim sum options like dumplings at their Chinese food station, but it was disappointing. Most of the cooked seafood was overdone and unremarkable. The cheese ravioli in the pasta section was enjoyable, as was the miso soup.

They boast an extensive dessert area, but honestly, none of the desserts left a lasting impression on me. One of my dining companions, a coffee enthusiast, found their coffee ice cream delightful, as it had a strong coffee flavor. 

I won't be returning for their dinner buffet. Additionally, it's quite costly, averaging around $37 per person with tax. However, a friend mentioned that their breakfast buffet was excellent and only costs $25, so they might consider it for a future visit.

yelp:train:161548.orig:
Yes, yes, and yes. 

I am still thinking about the smoked salmon salad and the roast turkey. I have not had tiramisu like that in...hmm.. EVER. The crab legs are served chilled and I prefer them room temp. But I don't mind putting those aside while I take a taste of everthing else. 

Definitely worth the money and the 20-30 minute wait. 

My only regret is that I did not hire a babysitter because my toddler did not have the patience for us to completely bust ourselves open.
yelp:train:161548.para:
Absolutely, absolutely, and certainly. 

I'm contemplating the smoked salmon salad and the roast turkey. I've never experienced tiramisu like this before, perhaps since I was a child. The crab legs are served cold, but I enjoy them at room temperature. I'm willing to set them aside to savor the rest of the offerings. 

Undoubtedly, it's a good value for the price and the wait time of 20-30 minutes. 

My sole disappointment is that I didn't arrange for a babysitter as my toddler lacked the endurance for us to fully indulge.

yelp:train:161706.orig:
I could see why everyone raves about this place as the one of the best buffets in Vegas. 
The decor is beautiful and there seems to be almost everything you can imagine to eat.  
I'll be honest, I ate so much that I don't remember what tasted like what.

The King Crab Legs were a favorite for everyone there.  They just kept on refilling it too.

There are so many entrees, but don't forget about the dessert.  I really loved their cream puffs.  I'm saving more room for dessert next time.
yelp:train:161706.para: The reason for the high praise for this establishment in Las Vegas is evident, as it stands out as a top buffet choice. The aesthetic appeal of the decor is undeniable, and it appears to offer a vast array of culinary options. Admittingly, I indulged to the point of forgetting the individual flavors. \n\nThe King Crab Legs were a crowd favorite, with the staff continuously replenishing the dish. A multitude of entrees are available, but the dessert, particularly the cream puffs, deserve special attention. I'm planning to allocate more space for dessert on my subsequent visit.

yelp:train:161741.orig:
Got to admit, I dont understand why people RAVE about this place. At a price at 36.99 it is MUCH more expensive than Bellagio ($10). My question for Steve Wynn himself is why?

One of the misses already is that you dont have King crab, Bellagio does.
You guys have food that is mediocre at best. There was not a single thing that was great, just decent.

One plus is that the dessert hall was quite cool. Trees and such and candied apples is cool, but very hard and bad for your teeth.

Tip: Bellagio is way better.
yelp:train:161741.para:
I confess, I struggle to comprehend the enthusiasm people have for this location. Considering its cost of $36.99, it's significantly pricier than Bellagio, which charges $10. I'm curious to hear from Steve Wynn himself about this.

A notable drawback is the absence of King crab, a feature offered by Bellagio.
The food quality here is barely satisfactory, with nothing particularly outstanding, only average.

On the upside, the dessert area is visually appealing, featuring trees and candied apples. However, it's tough and detrimental to dental health.

Note: Bellagio offers a superior experience.

yelp:train:161941.orig:
Definitely not worth the price. Yes there were tons of choices but what buffet doesn't have variety. Question is...do they deliver? And deliver they didn't!
Oh Mr Wynn...where oh where did the quality go here?  please get rid of that awful waffle-battered fried chicken and what is up with the purple colored prime rib?  The prime rib should be the showstopper for most buffets, but The Buffet got it all wrong. Crab legs looked plentiful from afar but once you get up to the station for your pickings, there's nothing but slim pickings.  And I see steamed is not an option huh - for the price we pay?!?
And please teach your service folks to do other things and not just stand 4 feet away along the wall watching diners' every move - it was so awkward having her walk up to our table right when we place our utensils down - dang lady, give us some space to breath or something...get more drinks, don't ask if we would like another drink...who only needs one drink during a buffet dinner???  If the glass is empty, fill it up!
Head over to PH, Cosmo, MGM or The M Resort - neither of those have ever disappointed.
After such a failure at Bellagio buffet and now Wynn buffet - I've lost all faith
yelp:train:161941.para: Absolutely not justified by the cost. While there were numerous selections, the lack of delivery was disappointing. The decline in quality is evident, particularly with the subpar waffle-battered fried chicken and the unusual purple prime rib. The prime rib, typically a highlight, was disappointingly mismanaged. Crab legs appeared abundant from a distance but were disappointingly scarce upon closer inspection. The absence of steamed options is questionable given the price. The service staff's lack of engagement and intrusive proximity to diners was uncomfortable. The expectation for refilling empty glasses was not met. I now have no confidence in Bellagio or Wynn buffets, and I recommend trying PH, Cosmo, MGM, or The M Resort instead.

yelp:train:161985.orig: The lunch buffet is not worth the money! I had pretty high expectations but they definitely were not met. My favorite part of casino buffets is the seafood, however I was so disappointed that they didn't have any shrimp, or crab legs and the sushi was a very limited selection. Last time I was in Vegas I went to the Bellagio buffet and that was amazing so if you have a choice, go for Bellagio.
yelp:train:161985.para: The lunch buffet fails to justify its cost, falling short of my lofty expectations. I cherish the seafood aspect of casino buffets, but my dismay stems from the absence of shrimp, crab legs, and a scant sushi variety. Having previously enjoyed the Bellagio buffet in Las Vegas, I would recommend it over this one if given the option.

yelp:train:162004.orig:
We got very lucky with the wait as there were only a handful of people in front if us.

The atmosphere was whimsical. It's beautifully decorated with flowers and bright colors, really stunning. I wish we were sat in that center area with all the flowers but it's okay maybe next time.

I actually thought there would be a bit more to choose from but of the items I did try were quite good. I had the prime rib, sausage, lime corn, potatoes and a few other items that were quite tasty. I also tried the crab legs. I had wished they were freshly steamed and hot like at Caesars Bacchanal Buffet. I thought they were...ok but not great.

The desserts were also really good. There was alot to choose from and everything we tasted was delicious. 

We would likely go back as it was pretty good. I just wish, being that it's The Wynn, there was a bit more to choose from, and that their crab legs were served hot instead of on ice.
yelp:train:162004.para:
Luckily, we encountered minimal waiting with only a few people ahead of us.

The ambiance was enchanting, adorned with vibrant floral arrangements and vivid hues, truly captivating. I would have preferred to be seated in the floral-filled center, but it's manageable for the future.

I expected a wider selection, yet the items I sampled were commendable. I savored the prime rib, sausage, lime corn, potatoes, and other flavorful selections. I also sampled the crab legs, which I hoped would be freshly steamed and piping hot like at Caesars Bacchanal Buffet. They were satisfactory but not exceptional.

The desserts were impressive, offering a generous variety, with each bite being delightful.

We're inclined to return, despite the wish for more options and hotter crab legs, given the establishment's prestigious reputation.

yelp:train:162435.orig:
Mediocre. Overpriced. Rude.

If you read those three words and still need to know the details, here you go: 

1) I guess me and my two buddies were just too embarrassing for a Sunday morning - we got shunted off into a weird pseudo-private room that felt like a cage (bars on the windows) where you could hear the constant binging of slot machines.

2) I ordered a drink with no ice.  So they watered it down.  

3) The food was just ordinary.  

4) The staff was annoying - repeatedly trying to take out dishes away before we were done.  My friend was half-done his meal and went to the bathroom; the waitress actually tried to take his food - instead of classily folding his napkin and just chilling the fuck out.
yelp:train:162435.para:
Subpar. Excessively costly. Unfriendly.

If those three terms don't convey the essence, here's a detailed explanation: 

1) It seemed like my group and I were too awkward for a relaxed Sunday brunch, leading us to a cramped, pseudo-exclusive space with bars on the windows, echoing the sounds of slot machines. 

2) I requested a beverage without ice, which they diluted. 

3) The cuisine served was nothing special. 

4) The service was irritating - the staff persistently attempted to clear our plates before we finished. My companion was in the middle of his meal when he went to the restroom; the waitress even tried to snatch his unfinished food, instead of politely folding his napkin and giving us some space.

yelp:train:162840.orig:
Located on the back side of the Wynn, overlooking the golf course and a massive waterfall, I don't think I fell for Steve Wynn's hotel video hype about feeling like you're in the Carolinas. I was treated to an exceptional meal that was beautifully prepared and well served.  They don't have a menu for children but they were more than happy to split a plate for my kids.

They have a Kobe beef carpaccio infused with a garlic truffle oil on the appetizer menu that is truly remarkable. ($21.00)

Yes, prices are on the high side, like all Wynn restaurants, with the chicken, my steakhouse bellwether at about $38.00.  Sides run about $8.00 average.

The restaurant is just a part of the hotel, not located away in some remote golf building. Just pass the slots and head out to the other end of the building and you're there.
yelp:train:162840.para: Positioned behind the Wynn, with a view of the golf course and a grand waterfall, I remain skeptical about Steve Wynn's claims of a Carolinas-like ambiance in their hotel's dining experience. However, I was impressed by a superbly crafted and efficiently served meal. Although there's no specific children's menu, the staff graciously offered to share a plate for my children. \n\nThe appetizer menu boasts a Kobe beef carpaccio enhanced with garlic truffle oil, a truly exceptional offering priced at $21.00. Prices are comparable to other Wynn establishments, with chicken priced around $38.00 and sides averaging $8.00. The restaurant is integrated within the hotel, easily accessible by passing the gaming area and proceeding to the opposite end of the structure.

yelp:train:163031.orig: I think the show is entertaining, eccentric, funny, and odd all rolled into one. It has a bit of comedy, some excellent music, some silly jokes and some bright paint. My favorite part was the lights featuring the \""Cowboys\"". If you go to the show, you'll know what I'm talking about. Toilet paper is also a part of the show. I won't tell you how :-) You will have to go and experience it for yourself. Honestly, I liked it okay. But my kids and husband absolutely LOVED it! It's worth it to go just once and try it out. You never know!
yelp:train:163031.para: The program is amusing, quirky, humorous, and unique combined. It includes elements of humor, outstanding tunes, whimsical puns, and vibrant artwork. The highlight for me was the "Cowboys" light display. Visit the event to understand my perspective. Toilet paper is also incorporated into the experience. I won't reveal specifics, but you'll grasp it through personal attendance. I found it satisfactory. However, it was exceptionally cherished by my children and spouse. It's worthwhile to attend just once to see if you enjoy it. The outcome is unpredictable!

yelp:train:163570.orig:
UPDATE 5/1/14:  I see where someone from Hilton made a response to my post but interesting enough, no one was able to give me any feedback or a return call on the investigation into my missing item when I called their insurance provider (Sedwick) and emailed their lost prevention person (Caleb R).  I finally got a generic letter in the mail today basically saying SCREW YOU--NOT OUR PROBLEM.  So much for good Hilton Honors Customer Service - NOT!!!!  Needless to say once I replace the laptop I will be seeking to invest/purchase timeshare property with another organization and NOT Hilton!!!  I thought the LVH (formerly Las Vegas Hilton) was the only bad seed int he bunch but now I think the entire chain is corrupt.



This review is regarding the housekeeping staff.....  BEWARE-- they are thieves. Laptop was left in room upon checkout but when I called the security/lost & found department there was no record of the cleaning crew turning it in -- which is standard procedure at any business.  Nice rooms but be  careful of your valuables being left out.
yelp:train:163570.para:
On 5/1/14, I observed that a reply came from a Hilton representative in response to my comment, yet no one provided me with any constructive feedback or a follow-up on my inquiry about my lost item when I contacted their insurance agent (Sedwick) and the lost prevention specialist (Caleb R). Today, I received a nondescript letter in the mail essentially accusing me of the issue, undermining the Hilton Honors Customer Service reputation. Consequently, I plan to invest in timeshare property with a different company, excluding Hilton. Initially, I believed the Las Vegas Hilton (LVH) was the only problematic entity, but now I suspect the entire chain is tainted.

This review pertains to the housekeeping staff, who are suspected of being dishonest. My laptop, left in the room upon checkout, was not found by the security/lost & found department, despite it being a standard business practice for them to return lost items. While the rooms are commendable, caution is advised when leaving valuables unattended.

yelp:train:163685.orig: This was the most romantic place i have ever been. It came with delicious food and great view of the bellagio fountain show. I was sad that i wasnt able to have a professional photo of us taken by their photographer that goes around, but ill be sure to hang on to her next time. Maybe next time we could sit outside in the summer so we can have the full romantic experience with the water show and scenery of Paris!! Overall, we had a wonderful and unforgettable dinner here. I will definitely be back.
yelp:train:163685.para: I experienced the most enchanting location in my life, complete with delectable cuisine and a stunning vista of the Bellagio fountain spectacle. Regrettably, I missed the opportunity to secure a professional couple's photo by their photographer, but I'll make sure to arrange it on my return. Perhaps our next visit could be in the summer, allowing us to enjoy the full romantic ambiance with the water display and Paris's scenic backdrop. In summary, our dinner was exceptional and memorable, and I am eager to revisit.

yelp:train:163917.para:
