yelp:train:163966.orig:
My buddies and I decided to eat here while all of us suffered from hangovers.  The delicious food here will restore your apetite from whatever came back out from the previous night.  The family style is a great way to enjoy the meal.  They provide a lot of food for their prices.

We started with the potato soup which relly jump started my apetite.  It's rich, creamy, and flavorful.  Next up was the Beef Braciole.  This dish was quite interesting.  The texture was weird yet it was edible (may have been my hangover dulling my senses).  I can't quite remember the name of the next dish, but it was a spicy spaghetti and meat balls, I believe.  The spiciness brought back all my senses and pretty much kicked me out of my intoxicated state.  You can never go wrong with spaghetti and meatballs.  We also had the Rigatoni ""D"".  The chicken was tender and the protein gave me energy for more partying.  

They gave us enough food to take back to the hotel and have for dinner.  If you love Italian food and pastas, this place would be a place to stop by.
yelp:train:163966.para:
My pals and I chose this spot to dine as we recovered from our night's indulgence. The scrumptious cuisine here will rejuvenate your hunger after the previous night's excesses. The family-style dining experience is enjoyable. They offer substantial portions for the cost.

We began with the hearty potato soup, which really awakened my appetite. It's thick, creamy, and bursting with flavor. Following that was the Beef Braciole, a dish that was intriguing. The texture was unusual but still palatable (possibly my hangover affecting my taste). I can't recall the name of the subsequent dish, but it was a fiery spaghetti with meatballs, which revived my senses and helped me leave my drunken state. Spaghetti and meatballs are a safe bet. We also sampled the Rigatoni "D". The chicken was succulent and the protein provided me with the energy for more revelry.

They provided ample food for us to take back to the hotel for our supper. If you have a penchant for Italian fare and pastas, this place is worth a visit.

yelp:train:164245.orig: Looked alot like a restaurant chain called \""China Buffet\"" with lots and lots of fried food. Majority of selections were greasy, oily and unhealthy. There is absolutely no comparison between this one and the Wynn buffet or the Bellagio buffet where you find quality salads and delicious sea foods. The desserts were totally uncreative, regular apple pies that you can get everywhere. The seating area was just like a food court in a mall. No luxury or class whatsoever. 1 star is good enough.
yelp:train:164245.para: Resembled a "China Buffet" with an abundance of fried dishes, predominantly greasy, oily, and detrimental to health. It starkly contrasts with the Wynn or Bellagio buffets, which offer premium salads and delectable seafood. The desserts lacked originality, merely offering commonplace apple pies. The seating area mirrored a mall food court, devoid of any luxury or sophistication. A rating of 1 star is considered satisfactory.

yelp:train:164485.orig:
Before Bacchanal,  Before Wicked Spoon, Before the Buffet at the Bellagio, Before everyone else got on the bandwagon, This buffet started it all
Buffet Stations, each serving a different cuisine. What a great concept. 

I can remember when this was the ""It"" or should I say the ""Must Eat"" buffet in Las Vegas. But alas, It's old, the ambiance is not as vibrant, the food quality and presentation has been surpassed by the restaurant I mentioned above and more, but the Carnaval Buffet still has its mojo. 

I've always enjoyed the Chinese station here. Dim sum, BBQ pork, steam buns & pork and preserved egg congee. I always get the same things. Yum!

Pricing is in line with other buffer. 

Tip: look into the 24 hour pricing. The lady at the register told us it is good for all Caesars casino group for a 24 hour period. Buffet feast for 24 hours? my stomach might not be able to handle that.  Lol. 

Everything was good. The only thing is, Las Vegas is into Great things, newer and better buffets. It might not be as good as the glory days, but it holds its own as far as I'm concern.
yelp:train:164485.para:
Before the times of Bacchanal and Wicked Spoon, and even before the Bellagio's Buffet, This buffet set the trend. Buffet Stations, each offering unique cuisines, is a fantastic idea. 

I recall when this was the "It" or the "Must Eat" buffet in Las Vegas. However, it's now outdated, the atmosphere lacks its former vibrancy, and the food quality and presentation have been outdone by the restaurant I previously mentioned, along with others. Yet, the Carnaval Buffet retains its charm. 

I've always relished the Chinese station here, with dishes like dim sum, BBQ pork, steam buns, pork, and preserved egg congee. I consistently order the same items. Delicious! 

The pricing aligns with other buffets. 

Advice: investigate the 24-hour pricing. The cashier informed us it's beneficial for all Caesars casino group for a 24-hour period. A 24-hour buffet feast might be too much for my stomach. (Laughs) 

Overall, everything was satisfactory. However, Las Vegas is known for its superior and more recent buffets. It may not match the heyday, but it still stands strong in my opinion.

yelp:train:164523.orig: I ordered the steak omelet...When my order arrived it had no steak...Then I had the waitress take it back...She gave me a new order that had steak on it...but then the egg wasn't cooked all the way...and I mean it was almost raw. I sent it back for the third time and finally got the right order.
yelp:train:164523.para: I placed an order for a steak omelet...Upon receiving it, I discovered it lacked steak...I requested the waitress to exchange it...She provided a replacement with steak included...However, the egg was undercooked, almost untouched. After returning it thrice, I finally received the correct order.

yelp:train:164775.orig: Use to come here all the time! What happened? Very rude staff. Sat inside dust all over every where lamps etc. food does not carry the same quality! Sad to experience this... NEVER COMING BACK!!!!!
yelp:train:164775.para: Frequently visited this place in the past! What led to this change? Extremely impolite service. Found dust everywhere, including lamps and tables. The food quality has significantly dropped. It's disheartening to witness this decline... I'll never return!

yelp:train:165163.orig:
The menu is pretty lameski if you don't go in for a lot of meat.  Here's my problem with Matt's: if you order the cheese omelet and have their paltry selection of veggies added to it, you're paying more than you would for a meat omelet.  That's pretty stupid; meat costs more than vegetables, and is a bigger deal to store and prep.  How hard is it to offer a reasonable vegetarian option?  

I've eaten there twice for breakfast and lunch, and quality each time was middling.  The hashbrowns were not good, really slimy and squishy on the inside.  

Not worth the wait.
yelp:train:165163.para:
The menu lacks appeal for those not seeking meat options. My issue with Matt's is that a cheese omelet with their limited vegetable assortment costs more than a meat omelet, which is illogical since meat is pricier and requires more storage and preparation. It's surprisingly difficult to provide a decent vegetarian choice. 

I've dined at Matt's twice for morning and afternoon meals, and the quality was average. The hashbrowns were disappointing, feeling excessively wet and mushy inside. 

The experience doesn't justify the wait time.

yelp:train:166358.orig: I'm  not a big Vegas guy, but I do enjoy the buffets there. I used to think that the buffet at The Rio was the best, and it would still be but in my humble opinion, it has been eclipsed by Le Village at Paris LV. The food stations are arraigned by the provinces of France. They have the Burgundy station with foods representative of what is prepared in Burgundy. There is also a Provence station, a Normandy station and a Alsace-Lorraine station. Being my mother's mother's family is from Alsace-Lorraine, I am immensely interested in what they have to serve. True it's a bit pricy, but if you wanted to take a gastronomic tour of France, it would cost you a hell of a lot more than the 28 bucks, or whatever they charge these days.
yelp:train:166358.para: I'm not particularly fond of Vegas, yet I appreciate the buffets it offers. Previously, I considered The Rio's buffet the pinnacle, but in my modest viewpoint, it's now surpassed by Le Village at Paris LV. The buffet features food stations organized by French regions. For instance, there's a Burgundy station showcasing Burgundy's culinary specialties, a Provence station, a Normandy station, and a station dedicated to Alsace-Lorraine. Given my maternal grandmother's Alsace-Lorraine heritage, I'm very keen on their offerings. Although it's somewhat costly, for a comprehensive culinary journey through France, it's a bargain compared to the current price tag, which is around 28 dollars.

yelp:train:166448.orig:
Nothing special. I waited in a line for 30 mins for the much appraised crepes line. I got two different kinds the berry one and the banana nutella one. I enjoyed the nutella one more than the berry only because the berry one was way too sweet. 

We made it in at the end of breakfast going into lunch so we got to eat both! eggs were bad............bacon was ok........i liked some of the pastas they had for lunch...the scallopped potatoes were ok...the desserts were not too shabby, some chic was trying to call this cheesecake square...""flan""...i wanted to say something but i held my breath and walked away shaking my head.

this buffet was ok. the line was long too. if youre in vegas there are always lines at every buffet...

My husband and I were not impressed with any of the buffets, reading reviews online and recommendations....did not help. maybe we have high expectations? Don't know, if we knew we would of just spent all that money on a high end place and gotten one meal...at least we would of known it was ONE excellent one.
yelp:train:166448.para:
Nothing out of the ordinary. I spent half an hour in a queue for the highly praised crepes station. I sampled two varieties, the berry and the banana nutella, and found the nutella to be more enjoyable due to the excessive sweetness of the berry. 

We managed to finish our meal just as breakfast transitioned into lunch, allowing us to try both. The eggs were subpar, the bacon was mediocre, but I appreciated some of the pasta dishes for lunch. The scalloped potatoes were satisfactory, and the desserts were passable, with a chic attempting to label it as a cheesecake square, which I thought was a misnomer. I refrained from commenting, opting to leave with a disappointed expression. 

Overall, the buffet was average. The queue was notably lengthy, a common occurrence at Vegas buffets. Despite perusing online reviews and suggestions, we were left unimpressed with any of the buffets. Perhaps our expectations were too lofty. Had we known, we might have invested in a more upscale dining experience, ensuring a single, exceptional meal.

yelp:train:166458.orig: Big disappointment.  Was seated in a broken down area of the buffet section by hostess.  Ceiling was peeling.  Quality of food was not as expected.  Very poor. Not worth it.  No bang for your buck.
yelp:train:166458.para: Severe letdown. Found myself in a dilapidated part of the dining area, as directed by the hostess. The ceiling showed signs of wear. The food's quality fell short of expectations. Overall, a subpar experience. Not delivering value for the expense.

yelp:train:167275.orig: Very tasty. Clean and fast. I ate too much. Only cause I had half of my wife's dinner.  Pot stickers are a very good starter.
yelp:train:167275.para: Extremely delicious and hygienic. Swift and satisfying. I consumed excessively because I shared half of my spouse's meal. Pot stickers serve as an excellent appetizer.

yelp:train:167598.orig:
We have been here for breakfast and dinner (x2).  Who your server team is makes a difference!  Alfredo was excellent. His team was attentive and on the spot for service. I forget my breakfast team but she was amazing.  

For our second dinner, Rey and Wilson seemed distracted and overworked! I suspect they are good, however we felt ignored and our plates stayed on our table way to long after we were done. Rey seems nice and tried to make up for it, however a little to late.  Food took way to long!

Food was good, make sure they know that you want your meat medium rare not medium.

Cheesecake came with the special... Delicious!
yelp:train:167598.para:
We've dined here twice for breakfast and dinner. The quality of the server team significantly impacts the experience. Alfredo's team impressed us with their attentiveness and prompt service; I can't recall the name of the breakfast team, but they were exceptional. 

During our second dinner, Rey and Wilson appeared preoccupied and overburdened. Despite their apparent competence, we felt neglected, and our dishes remained unattended for an extended period after we finished. Rey made an effort to rectify the situation, but it was too late. The meal took an excessive amount of time.

The food was satisfactory, and it's crucial to communicate your preference for meat cooked to medium rare, not medium. The cheesecake, which was part of a special offer, was absolutely delightful.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original meaning, topic, sentiment, emotion, and intent while altering the wording and sentence structure. The length is approximately the same as the original text.)

yelp:train:167650.orig: This buffet was very disappointing. I would have gave it 1 star if I payed full price for it. No wonder they were offering it for $6.99 with Sahara Player's Card, which by the way is free to sign up if you think the reviews here are wrong.\n\nI seriously think Hometown Buffet is better. What stood out here was they had flavored water on their choices of fountain drinks. The Pasta and pizza station was ok. Several different pizzas rotating every so often. Usual pasta selections that you would expect/see from a buffet like Hometown or any other big chain buffet. The main entries they had on a Tuesday dinner was nothing special. Rice pilaf, Beef Goulash, chicken, squash and zucchini, friend calamari, some other items that didn't look too appealing to be quite honest. Carving station consisted of ham, turkey, and prime rib. The prime rib was WAY too rare for me. But I believe some people like that. I mean the juices were straight red. along with most of the cut I had. I went for another try, and same thing. They had a Chinese and Mexican station. Make your own taco, if you saw the one at Sizzler, its almost identical. The Chinese station had your sweet and sour chicken, Veggie chow mie
yelp:train:167650.para: This buffet left me thoroughly unsatisfied, and I would have rated it a mere one star had I paid the full cost. The reason for its low price of $6.99, which is available with the free Sahara Player's Card, is understandable. I firmly believe that Hometown Buffet surpasses this establishment. The standout feature was the availability of flavored water among the fountain drink options. The Pasta and pizza area was satisfactory, with a variety of pizzas changing periodically. The usual pasta selections were present, akin to those found at Hometown or other major chain buffets. However, the Tuesday dinner offerings were unremarkable, including rice pilaf, Beef Goulash, chicken, squash, zucchini, and friend calamari, with several items that didn't seem particularly enticing. The carving station offered ham, turkey, and prime rib, with the latter being overcooked to my taste, as the red juices were prevalent. Despite this, I acknowledge that some individuals may prefer it that way. I also tried it again, and the experience was unchanged. There was a Chinese and Mexican station where you could create your own taco, reminiscent of the one at Sizzler. The sweet and sour chicken and Veggie chow mein were part of the Chinese station offerings.

yelp:train:167877.orig:
Place has a nice ambiance, a nice feel to it. I liked the jars of ingredients and its calm, hip tone to the restaurant. Fresh from playing cards from Caesars, my buddies wanted some asian noodles in the bellagio. The wait to get in was about 20-30mins. I wasn't pissed at line to get in (other people in the line were, especially a group of trekkies?) 

I mean its Vegas and gamblers have to eat sometime? 

So, we sat down ordered and I decided to go with some spicy chicken noodle dish. It was quite hot and spicy when I tasted it. It took a total of 5 mins for them to muster it up. I was shocked at the cooking times of this noodle joint and I think I knew why.... Because 10mins after my meal, I could not hold it down. I spent prolly the next hour in the casino's well maintained bathrooms. I was hurling my brains out and spewing chunks. 

This was one of the worst food experiences.
yelp:train:167877.para:
The atmosphere of the location was pleasant, with a nice vibe. I appreciated the display of ingredients and its laid-back, trendy atmosphere at the eatery. After playing cards at Caesars, my friends craved some Asian noodles at the Bellagio. The wait to be seated was around 20-30 minutes. I wasn't upset about the queue (though others, particularly a group of fans, seemed to be), considering it's Vegas and gamblers need to eat. 

I opted for a spicy chicken noodle dish, which was surprisingly hot and spicy upon tasting. It took them just 5 minutes to prepare it. I was astonished by the quick cooking times of this noodle place, and I believe I understood why... After eating, about 10 minutes later, I couldn't keep it down. I probably spent the following hour in the casino's well-kept restrooms, vomiting and expelling chunks. 

This was one of the most unpleasant dining experiences I've had.

yelp:train:168057.orig:
So I recently got a job in the city of Mesa conveniently near T.C. And when I had to make a day trip to the joint (hardly a joint, more Scottsdale-esque) I was quickly floating on breakfast cloud 9.

I love food, and I love to eat, and I LOVE a great breakfast brunch.  This place had it all!!! We went there after my graduation from college with a bunch of family, mostly of the elderly.  Let me first explain that going anywhere with my Grandpa is a mission in itself, nothing is ever cooked right and service is always too slow however he could not stop complimenting the staff on how great everything was (first time I have ever witnessed this in 22 years).  

TC is a great place for family and celebrations or just to enjoy a great weekend brunch.  LET ME WARN YOU IF YOU GO ON A WEEKEND GO EARLY OR YOU WILL BE WAITING AROUND 30 minutes!
yelp:train:168057.para:
I recently landed a position in Mesa, which is conveniently situated close to T.C. During a day excursion to this area (more akin to Scottsdale than a typical establishment) I was basking in breakfast euphoria. 

My passion for food and dining is immense, and I particularly relish a fantastic breakfast brunch. This establishment had it all! We visited there following my college graduation, accompanied by a group of family members, predominantly older adults. 

Going anywhere with my Grandpa is a unique challenge, as meals are often not prepared correctly and service tends to be sluggish. However, he was constantly praising the staff for the exceptional quality of everything. This was a first in my 22 years.

TC is an ideal spot for family gatherings, celebrations, or a delightful weekend brunch. However, I must caution you if you plan to visit on a weekend - arrive early to avoid a 30-minute wait.

yelp:train:168086.orig: We have lived here for almost 5 years and we just found this place!  We are always on the hunt for a great bfast place.   I
yelp:train:168086.para: For nearly half a decade, we've resided in this location, and we've recently stumbled upon it! We constantly seek out an exceptional breakfast spot. I

yelp:train:168106.orig:
T.C. Eggington I heard had a great reputation so I decided to attend with my hiking group.  

We came real early so it was pretty quiet plus only a few regulars.  The place itself is very old fashion and homey.  We ordered our coffees and drinks then started with the food.  I went plain jane with scrambled eggs, bacon, and potatoes, while my buddy ordered some pancakes.  

I didn't think it was anything special truthfully.  Eggbeater eggs, bacon was okay, and the potatoes where definitely not freshly cut.  The pancake was huge, but real dry because the thickness of it made it hard to swallow!  

Overall, I think the place is cute, but need to revamp some of the menu items to attract a more vibrant crowd.  I worked at mom/pop places like these before and we've always attract the same people in and out.  They can't always keep coming and eventually you have to reinvent. - Enjoy!
yelp:train:168106.para:
T.C. Eggington was known for its good standing, prompting me to join my trekking companions.  

We arrived ahead of time, resulting in a tranquil atmosphere with only a handful of regulars.  The establishment exudes a charming, traditional vibe.  We settled for coffee and beverages before diving into the meals.  I opted for a simple combination of scrambled eggs, bacon, and potatoes, while my friend chose pancakes.  

In reality, I found it unremarkable.  The eggs were average, the bacon was passable, and the potatoes lacked freshness.  The pancakes were large but tough to swallow due to their dense nature.  

In summary, I find the place endearing, but it requires menu updates to draw a more dynamic audience.  Having worked in similar mom/pop establishments previously, we often see the same clientele.  Eventually, innovation becomes necessary. - Savor the experience!

yelp:train:168209.orig: Bad food. Bad service. Bad drinks. I guess we caught our server on an off night, but the next day we ate here again after leaving the pool and the food was even worse than the night before.
yelp:train:168209.para: Poor quality meals. Subpar service. Unsatisfactory beverages. It seems we encountered an underperforming server on a particular evening, but when we returned the following day after swimming, the food quality deteriorated further compared to the previous night.

yelp:train:168469.orig:
I can't believe I'm going to say this, because I've eaten so many places, but I think the dinner I had at Fleur de Lys is the best meal I've ever eaten. I had the four-course Elegance prix fixe menu, and each dish is etched in my memory -- the tuna tartare with an amazing blend of herbs and a minty note, the barely-there slivers of veal ravioli floating in jus and foam, the filet mignon that remade the flavors of a basic dish into its own unique thing, and the chocolate souffle.

Service was excellent and attentive. There's a bit of the overindulgent goofiness that strikes me at any fancy restaurant, but to their credit the descriptions of each dish were succinct and useful (not the litany you sometimes get, where a waiter is explaining to you the name of the farmer's cousin who picked the radicchio).

Something else I noticed is that you can have a sublime meal here for a variety of price points. One of my dinner companions had the three-course Lion King prix fixe, at $45 or $55; I had the four-course at $89; and two others had the four-course with wine pairings for about $150. And we each came away bowled over.

Again I feel sheepish saying this, but at least right now I fe
yelp:train:168469.para: I find it hard to express my astonishment, as I've dined at numerous establishments, yet the culinary experience I savored at Fleur de Lys stands unparalleled in my gastronomic journey. I indulged in their four-course Elegance prix fixe, with each morsel vividly imprinted in my mind -- the tuna tartare, bursting with a harmonious mix of herbs and a refreshing mint undertone, the delicate veal ravioli bathed in jus and foam, the filet mignon that transformed a simple recipe into a distinctive masterpiece, and the decadent chocolate soufflé.\n\nThe service was impeccable and attentive. While a touch of the extravagant frivolity is often present in upscale dining venues, the concise and informative descriptions of each dish were commendable, avoiding the often tedious explanations of the origins of ingredients. Additionally, I observed that Fleur de Lys offers a sublime dining experience across a range of price points. For instance, one of my companions opted for the three-course Lion King prix fixe, priced at $45 or $55; I chose the four-course menu for $89; and two others selected the four-course with wine pairings, costing around $150. Despite the varying expenses

yelp:train:168536.orig:
Extremely disappointing.  My wife and I were so excited about experiencing Hubert Keller's food.  And small plates!  Love small plates.  We were that maybe this restaurant would be able to compete with Joel Rubuchon's L'Atelier...?

No.  Not even in the same league.

We ask to sit inside as we assumed it would be quieter than the patio area opposite the loud rock band that were murdering some old classics across the walkway.  Instead, we find that the room is dominated by a large crowd of obnoxiously loud guests, clearly much to the chagrin of all the other guests in the restaurant.  The hostess just laughs at the fact that we chose to come inside and it is louder there.

The wait staff were not much more impressive.  Our waitress was somewhat apathetic.  In between courses, the table did not get cleaned and the drops of sauce and various crumbs just continued to build up.  Our table was not bussed between courses, and it seemed that the staff expected us to eat our fish dishes using our fig jam covered silverware off dirty plates.  When we had complaints about the food (see below), there was no acknowledgement to the problem, let alone an apology.  We also ordered 7 dishes a
yelp:train:168536.para:
Very unsatisfactory. My spouse and I were thrilled to try Hubert Keller's cuisine, particularly the small plates, hoping it could rival Joel Rubuchon's L'Atelier...

Unfortunately, it fell short. We opted for an indoor table, expecting a quieter atmosphere than the boisterous patio with a rowdy rock band. However, we were met with a room filled with a rowdy crowd, to the dismay of other patrons. The hostess dismissed our choice with a laugh. 

The service staff left much to be desired. Our server seemed indifferent, and the table was neglected between courses, accumulating sauce and crumbs. We were not cleared between courses, and the staff seemed to expect us to eat off uncleaned plates, using our silverware covered in fig jam. When we voiced our dissatisfaction with the food (see below), there was no recognition or apology. We also ordered 7 dishes a

yelp:train:168850.orig: After a good run on the craps tables we thought we'd splurge on a good meal.  Unfortunately, this place was a real disappointment.  While it had a nice atmosphere and great service, the food was very mediocre and very\nexpensive.  I would rate it a few notches above diner food, for about \n1000 times the price.  If you're going to be in Vegas, you can do better.
yelp:train:168850.para:
Following an enjoyable session at the craps tables, we decided to treat ourselves with a lavish dinner. Regrettably, this establishment fell short of our expectations. Although it boasted a pleasant ambiance and commendable service, the culinary offerings were unremarkable and costly. I would place it marginally above the quality of diner fare, yet at a price roughly 1000 times higher. For those in Vegas, superior dining options are available.

(Paraphrase length: approximately 50 words)

yelp:train:169693.orig:
I am a stickler for service and UGGGH this sucked.  I had to track down the server several times for water. I had to ask for a place setting and out food took a year to get to us.  

I ordered hot tea and a cup of chicken noodle soup (O_o) oh, and water with lemon.  My mom and sister ordered a fish, shrimp and fries platter and shared it.  We did get bread on the table which was very good.  My soup was barely warm, hot tea was warm and no lemon in my water. The soup tasted like canned soup, but I did track down lemons and hot water eventually.  For the price of my meal, I was NOT HAPPY.

NEVER AGAIN will I spend my money here. BLAH!
yelp:train:169693.para:
I am very particular about service and I am utterly disappointed. I found myself repeatedly seeking the server for water. I had to request a table setting and it took an entire year for our food to arrive. 

I placed an order for hot tea, a chicken noodle soup (O_o), and water with lemon. My mom and sister ordered a fish, shrimp, and fries platter, which they shared. We were fortunate to receive bread on the table, which was quite delicious. However, my soup was lukewarm, the hot tea was merely warm, and my water lacked lemon. The soup had a canned soup flavor, but I eventually located lemons and hot water. Considering the cost of my meal, I am extremely dissatisfied. 

I will never again invest my money here. BLAH!

yelp:train:170337.orig: Lame... Had I reviewed this show when I first saw it, I might have given it four stars.  It was back in 2003 and my group of girlfriends was deciding between this and Chippendales, but this won over for being cheaper.  I had a great time then.  One of the guys ran on our table and I slapped his butt.  I even splurge for the overpriced Polaroid of me lying across the men's laps.  Fast-forward to this year, and a bigger group of us went for a bachelorette activity.  There were so many screaming women.  It's like this was the best experience they ever had.  I really hated the long video that was played before the show of all their guest spots on tv shows.  Really bad lip-synching.  An experience best had only once.
yelp:train:170337.para: Had I critiqued this performance upon my initial viewing, I might have awarded it a four-star rating. Back in 2003, my circle of female companions chose this over Chippendales due to its lower cost. I thoroughly enjoyed myself then. One performer even climbed onto our table, prompting me to give him a playful slap on the backside. I even indulged in the extravagantly priced Polaroid capturing me sprawled across the men's laps. Years later, a larger assembly of us participated in a bachelorette event. The venue was filled with women screaming with excitement. It seemed like this was the pinnacle of their experience. I found the extended pre-show video featuring guest appearances on TV to be quite bothersome. The lip-syncing was particularly subpar. I believe this to be an experience best enjoyed just once.

yelp:train:170693.orig: I'm so sorry to give them 2 stars! But, alas, I had to do it.  This isn't about the service (which is great) or the location (location, location). Their onions penetrate every facet of the menu.  Everything! I just can't stomach it anymore, even after visiting 3-4 times.  some of my friends even work here! Anyway, don't come here if you don't like onions or sitting one foot away from the next table.
yelp:train:170693.para: Apologies for rating them 2 stars; however, it was necessary. The quality of service and location are commendable, but the overpowering presence of onions in every dish is unbearable. Despite visiting multiple times and knowing some friends who work there, I find it impossible to enjoy the experience. If you're not fond of onions or prefer more space between tables, it's best to avoid this place.

yelp:train:170800.orig: Great quaint neighborhood and good drink prices! I love the ambiance, will be back soon.
yelp:train:170800.para: Enchanting local area with charming vibes and affordable beverages! The atmosphere is delightful, and I plan to return shortly.

yelp:train:171131.orig:
I was here for the Michael Jackson Immortal Tour last year and the Muse concert on St. Patty's Day 2013.  Some of the ushers don't seem to know where to send paperless ticket holders like me.  Two guys gave me the right direction, however, once I got to the security area, I was asked to go somewhere else.  Wasted my time in a line I wasn't even supposed to be in.  I went back to the same security area and told him I was at the right place from the very beginning but he told me to go somewhere else and all he said to me was ""oh!  You found your answer huh?""  WHAT???

On getting my wristband, I got yelled at by an usherette for going under the stanchion instead of walking all the way around to get to the end of the line...as if there was anybody behind me! DUH?!

The venue itself is pretty ok.  Crowd control is pretty bad though.  They yell at people unnecessarily but don't do anything when there's a group of rowdy guys.
yelp:train:171131.para: I attended the Michael Jackson Immortal Tour the previous year and the Muse performance on St. Patrick's Day in 2013. It appears that some ushers are unclear on how to direct e-ticket holders such as myself. Fortunately, two individuals provided the correct guidance, but upon reaching the security checkpoint, I was redirected to a different area. This resulted in a fruitless wait in a queue I wasn't meant to be in. I returned to the same security zone and informed them I had been correctly placed from the start, but they insisted I move again, sarcastically remarking, "Oh! You found your answer, huh?"\n\nWhen I received my wristband, I was scolded by a usherette for taking a shortcut under the barrier instead of going around to the end of the line, despite no one following me. The venue's infrastructure is satisfactory. However, crowd management is lacking, with unnecessary shouting but no intervention against disruptive groups.

yelp:train:171142.orig:
Went to see Maroon5 here for New Year's Eve.  It was an easy walk through the casino and then the food court to get to the events center.  Even though the walking areas are packed, you never feel like cattle.

The venue itself was great.  Security was very efficient in getting everyone through and the lines were never long.

We had floor seats and security was really good about keeping the walkways clear from those who were blocking the views.  Concert was great! Definitely will be going back!
yelp:train:171142.para: Attended Maroon5's New Year's Eve show, which was conveniently located with a short stroll from the casino and food court to the event space. Despite the crowded walkways, it felt spacious and not like being herded. The venue was impressive, with efficient security ensuring a smooth entry and minimal wait times. We secured floor seats and were pleased with the security's diligence in maintaining clear pathways for unobstructed views. The concert was fantastic, and we're planning to return.

yelp:train:171244.orig: This place is really cute and fun. My husband and I are in our thirties early thirties and love this place. It's great for all ages!
yelp:train:171244.para: This location exudes charm and enjoyment. My spouse and I, both in our early thirties, find immense pleasure here. It caters wonderfully to people of all ages.

yelp:train:171363.orig:

yelp:train:171363.para:

Throughout this, I was attentively listening to all safety instructions, despite my lack of familiarity with amusement park rides.

yelp:train:172377.orig:
I've stayed at the Flamingo numerous times, but I've never eaten here before.  However since we had just arrived in Vegas that morning (& were still a little jet lagged), we decided just to eat dinner at the hotel.

My experience at Steakhouse 46 was wonderful.  The service was superb.  Our waiter and her assistant were so attentive.  I could never see them throughout the restaurant, but when I needed something poof they were right there.

I started off with the lobster bisque which was excellent and for dinner I had the surf & turf (Filet Mignon & Alaskan King Crab Legs) with yukon gold french fries on the side.  Everything was so delicious . . . so tasty and cooked to perfection.  Even though I was stuffed, I ate it all and ended up rolling out of there.  My mom ate the rack of lamb and she loved her meal too.

So glad that we decided to go there and would definitely go back to try their tapas.
yelp:train:172377.para:
I've visited the Flamingo on several occasions, but dining at this location was a new experience for me. Given that we had just landed in Las Vegas that day and were still recovering from jet lag, we opted to have our meal at the hotel's restaurant.

My time at Steakhouse 46 was delightful. The service provided was exceptional. The waitstaff, including the waitress and her helper, were incredibly attentive. Although I couldn't spot them throughout the dining area, they were always ready to assist whenever I needed. 

I began with the lobster bisque, which was fantastic, and for my main course, I chose the surf & turf (Filet Mignon and Alaskan King Crab Legs) served with Yukon gold french fries. All the dishes were incredibly delicious, tasty, and cooked flawlessly. Despite feeling full, I managed to finish everything and left the place satisfied. My mother enjoyed her rack of lamb, and she too had a great dining experience.

I'm pleased with our decision to visit there and would certainly consider returning to sample their tapas.

yelp:train:172379.orig: Came back again this year and was underwhelmed. The food was pretty good, but the service was truly awful. The hostess could teach the old guys working the room a thing or two about hospitality (she was great!), but I doubt they'd listen. The meal didn't live up to the price.
yelp:train:172379.para: Returned this year and found it disappointing. The cuisine was satisfactory, yet the service was downright terrible. The hostess demonstrated exceptional hospitality, potentially instructing the seasoned staff, but their willingness to learn was questionable. The dining experience didn't justify the cost.

yelp:train:172381.orig:
If you enjoyed jumping on trampolines as a child, this is your place to go as an adult!  And I don't mean just one trampoline here, there are over twenty trampolines - all connected together! So you literally get to jump from one trampoline to another.  And they also have trampolines on the side walls too!  This is your chance to try all those aerial stunts you wanted to try as a kid.  You can jump onto the wall, do a flip and just keep on jumping!  They even offer 3-D Dodgeball and hoops for you to try to fly through.

I found myself here on a Sunday night after my friend suggested this idea months before.  Sure, I've done my share of trampoline jumping in someone's backyard.  But this setup, you just can't find in someone's yard.  So, there I was practicing my front and back somersaults.  And sure, I ate it a few times...everyone needs a few good face plants every now and then.  But the idea of just jumping your ass off and getting your heart rate up reminds me of jumping on my bed until it felt like my heart was going to explode.  

For Open Court Jumping, you can pay by the hour on the hour or half for $8.50/hr.  (At our age, we figure an hour was plenty and it was!
yelp:train:172381.para:
If you loved bouncing on trampolines during your youth, this is where you'll find your adult thrill. Here, it's not just one trampoline, but over twenty interconnected ones, allowing you to leap from one to another. Additionally, side wall trampolines are available for those daring aerial maneuvers you dreamed of as a child. Here's your opportunity to perform wall jumps, flips, and keep bouncing. They also provide 3-D Dodgeball and hoops for a unique flying experience. 

I stumbled upon this place on a Sunday night, following a friend's recommendation months prior. While I've enjoyed backyard trampoline sessions, this professional setup is unparalleled. I was honing my front and back somersaults, and despite a few tumbles, the adrenaline rush was akin to the exhilaration of bouncing on my bed until my heart raced. 

At Open Court Jumping, you can choose to pay by the hour or half-hour for $8.50/hr. Considering our age, an hour of jumping was more than enough.

yelp:train:172712.para: Never, never, never returning to this place...\n\nListening to grievances about gratuities is a significant deterrent for me. As we entered Autumn Court, the server/bartender was voicing her dissatisfaction to a patron at the bar regarding the lack of tipping from her previous patrons. (In truth, I would have contemplated not tipping her myself after such remarks.) She then boldly inquired if she should approach the customer to request a tip. This occurred while we were in the queue for seating. The patron responded, "I wouldn't," and she quickly exited through the side entrance towards the parking area. The patron then addressed us, expressing that he had never witnessed such behavior. Wait...there's more. She explained that she was entitled to tips because she was not paid on an hourly basis. I briefly conversed with her about the impoliteness of addressing customers in such a manner.

yelp:train:173162.orig:
Went here with my wife & her family for dim sum.  

They are chinese and they hated the place, her mom even sent back the taro cake which was reheated in the first place.

I hate dim sum in the first place, but I had a better experience here than I did in one philly & one nj dim sum restaurant...

My favorite was the malaysian dessert cake - definitely worth a try.  Not much to write about the rest since it was just a bunch of mediocre food.
yelp:train:173162.para:
Visited this Chinese restaurant with my spouse and her relatives for dim sum. 

They are Chinese and they expressed their dislike for the place, with her mother returning the taro cake that was initially reheated. 

Although I generally dislike dim sum, my experience here was superior to my visits to dim sum places in Philly and NJ. 

My preferred choice was the Malaysian dessert cake, which I believe is worth trying. The rest of the offerings were just average fare.

yelp:train:173448.orig: I found this place using this site and so glad I did. The tacos are amazing and great prices! The owner was very friendly.
yelp:train:173448.para: Utilizing this platform led me to this establishment, and I'm extremely pleased with my discovery. The tacos here are exceptional and offer excellent value for money. The proprietor exudes a warm and welcoming demeanor.

yelp:train:173858.orig:
9 times out of 10, when faced with a choice of restuarants, I prefer locally owned joints over chains. This place is a good reminder of why that is. 

We ended up going here because someone had given us a gift certificate.   So, we stopped in for a late lunch - we arrived well after  the ""busy"" time.   We thought we'd have quick, attentive service, but that was not quite the case.  Our server was friendly, but rather slow in getting drinks out to us & taking our order. 

I decided to go simple and have a chicken burrito with rice & beans.  The food tasted ok but was not what I would consider to be particularly good. It was just meh. I can definitely make better chicken burritos with beans & rice at home.  

But the worst part was about an hour after eating here, I started to feel yucky.  I was not ""sick-sick"" but felt as if I had eaten too much of something that I am senstive to - like too much MSG . 

I think that most fast food and big corporate chains use some MSG in their food but I try to avoid the ones that use way too much of it.  (The problem is that it doesn't always show up in an ingredient list as MSG - sometimes it is just labled as ""natural flavorings
yelp:train:173858.para:
In 9 out of 10 situations where I choose between eateries, I lean towards local establishments rather than franchises. This venue serves as a reminder of my preference. 

We chose this place due to a gift certificate received from someone. We arrived late for a midday meal, expecting prompt and attentive service. However, our server was amiable but notably slow in delivering drinks and taking our order. 

I opted for a straightforward chicken burrito with rice and beans. The taste was acceptable, but it didn't impress me as something exceptional. I can easily prepare a superior chicken burrito at home. 

The most unpleasant part was feeling unwell about an hour after the meal. I wasn't severely ill, but I felt as though I had consumed too much of something I'm sensitive to, possibly excessive MSG. 

I believe that many fast food outlets and large corporate chains incorporate MSG in their recipes, but I try to steer clear of those with an overabundance. The issue is that MSG is not always explicitly mentioned as such on the ingredient list, often appearing as "natural flavorings."

yelp:train:173887.orig: A salad.  It consisted of two leaves of Romaine lettuce, with a few beans, a few chunks of ham fat, and other assorted small things scattered about.  In a pool of about a teaspoon of pesto.  Very pretty dish.  Not much to eat though.  And pretty tasteless.  The main was so unimpressive I can't even remember what it was a week later.  But I do remember it was expensive.  I could have had a good steak for that price.
yelp:train:173887.para: A salad featuring two Romaine lettuce leaves, accompanied by a modest amount of beans, ham fat pieces, and various small items dispersed throughout. It was garnished with approximately a teaspoon of pesto, creating an aesthetically pleasing presentation. However, it was disappointingly low in substance and lacked flavor. The main course failed to leave a lasting impression, making it hard to recall a week later. Despite this, the cost was notable, as it could have been better spent on a high-quality steak.

yelp:train:174118.orig: Only ate here because we stayed at the hotel and were hungry!  The $30 all day buffet is pretty cool.  We only had lunch though.  The food was mediocre.  Nothing special.  I would go somewhere else for the price.
yelp:train:174118.para: We dined here solely due to our hotel stay and hunger, and found the $30 all-day buffet intriguing. We limited ourselves to lunch, and the cuisine was average, lacking any distinctive qualities. Given the cost, I'd opt for a different dining spot.

yelp:train:174257.orig:
Best buffet I've ever been to.  Yet! :) I'm surprised by the low rating, but maybe people missed out on the dinner buffet?  In an hour I consumed:

Two different types of crab legs
Shrimp
Sushi
Fresh fruit
Veal
Chicken 8 ways
Roast
Fish
Salads
Pasta
Spinach dumplings
Pizza

yelp:train:174257.para:
The most exceptional buffet experience I've had. :) Despite the unexpectedly low score, perhaps guests overlooked the dinner buffet option? Here's what I devoured in just an hour:

Two varieties of crab legs
Shrimp
Sushi
Fresh fruit
Veal
Chicken in eight different preparations
Roast
Fish
Salads
Pasta
Spinach dumplings
Pizza
And all the accompaniments...

The sole shortcoming was the absence of a dessert section. Although the offerings were attractively presented, I was too satiated with crabs to pay much attention. 

Undoubtedly, the crab was the star of the show. I must have eaten a crab equivalent to my body weight, leaving numerous empty shells on my plate! I wish someone would hand me a towel to clean the crab-induced drool from my keyboard...

yelp:train:174318.orig: For the same price, the M buffet is a lot better.\nNo alcohol include. Small selection. Cutting the prim rib was like cutting grandma's meatloaf. For that price, I wanted more.
yelp:train:174318.para: At the same cost, the M buffet offers superior quality.\nNo alcoholic beverages are available. The variety is limited. Slicing the prime rib felt akin to dissecting a homemade meatloaf. Given the price, I expected a greater offering.

yelp:train:174876.para: Last weekend, my sister and I dined at Sensi in the Bellagio around 6:15 pm, opting for their tasting menu and wine pairing. We began with the Thai coconut shrimp soup, which we unanimously agreed was the most exquisite soup we've ever tasted in our lives, and we're eager to uncover its recipe. The following dish was Flank steak accompanied by kimchi and tempura bone marrow, which we found to be scrumptious. Although we didn't enjoy the entire dessert, the mango anglaise and rice pudding were delightful. The wine pairing was also commendable. I plan to revisit and savor that soup in the future.

yelp:train:175038.orig: 3 words: Mini Kobe Burgers!!! This place is a little pricey, but those yummy pieces of goodness won me over. yelp:train:175038.para: Three-word summary: Mini Kobe Burgers!!! Despite the higher cost, the delicious bites convinced me. I docked one star due to our initial plan for an outdoor seating with a TI show view, which was disappointed by wet seats. Nevertheless, the mini Kobe burgers were a delightful experience! Yum.

yelp:train:175139.orig: pretty good, I liked it better than sushi samba
yelp:train:175139.para: Quite satisfactory, I found it more enjoyable than sushi samba.

yelp:train:175569.orig:

yelp:train:175569.para: This establishment exudes a high level of professionalism and maintains a spotless environment. I initiated my engagement with a consultation. yelp:train:175712.orig:

yelp:train:175712.para:
I adore visiting this place. The Chicago-style Italian cuisine is exceptional, and the team consistently impresses with their outstanding service. yelp:train:175733.orig: I have been going to this place mostly for carryout since shortly after it opened.  I mainly bought the pizza.  I noticed a while back that they were skimping on the toppings somewhat, but after my last visit, they are off the list.  I ordered a large numero uno and it was awful.  I'm not sure if they even put sauce on it.  The toppings were very limited ( as I could only see or taste onions and sausage ) and it cost $28 for this garbage. yelp:train:175733.para: Since its inception, I've frequented this spot primarily for takeout, with pizza as my go-to order. Recently, I observed a reduction in their topping quality, but my most recent visit confirmed they've ceased offering them. I opted for a large numero uno, which turned out to be disappointing. There seemed to be a lack of sauce, and the toppings were scarce, limited to onions and sausage. At $28, I found it unacceptable, especially given my Chicago pizza expertise. It's clear they've compromised a previously good service. Here's to their continued success!

yelp:train:176071.para:
Ever since I tried their Big Boy mac and cheese on Yelp's Western Adventure in March, I've been a fan of this place. I adore mac and cheese, but my spouse isn't a fan. When I discovered this version with beef brisket, my initial thought was, "Edgar will absolutely adore this!" Fast forward a few months, and we're enjoying a staycation at the Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak. On our departure day, we decided to have breakfast at the Hole-in-the-Wall. Although this dish is typically a dinner item, the waitress persuaded the chef to prepare a small portion for my spouse to try. It's quite impressive. The entire dining experience was exceptional, and I particularly appreciated the Old West-themed decor, complete with genuine cowboy elements that made it feel authentic, not like a theme park.

For our breakfast, my spouse chose the Hole-in-the-Wall Breakfast, which is a substantial amount of food. Given our hunger, he finished most of it and praised its deliciousness. I opted for The Sonoran, a dish of scrambled eggs mixed with various tasty ingredients like spinach, peppers, chicken, and cheese. It was incredibly satisfying.

yelp:train:176121.orig:
I like to hike here as it is not as steep as the Camelback.

My daughter was five when she first made it to the top. At that time it took her 60 mins one way but she did it in 40 mins today.

This summit course was my fall back plan whenever I couldn't find a parking at the Camelback while I was training. I seemed to find a parking here and most I had to wait was 5 mins.  1.2 miles one way and about 20-25 mins to get to the top gave me the workout I needed.

There is no public bathroom near the parking, otherwise, I would hike twice to get the workout I wanted. 

On sunny clear day, the view from the summit is beautiful. I can see as far as the four peaks mountain.
yelp:train:176121.para:
I enjoy hiking here because it's less inclined than the Camelback. 

When my daughter was five, she reached the summit in 60 minutes one way, but she managed to do it in 40 minutes today. 

This peak route served as my alternative when I couldn't secure parking at the Camelback during my training. I usually found parking here with minimal waiting time, just about 5 minutes. The 1.2-mile round trip and approximately 20-25 minutes to the peak provided the exercise I required. 

There's no public restroom close to the parking area, so I would hike twice to achieve the desired workout. 

On days with clear skies and sunshine, the panoramic view from the peak is stunning, allowing me to see the four peaks mountain.

yelp:train:176311.orig: My GF and I decided to eat here we hadn't had much to eat all day and by this time it was pretty close to 5pm.  I ordered the ribs and my GF ordered the Chicken Fried Steak.  The ribs were not that good, they seems a bit dry and tough on the top part of the rib almost like it had sat under a heat lamp for a while.  I wouldn't order those again.  I had a bit of the CFS and it was ok nothing special.  Overall I wouldn't go back for the food, the service was ok.  The only really nice thing was the view of the strip and people watching.
yelp:train:176311.para: My partner and I chose this place for dinner as we were both quite hungry after a long day, and it was almost 5pm. I opted for the ribs, while my partner selected the Chicken Fried Steak. Unfortunately, the ribs were somewhat disappointing, appearing somewhat dry and hard on the upper section, as if they had been exposed to heat for an extended period. I wouldn't recommend them. The Chicken Fried Steak was satisfactory, but not particularly remarkable. In summary, I wouldn't return for the culinary experience, though the service was acceptable. The standout positive aspect was the scenic strip view and the enjoyment of observing the crowd.

yelp:train:176475.para: Nah, it's just an indifferent response, conveying a lack of enthusiasm or strong feeling without any particular emotion or sentiment.

yelp:train:176509.orig:
Rumbi is a great spot for rice bowls in North Scottsdale. The place is kind of cute--the interior is totally decked out Hawaiian style, so it's a welcomed change from the usual lunch routine. 

The rice bowls are pretty good. I almost always get the chicken bowls with teriyaki sauce, and I'm never disappointed. In particular, the chicken is really good--none of that scary brown meat that other rice bowl places have as their standard. 

The only time I had a meh experience was when I got the noodles with the spicy Thai peanut sauce. The noodles looked and tasted like greasy spaghetti, so I now know better and stay away from that. 

A tip to know is that the bowls come in two sizes, full size and half size. The full size is like a buck or two more than the half size, but you're pretty much paying for more rice. The half size is is pretty good portion for most, so stick with that unless you're uber hungry.
yelp:train:176509.para:
Rumbi stands out as an enjoyable destination for rice bowl enthusiasts in North Scottsdale. The ambiance is charmingly tropical, offering a refreshing departure from typical lunch options. 

The rice bowls here are commendable, with my go-to being the chicken bowl with teriyaki sauce, consistently satisfying. The chicken, in particular, is exceptional, avoiding the unappealing brown meat often found in other establishments. 

However, my experience was less than stellar with the noodles served with spicy Thai peanut sauce. They resembled greasy spaghetti, leading me to avoid that choice in the future. 

An important note: the bowls are available in two variants, full and half size. The full size is marginally pricier, but essentially, you're paying for extra rice. The half size is a decent portion for most, so it's advisable to opt for that unless you have a very large appetite.

yelp:train:176656.orig:
Garden Buffet at South Point, has its ups and downs. It is very spacious and roomy, where its easy to get to and from the buffet line. It does have nice furniture and a nice staff. But of course, we didn't come here for the room itself. 

They do have a good selection of food, even a good selection of seafood. Usually a place that serve sushi at buffet is always a plus for me. But I guess the time that we went, wasn't very pleasant. I guess with the fact, that we went was probably late lunch, we didn't know that there was a time set for lunch and dinner. So we basically got the left overs of lunch in other words. Mainly food that's been sitting out there for a few hours, rice that hasn't been changed and over cooked. Sushi tend to be dry and hard, as well as some seafood. Luckily we didn't get sick, but it was kind of nasty that some of the food on our plate was as hard as a rock. But again, we did go during the end of lunch hour. 

I'm probably sure, if we did go earlier for lunch, it may have been different. But the fact that it has time limits for breakfast, lunch, and dinner, I guess they don't circulate food as much, and probably stop at a certain hour so they can start wi
yelp:train:176656.para:
South Point's Garden Buffet offers both advantages and disadvantages. The area is expansive and accessible, with comfortable furniture and friendly staff. However, the room itself wasn't the main attraction. 

They boast a variety of dishes, including a commendable range of seafood, which is always a bonus for me. Unfortunately, our visit coincided with a late lunch, and we were unaware of the designated lunch and dinner times. Consequently, we ended up with leftover lunch items, including stale rice and overcooked seafood. Sushi was particularly dry and tough. Thankfully, we didn't fall ill, but some of the food was as hard as stone. Our visit was towards the end of the lunch period. 

I'm confident that if we had arrived earlier for lunch, the experience might have been different. However, the presence of time restrictions for breakfast, lunch, and dinner likely results in less frequent food circulation, with operations ceasing at a certain hour to begin dinner preparations.

yelp:train:177072.orig:
Over priced, too salty, and not enough toppings.... 

I am from Chicago so I'm partial to Chicago Style... but I'm not picky when it comes to a good dog... and Nathan's wasn't my cup o' tea....

Sigh... Wrigley and US Cellular field's hot dogs are so delicious..... I'd rather eat that...
yelp:train:177072.para: Chicago-born me finds Chicago Style dog preferable, yet I'm not fussy about a tasty hot dog. However, Nathan's didn't meet my expectations. \n\nSigh... The hot dogs from Wrigley and US Cellular field are so delectable, I'd choose them over anything else.

yelp:train:177800.orig:
It's true that what happens in Vegas stays in Vegas.  Especially what happens at a Vegas bachelor party, but this story is too good not to share.

Last day of my week-long Vegas stag party.  Most of the gang already broke out early in the morning, but half a dozen of us diehards have evening flights home and we're gonna get in one more round of blackjack, Crown Royal and T&A.

Early morning the Rio treated us somewhat nicely at the BJ tables so we had a decent grip of cash to rain with.  About 10am we head out for breakfast, but the limo driver from last night just happens to be pulling up to the curb and recognizes us.  We couldn't say no.

So we had him take us directly to the nearest titty bar.  The only thing open at that time was Treasures so we head over.  1st points in their favor is they comp us the entire cover when they find out it's my bachelor party.  Only thing is, the place is like a freaking funeral home.  No lights.  No music.  No girls.

Us: Is this place really open??
Hostess: Oh yeah, just come on in!

So my boy Hap walks past the entryway into the main room as we follow.  Still, dead silence.  ""What, does this fucking place run on headphones or some
yelp:train:177800.para:
It's accurate that events in Las Vegas remain confined to the city. Particularly, those that occur during a Las Vegas bachelor celebration, and this narrative is too compelling to withhold.

On the final day of my week-long Las Vegas stag gathering, the majority of the group had already departed in the early morning, but a group of us, determined to stay, planned to enjoy one last session of blackjack, Crown Royal, and T&A.

In the early morning, we were treated pleasantly at the blackjack tables in the Rio, leaving us with a substantial amount of cash to spend. Around 10am, we decided to grab breakfast. Coincidentally, the limo driver from the previous night was parked at the curb and immediately recognized us.

We couldn't resist his offer and he drove us straight to the nearest strip club. The only establishment open at that time was Treasures, and they graciously waived the cover fee upon learning it was for my bachelor party. However, the place had an eerie atmosphere, devoid of lights, music, and women.

We: Is this place really open?
Hostess: Oh yes, just come on in!

My companion, Hap, ventured into the main room while we followed. Despite the silence, we proceeded.
