yelp:train:177888.orig: Very good food. Comparable to fast food in price but quality is far superior.
yelp:train:177888.para: Exceptional cuisine available at a cost similar to fast food, yet the quality significantly surpasses it.

yelp:train:178117.orig: My wife and I are Downtown regulars, and after a night of strolling around Fremont St. gambling and drinking we used to stroll over to the Golden Gate Casino's Bay City Diner, but since it became Du-par's prices have gone up and the food simply blows. Anyway, we now generally find our way to Magnolia's Veranda Cafe in the Four Queens, and while it's not dirt cheap, it's reasonable and the food is quite good, but like any place you visit it enough times and you long for change. After kicking around this place or the other, we settled on walking over to Sam Boyd's California Hotel and Casino to see what they had going on; all I can say is what a pleasant surprise Market Street Cafe was, remember we're talking about tasty/cheap \""after drinking food.\"" I'd say if you want a great Downtown dinner, try the Grotto or Hugo's Cellar, but if you're staggering around and need to put food in your stomach and don't care about atmosphere and are thinking cheap, good food, Market Street Cafe is as far as you need to look.
yelp:train:178117.para: My spouse and I frequently frequent Downtown, and following evenings spent wandering Fremont St., indulging in gambling and imbibing, we'd often head to the Bay City Diner at the Golden Gate Casino. However, with Du-par's pricing hikes and subpar cuisine, we've shifted our routine to Magnolia's Veranda Cafe in the Four Queens. Although not the most economical, it offers fair prices and commendable food, yet the familiarity breeds a desire for novelty. Exploring various establishments, we ultimately chose to visit Sam Boyd's California Hotel and Casino, where we were pleasantly taken aback by the Market Street Cafe's delectable and affordable post-drinking fare. For a memorable Downtown dining experience, consider the Grotto or Hugo's Cellar, but if you're seeking inexpensive, satisfying food without fussing over ambiance, Market Street Cafe is your destination.

yelp:train:178901.orig: Don't be a victim of Yelp and TV Hype.  This is a MASS QUANTITIES establishment, with no flavor, and questionable quality.  Front staff good, kitchen staff bad.  I ordered the \""famous\"" chicken and waffles.  Good grief, man.  The chicken (boneless breast) was dry and flavorless = cotton.  The waffle was far too dense, and tasted like cardboard.  I'm serious.  If you like Roscoe's, please heed my advice.  Wait staff was good, and apologetic when our food took over 30 minutes to get to us.  This was on a Sat. morning.  People that were seated after us were even done eating before we started.  Booooo.
yelp:train:178901.para: Avoid falling prey to Yelp and media exaggeration. This is a place that serves a high volume of customers, lacking in taste and uncertain in quality. The front team is commendable, but the kitchen staff leaves much to be desired. I tried their renowned chicken and waffles, and it was disappointing. The chicken, boneless breast, was utterly devoid of flavor, resembling cotton. The waffle was excessively heavy and had a cardboard-like taste. I urge those who appreciate Roscoe's to take my warning seriously. The service was decent, with the staff apologizing for the delay in our food, which took over 30 minutes. On a Saturday morning, we were the last to eat, while others finished before us. Disappointment indeed.

yelp:train:179057.orig:
Let me preface this review by saying, I've been to both this hash house and the one at Imperial Palace and this by far is a shitton better in terms of wait time, service, and dare I say even the food. 

I had a large group of famished, sunday-after-vegas-weekend-exhausted friends. All of them more than ready to show hash's infamously large plates what was up. Okay well maybe that could've just been my thoughts, really.

I was fortunate enough to have an eating partner willing to partake in my fatty adventure. The original request of a not so detrimental eggs benedict had been replaced by the andy's sage fried chicken benedict and a chorizo hash. Mind you, two very gargantuan orders. What a good sport, I almost kind of felt bad. Almost. 

Everyone got a variety of things which was of course, more food than anyone should ever force to digest in one sitting. We really enjoyed the sage fried chicken and chorizo orders --and were also the only two who finished all of our food. 

Side note, the fried chicken in and of itself was a bit dry. Luckily there was enough fat off the bacon, and the fried cheese to keep it moist. LOL. 

My friend got the kiwi watermelon drink thing whic
yelp:train:179057.para:
Begin this critique by noting, I've experienced both establishments, and undeniably, this one surpasses the other significantly in terms of waiting period, customer service, and even the culinary offerings. 

I was accompanied by a large circle of famished companions, emerging from a weekend of indulgence in Las Vegas. They were eager to sample the notoriously generous plates of hash. Perhaps this was merely my perspective. 

I was lucky to have a dining companion who was open to joining me in this indulgent feast. The initially suggested light eggs benedict was substituted with a substantial sage fried chicken benedict and a chorizo hash. It's worth mentioning, these were two massive orders. I found myself almost feeling guilty. 

Everyone received a diverse selection of dishes, which was, of course, more food than anyone should consume in a single meal. We all thoroughly enjoyed the sage fried chicken and chorizo dishes --and were the only two who managed to finish all our food. 

A side note, the fried chicken on its own was slightly dry. However, the excess fat from the bacon and the fried cheese helped maintain its moisture. LOL. 

My companion opted for the kiwi watermelon drink.

yelp:train:179207.orig:
Absolutely amazing food and service here. Waiters are very attentive, and the meal portions are gigantic! No wonder there's always a wait for a table. We had a party of 5 people, and waited for about 30 minutes for a table. But lemme tell ya - it was SO worth it. Everyone in our group loved their food, and there were certainly left overs when we were done!

The ingredients used in the food are such good quality, that you can really taste the freshness. The prices aren't too bad (most plates under $15), which is a great perk! Most trendy/high quality meals are much more expensive.

There is another restaurant location on the strip, but that wait is even worse than this one. It would be worth the drive into the surburbs of Vegas for a visit here!
yelp:train:179207.para: The food and service at this place are absolutely fantastic, with attentive waitstaff and generous portion sizes. Despite a 30-minute wait for a table with a group of five, the experience was incredibly rewarding, as everyone enjoyed the meal and there were leftovers. The high-quality ingredients used are evident in the fresh taste of the dishes, and the cost is reasonable, with most dishes priced under $15. Compared to other trendy, high-quality eateries, the prices here are more affordable. Although there's a longer wait at another location on the strip, it's worth the trip to the suburbs of Vegas for this dining experience.

yelp:train:180209.orig:
VERY disappointing, especially for a Vegas restaurant that charges an arm and a leg. Just for a restaurant itself, very very disappointing. 

This was supposed to be an Asian fusion type restaurant but it really lacked in Asian authenticity in terms of flavor. It seemed like the chefs just used different types of sauces  to compensate for lack of flavor which resulted in chaos. 

Fried rice with sausage: Very SMALL portion. Weird ""sweet and sour"" sauce spread over the rice. I would not order again. 

Pad Thai: Lacking flavor. Some type of sweet taste that I knew after one bite, I would get sick of it after subsequent bites. Very unauthentic. I would not order this again either.
yelp:train:180209.para:
Extremely unsatisfactory, particularly for a high-priced Las Vegas eatery. The restaurant, advertised as an Asian fusion, fell short in delivering genuine Asian taste, with flavors seemingly made up by various sauces, leading to a disorganized taste experience. 

Fried rice with sausage: The serving size was minuscule. The dish was drenched in a peculiar "sweet and sour" sauce. I would not be inclined to order it again. 

Pad Thai: It was devoid of flavor. A distinct sweetness was immediately apparent after the first taste, making it unappealing with each subsequent bite. It lacked authenticity and I would not consider ordering it again.

yelp:train:180754.orig: I have been using Gordon Biersh weekly for a team event for almost a year, and every time I have had incredible staff, great food, and every convenience.  The manager's treat you professionally and have really done a great job for us.  I highly recommend this location!
yelp:train:180754.para: For nearly a year, I've utilized Gordon Biersh's services for our team gatherings, consistently experiencing exceptional staff, delectable cuisine, and comprehensive amenities. The manager treats us with professionalism and has significantly contributed to our satisfaction. I wholeheartedly endorse this venue!

yelp:train:180869.orig: Just went for the first time last Friday night (5.2.08).    It's a small, independently owned restaurant that lends itself to conversation with your neighbors and a beer with the chef.   It's not your typical chain restaurant, nor does it try to be.   We had a huge table (14 people), which was hilarious considering the small/intimate size of the restaurant.     We ordered a couple of appetizers (Calamari and a Hummus Platter) - both of which were great.\nMy wife had the trout and I had the mussels and frites; they were both good enough that we were still talking about them the next day.   A good time was had by all and we'll be back soon.
yelp:train:180869.para: Last Friday evening (5.2.08), I visited a cozy, self-run eatery that encourages chats with nearby diners and enjoying a brew with the culinary expert. It's distinctly different from mainstream dining chains, maintaining its unique character. We gathered at a large table for 14, a comical contrast to the establishment's compact ambiance. We sampled some starters, including Calamari and a Hummus Platter, both of which impressed us. My spouse savored trout, while I relished mussels and fries, both dishes earning praise even the following day. The evening was delightful for everyone, and we plan to return soon.

yelp:train:181188.orig: I am very sad that I agreed to eat here.  The food was barely palatable and my drink came out COMPLETELY wrong twice.  Service was acceptable, but in the end we paid $40 for the pleasure of crappy food and a generally bad dining experience.  Blegh.
yelp:train:181188.para: I am extremely disappointed with my decision to dine here. The meal was hardly enjoyable to taste, and my beverage was incorrectly served twice. The service was decent, yet the overall experience, which cost us $40, was marred by subpar cuisine and a generally unsatisfactory meal. Blegh.

yelp:train:181277.orig: Breakfast service was good, prompt and friendly. This place offers your typical American breakfast fare at a price which is average for Vegas but more expensive that anywhere else in the USA. We had the corned beef hash with poached eggs. Nice. However table over from us had to send their breakfast steak back because it was gristly.\n\nI was tossing up to give this 3 stars. But the main thing that let it down was the $3.75 charge for brewed coffee.  The coffee was just terrible and I resented paying for it at any price.
yelp:train:181277.para: The breakfast here was served promptly and with a warm demeanor, featuring standard American breakfast options at a cost that's moderate for Las Vegas but higher than the national average in the U.S. We enjoyed the corned beef hash with poached eggs. However, the table next to us had to return their breakfast steak due to its tough texture. I was considering rating it 3 stars, but the significant downside was the $3.75 fee for subpar brewed coffee, which I found unacceptable regardless of the price.

yelp:train:181543.orig: Really good, cost effective specials and the steak was amazing
yelp:train:181543.para: Excellent deals and value specials, with the steak being exceptionally delicious.

yelp:train:181887.orig: Excellent service from the staff.  This hotel is a perfect choice if you don't want to stay in a casino (no smoking throughout!) but also want easy strip access.  While attached to the MGM Grand, access to The Signature is restricted only to those staying there so there is less hustle and bustle.  All amenities of The Signature as well as the MGM Grand are available to you.\n\nRooms are gorgeous and very well-appointed.
yelp:train:181887.para: The staff provides outstanding service. This hotel is an ideal option for those who prefer not to be in a casino environment (smoking is prohibited everywhere) and also desire convenient access to the strip. Being connected to the MGM Grand, The Signature's access is limited to its guests, resulting in a quieter atmosphere. You have access to all the amenities offered by both The Signature and the MGM Grand. The rooms are stunningly beautiful and meticulously furnished.

yelp:train:181967.orig: I had high expectations for the \""penthouse junior suite\"" we booked for our anniversary trip... Which is unfortunate because those expectations were squashed, to say the least. And shame on me for booking thru Blue Chip Vegas because they offered a better deal.. I can't emphasize more how much I DO NOT recommend making that same mistake. \n\nWe got to Vegas at 8am. Went to the hotel to see if we were lucky enough to check in early. The front desk rep stated that if we booked thru them, we could check in now, but our room thru blue chip is separate (rooms managed by a separate company on behalf of some rich guy that bought up a bunch of rooms as an investment) and she couldn't help me. Here's a cell phone number you can call -she says. OK... Call that, get VM. Call again, VM. Call again, they say - call back at 1 and we'll see. Ok...I can handle this, nothing to get upset about yet. I call at 1pm...VM. Three calls later, they say we can go check in. Great!! But then we get to the room and granted its a nice room with a beautiful view, as I check out the place I not only find someone's garbage in the silverware drawer, and someone's long black hair on the bathroom floor, but there
yelp:train:181967.para:
I anticipated a luxurious experience in the "penthouse junior suite" for our anniversary journey, but regrettably, those hopes were crushed, to put it mildly. I should have avoided booking through Blue Chip Vegas, as they provided a superior offer. I must stress the importance of not repeating this error.

We arrived in Vegas at 8am and headed to the hotel to see if we could check in early. The front desk employee informed us that if we had booked through them, we could check in immediately, but our room through Blue Chip was managed by a different company, and they couldn't assist us. Here's a contact number for you to call - she suggested. Alright, I'll call that number - I said. I called back, and they instructed me to call again. I called back, and they said - call back at 1, and we'll get back to you. I'm managing this situation calmly, with no cause for frustration yet. I called at 1pm - I said. After three calls, they confirmed we could check in. Excellent news! However, upon reaching the room, despite its attractive appearance and stunning view, I discovered littered silverware and long black hair on the bathroom floor, which was quite disappointing.

yelp:train:182005.orig: The rooms here were really really nice...fully stocked suite complete with microwave, stove, blender, and coffee maker. Actually finding the place is another story...the signage isnt real clear and I had to first go to the mgm counter to find out I was booked at the signature. I guess in the future I will be more aware of the layout, but new comers be prepared to get a little lost on your way in...
yelp:train:182005.para: The accommodations in this location were exceptionally pleasant and fully equipped, featuring a comprehensive suite with amenities such as a microwave, stove, blender, and coffee maker. However, locating the establishment proved challenging due to unclear signage, necessitating a visit to the MGM counter to confirm my reservation at the designated signature suite. Moving forward, I will be more conscious of the layout, but new arrivals should anticipate some difficulty navigating their way to the entrance.

yelp:train:182102.orig:
This hotel was fabulous and the staff were a pleasure to work with. We arrived at the hotel around midnight and the front desk staff greeted us with smiles and they went above and beyond for us. We was in tower 2 on the 37th floor and the view was to die for. 

Our one bedroom suite was flawless and everything was outstanding.  Anything you needed they made sure you received it. I love how each tower connected and how they all had a different theme, scent and flower arrangements. We also loved how it connect to the MGM grand. 

I stayed here for 7 days and I have no complaints. We would call housekeeping at 2am and they would come to assist us with smiles. This is by far the best hotel I've every stayed in and when I return to Vegas I'll be staying here again.
yelp:train:182102.para:
The hotel exceeded our expectations and the team was delightful to collaborate with. We checked in around midnight and the reception team welcomed us with warm smiles, providing exceptional service. Located in tower 2 on the 37th floor, the panoramic view was breathtaking. 

Our one-bedroom suite was impeccable, with every detail surpassing standards. The staff ensured we had everything we required. The interconnected towers, each with unique themes, scents, and floral decorations, added to our enjoyment. The seamless connection to the MGM Grand was also appreciated. 

I spent seven days there and have no grievances. We could reach out to housekeeping at 2am, and they would promptly assist us with their cheerful demeanor. This hotel is unparalleled in my experience, and I plan to return to Las Vegas and stay here once more.

yelp:train:182143.orig:
I dont write too many yelp reviews, and my goal is not to write this and make it sound too negative. My goal is to literately give the owner some business advice.
So last week my sister brought home lunch from Thai Basil. I was so impressed, and did not know that it was literately a minute down the road from our house. I thought wow, why have I never heard of this place before? The food is amazing, and the price is really good. 
Tonight my friends and I decided to go for dinner. The place was a little awkward (ex, a sign in the ladies restroom asking to ""dispose of toilet paper in the trash can"" vs the toilet as if we are in Mexico & the place reaking of bad cleaning chemicals). We were all ordering and I had pointed to something on the menu asking the waiter if it was what I was describing (seeing if it were the same thing my sister had brought home last week). He said yes, that it is. I said okay, I will have that.
Dishes came out one by one in 7-10 minute increments. We awkwardly sat waiting for everyone to get their food. Finally mine comes, (the photo posted seperately is what it is). Literately a dollar store bag of salad with thin chicken strips on top sprinkled with
yelp:train:182143.para:
I rarely compose reviews on Yelp, and I aim not to craft this to appear overly critical. My intention is to genuinely provide the proprietor with actionable business guidance.
Last week, my sibling returned home with a lunch from Thai Basil, which left me astonished. It was astonishingly close to our residence, a fact I hadn't realized. The culinary offerings were exceptional, and the pricing was quite reasonable. 
This evening, my companions and I opted for a dinner outing. The ambiance was slightly uncomfortable (for instance, a notice in the ladies' restroom urging to "dispose of toilet paper in the trash can" instead of the toilet, as if we were in Mexico, and a strong odor of poorly cleaned areas). We were all placing our orders, and I had indicated a dish on the menu to confirm with the server (to verify if it matched the dish my sister had brought home the previous week). He confirmed it was the same. I decided to order it. 
Dishes were served individually, taking 7-10 minutes each. We awkwardly waited for everyone to receive their meals. Finally, it was my turn, and here is the photo posted separately. Literally, it resembled a dollar store bag of salad with slender chicken pieces on top, sprinkled with

yelp:train:182472.orig: If you like big German style, then this is the place for you.\n\nAll the classic meals, friendly wait staff, and you can get your beer in a fish tank.
yelp:train:182472.para: If you appreciate substantial German cuisine, this is your ideal destination.\n\nEnjoy traditional dishes, welcoming service, and the unique experience of drinking beer in an aquatic setting.

yelp:train:182685.orig: I like local coffee houses. I prefer ANY local place over the big companies.
yelp:train:182685.para: I have a fondness for neighborhood coffee shops. I choose any local establishment over large corporations.

yelp:train:183204.orig:
We've been at least a half-dozen times, and have had above average service and excellent food the majority of our visits.  Especially loved the Sunday night discount ;-P.   When will they bring it back?!?

On our last visit, I tried the pulled-pork sandwich.  Oh. My. Lord!  It was delicious!  I have also enjoyed the ahi tuna salad.  The chiles rellenos are my least favorite dish, because they quickly get soggy in their sauce.  That said, my dear sissy LOVED hers. 

Don't know why it's listed as being a place you wouldn't take kids - our 6-year old LOVES their grilled cheese!  We, at least, have had good luck taking him there so far.  There seem to be families there every time we go, so I'd call it fairly kid-friendly.

Best feature - it's right off the AZ canal bikepath!  An easy ride if you'd rather not drive.
yelp:train:183204.para: We've frequented this place no less than six times, consistently receiving superior service and high-quality cuisine. The Sunday night discount is particularly cherished; we eagerly await its return. During our most recent visit, the pulled-pork sandwich was a standout, earning rave reviews for its deliciousness, as did the ahi tuna salad. However, the chiles rellenos tend to become soggy in their sauce, which is a personal preference. Despite this, my partner thoroughly enjoyed hers. The presence of children is surprisingly welcomed, as evidenced by our 6-year-old's love for their grilled cheese, and the establishment seems to cater well to families. The prime advantage of this location is its proximity to the AZ canal bikepath, offering a convenient alternative to driving.

yelp:train:183836.orig: I saw Jerry Seinfeld at Caesars Palace Las Vegas on Jan 30, 2009 and I wasn't impressed. He just wasn't that funny. It totally ruined my perception of him. However, his opening act was awesome.  I'm not sure, but it could have been comedian Tom Papa as the opening act.  I'd see Seinfeld again only if the tickets were free and I just wouldn't expect much. HUGE disappointment.  Save your money or go see Celine Dion, Bette Midler, or Jeff Dunham instead.
yelp:train:183836.para:
On January 30, 2009, I attended a show at Caesars Palace Las Vegas where Jerry Seinfeld performed, but I found him uninspiring and humorless, which negatively altered my view of him. The opening act, possibly Tom Papa, was quite impressive. I would only consider attending another Seinfeld show if the tickets were complimentary and I had low expectations. It was a significant letdown. I'd rather invest in seeing Celine Dion, Bette Midler, or Jeff Dunham.

yelp:train:184002.orig: I really am not a Chili's fan, but for dinner this was the best of all my options while I waited for my flight.  Thanks for seeming super annoyed that I was your customer, waiter.  And for literally flinging my paper napkin wrapped silverware at me.  Right into my face.  That was awesome.  At least you realized it quick enough and apologized, but you should have never done that in the first place.
yelp:train:184002.para: I must admit, I'm not particularly fond of Chili's, yet for my dinner during the flight wait, it turned out to be the superior choice among my alternatives. I appreciate your apparent frustration as my patron, waiter. Your action of forcefully tossing my napkin-wrapped cutlery directly at me was quite memorable. Although you acknowledged and apologized swiftly, such behavior should have been avoided from the outset.

yelp:train:184262.orig: Our last visit in June was very disappointing, but since I have been following Mario for nearly 23 years I passed it off as everybody has bad nights.  Went back after 4 months, had the pizza, was average, dough was soggy but had good flavor.  What really blew me was the wine list, pretty good, but whoa! serious price increases!  I love wine with good Italian food but they have gone into the stratosphere on pricing.  I guess all good things do come to an end, time to find another place, shouldn't be hard, lots of competition out there.
yelp:train:184262.para: Our recent trip in June left us disheartened, yet given my longstanding support for Mario spanning over two decades, I attributed it to occasional poor experiences. Returning after four months, the pizza was mediocre, with a dough that was too wet, yet it possessed a commendable taste. The wine selection was impressive, but the steep price hikes were startling. I enjoy pairing wine with excellent Italian cuisine, but the exorbitant cost has reached an unprecedented level. It seems all things must eventually conclude, and it's time to explore other dining options, which should be relatively straightforward due to the abundance of competitors.

yelp:train:185042.orig:
i came here 3-4 years ago and remember enjoying it. however this time around it wasnt nearly as great. we came in for brunch and with 12 people gratuity was included for a total of ~  $28 per person. 

the majority of my meal consisted of breakfast choices....waffles, sausage(rubber?), eggs, hashbrowns...

the highlight for mee was the fresh pineapples, grapefuit, &the prime rib...the prime rib + horseradish was the only thing that made me feel like i got my moneys worth. it was really tasty considering that the carved meats usually arent that appealing to me at buffets.

 the chinese section, seafood, churro, ESPECIALLY dessert was all very mehhhh...soo not worth wasting my hunger. 

cravings....psh i never have nor will i ever crave you!
yelp:train:185042.para:
Approximately three to four years back, I fondly recall my enjoyment here. However, my recent visit didn't match that level of satisfaction. We arrived for brunch with a group of 12, and the included gratuity brought the cost to roughly $28 per person. 

Most of my meal was breakfast items like waffles, questionable sausage, eggs, and hash browns. The standout for me was the fresh pineapples, grapefruit, and the prime rib, especially when combined with horseradish - the only aspect that felt like a good value for my money. Buffet meats typically don't appeal to me, but this was an exception. 

The Chinese, seafood, and churro sections, along with dessert, left me indifferent and unworthy of my hunger. 

As for cravings, I've never experienced them and I don't anticipate ever having them either.

yelp:train:185533.orig:
People have paid a Cover Charge here? 
Kidding right?
That is just plain dumb. 

It's a counter top with 8 stools, and then a smattering of low small square cushioned seats for another 20? 
It is just a space, not a room.
I didn't even hear one Beatles tune piped in.

Popped in at 5:30 before dinner and a show here at the Mirage.
I guess we made it in under the Cover Charge wire. Just ended up here. Nice visit. Could become crowded easy. I suppose it does too.

The waitress was a sweetheart. And it looked like a couple of ""Hostesses"" were setting up. One didn't fit in somehow...she had pert natural breasts.
yelp:train:185533.para:
Individuals have been charged a Cover Charge at this location? 
A joke, right? 
Absolutely foolish. 

Here's a countertop with eight stools, plus a few small, cushioned seats for an additional twenty. It's merely an area, not a room. I didn't catch a single Beatles song playing. 

I arrived at 5:30 before dinner and a performance at the Mirage. It seems we managed to stay under the Cover Charge limit. Just ended up here. It was a pleasant visit. It could easily become crowded. I assume it does. 

The waitress was very kind. It appeared that a few "Hostesses" were preparing. One of them seemed out of place somehow, with her naturally shaped breasts.

yelp:train:185709.orig:
Service: Spotty
Food: Above Average
Atmosphere: Awesome
Cleanliness: Top Notch
Music: Did not get it......
Mafioso wanna be factor: High

Service started out a little strained but got better as the evening went along.

Music was a little to loud, did not get the music selection for the  type of establishment.......

Place looks great, clean and fun.....

Food: Octopus appetizer was good not enough food on the plate though, Caprese salad was excellent, Brodo soup was bland, Sausage and Cabbage dish was excellent, Bolognaise was excellent , Vongole was excellent.

Server forgot to bring butter with the bread.

The wanna be mafioso's were out in full force, it was quite entertaining to watch how the old school get's it done!

I would go back and recommend this restaurant.

It is a bit over-priced but isn't everything in Vegas!
yelp:train:185709.para:
Service: Inconsistent at times, but improved throughout the night.
Food: Generally good, with some standout dishes and a few shortcomings.
Atmosphere: Exciting and enjoyable.
Cleanliness: Impeccable.
Music: Loud and not fitting the restaurant's vibe.
Mafioso-inspired element: Highly noticeable.

The initial service was somewhat tense but improved as the night progressed. The music volume was excessive and not suitable for the restaurant's theme. The venue is visually appealing, clean, and enjoyable. The appetizer was satisfactory, but the main dishes varied in quality, with some excellent choices and others lacking. The server neglected to provide butter with the bread. The presence of mafioso-inspired individuals was prominent and amusing. Despite the higher price point, I would return and suggest this eatery. It's a common occurrence in Vegas.

yelp:train:185996.orig: Never said I went on 8/2... Just posted my review that day. yelp:train:185996.para: I didn't mention my experience on 8/2, but I shared my review on that day. yelp:train:186014.orig:
Wow! I've never felt more like a burden to an operation. I've never posted a review (I usually just don't come back).

Tried to make some changes on a lunch order and you would think it was the craziest thing ever! ""Do you have any bread other than the honey whole wheat?"" ""No."" Can I switch the pretzel roll to the tuna sandwich?""  ""No we can't switch breads."" ""Why not?"" ""Those are the rules.""

I didn't want to mention that they serve panini as well (on honey whole wheat, I think not).

The baked ham and cheese sandwich (on a pretzel roll!) was pretty good although the side of garlic mash is pretty weird as a side.

C'mon guys.  Get a grip.  You have  ""Bakery"" in your name and I can't substitute bread on a sandwich?  You had more employees than customers this morning.   Think about changing your rules...
yelp:train:186014.para:
I've never experienced such a sense of being a nuisance to a business. I've never left feedback (I typically don't return).

I attempted to alter a lunch order, and it seemed like the most absurd request ever! "Do you have any other bread than the honey whole wheat?" "No." "Can I exchange the pretzel roll for the tuna sandwich?" "No, we can't change the bread." "Why is that?" "That's the policy."

I didn't feel the need to point out that they also offer panini (on honey whole wheat, I assume not).

The baked ham and cheese sandwich (on a pretzel roll) was quite decent, but the accompanying garlic mash as a side was rather unusual.

Come on, team.  Take a moment to reconsider your policies...

yelp:train:186213.orig:
I got introduced to Stinkweeds Records in Tempe while I was in college, and was blown away.  Up until that time, I was buying my music at the Memorial Union, and was blown away by their knowledge.

Stinkweeds is simply the best place to enjoy music.  As I got into records, and finding smaller, lesser known, indie artists, punk bands, and underground rappers, I discovered Stinkweeds.  They were able to discuss the artists that I liked, and recommend others.

Unfortunately, I don't buy much music any more and stick to the internet for most of my finds.  But every now and again, I will pop my head in to see what is going on.  Look at a few records, and talk a little underground music face to face.  

Unfortunately, record stores are going by the wayside, so support your local experts and keep them in business.  Yes, you might pay an extra couple of bucks for a cd then you would for the digital version online.  I know.  It's painful, but they appreciate it, and so will you.  Tell me the last time that someone at Best Buy or Barnes & Noble dropped a no-name band on you that you were impressed with.  

My guess is never.
yelp:train:186213.para:
During my university years, I encountered Stinkweeds Records in Tempe, which left me astonished. Prior to this, I frequented the Memorial Union for my music purchases, but their expertise was a revelation. 

Stinkweeds stands out as an unparalleled venue for music enjoyment. As I delved into records and unearthed obscure, indie, punk, and underground rap artists, I stumbled upon Stinkweeds. They adeptly engaged in conversations about my preferred artists and suggested others.

These days, I primarily rely on the internet for my music acquisitions, though I occasionally visit to browse records and engage in discussions about underground music.

Despite the decline of record stores, it's crucial to back local specialists to sustain their businesses. While it may cost a few extra dollars for a CD compared to its digital counterpart online, it's a small price to pay. These businesses value your support, and so do you.

I doubt you've ever been pleasantly surprised by a no-name band at a giant retailer like Best Buy or Barnes & Noble.

My assumption is that such an experience is rare.

yelp:train:186523.orig: Went to Brio with another couple last Saturday night for restaurant week. We were seated upon arrival which is always nice. Our server, Kelly, came to the table quickly and provided excellent service throughout the meal. I have been to Brio several times before and it was always a good experience and so was this time. All of us enjoyed our meals. The atmosphere is very nice too. Restaurant Week in regards to the price is an ok deal but nothing to go out of your way for.
yelp:train:186523.para:
Last Saturday, I joined a couple at Brio during the restaurant week. We were promptly seated upon arrival, a pleasant start. Our attentive server, Kelly, ensured a delightful dining experience with her prompt service. Having dined at Brio multiple times, I've consistently enjoyed myself, and this visit was no exception. The entire group relished their dishes. The ambiance adds to the charm. While the restaurant week offers reasonable pricing, it doesn't warrant special effort.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original meaning, topic, sentiment, emotion, and intent, but uses different words and sentence structures. The length is also roughly the same.)

yelp:train:186942.orig:
Ok, let me start off by saying, we didn't really eat here. We had reservations and we had every intention of eating here, but couldn't. Let me tell you why. It was LOUD. And I don't mean that kind of loud where you might have to speak a little louder to chat with your dinner mates. I mean the kind of loud where the music is at nightclub level and you have to yell to have a conversation. 

Now this might be a generation thing as my party of four are all in their 40s, but seriously, I just couldn't stay there. We asked the hostess for another recommendation and she immediately got us into Nove Italiano which was outstanding. They poured our drinks into plastic cups (so we could take them with us) and apologized - although they didn't owe us an apology...apparently we're just old! 

The girls at the hostess desk and at the bar were great. It wasn't them. It was us. I just hadn't read any other reviews that mentioned the noise level so I just wanted others to be aware.
yelp:train:186942.para: We didn't actually dine at this location, despite having reservations and the desire to do so. The reason for our departure was the excessive noise level, not the kind that necessitates raising your voice to converse with companions, but rather akin to a nightclub's volume. This might be a generational issue, as my group of four, all in their 40s, found it unbearable. We requested a different suggestion from the hostess, who promptly directed us to Nove Italiano, a place that exceeded our expectations. They served our beverages in plastic cups for convenience and offered an apology, though it wasn't due to any obligation on their part. The staff at the hostess desk and bar were commendable, but the issue was ours. I wanted to inform others about the noise level, as it wasn't highlighted in any other reviews.

yelp:train:187045.orig: N9NE was the place to be 5 years ago, let alone 10. It felt like a shell of its former self tonight. Half full on a Friday night, the magic is gone. Prices have gone up over the years, don't mind paying for solid cuisine but $59 for fatty lamb chops, no thanks. Staff worked hard and meant well, but the sizzle is out of this steak.
yelp:train:187045.para: Five years back, N9NE was a bustling hub, even more so a decade ago. Tonight, it's a mere shadow of its past glory. On a Friday evening, the enchantment has faded. While the cost has risen, I'm willing to invest in quality food, but $59 for greasy lamb chops is unacceptable. The staff put in effort and had good intentions, but the steak lacks its former appeal.

yelp:train:187051.orig: The food at this steakhouse was amazing and the service was also very good. I give it 4 stars because it's located in the Palms which, maybe it was just the weekend I went, does not have the same appeal it used to. The restaurant was not very crowded and the casino outside was basically empty. So while the food was fantastic, the trip over to the Palms seemed like a waste. I probably wouldn't take the cab ride over there again.
yelp:train:187051.para: The cuisine at this steakhouse was exceptional and the staff provided excellent service, earning it 4 stars. However, the location in the Palms, perhaps due to my visit during the weekend, lacked its former allure. The establishment was not bustling, and the adjacent casino was largely vacant. Despite the outstanding food, the journey to the Palms felt unnecessary, and I doubt I would opt for the taxi ride again.

yelp:train:187056.orig: We started going here for my daughters 21st bday and have been coming back last 7 years on our trips to vegas. I love this place everything is cool. Love the atmosphere steaks are yummy. desserts are great. Had one bad experience with a tasting menu they tried Christmas 2012 but just learned to stick with their awesome steaks. Service always good.
yelp:train:187056.para: Our family began frequenting this spot for my daughters' 21st birthday, and we've returned annually for the past seven years during our visits to Las Vegas. I adore this location, with its cool vibe. The ambiance and the delicious steaks are exceptional. The desserts are also impressive. We had a negative encounter with a tasting menu during Christmas 2012, but we've since decided to consistently enjoy their fantastic steaks. The service has always been commendable.

yelp:train:187120.orig:
Haven't been back to this place for at least 10 years, so much has changed! They used to give a tour of  Coca Cola's history and how it came to become so popular, but it is no longer there :( The lady told me it is not just a retail store.. Booo! 

One neat thing was being greeted by the live Coke Polar Bear. The photographer will take a picture with your own camera as well as take a ""Professional"" photo of you and whoever else you're with. We ended up buying the photo, because it was so darn hilarious when the Coca Cola bear bit my friend in the head (in a playful way of course). 

They do offer a Taste from around the World ($8), which is 16 small cups of different Coca Cola products from around the world. I must say, some of the samples tasted like mouthwash and some others tasted like bitter sprite.. Haha, so glad we live here in the US I guess :) 

All in all, a good place to visit when you want a break from the Casino and partying. It's right across the street from the Monte Carlo and a short walking distance from the Aria and the Bellagio.
yelp:train:187120.para:
After a decade, this location has undergone significant transformations, leaving behind its former offerings. The guided journey through Coca Cola's evolution and its rise in popularity is no longer available, which is disappointing. The establishment is more than just a retail outlet, as the informant pointed out with a hint of dismay. 

A memorable aspect was the encounter with the live Coke Polar Bear, which allowed for personalized photography with your device and a humorous professional shot, resulting in us purchasing the latter. The bear playfully nipped my companion's head, adding to the amusement. 

They provide a 'Taste from around the World' experience for $8, featuring 16 miniature cups of various Coca Cola flavors from across the globe. Some samples had a mouthwash-like flavor, while others were bitter like sprite, but we found it amusing. It's a relief to reside in the US, as it's a convenient location for a respite from the casino and revelry. It's conveniently situated next to Monte Carlo and a brief walk from the Aria and Bellagio.

yelp:train:187200.orig: I am a fan of this place, though the last time the wings were anemic, but the boneless ones were pretty good.  Love the Coke super soda machine.  The only real issue I have are the fries.  They put something on them that makes them sweet and they just don't taste rift.
yelp:train:187200.para: I appreciate this location, despite the wings being lackluster during my previous visit, however, the unbreaded varieties were commendable. I have a fondness for the Coke extra-large soda dispenser. The primary concern for me is the fries; they're coated with a sweet substance that detracts from their natural flavor.

yelp:train:187950.orig: Best pizza in Vegas. Great atmosphere too! Also seeing true italians who were there for a long time enjoying their food and their Italian beers has to mean that it must taste like original Italian made pizza. The pizza defenetly tastes like no other pizza I've had before. My girlfriend has been to Italy and she says that it tastes just like it did in Italy. The service was good too. We can't wait to go back again.
yelp:train:187950.para: The finest pizza in Las Vegas, complemented by a delightful ambiance. Observing authentic Italians relishing their meals and traditional Italian beers suggests the pizza's authentic Italian flavor. This pizza undeniably stands out from any I've tasted before. My partner, who has visited Italy, confirms the pizza's authentic Italian taste. The service was commendable as well. We eagerly anticipate returning.

yelp:train:188084.orig: Natalia was great.She is the restaurant manager and there was a problem with the ordering of the kids meals. We we're told the kids meals were drink, pizza and desert. When the waitress came back after we ate  she said sorry there is no more left for desert. She said sorry nothing we can do. But then Natalia came to the table and took care of the kids meals and said sorry for the inconvenience. I would of never gone back to there if it wasn't for Vanessa the waitress and natalia doing what they did and taking care of us. Food was awesome also.
yelp:train:188084.para: Natalia excelled in her role as the restaurant manager when an issue arose with the children's meal orders. Initially, the kids' meals consisted of drinks, pizza, and dessert. Upon returning after the meal, the waitress apologized for the lack of dessert and admitted there was nothing more to be done. However, Natalia intervened, rectified the children's meals, and expressed regret for the inconvenience caused. The quality of the food also impressed us. We would have refrained from returning to the restaurant if not for Natalia and Vanessa's exceptional service and care.

yelp:train:188122.orig: I know I know. The rule of thumb is that cool people have dogs. Well, I'm pretty cool. But I am also just a me. And I also have a job. And I also volunteer. Which means I also don't have the time a dog deserves. So instead I have cat dogs. They may look like cats, but please don't let that fool you. I have dogs that use a litter box and that can jump fences. And that fetch. And that always want to play. \n\nI also have cats that can find nearly nothing of interest in wag n' wash. Even though they mention having cat supplies. And even though there's a cat in the store. And even though my cats wag their tails.  Probably great for dogs. But not cats.
yelp:train:188122.para: I understand this. The general guideline suggests that laid-back individuals often own dogs. However, I consider myself quite laid-back too. But I am also myself, with a job and volunteer work. This implies I don't have the ample time a dog requires. Consequently, I opt for feline companions. They may resemble cats, but don't be deceived. I have dogs that utilize a litter box, leap over barriers, and enjoy fetching. They are always eager to engage in play. \n\nSimultaneously, I have cats that struggle to discover anything intriguing in wag n' wash. Despite their proclaimed cat essentials and the presence of a cat in the store, their tails wag, which is more dog-like behavior.

yelp:train:188767.orig: This place is OK, nothing special and if you come mid afternoon there is not much dim sum to choose from.  There are better places to get dim sum.
yelp:train:188767.para: The location is average, lacking any unique qualities, and if you visit in the early afternoon, the selection of dim sum is limited. There are superior spots for enjoying dim sum.

It was good, but not so memorable where it was worth that investment (at least not in my book). \n\nThe ambiance wasn't totally what I expected either. I was expecting so
yelp:train:189148.para:
Hoping to astonish my betrothed with a Las Vegas getaway, I meticulously arranged our itinerary, including reservations for our evening meals. We chose STRIPSTEAK and Bouchon for our primary courses, with STRIPSTEAK securing a prominent second spot in my preference. The cuisine was scrumptious, and the service impeccable -- there was no doubt about it. I savored the perfectly cooked tuna, while my betrothed relished the bone-in ribeye, appearing utterly content. We shared the bleu cheese scalloped potatoes as a side dish and indulged in the hamachi poppers, both of which were outstanding. It was enjoyable, but not so unforgettable that it justified the expense (at least in my perspective).

yelp:train:189647.orig: very very let down. service was super slow and food was garbage. I got the duck quesadilla thinking it was going to be great because of the reviews and everything but I was sadly mistaken. Perhaps I should have gotten the crispy quesadilla instead of the large soft one and there is where I went wrong. But in any case, the soft one is cut up and served covered in sauce and salad. So you have to eat it with a knife and fork. I am guessing my order was done and sitting for a while in the kitchen while they were finishing the other plates because it was super super soggy and had absolutely no other texture. It was super salty and very one-note. So maybe I was supposed to order the crispy small quesadilla or maybe this was a fluke on their part but I am not going back because of it.
yelp:train:189647.para: Extremely disappointed with the experience. The service was painfully slow and the food quality was subpar. I anticipated a delightful duck quesadilla based on positive reviews, but my expectations were misguided. Perhaps opting for the smaller, crispy version would have been wiser than the large, soft one, which turned out to be my error. Regardless, the soft quesadilla was served with sauce and salad, necessitating the use of utensils. I suspect my order lingered in the kitchen, resulting in an overly soggy texture with a lack of variety in taste. It was excessively salty and monotonous. Consequently, I won't be returning due to this unsatisfactory experience.

yelp:train:189824.para:

When we highlighted this, they mentioned it was the regular amount, so we requested more Raita, which was no issue. We also ordered desserts, but they were underwhelming as well. Additionally, the final bill included items we hadn't ordered, but fortunately, my friend noticed and when he brought it to the manager's attention, there was no remorse or acknowledgment of the error. 

Despite this, the following day we found a Groupon deal and decided to give it another try, opting for their Buffet. We suggested sitting at two separate tables, but the waiter reassured us it was fine and directed us to a spacious table. yelp:train:190245.orig:
When passing through Phoenix last week, we had dinner here on the recommendation of Yelp. Who knew you could get good British pasties in Tempe?

The pasties themselves were incredible. I had the bangers and mash, the wife had the chicken tikka masala. We loved each of them, and believe me that one pasty is enough to satisfy a big appetite.

We were not as huge fans of the fries/chips. Also, the waitress really had no idea about any of the beers on the menu. Since I am not knowledgable about British beer, this led me to order something I didn't really care for. Next time (oh yes, there will be a next time) I'll stick with the Lagunitas IPA.
yelp:train:190245.para: During our recent visit to Phoenix, we dined at this establishment based on a Yelp suggestion. We were pleasantly surprised to find excellent British pasties in Tempe. The pasties were outstanding, with my choice of bangers and mash and my wife's chicken tikka masala both being delicious. One pasty was more than enough to quell our substantial hunger. However, we were less impressed with the fries/chips. The waitress seemed unfamiliar with the beer selection, which resulted in me ordering a beer I wasn't particularly fond of. For our future visits, I plan to opt for the Lagunitas IPA.

We sat down looked at the menu, ordered some drinks and if you're like me and hate tea and sodas you are screwed and will have to suffer with disgusting tasting water. For our main we both had ramen with sushi on the side. I had tonkotsu with California rolls and I have never eaten ramen and sushi so bad. The broth was REALLY salty, the noodles and the pork were super chewy and the Cali rolls tasted so plain. Same with his meal might I add. Also, total mood killer! The music. It might just be me but I don't want to hear \""what does the fox say\"" on full blast while I'm eating my dinner... Last thing (I promise) when we left it was about half an hour till closing and I had noticed some of the chefs go out front. To get some fresh a
yelp:train:190552.para: My initial visit to this eatery will undoubtedly be my final one. I entered with optimistic anticipation based on positive Yelp reviews. Unfortunately, upon arriving an hour and a half before closing time, we were informed that AYCE was not an option. We perused the menu, placed some drink orders, and for those averse to tea and sodas like myself, it was a disappointing experience with unsavory-tasting water. Moreover, our appetizers consisted of gyoza that initially seemed soy sauce-infused but were actually vinegar-flavored. Our main course featured ramen with sushi on the side. I opted for tonkotsu with California rolls, but it was a regrettable culinary experience as the broth was excessively salty, the noodles and pork were overly chewy, and the California rolls were bland. My companion's meal was equally unsatisfactory. The music selection was also a significant detractor, with the repetitive lyrics of "what does the fox say" being particularly jarring during our meal. As we were leaving, it was nearly closing time, and I observed chefs exiting the premises, suggesting a lack of freshness.

yelp:train:191275.para:

yelp:train:191315.orig:
I use to love Kona Grill!  We decided to go today for Mother's Day and I thought it would be hit, but boy was I wrong!!  The place was not busy. The bar - YES, but the restaurant..not so much.  We ordered the calamari and it was horrible!!! The calamari had no meat! It seemed like they scraped off the bottom of the fryer and served it.  I thought it had to get better, but then we ordered our entree.  We ordered the Hawaiian Ribeye and I don't even think it was ribeye! I think a porterhouse or something, but definitely not a ribeye.  We also ordered a couple rolls of sushi which weren't bad, but my whole dining experience was already ruined.  My mom ordered their asian salad and she said it was too sweet.  The whole experience was horrible.  Our server forgot to give us soy sauce for our sushit and we waited quite a bit to get it. 

Towards the end of the meal I'm thinking I just wasted $100 on garbage!

I'm going to take the survey tomorrow and hopefully it will change something. I really liked Kona Grill and I would like to return, but based on my last visit - I doubt it.

It may just be a hit or miss kind of thing and I hope that others don't have the same dining experience
yelp:train:191315.para: Previously, I adored Kona Grill, but our Mother's Day visit left me disappointed. The venue was surprisingly quiet, with the bar bustling but the dining area lacking. Our calamari dish was a disaster, devoid of meat, as if it was merely fried scraps. I anticipated improvement with our main course, but the Hawaiian Ribeye was far from what I expected, more akin to a porterhouse. The sushi rolls were passable, but the overall experience was tainted. My mother's Asian salad was overly sweet, further marring the meal. I felt I'd squandered $100 on subpar food. I'll submit a survey tomorrow, hoping for a change. Despite my fondness for Kona Grill, I'm hesitant to return after this unsatisfactory visit. I hope others have better experiences. It seems like Kona Grill's quality might be inconsistent.

yelp:train:191598.orig: What is there to say about Nothing Bundt Cakes that hasn't been said a million times before. These are some of the best tasting cakes I've had and they come at a fairly decent price considering the quality of ingredients, packaging, etc. This was my first time actually going into the shop although I've had the cakes several times. I was surprised to see it so busy 30 minutes before closing. Even saw Scotty Nguyen (professional poker star) carrying out 3 cakes as he left. Staff was friendly and they had a small but decent selection of cakes in the display.\n\nRed Velvet, Marble and Chocolate Chocolate Chip all left with me and I honestly can't decide which is my favorite. They are all so delicious. While it may not be in budget for your \""everyday\"" cake, it is most certainly worth it for any special occasion. Now that I live only few minutes away, I'm sure I'll be back more often.
yelp:train:191598.para: Numerous opinions have already been shared about Nothing Bundt Cakes, but here's my take: The cakes I've tasted are exceptional, offering great value for money when considering the ingredients and packaging. This was my inaugural visit to the store, despite having sampled their cakes before. I was astonished by the bustling atmosphere just half an hour before the shop closed. Notably, I observed Scotty Nguyen, a renowned poker player, departing with three cakes. The staff exuded warmth and the display offered a modest yet commendable variety of cakes. I departed with Red Velvet, Marble, and Chocolate Chocolate Chip cakes, each equally delectable. While it may not be a regular indulgence, it's undeniably perfect for special events. Living just a few minutes away now, I anticipate frequent visits.

yelp:train:191606.orig: Never again. I absolutely LOVE Thai and was thrilled to find a local spot not too far from my new condo... however,  my excitement was short lived. We ordered crab rangoons, chicken satay, green beef curry and shrimp pad thai... where do I even start?!! First off, the crab rangoons had no undetectable crab and only a hint of cream cheese, the chicken satay was flavorless and tough, the beef curry was an odd consistency with a sad amount of meat and to top off this unfortunate meal, the shrimp on the pad thai was DISGUSTING! It tasted muddy and had absolutely NO seasoning. I tried to explain to the server about the flavor of the shrimp and she wanted to stand there and explain how the shrimp come frozen from the vendor... I could not care less where it came from lady IT'S GROSS! I kept telling her to have the cook make one yo taste and she just looked at me like no one was home. I honestly thought I was going to get sick from eating the one. I am totally bummed that I had such a horrible experience... the search for local Thai continues.
yelp:train:191606.para: I will never repeat this. I have a deep affection for Thai cuisine and was excited to discover a nearby restaurant near my new apartment... but my joy was quickly diminished. We ordered crab rangoons, chicken satay, green beef curry, and shrimp pad thai... where to begin?! To start, the crab rangoons lacked any discernible crab and merely had a slight cream cheese presence, the chicken satay was bland and chewy, the beef curry had an unusual texture with a disappointing quantity of meat, and to exacerbate this disappointing meal, the shrimp on the pad thai was absolutely revolting! It had a murky taste and was completely devoid of seasoning. I attempted to convey my concerns to the server, who insisted on explaining the shrimp's origin from the supplier... I couldn't be bothered by its origin, it was revolting! I kept urging her to have the chef taste it, but she just stared at me as if I was invisible. I genuinely feared I might fall ill from the shrimp. I am profoundly disheartened by this terrible dining experience and will continue my quest for local Thai cuisine.

yelp:train:192593.orig:

yelp:train:192593.para:

yelp:train:192704.orig: The food here was great! Wish there was more indoor seating, but the seating both indoor and outside is nice, live music sometimes, nice decor. yelp:train:192704.para: The cuisine offered was exceptional! I'd like more interior dining options, but the combination of interior and exterior seating is pleasing, with occasional live performances and appealing decor. yelp:train:194183.orig: Should've just stopped at McDonald's. SLOW service and unfriendly waitress. Any request was answered with a sour look. Took so long for the food to come and it was not anything special. The table next to us was sitting with dirty plates and old food the entire time we were here. Will not go back.
yelp:train:194183.para: Preferring to have ended at McDonald's, the place was marred by sluggish service and a surly server. Every inquiry was met with a grimace. The wait for our meal was excessively long, and the food failed to impress. The adjacent table was littered with unwashed dishes and stale remnants throughout our visit. I'm certain I won't return.

yelp:train:194341.orig: this place is always on our list of things to do downtown(where the actions at) ...it is a small casino packed with action...a good scene to observe...tourists and locals, yukkin it up, getting hopped up on cheap drinks...(football beers and high octane yards) and great snacks....live a little and have the deep fried oreos,twinkies and one of several hot dog variations.....nothing stuffy about this place....ive seen pimps, ho's, bro's and an assortment of drunks...all getting along....everyone needs a little mermaid in there life!
yelp:train:194341.para: This spot consistently appears on our must-visit downtown agenda, where the vibrant activities unfold...it's a compact casino brimming with excitement...an ideal location to witness the lively interactions between tourists and residents, enjoying affordable beverages like football beers and high-energy snacks...indulge in some fun with deep-fried treats like oreos, twinkies, and various hot dog styles...there's no pretentious atmosphere here...I've encountered a diverse mix of individuals including pimps, ho's, bro's, and a variety of inebriated folks, all coexisting harmoniously...everyone could use a touch of merriment in their lives.

yelp:train:194411.orig: We been going to Vegas since 1978 an this is the first year to stay downtown, easy walking everywhere friendly people an found the Mermaid Casino by accident, wow what a great place to have relaxing fun, we spend 4 nights there playing the slots an the video poker, didn't win a lot but we won every night, Connie was our main waitress an she took very good care of my wife an I with a smile on her face all night, she would give us a quick story on the downtown district an was always there with fresh drink for us even when we walked in the door, Mermaids will always be our gaming place from here on out, all the girls working there were very nice to us, its a lot bigger inside that it looks so give it a try one evening an you wont be sorry. Thank You Connie for making us feel at home an for your kindness, we will be back.   Bill & Ellen Woods
yelp:train:194411.para: Since 1978, we've frequented Las Vegas and this marks the first time we've chosen to stay in the downtown area. The ease of strolling around, the warmth of the locals, and the serendipitous discovery of the Mermaid Casino have made it an ideal spot for unwinding. Despite not winning big, we managed to secure a win each night, thanks to Connie, our dedicated waitress, who consistently provided excellent service with a cheerful disposition. Her engaging tales about the downtown area and her unwavering commitment to refreshing us with drinks, even upon arrival, have endeared us to this establishment. Mermaid Casino will be our go-to gaming destination henceforth. The staff, particularly the women, were incredibly hospitable towards us. We highly recommend giving it a shot for an enjoyable evening, and we'll certainly return. Our gratitude goes to Connie for her hospitality and kindness, which made us feel right at home. Bill & Ellen Woods.

yelp:train:194848.orig:
I found this place about a year ago and it is the best sushi I have had in Vegas, which I know is a biiiiiiig statement. 

Over the past 10 years or so I have eaten at dozens of sushi restaurants in this town (on the strip as well) and I can't say I have enjoyed any as much as this place. The fish is stellar, the customer service is amazing, and the rolls are innovative and flavorful.

What brought me back is the fact that I can easily eat $100 worth of sushi in one sitting. I prefer all-yo-can-eat venues because frankly, it's cheaper. Most of the time you find yourself at one of these places, the rolls are basic and not very good, or you are prohibited from ordering any of the ""good"" rolls. Not this place!!! If it is on the menu, you can order it (and as much as you like). Any app, roll, sashimi, nigiri; it's all fair game. The funny thing is the place is almost always empty! It's a really nice place right next door to Shakespeare's (a trendy bar). I am positive that this is just a secret among those who live in Green Valley. This place is a must-go for any Vegas sushi-addict.
yelp:train:194848.para:
About a year back, I stumbled upon this spot and it stands out as the top-notch sushi experience in Vegas, a claim I'm fully aware is quite bold. 

In the span of roughly a decade, I've sampled sushi at numerous establishments along the strip, yet none have surpassed this particular venue. The quality of the fish is exceptional, the service is outstanding, and the rolls are both creative and tasty. 

The reason I keep returning is the convenience of indulging in a $100 sushi feast in one go. I favor establishments that allow unlimited consumption as it's more cost-effective. Typically, other places offer subpar rolls or restrict orders of their premium selections. Not here! The menu is open for any item, from appetizers to sashimi, nigiri, and more. It's peculiar that the place is usually devoid of patrons. Located adjacent to the trendy Shakespeare's, I'm convinced it's a well-kept secret among Green Valley residents. For any sushi enthusiast in Vegas, this place is a non-negotiable destination.

yelp:train:195086.orig:

Also nice on the appetizer menu is a mini cuban sandwich when you just can't handle the big one. My kids always order it as the kids menu only has ham and cheese. yelp:train:196005.para: Taco Bell stands firm, consistently delivering satisfaction. And regarding health concerns, they provide lettuce, tomato, and cheese without any confirmed links to cancer. Taco Bell remains the go-to choice for a late-night meal!

yelp:train:196120.orig:
The rooms are clean and the service is decent, but the walls are thin enough to follow the television programming in the room on one side of your own while simultaneously enjoying the ecstatic moans and mattress squeaking from your neighbors on the other side. Thankfully the rooms come equipped with a refridgerator, and the constant grumbling  of the ancient cooling unit will do its best to drown out the ruckus in the adjacent rooms. If you're not the type of person who is lulled to sleep by the groan of struggling machinery, unplugging it will only give you the peace and quiet necessary to truly focus on the aforementioned activities of your neighbors.

If you're checking in here because it's stumbling distance from the establishment next door with women in various states of undress displaying their vertical barre workouts, then this place is for you, and you'll no doubt be either too drunk or too busy to mind the noises coming from the adjacent rooms or your ailing fridge.

However, if you're interested in an uninterrupted night of sleep, you'd best look elsewhere. Weeknights or weekends, the pattern is the same. Checking in here is like unwittingly signing a release to take
yelp:train:196120.para:
The rooms maintain cleanliness and offer satisfactory service, yet the walls are so thin that you can hear the TV broadcasts from one side while also being subjected to the boisterous sounds of your neighbors' mattress movements on the other. Fortunately, each room includes a refrigerator, which, despite its outdated cooling system, attempts to muffle the disturbances from nearby rooms. For those who find the hum of malfunctioning machinery soothing, disconnecting it may provide the silence needed to concentrate on the activities of your neighbors.

If your reason for staying is due to its proximity to a neighboring establishment where women are showcasing their vertical barre exercises, this place may suit you, especially if you're either inebriated or preoccupied, rendering you oblivious to the noises from the adjacent rooms or your malfunctioning fridge.

Nonetheless, for a peaceful night's sleep, it's advisable to seek accommodations elsewhere. The disturbance pattern remains consistent on weekdays and weekends. Opting to stay here is akin to unknowingly agreeing to endure the noise and disruptions.

yelp:train:197044.orig: this is a nice hotel that's located in a good spot in scottsdale as it is right by a stop for the free trolley which is decent but has some interesting drivers but i digress.  the lobby and the rest of interior has a very ultra contemporary feel to it.  the rooms are cool and the bathrooms are unique.  the pool area is really nice and the i don't if it was that particular day or not but the temperature was perfect.  the water was a bit salty but that's all good.
yelp:train:197044.para: This hotel in Scottsdale boasts a prime location, conveniently situated near a free trolley stop with intriguing conductors. The interior, including the lobby, exudes a modern and ultra-contemporary vibe. The accommodations are refreshingly cool, and the bathrooms stand out with their distinctiveness. The pool area impresses with its pleasantness, and even though the water's salinity might be slightly high, it's a minor detail. The temperature on that day was ideal.

yelp:train:197370.orig:

yelp:train:197496.orig:

I stopped in yesterday to see laminate hardwood flooring as well as vinyl planks and Associate Chris was very knowledgeable and helpful.  I had also taken a look at the flooring at Lowe's, but I was so impressed with the help I had been given here that I drove twice as far to buy here from Chris.

Chris wasn't on duty when I arrived, but Associate Jamie was also friendly & able to answer my remaining questions as I decided what to buy.  So far, we're at 5 Stars!

THEN, I got up to the checkout & THEY TRIED TO OVERCHARGE ME!  As a matter of policy, any business that cheats me on the money gets ONE STAR & I never return.  The flooring was clearly priced at $1.59/sq. ft. at the display & it rang up at $1.79.  Now this wasn't the fault of the cashier, but then she wanted to make it ""iffy"" whether or not I would get it at the advertised price.  NO IT ISN'T!

Ok, so after a few minutes of delay & hassle I left with my flooring at the posted price.  The service was so good from both Chris & Jamie that they saved this Home Depot from getting a vote to send it to Yelp 1-Sta
yelp:train:197496.para:
My initial experience with purchasing new flooring to replace outdated tiles in the living room was exceptional. I visited yesterday to examine laminate hardwood flooring and vinyl planks, where Associate Chris demonstrated great expertise and assistance. Although I had also considered options at Lowe's, the superior service I received here prompted me to drive twice the distance to make this purchase from Chris.

When Chris was unavailable upon my arrival, Associate Jamie stepped in, displaying a warm and helpful demeanor while addressing my remaining queries as I made my selection. Thus far, I'm giving this a 5-star rating.

However, I encountered an issue at the checkout when they attempted to charge me more than the displayed price of $1.59/sq. ft. for the flooring. This was not the cashier's fault, but they tried to create uncertainty about the advertised price. I firmly believe that the price should remain as advertised.

After some delay and frustration, I managed to leave with the flooring at the correct price. The outstanding service provided by both Chris and Jamie prevented this Home Depot from receiving a negative rating on Yelp.

yelp:train:197542.orig: Not only is this an awesome theme restaurant, it's also one of the Best Italian food in the Country. The entire atmosphere is a great place to take friends or even on a romantic date. The singer who does Frank Sinatra is FANTASTIC!!!!!  Order the Meatballs to start and you will be hooked. The bread, Butter, Pasta, Drinks, I could go on and on. You should be privileged to even get to eat at Capo's. This is a Legit Wise guy place. If your stuffy or have a stick up your ass or drink your wine with your pinkie finger out, or  you don't like the Italian attitude stay home or go to Wolfgang pucks. hahahaha
yelp:train:197542.para: This exceptional dining establishment not only offers an impressive theme but also stands out as one of the top Italian cuisine options nationwide. It's an ideal spot for gathering with friends or enjoying a date with a romantic touch. The Frank Sinatra-inspired singer's performance is truly remarkable. Begin your meal with the delectable Meatballs and you'll be captivated. From the bread and butter to the pasta and drinks, the culinary experience is extensive. It's an honor to dine here at Capo's, a place of genuine wisdom. For those who prefer a more conventional dining experience, or who don't appreciate the Italian flair, there are other options like Wolfgang Puck. Laughter ensues!

yelp:train:197805.orig:

yelp:train:198110.orig:
Been coming to Jason's since they had a location across the street from PV Mall back in the early 90's. Their restaurants are always pretty decent and the food is tasty good. This location on Shea appears to have had a remodel since we were here last time and the inside looks really nice.

The menu has changed a bit over the years and is smaller than I remember. They used to have a larger selection of stuffed potatoes and now only have a few. My favorite was a smokey BBQ Beef stuffed potato with tons of other goodies. I think you could even build your own at one time.

The wife and I usually go with the famous New Orleans 9"" FULL size Ham and Salami Muffaletta. It is hard to resist some additional Olive spread on the side and a little hot sauce to kick things up a notch. The sandwich is giant and we normally have a good portion to bring home for a snack later.

There are plenty of other options that are also fresh and tasty. Cool all you can eat Salad Bar to indulge yourself. Yummy Soups, maybe a bowl of Chili, as well as Wraps and Pasta if you desire. They also have a nice Kid's menu with the typical favorites for the little ones.

Friendly service and a casually comfort
yelp:train:198110.para:
Since the early '90s, we've frequented Jason's, located adjacent to PV Mall. Their dining establishments consistently offer satisfying fare, with flavorful dishes. The Shea branch seems to have undergone a recent renovation, presenting an impressively refined interior.

Over time, the menu has evolved, now featuring a more concise array of items. Notably, the once abundant selection of stuffed potatoes has been reduced to a few options. Among them, a smoky BBQ Beef stuffed potato, laden with various delicacies, remains a personal favorite. Previously, customers could customize their own.

Our regular choice is the renowned New Orleans 9" FULL size Ham and Salami Muffaletta. The temptation to add extra Olive spread and a dash of hot sauce is irresistible. This substantial sandwich often leaves us with enough to enjoy as a snack later.

A variety of other fresh and delectable choices are available, including a generous Salad Bar, delightful Soups, a bowl of Chili, and options like Wraps and Pasta. A kid-friendly menu also caters to the younger crowd with their preferred treats.

The staff consistently provides warm and inviting service in a laid-back atmosphere.

yelp:train:200714.para: Oysters, oysters, oysters.\n\nI'm not sure I'd find anything else more appealing here...the Penazzi offers oysters at a fantastic rate. yelp:train:201142.orig: Food is not very good, atmosphere isn't either. Lots of TVs is all they have going for them.
yelp:train:201142.para: The quality of the cuisine and ambiance are subpar, with the only redeeming factor being the abundance of televisions available.

yelp:train:201248.orig:
Sorry to be the bearer of bad news, but I went here to get a rejuvenating yummy bowl of goodness, which I could eat every day, and my hopes were thwarted.

I got about 1/2 way though my rare beef & flank Pho, when I was overcome with a deathly feeling.  My poor colleague said I turned pale white and looked awful.  I broke into a sweat and quickly paid our bill, dropped him off at work, and headed home.  

Thank goodness I live nearby.  I barely got through the front door before all systems went full reverse.  

With all the options out there, I think I'll have to scratch this place of my list.  Sorry :(  I had such high hopes.
yelp:train:201248.para:
Apologies for delivering unfavorable news, but my quest for a delightful, nourishing bowl of sustenance, which I would relish daily, was disappointed.

As I was halfway through my infrequent beef & flank Pho, I was struck by a severe illness. My coworker observed my pallor and distress. I broke out in perspiration and hastily settled the bill, escorted him to his job, and rushed back home.

I'm relieved to reside close by. I barely made it home before everything reversed. 

Considering the plethora of choices available, I'll have to remove this establishment from my list. I'm disheartened :( I had lofty expectations.

yelp:train:201651.orig: Love this place! All of their breakfast entrees are solid across the board - you really cant wrong ordering anything. yelp:train:201651.para: This location is fantastic! Their breakfast options are consistently excellent - there's no risk in trying any dish. Like any top-notch breakfast establishment, arriving early is recommended to dodge the crowds, and some patience may be required.

yelp:train:201699.orig: Decent all you can eat but a bit dirty inside. I'd rather eat at the Denny's next door then risk getting sick here again. Yes, I said again. yelp:train:201711.para: I've frequented this shop numerous times in search of the perfect item for my apartment. yelp:train:202181.para:
I never imagined I'd find myself at The Palms Hotel & Casino, where The Pearl was located and The Cure was performing. I reluctantly stayed at a small indoor bar while waiting for my identification. Surprisingly, a woman in her 50s recognized me, referring to me as "thick." 

'Really?'

"'Thick, huh? Like, you've got some curves, girl! Are you Latino or Mexican? Because you folks are definitely rocking some curves!"

'So, you're implying I'm overweight?'

"No, no, girl! Thick is a good thing. Brotherhood loves thickness!"

My tickets were situated in the Mezzanine section, three rows from the FOH (front of house)...right in the middle. The view was fantastic, the sound was great, and the seating was comfortable. The bar served a comprehensive menu, albeit at exorbitant prices. 

I appreciated the venue's size.
