I had a great time at this resturant on Pittsburgh light up night thanks to the excellent service I received. The decor is bright and colorful and the open kitchen is a real show. The food for the most part was really good. The problem was the items that were good were really good and bursting with flavor but they really over shadowed items that were less flavorful.  We made the mistake of ordering some  of the ""light up night special tapas"" that were put to shame by the rest of the meal. I was in a group of 4 at happy hour which allowed us to try many different tapas. 

We had 2 preparations of sushi,  the traditional preparation with shrimp was fantastic and fresh tasting while the avocado with corn prep paired with salmon was good but not as good as traditional.

We also had the beef brisket tacos and the salmon tacos, the beef tacos were very good with flavorful tender beef  but the salmon tacos which were a ""Light Up Nite special"" were not very flavorful at all and the fish, while cooked well was not seasoned at all. It was basically a small piece of fish on a tortilla.

We tried the Chicken quesadillas and Vegatarian tostada both very good with creamy melted the
yelp:train:233721.para:
I thoroughly enjoyed my dining experience at this Pittsburgh-themed restaurant during the light up night, largely due to the outstanding service provided. The ambiance is vibrant and full of color, and the visible kitchen adds to the spectacle. The majority of the dishes were delicious, although the standout flavors sometimes overshadowed the less intense ones. We regrettably ordered some of the "light up night special tapas," which were eclipsed by the rest of the meal. Dining with a group of four during happy hour gave us the opportunity to sample various tapas.

We sampled two sushi preparations, with the classic shrimp version being exceptional and refreshingly tasty, while the avocado and corn combination with salmon was satisfactory but didn't quite match the traditional.

We also sampled the beef brisket tacos, which were flavorful and tender, and the salmon tacos, a "Light Up Nite special," which unfortunately lacked flavor and were essentially a small piece of fish on a tortilla.

We tried the Chicken quesadillas and Vegetarian tostada, both of which were excellent, featuring creamy, melted cheese.

yelp:train:233946.orig: So the wife and I eat here at least every other week. She likes the omelettes and I usually get the nova and bagel. She thinks the omelettes are light and fluffy and this is the only place I've found with decent lox and bagels. This last experience might just have changed our opinion though. I ordered the corned beef sandwich, which in the past has been good, and she got her usual. Her omelette came out burnt and tough, and my corned beef was entirely inedible, it was dry, cold and flavorless. I never knew  corned beef could be that bad. The waiter made himself scarce after dropping the food. And the cashier made a joke when she asked me how everything was and I replied that it was horrible. When I said no i was serious that it was horrible, she said \""ok, sorry.\"" Completely uninterested in what was wrong or how they could improve it.\n\nWhile I've always thought this was the best deli food in town, that really has been mostly due to a lack of good competition. With the lack of concern I saw with customer satisfaction, though I would have to say it wouldn't take much competition to get me to go somewhere new.
yelp:train:233946.para:
The husband and wife dine here at least biweekly. She enjoys the omelettes and I typically opt for the nova and bagel. She believes the omelettes are airy and light, and this is the only establishment I've discovered with satisfactory lox and bagels. However, our recent visit might have altered our views. I ordered the corned beef sandwich, which has been satisfactory before, and she chose her regular. Her omelette was overcooked and tough, and my corned beef was unpalatable, dry, and lacking in taste. I was shocked to find corned beef could be so poor. The server avoided the scene after the mishap with the food. The cashier joked when I expressed my dissatisfaction, and when I clarified that I was genuinely upset, she apologized. She showed no interest in addressing the issues or suggesting improvements.

Despite my previous belief that this was the finest deli food in the area, that was mostly due to the absence of better options. The apparent disregard for customer satisfaction, however, would likely sway me to try a new place if there was more competition.

yelp:train:234403.orig: I love this place. Great food, great coffee, great views, great prices. And I love that it's local. You've gotta check it out.
yelp:train:234403.para: This location is fantastic. It offers delicious cuisine, excellent coffee, stunning scenery, and affordable costs. Plus, its local charm is irresistible. Definitely worth exploring.

yelp:train:234813.orig:
Great place for good food at a decent price.

Servings are huge...if you are coming with only 1-2 people, you're best to just buy one entree or pasta plate and maybe an appetizer or dessert if you want to bring food home (or have extras).

Had the spicy chicken Rigatoni and it was excellent.  Tons of food and tons of flavor!

The bread/oil/vin they serve is excellent as well.  No idea why, but it is just delicious.

Also ordered the calamari but it wasn't earth shattering..I'd probably skip it next time.

Server was great and very helpful.  Atmosphere is very ""homey"" and has a classic feel.

Check it out if you are thinking Olive Garden for dinner.
yelp:train:234813.para:
Excellent dining spot offering tasty meals at reasonable prices.

Portions are generous...if dining solo, consider purchasing a main dish or pasta plate, and perhaps a starter or sweet treat for takeaway (or extra portions).

Enjoyed the spicy chicken Rigatoni, which was outstanding. Abundant in both quantity and taste!

The accompaniment of bread, oil, and vin is also top-notch. Its deliciousness is a mystery, but it's undeniably delightful.

Additionally, I tried the calamari, but it didn't quite impress. I'd likely forgo it in the future.

The service was commendable and very supportive. The ambiance exudes a cozy, traditional vibe.

Explore this place if you're contemplating Olive Garden for your evening meal.

yelp:train:235762.orig:
We have continued to order pizza from here & have been more than pleased every time. I also have a new favorite salad, the Domenica & their house dressing.. O.M.G! I even bought a bottle of it the last time we were there for dinner, SO good. Unfortunately it doesn't have a slow pour top so my 10 year old ended up pouring more than half of it on his salad one night :( I will gladly spring for another bottle though, even at $4.99!

The pizzas we have especially loved were the Modesto & the San Gennaro. We ordered the family platter of Chicken Parmigana one night & while it was a TON of food for the money ($35.95 for about 15-20 breasts in a foil tray covered with sauce & cheese.. ended up being enough for lunch & dinner for 3 days!) it wasn't the best Chicken Parmigana I've ever had & we will probably just stick to their pizza for the most part.   

Also, try their Spumoni Gelato sometime, you won't be disappointed!
yelp:train:235762.para:
We persist in placing pizza orders from this place and have consistently been delighted with each delivery. I've also discovered a new go-to salad, the Domenica, along with their homemade dressing, which I couldn't resist purchasing a bottle of during our last visit for a meal. Regrettably, the bottle lacks a slow pour feature, leading to my child accidentally spilling half of it on his salad one evening. Despite this, I'm willing to pay $4.99 for another bottle.

In particular, we've developed a fondness for the Modesto and San Gennaro pizzas. We once ordered a family-sized Chicken Parmigana platter for $35.95, which included around 15-20 chicken breasts in a foil tray with sauce and cheese. It was ample for three days' worth of lunches and dinners, but it didn't quite meet our expectations for the best Chicken Parmigana experience. Hence, we'll likely continue to favor their pizzas.

Additionally, we recommend giving their Spumoni Gelato a try, as it's sure to exceed your expectations.

yelp:train:235887.orig:
I haven't been to Ginseng Korean BBQ II for a long time.  When there were not many Korean restaurants in Vegas, I used to take my friends or visitors to this place because they were staying one of the hotels on the strip and it was very convenient for them to come to have a warm meal after a show or shopping.  After having too much of buffet food, they always wanted to have some Korean food on the last day of their departure.
But, it is still pricey and they don't do AYCE Korean BBQ.
My cousin was in town with her friends and she wanted to have a dinner at Ginseng II.  She said she really liked their food every time she was in Vegas to try Korean BBQ.  Since she leaves in Korea town in LA & I'm pretty sure that she must have tasted the greatest Korean BBQ in LA.  I was wondering why she wanted to try the food that she could get better ones in K-town?
I agreed to have a dinner with her at Ginseng II right after Christmas.  The place was pretty busy with all the tourists.  We all shared some of the dishes including Bibimbap, Kimchi Jjigae, Kalbi, and Chadolbaegi(brisket).  I was amazed that all the dishes we had that night were so delicious!  Especially, the Kimchi Jjigae was outs
yelp:train:235887.para:
I haven't visited Ginseng Korean BBQ II recently. When there were limited Korean dining options in Las Vegas, I frequently brought my companions or guests to this establishment due to its proximity to one of the strip's hotels, offering them a convenient spot to enjoy a warm meal post-entertainment or shopping. Despite the buffet overindulgence, they always craved Korean cuisine on their final day. However, the cost remains high, and they don't offer all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ.

My relative was in town with her pals, expressing her desire to dine at Ginseng II. She consistently praised their food whenever she visited Las Vegas for Korean BBQ experiences. Given her frequent visits to Korea Town in LA, it's likely she's had superior Korean BBQ there. I pondered why she wanted to sample the food she could potentially find better elsewhere.

We decided to have dinner at Ginseng II after the holiday season. The venue was bustling with tourists. We all enjoyed a variety of dishes, including Bibimbap, Kimchi Jjigae, Kalbi, and Chadolbaegi (brisket). I was impressed by the exceptional taste of all the dishes that night, particularly the Kimchi Jjigae.

yelp:train:235976.orig: Great food great service.  I have eaten at great restaurants all over the world and if I do say so myself, I am an excellent judge.  You won't be disappointed.  This is one of my favorites in Pittsburgh.  Prices very good for what you get.\n\nSteve
yelp:train:235976.para: Exceptional cuisine and service. I've dined at numerous top-tier eateries globally, and I consider myself a discerning critic. Rest assured, you'll be satisfied. Among my preferred spots in Pittsburgh, the value for money is impressive. - Steve

yelp:train:236098.orig: My boss told me to stop by this place to grab cupcakes for my coworkers birthday and I'm glad he did! I really like this place because you get to choose your own frosting & fillings for it. I don't really like desserts that are overly sweet and I felt like their cupcakes were just right. The cake had a hint of the flavor and it wasn't overly sweet so it went perfectly well with the frosting.
yelp:train:236098.para: My supervisor instructed me to visit this shop to pick up customized cupcakes for a colleague's birthday, and I'm delighted he suggested it! I appreciate this establishment as it allows you to select your preferred frosting and fillings. I tend to avoid excessively sugary desserts, and I found their cupcakes to be perfectly balanced in sweetness, complementing the frosting without being overly sweet. The cake had a subtle taste, making it a harmonious match with the frosting.

yelp:train:236132.orig: Had a great dinner Friday Night at Big Ben.  Quick, courteous service. I had chicken diane, rice and veggies,  excellent!  My friends enjoyed fish and chips and chicken pot pie.  Food was awesome,  great drinks and entertainment was such a plus.  Always enjoy our time at the Pub!
yelp:train:236132.para: Enjoyed a fantastic meal on Friday evening at The Big Ben. The service was swift and polite. I savored chicken Diane, rice, and vegetables, all delicious! My companions relished fish and chips and chicken pot pie. The cuisine was outstanding, and the drinks and entertainment significantly enhanced our experience. We always look forward to our visits to the Pub!

yelp:train:236218.orig: Is there a negative star for a nasty burger place where you get ignored....you wait an hour for your medium well burger and its served to you MEDIUM RAW? The meat was so cold and pink I almost threw up... \n\nNEVER AGAIN!
yelp:train:236218.para:
Never will I return to a dismal burger joint where patrons are disregarded, enduring a wait of an hour for a burger that's served undercooked and cold, almost inducing nausea.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original sentiment of dissatisfaction and the intention to never return to the burger place, while changing the wording and sentence structure.)

yelp:train:236256.orig: We spent a week in Vegas and ate at at least 10 burger places during that time. This was the BEST one we found overall. The portions are large, everything was made perfectly, our waitress was great, the drinks were excellent, good people watching and best of all, its not over priced. I didn't think we would find a reasonably priced place on the strip, but here it is. Hidden in a corner. We will definitely be coming back during our next trip
yelp:train:236256.para: During our week in Las Vegas, we indulged in burgers from no less than 10 establishments. Among them, one stood out as the superior choice. The servings were generous, the preparation flawless, the service impeccable, and the beverages top-notch. The ambiance was enjoyable for observing others, and most importantly, it was reasonably priced. Contrary to our expectations, we discovered a budget-friendly option tucked away in a secluded spot. This place is earmarked for our return visit on our subsequent journey.

yelp:train:236303.orig:
I have been a fan of Firehouse subs for almost 8 years, since I ate at one of the very first restaurants in Jacksonville, Florida. When I stopped traveling for work, Firehouse was one of the chains that I missed the most.

One day, I was at Cars & Coffee across Eastern, stomach growling, grumbling, nay, SCREAMING for food. When it gets to this point, there is no easy decision, everything and nothing sounds good. Something caught my eye as my head turned to check out a loud car, a familiar white and red sign, no, it couldn't be. Scanning actively for the sign again, staring at it incredulously, I thought I had to be imagining something in my hunger induced haze.

Fortunately, I was not imagining it! I made my way across the street to make a Hook & Ladder intimate friends with my belly in short order. Ordering my food, I brought out my trusty Firehouse punch card from the East coast and asked the lady how long they had been open. I was absolutely SHOCKED to find out that they were celebrating their one year anniversary. How could such delicious food be so close to me, and they not advertise at all?!

My go-to order is always the Hook & Ladder with a sweet tea. The heated turkey
yelp:train:236303.para: For nearly a decade, I've cherished Firehouse subs, beginning with my first meal at an early Jacksonville, Florida eatery. Upon ceasing my work-related travels, Firehouse became a chain I sorely missed. One day, while famished and at Cars & Coffee, I spotted a familiar white and red sign, which I initially thought was a figment of my hunger-induced delirium. However, it was real, and I quickly made my way to the nearby Hook & Ladder to satisfy my craving. I used my East coast Firehouse punch card and was astonished to learn they were marking their first year. The proximity of such delectable food, without any advertisement, was astounding. My preferred choice remains the Hook & Ladder with a sweet tea. The heated turkey...

yelp:train:236308.orig: I love the taste and quality of their sandwiches. Their service is always polite and the place is always clean. The one downside for me is the price. At 17 dollars for two large sandwiches that's a bit steep for me. If I made it a meal then bam I am at  25 bucks for a couple of sandwiches, chips and a drink. I love their sandwiches but this is a once every six months type of place for me. If I am going to spend 10-15 dollars a person I will go somewhere that I get a waitress and get to take up a booth for an hour.
yelp:train:236308.para: I adore the flavor and excellence of their sandwiches. The staff consistently exhibits courtesy, and the venue maintains a spotless environment. However, the cost is a drawback for me. Paying 17 dollars for two substantial sandwiches, along with chips and a beverage, feels excessive. I cherish their sandwiches, but this establishment is a rare choice for me. When I'm willing to invest 10-15 dollars per individual, I prefer a place where I can enjoy a waiter's service and a comfortable booth for a longer duration.

yelp:train:236963.orig: Went to the AT&T store located inside the Galleria Mall.  3 different employees told us 3 different things about purchasing a new cell phone. We are already customers, and they still wanted to charge us extra for plans we didn't need. Then, when we called AT&T Customer Service, we got a great deal and when we told the employees in the store what AT&T told us on the phone, they were going to honor the new deal, but after showing us that they had the phone in stock, they then said it was \""store policy\"" that they would need to ship us the phone.  We felt they were trying to punish us for getting a better deal because we would have saved over $200! Very underhanded way to treat customers. Also, BEWARE of \""Authorized Dealers\""! They aren't actual AT&T stores and they won't tell you about good deals because they will lose money if they  do.  I would avoid this store!! Terrible attitude toward customers and they didn't care about us at all.
yelp:train:236963.para: Visited the AT&T branch within the Galleria Mall, where three separate staff members provided us with three distinct pieces of advice regarding the acquisition of a new mobile device. Despite being existing patrons, they attempted to impose additional charges for unnecessary plans. Upon contacting AT&T's customer support, we secured a favorable offer, which the in-store staff agreed to uphold until we demonstrated the availability of the device. However, they then invoked a store regulation necessitating shipment of the phone. We perceived this as a retaliatory act for securing a more advantageous deal, potentially saving us over $200. This tactic was deemed deceitful in customer relations. Caution is advised against "Authorized Dealers," as they are not genuine AT&T outlets and are unlikely to disclose beneficial offers due to potential financial loss. The store's customer service was notably dismissive, showing no concern for our experience. I strongly recommend steering clear of this establishment.

yelp:train:237127.orig: Had the best cheeseburger ever and I dont really even eat burgers. The salmon burger was a bit fishy but the place is really fun!!
yelp:train:237127.para: Enjoyed the ultimate cheeseburger, despite not being a regular burger consumer. The salmon burger had a slight sea flavor, yet the establishment was genuinely enjoyable!

yelp:train:237405.orig:
Wow, if only I would have gone back to MY OWN original review, I could've avoided this, lol.

Server was attentive, but gave off the vibe that we bothered her.  My mom's food was cold and instead of bringing her an entire new plate, they heated up the cut into food and brought it back, which scared me.

Pancakes were not very good, sausage was strange...

Now I will seriously NEVER be back..Overpriced and just not good food.

Shoulda just had McDonald's
yelp:train:237405.para:
Oh, if I had revisited my own initial critique, I might have dodged this situation, haha.

The server appeared attentive, yet conveyed a sense that we were an inconvenience. My mother's meal was served cold, and instead of presenting a fresh plate, they reheated the sliced portions and served them back, which alarmed me.

The pancakes were subpar, and the sausage tasted odd...

I am now absolutely determined to never return. The cost was exorbitant and the food quality was disappointing. I would have preferred McDonald's instead.

yelp:train:237569.orig:
I'm gonna take some heat for this, but I really don't care.  I LOVE Claim Jumper.  Say what you will about chain this and chain that, but I hold this restaurant higher than your average chain and with reason.

It takes everything bad about American dining - huge portions, over-the-top decor incl impressive old-school ceiling fans, fattening desserts and huge tedious menus and unabashedly flaunts it.  I call it the Sierra Nevada version of Cheesecake Factory.

I've been going here for years - so I may be blinded by the nostalgia value, but I think the food is of better quality than your typical chain.  I very rarely come here anymore because every location is far-flung since Claim Jumper is adored by suburban soccer parents from here to Chicago, but my buddy out in South Tempe got me to make the trek last week for his birthday.

My favorites here are:
* Tri-tip french dip, which is delicious and classically Californian.  
* Rotisserie chicken with red skinned mashed potatoes or cheese potatocakes as an option.
* Country Fried Steak - with the mashed potatoes adorned with a red apple. :)
* Parmesan crusted chicken with angel hair marinara.
* Meatball calzone which is bigge
yelp:train:237569.para:
I'm prepared to face criticism for this, but my feelings are indifferent. I have a deep affection for Claim Jumper. Despite opinions on other chains, I regard this establishment superior to the norm, and justifiably so.

It boldly embraces all the negative aspects of American dining - excessive portion sizes, extravagant decor including grandiose ceiling fans, indulgent desserts, and extensive menus. I liken it to the Cheesecake Factory's version of Sierra Nevada.

Having frequented this place for a long time, I might be influenced by nostalgia, but I believe the food quality surpasses that of typical chains. Although I seldom visit now due to its widespread popularity among suburban soccer parents, my friend in South Tempe persuaded me to make the journey for his birthday celebration.

Here are my top picks:
* Tri-tip french dip, a delightful and quintessentially Californian dish.
* Rotisserie chicken served with either red skinned mashed potatoes or cheese potatocakes.
* Country Fried Steak, complemented by mashed potatoes garnished with a red apple.
* Parmesan crusted chicken served with angel hair marinara.
* A generous meatball calzone.

yelp:train:237589.orig: this is a totally awesome place to eat. great service and staff. have not found anything on the menu that i did not like. the baby back ribs fall right off the bone and the potato soup is soooo creamy. you gotta try the onion rings but make sure you have more then one person to eat them. a huge order.
yelp:train:237589.para: This is an exceptionally delightful dining spot with outstanding customer service and a friendly team. I haven't encountered a single dish on the menu that I didn't enjoy. The baby back ribs are incredibly tender, easily separating from the bone, and the potato soup boasts a rich, creamy texture. The onion rings are a must-try, but it's wise to have a group for a substantial portion.

yelp:train:237623.orig: Took forever to get my food. Approximately 45 minutes for just a Kids Pizza and A Burger... I definitely would not recommend this location. And the manager's are so tacky... Never again...
yelp:train:237623.para: It took an excessively long time, around 45 minutes, to receive my order of Kids Pizza and a Burger. I strongly advise against visiting this place. The managers' appearance was unappealing, and I will not be returning anytime soon.

yelp:train:237828.orig:
I love this place for breakfast. With just a few menu choices, it's tough to go wrong. My personal fave, the Switch Benedict is a tasty combo of potatoes and eggs benedict is a scrumptious white hollandaise sauce. It may not be good for you, but it's great for your tastebuds.

Sadly, I've never seen this place busy, but seeing as how I've only been there on weekends, I'm not too surprised. I expect the light rail to help out a bit with this, as it really is a great place.

If you like Fez or Ticoz, be sure to hit Switch up.
yelp:train:237828.para:
This spot is my go-to for morning meals, thanks to its limited but reliable menu selections. The Switch Benedict, a delightful mix of potatoes and eggs benedict with a rich white hollandaise sauce, is a treat for the palate, despite not being the healthiest option. Although I've only visited on weekends and it's usually not crowded, I believe the introduction of the light rail could boost its popularity, as it's a fantastic dining destination. For fans of Fez or Ticoz, I highly recommend trying out Switch.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original meaning, topic, sentiment, emotion, and intent while using different wording and sentence structure. The length is also roughly the same as the original text.)

yelp:train:238445.orig: Had a blast here! Attended \""Ditch Fridays.\"" It's so much fun. They had different blow ups in the pool, only downside sometimes peoples drinks get knocked. A blast though!!!!
yelp:train:238445.para: Experienced an amazing time here! Joined the \""Ditch Fridays.\"" It's incredibly enjoyable. Various water activities took place, with the occasional inconvenience of spilled drinks. Absolutely fantastic!!!!

yelp:train:238513.orig: I cannot believe the lack of customer service in this store. At first I went to find a sales associate to find where these markers are that you can write on glass were, while he was nice and helpful, he was not very specific on where the markers were and I was still very confused on where to find the markers and which ones had the ability to write on glass. \n\nHowever, the real problem with this store began when I had to find another sales associate to give me more information about  the glass markers. I had to chase a sales associate through the store in order to find someone who could help me and when I finally caught up to her, she disappeared into the break room where I had to stand for 5 minutes waiting for her to walk out. When she finally did walk out, she was beyond rude and completely condescending when I asked her to help me find the glass markers. At first, she asked me if I was using them for creative purposes and not inhaling them even though I was carrying a glass jar that could easily prove that I am going to use the markers for \""creative purposes\"". Next, she informed me that in order to buy the markers I had to be over 18 in a completely condescending way. She
yelp:train:238513.para: I am astounded by the poor level of customer support in this shop. Initially, I sought a salesperson to guide me to the glass-writing markers, and although he was amiable and cooperative, he failed to provide clear directions, leaving me still uncertain about their location and which ones could write on glass. \n\nThe true issue with this store surfaced when I needed to consult another salesperson for further details on the glass markers. I had to pursue a salesperson throughout the store to locate someone who could assist me, and when I finally reached her, she vanished into the break room, making me wait for five minutes. Subsequently, she informed me that I had to be at least 18 years old to purchase the markers in a highly dismissive manner.

yelp:train:238941.orig: 4.9 / 5. One of the best pizzas in Phoenix. Got the New York special and it was excellent. You have to eat it with a fork because the crust is very thin and can't support the weight of the toppings. The cheese is creamier than most. Toppings were very fresh and meat quality very very good. Not sure what they could do better. Definitely going back.
yelp:train:238941.para: Rated 4.9 out of 5, this pizza establishment in Phoenix offers an exceptional New York special. The thin crust necessitates fork usage due to its delicate nature, unable to bear the toppings' weight. The cheese boasts a superior creaminess compared to others. Freshness is evident in the toppings, with the meat quality being exceptionally high. While improvements could be considered, the overall experience is compelling enough to warrant a return visit.

yelp:train:239063.orig: Ok, im writing this review after seeing the news on panera bread dogging gun  owners. Seems for not much of a reason panera has told all people with guns legally that we care not for your business.  Thats how their words on guns are being taken including myself as a gun owner.  \n  Considering the food and company it isnt a place i have to have. Bread and soup is their strong suit. The rest to me isnt all that for the price.  I do have to say in the past i did feel the customer service was pretty good though. Have not had a issue with their employees.  \n  So, in conclusion i will not be back till they back off my gun rights and stop trying to be johny-do-good in the public eye.
yelp:train:239063.para:
I'm penning this critique following the report about Panera Bread criticizing lawful gun owners. It appears Panera has expressed indifference towards gun owners, a sentiment shared by me as a firearm owner. 

Despite the food quality and the atmosphere, it's not a necessity for me. Their expertise lies in baking and soups. However, the value for money doesn't quite meet my expectations. I must admit, their customer service was commendable in the past, with no negative encounters with staff. 

To sum up, I won't be returning until Panera respects my gun rights and ceases their public image-boosting efforts.

yelp:train:239267.orig: Not the best venue in the area by a mile. They should rename it the Douchehouse. The unfortunate proximity to ASU and the all ages policy/PBR on draft really bring in the drunken jackasses who are there to talk rather than watch the show. Parking is a pain in the ass; the business complex next door was blocked off and the lot was full. The bathroom situation is a serious joke. I've never been in a place where the better option is to leave and go next door to piss. The DJ playing music before the show should be fired. You've got an incredibly hot electro-indie band about to come on, and you crank up the hip-hop and 70's disco? Retard.\n\nSound is good-that's the only positive thing I have to say. I won't be going back unless it's a band I absolutely have to see.
yelp:train:239267.para: The venue isn't the top choice in the vicinity, perhaps it deserves the moniker "Douchehouse." The unfortunate closeness to ASU and the policy allowing all ages, coupled with the draft beer, attracts rowdy individuals more interested in conversation than the performance. Parking is a significant hassle; the adjacent business complex was cordoned off, leaving the lot completely occupied. The bathroom facilities are downright comical. I've never encountered a location where the sensible decision is to exit and use the facilities next door. The DJ's choice of pre-show music is questionable and deserves termination. Despite the venue's sound quality being a solitary positive aspect, I'm hesitant to return unless it's a must-see band.

yelp:train:239268.orig:
I have to be honest, I really do not like this place. 

At all. 

I've been coming here for years . . I practically used to live here back when I was dumb enough to date boys who are in bands. I never remember liking it then, and after last nights show, my mind hasn't changed much. 

Its small. Its dirty. Its unorganized. I find it really weird that its located in a strip mall next to a burrito shop. On a sold out night, its next to impossible to get a drink at the over-sized bar that takes up 70% of the venue. Order 2 at a time... double fisting is the only way to booze at The Clubhouse. They offer food.. that is prepared at the restaurant next door and brought over.. which is also weird, but the nachos looked totally decent. The bathroom situation is terrible.. With only one stall, I waited in line for over 20 minutes. I know we women like to take our time, but come on bitches! Hurry up and pee!

The parking lot is a zoo, and there are never any spots. Park in the business complex right next door instead.. just don't let you little sister sneak out of a show early to sleep in the car because you will return with it surrounded by cops. 

I know I've said absolutely nothi
yelp:train:239268.para:
I must admit, I genuinely dislike this location. 

In all honesty, I've frequented this place for a long time, even residing there when I foolishly dated musicians. I never felt a fondness for it then, and my opinion remains unchanged after witnessing the recent performance. 

It's compact and untidy. It lacks order. It's peculiar that it's situated in a shopping center adjacent to a taco stand. On a fully booked evening, securing a beverage at the large bar occupying 70% of the space is a daunting task. You have to order two at once... double drinking is the only way to enjoy at The Clubhouse. They serve food, which is cooked in the adjoining restaurant and delivered, which is odd, but the nachos seemed quite acceptable. The restroom situation is appalling, with only a single stall leading to a 20-minute wait. While women may take their time, it's time to hurry up and use the facilities! 

The parking area is chaotic, with no available spots. Consider parking in the nearby business complex, but beware of your younger sibling sneaking out early to nap in the car, as you'll likely return to it surrounded by law enforcement. 

I've expressed my firm refusal

yelp:train:239430.orig: This place is adorable! I love the decor and ambiance!!  They have private rooms in the very front of the restaurant (unfortunately facing the parking lot!!) but they are beautiful!! The happy hour (at the bar only) from 5 - 7 pm is awesome.. they have bottomless mimosas for $8! \n\nThe rolls are great, averagely priced sushi for the location... You'd think Red Rock would be charging $15 minimum per roll, but no.. You can get a roll for $8 - $11 just like everywhere else.  Great place for a first date!
yelp:train:239430.para: This spot is charming! I adore the interior design and atmosphere!! There are exclusive rooms situated at the restaurant's forefront (regrettably, with a view of the parking area!!) yet they are stunning!! The happy hour (restricted to the bar from 5 - 7 pm) is fantastic.. they offer bottomless mimosas for $8! \n\nThe rolls are delicious, moderately priced sushi for the area... One might expect Red Rock to impose a $15 minimum per roll, but that's not the case. You can acquire a roll for $8 - $11, just like in other places. An excellent choice for a first date!

yelp:train:239507.orig: The sushi and sashimi were amazingly delish. I ordered to go and promptly picked up the order. It was well prepared and packaged to look as if they were plated. I was impressed at the attention to detail even with takeout. But more importantly the food was wonderful. The flavors explode in your mouth. Anyways, fresh sushi is the only way to go. It was a little pricey but hey...You're getting fresh food prepared as you order it. We will be back again.
yelp:train:239507.para: The sushi and sashimi were incredibly tasty. I opted for delivery and quickly collected my order. The preparation and presentation were meticulous, giving the impression of a restaurant-style presentation. I was taken aback by the care taken for takeout orders. However, the primary delight was the exceptional quality of the food. The flavors burst vividly in the mouth. In my opinion, nothing beats the freshness of sushi. It was slightly costly, but it's worth it for the freshly prepared meal you get to enjoy. We're planning to return.

yelp:train:239890.orig: Love my bevmo. I can always find what I want here. Service is great. Prices a great. My only complaint - I have a kiddo and it would be helpful if they offered to help me get the booze into my vehicle. Other than that I love my bevmo!
yelp:train:239890.para: I adore my beverage spot. It's always easy to locate my desired items here. The service is excellent and the prices are reasonable. My sole grievance is that assistance would be beneficial for me to transport alcohol to my car, especially with my child. Aside from that, I have a deep appreciation for my beverage spot!

yelp:train:240115.orig:
My friend and I decided to try this place while the rest of our group stayed in the hotel room sleeping because of the night before. I was so hungry I just wanted to eat anything. 

Fortunately the buffet had started here around 11am for 11.99 per person. (does not include drinks )

It was a Italian style buffet. Spaghetti , lasagna, meatballs , and Parmesan chicken. They also served a soup and salad.

I hate to say it but the food quality was very poor. My clam chowder was disgusting and the only thing I enjoyed from my plate was the fettuccine . I kind of stuffed myself with bread because I was worried I was not going to get my money's worth. 

I was surprised how cold some of the food was judging that they just opened the buffet right as we got in. We were even the first ones!
yelp:train:240115.para:
My companion and I opted to dine here as our peers remained in the hotel room recovering from the previous night. I was famished and was inclined to consume anything available. 

Luckily, the buffet commenced here at approximately 11am for a fee of 11.99 per individual, excluding beverages.

This establishment offered an Italian-themed buffet, featuring dishes like spaghetti, lasagna, meatballs, and Parmesan chicken. They also provided a soup and a salad.

Regrettably, the food's quality was subpar. The clam chowder was repulsive, and the only item I genuinely appreciated from my plate was the fettuccine. I ended up overindulging in bread due to concerns about the value of my expenditure. 

I was taken aback by the chill of some of the food, especially since they had just initiated the buffet upon our arrival and we were among the first patrons.

yelp:train:240265.orig: I really like this place.. Great tea, great service, locally owned store.. Can't beat it. Few yrs ago I remember working with the owner on a neighborhood school fundraiser, she donated the tea on many occasions. It's a great place to checkout.
yelp:train:240265.para: This spot is fantastic, offering excellent tea and service, with a local business vibe. I recall collaborating with the proprietor on a community school fundraiser, where she generously provided tea multiple times. It's an ideal location for browsing.

yelp:train:240503.orig: Born and raised in Phoenix, first time at Mel's Diner. We stopped for breakfast on our way back to Tucson. The staff was friendly and efficient. The meal was fresh, House Fries were homemade, not frozen. Pancakes were light and fluffy. We spent a little less than we would at IHOP and the food was much better. We'll definitely return to Mel's Diner.
yelp:train:240503.para: Originating from Phoenix, our initial visit to Mel's Diner occurred during our return journey to Tucson. The team was amiable and proficient. Our breakfast was served with fresh ingredients, and the House Fries were crafted from scratch, not stored in freezers. The pancakes were delightfully airy and tender. We managed to save a bit of money compared to IHOP, and the quality of the food surpassed expectations. We are committed to revisiting Mel's Diner.

yelp:train:241457.orig: What can I say about Chompie's that hasn't already been said? This place is amazing - delicious food, friendly staff, a clean building and oh, did I mention the delicious food? I never miss a chance to go to Chompie's.
yelp:train:241457.para: Chompie's is a remarkable spot - it boasts scrumptious cuisine, welcoming personnel, and a spotless environment. The delectable food is a highlight that I always look forward to experiencing. I never pass up an opportunity to visit Chompie's.

yelp:train:241708.orig: I don't think I'll be going back anytime soon. The new decor is really nice and fresh but it ends there. The food was not very good. No presentation and no taste. The only thing I liked was the wedding soup. I visited with 5 other people and they all said the food was not very good. Good things were the decor, no wait, fast service but that's it. I think they need an overhaul on the menu and some more spices to help the bland food.
yelp:train:241708.para: The prospect of returning to this place in the near future doesn't appeal to me. While the updated aesthetics are pleasing and invigorating, it's the culinary experience that falls short. The dishes lacked both visual appeal and flavor, with the exception of the wedding soup. During my visit with four others, we all concurred that the food quality was subpar. The only redeeming qualities were the decor, swift service, and the soup. I believe a comprehensive menu revamp and an infusion of more spices are necessary to counteract the food's lackluster taste.

yelp:train:241735.orig: This place use to be really good, but it feels as if it is run-down now. Our family of four was seated and it took an hour for our food to come out. \nAlso, the Caesar salad did not taste good. I ordered the eggplant Parmesan and it did not look appetizing at all. Our family also ordered chicken Parmesan and it was burnt all around the edges.\nThere are better Italian places to go. I don't like waiting an hour for my dinner.
yelp:train:241735.para: The location used to be excellent, but it now appears neglected. Our group of four was accommodated and it took a full hour for our meal to be served. \nAdditionally, the Caesar salad lacked flavor. I had chosen the eggplant Parmesan and it was unappealing in appearance. Our group also opted for chicken Parmesan, which was charred on the periphery. There are superior Italian restaurants available. I am not fond of the long wait for my meal.

yelp:train:241941.orig: We have been here 3 times now and love coming back. The appetizers and desserts are great, as well as the servers. I recommend doing the wine flight to try out a little of everything!
yelp:train:241941.para: Having visited this place thrice, we're delighted to return. The quality of appetizers and desserts impresses us, along with the attentive service. I suggest sampling the wine flight to experience a variety of flavors.

yelp:train:242347.orig:
My favorite Thai Restaurant in Las Vegas. It's a hidden little restaurant by chinatown. I ordered the House Special Tom Yum Noodle dish for lunch along with the Papaya salad. 

I also ordered to go the Duck Fried Rice, Pad See Ewe and even Pad Thai (which is not my fav Thai dish) and all three were amazing.

Price wasn't even expensive. Under $8.00 dishes. I love it!
yelp:train:242347.para: In Las Vegas, my preferred Thai eatery is tucked away in Chinatown. For lunch, I chose the House Special Tom Yum Noodle and Papaya salad. Additionally, I picked up the Duck Fried Rice, Pad See Ewe, and Pad Thai, all of which impressed me greatly. The cost was quite reasonable, under $8 per dish. I thoroughly enjoy it!

yelp:train:242455.orig: Just found out they were on Ch. 13's Dirty Dining in April.. ew
yelp:train:242455.para: Discovered they appeared on Channel 13's Unsanitary Eating in April - yuck!

yelp:train:242993.orig:

Pulled into the parking lot around 6:30am on my way home from work. Stepped inside the door to find that the bar is *immediately* to your left.  6 ft and I'm on a bar stool.  So far so good.

Ordered the usual gin and grapefruit tall, for $4.50.  The place was empty save for myself and another guy at the bar.   The bartender that day was Geno, she informed me that the owner of The Well used to be a bartender at the Coach House, just down the road.  

I asked about breakfast options and Geno recommended a coffee shop a few doors down that was supposed to have excellent take out.  I decided to take a pass on that and ordered a breakfast beer instead.  I ended up having a real nice time at this place, just the three of us chatting and hanging out, enjoying the mellow morning.   Geno is a local treasure, btw.
 
I was treated to the (by now) standard assortment of wild stories that have become a standard feature of my bar exploration adventures.   The highlight of this particular morning was the one about the male transvestite school bus driver that caused a ruckus by using the ladies room

yelp:train:243144.orig: I don't have a lot of experience with cars or car repair places. I never owned a car until moving to Phoenix. I went here when my husband's car needed some work and vowed to bring my car when the need arose.\n\nWell, 3 months and I'm not a customer. I got a discount on services because my husband referred me. This place is so freaking cool on the inside. The lounge is clean, comfortable, and visually appealing. The staff is hard working and honest. I'm referring EVERYONE I know to 180.
yelp:train:243144.para:
I lack extensive knowledge in automobiles or automotive service centers. I didn't possess a vehicle until relocating to Phoenix. I chose this establishment for my husband's car when it required maintenance and promised to consider it for my own vehicle in the future.

However, after three months, I haven't availed their services. I received a price reduction due to my husband's recommendation. The interior of this place is incredibly impressive. The lounge area is neat, cozy, and aesthetically pleasing. The employees are diligent and truthful. I'm recommending this place to all my acquaintances, and I'm calling it 180.

yelp:train:243179.orig: Please give this place a try, you will definitely be pleasantly surprised. \nI was amazed by the delicious food, relaxing and classy atmosphere, and the excellent service. If you are looking for a somewhat hidden treasure, this place is really it.
yelp:train:243179.para: I highly recommend experiencing this location, as you're bound to be delightfully astonished. \nThe delectable cuisine, serene and sophisticated ambiance, along with the superior customer care left me in awe. For those seeking a concealed gem, this establishment truly fits the bill.

yelp:train:243493.orig:
Last week while attending a conference in Las Vegas some colleagues made reservations for Aureole. I'm vegan, so I usually like to call ahead and just mention that and make sure something can be done, but someone else made the reservations, and it was last minute. I've never been treated as poorly or snottily from a supposedly high class restaurant as I was at Aureole.

I discretely asked the waiter if something could be done vegan when he came by initially to introduce himself. He replied ""oh, it is very difficult, but we will try."" I should have left right then. ""Just pick something out and I will talk to the chef."" ""OK, I'll take a look."" Every dish headlines with animal protein, but a fennel orzo that came with one dish sounded nice and maybe close to vegan if the fish that came with it was left off. When the waiter returned, I asked for the green salad and asked if the fennel orzo that normally came with fish could be made vegan. The waiter,without checking with the kitchen,said ""no, that would be difficult"" and offered no suggestions and asked no other questions. I said, ""OK, how about the spring rolls?"" ""Yes, that will be easy.""

5 minutes later -
yelp:train:243493.para: During a Las Vegas conference last week, my peers booked a table at Aureole without prior vegan arrangements. As a vegan, I typically pre-emptively communicate my dietary needs, but this was overlooked. At Aureole, I felt unappreciated and disregarded, despite its upscale reputation. When I discreetly inquired about vegan options from the waiter, he responded, "It's very challenging, but we'll attempt." I should have left then. Instead, I asked him to consult the chef. He agreed to check and returned shortly. Unfortunately, he informed me that all dishes featured animal protein, with the exception of a fennel orzo dish that could potentially be vegan if the accompanying fish was omitted. When I requested a vegan version of this dish, the waiter, without verifying with the kitchen, stated it would be "difficult" and offered no alternatives. I then asked about the spring rolls, which he confirmed would be "easy" to accommodate. However, this conversation took place just five minutes later.

yelp:train:243701.orig:
First off, it still surprises me that people don't know what they're getting into at this place. There are signs up explaining the premise, AND they ask you if you've been there. So... Every trip to Dick's is different. Each server will be different from the last. 

We went around 4 in the afternoon with my teenage daughter and 8 yr old.  My kids got a kick out of the place, and the server was age appropriate with his Dick-like ways. He made my little girl a hat that says ""I pee in the pool"" and she thought it was hilarious. 

But holy crap it's expensive. $4.00 for a soda? Pay the .75 for water. Yes, you have to pay for water but the cups are great to refill when you're walking the strip.  I think they had 2 for 1 drinks at the bar but I didn't have any.  The food was ok. Typical bar food that is crazy overpriced. Yikes. I think we paid around $65 for 5 of us, and only one person ate an entree, we shared an app and got one dessert.  Half our bill was probably for soda. Ugh. 

I will only go back to this place if someone is just dying to go the next time I'm in Vegas.
yelp:train:243701.para:
Initially, it astonishes me that individuals remain unaware of what they're stepping into at this establishment. There are notices detailing the concept, and they inquire if you've visited before. Consequently, every visit to Dick's is unique. The service personnel will vary with each visit. 

We arrived at approximately 4 PM with my teenage daughter and an 8-year-old. My children thoroughly enjoyed the ambiance, and the server was suitable for their age, embodying the Dick-inspired demeanor. He crafted a humorous hat for my youngest daughter that proclaimed, "I pee in the pool," which she found amusing. 

However, it's quite shocking how costly it is. A soda costs $4.00, while water is priced at just 75 cents. Yes, you must pay for water, but the cups are excellent for refilling while strolling the strip. They offered 2-for-1 drinks at the bar, but I didn't partake. The food was average, typical of overpriced bar fare. It's quite alarming. We spent roughly $65 for five of us, with only one person consuming an entree. We shared an appetizer and one dessert. I suspect half of our bill was for sodas. Disappointing. 

I'll only revisit this place if someone is

yelp:train:243813.orig: Love it!  This place was a lot of fun, had a great band and a decent sized dance floor.  It was fun partying upstairs under the stars while The Streets played set after awesome set.  It's a mixed crowed.  I didn't feel like the oldest one there.  I don't know about the food.  I didn't even know they served food!  It was free to get in and drinks were about $6 bucks.  I would definitely go back.  We made a night of it and were very pleased.
yelp:train:243813.para: This venue was incredibly enjoyable, featuring an excellent band and a substantial area for dancing. The upstairs party under the night sky was energized by The Streets' consecutive impressive performances. The crowd was diverse, and I didn't feel out of place. The food situation was unclear to me, as I wasn't aware of any food service. Entry was free, and beverages cost around $6. I'm inclined to return and would recommend making the most of the night, as we were thoroughly satisfied.

yelp:train:244050.orig: I am very picky with restos but with our original flight cancelled, I had to give up my reservations at Mon Ami Gabi. So the hubby and I walked the strip hunting down a place to grab some grub. We decided to check this place out. Typical Vegas resto, loud BUT the gal was gracious enough to ask us if we want to be seated at the back. Adam was our server and he was a gem. We are easy diners, got the staples, guac with chips (in love with avocados) and split the fajitas. Food was good, the mango margarita was yummy but our server made a difference between as so-so dinner to an enjoyable one!
yelp:train:244050.para: I have a discerning palate when it comes to dining establishments, yet due to our initial flight being called off, I had to relinquish my bookings at Mon Ami Gabi. Consequently, my partner and I strolled along the strip in search of a suitable eatery. We opted to try this particular venue. It's a standard Las Vegas eatery, boisterous yet the lady behind the counter kindly inquired if we preferred a seating spot at the rear. Adam served us and proved to be exceptional. We're not fussy eaters, opting for the basics, avocado toast with chips (we're avocado enthusiasts), and we shared fajitas. The meal was satisfactory, and the mango margarita was delightful. However, our server elevated what could have been an average meal to a pleasurable dining experience.

yelp:train:244125.orig: There weren't many options in this wing of Charlotte's airport, and we were starving, but had we read the reviews we would have skipped Stock Car Cafe. As others have noted, service was prompt and fine, but the food was so bland and boring for what you pay. I would rather have spent less for fast food and gotten the same quality for less.
yelp:train:244125.para: The limited choices in this section of Charlotte's airport left us famished, yet had we perused the reviews, we would have bypassed Stock Car Cafe. While others have pointed out that the service was swift and satisfactory, the fare was uninspiring and unexciting considering its price. I would have preferred to invest less in quick-service meals and receive comparable quality for a lower cost.

yelp:train:244573.orig: At our recent Vegas trip, we stayed at the PH Westgate Towers and this joint was situated nicely in the hotel.  It will now be a staple for us every time we're in need of a good sandwich.  We tried the Earl's Club and the Full Montagu (both hot).  I don't know what they put in their sandwiches...maybe crack (j/k)??  The sandwiches were awesomely delicious!  My only complaint is that I wished they were bigger!
yelp:train:244573.para:
During our latest visit to Las Vegas, we chose to stay at the PH Westgate Towers, where this establishment was conveniently located within the hotel. It has now become a regular go-to for us whenever we crave a tasty sandwich. We sampled the Earl's Club and the Full Montagu, both served hot. I'm uncertain about the ingredients in their sandwiches, perhaps some sort of crack (just kidding)? However, the sandwiches were incredibly scrumptious! My sole grievance is that they could have been larger in size.

yelp:train:244598.orig: Overpriced, small portions.  The sandwich (a club) tasted fine, but it's about 6 inches long and was like 7 bucks.  Believe it or not, Subway is a better deal for both quantity and the fact that you can customize your sub, unlike at Earl.\n\nThis place is for casino drunks that want to eat late night and don't care about wasting money, but simply want something to eat.  My wife and I tried it out in the late afternoon and regretted it.  We actually like Quizno's better too!
yelp:train:244598.para:
The sandwich, priced at around $7 and measuring just 6 inches, was satisfactory in taste at this establishment. However, it's more cost-effective to choose Subway, which offers more quantity and customization options compared to Earl's. This venue caters to individuals seeking late-night sustenance post-gambling, who are indifferent to financial waste. My spouse and I experienced regret after trying it during the afternoon, as we prefer Quizno's.

yelp:train:245541.para: I ordered fried chicken that turned out to be overly dry, and unfortunately, I ingested some bone pieces. Gross! The pancit lacked flavor and was utterly disappointing. I'm definitely not returning to sample any other dishes. (

yelp:train:245560.orig: Food are ok but they have the best ube boba tho. I use to work here like 2 years ago and I decided just to order something that doesnt involve them cooking because truthfully they dont wash the dishes correctly, they reuse the sanitize water over and over even if it had some food in it. YUCK! I am sorry.
yelp:train:245560.para: The food is acceptable, yet the ube boba here stands out as exceptional. I previously worked here for two years and chose to order items that don't require their cooking, as they have a habit of reusing sanitized water repeatedly, even if it contains remnants of food, which is quite unappetizing. I apologize for this.

yelp:train:245920.orig:
Alright, so here's the thing:  I like to drink.  It's something I do well, and I figure that anything you can do well should be done often.  With that being said, I do not take it lightly when a restaurant names itself after an alcoholic beverage (we'll get to Jimmy Buffet's Margaritaville later).

That being said, it was my brother of all people who introduced me to Sake Bombers.  He said to me ""Las Vegas rolls, chicken wings and a sake bomber will do you just right.""  He wasn't lying.

The problem that people may have with me reviewing a sushi bar is that I don't eat seafood.  I'm allergic to a lot of it.  So you may be thinking ""Why in the shit am I reading this, you twit?""  Well, because I'm not allergic to alcohol or appetizers, two things that Sake Bombers does well.  

The chicken wings they serve have an Asian influence and a spice to them, though I wouldn't call them spicy.  They're a dry rub, not sauced, and they're swear-to-god delicious.  Now, I don't eat sushi, but I'm told by all that accompanied us that the Las Vegas roll, with jalapeno in it, and the White Castle roll, with cream cheese and horseradish, are delicious alternatives to the more standard f
yelp:train:245920.para:
I enjoy consuming alcohol, and I believe in doing things proficiently, hence I do it frequently. However, I don't appreciate it when a dining establishment is named after a drink (we'll discuss Jimmy Buffet's Margaritaville later).

My brother, who is not a seafood eater due to allergies, was the one who introduced me to Sake Bombers. He assured me that "Las Vegas rolls, chicken wings, and a sake bomber will satisfy you perfectly." He was indeed correct.

People might question why I'm reviewing a sushi establishment when I can't consume seafood. The reason is that I'm not allergic to alcohol or appetizers, which Sake Bombers excels at. 

The chicken wings they offer have an Asian flair and a hint of spice, but they're not overly spicy. They're seasoned with a dry rub rather than a sauce, and they're incredibly tasty. Even though I don't partake in sushi, those who joined us rave about the Las Vegas roll, featuring jalapeno, and the White Castle roll, with cream cheese and horseradish, as excellent substitutes for the usual offerings.

yelp:train:245928.orig: This place isn't terrible but....I've had better.\nThe outside is tacky and it was hard to find the entrance. \nThe set up is just weird, its more of a bar than a sushi place. Like a run down bar not a nice bar or even Applebees equivalent. Wait time for your food was long. The sushi fell apart easily and the Crunch Roll was more gritty like sand than \""crunchy\"". They are trying, I will be back in few months to try it again. Hope its better.
yelp:train:245928.para: The location isn't awful, but I've experienced better.\nThe exterior appears cheap and locating the doorway was challenging.\nThe arrangement is odd, resembling a deteriorated bar rather than a sushi restaurant or a place like Applebees. The wait for a meal was lengthy. The sushi disintegrated quickly and the Crunch Roll had a gritty texture, akin to sand, not the desired "crunchy" sensation. I'll revisit in a few months to see if there's improvement.

yelp:train:246044.orig: Even though pho is not on the higher end for demands in vegas, we came here to dine for breakfast during our vacation since my boyfriends parents' previous experience was good. despite that fact, what we experienced this time around was nothing compared to what it was before. The pho was edible, but not what you'd settle for if you knew how pho is really supposed to taste like. A few of us thought that the broth tasted weird, and that the meat somehow tasted fake. Personally, i thought it was mediocre, just not the high quality kind you'd expect from a vietnamese-rooted restaurant. At the end of our meal, the check came out to be 102, with only 8 of us all ordering pho, which does not add up. I guess somewhere along the way, the math got messed up, or they tried to gyp us due to our large party. either way, go elsewhere for pho if you're considering this place. if not, then save your cravings for when youre back home!
yelp:train:246044.para: Despite pho not being a high-demand dish in Vegas, we chose to have it for breakfast on our trip because of my boyfriend's parents' positive past experiences. However, our recent encounter fell short of their memories, with the pho being merely tolerable rather than satisfying. Some of us found the broth unusual and the meat artificially flavored. I personally deemed it average, lacking the expected excellence from a restaurant with Vietnamese origins. The bill of $102 for eight people who ordered pho seemed off, suggesting a possible miscalculation or an attempt to overcharge due to our group size. It's advisable to seek other pho options if you're thinking of this place, but if not, hold off on your pho cravings until you return home.

yelp:train:246420.orig: This place has just about everything you need as a \""Super Target\"". I used to go to the nearby Walmart but Target is just a much more pleasant shopping experience. It's clean and much less crowded. I've come at various times and never had to wait long at checkout. Parking is easy at this location. I've also found some really go deals here.
yelp:train:246420.para: This establishment offers nearly all the essentials for a "Super Target" shopping trip. I formerly frequented the adjacent Walmart, but I've discovered that Target provides a significantly more enjoyable and serene shopping environment. It maintains a tidy appearance and is noticeably less congested. I've visited at different times and consistently experienced swift checkout processes. The parking situation at this spot is convenient. Additionally, I've encountered some excellent bargains here.

yelp:train:246472.orig: I live on the west side of town and I still make the drive for this place.  The customer service is always great and the food doesn't get any better than this. yelp:train:246472.para: I reside on the western part of the city and continue to travel for this spot. The level of customer service is consistently excellent, and the cuisine here is unparalleled. yelp:train:246522.orig: Love small airports like these.  Traveling is so fast and easy here.  Returned a car rental, checked in at the ticketing desk, went through airport security and arrived at the gate in under thirty minutes total.  That's the way I like to travel!
yelp:train:246522.para: Enjoy the convenience of these compact airports. The journey is remarkably swift and hassle-free. I returned a vehicle rental, proceeded to the check-in counter, passed through security, and reached the boarding gate in less than half an hour. This is my preferred mode of travel.

yelp:train:247319.orig:
Talk about visual orgasms! As a Beatles fan, I was so excited to watch LOVE as my first Cirque show during my first trip to Vegas, and it actually exceeded expectations.

Favorite performances were Lucy In The Sky With Diamonds and Octopus's Garden, but all of the song interpretations were amazing. I'm also glad they included my much beloved Eleanor Rigby.

Pro-tip: After asking at will-call if they had better seats available, we were moved from Section 209 Row R to Section 200 Row N. There really is no bad seat in the theatre, but it's good to note that Row N is at the edge of the bedsheets/clouds used to cover the lower audience during one number. We were able to see what went on above the sheets as well as the actors moving underneath. Double win!
yelp:train:247319.para:
Discuss the thrill of visual ecstasy! Being a devoted Beatles enthusiast, I was thrilled to experience LOVE as my inaugural Cirque spectacle on my inaugural Vegas visit, surpassing my anticipations.

Highlighted acts included Lucy In The Sky With Diamonds and Octopus's Garden, with all song renditions being exceptional. I'm also pleased they featured my cherished Eleanor Rigby. 

Advice: Upon inquiring at the will-call desk about superior seating, we were relocated from Section 209 Row R to Section 200 Row N. While no seat is subpar in the auditorium, it's worth mentioning that Row N is positioned at the boundary of the bedsheets/clouds that conceal the lower audience during a particular performance. We had the advantage of observing both above and below the sheets, as well as the performers' movements. A double triumph!

yelp:train:247660.orig:
I was taken here while visiting from Chicago and had one of the best margaritas of my life.  I tried the house (on ice with salt) and it was fantastic, but what I couldn't get enough of was the strawberry-lime one.  I couldn't taste a drop of alcohol...and that's when you know you have a good mixed drink on your hands. I honestly could have had three more it was so tasty, but my childlike tolerance for boozin did not allow it.  

The bartender was super nice and friendly, we had many refills of the chips and salsa (damn you, I can never resist), and it was all in a southwestern chill environment.  Supposedly the tacos are top-notch, I will have to give them a whirl next time I'm in town.  

I highly suggest going here for a happy hour or dinner.
yelp:train:247660.para:
During my stay in this location while away from Chicago, I experienced one of the most delightful margaritas of my existence. I sampled the house variety served chilled with salt, which was exceptional, but it was the strawberry-lime concoction that truly captivated my palate. Notably, I didn't detect any alcohol, indicating a high-quality mixed beverage. Despite its irresistible flavor, my youthful resistance to alcohol prevented me from indulging further. 

The bartender exuded warmth and friendliness, and we enjoyed numerous servings of chips and salsa, which I found hard to resist. The ambiance was relaxed with a southwestern vibe. I've heard the tacos are excellent, and I plan to try them on my next visit. 

I wholeheartedly recommend visiting for either happy hour or dinner.

yelp:train:247696.orig:
Would I go back here if/when I return to Scottsdale? Heck yeah!!!!!  When we were there last November there were 5 adults and one child in our family group wandering around the area looking for something to eat.  The one place we tried to get into you couldn't get in without a crowbar so we wandered past this, took a look at the menu and said why not!

So glad we did!  Good sangria, interesting patio area (felt more like an alley but cool), great chips and salsa, and good food at a good price.  No one, not even the kid complained about their food.  And this was the first time in my life I had fajitas with zucchini in them! YUM!  Plus, most veggies that come with fajitas are usually limp beyond limp and on the bland side.  Theirs had some spice to them.  

With drinks and food our whole bill for all of us was around 100$.  Not bad for a place in Old Scottsdale.
yelp:train:247696.para:
If/when I revisit Scottsdale, I'd certainly return! In November, our family of six, including a child, roamed the vicinity searching for a meal. We couldn't access a particular spot without a crowbar, so we explored another, perused the menu, and decided to give it a try!

I'm delighted we did! The sangria was excellent, the patio area, though resembling an alley, was enjoyable, the chips and salsa were top-notch, and the food was delicious and reasonably priced. Not a single person, even the child, voiced dissatisfaction with their meal. This was the first occasion I've ever had fajitas with zucchini! Normally, fajita veggies are limp and bland, but not here. They had a hint of spice. 

Our total bill for everyone, including drinks and food, was approximately 100$. That's quite reasonable for a spot in Old Scottsdale.

yelp:train:248033.orig: Decided to check out Ground Control last night based on a reviews on AZ Central as one of the best wine bars.. I totally disagree.  Service was terrible, one person I particular was rude when we interrupted time with his girlfriend.  Had to ask for water, plates, napkins, check, etc.  The wine was decent as well as a couple of appetizers. But pass on the cheese board...  3 small slices for $14. I was looking forward to the European concept but in Europe, they are more helpful and friendly...
yelp:train:248033.para:
Based on positive feedback from AZ Central, I chose Ground Control for its acclaimed wine selection. However, I strongly contest this view. The service was subpar, with a specific individual displaying unpleasant behavior when we disrupted their personal time. We had to request basic items like water, plates, and napkins, and even the check process was cumbersome. While the wine quality was acceptable and some appetizers were enjoyable, I would advise against the cheese board, which offered only three small slices for $14. I anticipated a European-style experience, but found the staff less accommodating and amiable than in Europe.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original sentiment, topic, emotion, and intent while altering the wording and sentence structure. The length is also kept relatively the same.)

yelp:train:248393.para:

*Cuisine = standard, swiftly made American fare
*Service = satisfactory
*Ambience = intriguing
*Cost = acceptable

yelp:train:248708.orig:
do yourself a favor and go to sushi roku across the street.

the spicy tuna wasn't spicy.
the bottom fell out of my boyfriend's water glass inexplicably (ok, not their fault necessarily).
the rolls were microscopic.

i should have tried some of the entrees instead of ordering just sushi. but when you're known for being a sushi restaurant, your rolls should be on par.

i did really appreciate the wonderful customer service, though. when the mysterious water debacle occurred, the staff was apologetic and comped our $27 kobe gyoza appetizer, in addition to bringing us another dish on the house.
yelp:train:248708.para: Opt for a visit to sushi roku just down the road. While the spicy tuna lacked heat, the unexpected incident with my boyfriend's water glass was handled with understanding, and they generously compensated with a complimentary $27 kobe gyoza starter and an additional dish. Despite the small roll sizes, I acknowledge the exceptional customer service provided. I might have considered other menu options, but as a sushi establishment, maintaining standard roll sizes is expected.

yelp:train:248775.orig:
Koi was very good!! 

Me  and one of my girls went to Koi for dinner on our first evening in Vegas. We weren't hella hungry so we just ordered something to share btwn us. To make the review easier to read, Ill just list what we had:

Spicy Tuna Roll: Good...same as any other spicy tuna roll I've had.

Dragon Roll: Consisted of bbq eel, shrimp tempura, crab and seaweed (obviously). That was the BEST dragon roll I ever had! They sprinkled the roll with tempura shavings I think. The roll literally melted in my mouth. Very good.

Miso Soup: Good...same as any other miso soup

Sake: we got the blueberry infused one. BOMB! Definitely recommend that,it was like soda...and had me buzzin even more than I was before we got there hahaha.

Will definitely come back!
yelp:train:248775.para:
Koi provided an excellent dining experience! 

On our initial night in Las Vegas, my partner and I decided to dine at Koi. Not extremely famished, we opted for a shared dish. Here's a concise rundown of our meal for easier comprehension:

Spicy Tuna Roll: Satisfactory, similar to other spicy tuna rolls I've tasted.

Dragon Roll: A blend of barbecue eel, shrimp tempura, crab, and seaweed. It was the most delicious dragon roll I've ever tasted! They added tempura shavings, and it dissolved delightfully in my mouth. Exceptional.

Miso Soup: Satisfactory, akin to other miso soups.

Sake: We chose the blueberry-infused variety. Outstanding! Highly suggest it, it felt like soda and intensified my buzz even more than before we arrived, haha.

We're certain to return!
