yelp:train:249950.para: The ambiance is pleasant, the service is commendable, and the cuisine is exceptional, especially the large and fresh lobster tails. I enjoy visiting for the seafood, it's a delightful indulgence. The staff is consistently helpful and adept at managing large parties.

yelp:train:250006.orig: I agree this place kind of sucks.  Food is average. and although it looks really nice no one ever seems to be there.  It is always dead.  they have great TV's and I think the place should hop but instead it is not.\n\nGo to tanked fish next door. everyone else does.  This place looks really good and I like the bar set up. reason for 2 stars.
yelp:train:250006.para: I concur that this location somewhat disappoints. The cuisine is fairly standard, and despite its appealing appearance, it's perpetually empty. The ambiance is lifeless, and while the televisions are commendable, the establishment fails to thrive. I'd recommend visiting the popular Tanked Fish next door. Although the decor is attractive and the bar setup is enjoyable, I'm rating it two stars.

yelp:train:250203.orig:
It is a must do in Vegas- a ritual. 

Caramel hazelnut napolean with coffee. Nothing beats it. I don't even like dessert but this is an addiction, a new delicious addiction I must fix every time I come to Vegas. 

I also had the Chicken Cocktail sandwich. It was yummy but I thought the tomato wasn't fresh enough for my taste. 

Just go already. Trip out on the mock silver plastic utensils. On a totally separate tangent: why do they call it silverware when it's not silver???
yelp:train:250203.para:
In Las Vegas, indulging in a caramel hazelnut Napoleon with coffee is an essential experience, akin to a rite of passage. Despite my usual aversion to sweets, this particular confection has become a compulsive craving I can't resist each time I visit the city. 

Additionally, I sampled the Chicken Cocktail sandwich, which was enjoyable, but I found the tomato's freshness lacking according to my standards. 

Don't delay any further. Immerse yourself in the experience of dining with plastic utensils that mimic silver. Shifting gears slightly: why is it referred to as silverware when it doesn't contain any silver?

yelp:train:250847.orig: The Santan Brewery Octoberfest is a bust. $15 bucks a head plus $5 dollars a beer to look at commercial tents. They need a lot more \""bling\""  or vendors to make it worthwhile.  We spent two hours and looked at everything twice.
yelp:train:250847.para: The Octoberfest at Santan Brewery is lively and packed. Attendees pay $20 per person and $5 per beer to view commercial tents. The event requires additional "bling" or vendors to enhance its appeal. We dedicated two hours and revisited all attractions.

yelp:train:250861.orig:
The computer was down with no way to conduct any business after the long Memorial Day weekend.  I waited a few minutes and then decided to go work out at SCC.  Upon returning a couple of hours later the computer was still down.  I asked if this happens often and it has happened before after long holiday weekends. So how much time was lost by the public today?  How much gas was wasted because there was no Plan B?  

I received a notice in the mail and have two months to update my driver's license  photo.  However, you can bet I will not be at Motor Vehicles on Monday July 7th for a repeat (?) performance.  I actually like my old photo and think I look like the photo so why do I have to get a new one?

Update: On my second visit there were hardly any customers so the photo update went smoothly.  My number was quickly called with pleasant chit chat.  The only "" problem"" was the new photo didn't show as much hair as there should have been.  I  commented the camera must be broken which drew a chuckle but I am sure my remark is made hundreds of times.   Maybe the camera will be fixed the next time around?
yelp:train:250861.para:
The computer malfunctioned and rendered it inoperable following the extended Memorial Day break. I opted to exercise at SCC and returned a few hours later to find the issue persisted. It's a recurring problem post-lengthy holiday periods, leading to public time and fuel wastage due to the lack of alternatives. 

I got a letter stating I have two months to renew my driver's license photo. However, I'm certain I won't visit Motor Vehicles on July 7th for another round. I prefer my current photo and believe it accurately represents me, hence my reluctance to change. 

During my second visit, the office was almost empty, making the photo update process hassle-free. My turn came quickly, and the interaction was friendly. The only minor issue was that the new photo didn't capture as much hair as expected. I joked about a faulty camera, which elicited laughter. I'm sure this is a common complaint. Perhaps the camera will be rectified in future visits?

yelp:train:251660.orig:
I get why they have four stars, it's a hip place with electronica music playing in the background, and that seems to be a Vegas standard now.  However, I can't say ill be making my way back.

They have a variety to choose from for AYCE, with the whole inside menu strictly rolls.  When I do AYCE, I only go for nigiri.  As I've posted before, I'm not really into rolls because its usually covered in sauce, with very little filling.  I guess it's what Americans love though... Sauce on everything.  I'm guilty as well, just not on my sushi.

Anyway, the fish was really poor quality.  After my initial order, I couldn't bring myself to order any more.  I love my fish to taste like fish (if that even makes sense).  The fish here had no taste whatsoever.  All I could taste was the vinegar from the rice.

I thought it was cool they served oysters, but it was pretty blah.  There was no flavor at all.  It tasted like water.  It did not have that ""taste like the sea"" quality.  I don't know.  It just didn't taste like anything.  The baked mussels were not very good. Overcooked. No flavor.  Too chewy.

Tofu was ok, but too much sauce, and it was overly sweet.  Desserts were boring.  No
yelp:train:251660.para:
I understand the reason behind their four-star rating; it's a trendy spot with electronic music in the air, a common feature in Las Vegas. Nevertheless, I won't be returning.

They offer a range of options for all-you-can-eat (AYCE), with the entire menu consisting of rolls. When I opt for AYCE, I prefer nigiri over rolls, as I find rolls typically saucy with scant filling. It appears to be a popular preference among Americans, who often enjoy sauce-laden dishes. I admit to indulging in sauces myself, but not on my sushi. 

In terms of quality, the fish was subpar. After my first order, I lacked the desire to order more. I appreciate my fish to have a distinct taste, but the fish here was devoid of any flavor, with only a hint of vinegar from the rice. 

The oysters were underwhelming, lacking any taste. It tasted like water, missing the characteristic "sea" flavor. It was as if it didn't have any taste at all. The baked mussels were also disappointing, overcooked and lacking in flavor, with a chewy texture. 

The tofu was passable, but the excessive sauce and overly sweet taste detracted from its quality. The desserts were uninspiring

yelp:train:252186.orig:
Warm butter cake! It is the signature dessert of the restaurant that is sweet and fluffy in a round cake that can feed 2 or 3 easily. I really don't have the words to describe it but suffice it to say you need to get it. And do what we did...have your dessert first! That suggestion got the server an extra tip!

As for the rest of the meal, it was heavenly. The steaks and the sides were huge. I had the prime rib and my companion had the ribeye. Both were delicious. There wasn't anything bad about the meal. 

We were there two weeks ago and the restaurant was full particularly the bar. The dining room is dimly lit and intimate. For those who are visually challenged in dim light, bring your readers!
yelp:train:252186.para: The restaurant's renowned butter cake, a delightful and substantial round dessert perfect for two or three, is a must-try. It's challenging to find the right words to express its irresistible charm, but it's undeniable that you should indulge. Following our lead, we enjoyed dessert before the main course, which resulted in a generous tip for the attentive server. The entire dining experience was sublime, with generously portioned steaks and sides. The prime rib and ribeye were both exceptional, with no negative aspects to the meal. Visiting two weeks prior, the establishment was bustling, especially the bar area. The dining room's soft illumination creates a cozy atmosphere. For those with visual impairments in dim lighting, consider bringing a reader for an enhanced experience.

yelp:train:252383.orig:
Having just sampled Capriotti's again, this time at Night of the Living Neon, where they were very generous sponsors, I took my break from the slots at Red Rock for my Wednesday night Food Court Feast.  :)   Their Bobby was calling to me, but I decided to lower the carb quotient by going for their Cole Turkey sandwich.  I guess I didn't realize that, unlike all the other sub joints, Capriotti's uses REAL, FRESH turkey!!, and that helps explain why their prices are a bit higher than the competition.  

The sandwich was super.  I asked for the Russian dressing on the side, and I was given a container big enough to dress my next four salads.  The turkey was moist, the provolone really good, and the cole slaw just the way I like it.  My only complaint is that their Small sandwich, at 9"", is just too big for me.  I'd love to see a smaller one at a smaller price, but I bet not too many people would share this nit.  

I'm a fan!
yelp:train:252383.para:

I didn't know that, unlike other sub shops, Capriotti's uses genuine, fresh turkey, which might be the reason for their slightly higher prices.  

The sandwich was exceptional. I requested the Russian dressing on the side and was provided with a large enough container to dress my subsequent four salads. The turkey was succulent, the provolone delicious, and the coleslaw perfectly to my liking. My only gripe is that their Small sandwich, measuring 9 inches, is too large for my preference. I'd appreciate a smaller version at a reduced price, though I suspect few would agree with this minor criticism.  

I remain a loyal fan.

yelp:train:252399.orig: I need to start by saying that I am NOT the type of person that gets a manicure or even goes to a spa. The reason I went today is that I needed a pro to fix my cuticles before my wedding.\n\n That being said, I enjoyed my time here. I went for a regular manicure. Overall, I enjoyed the process and was relaxed, but a few things would keep me from returning soon:  1) My tech was funny and easy to talk to, but I was a bit skeeved by the fact that she blew big bubbles with her gum while clipping my cuticles. 2) They had a limited choice of polish colors. I usually paint mine something crazy (neon pink, black, obnoxious glitter) and the various shades of red and pink weren't to my liking. The meadow green I picked was the loudest color there and while it's cute, I'd like something weirder. All in all, I'll definitely go back in the winter when my skin and nails are particularly awful.
yelp:train:252399.para: I must clarify that I'm not someone who frequents nail salons or spas. However, I decided to visit today because I required professional assistance to address my cuticles in preparation for my wedding.\n\nDespite this, I found the experience pleasant. I opted for a standard manicure and found the entire process enjoyable and calming. Nevertheless, there are certain aspects that might deter me from making a return visit soon: 1) The technician was amusing and approachable, but I felt slightly uncomfortable with her habit of blowing large bubbles with gum while trimming my cuticles. 2) The range of nail polish colors was somewhat restricted. I typically choose vibrant and unconventional colors like neon pink, black, or glittery shades, but the available red and pink hues didn't meet my preferences. The meadow green I selected was the most vibrant option, though it's cute, I'm inclined towards more eccentric choices. In summary, I am inclined to revisit during the colder months when my nails and skin are in dire need of care.

yelp:train:253158.orig: It's always amazing how the garden is set up to wow the crowds of tourists and locals who stop in on a daily basis. I try to get here for each theme to see what they have come up with next. I recently went for Christmas and was impressed. From penguins to polar bears and a canopy where it looks like you are standing in a snow storm this place is a must see for all.
yelp:train:253158.para: The garden consistently captivates both tourists and residents with its daily allure. I make it a point to visit each section to witness their latest creations. My recent visit during the festive season left me in awe. The array of creatures, from penguins to polar bears, and the snow-like canopy, make this location an essential attraction for everyone.

yelp:train:253438.orig: In 5 years of coming to LV, this has to be the saddest buffet in LV.  We had enjoyed the Spice World Buffet at Planet Hollywood the morning before but opted to \""eat local\"" Sunday morning.  What a mistake!  I don't know where Ryan T.  ate as there was NO wait service at all. The food and drinks were totally self service.   No half and half for coffee (non dairy creamer only).  An extremely limited selection with powdered scrambled eggs, frozen pastries, no egg white omelets, watered down juices, Eggo waffles, soupy oatmeal and a fruit bar consisting of  tired looking melon evoked a Days Inn free breakfast buffet rather than a $20+ Vegas Sunday brunch.The shrimp looked so old no one in my party dared take anything from the fish area (lox and two kinds of boiled shirmp)  The carvery had a Hormel type ham and a turkey breast evoking Louis Rich, but no one to cut it. It was truly pitiful.  The take away is ask to view the buffet before committing to purchasing and avoid the Luxor MORE as a breakfast option,
yelp:train:253438.para: Over a span of five years in Las Vegas, this buffet stands out as the most disheartening in the area. We had previously savored the Spice World Buffet at Planet Hollywood, but chose to dine locally on a Sunday. Regrettably, it turned out to be a poor decision. I'm uncertain where Ryan T. found his meal, as there was absolutely no wait staff present. The establishment operated on a self-service basis for both food and beverages, offering only non-dairy creamer for coffee and a severely restricted menu featuring powdered eggs, frozen pastries, and a fruit bar that resembled a subpar Days Inn breakfast buffet, rather than a premium Vegas Sunday brunch. The seafood appeared aged, deterring anyone in my group from sampling the lox and shrimp. The carvery presented a Hormel-style ham and turkey breast reminiscent of Louis Rich, yet lacked any slicing service. It was genuinely disappointing. The lesson learned is to inspect the buffet before spending money and to steer clear of the Luxor for breakfast.

yelp:train:253553.orig: I just had breakfast at More and paid $18 (with tax) and I feel that the Luxor should be ashamed of this place. The selection is incredibly sparse and bland. There are multiple stations with food, but they all have the same items: bacon, biscuits & gravy, breakfast potatoes, etc.. The only edible food available was the fresh fruit, and that's all I could eat after sampling the hot options. $18 for a banana and some melon. This experience has written me off of Las Vegas buffets; thank you More buffet.
yelp:train:253553.para: After dining at More and spending $18 (including tax), I am dismayed by the Luxor's lackluster dining options. The variety is severely limited and uninspiring, featuring repetitive choices like bacon, biscuits & gravy, and breakfast potatoes. The sole palatable item was the fresh fruit, which I ended up consuming after trying the hot dishes. I'm now disillusioned with Las Vegas buffets, especially More's, and I'm grateful for this eye-opening experience.

yelp:train:253894.orig: Great first impression!! I called to place a to-go order and although they literally were closing in ten min, the gentleman on the phone was super cool & acted as though it was hours earlier. There was absolutely no hint in his voice of annoyance at the last minute order, as so many restaurant workers would have displayed. I cannot express how accommodating he was on the phone, it was such a relief after having just gotten home from the airport. Exceptional food, had the chicken pita, tzatsiki, and their signature crazy fries (with feta!). Can't wait to return.
yelp:train:253894.para: Fantastic initial encounter! I dialed to request a takeout and despite them about to shut down in a mere ten minutes, the man on the line was incredibly chill and seemed as if it was a long time ago. There was not a single trace of irritation in his tone regarding the urgent order, unlike the typical response from many eatery staff. His exceptional hospitality over the phone was a huge comfort after arriving home from the airport. I thoroughly enjoyed the excellent cuisine, including the chicken pita, tzatsiki, and their unique, feta-topped fries. I'm eagerly anticipating my next visit.

yelp:train:254280.orig: My family and I were in the shopping plaza this morning.  Our 4 year old son needed a haircut so he and I walked into the salon and asked if they could do a children's haircut.  Instead of a \""good morning\"", a smile, and an answer to the question, the lady sitting at the front desk replied, \""we don't do children's prices\"".  That wasn't my question and her delivery was such that I felt like I was somehow being judged financially.  It gave me flashes of Julia Roberts in Pretty Woman when she was trying to buy a dress.  I didn't care about the price.  I was asking a question because some salons prefer to not do such a young person's hair.  Your salon missed out on 2 clients today and a lesson in etiquette and good customer service is needed by those greeting customers as they walk in the door.
yelp:train:254280.para: This morning, my family and I were at the mall. Our four-year-old son required a haircut, so we went to the salon and inquired if they provided children's haircuts. Instead of a friendly greeting and a direct response, the lady at the reception counter stated, "we don't offer children's rates." This response, delivered in a manner that made me feel judged about my financial situation, reminded me of Julia Roberts' experience in Pretty Woman. I wasn't concerned about the cost; I was seeking information because some salons choose not to cater to young children's haircuts. The salon lost two potential customers today and it's clear that they need to improve their customer service and etiquette, especially for those who are welcoming customers at the entrance.

yelp:train:255430.orig:
East End is a brewery, not a restaurant. Don't expect to sit down for pizza and brews. Most of the space is filled with brewing equipment - tanks and such. What you can do is sample a bunch of beers, and walk away with some.

It's a challenge to find East End. There's no sign. Just an open door in a brick warehouse. And an empty keg sitting outside. Our first time, we didn't think we could possibly be in the right place. Until we saw people leaving with beer.

You can only visit during growler hours. Inside there's a low bar straight out of high school chem. You can sample the eight or so beers on tap. And chat about the beers or anything else. And be impressed at how many people manage to find the place. The beers are tasty.

Then when you're ready, pick a beer or two to get a growler of. A growler is a half gallon jug they filled from the tap. They also usually have a special beer or two in bottles. Typical brewery swag is also available - pint glasses, t-shirts, etc., to prove that you actually found the place.
yelp:train:255430.para:
East End functions as a brewery rather than a dining establishment, so anticipate not dining on pizza with your beers. The majority of the area is occupied by brewing apparatus like tanks. Here, you can taste various beers and take them with you. 

Locating East End can be tricky as there's no visible sign. It's an unmarked entrance in a brick building with an unused keg outside. On our initial visit, we doubted our location until we observed people exiting with beer. 

Visits are limited to growler times. The interior features a basic high school chemistry-style bar. Here, you can try the approximately eight beers on tap and discuss them or any other topic. The popularity of the place is evident, and the beers are enjoyable. 

When you're prepared, select a couple of beers to fill a growler. A growler is a half-gallon container filled from the tap. They also often have a few special beers in bottles. Brewery merchandise like pint glasses and t-shirts are also available to confirm you've found the right place.

yelp:train:255928.orig: So lame. They don't have the decency to let people know on their restaurant.com ad that they no longer accept certificates, so we drove all the way there for nothing. We LOVE Mexican food, but this place lost present and future business from us. Shame on you Loco Patron.
yelp:train:255928.para: They lack the courtesy to inform potential customers on their restaurant's website about discontinuing certificate acceptance, resulting in a wasted trip for us. Despite our fondness for Mexican cuisine, this establishment has inadvertently forfeited both current and future patronage from us. It's disappointing on the part of Loco Patron.

yelp:train:255957.orig: Better than Macayos, but we all know that's not saying much. Unfortunately, it's a little pricey for mexican food and really not all that great. yelp:train:255957.para: While it surpasses Macayos, the truth is that this isn't a significant distinction. Regrettably, it comes with a hefty cost for Mexican cuisine and doesn't quite meet expectations. When I genuinely desire high-quality, traditional Mexican fare, I typically end up driving to Tow-Carolinas at Peoria and 91st Avenue.

yelp:train:256087.orig: Super friendly and attentive service, from the front desk, to the wait staff to the sommalier - they anticipated our very large group's every need.  And this was on a VERY busy Monday evening at NAB. The food was decent, although was a bit disappointed there was no grass fed meat on the menu at those prices.  Wine selection fantastic, we had a bottle of the Hansel Pinot (one of the few under $100) and it blew everyone away.  The Stonestreet Upper Barn Chardonney on the Som's recommendation was fantastic as well.  It's not too noisy so you don't have to yell to be heard or keep asking people to repeat themselves.  \n\nWhat else can I say, with all the options you have at the Venetian, you can't go wrong here.
yelp:train:256087.para: The service at NAB was exceptionally warm and proactive, catering to our substantial group's requirements from the receptionists to the waiters to the sommelier. Despite the high volume of activity on a Monday evening, the food quality was satisfactory, albeit slightly underwhelming due to the absence of grass-fed meat options at affordable prices. The wine assortment was impressive, with a standout being the Hansel Pinot, which impressed everyone and was priced reasonably. The Stonestreet Upper Barn Chardonney, suggested by the sommelier, was also highly commendable. The ambiance was not overly loud, ensuring clear communication without the need for raised voices or repetition. In summary, with the plethora of choices available at the Venetian, it's a safe bet to have a great time.

yelp:train:256584.orig:
When I first saw this place I was little like ummm we are really going in there? But I am so glad we did! Most of the bars were really crowded except for one in the corner where no one was. Me and my friends went over and the super friendly bartender was more then happy to serve us. She gave us some great deals. The first was that she gave me a 2 for 1 on my rum and coke (2 shots for the price of 1). She then offered to give us free shots if we bough a bandanna. (There was some sort of contest and her boss told her she needed to up her numbers.) My friend got a bandanna and we all come some delicious shots. 
We then all took a turn riding the bull which was such a blast. Sadly I was too tipsy to be much good, but it was still fun none the less. Even if you sucked the crowd was on your side. 
As we were getting ready to leave I had to have a bandanna of my own. I went back to my favorite bartender and she offered up another round of shots for my bandanna.
Free shots, fun bandannas, and a mechanical bull. What else do you need?
yelp:train:256584.para: Upon my initial visit, I was hesitant, almost questioning our decision to enter. However, I'm extremely pleased we did. The majority of the bars were packed, but there was a solitary spot in the corner that was empty. My companions and I approached and were greeted by an exceptionally welcoming barmaid. She was delighted to provide us with some fantastic offers. She offered me a rum and coke deal where I received two shots for the price of one. She also suggested we get free shots if we purchased a bandanna, as part of a contest to increase sales. My friend bought a bandanna, and we all enjoyed some tasty shots. \n\nWe then all had a chance to ride the bull, which was a thrilling experience. Unfortunately, I was too intoxicated to perform well, but it was still enjoyable. The crowd was supportive regardless of our performance. As we prepared to depart, I decided to acquire a bandanna for myself. I returned to my preferred barmaid, who generously offered another round of shots in exchange for my bandanna. So, it's really just free shots, enjoyable bandannas, and a mechanical bull. What more could you possibly need?

yelp:train:259769.orig:
Overall, I'd tend to choose Trader Joes over F/E. In most cases the food tastes better. That and F/E sells some of the same stuff as Safeway for more.

F/E is supposed to be a healthy affordable store. Milk isn't healthy (and it's in too many of their products that don't need it -- fail for someone lactose intolerant), and the prices on some of your the meals here are just slightly lower than going to a restaurant for better food. 

If they would price match and produced better food without lactose all over the place, I'd give this place a better rating. Otherwise, it's just a place to go if I'm in the area or the rest of the places are closed.
yelp:train:259769.para:
Generally, I'd opt for Trader Joe's rather than Fresh & Easy. The taste of the food is superior in most instances. Additionally, Fresh & Easy offers items similar to those at Safeway but at a higher cost. 

Fresh & Easy is marketed as a health-conscious and cost-effective store. However, milk, which is not particularly healthy, is frequently included in their products that don't require it, posing a problem for those with lactose intolerance. The cost of some meals here is marginally less than dining out for superior quality food. 

If Fresh & Easy could align their pricing with competitors and improve their food quality by eliminating lactose, I'd assign a higher rating. Otherwise, it serves as a convenient option when I'm nearby or when other establishments are unavailable.

yelp:train:259813.orig: Ok place. Good for beer and relaxing. Just plan on staying a while. Sat at a table for 15-20 minutes before a server took our drink order. It took 30 minutes to get food and after asking for the check it took aboit 20 minutes before our server dropped it off. I might come back if I'm planning on staying a while. Other wise I'll try a place that pays more attention to the service.
yelp:train:259813.para: This spot is ideal for enjoying a beer and unwinding. It's worth staying for an extended period. We lingered at a table for about 15-20 minutes before a waiter attended to our drinks. The food arrived after a 30-minute wait, and it took another 20 minutes to receive the bill. I'll consider returning if I intend to linger, but for quicker service, I'll opt for a different establishment.

yelp:train:260187.orig:

yelp:train:260187.para:
Engrossing!

yelp:train:260447.orig:
I kind of feel bad giving this place only 1 star but I've given them many chances and 1 star is what they deserve. 

The food is overall pretty good. Whoever the chef is, bravo. It's worlds better than the typical Italian slop in this area. However, the variety and selection are lacking. As for the service, if there were stars that went the other way, I would give it a -5. I've been here three times and have never had good service. As a matter of fact, the last time I was there we had to walk out leaving a big fat 0 on the tip line. I really hate doing that too but when you're ignored for 20 minutes when there's no one else in the place you deserve it. 

This restaurant is also wayyyyyy too stuck up for its own good. I roll my eyes just thinking about it. None of the times I've been there has there been a decent crowd either. Maybe that should tell you something.
yelp:train:260447.para:
I somewhat regret rating this establishment a mere 1 star, despite offering numerous opportunities for improvement and acknowledging their right to this score. 

The culinary offerings are generally commendable, with the chef earning my applause for surpassing the commonplace Italian fare prevalent in this region. Nevertheless, the diversity and assortment fall short. In terms of service, had there been a system of negative stars, I would have assigned a -5. Having visited thrice, I've consistently encountered subpar service. The most recent visit culminated in us leaving a substantial zero on the tip line. I harbor a strong aversion to this, yet I believe they merit it when overlooked for an extensive period in a seemingly deserted venue. 

Additionally, this dining place appears excessively pretentious, to the point of self-sabotage. The thought of it alone prompts my eye-rolling. The lack of a substantial patronage during my visits should serve as a telling sign.

yelp:train:260983.orig:
I went here today for my bi-monthly eyebrow wax and I made a note that I have to update because since my last review this has really been my go-to place for eyebrows and they've always been great. This in large part has to do with the fact that they appear to now have a dedicated wax lady on hand, instead of just letting whoever isn't doing a pedicure take care of you.

I'm really mad at myself for this, but I cannot remember her name! I know it starts with a Z, so that should narrow it down for you. For the sake of this review, I'll act like we're old friends and Z is my cute little best friend nickname for her. Z is great. She always compliments my eyebrows and never asks if I ""want upper lip"". G + Z = BFF 4 Life
yelp:train:260983.para:
Today, I visited this location for my regular eyebrow waxing session and jotted down a reminder to update my review. The reason I consistently choose this place for eyebrow care is due to their introduction of a specialized waxing professional, rather than relying on someone who isn't performing a pedicure. 

Regrettably, I can't recall her name, but I'm aware it begins with a 'Z', which should help you identify her. In this review, I'll pretend we're old pals and refer to her as my adorable 'Z' nickname. G + Z = Best Friends Forever for Life

yelp:train:261380.para: Egg not fully cooked, generally of very low quality.

yelp:train:262066.orig: This review is for the Xtreme Couture MMA camp.  Randy Couture hosts these camps about twice per year and they are limited to 40 people.  My significant other recently attended the camp and had nothing but positive things to say about the experience. I watched a couple of the sessions and was amazed at how large and clean the gym area is.  I have been inside several MMA gyms and most are much smaller and don't always smell so great. yelp:train:262066.para:
This critique pertains to the Xtreme Couture MMA training sessions, which are conducted by Randy Couture roughly twice annually and accommodate a maximum of 40 participants. yelp:train:262713.para:
When CUT initially launched in Las Vegas, I was eager to experience it, fueled by the buzz surrounding the Beverly Hills branch. For my fifth wedding anniversary, I decided to indulge. 

5 stars for service - Despite our early (5:30pm reservation) arrival and a 20-minute delay, we were promptly seated after a brief interaction with the hostess. Our waiter made an immediate introduction. Throughout the evening, we were frequently attended to, and our water glasses were perpetually refilled (we opted for tap water, not bottled). We finished our meal swiftly (the entire dining experience lasted approximately 2 hours), yet we never felt hurried or pressured. The timing of the dishes was well-synchronized with our consumption, allowing ample time to digest between courses. Excellent communication between the front and back of the house!

4 stars for food - We were greeted with cheddar cheese puffs as a starter, which were not like Cheetos but reminiscent of Red Lobster chef muffins. Delicious. However, they were not included on the bread tray. My wife chose the fava bean and artichoke salad as her starter, which was unexpectedly unattractive. As someone who doesn't particularly enjoy beans, I might be prejudiced. My wife regretted not selecting a different dish

yelp:train:263002.orig: Rolls have been better and service was good today. 1 star back.
yelp:train:263002.para: Service quality improved and rolls tasted great today, but I'm still rating it 1 star.

yelp:train:263113.orig:
I read several of the reviews & they are consistent with what I've experienced.  I've been to this place about 5 times...both for lunch...and late night.  The food is actually pretty good.  I've had the BBQ pork & fries and it was very good.  At night, the place is fun.  They have the bull to ride...and it's interactive to meet people.

But, the BIG, BIG drawback is the service.  Seems like other people have had the same experience -  it's downright terrible.  Every single time I've been there I've had some issue (I'm not that picky either).  The service is very, very slow.  They hired some hot girls..but they certainly aren't the brightest.  The charged my friend for several drinks that we didn't have...and it took them almost 1/2 hour to correct it.

Because of the service, I can only give this place 2 stars.  Good food but I think it's run by a high Shool student.
yelp:train:263113.para:
I've perused numerous reviews, and they align with my own experiences. I've visited this establishment around five times, enjoying both lunch and late-night outings. The cuisine is genuinely commendable, with the BBQ pork and fries being exceptional. The ambiance is lively at night, offering interactive bull riding and social opportunities.

However, the significant downside is the subpar service. It appears others have shared this sentiment, describing it as abysmal. I've encountered issues every visit, despite not being overly discerning. The service is notably sluggish. Although they employed attractive young women, they seem to lack intelligence. They erroneously charged my companion for drinks we didn't consume, and it took nearly half an hour to rectify the mistake.

Due to these service issues, I'm rating this place a mere 2 stars. The food quality is good, but I suspect it's managed by someone with limited experience, possibly a high school student.

yelp:train:263427.orig: Just one word: YUM!\n\nOne of the better establishments on Mill. The ice cream is pretty good, and I like the cookies--nice and thin. They make all different kinds, but I just go with chocolate chip. Then you choose an ice cream (I like the oreo) and they will make a sandwich out if it. I get the half size (one cookie folded in half) and it is huge! The prices are pretty low, and my boyfriend likes the fresh lemonade they have (doesn't  mix well with ice cream though). The service is good, and the owner is usually there and is really friendly. A nice alternative to the over-priced Coldstone down the block ...
yelp:train:263427.para: Exclaiming: YUM!\n\nA top-notch spot on Mill Street, boasting delectable ice cream and thin, tasty cookies in various flavors, with a preference for chocolate chip. Here, you can select your ice cream (favoring oreo) and have it sandwiched with a cookie (half-sized fold). The pricing is reasonable, and my partner enjoys their fresh lemonade, though it doesn't pair well with ice cream. The service is commendable, and the owner, who is often present, exudes warmth. A delightful option compared to the costly Coldstone just a few steps away.

yelp:train:263712.orig:
I love ordering their food Thai-Hot (thats the hottest you can get here). If you like you're food spicy, you can't go wrong. Their pre-meal salads; which come with every dine-in meal, has an awesome salad dressing. They also sell their salad dressing for ($5) to take home. I forget how many oz. they said it was. I think its close to 12 or 16, but don't quote me on it. Every meal seems to come with a slice of fresh cut watermellon.  The watermellon is a nice refreshing pre or post meal snack and also light on the added calories; although the rest of the meal may not be.

My favorite dish is their garlic dish; either rice or noodle, ive had it with chicken and tofu before. The tofu is prepared in such a way that it has a crispy outside and a buttery inside. I don't think that I've ever ordered a tofu dish before and thought ""I might order this again some time."" 

Their lunch meals will cost you about $10-$11 after tax + tip, so I don't visit all the time, but they are a great choice if you can't stop thinking about thai food and you're in the midtown area near central ave and thomas.
yelp:train:263712.para:
I adore their Thai-Hot menu selection, which is the spiciest option available here. If you enjoy spicy food, you're bound to be satisfied. Accompanying every dine-in meal is a delicious salad with an impressive dressing. They also offer this salad dressing for purchase at $5 to enjoy at home. I'm uncertain about the exact ounce measurement, but it's likely around 12 or 16 ounces. Each meal is accompanied by a slice of fresh watermelon, perfect for a refreshing snack before or after eating, without adding too many calories.

My go-to dish is their garlic-infused rice or noodle, which I've tried with both chicken and tofu. The tofu is cooked to perfection, with a crispy exterior and a creamy interior. I've never ordered a tofu dish before, but I'm considering doing so again in the future.

Lunch meals at this place are priced between $10-$11 after tax and tip, which is why I don't visit frequently. However, it's an excellent option for those who have a craving for Thai food and are located in the midtown area near Central Avenue and Thomas Street.

yelp:train:264089.orig:
Crowded. Cheesy. But it's free.

Wow, so you really get what you pay for. This show is free and you shouldn't expect much. The viewing area gets really crowded and when it's your typical sweltering day in Vegas, this viewing area can be the worst place to be. 

The show is really bad. I miss the old show that used to be in this same lagoon, it actually made sense. Oh well, can't dwell on the past. 

Good: It's free.

Bad: Terrible show and packed viewing area.

Final: If you happened to walk by it and it's not crowded, stop and watch it so you can experience how bad it is.
yelp:train:264089.para:
Packed and subpar. It's complimentary, but don't anticipate a high-quality experience. On hot days in Vegas, this lagoon's viewing spot can be quite unpleasant. 

The quality of the show is disappointing. I long for the previous version that used to take place here, which had a coherent narrative. It's time to move on from the past. 

Pro: It's cost-free. 

Con: The show is of poor quality and the viewing space is overly crowded. 

Conclusion: Should you stumble upon it and it's not overly crowded, consider watching it to understand its lackluster nature.

yelp:train:264474.orig: This place was on triple D. One of the best tequila line ups I have seen and their beer selection is off the charts. I got the 4 taco sampler with plantains and chips and salsa. Also got a Mexican coke, in a glass bottle (the only way to have a coke).  Service was prompt and everyone was nice. It was a Tuesday night and a little slow.  There was a live band with a jazz flute. Nice touch.
yelp:train:264474.para: This establishment was highly rated on Dirty Dishes. I witnessed an exceptional array of tequila presentations, and their beer variety was unparalleled. I indulged in a 4-item taco platter featuring plantains and chips, accompanied by salsa. Additionally, I enjoyed a Mexican-style soda served in a glass bottle, the only acceptable way to savor it. The service was swift and the staff was amiable. It was a Tuesday evening with a moderate crowd. A live jazz flute band added a delightful ambiance.

yelp:train:264821.orig: The Yard House at Town Square is one of my favorite places for lunch or happy hour.  I like the large beer selection and all the menu items too.  My favorites are the double mac n cheese and the street tacos.  The burgers are very good too.  The staff is always awesome very friendly and take the time to really provide good customer service even though they are really busy.  I never feel rushed there.  It doesn't matter if its dining for two or twenty the service is always the same.  definitely a thumbs up in my book.
yelp:train:264821.para: Town Square's Yard House is a top spot for my lunch or happy hour outings. I appreciate the extensive beer variety and the diverse menu offerings. The double mac 'n' cheese and street tacos are my personal favorites, along with the quality burgers. The team is consistently outstanding, offering warm hospitality and prioritizing excellent customer service, even during peak times. I never feel hurried, and the service remains impeccable regardless of the number of diners. It's undoubtedly a solid recommendation from me.

yelp:train:264944.para: Bustling airport dining establishment. Sufficiently stated.

yelp:train:264953.orig: Okay, what is everyone ordering here because I recently had dinner here with my BF and we both thought it was very mediocre. \n\nWe tried 4 different types of rolls and the mixed tempura and thought everything was just okay. yelp:train:264953.para: Alright, what dishes are people choosing in this sushi spot since I had a meal here with my significant other and we both found it to be quite average? \n\nWe sampled four kinds of sushi rolls and the combination of tempura was just satisfactory. yelp:train:265541.para: The food was exceptionally delightful, as Larry David would say, but the service left us puzzled. It wasn't the most convenient arrangement. However, the tempura green beans stood out as a standout dish. The rest of the offerings were commendable. Despite the minor hiccup, I'd be inclined to revisit.

yelp:train:265918.orig:
Been here multiple times even as a child and still disappointed. 
Only went here again (in years) on Christmas believing that it might of improved & probably have better food since it's the holidays......but nope......still the same as it ever was. 

HARDLY any food choices. I think the Dessert section had MORE choices than the dinner section too. 

I really don't understand why there's always a line here. Mc Donald's in Midway is better than this. 

Really one star; gave it another for the chocolate fudge cake they had (probably the only good thing there in my opinion).
yelp:train:265918.para:

I struggle to comprehend the constant queues here. I find the McDonald's in Midway superior to this establishment. 

I'd rate it one star, but I'll give it an extra point for the chocolate fudge cake, which I believe is the only redeeming aspect.

yelp:train:266030.orig: They charged a cover, were stingy with the liquor, and the DJ sucked. Disappointing.
yelp:train:266030.para: They demanded a fee, were frugal with the drinks, and the disc jockey performed poorly. A letdown indeed.

yelp:train:266168.para:

yelp:train:266683.orig:
Unassuming deli spot with a huge menu including their own crafted meats, bagels, breakfast, and desserts. 4.5

Food: 4.5, Atmosphere: 3, Service: 4
Cost to worth it rating: 3
Return worthiness: yes!
Eve award: best non-burger sliders I've ever had

Highlights:
- Jewish sliders: tender sliced beef brisket on top of deliciously seasoned crispy potato pancakes in between 2 soft dense shiny challah buns. Top in with the gravy it comes with, and you're close to true bliss. Amazing!!! Though that man vs food guy tried to eat a dozen in a half hour--that's a bit much.
- Corned beef hash: one of my fave breakfast items and this is one of the best. Smooshed ground version with crisped edges but not processed tasting or too salty
- Fries: crispy wedges but potatoey soft inside. Fantastic when dipped in the gravy
- Brisket dip: twist on the traditional French the hub enjoyed
- Could take large groups: we had 16 and there was a party in the back room with 30

Lowlights:
- Some breakfast items have time restrictions: things like eggs benedicts are only served til 3pm (there was a crazy one I wanted to try on top of a potato pancake)

Had a great family meal here and would come
yelp:train:266683.para:
Casual deli with an extensive selection of homemade meats, bagels, morning fare, and sweet treats. 4.5 stars for food, 3 for ambiance, and 4 for service. The cost-to-value score is 3, but it's definitely worth returning to. Eve's accolade: the finest non-burger slider experience I've encountered.

Key Highlights:
- Jewish sliders: succulent sliced beef brisket atop flavorful crispy potato pancakes, nestled between two shiny, dense challah buns. Enhanced with the accompanying gravy, it's a near-perfect delight. However, the man vs. food enthusiast who attempted to consume a dozen in half an hour might find it excessive.
- Corned beef hash: a beloved breakfast dish, and this version is among the best. It's a ground beef version with crispy edges, but it's not overly processed or salty.
- Fries: crispy on the outside, soft on the inside. They're especially delicious when dipped in the gravy.
- Brisket dip: a unique take on the traditional French dish that the hub enjoyed.
- Accommodating large groups: we hosted 16 and there was a lively gathering in the back room with 30.

Minor Draw

My kid had the roadies or w/e they were supposed to be like slider's there was 2 missing the meat! So we call to see what's up maybe they had an off night. YAY!\n\nWe decide to take some friends with us since it was FREE. Well once again it was pretty gross no one really ate much, 2 people got their filets they ended up well done.
