yelp:test:457.orig:
Having grown up in North Carolina, I've had lots of Barbecue (and I also smoke my own).  I feel I can adequately judge the quality of BBQ.  This particular establishment was unique in that it's right off the side of a highway and has drive-in microphones and ordering stations straight out of the 50's.  I did feel a little uneasy in the parking lot as it was in a shady part of town, but not a big deal.  I ordered the 1/4 Barbecue chicken meal and substituted potato salad for the slaw and onion rings for the fries.  In addition I ordered a ""Minced"" barbecue sandwich, which is the classic barbecue that people would think of when talking about North Carolina style BBQ.   

First let me say that FoodNetwork came to this establishment for the unique nature of the 50's style drive-in and for the unique way that the pieces of barbecue chicken are prepared.  They are deep fried and then dunked in barbecue sauce.  I will say that it is unique; however as the above would suggest, it is quite greasy.  It was ""okay"" but I wouldn't say it is anything to specifically come here for.  

As for the barbecue, it is also ""okay;"" I can safely say that the meat is not smoked (there is no
yelp:test:457.para:
Having been raised in North Carolina, I've sampled ample Barbecue and even mastered the art of smoking my own. I believe I possess the expertise to assess the quality of BBQ. This specific venue stood out as it's situated adjacent to a highway, featuring drive-in microphones and ordering counters reminiscent of the 1950s. Although I felt slightly apprehensive in the dimly lit parking area, it wasn't a significant concern. I opted for a quarter portion of Barbecue chicken, swapping out the slaw for potato salad and onion rings for fries. Additionally, I chose a "Minced" barbecue sandwich, a quintessential North Carolina BBQ that comes to mind. 

Before delving into the details, it's worth noting that FoodNetwork visited this establishment due to its distinctive 1950s drive-in ambiance and the unconventional preparation of the barbecue chicken pieces, which are deep-fried and then submerged in barbecue sauce. While this method is indeed unique, it results in a notably oily texture. I would describe it as merely satisfactory, but it doesn't warrant a specific visit. 

Regarding the barbecue itself, it's also fair to say it's merely satisfactory. I can confidently assert that the meat is not smoked, as

yelp:test:471.orig:
I've heard this restaurant from listening to NPR in Charlotte, so I went and invited some of my friends and decided to come here to check it out. Here are my reviews.

Venue - the ambiance inside the restaurant is like being in Japan. If you have a large group of people, your group will be sitting as if you're sitting on a floor, but your not. The sits are elevated and the center piece is wide open. It's a comfortable sitting arrangement.

Sushi - the Unagi (Eel) was cooked perfectly. The softcrab shells are not bad, but I had better ones before.  The rice was cooked very well not to sticky or clumpy. They need better selections in sushi.

Presentation - the restaurant lacks in presentation.  It was a very simple dish put together.  

Sake - they are pricey. $15.00 minimum. 

Ramen - the soup was very tasty.  

Overall,  if you are craving for ramen, this is the best place so far I've tasted. As for sushi, I would only come here once. I've had much better sushi with awesome presentation and much better selections in California before.  I still have yet to find a sushi that will replace my experienced in California. Also, if you don't tip enough. You will be called back
yelp:test:471.para:
After tuning into NPR in Charlotte, I chose this eatery for a group outing. Here's my critique:

Setting - The interior gives off a Japanese vibe. Large groups will find themselves seated on raised platforms, with a spacious centerpiece. It offers a cozy seating experience.

Sushi - The Unagi (Eel) was expertly prepared. The softcrab shells were decent, but I've had superior ones elsewhere. The rice was well-cooked, avoiding any stickiness or clumpiness. However, they could improve their sushi variety.

Presentation - The establishment falls short in presentation. The dishes were presented in a straightforward manner.

Sake - The cost is steep, with a minimum of $15.00. 

Ramen - The soup was delicious. 

In summary, if you're in the mood for ramen, this place is top-notch based on my experiences. However, for sushi, I'd only visit once. I've previously enjoyed better sushi with impressive presentation and a wider selection in California. I'm yet to find a sushi that can match my past experiences in California. Also, be mindful of tipping; insufficient tips may result in a return visit.

yelp:test:475.orig:
While there were no insect carcasses in my food, I was still not very impressed with my meal at PF Chang's.  I went for a ""business lunch"" with my boss.  Who thought I would ever enjoy working more than eating??--I think this meal was a first!

I got steamed veggies and brown rice.  Now I expected it to be pretty bland, since it mentioned no sauces added at all.  But the vegetables were rubbery, not crisp like they should be after a good steaming. The rice was pretty underdone as well, so all-in-all, they got nothing right.  I tried adding some sauces to liven it up a bit, but it was too little, too late.

Perhaps the biggest disappointment was the egg drop soup.  I usually add pepper to mine because I like the extra kick, but this needed much more help than a little pepper.  It was very bland, and didn't taste like anything.  Tasteless egg in water is definitely NOT something you want to keep eating.  And, of course, there was no salt and pepper on the table, so I couldn't even enjoy it the way I like. 

Because I didn't pay, I didn't complain to the waiter, but normally this would not have passed by me.  Though the lunch prices are pretty reasonable, I still would not r
yelp:test:475.para:
Despite the absence of insect remnants in my dish, my experience at PF Chang's for a professional lunch with my supervisor left me underwhelmed. I anticipated a lackluster meal, given the absence of any sauces, but the steamed vegetables were disappointingly tough, and the rice was undercooked. Attempting to enhance the flavor with additional sauces proved futile. The egg drop soup, a staple of my order, was particularly disheartening, lacking in taste and requiring more than just a sprinkle of pepper for improvement. The absence of seasoning options on the table further diminished my dining experience. Although I refrained from voicing my dissatisfaction due to not having paid, I would typically not overlook such a subpar meal. Despite the reasonable lunch prices, I would hesitate to recommend this establishment.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original meaning, topic, sentiment, emotion, and intent while using different wording and sentence structure. The length is roughly the same as the original text.)

yelp:test:568.orig: This is a great bar if you have kids.... I know that sounds weird but listen. They have a beach  and tiki bar in the rear with cornhole, beer pong, ping pong, horseshoes etc.... They have a stage out there for live music. Big portions of food for not alot of cash. Becoming a Friday night tradition
yelp:test:568.para: If you're traveling with children, this establishment is an excellent choice... It may seem unusual, but pay attention. They offer a beach and tiki bar area at the back, complete with cornhole, beer pong, ping pong, and horseshoes. There's also a stage for live performances. Enjoy generous food portions at an affordable price, making it a beloved Friday night ritual.

yelp:test:581.orig: I took my car here to get my brakes replaced.  They did the work quickly and at a good price.  I went here on a recommendation from a friend, and now I recommend it to my friends when they need work done.
yelp:test:581.para: I brought my vehicle to this place for brake replacement. They completed the task efficiently and offered a reasonable cost. A friend suggested this location, and now I suggest it to my peers for their service needs.

yelp:test:582.orig: 4 stars for Hardee's ?!?  It's no Culver's by a long shot but that Thick Burger was damn tasty !   I don't know if the restaurant was clean but the drive thru service was good.
yelp:test:582.para: 4-star rating for Hardee's ?!? Although it doesn't match Culver's standards, the flavorful Thick Burger was exceptionally delicious! The cleanliness of the place is uncertain, but the drive-thru service was commendable.

yelp:test:605.orig: I was bringing my family to Cracker Barrow today a group of 6 but after hearing they fired a 73 year old Vet for handing out a Corn muffin I changed my mind...... I hope others feel the same way......
yelp:test:605.para:
I had plans to take my loved ones to Cracker Barrow with a party of six, but upon learning they dismissed a 73-year-old veteran for distributing a Corn muffin, I reconsidered my decision... I trust others will share this sentiment.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original message about changing plans due to a controversial incident involving a veteran and a Corn muffin, while expressing a hope for shared feelings among others. The length is kept similar to the original text.)

yelp:test:607.orig: Another chain sit down by the mall,  but not at the top of my list. The food hasn't seemed to change since I've gone here except for less options.  Waiting for a table is common unless you go at really off peak times. Recently got a burger there. Asked for well done,  and burger arrived bloody and red.  Waiter took it back and about 5 minutes brought the same burger back and was still pink on the inside.  Was offered something else,  but the others I was with were already done.  Did get a coupon for a return visit. Good deal with the 2 for $20 and an app if your food is cooked right.
yelp:test:607.para: Not at the forefront of my preferred dining spots, this mall-adjacent chain offers unchanged culinary offerings with fewer choices. Table reservations are typical unless visiting during non-peak hours. I recently ordered a well-done burger, which was served bloody and red. The staff corrected the issue, but a similar, undercooked burger was re-served after a brief interval. An alternative dish was suggested, though my companions had finished theirs. I received a voucher for a future visit, which seems like a fair trade-off for the 2-for-$20 deal and the promise of proper food preparation via their app.

yelp:test:615.orig: I've been to Monty's at least once for every meal. The omelettes are to die for, huge in quantity unique in ingredients- highly recommend the spinach and feta. The salads are the same thing, definitely large and delicious. Last night I went for dinner and got the meatless loaf, and now I want the recipe for the cashew gravy (if my memory serves me correctly, it was cashew...) to put on EVERYTHING. Amazing shakes and malts complete the perfect comfort/diner food experience.
yelp:test:615.para: I've frequented Monty's for each meal at least once. The omelettes are exceptional, abundant in size and distinct in ingredients, I wholeheartedly suggest the spinach and feta. The salads match this standard, being generously portioned and tasty. Recently, I dined there and opted for the meatless loaf, and now I'm keen on obtaining the cashew-based gravy recipe (assuming my recollection is accurate, it's cashew-based) to season all dishes. The delightful shakes and malts round off an ideal comfort/diner food experience.

yelp:test:627.orig:
I really dislike Menard's.  For every positive interaction I have, I have two negatives ones.  My husband and I just bought a house, so you can imagine how much time we spend here.  I prefer Home Depot but the prices are so much lower at Menard's.

In the matter of two weeks, all of this happened:

1. I bought a can of paint for our guest room.  I wanted the best paint, with the primer, all the bells and whistles.  I was covering purple.  I needed it.  The salesperson said I could pick from any four.  Yet, he could not tell me why one was rated higher or called premium over the other.  It was weird.  Like here are your options but I can not tell you what their difference really is.  And some were the same brand.

2. When painting the ceiling of said room, we open up a can of paint and notice it has clumps in it.  This paint was about six months old.  Nothing happened to it.  So we go back to Menard's.  We have shopped at several area Menard's, because we are about convenience.  The lady at the counter was SO rude.  We did not have our receipt and could not find it in their system.  We pay for most things in cash and apparently this is NOT a good idea at Menard's.  It had a Me
yelp:test:627.para:
I truly have a strong aversion to Menard's. Every positive encounter I experience is overshadowed by two negative ones. Since we recently purchased a home, the amount of time we dedicate to it is significant. Despite this, I lean towards Home Depot, yet I find Menard's prices to be considerably more competitive.

In just two weeks, the following events unfolded:

1. I sought out the finest paint for our guest room, complete with primer and all the extras. I was aiming for a purple hue and it was essential. The salesperson offered me a choice of any four, but couldn't explain why one was superior or premium compared to the others. It was perplexing. It felt like they were presenting options but couldn't clarify the actual distinctions. Additionally, some were from the same manufacturer.

2. While painting the ceiling of that room, we discovered clumps in the paint can, which was approximately six months old. Nothing had affected it. We returned to Menard's, having shopped at various local Menard's for their convenience. The cashier at the counter was extremely unpleasant. We couldn't locate our receipt and it wasn't recognized in their system. We usually pay in cash, but it seems that's not a preferred method at Menard's. It had a Me...

yelp:test:653.orig: I have been to The Ultimate several times for massages with Ellen and would highly recommend her.  She is very personable, friendly and professional.  I feel extremely relaxed after our sessions.  I also used Ellen for a prenatal massage when pregnant. Being as big and uncomfortable as I was, I was worried if I would be able to relax fully.  Ellen has blankets and pillows just for that reason! Super comfortable and she remembers to ask about the baby after she was born. Highly recommend!\n\nThe only reason I did not give 5 stars was that the hallway outside the room can get a bit loud if people are walking down, talking or laughing. They should maybe make that more of a quiet space with notices that people are in session.  Nothing Ellen could help though!
yelp:test:653.para:
I've visited The Ultimate multiple times for massages with Ellen, and I wholeheartedly suggest her services. Ellen is incredibly approachable, amiable, and maintains a high level of professionalism. Post-massage, I am left feeling incredibly at ease. I also sought Ellen's expertise for a prenatal massage during my pregnancy. Given my considerable size and discomfort, I was apprehensive about achieving complete relaxation. Fortunately, Ellen provided extra blankets and pillows for this purpose. The comfort was unparalleled, and she always inquired about the newborn after delivery. I wholeheartedly endorse her services.

The sole reason I refrained from awarding a perfect score was the noise level in the hallway outside the room when people are moving, conversing, or laughing. It would be beneficial if they could create a more serene environment with signs indicating that clients are in session. However, Ellen's assistance in this regard was not applicable.

yelp:test:662.orig: For the all hype this places gets, it sure didn't live up to it. Sure, it was busy- what place isn't on a Friday night in Wisconsin. Rail drinks were prices right- two drinks for $6.00. I ordered the lake perch- what a DISAPPOINTMENT. If you've been to Door County/eastern WI and had perch there, don't bother with Tobys perch. It was not good. My cottage cheese was warm, and my date's \""salad\"" was lettuce with salad dressing plopped on it. No veggies, croutons- nothing. The server was nice enough, for bring so overwhelmed and busy.
yelp:test:662.para: Despite the significant buzz surrounding it, it failed to meet expectations. Certainly, it was bustling, as any Friday night spot in Wisconsin would be. The cost of rail drinks was reasonable, at $6.00 for two. I opted for the lake perch, which turned out to be a letdown. If you've enjoyed perch in Door County/eastern WI, you might want to skip Tobys' offering. It fell short of quality. My cottage cheese was lukewarm, and my companion's "salad" consisted merely of lettuce with a random splash of dressing, devoid of any vegetables or croutons. The attentive server, despite the hectic environment, did their best.

yelp:test:700.orig: Decent drinks + chill atmosphere + Irish Nachos (oh God yes) + lack of sketchy people grinding on you = WIN.
yelp:test:700.para: Quality beverages + relaxed vibe + irresistible Irish Nachos + absence of troublemakers = A definite win.

yelp:test:726.orig: Clybourne is the best student bar in Champaign. Unlike most of the other campus bars, Clybourne offers a multi-floored facility, with plenty of room for sitting, drinking, and dancing. Prices are awesome! Thursdays feature $1 Coronas, Tuesdays are \""Wine Nights\"" where they serve $8 bottles of wine and champagne. Sundays, my favorite, are $1 you-call-its. The music is always great and the place is slammed most nights of the week. I've hosted lots of parties there-- and I always get a ridiculous amount of booze for the prices I pay (also get a private room).
yelp:test:726.para: Champaign's premier student bar, Clybourne, stands out from its campus counterparts with its spacious multi-level setup, providing ample space for patrons to relax, enjoy beverages, and groove. The cost-effectiveness is impressive! Thursdays bring $1 Coronas, Tuesdays host "Wine Nights" with $8 wine and champagne, and Sundays offer $1 you-call-its. The music quality is consistently high, and the venue is packed throughout the week. I've thrown numerous gatherings there, and I'm consistently amazed by the quantity of drinks I receive for the prices I pay, including access to a private room.

yelp:test:727.orig:
They seem to have everything. Obscure films, B films, foreign films, nearly every weird movie I've found out on the internet, they have it. (One time there was some anime I wanted to see but they didn't have, but they explained that all the copies out there were pirated, and they'd be happy to add it to their collection if I could find a legitimate source for them.)

Secondly... its pretty cheap if you buy a renters block.

I kind of wish there was a way to return videos without wading into campus, though.
yelp:test:727.para:
It appears they possess a vast array of cinematic works, including indie, B-grade, and international films, as well as most unconventional movies discovered online. (Once, I desired a specific anime, but they informed me that all available copies were illegally copied, and they would gladly include it in their library if I could provide a genuine source.)

Additionally, the cost is quite reasonable when purchasing a rental block.

I somewhat regret the lack of a method to return videos without having to navigate through campus grounds.

yelp:test:728.orig: It's like a portal into a chasm of anime, classics, world, documentary and varied films and cartoons. For Champaign, these guys really have an outstanding collection of rare films.\n\nWhat prevents me from giving it 5 starts is their stupid rule that you must have a special card and meet special requirements to rent a film from them, including being over 18 (for *ANY* film)
yelp:test:728.para: This platform serves as a gateway to a vast array of anime, timeless classics, global cinema, documentaries, and diverse animations and movies. The collection boasts exceptional rarity, particularly for Champaign's aficionados.\n\nThe reason I withhold a full 5-star rating is their peculiar policy mandating a unique card and specific conditions to be met for renting any film, notably requiring an age of 18 or above.

yelp:test:739.orig: The sangria here is awful. I think it was a tequila sunrise. The food is greasy and not in a good way. The only thing good was the goat cheese. But it is goat cheese. How can you mess that up?
yelp:test:739.para: The sangria served here is disappointing, possibly akin to a tequila sunrise. The cuisine is unappetizingly oily. The sole positive aspect was the goat cheese, which is questionable to ruin. How could one tarnish such a simple delight?

yelp:test:742.orig: I love this place.  My friends and I try to have a 'girl's night out' once a month and we frequent Radio Maria because of the delicious cuisine and the atmosphere.  It is relaxing and has several conversation pieces.  The service is spectacular.  This is one of my favorite local spots to dine in Champaign
yelp:test:742.para: Champaign is a cherished local dining destination for me and my pals. We aim to organize a monthly 'girl's night out' and often choose Radio Maria due to its delectable food and welcoming ambiance. It provides a calming environment with various engaging topics. The level of service is exceptional.

yelp:test:755.orig: Wow. I have been going to this practice for 3-4 years. I have had some troubles with them in the past but this is the kicker of them all. I just called and explained to the person at the front desk that I have been having some breast pain and didn't know if I should come in earlier than my Oct. 1st  Well Woman exam. Her response was, \""Well, if you come in early you will have to pay for an office visit.\"" I said, \""well if I wait I'll just talk to her about it at my Well Woman.\"" Her reply, \""if you talk to her about it then, then you will be charged extra.\"" My reply, \""just for talking about it??\"" Her reply, \""yup, I don't know what to tell you. Just go to your primary care physician.\"" I then explained to her that this was a gynecological issue... No response. Her overall tone was brash, rude, and short. Did I mention uncaring.\n\nUnbelievable. Never, ever have I been so appalled. A woman calls and says she has breast pain and isn't sure if she should come in and this is how the front desk responds!! I'm outraged and waiting for someone to call me back from the office. I think Dr. Johnstone has the right to know how the front desk is treating her patients.
yelp:test:755.para:
I've been attending this clinic for about 3-4 years now. Despite previous issues, this situation stands out as particularly upsetting. I recently spoke to the receptionist, mentioning my recent breast discomfort and uncertainty about scheduling an earlier appointment than my upcoming October 1st check-up. Her reply was, "If you come in early, you'll have to cover the cost of an office visit." I suggested, "Well, if I wait, I can discuss it during my Well Woman appointment." She retorted, "If you discuss it then, you'll incur additional charges." I questioned, "Why charge for just discussing it?" Her response was, "Yes, that's correct. Just visit your primary care doctor." I clarified that it was a gynecological concern, but received no further reply. Her tone was abrasive, impolite, and brief. I've never felt so disregarded. I'm incensed and anticipate a call back from the office. I believe Dr. Johnstone should be informed about the front desk's treatment of patients.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original sentiment, topic, emotion, and intent while altering the wording and sentence structure. The length is approximately the same as the original text.)

yelp:test:767.orig: HUGE disappointment!!!! Stopped for a quick dinner before a show. Ordered 2 burgers medium. They came out extremely well done & the buns were hard & dry. The waitress took them back to the kitchen & returned with 2 more well done burgers! What the heck?! When we told her (& showed her), she apologized & took 20% off the bill. We didn't have time for round 3. They didn't even send a manager over. $30 for an inedible meal. We will not be back. I'd recommend trying somewhere else.
yelp:test:767.para: Extreme dissatisfaction! We grabbed a fast meal before an event. We requested two medium-sized burgers. They arrived overcooked with tough, parched buns. The server brought them back and replaced them with two more overcooked burgers. What a mess! When we pointed it out and presented the evidence, she apologized and reduced our bill by 20%. Unfortunately, we didn't have the chance to try again. No manager was summoned. A $30 bill for a completely unpalatable meal. We'll definitely not return. I suggest going elsewhere.

yelp:test:771.orig: I have been going to this IHOP every month for 4 years. Our group is anywhere from 8 to 25. There are only two places in the restaurant that accommodate groups and for the most part, we have been seated relatively quickly. Over the past year, service has gone down hill. It started taking forever to get our order taken, get our drinks, or get our food. We are a very forgiving bunch and know it's not easy to serve a large group but as service started really sliding, our last trip ended the relationship. We had about 20 people and knew we would have to wait a bit, but after 30 minutes, we inquired how long and it was like \""your waiting for a table?\""the kept sitting people at the tables that only could accommodate large groups. How can you not remember a group when they take up the whole lobby? We called a near by breakfast place and they were thrilled to have our party, which grew smaller since some left at that point. We found a new home and they will get 5 stars on my review.
yelp:test:771.para: For the past four years, I've frequented this IHOP monthly with a group size ranging from 8 to 25. Generally, we've been able to find seating promptly at two designated areas for large groups. However, in the last year, the service quality has significantly deteriorated. It began to take an excessive amount of time to have our orders processed, receive drinks, or obtain our meals. Despite our understanding of the challenges in serving a large group, the decline in service quality led us to end our relationship after a 20-person gathering. After waiting for 30 minutes without a clear timeframe, we were met with indifference from staff who seemed to forget about our group. We then opted for a breakfast spot nearby, which welcomed our smaller group and received a glowing review from us. We've since found a new dining destination and are confident in giving it a 5-star rating.

yelp:test:804.orig:
This should have been a better experience... 

I'll begin with the food.  We arrived on a Sunday afternoon after a visit to the Phoenix Art Museum.  We ordered a BLT salad off the lunch menu and a manicotti dish.  We also included a cup of the minestrone soup for a buck.  The salad was good and was accompanied by fresh, hot bread.  The minestrone soup was outstanding.  The salad and soup were brought out early, as we requested, and we had ample time to complete the salad before our entree arrived.  The manicotti was fine and a good enough portion size that we had to box some.   So far, a good dining experience.

Then the bill arrives.  The salad was 8.50 and then entree was full price.  We questioned the bill, as the ""lunch menu"" said the salad would be 5.99 and the entree 1.50 off.  The server actually apologizes and says he'll have the manager correct the mistake.  Then he comes back and tells us ""Sorry, manager says lunch prices only apply Mon-Fri"".  Nowhere on the menu does it say lunch only applies Monday through Friday, and we were never told.  I didn't press the issue, paid the bill and off we go.  

What could have been an overall pleasant experience ruined by
yelp:test:804.para:
This should have been a more enjoyable experience... 

Let's start with the meal. We got there on a Sunday afternoon following a trip to the Phoenix Art Museum. We ordered a BLT salad from the lunch menu and a manicotti dish. We also got a cup of minestrone soup for a dollar. The salad was tasty and came with fresh, warm bread. The minestrone soup was exceptional. The salad and soup were served early as we had asked, giving us enough time to finish the salad before our main course arrived. The manicotti was satisfactory and the portion size was adequate, leading us to box some. So far, it was a satisfactory dining experience.

Then the check comes. The salad cost 8.50 and the main course was at full price. We raised concerns about the bill, as the lunch menu indicated the salad would be 5.99 and the main course 1.50 off. The server apologized and promised to have the manager rectify the error. However, the manager informed us that the lunch prices only apply from Monday to Friday. This was not communicated to us, nor was it stated on the menu. I chose not to press the matter and paid the bill, then left. 

What could have been a delightful experience was marred by this issue.

yelp:test:812.orig: This has been my car wash since I lived in midtown off 3rd street and Thomas. They do a great job, and are very accommodating if they miss a spot. They tend to be somewhat expensive, but then again they are not scratching your car with machines. I used to get the side wash with my Audi because of some modifactions that kept it from being on the rails, and for $15 you couldn't get a better wash in town. \n\nI don't recommend their detail service, as they are not very complete, but for car washes A+
yelp:test:812.para: I've been utilizing this car wash facility in midtown, near 3rd street and Thomas, for years. They consistently deliver excellent service and are understanding if they overlook a spot. Although their prices are on the higher side, they refrain from damaging your vehicle with machinery. Previously, I opted for the side wash for my Audi due to certain alterations that prevented it from being stable, and at $15, it offered superior cleanliness in the area. However, I would not suggest their detailing service as it lacks thoroughness, but when it comes to car washes, they deserve an A+ rating.

yelp:test:883.orig:
This has to be the most ghetto and disrespectful dive I've ever been to. I usually don't play the race card, but unless you are a Spanish speaking Latino you will not be treated well by the staff.

As soon as I walked up to the counter, a pregnant cashier rolled her eyes and asked dully what I wanted. I couldn't pronounce the name of the combo I wanted but I blurted out the number associated with it and it had a picture. She looked over her shoulder at one of her associates and said something. The only words I caught were ""token gringo customer.""

They shared a giggle.  They were speaking in that half-assed Spanish that has a little English mixed in. Suffice it to say I was offended and promptly cancelled the order. I have not returned since then
yelp:test:883.para:
This location must be the most degrading and insulting dive I've encountered. Normally, I refrain from invoking racial issues, but it's clear that non-Spanish speaking Latinos will not receive proper treatment from the employees.

Upon approaching the counter, a pregnant cashier glared at me and inquired in a monotonous tone about my desired item. Unable to correctly articulate the combo's name, I mentioned its number, which displayed a picture. She glanced at a colleague and muttered something. The phrase I discerned was "token gringo customer."

They chuckled. They were conversing in a subpar Spanish with a bit of English interspersed. It's evident that I felt insulted, leading me to immediately cancel the order. I have not revisited the place since that incident.

yelp:test:918.orig: I have had terrible luck with this lawn service recently. Please do not furnish Sergio with your credit card number; he will put the card through on PayPal, which is very hard to stop when he is processing fraudulent charges. His crew stole a valuable tree-lopping tool from me at a house I was leasing right before I moved out. Then, after I moved out, he has billed me for monthly services for two months running because, despite being informed by me on the phone, he claims that I have to terminate his services in writing. \nThis is the worst consumer experience I have had in years and I feel that this behavior has to be stopped. I'm certain most people don't count obtaining a new credit card and taking a trip to small claims court as among the experiences they are looking forward to when hiring a landscaper.
yelp:test:918.para: Lately, I've encountered significant issues with the lawn care company I've engaged with. Refrain from giving Sergio your credit card details, as he intends to use PayPal for transactions, which is notoriously difficult to reverse once fraudulent charges are made. A cherished tree-cutting instrument was unlawfully taken by his team from my rented property just before I vacated. Following my departure, I was charged for monthly maintenance for two consecutive months, despite my verbal notification to him that services must be formally canceled. This has been the most distressing customer service encounter I've faced in a long time, and I am convinced that such conduct must be curtailed. I am certain that most individuals would not anticipate having to deal with credit card replacement and small claims court visits as part of their landscaping service experience.

yelp:test:960.orig: What happened to all of the coverage on the local sports?  The Arcadia News used to be very supportive and involved in Arcadia High School athletics.  No articles and only some pictures of some of the sports these days.  Shouldn't a local paper support its local high school?
yelp:test:960.para: Why is there a noticeable decline in the local sports coverage by The Arcadia News? Previously, this publication demonstrated considerable backing and participation in the athletics of Arcadia High School. Nowadays, it's mostly devoid of articles and limited to a few sports images. Isn't it expected for a community newspaper to uphold its local high school's sports?

yelp:test:979.orig:
I was across the street for a Dr appointment and decided to step into the AJs after to browse since it was ""right there"". Haven't been into one in years for the same reason that I probably won't return after the recent visit: way overpriced for things I can buy elsewhere. So, you'd think that their deli or bakery or something would stand out, but not that I can tell. I was there in the AM so I did try a slice of the breakfast pizza that was out in the deli. First off, it took me several minutes to be served because the staff was busily ignoring me. Then when I did finally get my slice, I went to pay and eat it, and the thing was cold and chewy. The crust was just so tough. The eggs were somewhat dried out. I was seriously underwhelmed. 

The store was practically dead the whole time I was wandering around. The staff outnumbered the patrons BY FAR. How do these p
yelp:test:979.para:
I found myself on the opposite sidewalk for a medical consultation and opted to explore the AJs nearby, as it was conveniently close. I haven't frequented one in a long time, primarily due to its exorbitant prices for items I can acquire at standard grocery outlets. Most of the merchandise in the shop is readily available at any typical supermarket for a lower cost. They offer a limited selection of upscale goods, but I can locate those elsewhere as well. 

One would expect their deli or bakery section to be distinctive, but it didn't impress me. I contemplated sampling something from the bakery display, but the prices were excessive and the presentation unappealing. I visited during the morning, so I sampled a slice of the breakfast pizza from the deli. It took a while to receive service since the employees seemed preoccupied with other tasks. When I finally got my slice, it was cold and chewy, with a tough crust and somewhat dehydrated eggs. I was thoroughly disappointed. 

The store was almost empty while I was meandering around. The number of employees greatly exceeded the number of customers. How do these pizzas...

yelp:test:990.orig:
I've been popping into the George and Dragon nearly every Thursday since last April for trivia nights.  I like the place.  The trivia host is entertaining and the place feels worn in, but not worn down.  I feel comfortable and welcome every time I visit.  Most weeks I end up ordering a couple beers from the rather large selection.  The drink prices, while high for some people's tastes, are comparable to what I've seen in other places.  Imports are going to cost more, it's the price you pay to have a selection of Boddington's, Murphy's and Guinness all in one place, among other things.

Normally on trivia nights I don't end up getting food, as although I find their portions proportional to the prices, I don't feel I need to eat half my weight in fish and chips in one sitting.  I have no qualms with the quality on the few occasions I've grabbed some eats, for example the curry chicken is very flavorful and highly recommended.  The dragon wings are another of my favorite, spicy but not overwhelming.  The fish and chips, as previously mentioned, are served on a giant platter and have generally been excellent.

I recommend at least one visit to this bar.  Don't be scared off by the
yelp:test:990.para:
Since last April, I've made it a habit to visit the George and Dragon every Thursday for trivia nights. I appreciate the ambiance of the place, with an engaging trivia host and a cozy, well-maintained atmosphere. I always feel at ease and welcomed during my visits. Most times, I end up choosing a couple of beers from their extensive range. The prices are a bit steep for some, but they're on par with other establishments. The higher cost of imports is justified by the convenience of having a variety of beers like Boddington's, Murphy's, and Guinness available. 

On trivia nights, I usually skip the food, as I find the portions reasonable for the price. However, I've had no issues with the quality of the food when I've tried it, such as the delicious curry chicken and the spicy yet balanced dragon wings. The fish and chips, which I've mentioned before, are served generously and consistently well. 

I highly suggest making at least one trip to this bar. Don't let the prices deter you.

yelp:test:1000.orig: Wow. Just, wow. As a former employee of this location, I'm sorely disappointed. I used to be a hostess here and always LOVED the food. So I figured I'd take my boyfriend to grab a nice breakfast. Boy was I wrong. I ordered the huevos rancheros with chorizo (always been my favorite) and ended up with eggs and bland potatoes, with chunky sour cream (ew) and a light sprinkling of chorizo. Um, what? I paid almost 30 bucks for this? The food was bland and not good at all. I couldn't even finish my meal it was that bad. I'll never go back. How disappointing. Maybe you should stop recruiting your employees/chefs from McDonalds. The good egg has really let itself go.
yelp:test:1000.para: As a past worker of this place, I'm deeply disheartened. I was a breakfast hostess who adored the cuisine here, so I thought I'd treat my partner to a delightful morning meal. However, I was mistaken. I chose the huevos rancheros with chorizo (my preferred choice) but received just eggs and tasteless potatoes, with overly chunky sour cream (gross) and a minimal sprinkle of chorizo. What a letdown! I paid nearly 30 dollars for this underwhelming dish. The food was unappetizing and utterly unsatisfactory. I won't be returning. Perhaps it's time to reconsider your hiring practices, especially for your staff and chefs. The quality of your establishment has significantly declined.

yelp:test:1004.orig: This was my first experience eating Jack in the Box since I moved from GA to AZ 2 days ago. The service was horrible! Cashier had attitude when I told her I was still reviewing the menu. When I was ready to place my order she was very rude & sighing as if she needed me to speed up. Then I watched as she prepared her food, placed it on a tray & walked off as my food sat in the window. The drive-thru person came to see if I had been helped & proceeded to bag my food after I told him I was waiting. This place needs better service.
yelp:test:1004.para: My initial visit to Jack in the Box following my relocation from GA to AZ just two days prior was marred by poor service. The cashier displayed a negative demeanor when I was perusing the menu, and when I was prepared to order, she was impolite and seemed frustrated, as if I should hasten my decision. I observed her food preparation, which she then left on a tray, while my meal remained untouched in the window. The drive-thru attendant checked if I had been assisted and bagged my food after I indicated I was still waiting. Clearly, this establishment requires improvements in customer service.

yelp:test:1025.orig: Must have been an off day last time. These partners are phenomenal!
yelp:test:1025.para: It seems like there was a rough patch previously. The collaboration with these individuals is truly exceptional!

yelp:test:1035.orig:
Have been dying to try this kosher place for some time.
Went tonight and ordered a large 3 cheese pizza.  O M G american cheese???
I asked also for baked ziti and the lady said her ziti can't keep for a week so they don't make it.
Are you kidding me?
It was 19.00 with a drink.
I put the pizza in the trunk and went to La Bella
yelp:test:1035.para:
I've been eager to experience this kosher eatery for a while.
Decided to visit last night and ordered a hefty 3-cheese pizza.
I also requested baked ziti and was informed by the woman that their ziti spoils within a week, hence they don't prepare it.
Are you serious?
The total came to $19 with a beverage.
I placed the pizza in my car and proceeded to La Bella.

yelp:test:1051.orig: I miss Karsh's (no longer live in AZ), although I really like Bea's Bakery out here.  Chompies' bakery rivaled them on some items, but Karsh's made the BEST cakes.....I got one for my daughter's Bat Mitzvah.....and smaller cakes for birthdays and such.  Absolutely YUMMMMMMMMY.  Perfect cake, perfect icing.  Great challah, too.  Their other bakery items were also quite good....rugelach, hamentashen, brownies, cookies.  I'm just glad I didn't live close to them when I lived there.  Downside...they were always crowded, and I always had to wait awhile before getting served.
yelp:test:1051.para:
I yearn for the presence of Karsh (who has departed from AZ), but I thoroughly enjoy Bea's Bakery in this area. Chompies' bakery was a close competitor on certain products, yet Karsh's cakes were unparalleled. I procured one for my daughter's Bat Mitzvah, along with modest cakes for celebrations. The taste was sublime, with flawless cake and icing. Their challah was also commendable. Other bakery items like rugelach, hamentashen, brownies, and cookies were notably good. I'm relieved I didn't reside nearby during their tenure. The downside was the constant bustle and the need to wait for service.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original meaning, sentiment, emotion, and intent, while altering the wording and sentence structure. The length is approximately the same as the original text.)

yelp:test:1072.orig: To be honest, this place sucks so much as compared to how it used to be. Like all vintage clothing stores, you have to dig through piles of crap to find that one diamond in the rough. Buffalo Exchange is no longer like that store. Now, you just dig through garbage and getting nothing out of it but a grimy feel and a fetid stench of indigence on your hands. I also found out, after selling some clothing here that Their selection here just sucks.\n\nThe only thing that's generally alright is their shoe selection. I got a pretty sweet pair of Nikes for $30.
yelp:test:1072.para: Honestly, this location has significantly deteriorated compared to its former glory, much like other vintage apparel shops where you sift through rubbish to unearth a hidden gem. Unlike those stores, Buffalo Exchange has transformed into a place where you merely sift through trash, leaving you with a dirty sensation and a pungent odor of poverty clinging to you. Moreover, I discovered that their assortment of items is subpar. The sole aspect that consistently meets expectations is their shoe collection. I managed to secure a decent pair of Nikes for a mere $30.

yelp:test:1073.orig: New year, new clothes, time to update my closet.  A great way to sell some clothes for cash is at Buffalo Exchange.  They give you 33% for the value of the clothes or 50% for in store credit.  The staffs are so friendly.  I just love the store that doesn't smell like something died like other consignment stores.
yelp:test:1073.para: A fresh start with a new wardrobe, it's time to refresh my closet. Selling clothes for money can be done effectively at Buffalo Exchange. They offer a 33% cash value or 50% store credit for your items. The team is incredibly welcoming. I adore the shop that maintains a fresh atmosphere, unlike other consignment stores where a foul odor might linger.

yelp:test:1092.orig: Pretty good subs. The pastrami is to die for.
yelp:test:1092.para: Excellent substitutions. The pastrami is absolutely mouthwatering.

yelp:test:1093.orig: Holy cinnamon all up in your face!  Cinna-cones, cinna-brooms, cinna-wreaths,  cinna-scents galore! Everything smells like cinnamon and I hate the smell of cinnamon! yelp:test:1093.para: Cinnamon-infused aromas assault my senses! Cinnamon-themed items, cinnamon-scented fragrances, cinnamon-inspired decorations abound! The scent of cinnamon pervades everything, and I detest this cinnamon odor! Even a day post-shopping, I burped and it reeked of cinnamon! \n\nJoyful Festive Season!

yelp:test:1104.orig: awesome burgers.  decent service.  good atmosphere.  it's a dive bar.  just fyi.  with good food.
yelp:test:1104.para: Exceptional burgers and commendable service. The ambiance is inviting, characteristic of a cozy dive spot. It's worth noting for its delicious cuisine.

yelp:test:1112.orig: Either they need to hire more baristas or they need to work in faster pace.  I ordered a very simple drink and waited for over 5 minutes for it.  It was also during evening rush hours, but that shouldn't be the reason why my drink took a long time to make.  Not impressed at all.
yelp:test:1112.para: They must either recruit additional baristas or increase their service speed. I placed a basic beverage and had to endure a wait of more than five minutes. This occurred during peak evening hours, yet it shouldn't justify the extended preparation time. Completely dissatisfied.

yelp:test:1116.orig: I use to like Ulta. At least, I think I did. I often went to the Ulta at MetroCenter before it closed, and when it did, I had no choice but to start visiting this Ulta. If it were not for the specific makeup I needed I wouldn't bother coming here. The customer service is non-existent. These so-called makeup artists or whatever they are, shouldn't even exist. To this day, not one of them has ever offered to help me when I go to the store. They stare at me when I walk by but continue chattering away to each other, or seek out the one blonde in the store. I walk in, pick up what I need and get the heck out of there. \n\nThe stuff is overpriced. You can get the drugstore brands of makeup for way cheaper anywhere else. The coupon thing is a joke. The points are a waste. Spend hundreds of dollars for a free hair brush?! Are you kidding?!
yelp:test:1116.para: Previously, I had a fondness for Ulta, though I'm uncertain now. I frequented the Ulta at MetroCenter until its closure, after which I had no alternative but to frequent this Ulta. I would only visit if I required a particular makeup product. The customer service is notably absent. The individuals claiming to be makeup experts should not be present. Despite my visits, none have extended assistance. They simply observe me as I pass and converse amongst themselves, or target the lone blonde in the store. I enter, acquire what I need, and promptly exit. \n\nThe prices are exorbitant. You can find drugstore makeup brands at significantly lower prices elsewhere. The coupon system is deceptive. The accumulated points are futile. Why spend hundreds on a complimentary hair brush? It's absurd!

yelp:test:1123.orig: Very reasonably priced and a higher quality pedicure than I expected.  I will be returning.
yelp:test:1123.para: The cost is quite reasonable and the pedicure's quality surpassed my expectations, prompting my decision to make a return visit.

yelp:test:1128.orig:
My wife and I used to love Arriba's, til recently when we joined some friends at the end of their table for dinner. We arrived about an hour after they did, and they were finished when we got there.
 I ordered a stuffed poblano chili dish and it really was not good at all. Bad enough that the food was bad, but when we were ready to leave, we asked the waitress for our check, so she gives us a check for the whole table.
 My wife said, ""No-we want our check only"" and the waitress said that they do not do seperate checks, which is B.S. because we always have gotten seperate checks at the Arriba's in Arrowhead. This created a big hassle for us because we never carry cash, so my wife had to pay back one of her friends for our share of the bill the following week.
 This is no way to conduct a business, and I also sent the main office an email telling them about what had happened, but they never answered the email. I guess customer satisfaction means nothing to them, so we will NEVER go back! 

 Anyplace can roast chilis, so thats nothing special for Arriba's.

 Macayos is the place from now on, and the food there is superior to Arriba's.
yelp:test:1128.para:
My spouse and I formerly enjoyed dining at Arriba's, but our experience took a turn for the worse when we joined friends for a meal. We arrived an hour late, and by the time we arrived, they had already finished eating. I opted for a stuffed poblano chili dish, which was disappointingly subpar. When it was time to pay, we requested individual checks, but the waitress informed us that separate checks weren't an option, despite our previous experiences at Arriba's in Arrowhead. This led to complications as we lacked cash, forcing my spouse to reimburse a friend for our portion of the bill later on. This incident highlighted a lack of customer care, prompting me to write a complaint to the main office, which was disregarded. Consequently, we've decided to choose Macayos for our future dining experiences, as their food quality surpasses that of Arriba's.

Anything else but Arriba's can prepare chilis, so it's not a unique selling point for them.

Macayos will be our new go-to, as their food quality is superior to that of Arriba's.

yelp:test:1144.orig: 15 minutes to make an egg salad sandwich with only 4 orders ahead of me? When I open my bag, there is only half a sandwich? WTF? I go back and they acknowledge the mistake and proceed to make a half sandwich with and old piece of bread that was likely left over from lunch 5 hours prior.\n\nThere are too many places in this area to mess up that bad on a simple sandwich order to go back and try it again.
yelp:test:1144.para: Only 15 minutes to prepare a half-assembled egg salad sandwich with 4 orders in queue? Upon discovering my bag contains just a half sandwich, I'm baffled. I return, and they recognize the error, opting to create a subpar half sandwich using a stale bread remnant from a lunch served 5 hours ago.\n\nThe frequency of such blunders in this locale for a basic sandwich order is too high to warrant another attempt.

yelp:test:1162.orig: Only reason I come here is because I get $5 off the total before 9am on Sunday. This recent experience, they forgot to clean the dashboard (dust, dust and more dust) and I almost drove off with the marker of my wash on my windshield?! yelp:test:1162.para: The sole motivation for my visits is the $5 discount on the pre-9am Sunday total. I've had a recent incident where they neglected to clean the dashboard, resulting in a layer of dust and nearly causing an accident with the wash marker on my windshield. These are the two critical aspects that require cleaning post-car wash. Without this necessity, I wouldn't be here. Straightforward.

yelp:test:1176.orig: Maybe it was the time of day (afternoon) but something was very off today. The cheese plate arrived long after the entrees, my companion's bacon wrapped scallops seemed uncooked and raw.   The chicken schnitzel was fine.   Good beer and wine selection.  Slow service.
yelp:test:1176.para: Perhaps the afternoon timing affected the day, as the cheese platter came much later than the main courses. My dining partner's bacon-wrapped scallops appeared undercooked and raw. However, the chicken schnitzel was satisfactory. The beer and wine choices were commendable. The service was noticeably leisurely.

yelp:test:1180.orig:

yelp:test:1180.para: On April 4, 2014, I visited a store where Daniel provided excellent assistance in upgrading my phone. Later, on April 12, 2014, I returned with my disabled wife to exchange a faulty item and upgrade her phone. The store's location of a McDonald's 100 yards away was suggested for her bathroom needs, which upset both my wife and me. Several young employees dismissed our concerns with indifference. yelp:test:1221.orig: Really a nice little find. Four stars for the gyro dinner, veggie plate and greek salad. They were all really good and the price is definitely right. i will definitely be back here again!
yelp:test:1221.para: A delightful discovery indeed. I award four stars for the gyro meal, vegetable dish, and Greek salad. All were exceptional in quality and the cost was quite reasonable. I am certain to return to this place in the future!

yelp:test:1259.orig: This is a great place to go in the morning or late at night after partying.  I will forever enjoy going to this place because it reminds me of truck stop food while traveling.  The hungry traveller will always fill you up with bottomless pancakes but the country fried steak is also something I always get.  It gets 4 stars because sometimes they are understaffed and takes a bit to get service.  But when I go, I'm usually not in a hurry anyways.  The staff is always friendly day or night. Even a simple side salad is fresh and deserving of props.  The awesome thing is the fresh desserts and pie will satisfy any drunk or Sunday camper.  If you're tired of the usual IHOP or hole in the wall breakfast place, enjoy the old school diner atmosphere that th\nis place has to offer.
yelp:test:1259.para: This location is perfect for morning visits or late-night outings post-celebration. I will always cherish visiting this spot as it evokes memories of truck stop meals during journeys. The famished wanderer will always satiate you with endless pancakes, and I consistently opt for the country-style steak. Despite occasionally being understaffed and service taking a little longer, I'm not usually rushed when I visit. The staff maintains a warm and welcoming demeanor throughout the day and night. Even a simple side salad is crisp and merits praise. The delightful aspect is the freshly baked desserts and pies that cater to any intoxicated or leisurely Sunday explorer. If you're bored with typical IHOP or nondescript breakfast spots, relish the nostalgic vibe of this traditional diner.

yelp:test:1267.orig:
02.05.10-02.08.10

We paid $150 + $5/day parking for our entire stay.  After reading the other Yelp reviews, I was really afraid of getting jumped (or worse).  But low expectations sometimes are good.

We checked in Friday night; they had no problem switching our king sized bed to a double bed suite.  The suite has a mini fridge and a microwave.  Definitely necessary after long nights of partying.  We are two doors down from the gym.  There are two flat screens.  Definitely better than expected.

Free made-to-order breakfast every morning.  Weekdays until 9:30, weekends until 10:00.  French toast, omelets, hash browns, etc.  It's pretty awesome if you can actually wake up for it.  The chefs actually come over to the tables to check up on how you're doing.  

The pool/hot tub is open from 6:00 a.m. to midnight.  Also amazing after a long day of hiking, or shopping, whatever floats your boat.

Recommend!
yelp:test:1267.para:
02.05.10-02.08.10

Our accommodation cost us $150 plus $5 per day for parking during our full-length visit. Initially, I was apprehensive about safety concerns based on other Yelp feedback, but setting low expectations can be beneficial. 

Upon arrival on Friday evening, the staff effortlessly converted our king-sized bed to a double bed suite. The suite includes a mini fridge and a microwave, which are quite handy following extended nights of revelry. It's conveniently situated just two doors away from the fitness center, with two large televisions. The experience surpassed our anticipations. 

A complimentary breakfast, prepared to order each morning, is available from weekdays until 9:30 and weekends until 10:00. The menu offers French toast, omelets, hash browns, and more. The chefs even attend to the guests at their tables. 

The pool and hot tub are accessible from 6:00 a.m. to midnight, providing a refreshing respite after a day filled with activities like hiking or shopping. 

This place is highly recommended.

yelp:test:1280.orig: Went to meet my mom for lunch last Friday with my little guy.  Instead of being greeted by the host staff, Carol walked up to me and announced that my stroller won't fit in the restaurant and that she would have to take it in the back.  What?  Ok...  This Britax B-Ready apparently warranted a scolding.  Carol was so incredibly rude and my stroller would have easily fit at a table- minus a chair.  What exactly is their procedure for wheelchairs or other special needs devices?  Do they simply not fit or are they not pleasing enough to the eye to accommodate?  They might want to come up with a better story and take a more discerning eye to the host staff.  I've always had such great experiences here in the past; what a disappointment.  We'll be over at Chelsea's.  They're cool with my wheels.
yelp:test:1280.para: Last Friday, I had lunch with my mom and my child. Instead of the usual warm welcome from the staff, Carol approached me and informed that my Britax B-Ready stroller wouldn't be allowed inside the restaurant, and she'd have to take it to the back. Surprised, I wondered about their policy for assistive devices. It seemed like Carol's behavior was unprofessional, and my stroller would have easily fit at a table without a chair. Perhaps they need to reconsider their approach and train their staff to be more considerate. Despite my previous positive experiences, this incident left me disappointed. We'll be heading to Chelsea's instead, where they're more accommodating to my stroller.

yelp:test:1289.orig: I'm stuffed!  No please, no more food!  Wait, it's free?  You just want to give me extra food because you feel like it?  Alright, I guess I could sacrifice and eat this delicious chocolate cake and free cookies you put in my valeted car!\nI swear that is how it is every time I dine at Vincent's.  They love providing extra treats which is why this place exceeds five stars.  The food alone is divine!  I love every item on their menu!  The souffles are to die for as well.  But they always seem to go above and beyond every meal.  If only every restaurant had the same level of customer service!
yelp:test:1289.para:
I'm completely full!  Absolutely not, I don't need any more food!  Hold on, it's complimentary?  It appears you're simply offering additional edibles out of goodwill. Fair enough, I'll relent and indulge in this scrumptious chocolate cake and complimentary cookies left in my parked vehicle!  I can't deny that this is the pattern when I visit Vincent's. Their penchant for supplementary delights is why this establishment is rated above five stars. The cuisine itself is sublime! I adore every dish on their menu! The soufflés are exceptional too. However, they consistently surpass expectations with their service. It would be wonderful if all eateries matched this standard of customer care.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the same meaning, topic, sentiment, emotion, and intent as the original text, while using different wording and sentence structure. The length is also roughly the same.)

yelp:test:1303.orig:
= = = = = =  THIS REVIEW IS FOR PETER PIPER'S WEEKDAY LUNCH BUFFET!  = = = = = =

This is a huge place, very inexpensive, & offers a buffet lunch of three kinds of salad, several pizza choices, & bread sticks.  Both the salads & the pizza were blah, & there was no other pasta, soup, potato salad, cottage cheese, or anything else like that to nibble on.  With rather loud music was playing, I couldn't enjoy reading the paper while I ate, so I bit down a few slices & left.

Ci Ci's next door is a better choice.
yelp:test:1303.para:
= = = = = =  THIS EVALUATION IS FOR PETER PIPER'S DAILY LUNCH BAR!  = = = = = =

This establishment is spacious and affordable, presenting a buffet lunch featuring three varieties of salad, multiple pizza options, and bread sticks. However, both the salads and pizzas were unremarkable, and there was a lack of additional items such as pasta, soup, potato salad, cottage cheese, or similar snacks. The loud music made it difficult to read while dining, leading me to consume a few slices and depart. 

Ci Ci's adjacent location is a superior alternative.

yelp:test:1308.orig: Five stars due to this being the best Panda Express I've ever visited. The girl behind the counter was polite to the person in front of me OFFERING samples to them. When I stepped up she was super polite to me and offered me samples as well, and thanks to the sample I ended up getting the honey sesame seed chicken. Absolutely delicious. I asked for both noodles and rice and I expected the usual half-assed scoops of both but this girl hooked it up big time on everything! Despite all these bad reviews I will definitely be a repeat customer!
yelp:test:1308.para: This Panda Express experience earned five stars for being the most exceptional visit I've had. The counter attendant was courteous to the customer ahead of me, presenting samples. When I approached, she maintained her polite demeanor and provided me with samples too. Thanks to the sample, I chose the honey sesame seed chicken, which was incredibly tasty. I requested both noodles and rice, anticipating average portions, but the attendant exceeded expectations in every aspect. Despite encountering numerous negative reviews, I am committed to becoming a regular patron.

yelp:test:1311.orig: I was lucky enough to get two tickets to the opening night of Giselle. What a beautiful performance. The scenery was beautiful, the dancers were great, the story was easy to follow for those of us who don't have training, overall it was amazing. This production made me want to go to the ballet again and again! Very professional and very entertaining.
yelp:test:1311.para: I had the fortune to secure two passes for the premiere of Giselle. It was a stunning show. The set design was exquisite, the dancers excelled, the narrative was accessible even for those without formal training, and in total, it was awe-inspiring. This rendition sparked a desire in me to revisit ballet performances repeatedly. It was executed with high professionalism and provided immense enjoyment.

yelp:test:1314.orig: I have never been so disappointed in an oil change! First they took my car and told me they would contact me when it was ready so I was free to do some shopping in Costco next door.  They never called.  I walked back over to pick up my car to find they never touched it and refused to work on it.  They said they heard a noise in the engine and would not tell me what it was.  (I had it checked out at different place).  Sears told me my engine could blow up at any moment.  All that was wrong was the O2 sensor was broken (nothing to cause and engine to blow up).  These guys were just lazy and did not want to do any work.  They chose to scare me instead.  I will never go back to a Sears Auto Center for anything.
yelp:test:1314.para: I've never felt such frustration with an oil change service before. Initially, they took my vehicle and assured me they'd notify me upon completion, allowing me to shop at the nearby Costco. However, they failed to call. Upon returning to retrieve my car, I discovered they hadn't serviced it and declined to assist further. They mentioned an engine noise but wouldn't disclose details. I sought a second opinion elsewhere. Sears warned me of a potential engine explosion, which was unfounded as the only issue was a malfunctioning O2 sensor. Their lack of effort and intent to intimidate left me with a strong aversion to returning to a Sears Auto Center for any services.

yelp:test:1326.orig: My son likes to go there for poppers on the weekend.  His second choice is the chocolate chip coffee cake.  This is the second weekend in a row that they have been out of both.   The first time, I thought it was a fluke.  Two weekends in a row is a trend.  If you run out of something daily, make more of it.  Obviously, there's now more of a demand for both of these.  You can make more of them to meet the demand or don't and demand will go down from people like me not coming back to your store.  Dunkin Doughnuts, here we come again!
yelp:test:1326.para: My boy enjoys visiting that place for poppers during weekends.  His alternative preference is the chocolate chip coffee cake.  This occurrence marks the second consecutive weekend they've run out of both. Initially, I assumed it was a one-time incident. However, two consecutive weekends suggest a pattern. If items are consistently unavailable, it's time to increase production. The apparent rise in interest for both items indicates a need for more supply. Failing to do so may result in customers like me ceasing to patronize your establishment. Anticipate another visit to Dunkin Doughnuts soon.

yelp:test:1327.orig: My stylist was very knowledgeable. Yay, 13$/haircut!  She even knew about my natural curls & told me how that would work w/haircuts I wanted. Thanks!
yelp:test:1327.para: My hairstylist was incredibly well-informed. Fantastic, 13$ per haircut! She was aware of my inherent curls and explained how they would complement the haircuts I desired. Appreciation!

yelp:test:1332.orig:
I've been in many presidential suites, few better than the one here.
Everything is superb.
Attention to detail, focused and sharp.
And the room itself?
Romantic with it's outdoor showers, making you feel almost naughty when showering.
And room service?
I enjoyed the eggs benedict, although it was somewhat cold.

Too bad I onlly have until till two o'clock to get this room cleaned and ready for shift manager inspection.
yelp:test:1332.para:
I've had the opportunity to stay in various presidential suites, but none surpass the quality of this one.
The overall excellence is evident.
The meticulousness and precision are commendable.
The ambiance of the room is charming, with outdoor showers that evoke a sense of mischief during use.
Regarding the room service, I found the eggs benedict to be enjoyable, albeit a bit chilly.

Unfortunately, I only have until 2 o'clock to ensure this room is spotless for the shift manager's evaluation.

yelp:test:1344.orig: I've eaten majority of their menu and haven't found anything that I haven't liked.  It's a great place for any meal.  My boyfriend is more a breakfast person and I'm more of a lunch person so this place is perfect for us.  I love their avocado pizza - we did it with proscuitto once and it was fantastic.  The spicy tuna roll makes a great appetizer.  The white sangria is probably one of the best I've had in Phoenix.  For dessert, the red velvet cupcake is unbelievable - the frosting is the best part.  The parking kinda stinks but you can always park across the street at arcadia room and walk to LGO.  Can't say how much I love this place!
yelp:test:1344.para: I've sampled most of their dishes and haven't encountered anything I didn't enjoy. It's an excellent spot for any meal. My partner prefers breakfast, while I favor lunch, making this establishment ideal for us. I adore their avocado pizza, especially with prosciutto, which was outstanding. The spicy tuna roll serves as an excellent starter. The white sangria here is among the finest I've tasted in Phoenix. For dessert, the red velvet cupcake is remarkable, particularly the frosting. Parking is somewhat lacking, but you can always find a spot across the street at arcadia room and walk to LGO. I can't express my affection for this place enough!

yelp:test:1359.orig: Parking is always a jam, but the food and atmosphere rocks.
yelp:test:1359.para: The parking situation is consistently congested, yet the cuisine and ambiance are exceptional.

yelp:test:1360.orig: I have enjoyed Postino's for a long time.  The Monday and Tuesday night madness are for those who have the patience to have a great deal.  This location is great due to the patio and indoor seating.  I've always enjoyed the prosciutto with brie sandwich.  Try to bring cash when possible for valet.. Parking can get pretty crazy.  \nService is always Outstanding!  Worth the drive and wait!
yelp:test:1360.para: For an extended period, I've relished the experience at Postino's. The Monday and Tuesday evening hustle caters to those with the endurance for a substantial reward. The venue's appeal stems from its patio and interior accommodations. I've consistently savored the prosciutto and brie sandwich. It's advisable to carry cash for valet parking, as it can become quite hectic. The service consistently exceeds expectations, making the journey and wait time well worth it.

yelp:test:1365.orig: i thought it was good and it's cheap mexican. just dont expect anything fancy-don't know that i would actually eat inside.
yelp:test:1365.para: I considered it satisfactory and it's affordable Mexican cuisine. However, don't anticipate anything overly elaborate, and I'm uncertain if I would dine indoors.

yelp:test:1402.para:
Amazed. 
I reached out beforehand to inquire about the issues with our bicycles (we're proficient in bike repairs but lack extensive tools for certain problems). He suggested we bring our bikes for a complimentary assessment, and they would probably be able to repair it at a minimal cost. I was thrilled!

My partner and I took a bus to arrive at this location (since we only own bikes). The journey took us approximately one hour on a Sunday. Upon arrival, he examined our bikes and informed us that it would cost $10 for a chain (which seems fair) and $15 to install it. I was taken aback, WHY would you charge me more than the chain itself to install it, especially when I could have used my small chain tool and completed the task in just a few minutes? That was outright nonsense.

He also mentioned a $25 fee for attaching a front brake. I couldn't believe it. I glanced at my watch to confirm it wasn't April Fool's Day.

Subsequently, after my partner stepped outside, I discovered that they wouldn't be fixing our bikes on that day (when the total repair would have been completed).

yelp:test:1436.orig: The atmosphere is decent, but the food is absolutely terrible.  It is nothing but chewy meat covered in cheap cheese and grease.   The quesadillas are served in a pool of grease and the nachos are some of the worst in Phoenix,  The quality is an insult to the prices charged and an affront to good Mexican food.  Stick with the beer.
yelp:test:1436.para: The ambiance is satisfactory, yet the cuisine is utterly disappointing. The dish consists of tough meat enveloped in low-grade cheese and excessive grease. Quesadillas arrive drenched in grease, ranking among the poorest in Phoenix. The quality starkly contrasts with the cost, disrespecting authentic Mexican cuisine. Opt for the beer instead.

yelp:test:1455.orig: This isn't the worse place I've been. In fact the pedicure was really pretty good, but the manicure chipped the very next day! They aslo gave me a kind of hard time about paying with card, even though i tipped in cash. I only went here for a wedding and i don't think I'll be going back.
yelp:test:1455.para: The location isn't the most disappointing I've encountered. The pedicure was quite appealing, yet the manicure failed to last even a day. They also seemed to be somewhat difficult when I attempted to pay with a card, despite my cash tip. I visited solely for a wedding and I doubt I'll return.

yelp:test:1473.orig: Good selection, usually helpful people working out in the plants, but customer service falls apart when you get to the counter--very slow. Bought a 15G tree last time, paid for planting, which was all fine initially. However, the tree lost nearly all its leaves within a couple weeks. We called them and they told us not to be concerned. Well, we waited for the tree to recover but it ultimately died; so called them back (now a few months later). They scheduled someone to come out to \""check it\"", but they were a no-show for the scheduled appointment. Called again, and the run-around started. NOW they needed an invoice number (provided) and were supposed to call back. No call back. Called again to check; no call back. Called to complain--no call back. We've just given up, on getting this tree replaced, as well as ever going back to Whitfill. Buyer beware.
yelp:test:1473.para: The plants typically have a good variety and helpful staff, but the customer service deteriorates at the checkout point, characterized by sluggishness. I purchased a 15G tree previously, and the planting process was satisfactory at first. Regrettably, the tree rapidly lost most of its foliage within weeks. We reached out to them, and they reassured us not to worry. Despite our patience, the tree eventually perished; hence, we contacted them again, several months later. They arranged for a visit to assess the situation, but the individual failed to show up for the planned visit. Subsequent calls led to further confusion. Now they require an invoice number, which we provided, and they promised to call back. However, there has been no response. We've decided to abandon the idea of replacing the tree and to never return to Whitfill. A word of caution for buyers.

yelp:test:1493.para:
My significant other and I decided to visit Joey's, a place we'd seen for years but never entered. The surprise of finding it deserted on a Wednesday night at 6:30pm was immense. The ambiance was unsettlingly quiet, with dim lighting and a vibe reminiscent of a grandma's living room. The air conditioning was malfunctioning, failing to provide relief from the heat. The food, although resembling typical Italian cuisine, was oddly out of place, leaving me feeling uncomfortable after consumption. I would advise steering clear of the olive-flavored ice tea.

She's a rescue who is still very nervous around strangers (and vacuums, doorbells, and wood flooring), and her size can make her a real monster when she's scared. Yet she still needs annual checkups and booster shots, and Lookout Mountain is the lucky winner.
