They even had Stella Artois (my favorite beer) on tap!\n\nThe service here was okay at best, but the food was disappointing, especially after having an amazing experience at another RT. If you want to eat at a Ruby Tuesday, you might as well go to one in the midwest. Stay away from this one.
yelp:test:4323.para: My girlfriend insisted on dining here after being influenced by the ads in So Cal. Having previously enjoyed a Ruby Tuesday in Cleveland, OH, I anticipated a similar experience. However, this establishment was entirely distinct. Externally, it resembled a Cocos or Sizzler. The Cleveland Ruby Tuesday had a more refined Chilis vibe with an improved menu, including Stella Artois, my preferred beer. The service was mediocre at best, but the food fell short, particularly when compared to a memorable visit to another RT. For Ruby Tuesday enthusiasts, it's advisable to choose a midwestern location and avoid this one.

yelp:test:4333.orig:
This is one of the better places to go for curry!

I like the hole-in-wall family owned feel.  Everything I've had here has been good, but they truly shine when it comes to curry.  There are other Thai places I like more, but if I may emphasize just one more time, there are none that I like more in town for curry.

A few of my friends that lived in Thailand or have Thai parents will only eat here...that says something good i my book.
yelp:test:4333.para:
This spot stands out as an excellent choice for enjoying curry dishes!

The cozy, family-run atmosphere appeals to me. All the meals I've tried here have been delightful, but they excel particularly in their curry offerings. While there are other Thai eateries I prefer, I must stress once more that none in this area surpasses them for curry aficionados like myself.

Several acquaintances with Thai heritage or residency in Thailand exclusively dine here, which speaks volumes in my opinion.

yelp:test:4348.orig: Have you often wondered why so many middle-aged  Japanese people here in Las Vegas always tell you that they go to SUSHI ON RAINBOW for sushi instead of the multi-million dollar bankrolled sushi restaurants like Kabuto or Goyemon? Why do these former or current Japanese nationals prefer to eat at an older sushi bar that doesn't have fancy or exciting d\u00e9cor? The answer is that SUSHI ON RAINBOW to MANY of us people of Japanese descent is actually a symbol of pride for our community. And, the owner is a very respected man to us Japanese-Americans.\n\nWhen I was a little kid in Southern California, I first heard about Shogo-san and the famous sushi restaurant in Newport Beach. Sushi just did not exist in the area. Everytime a sushi restaurant poped up, it would quickly go out of business. Remember that sushi, and the idea of eating raw fish was not accepted by the American mainstream back then. The sushi bar that Shogo worked at was the only sushi bar in the area that had made it. Japanese people would drive 50+ miles just to eat there. Shogo-San was one of the 1st generation sushi chefs, along with the famous Ichiro Mashita who came to America from Japan with a dream to one day p
yelp:test:4348.para:
Have you frequently pondered why numerous middle-aged individuals of Japanese heritage in Las Vegas consistently recommend SUSHI ON RAINBOW for their sushi dining experiences over high-end, well-funded establishments such as Kabuto or Goyemon? The reason these former or present Japanese nationals opt for an older sushi establishment lacking in extravagant or thrilling ambiance is that SUSHI ON RAINBOW holds significant pride for our Japanese community. Moreover, the proprietor is highly esteemed among Japanese-Americans.

As a child growing up in Southern California, I first learned about Shogo-san and the renowned sushi establishment in Newport Beach. At that time, sushi was virtually non-existent in the region. Whenever a sushi restaurant emerged, it would swiftly close down. The concept of consuming raw fish was not embraced by the American mainstream during that era. The sushi bar where Shogo worked was the sole one in the vicinity that managed to survive. Shogo-San was among the pioneering sushi chefs, alongside the celebrated Ichiro Mashita, who migrated to America with aspirations to eventually become a sushi master.

yelp:test:4356.orig:
Okay I have to give it two stars just because it really isn't much more than a nice Motel 6 or Best Western that is in Las Vegas.  With that said though I was completely shocked with my stay.  My wife and I stayed one night just to catch some sleep before me moved over to one of the other hotels on the strip, and I was fearing the worst.

We paid $20 for one night, and I closed my eyes while opening the door to my room, half expecting to find a room that would make me wish my wife would let us sleep in the car.

The room was quite clean, surprisingly decent sized, and the bed was even somewhat comfortable.  I would definitely NEVER stay here for more than one night, but if you need a place for a one night layover or looking for an incredibly cheap place to stay, you may want to check it out.
yelp:test:4356.para:
I'm awarding it two stars as it essentially mirrors a standard Motel 6 or Best Western in Las Vegas. Despite this, I was taken aback by my experience. My spouse and I opted for a single night's rest before relocating to another hotel on the strip, anticipating a less-than-ideal situation.

We invested $20 for one night, and upon entering the room, I braced myself for a subpar space, hoping my partner would agree to sleep in the car instead.

The room was surprisingly clean, adequately spacious, and the bed offered a level of comfort. I would not recommend staying here beyond a single night, but it might be worth considering for a one-night layover or for those seeking an exceptionally affordable accommodation.

yelp:test:4389.orig:
Great breakfast food at OPH.  Had the Belgin Waffles with a side of bacon.  The bacon was thick & delicious.  Ok, I don't get bacon often.  The Belgin Waffle was light and had a good taste.

If you are a grandparent or grandchild (55+, 12 & under) they have a good deal.  Under $5 for 3 pancakes, eggs & meat.

I recommend eating here vs. the breakfast buffet ($8).  The food tastes better.
yelp:test:4389.para: Enjoy a delightful morning meal at OPH, where I savored the Belgin Waffles accompanied by succulent bacon. The bacon's richness and flavor stood out, even though I don't frequently indulge in it. The waffles were airy and had a pleasing flavor. For families, especially grandparents and grandchildren aged 55 and above, there's a special offer: get three pancakes, eggs, and meat for under $5. I suggest choosing this place over the breakfast buffet, which costs $8, as the quality of the food is superior.

yelp:test:4409.para: Delycios maintains a steadfast commitment to upholding the original sentiment, topic, emotion, and intent, while employing a distinct lexicon and varied syntactical arrangements, all the while preserving the approximate length of the initial statement.

yelp:test:4415.orig:
Just left this office and I've never been so impressed by a dental visit before!
New patient paperwork was minimal, wait time was barely enough to read 2 pages of my book, and I was introduced to Anita- the cheerful, friendly, and professional dental assistant with who I would spend the majority of my visit. 

Anita was downright bubbly and made an effort to get to know me as a person while also maintaining professionalism, explaining every procedure she was going to do, and giving additional dental info tidbits to help keep my teeth as healthy and attractive as possible. Dr. Ozaki was also super professional and made sure to go over my concerns before moving on, making it very clear that he could always be reached in the event of an emergency. Anita mentioned she has worked for Dr. Ozaki for decades, which I think speaks volumes about their level of professionalism and patient care.

Ultimately spent just over an hour here including xrays, cleaning, and scheduling additional work for a chipped tooth. Front desk staff were super helpful at answering some questions about my dental insurance coverage and went out of their way to look up pricing to replace a retainer. Super impre
yelp:test:4415.para: Exited the dental clinic feeling incredibly satisfied with the experience, noting the streamlined new patient forms, a brief wait that allowed me to read a few pages, and the majority of my time spent with Anita, a vivacious, amiable, and professional dental assistant. Anita's enthusiasm shone through as she engaged with me personally, while upholding a professional demeanor, detailing each procedure and offering extra dental advice to maintain my teeth's health and appearance. Dr. Ozaki's professionalism was evident as he addressed my concerns thoroughly before proceeding, assuring me of his availability for emergencies. Anita's long-standing tenure with Dr. Ozaki further highlighted their commitment to professionalism and patient care. The visit, which lasted just over an hour, included X-rays, cleaning, and arranging further treatment for a cracked tooth. The front desk staff were exceptionally helpful in clarifying my dental insurance queries and proactively sought out pricing for a retainer replacement. Super impressed

yelp:test:4438.orig:
mmmmm...,,,,mmm... bad! This place was definitely not what a majority of my co-workers had described it.  How can you burn chicken that bad? Here are my ratings for their service:

Customer Service - 5 Stars
Chicken Pasta - 1 Star (only because the chicken wasn't burnt)
Mashed Potatoes - 1/2 Star (only for the effort)

I ordered the family 4 meal and it was terrible.  I was hoping to write a good review, but the chicken pasta was soaked in thousand island dressing.  Not a huge fan of thousand island sauce unless i can use it on my ""In & Out"" burger.  

Mashed Potatoes? Sooooooo disappointed, they covered my mashed potatoes with gravy for me so when i got home it had all blended in together.  Husband was not happy.  

Chicken was very bland in seasoning, but thanks to the charred areas, there was a burnt taste at least.  

I wish I could say more about the place, but unfortunately ""this is all she wrote"".
yelp:test:4438.para:
Oh no, this location was far from what most of my colleagues had praised it. How could they ruin the chicken to such an extent? Here are my evaluations for their service:

Customer Service - 5 Stars
Chicken Pasta - 1 Star (only due to the chicken not being charred)
Mashed Potatoes - 1/2 Star (merely for the attempt)

I opted for the family 4 meal and it was utterly disappointing. I had hoped to pen a positive review, but the chicken pasta was drenched in thousand island dressing. I'm not particularly fond of thousand island sauce unless I can enjoy it on my "In & Out" burger. 

Mashed Potatoes? Extremely let down, they mixed gravy with my mashed potatoes, resulting in a blended mess when I arrived home. My husband was not pleased. 

The chicken lacked flavor in seasoning, but the burnt bits provided at least a hint of charred taste. 

Regrettably, I can't share more about the place, as "this is all I have to say".

yelp:test:4459.orig: The company is a rouse!  Mike Ferry pays his sales staff a little above minimum wage...hourly.Some of these individuals have backgrounds like waitressing and internet gambling. Less than one percent are college educated!  Many clients request to get out of their coaching contracts because it DOES NOT WORK!!  It is a TOTALLY unprofessional business environment with male members of the call center sales team making BLATANT lude and sexual comments.\n\nAs a result, a formal complaint has been made with the EEO.
yelp:test:4459.para: The firm is in disarray! Mike Ferry compensates his sales team slightly above the minimum wage on an hourly basis. Some team members have prior experience in roles such as waitressing and online gambling. Fewer than one percent hold a college degree. A significant number of clients seek to terminate their coaching agreements as they find them ineffective. The business atmosphere is entirely unprofessional, with male call center sales representatives openly making inappropriate and sexually suggestive remarks. Consequently, a formal grievance has been lodged with the EEO.

yelp:test:4486.orig: I can't actually comment on the food.  The place looked nice relative to a lot of neighboring establishments and was recommended by our lunch-time server @ Nola (very good Creole) and our concierge.  My low rating comes from the fact that I called twice to make a reservation and no one answered.  After taking a cab from downtown we learned there was a private party and we wouldn't be able to take in the Jersey Shore fist pumping scene (thanks Callan W for the visual).  Simply disappointed in the lack of basic customer service.\n\nWe ended up down the street at the Pittsburgh Steak Company.  Not sushi but the gorgonzola filet melts in your mouth!!
yelp:test:4486.para:
The ambiance of the venue was pleasing compared to nearby options, as suggested by our lunch-time server @ Nola, who is excellent in Creole, and our concierge. However, my modest rating stems from my unsuccessful attempts to secure a reservation twice, with no response. Upon arriving by cab from downtown, we discovered a private event, preventing us from experiencing the Jersey Shore's iconic fist pumping. The absence of fundamental customer service left us feeling let down.

In the end, we opted for the Pittsburgh Steak Company, which, while not offering sushi, delivered a delectable gorgonzola filet that melted delightfully in our mouths. (Thank you Callan W for the visual reference.)

yelp:test:4497.orig: I passed by this place and just decided to try it. I tried their burger. Man..it was so good. Best bang for the buck. Especially if you're a student.. I had plenty of fries. Completely stuffed. =) Definitely coming back here again.
yelp:test:4497.para: I stumbled upon this spot and opted to give it a shot. I sampled their burger and it was incredibly delicious. A fantastic value for money, particularly for students. I indulged in a generous portion of fries and felt thoroughly satisfied. I'm certain I'll return.

yelp:test:4498.orig:
I've only been here once and according to my friend, when he was here earlier in the year it was waaaaaaay better but I found the food very bland and warm, friendly service and cute atmosphere couldn't make up for it. 

We tried the crab and artichoke dip and for dinner, inspired by Kitchen Confidential, I had one of their specials, a flounder filet with polenta. I'm usually expecting polenta to be this creamy, mushy puddle of heaven but here it was more like a quiche. So there was the flounder and a slice of polenta on their opposite sides of a plate, they didn't seem to go together. I wonder if it has anything to do with skipping out on the salsa that was supposed to go on top of the fish but I can't see how some chopped tomatoes would've made this any better. The dip was also plain and largely unmemorable. 

I did like the decor and the format, they have a smaller, quieter back room with just a few tables and a nice-looking, dark bar and more seating in the front. It's really romantic and I wish the food was tastier.
yelp:test:4498.para:
I've visited this place just once, and my companion mentioned it was significantly superior when he went there earlier this year. However, I found the cuisine to be quite uninspiring, with the food tasting dull and lukewarm, despite the welcoming staff and charming ambiance. 

We sampled the crab and artichoke dip, and for our main course, I opted for a special dish, a flounder filet served with polenta, as per the influence of Kitchen Confidential. Normally, I anticipate polenta to be a rich, soft delight, but here it resembled a quiche. The flounder and polenta were placed on opposite sides of a plate, seemingly mismatched. I ponder if the omission of the salsa, which was intended to accompany the fish, might have contributed to this, but I struggle to imagine how additional chopped tomatoes could have enhanced the experience. The dip also failed to impress, being rather forgettable. 

I appreciated the decor and the layout, featuring a cozy, tranquil back room with limited seating and an attractive, dim bar area. It exudes a romantic vibe, yet I long for the dishes to be more flavorful.

yelp:test:4519.orig:
Since I have family that lives down the street, I have been coming to Big Jim's for over 20 years. I used to really enjoy coming here but stopped visiting several years ago. Although the food was always good, the place was getting dirtier every time I was there.

Yesterday my wife and I decided to stop for lunch. I figured that the place was probably cleaned up since the Diners, Drive-ins and Dives episode. After being seated, I wanted to leave. To be honest, I don't know why I stayed. Nothing had changed. In fact I think it got worse.

The floor was filthy. There was food under tables that looked like it was there for days. Remember, I was here for lunch and they just opened. The tables and chairs in the dining room looked as though they were purchased at a yard sale. Very old and falling apart.

The only reason I'm giving this two stars is because the service and food was good. I had an Italian hoagie and my wife had a salad. Both tasted good but I really couldn't enjoy it.

I kept thinking that if the dining room was this dirty, what is the kitchen like?
yelp:test:4519.para:
Having family nearby, I frequented Big Jim's for more than two decades, but I ceased my visits a few years back. The food consistently tasted great, but the cleanliness declined with each visit. Recently, my spouse and I chose to dine there. I assumed improvements had been made following a Diners, Drive-ins and Dives feature. However, upon being seated, I felt an urge to leave. I couldn't pinpoint my reason for staying. In reality, the situation seemed to have deteriorated further.\n\nThe floor was in a state of disarray, with remnants of food under tables that appeared untouched for days. Despite the restaurant's recent opening, the dining room furniture seemed second-hand and in disrepair. The only aspect that merited a two-star rating was the quality of service and food. I had an Italian hoagie, and my wife enjoyed a salad. While the taste was satisfactory, the overall experience was marred by the uncleanliness.

I couldn't help but wonder about the condition of the kitchen, given the visible state of the dining room.

yelp:test:4537.orig: The \""chicken\"" was soggy and a little rubbery.  The ice looked like it was icicles from the side of the building (It was winter when went).  The waiter was a friendly guy and very nice, although I'm not sure what is going on with the food...I've never been there since.
yelp:test:4537.para: The "chicken" turned out to be damp and somewhat elastic. The ice resembled icicles, likely due to the winter season when I visited. The waiter exuded friendliness and kindness, yet I remain uncertain about the food quality, leading me to avoid returning.

yelp:test:4540.orig: Horrible customer service! The WORST i've experienced in a long time - in fact, I don't think I've EVER been treated with such disrespect. I asked a simple question about what the person ordered who was with me and the young ladies working glared and cut eyes at me - awful attitudes. My guess is the 2 girls working must be related to same because there is no way anyone with common business sense would hire such disrespectful workers with no clue about offering acceptable, good customer service.
yelp:test:4540.para: Terrible service from the customer support team! The most disappointing encounter I've had for a long period - I'm convinced I've never been met with such disdain. When I inquired about the order of the individual accompanying me, the young employees glared and avoided eye contact, displaying extremely unprofessional behavior. I suspect the two girls employed might be family members, as it's highly unlikely that a business with sound judgment would employ such uncouth staff lacking in basic customer service skills.

yelp:test:4558.orig:
I have many fond memories at Lulu's. It was my first off campus dining experience while I was at CMU. Food was plenty and affordable. Yesterday, I went back for the first time in more than 5 years. 

The positives:
- things haven't changed
- affordable pricing
- generous portions
- fast service
- variety

The negatives:
- things haven't changed
- variety (see more explanation below)
- overly-Americanized ""Asian"" food
- bubble tea overly sweet and artificial

I stick with what I know is decent:
- Crab Rangoons
- Beef Chow Fun
- Pan Fried Noodles
- Wonton Noodle Soup

This really isn't a place where you should try something new. If you decide to dine here, check out the reviews and pick which has the most votes.
yelp:test:4558.para:
Many cherished recollections are associated with Lulu's, marking my initial foray into off-campus dining during my time at CMU. The fare was abundant and economical. Recently, I revisited for the first time in over half a decade. 

The positives:
- No significant alterations
- Economical costs
- Large servings
- Swift service
- Diverse menu

The negatives:
- No significant alterations
- Diversity (refer to further explanation below)
- Excessively Americanized Asian cuisine
- Overly sweet and synthetic bubble tea

I consistently opt for what I deem satisfactory:
- Crab Rangoons
- Beef Chow Fun
- Pan Fried Noodles
- Wonton Noodle Soup

This isn't a venue for culinary experimentation. If you choose to eat here, peruse the reviews and select the dish with the highest number of endorsements.

yelp:test:4636.orig:
I love Gullifty's!!! Its a really excellent place to get some dinner or dessert with your friends before a night out or just to spend some time catching up. 

Friday and Saturday nights can have a little bit of a wait, so be prepared for that. The desserts are way better than some of the reviewers here give them credit for and they have a really excellent wide variety to choose from. 

Private lot in the back as well as street park all require coins for the meter (pain!) but, when i'm back in pittsburgh about once a year, a stop to gullifty's is always on my to-do list!
yelp:test:4636.para:
Gullifty's is a fantastic spot for dining or desserts with companions before an evening event or for relaxed catch-ups. 

On Friday and Saturday evenings, there might be a slight delay, so come prepared. The desserts surpass the praise given by some reviewers and offer an impressive range of options. 

Both the private lot and street parking necessitate coin payment for the meter, which can be inconvenient, but I always include a visit to Gullifty's in my annual Pittsburgh itinerary!

yelp:test:4649.orig: I ve been living here for a year and have faced no problems at all. The apartments on the penthouse floor which is the 22nd floor are great. You have an option of choosing an apt with new appliances which are much better than the really old ones. The maintainence staff and the office are always available and helpful. I did have some problems with the dishwasher and the kitchen sink but it was fixed.
yelp:test:4649.para: For the past year, I've resided here without encountering any issues. The penthouse units located on the 22nd floor are exceptional. You can select an apartment equipped with modern appliances, superior to the outdated ones. The maintenance team and the office staff are consistently accessible and supportive. I experienced some issues with the dishwasher and kitchen sink, but they were promptly resolved.

yelp:test:4650.orig: Came back, and I'd write the exact same review all over again.\n\nNow pass me the potato gnocchi, please. And as for Tony P's issue, sorry Tony - but go marry yourself that British chic and bring her back here for some good Gnocchi and Chianti! I'll buy if you do!
yelp:test:4650.para: Returned and I would repeat the identical review once more.\n\nHand me the potato gnocchi, please. Regarding Tony P's problem, I apologize, Tony - but consider marrying the British elegance and invite her for some delicious Gnocchi and Chianti! I'll purchase if you do!

yelp:test:4652.orig:
You'll have to forgive me. I live in Los Angeles where there is valet parking for hamburgers and top chefs have food trucks that can be found here, there and everywhere. A burger with a side of fries smothered in Duck Confit with White Truffle Sauce - so perhaps the bar is a tad higher than here in - ack - Pittsburgh where I found myself searching for sustenance before attending the wedding that brought me here. I only hope the godawful mess I actually ate doesn't rear it's ugly head mid-ceremony.

It sounded like such a novel concept, a sandwich with all the sides just piled on. After all, it's all going to the same place, right? Having been born and raised in Chicago it was a familiar concept. The noble Chicago Dog, a study in contradictions: sweet and sour, spicy and mild, hot and cold - a veritable melange that blends and tantalizes from the first bite to the last. Yes! I'll try it!

With my omnivore brother and his lovely wife I made my way through the chilly streets of downtown Pittsburgh on this frosty Saturday. A bustling little metropolis, scant parking so (I am shamed to admit) I pulled in a nearby lot that charged an $8 flt fee. A small price to pay, I reasoned, for
yelp:test:4652.para:
Apologies for any inconvenience. I reside in Los Angeles, a city where hamburgers are valet-parked and renowned chefs operate food trucks throughout. Imagine a burger accompanied by fries drenched in Duck Confit and White Truffle Sauce - the standard here may be slightly elevated compared to Pittsburgh, where I was in search of nourishment before a wedding that led me here. I sincerely hope the unpleasant meal I consumed doesn't disrupt the ceremony.

The idea of a sandwich loaded with all the sides seemed intriguing, akin to a journey to the same destination. Having grown up in Chicago, this concept was already familiar to me. The iconic Chicago Dog, a paradoxical blend of sweet and sour, spicy and mild, hot and cold - a harmonious mix that delights from the first bite to the last. Indeed, I'm eager to give it a try!

Accompanied by my omnivorous brother and his charming wife, we navigated the cold downtown Pittsburgh streets on this frosty Saturday. A lively city with limited parking, I reluctantly paid an $8 flat fee for parking in a nearby lot. A minor expense, I justified, for the convenience it provided.

yelp:test:4661.orig: I love this pizza. If you like sweet sauce then you need to try this pizza.
yelp:test:4661.para: If you enjoy a dessert-like sauce, this pizza is a must-try.

yelp:test:4663.orig: Good Stuff!  Everything on the menu is pretty good.  They usually have a few decent beers on tap too!  The place gets busy, though, so be prepared to wait.
yelp:test:4663.para: Excellent choices available! The menu boasts a variety of tasty options. They typically offer a selection of commendable craft beers on tap. However, it tends to be crowded, so anticipate a bit of a wait.

yelp:test:4675.orig:
For years now, I have been telling my boyfriend about my hopes and dreams in life.  One that kept coming up, time and time again, was that I wanted to hug a penguin someday.  I was resigned to the fact that this would never happen - where on earth would I possibly be able to hug a penguin?  Antarctica?  Not going there.  Zoos - yeah, they have gates separating me from the huggable waddlers.  So it was just another dream destined to never come true - until my 26th birthday when my boyfriend presented me with two tickets to the Penguin Encounter at the National Aviary.

I was so childishly excited when we arrived at the Aviary one Saturday.  We were early for the penguin encounter, so we explored the rest of the Aviary first.  I was surprised at how delightful and interesting it was - yeah it's just birds, but like - who knew birds could be so cool?  It's essentially a zoo for birds, which sounds boring, but it is not!

My favorite part (besides the penguins) was going in the tropical habitat room.  This trainer gathered up a big crowd of us and did a feeding demonstration which was awesome.  Only kids got to be participants - well, it was an unspoken rule, but how dumb would I l
yelp:test:4675.para:
For a long time, I've shared my aspirations and ambitions with my partner. A recurring wish was to embrace a penguin at some point. I accepted that this was an unattainable fantasy - where could I possibly find a penguin to hug? The thought of Antarctica was out of the question, and zoos were off-limits due to their barriers. It seemed like a dream that would remain unfulfilled until my 26th birthday, when my boyfriend gifted me two tickets to the Penguin Encounter at the National Aviary.

I was overwhelmingly thrilled when we reached the Aviary on a Saturday. Being early for the penguin encounter, we took the opportunity to explore the rest of the Aviary first. I found the place surprisingly enjoyable and intriguing - it's essentially a bird sanctuary, which might sound mundane, but it's far from it!

My absolute favorite part (apart from the penguins) was the tropical habitat room. Here, a trainer engaged a large group of us in a feeding demonstration that was truly impressive. Only children were allowed to participate, though it was an unwritten rule - how foolish would I be to disregard it!

yelp:test:4694.orig: No HEAT late Sunday (January) night and no one around to tell.  45 degrees for a 3 hour movie.  Too many options to go back here! Good Luck!
yelp:test:4694.para: No warmth on the chilly Sunday evening of January, with no one present to inform. A temperature of 45 degrees for a 3-hour film. An abundance of choices deterring a return visit. Wishing you good fortune!

yelp:test:4710.orig:
I love salad bars. Love. LOVE. 

But I can't eat here. And by that I don't mean that it isn't veg-friendly - it most def is - I mean that the quality of ingredients, salad, toppings, potato bar, made-from-powder soups are so low that I get scared. Fear is an appetite inhibitor. 

I've hit this trough three times, and had gurgley tummy after each and every one. The ladies that work here are totally great - even acknowledge and remove and replace, say, the cukes, when I express concerns about their harboring of evil bacteriums and such (WOW they smelled weird last time I was here). But any effort on my part to save my and others' bellies from grossville feels like polishing the brass on the Titanic. 

So I continue to harass Sweet Tomatoes via email, monthly, with the hopes that one day we'll actually have a decent Bar in Charlotte. Fingers crossed. I might start a petition. Let me know if you want to sign.
yelp:test:4710.para:
I have a deep affection for salad bars. However, I am unable to consume there. This isn't due to a lack of vegetarian options - they are abundant - but rather the subpar quality of ingredients, salads, toppings, and powdered soups that instill fear in me, which can suppress appetite. 

I've experienced this issue thrice, each time resulting in an unpleasant stomach upset. The staff are commendable, even going as far as to acknowledge and rectify concerns about potential bacteria in items like cucumbers (which had an unusual odor during my last visit). Despite my efforts to prevent unpleasant experiences, it feels like trying to polish the Titanic. 

Thus, I persist in sending monthly emails to Sweet Tomatoes, with the aspiration that one day we'll have a respectable salad bar in Charlotte. I'm considering starting a petition and would appreciate your support if you're willing to sign.

yelp:test:4750.orig:
This funky little eatery in the South End has grown quite a bit (not in size, but in appeal) over the last few years.  What started as not much more than a rather ugly yellow cinder block building on an oddly-shaped lot is now that and more - they've added some landscaping, a paved lot instead of the gravel parking and a nice outdoor eating area too.  Inside the food is the same great, simple combinations you're used to getting.

The cramped quarters also haven't changed much, but that's just part of the appeal.  As strange as it may sound, the sheer volume that moves through this place makes it possible to place your order and get a table by the time the order is ready - provided everyone cooperates and doesn't hog their table out of their place in line.  When you're done, get up and let someone else have the table, and everything keeps moving as it should.

Table tops still contain business cards from around town, and there is plenty of artwork to see as well, and the atmosphere is worth coming for, but it's the food that should keep you coming back.  While the burrito is the namesake of the place, make sure you try the quesadilla too.  They are excellent.
yelp:test:4750.para:
This unique dining spot in the South End has significantly increased its charm (not in dimensions, but in allure) over recent years. What began as a rather unattractive yellow cinder block structure on a peculiarly-shaped plot has transformed into more than that - they've incorporated landscaping, replaced the gravel parking with a paved area, and established a charming outdoor dining space. Inside, the cuisine maintains the same excellent, straightforward pairings you're accustomed to. 

Despite the limited space remaining largely unchanged, this is part of the charm. Even though it may seem odd, the high turnover of patrons allows you to order and secure a table by the time your food is ready, assuming everyone plays fair and doesn't monopolize their table. After finishing, clear your table for the next customer, and the flow remains smooth. 

The table surfaces still display local business cards, and there's ample artwork to admire, making the ambiance a draw in itself. However, it's the food that should be the main reason for your return. While the burrito is the restaurant's signature dish, don't overlook the quesadilla - it's truly outstanding.

yelp:test:4789.orig:

Haven't been to Pike's in quite some time and this was my first go for lunch. Decided to dine al fresco and enjoyed every second of it. This time 'round, didn't go for anything on the sweet side of things, but rather went for the lunch menu solely. 

Started with the mozzarella sticks. Both myself and my dining counterpart were shocked that they weren't the ""out of the bag"" variety. These appeared to be hand breaded with a higher quality cheese than typically served. Marinara was standard, but the mozz sticks themselves were great. They also weren't covered with the typical panko, moon dust, crappy breading like usual.

Went with the buffalo chicken sandwich for my entree. Holy craaaaaap. Ditch the bun, eat a few of the house-made chips, and enjoy the chicken. Not only is this sucker lightly breaded and flavored well with the buffalo sauce, it's straight up baptized in the sauce. Swimming, rather. I'm usually not for a pool o
yelp:test:4789.para:
Equal parts traditional soda shop, eatery, tavern, and social spot. The spot's location is key here. Situated in a highly pedestrian-friendly area of South End, Pike's stands out with an extensive menu featuring numerous desserts and regional delicacies.

Had not visited Pike's for a while, and this was my initial lunch experience. Opted for an outdoor dining experience and thoroughly relished it. This time, I steered clear of the sweet offerings, focusing solely on the lunch menu. 

Kicked off with the mozzarella sticks. Both I and my dining companion were taken aback that they weren't the "pre-packaged" variety. These seemed to be hand-breaded with a superior cheese quality than what's usually served. The marinara sauce was standard, but the mozzarella sticks themselves were excellent. They also lacked the typical panko, crumb dust, or subpar breading that's common. 

Chose the buffalo chicken sandwich for my main course. Holy smokes. Abandon the bun, indulge in a few of the homemade chips, and savor the chicken. This dish is not only lightly breaded and well-seasoned with buffalo sauce, it's practically drenched in it. I'm

yelp:test:4799.orig: I found this monogramming place in Dilworth and, although I don't need anything monogrammed at the moment, I wanted to check it out for the future. You walk in and are basically on top of everything; there is a pathway cleared amongst all the items and 2 counters that forces you in and around the store even if you don't want to go. I was immediately looked at as if I were in the wrong place as I had nothing in my hands to be monogrammed, and was quickly and snottily asked if I was dropping anything off. I was stuck behind a gaggle of women debating which Kate Spade purse they wanted done as I desperately tried to get out but could hardly make my way around them. I may try again when I actually have the need for some monogramming, and I will try to overlook the pretentiousness of the employees and clientele.
yelp:test:4799.para: Upon discovering a monogramming shop in Dilworth, I decided to explore it despite not requiring any current monogramming services. Upon entering, I felt surrounded by the store's layout, with a clear path amidst the merchandise and two counters that seemed to compel me to navigate the space, even when I had no intention of doing so. I was quickly perceived as out of place, with no items to be monogrammed, and was hastily and rudely inquired if I intended to hand over anything. I found myself hindered by a group of women discussing their Kate Spade bag preferences while I struggled to move past them. I plan to revisit when I genuinely need monogramming services, and I'll attempt to disregard the air of superiority among the staff and customers.

yelp:test:4803.orig: The decor is just so fun and upbeat! I'm usually there a little later in the day, so it's not too busy or smelly. Everything is clean, everyone is friendly, and I always look prettier coming out than I do going in!
yelp:test:4803.para: The ambiance is incredibly lively and cheerful! I tend to arrive a bit later, so it's not overly crowded or unpleasant. The place is spotless, the people are welcoming, and I always feel more radiant when I leave than when I arrive!

yelp:test:4879.orig: If you're at the hospital and want something other than hospital food, this place may be the ticket.  Right across the street, you can get a good variety of food.  It's quick and easy and not too expensive.  Just don't go for the atmosphere because, well, there isn't much.  But keep your head down and that won't matter much.
yelp:test:4879.para: Should you find yourself in a hospital seeking a meal alternative, this location could be your solution. Directly adjacent, a diverse selection of dining options awaits. They offer speedy service at a reasonable cost. However, the ambiance is lacking, but maintaining focus will minimize its impact.

yelp:test:4887.orig: The food here is good, but wasn't exactly what I was expecting. Everything was was good quality and well prepared (and fast!) and the price was very reasonable. My wife and I both ordered the 1/4 rotisserie chicken (white) which came with cornbread and two sides. I got the baked beans and the special: spicy mac & cheese. The first thing I tried was the cornbread, and found it had jalape\u00f1os and whole kernels of corn baked in. I know some people really like the whole corn in the cornbread thing, but I'd rather keep my breads and vegetables separate. Next up was the spicy mac & cheese. I love mac & cheese, and I've become a big fan of having a bit of hot sauce added to give it some kick, so I was really excited about this. It certainly had the spicy; it had lots of jalape\u00f1os mixed in and was quite hot. What it was lacking was the cheese. There was no creaminess to it at all. The baked beans, however, were very good. They also had jalape\u00f1os mixed in (are you sensing a theme here?), but only had a subtle kick which was balanced with a slightly sweet tangy sauce. As for the chicken, the flavor was excellent but most of the breast was pretty dry. The wing, on the other hand
yelp:test:4887.para: The cuisine served here is commendable, although it didn't quite meet my anticipations. All items were of high quality, expertly cooked, and served promptly, with the cost being quite affordable. My spouse and I both opted for the 1/4 rotisserie chicken (white) accompanied by cornbread and two side dishes. I sampled the cornbread first, discovering it contained jalapeños and whole corn kernels baked within. While some individuals appreciate the inclusion of whole corn in their cornbread, I personally prefer to maintain a distinction between my breads and vegetables. Following that, I tasted the spicy mac & cheese. As a mac & cheese enthusiast, I've grown fond of adding a dash of hot sauce for an extra punch, and this dish delivered on the spicy note with generous amounts of jalapeños, though it was notably lacking in creaminess. The baked beans, however, were quite enjoyable. They also featured jalapeños with a mild heat, complemented by a slightly sweet and tangy sauce. The chicken had a great flavor, but unfortunately, most of the breast was quite dry. The wing, in contrast, was satisfactory.

yelp:test:4915.orig: I will not be returning as a client due to an extremely rude female doctor that attempted to reprimand me for questioning the services rendered as well as the amount of the bill. It is our right as a client to ask questions about what we are paying for as well as question the care for our animals, and as a business it is their job to make the clients feel comfortable enough to do so. They did the very opposite and unfortunately most of my prior visits there have been met with rude cold customer service. If they can't provide their human clients with respect and kindness when we are the ones footing the bill \nit is unnerving to think how they treat the animals when they are in their care.
yelp:test:4915.para: I am opting out of being a client because of a notably impolite female veterinarian who tried to scold me for inquiring about the services provided and the bill's cost. It is our entitlement as clients to seek clarification on our expenditures and to question the animal care we receive. This responsibility lies with the business to ensure client comfort in doing so. They failed to uphold this, often delivering unfriendly and cold customer service during my previous visits. The worrying aspect is how they might treat the animals under their care if they can't show respect and kindness to us, the ones paying for the services.

yelp:test:4938.orig:
After I THOUGHT I had ordered a stack of pizzas for a meeting to be delivered at 11:45 am, I called at noon to inquire as to the whereabouts of our lunch to be told I had placed the order for 11:45 PM - ACK!  Panic! SH**!!!!  Whomever the gentleman was who answered the phone put the pizza makers to work immediately and 9 pizzas and an order of wings were delivered within 30 minutes, smoking hot and correct.  5 stars for the excellent customer service that saved me from being drug out back and beaten like a pinata by the hungry mob of nerds... er um... architects.  

Our office orders from this Papa John's quite frequently for meetings and late nights that require the delivery of dinner.  They always get the orders correct, the pizza is always delivered hot and they always bring a stack of plates and napkins - which is nice so we don't have to eat off of legal folders and wipe our hands on our pants.

THANK YOU, PAPA JOHN'S!
yelp:test:4938.para:
Upon realizing I had mistakenly requested pizzas for a 11:45 PM delivery instead of 11:45 AM, I reached out at noon to check on our lunch. I was informed of the error, which caused me to panic and express my frustration. The person who answered the call promptly instructed the pizza makers to start, resulting in 9 pizzas and wings being delivered within half an hour, piping hot and accurate. I awarded 5 stars for the outstanding customer service that prevented me from being overwhelmed by a group of demanding professionals. Our office regularly places orders with Papa John's for meetings and late-night gatherings, and they consistently deliver the correct order, hot pizza, and sufficient plates and napkins, eliminating the need for us to eat off of official documents or use our clothing to clean up. 

THANK YOU, PAPA JOHN'S!

yelp:test:4939.orig: Ordered food around 8:00 now it's around   11:30, called twice but no answer- weird for a restaurant that is open until 1:30 A.M and has already charged my credit card. When I finally got my food it was cold and sucked- I'm not a food snob either (papa John or dominos delivery pizza is fine by me). The pizza was awful, wings were soggy, and mozzarella sticks were cold on the inside. If you're looking for good service and food aim elsewhere this place was awful- bad enough for me to take the time to download this app, and make a review..
yelp:test:4939.para: At approximately 11:30, after placing an order at 8:00, I experienced no response despite two calls. This is unusual for a venue operating until 1:30 A.M. and having already processed my payment. Upon receiving my meal, it was lukewarm and disappointing, even though I don't consider myself a picky eater (I'm fine with Papa John or Dominos pizza). The pizza quality was subpar, the wings were damp, and the mozzarella sticks were chilled inside. For those seeking excellent service and quality food, this location falls short. I felt compelled to write a review on this app after enduring this unsatisfactory experience.

yelp:test:4944.orig: Favorite delivery pizza in town.  Great selection of pies!  Delicious.  Only place we order from now.
yelp:test:4944.para: Top pizza spot in the area. Excellent variety of pies available. Tastes fantastic. Our sole choice for orders.

yelp:test:4962.orig:
Spoiler: I don't golf.

I've been to Leatherman's twice recently, once to play at the driving range and once to play miniature golf.  They have a decent selection of clubs that you can borrow if you're like me and have nothing related to golf.  The pro shop looks pretty cool and the people were nice when I was in buying a bucket.

Now the fun stuff, miniature golf.  This isn't one of those courses with giant animals & cheesy holes, but its a well maintained 18-hole course with a few sneaky holes.  Adults are $7.00 and it is pretty challenging - I got nowhere near par, but it definitely was fun!
yelp:test:4962.para:
Spoiler alert: Golf isn't my thing.

I've visited Leatherman's twice lately, once for hitting balls at the driving range and once for miniature golf. They offer a good range of clubs for borrowing, especially for those unfamiliar with golf, like myself. The pro shop is quite appealing and the staff were friendly when I purchased a bucket.

Now onto the enjoyable part, miniature golf. This isn't a course featuring oversized creatures and humorous obstacles, but a well-kept 18-hole course with some cleverly designed holes. Adults pay $7.00 and it's quite demanding - I didn't reach par, but it was definitely enjoyable!

yelp:test:4973.orig: Finally came in here once recently. It's pretty ok. Nothing to write home about, but decent food not too overpriced.
yelp:test:4973.para: Recently made it here once again. It's fairly satisfactory. Not particularly remarkable, yet the meals are reasonably priced and enjoyable.

yelp:test:4983.orig: Incompetent idiots; these people are. Don't waste your time with this Enterprise location. Thumbs down.
yelp:test:4983.para: These individuals are utterly inept; avoid this Enterprise site at all costs. A firm thumbs down.

yelp:test:5009.orig: To quote Arrest Development, \""I've made a huge mistake.\""
yelp:test:5009.para: Following the sentiment of Arrest Development, one could express, "I've committed a significant error."

yelp:test:5018.orig: Stonecrest Chick-Fil-A is my favorite by far.  They do a phenomenal business and are very well organized.  They hire young folks and train them well.  When busy, they bring the food to your table and are constantly circulating asking if there's anything you need including re-filling beverages.  Everyone seems to have a great attitude which is hard to find in the service industry!  This particular location also seems to have a lot of special events (free breakfasts, buy a combo-get a kid's meal free, etc).  If you live in the area, be sure to sign up for their text updates so you can stay up to date with their offerings!  I wish I owned this place....CASH COW!  Did I say cow?!?  Eat more chicken...
yelp:test:5018.para: My top pick is Stonecrest Chick-Fil-A, which excels in operations and maintains excellent organization. They actively recruit and skillfully train their youthful employees. During peak times, they deliver food to customers and proactively inquire about additional needs, such as refilling drinks. The staff consistently exhibits a positive demeanor, a commendable trait in the service sector. This spot also hosts numerous special promotions, like complimentary breakfasts and kid's meal deals with combo purchases. Residents should register for their text alerts to keep abreast of their ongoing deals. I'd love to have this establishment under my ownership; it's a profitable venture! Chick-Fil-A, indeed, is a 'cash cow'! And let's not forget about their delicious chicken offerings.

yelp:test:5077.orig:
I have never been to the store itself but walked by many times. My boyfriend picked up some lotion, soap and body wash for me for our anniversary and let me just say, he did a good job. The lotion is heavenly and I use it all the time. And the soaps are nice too. We will definitely be 
stopping by here the next time we need a nice gift.

Edit - I just wanted to add my boyfriend calls this place ""My Hookup."" I always get something from there for Valentine's Day, birthdays, etc and I LOVE it!  :)
yelp:test:5077.para: I've never entered the shop, but I've passed it frequently. My partner chose lotion, soap, and body wash for our anniversary, and I must say, he excelled. The lotion is divine, and I frequently use it. The soaps are also pleasing. We'll be returning to this place for our next occasion to find a thoughtful present. \n\nAddendum - I wanted to mention that my boyfriend refers to this place as "My Hookup." I always receive something from there for occasions like Valentine's Day and birthdays, and I adore it! :)

yelp:test:5089.orig: This place is the American Gothic of breakfast food and decor, purposefully bland.\n\nIf I were to take a guess, this place gets most of its high ratings because of it's proximity to campus/greek row. A quaint place for sorority girls to quell their hangovers with tasteless food while telling stories about last night.
yelp:test:5089.para: This establishment embodies the American Gothic aesthetic in both cuisine and ambiance, intentionally unremarkable.\n\nBased on my assumption, its high acclaim likely stems from its location near campus and Greek Row. A charming spot for sorority women to soothe their post-celebration headaches with uninspired fare while reminiscing about the previous evening.

yelp:test:5103.orig: I've now order take out a couple of times from here and GUESS WHAT? They will send you coupons if you order online! What?! BTW, the Indo mac and cheese is amazing.
yelp:test:5103.para: I've recently opted for delivery from this place a few times and LOOK OUT! They're offering discounts if you place your order through their website! Oh, and by the way, their Indian mac and cheese is absolutely fantastic.

yelp:test:5116.orig: Seriously disappointing experience at this restaurant. The service was so slow and our waitress was beyond dull and unfriendly. I'm usually crazy about any type of Mediterranean bread, but the bread I had at Husnu's was dry and thick. When our food finaaaaally came it was another disappointment! Everything on my plate and on my husband's plate was smothered in yogurt sauce. There are way, way, way better Mediterranean restaurants in Madison - this place was not worth the money I reluctantly handed over.
yelp:test:5116.para: I had a truly unsatisfactory time dining at this establishment. The service lagged significantly and our server was exceedingly dull and unapproachable. Normally, I'm quite fond of Mediterranean bread, but the bread at Husnu's was disappointingly dry and dense. The food, which took an eternity to arrive, was yet another letdown. Both my plate and my husband's were drenched in yogurt sauce. There are much superior Mediterranean eateries in Madison - this venue did not justify the reluctantly paid sum.

yelp:test:5117.orig: Love the food - great kebabs! Especially lamb. Raspberry chicken dish - delicious. Service is excellent. Owner is devoted to the quality of food and enjoyment of customers. He is often there to greet customers! Great atmosphere - great music. Great hummus! Oh - and try the dumplings! yum yum!
yelp:test:5117.para: Enjoy the delectable cuisine, particularly the succulent lamb kebabs and the mouthwatering raspberry chicken. The service is impeccable, with the proprietor passionately committed to culinary excellence and customer satisfaction. He frequently welcomes guests with warmth. The ambiance is vibrant, complemented by lively tunes. The hummus is exceptional. Don't miss out on the delightful dumplings! Yum yum!

yelp:test:5124.orig: Great looking restaurant.  We couldn't enjoy the atmosphere though since they crammed everyone in the restaurant into one tiny section.  I agree with the comment about the food being a joke.  Service wasn't great either - lots of employees around but few smiles or greetings.  Don't be fooled by the looks of this place if you want to have a nice dinner.
yelp:test:5124.para: The restaurant boasts an impressive appearance. However, the ambiance suffered due to overcrowding in a confined area. I concur with the critique regarding the subpar quality of the cuisine. The service was lackluster as well, with numerous staff members but a noticeable absence of warmth and friendliness. Avoid being misled by its exterior if you're seeking a pleasant dining experience.

yelp:test:5185.orig: Like Clay P who posted before me, I too love pancakes. Though I love chocolate chip pancakes. But like Clay I did not love the ones that I got a the Original Pancake House. Typically, restaurants just don't do it the way I like them and I have come to expect that. Grading OPH on those terms, they did a respectable job. It is definitely a worthwhile destination for a pancake lover.
yelp:test:5185.para: Similar to Clay P's previous comment, I share a fondness for pancakes, particularly those with chocolate chips. However, akin to Clay's experience, I found the pancakes at the Original Pancake House unsatisfactory. Generally, eateries fail to meet my personal preferences, leading me to rate OPH fairly. Despite this, I consider it a valuable spot for anyone with a penchant for pancakes.

yelp:test:5248.orig: The staff is really nice, and it is a cute little shop, but OMG flies galore!  Flies crawling all over the doughnuts, flies dive bombing all around the store.  The only thing this place needs to complete it is Jeff Goldblum.
yelp:test:5248.para: The team is incredibly friendly, and the shop is adorable, yet the presence of numerous flies is overwhelming! Flies are swarming over the pastries, aggressively swooping around the premises. The sole enhancement this establishment requires to reach its full potential would be the addition of Jeff Goldblum.

To begin with, I was charged $3 more this time - for the exact same item.  I questioned it, and was told they obviously charged me incorrectly the first time.  I wasn't happy about it, but what could I do. The dress also did not have that same sparkling brand new appearance to the fabric it had when they cleaned it the week before.  I took it back inside and pointed out the non-removed stain and the dark x one that hadn't been there before.  The woman said they would try to get it out and I could pick it up on Friday.  I left, and had been gon
yelp:test:5280.para: I am astonished! I brought the identical dress for a second cleaning after wearing it, and this time my experience was completely reversed from the initial one. Initially, I was charged an additional $3 - for the same garment. I inquired about it, and was informed that they must have made an error in the previous charge. yelp:test:5287.orig: Eh! Taste fresh for take out, I guess. I ordered the Spicy Basil with Beef. The sauce was spicy, and the vegetables were fresh, well-prepared, and plentiful. A little too plentiful. I only had a small portion of beef in my meal so I won't be returning. :-(
yelp:test:5287.para: I opted for takeout with a Spicy Basil and Beef dish. The sauce had a fiery kick, and the vegetables were crisp, meticulously cooked, and abundant. However, the portion of beef was disappointingly small, leading me to decide against future visits. :(

yelp:test:5322.orig:
It's passable. Just don't try calling the front desk. Service here is good when you can find the people or they're not on the phone. On the cell phone, with their friend, that is. -1.

The rooms were pretty small, but they got the job done. They were in the middle of remodeling, and I think we still had an unremodeled room. I say this because the beds were noticeably softer in another room that we had than the one I stayed in. -1

There was a sick stain on one of the box springs, it looked like blood. -1.

Plenty of parking, close enough to campus, easy access from I-74.
yelp:test:5322.para: The service is acceptable, but avoid contacting the reception. The staff is more responsive when they're not on the phone, especially when using their mobile devices. The accommodations were somewhat compact, yet functional. They were undergoing renovation, and it seems some rooms remained untouched. The difference in bed softness was evident when compared to another room we occupied. There was a concerning blood-like mark on one of the box springs. Adequate parking was available, and it was conveniently located near the campus, with straightforward access from I-74. -1

yelp:test:5327.orig:
This locksmith store seems to know what they are doing and the only locksmith store that is capable of duplicating my key. However, I was left standing there in the store without a word on for close to 10 minutes after requesting a key to be duplicated... 

When I said ""Excuse me, I don't mean to rush you, but could you tell me how long the process will take?"" I was given back the key by the owner and told that he would not be rushed. I responded ""I did not mean mean to be rude or anything"" he just walked away with his back turned against me. 

The other employee apologized and told me to come back another time.

In all honesty, how can you be the owner of a business and treat customers with so little respect and courtesy. I am not a fan.
yelp:test:5327.para:
This locksmith shop appears proficient and is the sole establishment skilled in copying my key. Nevertheless, I was left unattended in the shop for almost 10 minutes after asking for a key duplication. 

When I politely inquired about the duration of the process, the proprietor handed me the key and assured me that he wouldn't be hurried. I clarified that I wasn't impolite, but he nonchalantly left me behind. 

The other staff member expressed regret and suggested I return later. 

In reality, how can someone run a business and disregard customers with such disrespect and lack of politeness. I am not pleased with this.

yelp:test:5347.orig:
Nothing is new here about my bad experience. But hopefully I can shed some light into their evil world. And then the travelers can choose wisely.

US Worst has retained its title for me in 2011.

Typical story. Mechanical failure. Flight was delayed in Palm Springs. I missed the connection in Phoenix. I was rescheduled for later flight. A delay of 4 hours.

I always avoid US Worst but sometimes it's just impossible. It helps when US Worst is part of Star Alliance (Wrong... more later). I was a United Premier member. I thought I still can get my benefit on US Worst. That's a wrong assumption.

I have experienced nightmares on more than 50% of US Worst flights. More so lately... 100% in past 2 years (2 flights). Luckily I've shifted all possible flights to other not so worst airlines.

To make a long tedious nightmare educational:
1) US Worst does not recognize the full status of United Premier. Not like United and Continental.

2) It's business as usual for US Worst. The costumer service rep expressed indifference. It reminds me of rental clerks in Las Vegas and FlorIda (""you don't like it? Too bad! Move aside, there's a long line waiting for our premiere service"")
yelp:test:5347.para:
Despite my recurring negative encounters, I aim to illuminate their malevolent operations. This insight may guide travelers in making informed decisions. In 2011, US Worst maintained its infamous status for me. A typical narrative involves mechanical breakdowns, resulting in flight postponements in Palm Springs and missed connections in Phoenix, with a subsequent rescheduling and a four-hour delay.

While I typically steer clear of US Worst, there are instances where it's unavoidable. I assumed that my United Premier membership would offer benefits on US Worst flights, but that was a mistaken belief. I've had nightmarish experiences on over half of my US Worst flights, with a recent trend of 100% in the last two years (two flights). Fortunately, I've relocated all feasible flights to less problematic airlines.

To educate through a lengthy, agonizing experience:
1) US Worst does not acknowledge the complete privileges of United Premier, unlike United and Continental.
2) US Worst operates as usual, with customer service representatives showing apathy. This mirrors the indifferent attitude of rental clerks in Las Vegas and Florida ("You're not satisfied? That's unfortunate. Move aside, there's a long queue for our top service").

yelp:test:5371.orig: Loved the location for First Fridays! I loved the older crowd and more of a family atmosphere. The exhibits were absolutely wonderful. Coming from NYC and Chicago, I was not expecting too much having been spoiled with the likes of the Met, Moma, Art institute of Chicago, and museum of contemporary art in Chicago, but I was wrong! There was a special under water theme area with adorable DIY crafts and nibbbles (similar to first friday in Chicago). The fashion section was also great as was the modern exhibits with heavy hitters like my favorite Rothko. I grew a lot of appreciation for some new artists. The museum is a great size in that it is actually accomplishable in a night and similar in size to the Guggeheim. Some areas leave something to be desired but I have no regrets leaving. It was a fabulous time.
yelp:test:5371.para: Adored the venue for First Fridays! I cherished the mature demographic and a familial vibe. The displays were utterly impressive. Coming from NYC and Chicago, where I was accustomed to the Met, Moma, Art institute of Chicago, and contemporary art museum, I was pleasantly surprised! There was a unique underwater theme zone with cute do-it-yourself crafts and snacks (akin to Chicago's First Fridays). The fashion segment was also commendable, as were the modern exhibits featuring renowned artists like my preferred Rothko. I developed a newfound respect for several emerging artists. The museum's size is ideal, as it's feasible to explore in a single evening and comparable to the Guggenheim. Although some areas could improve, I departed without any regrets. It was an exceptional experience.

yelp:test:5396.orig: Boo on the Food! This place is way over hyped. They tried to charge $7 for a little waffle and 2 cold, greasy chicken thighs. Not impressed at all. The only reason it gets 2 stars is because the waiter was nice and the place looked cool. \n\nFirst impressions are everything, so they say, and in this instance I would agree. Since moving here over a year ago I have heard people go on and on about Lolo's chicken and waffles, especially when they find out I moved from the south. \""Oh it is the best soul food\"", \""They have the best fried chicken I have had anywhere..\"" are some of the things people have said. We live in Mesa and there is not a location near us but this morning  we were running errands in Phoenix and drove about 15 minutes out of our way so I could finally try this place that so many people have raved about. The place was decorated nice, it was not too long after they opened and it was not busy, we were seated right away. Took about 10 minutes before we saw a server, our drinks were brought out fairly quick and our order taken. Our food came out pretty quick but what difference does quick service make when the food is cold? The skin on the chicken was not even crisp
yelp:test:5396.para: Scorn the Cuisine! This establishment is excessively exaggerated. They attempted to demand $7 for a modest waffle and two cold, oily chicken thighs. Completely unimpressed. The sole reason for awarding it 2 stars is due to the courteous waiter and the appealing ambiance. \n\nFirst impressions are crucial, as they claim, and in this scenario, I concur. Having relocated here over a year ago, I've heard numerous discussions about Lolo's chicken and waffles, particularly when I mention my southern origins. Quotes like, "It's the finest soul food," and "They serve the crispiest fried chicken I've ever tasted," are common. Despite living in Mesa with no nearby location, we ventured to Phoenix today, driving 15 minutes out of our way to finally experience this highly praised place. The decor was pleasant, it was not crowded, and we were seated promptly. It took roughly 10 minutes to be served, and our drinks arrived quickly. However, the speed of service is inconsequential when the food is served cold. The chicken skin lacked the desired crispiness.

yelp:test:5443.orig: Really cool lights at the fair tonight look to the north and see such a delight.\nWell last night was the last day of the fair is closed it's gone now for next year but they will be the next fair in the spring.
yelp:test:5443.para: The captivating illuminations at the fair this evening point north and evoke sheer joy.\nThe fair concluded last night, but it's now closed for the upcoming year. However, anticipation builds for the next event, which will take place in the spring.

yelp:test:5484.orig:
The food is always been amazing there and they have great deal
When my wife wants to go out to breakfast that is where we go

The omelettes are the best
yelp:test:5484.para:
The cuisine consistently impresses and they offer a wide selection
When my spouse desires a morning meal, that's our chosen spot

Their omelettes are unparalleled in quality

yelp:test:5559.orig: Best place in the valley for dim sum.  They are always consistent.  I've been coming here for over 10 years.  Since I'm allergic to MSG and dim sum always contains MSG, I often order off the menu and request no MSG.  I'll eat some of the dim sum and suffer the effects of MSG afterwards.  My dim sum favs - har gow, sui mai, char sui bao, and coconut dessert.  Dinner - best peking duck with the buns and steamed fish.  Overall, good place for chinese.
yelp:test:5559.para: The ideal spot in the valley for savoring dim sum, renowned for its unwavering quality. Having frequented this establishment for more than a decade, I've developed a preference for customizing my orders to exclude MSG due to my sensitivity. Despite this, I occasionally indulge in the dim sum and endure the MSG repercussions. Among my preferred dim sum selections are har gow, sui mai, char sui bao, and coconut-based sweets. For dinner, I highly recommend the exceptional Peking duck served with accompanying buns and steamed fish. In summary, it's an excellent venue for Chinese cuisine aficionados.

yelp:test:5594.orig: This is actually kind of sad. The customer service here is very good. Food was served quickly and tasted fine. Here's my problem. I ordered a 3 pc meal. What I got was two pieces of chicken (leg & thigh) and the one thigh had been cut into two pieces. No, really, I'm not kidding! (see photo) WTF? Are you kidding me. Then, once you get to your table and sit down, you realize the Salt Police have left a note insinuating that your eating too much Sodium and you need some extra exercise if you want the salt shaker because you have to get back up and go get one. COME ON GUYS! For a $10 meal I want 3 REAL pieces of chicken and a salt shaker! Ugh!
yelp:test:5594.para: It's somewhat disappointing. The service provided is commendable, and the meal was delivered promptly with satisfactory flavor. However, my issue lies here. I had ordered a trio of dishes. Instead, I received two chicken portions (leg and thigh) and the thigh was further divided into two. I assure you, this is not a joke. (Refer to the attached image). What's going on? Are you joking? Upon seating and dining, a note from the Salt Police suggests excessive sodium intake and recommends additional exercise to obtain a salt shaker. This is unacceptable! For a $10 meal, I expected three authentic chicken pieces and a salt shaker. Frustrating!

yelp:test:5661.orig:
I can't remember how we came upon this company, but dealing with this company last year was very pleasant.  After calling several A/C companies, we settled on having this company put in the new A/C unit with a good warranty on it.  We had a Carrier unit put on and it was in the middle of the range in terms of price - not the cheapest nor the least expensive.  

I think after everything was said and done, it was close to $7K for a new ground unit to adequately cool an almost 1800 sq ft home in central AZ.  

They did not try to high pressure sell us or anything.  Once we decided and set up the appointment, they came at the time they said they would and installed the outside unit as well as replaced the heater coil or whatever it's called up in the attic.

We were up and running in no time and the electric bills have been lower with a new more efficient unit.  It keeps the house cool and works great.  We typically don't run the unit in the winter - the heater, so at least part of the year it gets rest.

Would use this company again.  Very professional.
yelp:test:5661.para:
I'm uncertain about the origin of our discovery of this business, but our interaction with them the previous year was exceedingly agreeable. Following discussions with multiple HVAC providers, we chose this company for the installation of a new air conditioning system with a solid guarantee. We opted for a Carrier model, which was priced reasonably, neither at the lowest nor the highest end. 

In retrospect, the total cost for a new ground-level cooling system to sufficiently cool a nearly 1800 sq ft residence in central Arizona was close to $7K. 

Their approach was not aggressive in sales tactics; once we made our decision and scheduled the service, they adhered to the agreed-upon timeline, installing the external unit and replacing the attic's heating component as promised. 

The system was operational swiftly, and we've noticed a reduction in our electricity expenses due to the new, more efficient unit. It effectively maintains a cool environment and functions flawlessly. We usually don't use the unit during winter months, allowing the heating system to take over part of the year. 

We would certainly consider this company for future needs. Their professionalism was commendable.

yelp:test:5689.orig:
So I live in the ghetto and this is the Home Depot I go to even though there is one a tad closer to my house. 

The staff here is always very friendly and very very helpful! On my recent trip Denny in the hardware section was beyond helpful, I wouldnt have been able to complete my project without his help!

yelp:test:5689.para:
I reside in the slum area and this is the Home Depot I frequent, despite a slightly nearer option available. 

The employees here consistently exhibit exceptional friendliness and assistance. During my latest visit, Denny in the hardware department was incredibly supportive, without his aid, I wouldn't have finished my task. 

My partner and I also acquired carpeting from this store for our bedrooms. The appearance is impressive and the installation was swift.

yelp:test:5716.orig:
Movers Beware- Before you use this company- read this!  We used this company because the salesperson said they were the best and that they had no complaints.  They didn't have any complaints when I checked.  When the packers showed up, and the truck, everyone was great.  I even went out and bought everyone lunch so they could eat because otherwise they were not going to take a break during packing or loading.

If you pick option # 1 they ""dump"" the furniture wherever and you place it later after they leave.  At least that's what I was told when the truck arrived to our new house in CO.
