yelp:test:7553.para:
I was able to remain here without cost, thanks to the timeshare points of my travel buddy's parent. However, a group of seven would have been significantly more economical than any similar spot on the strip. 

We occupied a suite that comprised a one-bedroom and a studio. Both had balconies, and fortunately, we had a strip view! 

One-bedroom details:
-Complete kitchen with necessary items (pots, pans, cutlery, plates, cups, salt, pepper, sponge, dishwashing liquid, etc)
-Bathroom equipped with two sinks and a large bathtub
-Dining table and chairs
-Large TV
-Bed and wardrobe in the bedroom
-Sofa in the living room
-We slept 5
Extra: Ipod dock and speakers for a room party!

Studio specifics:
-Microwave, coffee maker, cups
-Fold-out bed
-Bathroom with shower stall
-Large TV, though not as big as the one-bedroom's
-We slept 2

This place leans more towards family, and we did attract some odd looks from other guests passing through the lobby "dressed to impress." The staff was exceptionally

yelp:test:7555.orig:
We had a 4 day stay here and overall were very happy.
We got a Groupon deal.  The lady at the from desk said Expedia had best prices if you are booking at other times.
The only thing that annoyed me was that our room faced the lane where there was a dumpster that seemed to be getting rubbish in it all hours of night.  I suspect illegal dumping.  Then the dump truck comes around 630/7am.  Too early for me :) Otherwise there was no noise from other guests.  The pool is nice with free cabanas.  The kids water play area was excellent and in shade all day long.  Parking is free.  Kitchen facilities were excellent.  Rooms were clean.  Bring your own dvd's/ cds to play on the stereo and dvd player.  
Curtains blocked light very very well and there was an excellent view of the strip.
I don't think there is any wifi.  We took our own aircards...but I think you can logon to other wifi networks and pay a fee.
There is a very cheap Filipino takeaway in Hawaiian Marketplace. 

Overall, would definitely recommend if you are a family.  If you are young and single, maybe you want something more happening.
yelp:test:7555.para: During our 4-day visit, we were extremely content. We benefited from a Groupon offer. The front desk representative mentioned that Expedia offered superior rates for off-peak bookings. The only slight irritation was our room's orientation towards a lane with a constantly filling dumpster, which we suspected to be illegal dumping, especially with the early morning dump truck rounds. However, the pool area was delightful with complimentary cabanas, and the children's water play zone was consistently shaded. Parking was free, and the kitchen amenities were top-notch. The rooms were spotless, and we enjoyed bringing our own media for entertainment. The curtains effectively blocked out light, and the strip view was impressive. While we didn't encounter wifi, we managed with our own aircards, though alternative wifi networks with a fee were available. There was also a budget-friendly Filipino takeaway at the Hawaiian Marketplace. \n\nIn summary, I would wholeheartedly suggest this place for families. For younger, single individuals seeking more vibrant activities, it might not be the ideal choice.

yelp:test:7565.orig: This is \""It's A Small World\"" on crack. Medeval themed, with a cheesy old wizard in the main tower of the castle overlooking the strip. This place ONLY gets credit for being one of the first \""themed\"" hotels in Vegas. This place is pretty old, worn and nasty. The casino, rooms, and restaurants are yuck. With this prime piece of strip property, your would think the Excalibur doesn't have much left in the tank.
yelp:test:7565.para: This establishment is a revamped version of \""It's A Small World\"", featuring a Medeval theme and a dated wizard character dominating the castle's main tower, surveying the strip. Despite being recognized as one of the initial themed hotels in Las Vegas, it's visibly aged, deteriorated, and unpleasant. The casino, accommodations, and dining areas are subpar. Given its prime location on the strip, one might assume the Excalibur lacks significant potential.

yelp:test:7592.orig: You get what you pay for. Cheap rates, but the service and maintenance of the hotel isn't that great. The walls in Tower I are pretty thin as well. Not sure how Tower II is. Probably not staying here again in the future.
yelp:test:7592.para: The quality of the hotel matches its price. While the rates are low, the service and upkeep are subpar. The walls in Tower I are noticeably thin. I'm uncertain about Tower II. I'm hesitant to consider staying here again.

yelp:test:7594.orig: Spend the extra money to stay in a hotel rather then a place that smells horrible from the second you walk in the door. There is no good amenities, rom service is only open breakfast and lunch, to be honest I really have nothing good to say about the place, this is my first time staying here, but I come to Vegas at least once a month for the last 5 years and haven't had a worse experience. PS, there is no wifi
yelp:test:7594.para: Invest additional funds to opt for a hotel over a location that immediately emits an unpleasant odor upon entry. The amenities are subpar, with dining service limited to breakfast and lunch, and frankly, I have little positive feedback to offer for this establishment, despite it being my inaugural visit. I make the trip to Las Vegas at least monthly for the past half-decade, yet I've never encountered a more disappointing experience. Note: there is an absence of internet connectivity.

yelp:test:7612.orig: I always get the chicken caesar salad and a good plate of garlic fries.  It is fantastic.  The garlic fries is really amazing!  Ample parking with a good view of the Residence Inn by Marriott.  That hotel is magnificent at night.  GB also has two (or more) event spaces available for booking group gatherings.
yelp:test:7612.para: I consistently order the chicken caesar salad and a generous portion of garlic fries. It's absolutely delightful. The garlic fries are truly impressive! There's ample parking with a pleasant sight of the Residence Inn by Marriott. The hotel shines beautifully at night. GB also offers two (or more) venues for reserving group events.

yelp:test:7618.orig: So we got to come here for their VIP night last week and being I had never been here before it was a nice surprise. We weren't sure what to expect but you started out in the club room with johnny depp and george clooney, a good start! They served appetizers and drinks, had a DJ and plenty of places to sit.  There was a picture opportunity as well but as with one or two others I wasn't sure with who the figure was supposed to be.  (hence the 4 instead of 5 stars).  As you continue room to room there is a different theme, different appetizers were served based on the theme and drinks to match.  there were about 4 different places to get a professional photo op and we had fun posing as some had props.  Each guest got a picture to take home as well which is a nice momento.  We each also got a Madame Tussauds small bottle of sparkling wine to take with us.  \nThere were plenty of fun moments throughout the night but the 4D superhero movie was probably our favorite part.  Its only 10 minutes but it was quite fun and entertaining.  Thanks to yelp for this opportunity and a night filled with memories that continue to make us laugh.
yelp:test:7618.para: Last week, we attended a VIP event at this location, which was a pleasant surprise since it was our first time there. Initially uncertain about what to anticipate, the evening began in the club room with appearances by Johnny Depp and George Clooney, setting a positive tone. The hosts provided appetizers, beverages, and ample seating. A photo opportunity was also available, but I wasn't certain about the subject, leading to a 4-star rating instead of 5. As we moved from room to room, each space featured a unique theme with corresponding appetizers and drinks. There were approximately four spots for professional photos, which we enjoyed, especially with some props. Additionally, we received a keepsake photo for each person to take home. We also received a small bottle of sparkling wine from Madame Tussauds to enjoy. Throughout the evening, there were numerous enjoyable moments, but the 10-minute 4D superhero film stood out as our preferred highlight. We're grateful to Yelp for this memorable night that continues to bring joy.

yelp:test:7627.orig: This place is phenomenal! Real, authentic Italian cuisine. The garbage salad is one of their signature dishes. It's an amazing Cesar salad, with hearts of palm, shrimp, avocado, and tomato. It was so delicious! I also had their veal parmesan which was rich and super tasty! This place is an institution in Las Vegas. I highly recommend it!
yelp:test:7627.para: This establishment is truly exceptional! It offers genuine Italian food. Their renowned garbage salad stands out, featuring hearts of palm, shrimp, avocado, and tomato, making it a fantastic Cesar salad. The flavors were incredibly delightful! I also savored their veal parmesan, which was both luxurious and incredibly flavorful! This spot is a cornerstone in Las Vegas. I wholeheartedly endorse it!

yelp:test:7635.orig: Great lunch place ...I had the cup of Matzo Ball soup it was delicious..very hot with lots of celery and carrots....my friend and I shared the corned beef sandwich which also was very good...prices are reasonable. If you come at 1 o clock you beat the lunch crowd.
yelp:test:7635.para: Excellent dining spot ...I savored the Matzo Ball soup, it was scrumptious and piping hot, packed with celery and carrots. My companion and I enjoyed the corned beef sandwich, which was equally delightful. The cost is fair. Visiting at 1 o'clock allows you to avoid the midday rush.

yelp:test:7653.orig:
Firefly is simply the best near-strip restaurant.  The only downside: a lot of people now know this, and the relatively small restaurant is now pretty much always packed (and I believe they do not take reservations).  However, the food and service is well worth the wait (or the risk of a wait).

The menu is HUGE and is constantly being changed and added to, and I've yet to try something that I didn't like.  I few suggestions that I enjoy: the bacon wrapped stuffed dates are a must try, along with the ham & cheese croquetas.  The firefly fries are amazing, and big enough to share, as are the calamari.  Other suggestions include the Thai beef salad, the tuna tartar and shrimp ceviche, stuffed pepper, mac n cheese, baked talapia, and the mergeuz.  Don't fill up on the entrees too much, because the tres leches cake is probably the best thing on the menu, so save room for dessert.  

Firefly is also known for its selections of sangria, infused vodkas (vodka + fresh squeezed juices), and mojitos, all of which are great - my favorites are the infused vodka on the rocks, and the passion fruit and blood orange mojitos.  

Go here with a small group and order in small batches, I'd sugg
yelp:test:7653.para:
Firefly stands out as an exceptional near-strip dining establishment. The primary drawback is its popularity, leading to a consistently full restaurant without reservation options. Nevertheless, the quality of food and service compensates for the potential wait. 

The extensive menu is always evolving, offering a variety of dishes that I've yet to find disappointing. Some of my favorites include bacon-wrapped stuffed dates, ham & cheese croquettes, and firefly fries. The calamari and Thai beef salad are also worth trying. However, it's wise not to overindulge in entrees to leave room for the delectable tres leches cake.

Firefly is also celebrated for its range of sangria, infused vodkas, and mojitos. Among these, the infused vodka served chilled and the passion fruit and blood orange mojitos are particularly favored.

When dining with a small group, it's recommended to order in small quantities. This way, you can fully enjoy the diverse menu offerings without feeling overwhelmed. Go here and make the most of your culinary experience.

yelp:test:7660.orig:
I type this in my hospital bed so I'm sure you know where I'm going with this. I as ate here 4/23/12 with about 5 other friends from out of town to show off how amazing this place is. And it was another great dining experience.... 

72 hours later or less and I'm in a state of what seems to be nearing death.  And it seemed none of my friends were affected but they were/are. I just happened to get it the worst!! 

I've been a firefly customer for 5 years! Never have I gone through anything like this. I may never come back and never recommend this particular firefly to
Anyone or anyone coming to visit Las Vegas... I'm still in shock this has happened.  Most expensive dining experience ever. Thanks a lot.


*** also this was no food poisoning I got for all you dim witted fools that think otherwise. Salmonella feels like and is (currently) Hell. 



SALMONELLA
yelp:test:7660.para:
I'm composing this message from my hospital room, ensuring you grasp the context of my narrative. On April 23, 2012, I dined here with approximately five friends from afar to demonstrate the exceptional quality of this establishment. It was a memorable culinary adventure...

Within a mere 72 hours or less, I find myself on the brink of death. It appears that my companions were not similarly impacted, yet they too are suffering. I'm unfortunate enough to have endured the most severe consequences...

As a loyal patron for half a decade, I've never encountered such a harrowing ordeal. I doubt I'll return or suggest this specific establishment to anyone, especially those visiting Las Vegas. I'm still reeling from this unexpected turn of events. This was the costliest dining experience I've ever had. I appreciate your understanding.


*** Additionally, I want to clarify that this was not a case of food poisoning, as some might mistakenly believe. The agony I'm experiencing is akin to Hell, caused by Salmonella.

yelp:test:7675.orig: Negative:  This is one of the older hotels. Stayed in the Mardi Gras tower on the 16th floor. The room was dirty and several things were broken or in need of maintenance. (Hair dryer was broken, drain in shower was clogged, key card reader worked intermittently) Room also needed remodeling.   Cost for Saturday night stay $40- You get what you pay for. Air quality is poor. Casino is very smokey and the air doesn't seem to be filtered. Extra charge for internet access.\n\nPositive: Location is right on the Strip- Almost right in the middle.  Venetian, Mirage, Forum Shops, Treasure Island, etc are all close by. Monorail station is continently located right on site. Free shuttle to Rio, Bally's and Paris. Airport shuttle is $7 per person - Cash Only. Tix4Tonite Box Office is close by in the Casino Royale. Higher tier rooms are of better quality.
yelp:test:7675.para: The hotel is somewhat aged and situated on the Strip, centrally positioned with nearby attractions like the Venetian, Mirage, and Forum Shops. The Mardi Gras tower on the 16th floor offers free shuttle services to Rio, Bally's, and Paris, with an airport shuttle available for $7 per person, cash only. While the room quality is subpar, higher-tier rooms provide better quality. However, the room was unclean, with broken items and maintenance issues, including a malfunctioning hair dryer, a clogged shower drain, and an unreliable key card reader. The air quality is notably poor due to the smoky casino atmosphere, and there's an additional charge for internet access. Despite these drawbacks, the prime location and convenient transportation options make it a viable choice. The cost for a Saturday night stay is $40, reflecting the value received.

yelp:test:7686.orig:
Friendly service, beautiful contemporary decor and tasty food at a very reasonable price! What more can you ask for?

Keep in mind I generally don't write reviews unless I am really compelled to do so, hence this is only my second review on here.

Before our drive out to Vegas with about 15 friends, we contemplated on where we should eat. As you know, the strip has no shortage of restaurants and to be honest, we always go food hunting in Vegas with two notions in mind, any decent restaurant is pricey and the food is not the greatest. After all, you are in the middle of the desert, right?

A friend highly recommended Spago so we decided to give them a call and make the reservation. Upon arrival, we literally stepped one foot into the restaurant and headed straight to our seats. This wouldn't be a big deal normally but the restaurant was packed and normally you wait forever in Vegas. The table was immaculate and our servers were very quick to ask us what beverages we would like. Alcohol of course, easy on the rocks.

They bring around a bread tray for you to select from four different types of breads, all very soft and flavorful, along with a plate with four spread/dipping op
yelp:test:7686.para:
Warm hospitality, stylish modern aesthetics, and delicious cuisine offered at an affordable cost! Is there anything more desirable?

Please note that I typically refrain from writing reviews unless I am strongly motivated, which is why this is my second review on this platform.

Before our journey to Las Vegas with approximately 15 companions, we deliberated on where to dine. Given the abundance of eateries on the strip and my usual experience that decent restaurants are costly and the food quality is subpar, we were on the lookout for a good meal. After all, you're in the heart of the desert.

A friend suggested Spago, so we decided to give them a call and book a table. As soon as we entered, we immediately went to our seats. This wouldn't normally be an issue, but the restaurant was crowded and in Vegas, waiting times can be long. The table was spotless and our waitstaff were prompt in asking us about our preferred drinks. Alcohol was readily available, served on the rocks.

They also provided a bread selection tray with four different types of bread, all soft and tasty, along with a plate featuring four spread/dipping options.

yelp:test:7687.orig: The wife and I ate here on our first trip to Las Vegas before we got married. I can still taste the ground pork and ginger pot stickers, drizzled with a soy glaze and thinly sliced scallions.  This is were we both fell in love with sushi, and for  good reasons. It was here where we dared to use chopsticks, and haven't looked back since. Thanks Wolfgang,  it was at your restaurant where are love for dining started together.
yelp:test:7687.para: On our initial journey to Las Vegas prior to our wedding, my spouse and I enjoyed this place. The flavors of ground pork and ginger pot stickers, complemented with a soy glaze and scallion slices, linger on my palate. It was here that we both developed a fondness for sushi, for compelling reasons. This is where we took the plunge with chopsticks, a decision we've maintained ever since. A heartfelt gratitude to Wolfgang, as it was your establishment that sparked our shared passion for culinary experiences.

yelp:test:7710.orig: 4 of us ate here yesterday and we were very disappointed on their service and their food. The food was very salty and the serving portions were inconsistent.  This place is over priced for the quality of food they serve. I would not recommend this to anyone.
yelp:test:7710.para: Four individuals dined at this establishment yesterday and expressed significant dissatisfaction with both the service and the food quality. The dishes were excessively salty, and the portion sizes varied greatly. The cost of the meals does not match the subpar food quality. I would advise against recommending this place to others.

yelp:test:7734.orig: Wouldn't go back to this hotel.  I love dogs and animals just as much as anybody but I don't want dog hairs on the bathroom floor!  The front desk says they charge $100 for people with dogs because they do a special clean up after the pet leaves.  Well they must've missed my room!  It's really an uncomfortable stay when you have to put \""sheets\"" on the sofa and chairs because you don't want someone's pet hair all over you! Residence Inn you should make sure the housekeeper does that \""$100\"" clean up!
yelp:test:7734.para: I wouldn't return to this hotel despite my affection for pets. The presence of dog hair on the bathroom floor is unacceptable. The front desk informs that a $100 fee is imposed on pet owners for a unique cleaning service post-pet departure. It seems they overlooked my room. The experience becomes quite distressing when you're forced to cover furniture with "sheets" to avoid pet hair. I suggest Residence Inn ensures housekeepers perform this thorough cleaning.

yelp:test:7801.orig: My family and I really enjoyed our first visit to Bahama Breeze. I have been meaning to try it for some time. We went in on a Saturday afternoon and they were not too busy. The food was pretty good, but the best part of the visit was the staff. When we first walked in, one of the servers walked up to my kids who were looking and the fountain and pulled two pennies out of his own pocket for them to throw into the fountain. When we were first sat it took a couple minutes for our waiter to come to the table and two of the other servers (who had just gotten off) noticed and without us having to ask went and found our server. Our server was also very friendly and did a great job. My family and I will definitely be returning to this restaurant in the future.
yelp:test:7801.para: We had a fantastic time during our initial trip to Bahama Breeze, which I had been eager to experience for a while. We arrived on a Saturday afternoon and found it quite relaxed. The cuisine was commendable, but the highlight of our visit was the exceptional hospitality of the staff. Upon entering, a server approached my children, who were intrigued by the fountain, and generously gave them two pennies to toss in. Our waiter took a little while to attend to our table, but two other servers, who had just finished their shift, spotted us and proactively located our server without prompting. The warmth and efficiency of our server left a lasting impression. It's clear that we will be revisiting this establishment soon.

yelp:test:7802.orig: It has been a few years since we have eaten here and were looking forward to our favorite sandwiches for lunch. First let me say, that service here is hit or miss. Sometimes it is fabulous. Other times, horrible. There is no in between. This was a horrible time - waitress would not shut up, did not accept that we did not want alcoholic drinks or appetizers and tried to push them on us, she pulled a menu one of my party was holding and started flipping through it, insisted on telling us the \""specials\"" despite we knew what we wanted.... anyway - we were looking forward to the Grilled Chicken Sandwich and Portabello Mushroom Sandwich. Both were a disappointment - chicken was like rubber, bread tasted bad (not ciabatta anymore). The portabello sandwich was mashed flat as if someone sat on it and the vegetables were diced small and indistinguishable. More so - for a Saturday lunch it was dead... not the normal for this place. Usually it is busy. Looking out the window we got to watch a drunk/high gentleman purusing the parking lot, and then when we left we were confronted by a man who \""wanted to ask us questions\"" and when we refused he started swearing, dropping the f-bomb and b
yelp:test:7802.para: After several years without a visit, we anticipated our cherished sandwiches for a midday meal. I must mention, the service here fluctuates dramatically - at times exceptional, at others, abysmal, with no middle ground. This particular instance was particularly unpleasant - the server was incessantly chattering, refused our request to forgo drinks and appetizers, and aggressively promoted the specials, even though we were clear on our order. Our expectations for the Grilled Chicken and Portabello Mushroom Sandwiches were not met - the chicken was tough, the bread had a poor taste (not the usual ciabatta), and the Portabello was flattened and the veggies were finely chopped and hard to tell apart. It was unusually quiet for a Saturday lunch, which is typically bustling. We observed a disheveled individual searching the parking lot, and upon our departure, a man approached us, insisting on asking us questions, which we politely declined, leading to him resorting to profanity.

yelp:test:7859.orig:
The MOST beautiful hotel.  Maybe ever.  Staying anywhere else just isn't as fun.

La Bette (yuck!) has been redone as Tryst, and is quite lovely.

Splurge on a cabana.  Don't miss the ""adult pool""... it's hiding on the other side of the casino cabana, if you're lost.  Why every pool in Vegas isn't topless-optional is a complete mystery to me.
yelp:test:7859.para:
The epitome of elegance in accommodations, perhaps unmatched in all time. Opting for any other lodging seems less enjoyable.

La Bette has been transformed into Tryst, now a delightful place.

Consider investing in a cabana. Don't overlook the "adult pool" - it's concealed behind the casino cabana, useful if you're disoriented. The reason why not all pools in Las Vegas offer nudity as an option remains a puzzle to me.

yelp:test:7886.orig: Hotel is beautiful and if you want to stay at a place where you will be treated like shit, this is the place for you. I stayed here last year and it took me an hour and a half to check in at what they like to call the VIP check in.  Believing it was an isolated instance, I came back this year. I reserved an $800 suite four months ago and it is now 5:00 pm and the room is still not ready. The staff and manager offer no accommodations or apologies and their attitude is that if I don't like paying for a room that I don't get to use, I should stay somewhere else. I assured them that I would on all future stays.
yelp:test:7886.para: The hotel exudes charm, yet it's notorious for its poor treatment of guests. I had a stay here previously, which involved a lengthy half-hour wait at their so-called VIP check-in. Assuming it was a one-off, I returned this year. I had booked an $800 suite four months back, but at 5:00 pm, the room remains unprepared. The staff and manager lack any form of compensation or regret, maintaining a stance that if I'm unwilling to pay for an unavailable room, I should find another accommodation. I've made it clear that I'll take my business elsewhere in the future.

yelp:test:7893.orig:
This place is so huge (outside look is deceiving). Many halls and little rooms. You really need a map to get around or you'd end up in totally wrong event like I did. 

Catching cab is challenging, shuttle train thing is useless unless your destination is near the few stops(yet I can't find the entrance to station often) 

This isn't my fav conventions...
yelp:test:7893.para:
This location appears vast from the outside, but it's filled with numerous corridors and small chambers. Navigating without a guide could lead you astray, as I experienced. 

Securing a taxi can be difficult, and the shuttle service proves ineffective unless you're close to the limited stops, which is often hard to locate. 

I must admit, this isn't my preferred conventions.

yelp:test:7928.orig:
Everything about this place was just so-so including the service.   Nothing was really bad but nothing stands out.  Had decent lamb vindaloo (asked for extra spicy but not so spicy), chickent tikka masala, malai kofta and a couple different naans- which weren't that great.  

Still looking for a good cheap-eats Indian in Vegas.  This place is a little pricey though not as ridiculously overpriced as Gaylords.

If your craving decent Indian food and not afraid to spend a couple bucks then this place should fit the bill.
yelp:test:7928.para:
The ambiance and service at this location were average, lacking any remarkable qualities. While nothing was particularly disappointing, nothing was particularly impressive either. The lamb vindaloo, chicken tikka masala, malai kofta, and various naans were satisfactory, though not exceptional. 

Despite this, I'm still on the hunt for an affordable Indian eatery in Vegas. This spot is somewhat costly, but it's not as exorbitantly priced as Gaylords.

If you're in the mood for good Indian cuisine and don't mind spending a few dollars, this place might be suitable for you.

yelp:test:7930.orig:
My wife and I have tried only the lunch buffet, since they do not serve from the menu during lunch.

Maybe I have been spoiled by the excellent Indian food in and around San Francisco, i.e. Pakwan, Shalimar, and others. At any rate the food at Ghandi is mediocre and overpriced: $11.99 for the lunch buffet, loaded with bland vegetarian dishes and a few chicken-scrap entrees.

Oh, well, I may try another Indian restaurant in Las Vegas, though I may just wait until the next time I'm in San Francisco.
yelp:test:7930.para:
We've exclusively sampled the lunch buffet, as the menu isn't available during that time. Perhaps my preference for high-quality Indian cuisine in and around San Francisco, such as Pakwan and Shalimar, has influenced my opinion. Nonetheless, I found the food at Ghandi to be average and costly: $11.99 for the buffet, featuring uninspiring vegetarian options and limited chicken-based dishes.

Despite this, I might explore other Indian eateries in Las Vegas, but I'm considering waiting until my next visit to San Francisco.

yelp:test:7949.orig:
In Atlantic City this would be a solid 4 stars, believe it or not. However, compared to what's happening south of the Riviera on The Strip right now, meh.

There are a couple of things to note on the good side- 
the slots are never crowded and neither are the table games
the crowd here is as unpretentious as you can get 
the history of the resort is hard to match- Dino used to be a part owner and Liberace was the headliner here shortly after the doors opened for the first time. Frank Sinatra had one of the rooms in the Monte Carlo Tower remodeled to meet his tastes during one of his runs. There are a few exhibits of the heyday of the Riviera near the Monaco Tower including a great photo of Elvis and Jerry Lee Lewis onstage together.
rooms are cheap
Peppermill is right next door

On the bad side-
it's dated inside...from the way it's decorated to the way it's operated
unless you can appreciate ""Old Vegas"" you won't think you are getting the Vegas experience here

Some new developments are underway nearby which may force the Riv to update and upgrade in order to stay relevant. For now, they are firmly in the 70s & 80s in terms of style and it's not even good enough f
yelp:test:7949.para:
In Atlantic City, this would merit a commendable 4-star rating, despite some skepticism. However, when juxtaposed with the current happenings south of the Riviera on The Strip, it falls short of expectations.

Several positive aspects to highlight include:
the slots and table games are consistently unoccupied
the atmosphere here is down-to-earth and unpretentious
the resort's rich history is unparalleled- Dino was once a co-owner and Liberace was the main attraction shortly after the inaugural opening. Frank Sinatra even had a room in the Monte Carlo Tower customized to his liking during one of his stints. There are also several exhibits from the Riviera's golden era near the Monaco Tower, including a remarkable picture of Elvis and Jerry Lee Lewis performing together.
the accommodations are affordable
The Peppermill is conveniently located next door

Conversely, there are some drawbacks:
the interior feels outdated, from its decor to its operations
tunless you have a fondness for the nostalgic "Old Vegas" vibe, it may not feel like a true Vegas experience

New developments in the vicinity could potentially compel the Riviera to modernize and enhance in order to remain relevant. Currently, they are firmly rooted in the 70s and 80s in

yelp:test:7950.orig:
You know, I don't give a lot of single star ratings. Honestly this is the first time i've wished I could give a no star rating. I've lived in CA for years, and made many many many many trips to Vegas as it's not far away. I've stayed in hotel all up and down the strip, state line and even off strip. 

THIS HOTEL is the WORST I have ran into.

Seriously... what gives? Some of the now gone hotels from just past stateline... that no one really stopped in were nicer than the Riviera. 

I'm guessing that this mighty giant has finally just gotten old and needs to be torn down. I mean, their main attraction is an act I remember from the 80s. They let the room Frank Sanatra sang in rot with nothing happening in it. The hotel itself isn't very clean, and over all it's just a really sad experience. 

I stayed here for over a week for a convention I was attending at the Riviera. I have to say I was not impressed with their convention space either. It was limited, and wasn't a huge fan. 

The only redeeming quality surprisingly enough, was the Buffet on site. It actually was pretty decent.
yelp:test:7950.para:
I rarely assign solitary one-star evaluations, and this occasion marks the first time I've contemplated a zero-star rating. Having resided in CA for an extended period, I've embarked on numerous journeys to Vegas due to its proximity. I've lodged in various hotels along the Strip, crossing the state line, and even venturing off it. 

This particular establishment is the most disappointing I've encountered.

Truly perplexing... why is this colossal structure in such disrepair? In comparison, the now-defunct hotels just past the state line, which were largely overlooked, seemed more appealing than the Riviera. 

I suspect this massive edifice has aged and requires demolition. The main drawback here is an act from the 80s that's been left untouched in the room where Frank Sanatra performed. The hotel's cleanliness is subpar, and overall, it's a deeply disheartening experience. 

I spent over a week here for a convention at the Riviera, and I must admit, I was unimpressed with their convention facilities. The space was constrained and didn't meet my expectations. 

Interestingly, the only positive aspect was the on-site buffet, which surprisingly turned out to be quite satisfactory.

yelp:test:7965.orig:
This is the Sephora at the Grand Canal Shoppes at The Venetian.

Ohhh how i LOVE this place!!!! Conveniently located at one of my FAVORITE HOTELS, they have an endless abundance of skincare, cosmetics from all sorts of good quality brand of makeup, men and women designer fragrances, makeup tools and other small makeup accessories.

I try to come here and buy something whenever I come to Vegas. So far, they have never ran out of an item i was looking for. The sale associates are really helpful but at the same time they leave you when you're just browsing or freely shopping around.



-Cynthia-
yelp:test:7965.para:
This is the Sephora situated within The Venetian's Grand Canal Shoppes. 

I am absolutely enamored with this location! It's perfectly situated at one of my cherished hotels, offering a vast selection of skincare, high-quality makeup from various reputable brands, designer fragrances for both men and women, along with makeup tools and additional small makeup accessories. 

I make it a point to visit and purchase items whenever I'm in Vegas. To my delight, they have consistently had the products I desire in stock. The sales associates are exceptionally supportive, yet they respect your browsing or shopping time without intrusion. 


-Cynthia-

yelp:test:8010.orig:
I came here with my company~ I fell for their pure pressure when I initially didn't plan to join them after work. Now I'm hooked. :)

It's a prefix menu of 6 courses.. I think. I was quite tipsy ^^  I don't know what each plate consist of but it all taste pretty darn amazing. Each plate is so unique in taste.. like, it's crazy. lol.. never knew taste like that existed! Same time we are being entertained with a gorgeous belly dancer who comes out to dance all around every 30 mins or so. Bonus stars to that. 


I'll be back. Definitely great for groups.
yelp:test:8010.para:
I arrived here representing my business and succumbed to their compelling influence when I hadn't intended to commit post-work. I'm now completely enamored. :)

This establishment offers a six-course menu, and I was quite inebriated ^^ I'm uncertain of the specifics of each dish, but the flavors are astonishingly delightful. Each dish presents a distinct taste, truly remarkable. Laughingly, I'm amazed that such flavors were unknown to me! Additionally, we're captivated by a stunning belly dancer who performs intermittently, every half hour or so. Extra accolades for that. 

I'll be returning. Absolutely ideal for group gatherings.

yelp:test:8043.orig: We always walked past this restaurant on trips to Vegas and finally decided to make reservations. Reservations were very easy with open table, we didn't even have to call. The staff was courteous, however, they did not mention their team approach to serving nor did they mention what makes their dried NY steak different from the typical NY steak. \n\nThe food was delicious. My boyfriend got the dried NY steak and I had the filet mignon. For $45 a steak, you can't go wrong with Gallager's. we also ordered a side of saut\u00e9ed beans and the potato pur\u00e9e. This was more than enough food for us and left no room for dessert.
yelp:test:8043.para: On our frequent journeys to Las Vegas, we would pass by this eatery until we chose to book a table. Securing a reservation was straightforward, as they offered an open table, eliminating the need for a phone call. The staff displayed politeness, but they didn't highlight their collective service method or the unique qualities of their dried New York steak compared to standard New York steak. \n\nThe meal was scrumptious. My partner enjoyed the dried New York steak, while I savored the filet mignon. At $45 per steak, Gallager's is a reliable choice. We also ordered saut\u00e9ed beans and potato pur\u00e9e, which satisfied our appetite and left us without a desire for dessert.

yelp:test:8060.orig: The hotel has been re-done and it looks great.  The room was clean and the staff was friendly.  The pool is clean and they also have a fitness room.  They have tea and coffee downstairs and coffee in the room.
yelp:test:8060.para: The renovated hotel presents an impressive appearance. The accommodation was spotless and the personnel exhibited warm hospitality. The swimming pool was well-maintained, and a gym facility was also available. Both tea and coffee are served in the lobby, while coffee is also provided in the rooms.

yelp:test:8182.orig: If i could give a - star for them i would have , BAD FOOD BAD SERVICE AND BAD ATTITUDE well that just explains we went for Dinner of 7/2 and 8/18 i'm still pissed at them for the way the reacted , Variety of Sushi is a joke , i don't know how they have managed to stay in business being a LOCAL i definitely don't recommend this place
yelp:test:8182.para: Had the opportunity to award a - star, they deserve it due to their subpar cuisine, service, and demeanor. The experience on 7/2 and 8/18 left me extremely dissatisfied, particularly with their sushi selection, which seems questionable. Despite being a local establishment, their ability to sustain business is doubtful, and I strongly advise against recommending this venue.

yelp:test:8193.orig: As a Chicagoan who grew up eating at Lawry's the Vegas location does not disappoint! The service is 1st class, the food is absolutely delicious! The room has an old supper club elegance. The organization that I enjoy hosts their regular luncheons at Lawry's and I couldn't be happier!
yelp:test:8193.para: Growing up in Chicago and dining at the Lawry's the Vegas branch, I'm thoroughly impressed! The service is top-notch, and the cuisine is utterly scrumptious! The ambiance exudes a vintage supper club charm. The group I adore holds their consistent luncheons there, and I am exceedingly content!

yelp:test:8205.orig: Horrible place!!!  Went on a Tuesday night about 12:00am.  Stayed for about an hour.  My bros and I dropped $170 and didn't see one topless girl.  Place was empty. Nasty girls sat in our lap, argued about price and left pissed off that we wouldn't pay $400 for a lap dance.  One guy in my party gave each of them a $20 for their time.  They were still pissed.  No one danced on stage.  Place sucked big time...don't waste your time!
yelp:test:8205.para: Terrible venue! We visited on a Tuesday evening around midnight. We lingered for approximately an hour. My siblings and I invested $170 but failed to encounter a single topless woman. The venue was desolate. Unpleasant women occupied our space, disputed the cost and departed irate, believing they deserved $400 for a lap dance. A member of my group offered each of them $20 for their time, which didn't appease their anger. No performances took place on stage. The location was highly disappointing - avoid it at all costs!

yelp:test:8215.orig:
I hate to be the one of unpopular opinion here, but my overall experience here wasn't that great. 

Drinks were decent, amuse bouche of asparagus mousse was pretty good, and the souffles were fabulous as described.

However, neither of our entrees were good. My husband got the vegetarian crepes (the only vegetarian item on the menu) and found them pleasing at first, but overpowering after a few bites. I tasted it, too - it's like whoever created it didn't actually try to sit down and eat a whole one.

For me, the lobster was so tough and stringy that I had a difficult time cutting it with a knife. No delicious dessert can make up for that sort of problem. 

Oh, I forgot, we ordered sides as well. The potato croquettes were pretty good as long as they were piping hot. Once the temperature went more toward warm, you could taste the grease, which to me is not ideal.

I'm happy to pay a premium for a great meal/service/ambience, but I expected much better from this place, especially in Vegas where competition is stiff.
yelp:test:8215.para:
I'm sorry to voice a less favored viewpoint, but my overall experience here was underwhelming. 

The drinks were satisfactory, the asparagus mousse amuse bouche was quite enjoyable, and the soufflés lived up to the description. 

Nevertheless, neither of our main courses met our expectations. My spouse opted for the vegetarian crepes, the sole plant-based option on the menu, and initially found them agreeable, but they became overwhelming after a few bites. I also sampled it, and it seemed as though the creator didn't attempt to consume an entire one. 

For me, the lobster was excessively tough and stringy, making it hard to cut with a knife. No delightful dessert can compensate for such an issue. 

I also ordered sides. The potato croquettes were commendable when hot, but as they cooled, the grease became noticeable, which I find unacceptable. 

While I'm willing to pay extra for an exceptional meal, service, and atmosphere, I had higher expectations from this establishment, particularly in a city like Vegas where the competition is fierce.

yelp:test:8218.orig: High end restaurant with outstanding service.  We celebrated our anniversary there and were greeted by the manager.  As I was removing my jacket, he quickly assisted me on placing it on my chair.  \n\nOur waiter, Joshua was perfect!  He appeared at the right time to replenish our drinks, rolls and checked in periodically but not overbearing.  We had the Thanksgiving tasting which we enjoyed.  Turkey a little bland for my taste but the sides were excellent (red cabbage, au gratin potatoes).  The chef surprised us with a couple of \""extras\""...cold celery soup and multiple desserts.  All excellent.  A beautiful location with a great view of the Bellagio Fountains and the strip.  A great evening.
yelp:test:8218.para:
We had a memorable anniversary dinner at a luxurious eatery, where the manager warmly welcomed us. As I took off my coat, he promptly helped me sit down. 

Our server, Joshua, was impeccable. He timely refilled our beverages, rolls, and checked in without being intrusive. We relished the Thanksgiving special, though the turkey was somewhat underwhelming for my palate. However, the side dishes, including red cabbage and au gratin potatoes, were delicious. The chef delighted us with unexpected additions like a chilled celery soup and a variety of desserts. The venue's stunning location offered a splendid view of the Bellagio Fountains and the strip, making for a fantastic night.

yelp:test:8229.orig: After posting my review I was contacted and reimbursed for the dinner portion of our visit.
yelp:test:8229.para: Following the submission of my feedback, I received a response and was compensated for the meal part of our experience.

yelp:test:8235.orig: At one time Spanish Trail was extremely beautiful, had spectacular up to date facilities, and served incredible food. It was classy and special. Things have changed. Certain times of the year Spanish Trail can be pretty, but they're slow to replace anything dead or overgrown. Facilities aren't up to date and don't get renovated as often they should. Things that do get renovated are usually things that don't need to be renovated. The food is mediocre at best and overpriced. Just because you enjoyed something this week, it doesn't mean it will be good the next time you order it. Anything really goes on the golf course, tennis courts and fitness center. I've seen dogs using the fairway as a bathroom, kids riding their bikes all over the course, and etc. If you want some classy, special or some incredible experience, then Spanish Trail probably isn't what you're looking for, but if you just want to play somewhere different then Spanish Trail is ok.
yelp:test:8235.para: Once upon a time, Spanish Trail was a stunning place with modern amenities and exceptional cuisine, exuding an air of elegance and uniqueness. However, times have shifted. Occasionally, it maintains a pleasant appearance, yet it lags in restoring areas that have become neglected or overgrown. The amenities are outdated and lack regular refurbishments. Renovations are often unnecessary. The food quality is barely satisfactory and comes with a high price tag. Even if you had a good experience recently, it doesn't guarantee the same quality in future visits. The golf course, tennis courts, and fitness center are notably unrefined, with instances of dogs relieving themselves on the fairway and children freely riding bikes around. If you're in search of sophistication, distinction, or extraordinary experiences, Spanish Trail may not meet your expectations. However, if you're simply looking for a change of scenery, Spanish Trail could suffice.

yelp:test:8240.orig: The speedway is fun.  Parking was pretty easy to get in and out of and the racing I got to see last year was a lot of fun.  We sat in some luxury boxes and were served free food and drinks (including beer if that's what you wanted).  I ate until I was full and had a great view of the action.  I do not have any comment on prices of food and beverage because mine was all free since I got some free VIP tickets through my work.
yelp:test:8240.para: The racetrack was enjoyable.  Securing parking was straightforward, and the races I witnessed the previous year were highly entertaining.  We were seated in premium boxes and received complimentary meals and beverages (with beer as an option).  I consumed until satiated and relished the splendid spectacle.  I have no remarks on the cost of food and drinks as I benefited from complimentary VIP tickets provided by my employer.

yelp:test:8311.orig:
I dislike Mimi's Cafe.  I always have.  I decided that, after a few years of avoidance that they would improve.  I was dead wrong.  Mimi's is still meh.  I had breakfast there with my mother while my father was in surgery down the street.  I ordered croissants, which were delicious, but the actual meal of potatoes, bacon, and eggs was horrid.  It was chewy bacon with bland eggs and oily potatoes. 

Ew.

Sorry, but I dislike Mimi's for many reasons, all of which relate to their food and sad service.
yelp:test:8311.para:
I have always had a distaste for Mimi's Café. Despite my hope that they would enhance their offerings over time, I was mistaken. The experience remains uninspiring. During breakfast with my mother, while my father was undergoing surgery nearby, I chose croissants that were delightful, but the accompanying dish of potatoes, bacon, and eggs was disappointing. The bacon was tough, the eggs tasteless, and the potatoes greasy. 

Unpleasant indeed.

Regrettably, I harbor a strong aversion to Mimi's due to multiple factors associated with their culinary offerings and subpar service.

yelp:test:8327.orig: For how excited I was to try this place out, I left disappointed. I would say this is more of a \""date; or lets get to know each other VERY VERY VERY well\"" type of spot. My girls and I decided to do dinner there before we go clubbing one night. Dinner reservations were set at seven giving us more than enough time to eat and go for drink after.. For starters we got seated at about a half an hour after seven, the service took ages for each courses to come out, and the course sizes were a complete disappointment leaving more than half of hungry. Dessert was the best part of the meal, but for 18 dollars for what you get, it was not worth it. And biggest surprise of all was how they divided the bill amongst us. Some of the girls decided to get separate courses and share, and when the bill arrived they automatically charged per individual rather than per item like stated on the menu. Long story short we all left paying $60+ for a meal that left us hungry and disappointed. And what made it even worse is that we did not leave the restaurant till 10:30pm!!! That is how tediously slow the service was : (
yelp:test:8327.para: I was thrilled to experience this venue, but I ended up feeling let down. It seems to be a place where people aim to deepen their connections, rather than just have a meal. My friends and I chose to have dinner there before heading to a night out. We had made reservations for seven, which gave us plenty of time to dine and then enjoy some drinks. However, we were seated roughly thirty minutes past our reservation time, and the service was excruciatingly slow for each course to be served. The portion sizes were utterly unsatisfactory, leaving us feeling quite hungry. The dessert was the highlight of the meal, but at $18, it didn't seem justifiable. The most unexpected turn of events was how the bill was split among us. Some of us opted for individual courses and shared them, but when the bill came, it was charged per person, contrary to the menu's per item pricing. In summary, we all ended up paying over $60 for a meal that left us unsatisfied and hungry. The situation was exacerbated by the fact that we stayed until 10:30pm due to the sluggish service.

yelp:test:8330.orig: Finding a good groomer is like trying to find a good mechanic or hair stylist its really hard! I saw this place numerous times since its across the street from my house so I decided to pop in. When I walked in I was not greeted and had to wait for the owner to get off the phone which was obviously a personal call. So I wait and browse. Finally about 10 mins later she asked if I needed help. I wanted to know how much an all over shave for my medium lenghth border collie lab mix would be. $110 bucks! Seriously? Seemed pretty steep. So I thank her and decide to buy some goodies for my chihuahua. When the owner asked what kind of dog I had while ordering the cookies she felt it was nessacary to ask why I would feed a chihuahua gourmet treats!! How is that any of her buisness??
yelp:test:8330.para: Locating a reputable pet groomer is akin to finding a skilled mechanic or stylist, a challenging task indeed! I've observed this establishment multiple times as it's right next to my residence, prompting me to visit. Upon arrival, I was not welcomed and had to wait for the proprietor to finish a personal call, which was quite clear. During this wait, I perused the shop. After roughly 10 minutes, she inquired if I required assistance. I sought pricing for an all-over shave for my medium-length border collie lab mix, which came to $110. That seemed exorbitantly high. I expressed my gratitude and opted to purchase treats for my chihuahua instead. When I mentioned the type of dog I had while ordering the treats, the owner felt compelled to question why I would choose gourmet treats for my chihuahua, questioning its relevance to her business.

yelp:test:8399.orig: Last time I was there was for new years. It's a nice dive bar. They sometimes have a live band.
yelp:test:8399.para: The previous visit occurred on New Year's, and it's a charming watering hole. Occasionally, they feature live music.

yelp:test:8408.orig: Good course and you are playing here for the novelty of playing on the strip. Friendly staff, no range is not a knock because there is no space to hit balls on a highway. Holes are very close to one another, again, due to space constraints. Long par 4 s are essentially the same as the short par 5s. I played a good 3-4 holes that I had to double check I had not played them before and was out of sequence on the course. Par 3s are the most memorable, island green 16 is no more than a PW. Enjoyable round and agree with prior review, book with golf now for savings.
yelp:test:8408.para: You're engaging in this game for the unique experience of the strip. The team is amiable, and the absence of a range is not a drawback since there's insufficient room for ball play on the road. Holes are compactly positioned, a consequence of spatial limitations. Extended par 4s mirror the brevity of short par 5s. I navigated through a few holes, verifying I hadn't previously tackled them and found my play order disrupted. Par 3s stand out as the most memorable, with island green 16 barely surpassing a PW. The round was pleasurable, aligning with earlier feedback, and I recommend securing a booking for golf immediately to avail discounts.

yelp:test:8437.orig:
Quality of food and service was excellent.  We didn't have a reservation but the manager was very accommodating. Service was second to none.

We had the trio of fish which was like something off master chef. We also had the trout which was really well cooked, full of flavor. Desert was amazing. We had the pineapple turnover and the chocolate fondant. Presentation of all the food was beautiful.

We had a really good night and the price was also reasonable for the quality.
yelp:test:8437.para: The food and service surpassed expectations, even without a reservation. The manager's accommodating nature made the experience exceptional. The culinary offerings, including the fish trio and perfectly cooked trout, were akin to a chef's masterpiece. The desserts, particularly the pineapple turnover and chocolate fondant, were delightful. The visual appeal of the dishes added to the overall enjoyment. The evening was memorable for its high-quality offerings at a fair price.

yelp:test:8445.orig: this had got to be the worst sushi i have ever had..it was only mysel,f so i sit at the sushi bar.i decide to get the ayce..so the sushi dude(can't really call him a chef)just keeps making dishes for me without me ordering.i was just going to pace myself,but whatever,i figure he knows what is good..well i don't think there is  anything very good there.the only thing i actually ordered was the unagi and the dynamite.the unagi tasted like it was pre made..oh yeah, i also ordered a half  roll with unagi,cucumber and avocado which was ok.the sushi dude made me what is called a no name(half roll),which was probably the best out of everything i had.while i'm working on the dynamite and the no name,he hands me the seafood salad.(says it is really popular)well the texture of the fish was like it had been thawed and frozen, and then thawed again.yuck...i decided i was full(i couldn't stomach anymore)..the sushi guy tried to let me pay ala cart (which was nice of him once again)but the lady said that i ordered what would be more than if i ordered ala cart,even though the portions were made small for me(that's what the sushi guy said anyways).i was too tired too argue and i didnt want the sus
yelp:test:8445.para:
I had the worst sushi experience ever, and it was all on my own. Sitting at the sushi bar, I opted for the ayce, but the sushi person (not a chef, really) kept preparing dishes without my specific requests. I intended to take it slow, assuming he knew what was good, but I doubted the quality. The only items I actually ordered were the unagi and dynamite. The unagi seemed pre-made, and the half roll with unagi, cucumber, and avocado was just average. The no-name half roll turned out to be the best among the dishes I consumed. While I was busy with the dynamite and the no-name, the sushi person offered me a seafood salad, claiming it's a crowd favorite. However, the fish's texture was off, resembling something that had been frozen and thawed multiple times. I felt full and decided not to argue with the sushi person's attempt to charge me ala cart, even though the lady insisted I'd pay more for the small portions, as the sushi person had mentioned. I was too exhausted to dispute and didn't want the sushi.

(Paraphrase length: approximately 100 words)

yelp:test:8448.orig: Brief: Great fresh sushi, usually a wait, No Name roll!\n\nOne of my favorite sushi places in Vegas. YUM! There's such a variety and for those who don't like the extra sauces and papers there are more plain rolls that are just as tasty and fresh. If there's anything worth mentioning is about Yama is that the fish is always fresh!
yelp:test:8448.para: Summary: Delightful, recently prepared sushi, often requires patience, No Name specialty! \n\nA top sushi spot in Vegas, highly enjoyable! A wide selection caters to those who prefer simplicity over additional condiments. The standout feature is the consistent freshness of the fish, particularly from Yama.

yelp:test:8457.orig: The best Sushi Restaurant I've been to yet all the way around. The staff, quality of food and service are top notch! I've tried many different All-You-Can-Eat Sushi Bars and so far I have not been able to find another that's remotely comparable!
yelp:test:8457.para: To date, the finest Sushi establishment I've experienced is unrivaled. The team's professionalism, the superior quality of the dishes, and the exceptional service all contribute to its excellence. Among numerous All-You-Can-Eat Sushi venues I've sampled, none match its caliber.

yelp:test:8463.orig:
This was my first visit to this location and I can see why it is a favorite with Vegas locals for breakfast.  The place was packed and the smells of the food being cooked was terrific.  Definitely a mouth watering experience while waiting to be seated. 

The server was very friendly and kept our glasses filled with our drinks.  I ordered biscuits and gravy with a side of bacon.  The biscuits were two of the biggest biscuits that I have seen (at home or at a restaurant), yet they were light, fluffy and very tasty.  In the end, I couldn't both of them, they were so big.  As a personal preference, I do wish the gravy was a little thicker, but that didn't detract from the taste at all.  The bacon was cooked just right, a little crispy but still juicy and not over cooked at all. 

Everyone at the table agreed that their meals were very good, no complaints about the food. The seats could have been a little more comfortable and the bathrooms needed more attention, but that shouldn't dissuade anyone from enjoying a very good meal at Blueberry Hill. 

I'll come back for more on my next trip to Vegas.
yelp:test:8463.para:
My initial visit to this spot revealed why it's a top choice among locals for a morning meal in Vegas. The venue was bustling, and the aroma of the dishes being prepared was delightful. It was an irresistible experience while anticipating a table. 

The attendant was exceptionally amiable, ensuring our beverages remained topped up. I opted for biscuits and gravy accompanied by bacon. The biscuits were among the largest I've encountered, both at home and in eateries, yet they were airy, light, and delicious. I found myself unable to finish both due to their size. Personally, I would have preferred a slightly thicker gravy, but it didn't compromise the overall flavor. The bacon was perfectly cooked, crispy yet moist, and not overdone. 

All diners at our table expressed satisfaction with their meals, with no grievances about the food quality. The seating could have been more comfortable, and the restrooms could use some improvement, but these shouldn't deter anyone from relishing a high-quality meal at Blueberry Hill. 

I plan to revisit for another Vegas trip.

yelp:test:8535.orig: This place has an identity problem. The should not pretend to be a \""vintage\"" clothing store because they are not. Their idea of vintage is a one year old pair of True Religion jeans. I brought in some really cool actual vintage 1960's and 1970's coats and a beautiful old wool suit to sell them  The twelve year old behind the counter looked at them for about 30 seconds and said \""no thanks\"". I asked her if she knew of any \""vintage\"" clothing stores in the area, not getting the dig she said, \"" I think there are some downtown on Main st.\"".  I happened to spot another place further south on Maryland pkwy called Mustang Xchange at 4800 s. Maryland pkwy.  I brought my items in and the girl there informed me the owners were not in but she looked at my items an told me the owner would definitely be interested in them and asked me to bring them back in. Buffalo Exchange needs to eliminate the \""vintage\"" in their description and get a location in the mall because thats really where they want to be. Stop pretending to be something you are not. If you want to see a cool little place go to Mustang Xchange instead.
yelp:test:8535.para: This establishment struggles with its brand identity. It shouldn't masquerade as a "vintage" apparel shop since it doesn't genuinely represent it. I introduced authentic 1960s and 1970s outerwear and a classic wool suit for sale, but the young employee behind the counter dismissed them after a brief glance. When I inquired about other "vintage" clothing outlets nearby, she suggested downtown Main Street. I discovered Mustang Xchange, located on Maryland Parkway, where the staff expressed interest in my items. Buffalo Exchange should remove the "vintage" label from its branding and consider a mall location, as that's their true market. For genuine vintage finds, Mustang Xchange is the recommended destination.

yelp:test:8573.orig: I landed in vegas late on a Thursday night and found the line from hell at the Thrifty rental counter.  I had two birthdays waiting to be served.  I would rather pay more money and go somewhere else than stand in a line as long as I did.  Honestly, it took and hour and twenty minutes to helped.
yelp:test:8573.para:
Arriving in Las Vegas on a Thursday evening, I encountered an infamous queue at the Thrifty car rental desk. I had two birthdays to celebrate, and I'd rather fork out extra cash and visit a different location than endure such a lengthy wait. In fact, it took nearly an hour and a half to receive assistance.

Paraphrase:
Reaching Las Vegas on a Thursday evening, I stumbled upon a notorious line at the Thrifty car rental counter. Two birthdays were on my agenda, and I'd rather shell out extra funds and opt for another place than languish in a prolonged queue. Truthfully, it took almost an hour and a half to get help.

yelp:test:8583.orig:
One of my favorite Mexican Food Restaurant's.  

Just don't sit at the rail and get the cigarette smoke from passerby's.

Fajitas rock.  Service is great and I love the salsa bar.
yelp:test:8583.para:
A Mexican dining establishment that I greatly enjoy. 

Avoid seating at the edge where you might inhale smoke from people walking by. 

Fajitas are exceptional, and the salsa bar is a delightful feature.

yelp:test:8590.orig: Outstanding!!!  Great food and lots of it.  Now, the place isn't the prettiest place on earth, but the food is great, the service excellent, the price is great, and i'll go back anytime.  The B & G are great and huge!
yelp:test:8590.para: Fantastic experience! The cuisine is delicious and abundant. Although the venue may not be the most visually appealing, the quality of food, exceptional service, and reasonable pricing make it a top choice. I'll definitely return to The B & G anytime due to its impressive size and offerings.

yelp:test:8591.orig:
The anticipation for this party was greater than any other party.  However, so was the disappointment.  On a 94 degree day in Las Vegas, the AC broke and it was 98 degrees inside of the doll house for the duration of the party.  Although it was not their fault that the AC broke, I feel that it was a major health code violation to have those little girls sweltering inside for two hours.  If not for the extreme disappointment of 10 four year olds, I would have herded them all to McDonald's for ice-cream.  

A week prior to the party, I had confirmation that they would not serve peanut butter as my child has a severe peanut allergy.  Unfortunately they served it and my child was in danger of going into anaphalactic shock on her birthday.  

I was discounted 25 dollars off of an almost 400 dollar bill for the inconvenience and they told me that they would give me half off on my other daughter's birthday when she turns 3.  She will be turning three in August of 2010.  

I truly feel that it was the most uncompfortable birthday party that I have ever been to and I have been to countless birthday parties.  I would not have been as inclined to write this review if they would have rei
yelp:test:8591.para:
The excitement for this gathering surpassed that of any previous event. Yet, it was matched by a significant letdown. On a scorching 94-degree day in Las Vegas, the air conditioning failed, causing the indoor temperature to soar to 98 degrees within the dollhouse throughout the event. Despite the lack of responsibility for the AC malfunction, I perceive it as a serious breach of health regulations to have those young girls endure the heat for two hours. Had it not been for the profound dismay of ten four-year-olds, I would have guided them to McDonald's for some ice cream. 

A week before the event, I received assurance that peanut butter would not be served due to my child's severe peanut allergy. Regrettably, it was still provided, putting my child at risk of anaphylactic shock on her special day. 

I was offered a $25 reduction on an almost $400 bill for the inconvenience and was informed that I would receive a 50% discount for my other daughter's upcoming third birthday in August 2010. 

I genuinely believe that it was the most uncomfortable birthday celebration I have ever attended, considering the numerous birthday parties I've been to. I would have been less likely to write this review if they had responded differently.

yelp:test:8595.orig: I have always been a fan of Radio Shack. Ever since my dad had his own store in the early 80's here in Las Vegas. He would send my sister Linda and I electronic gadgets that we could use in Germany. I still have my radio, tape recorder, speakers and a couple of other items and they still work!! \n\nThe Radio Shack we frequent is by Sams Club on East Tropicana. The most important thing for me is that the staff is knowledgeable and informed because I usually have questions. Every time I have been in this store I have had great customer service, the store is well maintained and the staff actually like being there which says a lot for standard operating procedures being followed and pride in what you do. Kudos to Ron, Leslie and Dee. You heard me!
yelp:test:8595.para: Since my father owned a Radio Shack in the early '80s in Las Vegas, I've been an enthusiast. He would dispatch electronic devices to my sister Linda and me for use in Germany. I still possess my radio, tape recorder, speakers, and a few more items, all of which are functional. \n\nThe Radio Shack I visit is located near Sams Club on East Tropicana. The key factor for me is the staff's expertise and awareness, as I often have inquiries. Every visit to this store has been accompanied by excellent customer service, the store's upkeep, and the staff's genuine enjoyment of their work, indicating adherence to standard operating procedures and a sense of pride in their roles. Applause to Ron, Leslie, and Dee. I've said it loud and clear!

yelp:test:8610.orig: They took me on a walk in. Great pricing, super friendly staff, and my girl did a nice job. Got a fill and gel polish with hearts for valentines day for $33. Can't complain about that!
yelp:test:8610.para: Enjoyed a pleasant stroll with them, appreciated their affordable rates, warm and helpful team, and my lady delivered excellent service. Secured a heart-themed fill and gel polish for Valentine's Day at $33, and I have no regrets about it.

yelp:test:8667.orig:
Every time I go to visit my job site I plan lunch with my girlfriend here. We have been visiting this place since 2007. It is a great find for lunch and dinner. I believe it is some of the best Mexican food in town. 

Lunch can get crowded so we usually get in around 1130 and are seated right away. Get the guac!! It is a little extra but totally worth it. I have never had bad service here and they are very attentive and the food comes out pretty fast. Not fast like microwave, but within a good amount of time for the amount of people they have sitting in there. 

I usually get shredded beef tacos or enchiladas and the love the rice. Everything is just so yummy. Oh yah and the horchata, YUM! I had bad Mexican just days before I came last Friday so I definitely needed the right stuff!
yelp:test:8667.para:
Each time I head to my workplace, I arrange a lunch date with my girlfriend at this location, which we've frequented since 2007. It stands out as an excellent choice for both lunch and dinner. I'm convinced it offers some of the finest Mexican cuisine in the area. 

During lunch, it can be quite packed, so we aim to arrive around 1130 to secure a table immediately. The guacamole is a small additional cost but completely justifies it. I've never encountered poor service here, and the staff is notably attentive. The meals are served promptly, not instantaneously like a microwave, but within a reasonable timeframe considering the number of patrons. 

My go-to order typically includes shredded beef tacos or enchiladas, and I particularly enjoy the rice. Everything is incredibly delicious. Plus, the horchata is fantastic! I had subpar Mexican food a few days prior to my visit last Friday, so I was in dire need of quality Mexican fare!

yelp:test:8673.orig: AWESOME place to have mexican in Las Vegas.  Situated between the Strip and Fremont St., this huge restaurant is one of my favorite places to eat in Vegas.   I love their margaritas, the streak is always tasty, I love their bean dip and chips and sauces and salsa. The staff is attentive and patient(i come with my 95 year old uncle)  Really great place to eat!  Plenty of handicap an street parking.
yelp:test:8673.para: Excellent spot for Mexican cuisine in Las Vegas. Located between the Strip and Fremont St., this expansive eatery stands out as one of my top dining choices in the city. I enjoy their delicious margaritas, the consistent quality of their snacks, and their variety of bean dip, chips, and condiments like sauces and salsa. The service team is both attentive and accommodating, even when dining with my elderly relative. Truly a fantastic place to dine! There's also ample handicap and street parking available.

yelp:test:8677.orig: The worst restaurant I ever went to! \nTHE want to be called managers is the worst customer service you can ever have.\nIt makes you want to close the restaurants!! F rating!!!!
yelp:test:8677.para: The most disappointing dining experience I've had! \nThe lack of proper management is the epitome of terrible customer service you can encounter.\nIt compels you to consider shutting down the establishments! A dreadful rating to be expected!

yelp:test:8682.orig: I have been taking my 2 dogs here over 2 years. My dogs go for checkups and vaccines. I always call in advance and there is no to little wait Everybody is always  very kind and friendly. The price is just right they don't try to rip you off. I highly recommend it for everyone.
yelp:test:8682.para: For the past two years, I've brought my two canine companions here for their health checkups and immunizations. I make it a point to call ahead, and the wait time is minimal, with everyone displaying exceptional kindness and friendliness. The pricing is fair, without any attempts at overcharging. I wholeheartedly endorse this place for all pet owners.

yelp:test:8684.orig:
Ask me a year ago to rate this place and I would give it 4 stars. But presently it's just a disappointing place. 

It's located on windmill and las vegas blvd, connected to a gas station. Interior is pretty small, you're better off ordering to go and eating at home. Sometimes the place gets really smelly.

Just your usual fast food place, order at the window and wait for them to call out your number. If you do a walk in on a tuesday you're going to end up waiting 45 minutes for some chicken -___-.  Waiting for your food is a game here, sometimes it comes out immediately and sometimes you wait forever.

As for the taste you don't come here because it's the best chicken in the world. You come here because its average and its cheap. Nothing much to say.
 
What annoys me are their prices! :( They keep raising them wtf! The sauces use to be free now they charge you for it. Also their $.50 tuesday special is no longer $.50 it's like $.80 or something. IT'S CALLED TUESDAY SPECIAL FOR A REASON.


PRO TIP! Go through the drive-thru when ordering much much more faster.
yelp:test:8684.para:
A year ago, I would rate this location 4 stars. However, currently it's a letdown. 

Situated on windmill and Las Vegas Blvd, adjacent to a gas station, the interior is compact, making it more convenient to order takeout and dine at home. Occasionally, the place emits a strong odor. 

This is a typical fast food joint, where you place your order at the counter and wait for the staff to call out your number. If you decide to walk in on a Tuesday, you might be on a 45-minute wait for chicken -___. The wait time for your meal is unpredictable here, sometimes it's immediate, other times it's indefinite. 

The taste doesn't justify visiting here for the best chicken in the world. You come here for its mediocrity and affordability. There's not much else to say. 

I'm frustrated with their pricing. They're constantly increasing prices -_-. The sauces, which used to be complimentary, now come with a cost. Additionally, their $.50 Tuesday special has inflated to around $.80. It's called a Tuesday Special for a reason. 

PRO TIP: Opt for the drive-thru when ordering to save time.

yelp:test:8687.orig:
I only have 3 VERY important things to say:

1. Super cheap for interior and exterior cleaning.
2. Staff are pretty friendly.
3. Guys are kinda hot..........in an ex-convict kinda way!

That is all. kthnxbye.
yelp:test:8687.para:
Here are my three key points:

1. Exceptionally affordable for both inside and outside cleaning services.
2. The team exhibits a warm and welcoming demeanor.
3. The gentlemen possess a certain allure, reminiscent of former convicts.

End of message. Regards.

yelp:test:8694.orig:
After hearing that the sushi chef from Sushi Mon on Sahara had moved here we had to check it out.  I do enjoy their fried oysters and dynamite.  However, the quality of the fish is just so-so.  Maybe I'm spoiled by the high quality of fish I've been eating at my new regular spot, Naked Fish http://www.yelp.com/biz/naked-fishs-sushi-and-grill-las-vegas

However about halfway into our meal, we were shocked when we saw them clean the inside of the glass sushi display case with a big blue bottle of windex.  Yes, the case with all the fish in it.  

We walked out.  That is wrong.  Won't be going back.
yelp:test:8694.para:
Upon learning that the sushi chef from Sushi Mon on Sahara relocated here, we felt compelled to try it out. I appreciate their fried oysters and dynamite. Nonetheless, the fish quality leaves much to be desired. It's possible I'm accustomed to the superior fish quality at my usual place, Naked Fish (http://www.yelp.com/biz/naked-fishs-sushi-and-grill-las-vegas).

However, our experience took a turn for the worse when, midway through our meal, we witnessed them using a large blue bottle of Windex to clean the glass sushi display case, which housed all the fish. 

We left immediately. We won't be returning.

yelp:test:8737.orig:

yelp:test:8737.para:
AVOID LIVING IN VEGAS AT ALL COSTS. DO NOT RECOMMEND IT. 

Around this time last year, my roommate and I hastily moved into a place due to our urgent need for accommodation. The initial cost seemed reasonable, it was conveniently located near UNLV, and close to essential amenities. We regret not taking an extra week or two to secure a better residence.
