yelp:test:8756.orig: Had the shredded beef bowl. AWESOME! Perfect rice, well seasoned pintos, tender and lean beef all with a citrus-cilantro-mint sauce to tie it together. Chicken soup would cure the worst of colds!!!
yelp:test:8756.para: Savored a bowl of shredded beef, absolutely fantastic! The rice was impeccable, the pintos were expertly seasoned, and the beef was both tender and lean, all complemented by a delightful citrus-cilantro-mint sauce. Chicken soup would surely alleviate the most severe cold symptoms!

yelp:test:8780.orig: Meh is about right. This store is basically the same as the Smith's just up the street, only with higher prices and not as much selection. I come from California where everything is a ripoff ... and the prices here are just as bad if not worse. I don't remember it always being that way, but that's the way it is now. \n\nOh well. It's not like there aren't a ton of other grocery stores within a 90-second drive.
yelp:test:8780.para: The store offers a mediocre experience, akin to Smith's across the road, albeit with elevated costs and a narrower range of products. Coming from California, where I perceive everything as overpriced, I find the prices here equally, if not more, exorbitant. It seems this has always been the case, but it's the current reality. \n\nDespite this, there are numerous other nearby grocery options that I can reach within a swift 90 seconds.

yelp:test:8858.orig: I tried this place out because it's close to where I live. Gel manicures I've gotten at other salons always last for 2 1/2 to 3 weeks. My first gel manicure I got here started peeling after 10 days, so I returned to get a polish change and gave them another shot. AGAIN, my nails started peeling this time only after 8 days!! The staff isn't very friendly either. Go elsewhere!
yelp:test:8858.para: I decided to check out this spot as it's near my residence. I've experienced gel manicures at different salons that typically endure for about 2 1/2 to 3 weeks. However, my initial gel manicure here began to peel after just 10 days, prompting me to return for a polish adjustment. Once more, my nails began to peel after a mere 8 days! The staff's demeanor is also lacking in friendliness. I recommend going to a different place.

yelp:test:8931.orig: Amazing. Delicious. I eat way too much of it! They have Shiner Bock on tap, which is another plus. Yes, it's a wait, so go with a group of friends and order some pitchers while you wait. Or get take-out or delivery if you don't have time to be social. But don't miss the goodness.
yelp:test:8931.para: Incredible and scrumptious! I indulge in excessive amounts. The availability of Shiner Bock on tap is an added advantage. While there's a wait, it's worthwhile to gather friends and order pitchers to pass the time. Alternatively, opt for take-out or delivery if you're pressed for time and prefer solitude. However, don't overlook the delightful experience.

yelp:test:8935.orig:

yelp:test:8938.orig:
I will say that I do go here, though very sporadically. I gave it two stars, but it's because of my tastes, which I will explain in detail.

When I do go, it's always early in the evening. I don't like going to this bar when it's crowded, as it's excessively crowded. It's worth a trip if you're into the scene or are visiting Phoenix and want to experience the scene. This is definitely one of the Valley's landmark bars. If you're going alone and don't mind spending the evening by yourself (i.e. people-watching) it really isn't that bad. If you want to mingle with people, this bar isn't a great atmosphere for that. People generally go in cliques and you'll notice that the bar is full of clique-clusters. It definitely is not one of the friendlier bars in the Valley. It also seems to have an ""instant snob"" effect on people. 

Now, for pluses... Amsterdam does have a beautiful outdoor area, which is suitable for smokers. You can not only take your drinks out there, but there is an outdoor bar at which you can get drinks. It's a nice area to have drinks in the spring, fall and early/late summer. Most of the summer it can still top 100 degrees even late at night and winter nights
yelp:test:8938.para:
I frequent this place occasionally, but not regularly. I rated it two stars, reflecting my personal preferences, which I will elaborate on further.

When I visit, it's usually during the early hours of the night. I prefer not to go when it's packed, as it becomes overwhelmingly crowded. It's worth visiting if you're interested in the local scene or are in Phoenix and wish to immerse yourself in the atmosphere. This establishment is undoubtedly a key landmark in the Valley. If you're going solo and don't mind spending time on your own (e.g., observing others), it's not particularly unpleasant. However, if you're looking to socialize, this bar doesn't provide a conducive environment. You'll observe that people tend to stick together in groups, and the bar is often filled with these groupings. It's not known for its welcoming nature. Additionally, it seems to have a "snobbish" effect on individuals. 

On the positive side, Amsterdam boasts a stunning outdoor space, ideal for those who smoke. Here, you can enjoy your drinks outdoors, and there's even an outdoor bar where you can order drinks. It's a delightful spot to have a drink during the spring, fall, and early to late summer. Despite most of the summer nights still reaching temperatures above 100 degrees even

yelp:test:8960.orig: The best!  I haven't been there in years and the last time we went it was a 3.5 hour wait but so worth it!  Great for a date if you want to get to know someone waiting in line so long.  \nMy advice is to arrive at 330pm so that way you can be one of the first in line and eat with the first seating at 5pm.
yelp:test:8960.para:
Excellent choice! I haven't visited this place in quite some time, and our previous visit involved a 3.5-hour wait, but it was completely worth it. Ideal for a date to bond with someone during the lengthy queue. 

My suggestion is to arrive at 3:30pm, ensuring you're among the early birds in line, allowing you to enjoy the first seating at 5pm.

yelp:test:8967.orig: This place is completely and overwhelmingly overhyped. The pizza was tasteless and probably one of my least favorite I've ever had. Grazie and Grimaldi's are by far greater and underrated. Pizza Bianco had dust that should warrant the attention of the health department. If I could I would give this place 4 thumbs down. Overrated!!!!
yelp:test:8967.para: This location is excessively and utterly hyped up. The pizza tasted bland and undoubtedly ranks among my least preferred experiences. Comparatively, Grazie and Grimaldi's are significantly superior and underappreciated. Pizza Bianco's presence of dust merits serious health department scrutiny. I would unhesitatingly rate this establishment with a 4-star disapproval. Absolutely overrated!

yelp:test:8974.orig:
Had heard about Durants for years and finally went last night.  This review is not kind so if you are a fan, you should go to other reviews.

Positives:  
Atmosphere
Old school decor (straight out of the 60's)
Courteous wait staff

Negatives:
Horribly over priced-  I've had a better Ribeye at Houston's and it didn't cost $48.

Steak quality was not what I expected.  Ribeye is a well marbled steak, but these had a lot of gristle, were not nearly the quality I'd expect for the 5 star price.

5 Guys and Red Robin make much better fries....seriously, I have shoe laces that are firmer.

One person in my party complained about the lack of steak quality and had a plateful of gristle and fat on his plate.

My verdict.... I was anticipating a steak dinner that was top notch.  It was far from that.  Perhaps they just had a poor quality slab to cut the steaks from, but at $50 a steak, someone in the kitchen should gave caught it.  Plenty of other great places in Phoenix to eat a marvelous steak....and I prefer those after this dinner.
yelp:test:8974.para:
For years, I've been aware of Durants and decided to visit last night. This critique is harsh, so if you're a supporter, consider exploring other reviews.

Positive aspects:
- The ambiance
- Vintage decor reminiscent of the 60s
- Friendly service staff

Negative points:
- Exorbitantly expensive - I've enjoyed a superior Ribeye at Houston's for less than $48.
- The steak didn't meet my expectations. Ribeye should be well-marbled, but these were laden with gristle and fell short of the expected quality for a 5-star price.
- I found the fries at 5 Guys and Red Robin to be superior.
- One person in my group was dissatisfied with the steak quality, having a plate full of gristle and fat.

In conclusion, I expected a top-tier steak dinner, but it was disappointingly subpar. It's possible the kitchen used a low-quality cut, but at $50 per steak, it's hard to believe they missed it. There are numerous excellent steak places in Phoenix, and I'd rather dine there after this experience.

yelp:test:8975.orig:
As a part of the Steak Out, our most recent visit was to this Valley favorite. 

For sure: KILLER shrimp cocktail. Although there were only 4 pieces, they give new meaning to the phrase Jumbo Shrimp and, despite their size, they were not tough or iodine-y. The flavor was fresh and the cocktail sauce could clear the very worst sinuses!

The roasted garlic mashed potatoes must use REAL roasted garlic -- like, roasted in house, not just minced garlic tossed in! The sweet, earthy flavor was subtle which was perfect, because it didn't destroy your palate for the rest of the plate.

I was surprised by the wine list: not a huge. very accessible, relatively speaking.

But, we're on a quest for the best steak. This one? It gets very high marks!  Excellent seasoning on the meat. Preparation in terms of temperature was adequate (although, it was more on the medium rare side; I would argue that is the side to err on!).
yelp:test:8975.para:
During our latest Steak Out event, we enjoyed a beloved spot in the Valley. 

Undoubtedly, the shrimp cocktail was outstanding, even though it was served in just four pieces. It redefined the concept of Jumbo Shrimp, maintaining a tender texture and a fresh taste, with a cocktail sauce potent enough to alleviate even the most severe congestion. 

The mashed potatoes, infused with genuinely roasted garlic, were subtly sweet and earthy, enhancing the dish without overpowering your taste buds. 

The wine selection was modest but easily approachable. 

However, our primary goal is to find the ultimate steak, and this one deserves top ratings. The meat was expertly seasoned and cooked to a medium rare temperature, which I believe is the ideal choice.

yelp:test:8980.orig: Just went to the Friday night game vs Cubs.  We tried a new section-Friday's Front Row inside the restaurant in the outfield.  I was impressed.  We sat in the front row pretty much over the left outfield and you could see in the bullpen also which was kind of cool.  There is a waitress for the section and she did a great job.  Tickets were $20 per which I thought was nice.  You can also get served alcohol throughout the whole game if you are the kind of person that gets anxiety about the whole last call thing in the 7th.
yelp:test:8980.para: Attended the Friday evening match against the Cubs, opting for the Friday's Front Row dining area located in the outfield. I found it quite impressive. Our seats were positioned near the left outfield, offering a clear view of the bullpen as well, which was intriguing. A dedicated waitress served the section efficiently. The tickets were priced at $20 each, which I considered reasonable. Additionally, for those who experience anxiety about the final call in the 7th inning, they can enjoy drinks throughout the game.

yelp:test:9029.orig:
I went to Lux for brunch with some friends and the food was pretty good. First off, the line was REALLY long, which is both good and bad. Bad, for obvious reasons, but good because it tells you that they are popular, which would usually hint at the quality of the food you will eventually consume. 

Second, they are kind enough to get drink orders while you wait in line so that you can start having your coffee, tea, juice, or whatnot, while you wait for your food. Third, the decor of Lux was cool enough to distract me while my friends and I waited for our breakfast to be prepared. Lots of retro-looking lamps on the tables combined with art from local artists made for a warm and welcoming atmosphere. 

When our food did arrive, we were all satisfied! I got the Aunt Gladys's homemade salsa over four strips of tender belly bacon, three scrambled eggs, white cheddar, and hash, which was pretty delicious. My two friends also really enjoyed their meals. I'm giving them 4 stars because I did think that their food was a bit over-priced for what you got, both in portion size and quality. I mean, it was $5 for a glass of orange juice... Other than that, I was very satisfied with the exper
yelp:test:9029.para:
I visited Lux for a morning meal gathering with companions, and the cuisine was quite enjoyable. Initially, the queue was extremely lengthy, which has its pros and cons. The downside is clear, but the lengthiness suggests popularity, often indicating the food's potential quality. 

Next, they graciously take drink orders while you're queued up, allowing you to sip on your beverages as you await your meal. Additionally, the ambiance of Lux was engaging enough to keep me entertained while I waited for our breakfast to be ready. The presence of vintage-style lamps on the tables, along with local artwork, created a cozy and inviting environment. 

Upon the arrival of our dishes, we all found ourselves content. I savored Aunt Gladys's homemade salsa served with four strips of succulent belly bacon, three scrambled eggs, white cheddar, and hash, which was quite tasty. My two companions also expressed their satisfaction with their dishes. I'm rating them 4 stars, as I felt their food was slightly costly considering the portion size and quality. For instance, a glass of orange juice was priced at $5. Apart from that, I was thoroughly pleased with the overall experience.

yelp:test:9057.orig:
This is a humble eatery, a pleasant surprise in the midst of a sordid neighborhood. The restaurant is choc-a-bloc on a weekend evening. So it is best to arrive around 7 pm, not later than that.

As indicated on their menu they start preparing the food only after the order is placed leading to a considerably long wait (45 mins to one hour). However, during the waiting period their customers have quite a few occupations like looking at the paraphernalia on the walls, sipping margaritas, devouring the crunchy tacos, listening to the loud Spanish music or looking at what other people are eating. 

Whatever their clients choose to do, there comes a time when the waiter places the hot plate on the table, they pick up the fork, take a mouthful and then there is calm in the din of Los Dos Molinos. In fact there is a near- Nirvana experience with every bite of the carnitas or enchiladas. 

At the end the brusque manner of the waiting staff is forgotten, so is the long wait and restlessness.
yelp:test:9057.para: This modest dining spot offers an unexpected delight in an otherwise grim area. The eatery is packed on weekend evenings, so aim to arrive by 7 pm to avoid delays. The menu notes that dishes are only made once an order is given, resulting in a wait time of 45 to 60 minutes. Yet, during this period, patrons engage in various activities such as examining the decor, enjoying margaritas, savoring crunchy tacos, absorbing the vibrant Spanish tunes, or observing others' meals. \n\nEventually, the waiter serves the hot plate, and diners take a bite, finding tranquility amidst the bustling atmosphere of Los Dos Molinos. In fact, each morsel of carnitas or enchiladas provides a near-meditative experience. By the end, the impatient demeanor of the service staff and the initial restlessness are both overlooked.

yelp:test:9058.orig: Always a great place, we visit Los Dos 1-2x everytime we are in Phoenix yearly. This time we gave the Mesa location a go, opposed to the original. Food and service were great as usual, however the food didnt seem as spicy as at the original Los Dos and the ambiance is not the same...has more of the standard restuarant look and feel. Not a knock at all...still amazing food regardless!!!
yelp:test:9058.para: Every year, we make it a point to dine at Los Dos in Phoenix, typically twice. This time, we opted for the Mesa branch instead of the original. The food and service remained excellent, but the dishes lacked the usual spice level found at the original Los Dos, and the atmosphere differed, presenting a more conventional restaurant vibe. However, this hasn't detracted from the overall enjoyment of the meals!

yelp:test:9064.orig: First off, was never offered water throughout entire night!!!!!Gf's tea was never refilled, never brought out silver ware even after being asked to bring some effin silverware.  No God for saken soy sauce plate which comes standard in every single friggin Sushi rstrnt in the entire world. Our waiter, after waiting for sliverware was seen sitting down watching Tv.  The music was absolutely horrible, in the short amount of time we were there we heard a atrocious mixture of music consisting of sweet cherry pie....Craig david crap, country....80's rock.....Maria Carey love ballads....just horrible.  NO toilet paper in women's bathroom.   On a lighter note the decor is cool, too bad the music doesn't match the ambiance of the rstrnt!!  The food was ok, however they spilled sauce all over appetizers and still served it ....the Sushi was ok....worthy of two stars.  The cod breading was overly salty, however the fish was decent!
yelp:test:9064.para:
Initially, we were not provided with any water during the entire night, and the tea for my partner's consumption was never replenished or served on silverware, despite requests. There was a noticeable absence of a standard soy sauce plate, which is typically included in every sushi restaurant globally. Our server, after being asked for silverware, was observed to be lounging and watching television. The auditory experience was unbearable, with a jarring blend of music ranging from sweet cherry pie tunes, country hits, 80's rock, to Mariah Carey's ballads, all contributing to an unpleasant atmosphere. Additionally, the women's restroom lacked toilet paper.

On a brighter note, the restaurant's decor was stylish, but unfortunately, the music did not complement the ambiance of the establishment. The food was satisfactory, though we encountered an issue with sauce spillage on appetizers, which were still served. The sushi was acceptable, earning it a two-star rating. The cod's breading was excessively salty, but the fish itself was of decent quality.

yelp:test:9068.orig: This was one of my early favorites when I first started living here two years ago.  I love their chips and hot sauce.  Some of the best in Phoenix.  Last two visits really missed the boat.  This last time the service was so bad that I had to chase my waiter down just to get my order delivered correctly.\n\nFood is pretty good.  Love the Baja Burro.  But, two less than great service experiences--I won't be back.
yelp:test:9068.para: When I moved here two years back, this place quickly became one of my top picks. I'm a big fan of their crispy chips and spicy sauce, and they're considered top-notch in Phoenix. However, my last two visits were disappointing due to subpar service. During the most recent visit, I had to pursue my server to ensure my order was accurately delivered. Despite the food being generally good, and my fondness for the Baja Burro, the two instances of poor service have led me to decide against returning.

yelp:test:9077.orig:
Went here last night and the night started ok. There were only 3 other people in the place and we had the worst service ever. No drink refills or help! The mangaer/owner she didn't show any care when i talked to her and i will never eat here again. Also you could hardly get into the rest rooms because of the clutter of tables and chairs.

Food was ok but nothing to write home about or worth the price they were charging. No wonder they rely on coupons to get people in to their place.

also becareful with their happy hour specials as i asked for a $2.00 special and she brought me out a large draft and then charged me more saying i didn't ask for a bottled beer.

Horrible management and tactics! BEWARE!!!
yelp:test:9077.para: Last evening, the experience began reasonably well with only a handful of patrons present. However, the service was abysmal, with no refills or assistance provided. The manager/owner displayed a lack of concern when I communicated with her, leading me to vow never to return. Additionally, navigating the restrooms was challenging due to the excessive arrangement of tables and chairs. The food quality was average, failing to justify the high prices. The establishment's dependence on coupons to attract customers is evident. Furthermore, be cautious with their happy hour deals; I was misled into paying extra for a $2.00 special when I was only offered a large draft instead of a bottled beer. The management's poor strategies and tactics are a clear warning.

yelp:test:9080.orig:
Creepy.

Barbie dolls servicing men of all shapes and sizes from drunk losers to drunk high rollers in an incredibly dark, smelly warehouse. I couldn't tell if these ""girls"" were actually girls.

And we almost got tangled in a hate crime. A drunk jerk of unlimited stupidity thought a couple of guys in our group were gay and wanted to bash their heads in. We all left immediately before he could call in his KKK/Nazis brothers to help.

I hate strip clubs.
yelp:test:9080.para:
Unsettling.

In a dimly lit, foul-smelling storage facility, Barbie dolls catered to men ranging from inebriated underachievers to inebriated affluent individuals. It was unclear whether these "girls" were genuinely female.

We narrowly escaped a hate incident. An inebriated idiot with boundless foolishness misinterpreted a few men in our group as homosexual and sought to assault their heads. We promptly departed to avoid his KKK/Nazis allies joining in.

I have a strong aversion to strip clubs.

yelp:test:9101.orig: If you like staying at the slums and love horrible customer service, I would recommend this place.  Talk about a waste of money. \n\nFrom the time that you call and reserve your hotel, the phone CSRs sound like they don't want to be at their job......Seriously.  They sound unmotivated.  Their attitude is \""\""next..\""
yelp:test:9101.para: If you enjoy residing in impoverished areas and have a penchant for poor service, this establishment might be suitable for you. It's essentially a financial misstep. \n\nFrom the moment you dial and book your accommodation, the representatives on the phone seem disinterested in their roles...truly. Their lack of enthusiasm is palpable, as if they're merely going through the motions with a sense of "what's next?"

yelp:test:9107.orig: The service is ok, but the food was worth it.  I like the fact that the food is not over priced like in most Vegas eateries.  The wine list is absolutely one of a kind, especially if you like German Reislings!\n\nI would come back, our food was excellent, looking forward to the next trip!
yelp:test:9107.para: The food quality justifies the service, which is satisfactory. I appreciate the reasonable pricing, unlike the usual high costs in Las Vegas dining spots. The wine selection stands out, particularly for those who enjoy German Rieslings. I am eager to return, having thoroughly enjoyed the meal and anticipating our next visit.

yelp:test:9111.orig:
Tired of overpriced hotel foods, long buffet lines, hassle of finding great places to eat...well look no further. The best Thai restaurant in Las Vegas is at Lotus of Siam and it's only a 7 min drive from the strip off Sahara. Best make reservations if you have parties of 4 or more since this place always has a wait.

Here are a few musts from the menu:

1) Thai iced tea
2) Garlic Prawns (they fry them season them and still keep the skin on...must have)
3) Duck curry (spicy levels from 1-10, we had the 8 and it was pretty spicy...so stick with 5-6 for those who just want a medium kick)

Staff's very attentive and supposedly they have a great wine selection, but I have yet to try anything. I always make a pit stop anytime I come back to Las Vegas...I found a gold mine.
yelp:test:9111.para:
Exhausted with the high costs of hotel dining, endless buffet queues, and the difficulty of locating excellent eateries, you won't have to search any longer. The top Thai eatery in Las Vegas, Lotus of Siam, is conveniently located just a 7-minute drive from the Strip on Sahara. It's recommended to book a table in advance for groups of 4 or larger due to its popularity and potential wait times.

Here are some essential menu items to try:

1) Thai iced tea
2) Garlic Prawns (cooked, seasoned, and served with skin intact - a must-try)
3) Duck curry (spiciness ranging from 1-10, we opted for level 8 and it was quite hot - for those preferring a milder taste, levels 5-6 are suggested)

The staff are highly attentive and are rumored to have an impressive wine list, although I have not yet sampled it. I always make a detour to this place whenever I visit Las Vegas again, as it has proven to be a valuable find.

yelp:test:9119.orig: The best Thai food I had in long time.  I started with Sa-Tay of chicken.  Very good pickle vegetables and a delicious peanut sauce.  I enjoy it immensely.  My girlfriend had the Tom Yum Kai.  She really enjoyed the soup.  I was lucky and got to try it before she ate it up.  I agree, the soup was great.\nI had the drunken seafood noodles with spice level of 7.  It was spicy but satisfying.  The food was delicious and the spicy sauce was incredible.  We came pretty late but service was still very good.  Definitely, will be back again.
yelp:test:9119.para: I experienced exceptional Thai cuisine recently, beginning with Sa-Tay chicken. The pickled veggies and peanut sauce were outstanding, and I thoroughly relished it. My companion savored the Tom Yum Kai soup, which she found delightful. I was fortunate to sample it before she finished it. I concurred, the soup was excellent. I also tried drunken seafood noodles with a spice intensity of 7. It was fiery yet gratifying. The overall food quality was superb, particularly the spicy sauce. Despite our late arrival, the service remained commendable. I am certain to revisit.

yelp:test:9134.orig:
Review of Buffet:

UGH!  It was very very underwhelming. 

Maybe regular menu is great, but do not get the buffet IMHO.  About half the restaurant was eating the buffet... unfortunately I was in the idiot half of the crowd.
yelp:test:9134.para:
Buffet critique: 

Disappointing indeed! 

While the standard menu might be commendable, I personally advise against the buffet option. To my dismay, I found myself amidst the less satisfied half of the dining area.

yelp:test:9171.orig: I always stop by this place when I stay at the MGM. Especially for lunch. Everything on the menu is usually really great. The service is always on point and one time Emeril was there walking around signing autographs and stuff. Thats Vegas for you.
yelp:test:9171.para: Whenever I'm at the MGM, I make it a point to visit this spot, particularly for a midday meal. The menu consistently offers exceptional fare. The staff maintains impeccable service, and once, Emeril was present, engaging with fans and signing memorabilia. That's the essence of Las Vegas.

yelp:test:9197.orig: We bypassed the wait by grabbing seats at the bar.  Great beer selection, we went with a pitcher of fat tire which was new to us East Coasters.  Delicious burgers, huge and juicy.  We also had the deep fried pickles which were surprisingly tasty.  Overall it was a great place to sit, grab a burger and relax.
yelp:test:9197.para: Avoiding the queue, we opted for bar seating. Enjoyed a diverse range of beers, choosing a fresh pitcher of fat tire, a novel choice for East Coast dwellers. Savored large, succulent burgers. Additionally, we relished the unexpectedly delightful deep-fried pickles. In summary, it was an excellent spot to unwind, enjoy a burger, and take in the ambiance.

yelp:test:9208.orig:
Had dinner at the burger bar before heading to a show. There wasn't any wait on a Saturday at 7. Server did a great job greeting and taking out order.  

Loved the wide selection and choose stellar on draft. Ordered a ceasar salad which was a good sized portion to share. Ordered the custom made burger- angus beef, jack pepper cheese, with jalapeño. The burger was cooked to a perfectly to medium. Favorable and juicy. The true test that the burger stayed together when you hold with you're hands while eating it. 

Totally recommend to eat here. 

Tota
yelp:test:9208.para:
Savored a meal at the burger joint prior to attending a performance. On a Saturday evening at 7, there was no wait time. The attentive server efficiently greeted and served our order. 

Enjoyed the extensive menu and selected an excellent draft. Opted for a generous ceasar salad, ideal for sharing. I ordered a personalized burger made with Angus beef, jack pepper cheese, and jalapeño. The burger was cooked to a perfectly medium level, favorable and juicy. The real test was the burger's ability to maintain its integrity when held in your hands while eating. 

Highly suggest dining here. Tota

yelp:test:9234.orig:
Mesa Grill was extremely overpriced and the service was annoying. I understand it's Vegas, but for the prices, I expected better, quieter service. Our waiter came up every five minutes trying to take our plates, pouring water in between us and our conversations, asking questions... I understand being diligent but this was annoying. 

The pork loin was the best thing any of us got. It was definitely very good. So was the shrimp tamale. I think that's actually the best thing on the menu, but quite rich so you can split that and the pork with someone and be totally satisfied as the portions are huge.

One of us had the coffee crusted steak, and the rub was just too spicy to really enjoy the meat. The fish was bland and slightly overcooked. Desserts were awful. Seriously, how hard is it to make good churros? The donuts at a fast food restaurant are better!

If you are a fan of Bobby Flay's other restaurants -- Bar Americain is one of my favorites -- you will be very disappointed here. The quality, service and atmosphere are just so mediocre it really disappoints. Oh, and the price - I think it's more expensive than eating in his restaurant in Manhattan, which is just mind-bogglin
yelp:test:9234.para:
Mesa Grill's pricing was excessively high and the service was irritating. While acknowledging the Vegas setting, I anticipated superior, more tranquil service for the cost. Our server was excessively attentive, interrupting our discussions and inquiries every five minutes with our dishes, which, although well-intentioned, was bothersome.

The pork loin and shrimp tamale stood out as the best dishes, offering excellent quality. These items, along with the generous portion sizes, could be shared between two people to achieve full satisfaction.

One of us opted for the coffee-crusted steak, but found the rub excessively spicy, detracting from the meat's enjoyment. The fish was uninspiring and slightly overdone. Desserts were disappointingly subpar. The challenge of crafting superior churros was underestimated, with fast food donuts outperforming them.

For enthusiasts of Bobby Flay's other establishments, such as Bar Americain, which I hold in high regard, Mesa Grill falls short. The mediocrity in quality, service, and ambiance is disheartening. Moreover, the cost is perceived as higher than dining in his Manhattan restaurant, which is quite perplexing.

yelp:test:9293.orig: I know that this is an institution but it really isn't worth the price. I think if I were drunk at 3:00am though, then I would be writing otherwise.\n\nDon't bother unless you're drunk. Go for the hot dog.
yelp:test:9293.para: I acknowledge it's an establishment, yet its value doesn't justify the cost. If I were inebriated at midnight, my perspective might differ. Refrain from engaging unless you're under the influence. Opt for the hot dog instead.

yelp:test:9306.orig: Wanted to see why the reviews are so high for this place.  I have to say it was an experience to try at least once while visiting Pittsburgh.  We sat at the counter and that was a fun to eat there.  We shared a Pastrami sandwich and I thought the meat portions were small, mostly cold slaw and fries in your sandwich.  The pastrami was average and I would have liked more of that then the other items.  It was a big sandwich and enough for us.  We didn't have to order any fries, but we forgot it was in the sandwich.  The fries could be crisper and I thought they were tasty, but too soft for me.\n\nOverall, I say go there once to experience it.  There's not a lot of attention from the staff, bc the place is so busy.  I don't need to go back.   If you miss getting a chance to eat there.....then catch it the next time you visit, not a must to visit.
yelp:test:9306.para: I was curious about the high ratings for this establishment and decided to give it a try during my time in Pittsburgh. We chose to dine at the counter, which provided a unique dining experience. We opted for a Pastrami sandwich, but found the meat portions to be modest, with a predominance of cold coleslaw and fries. The pastrami itself was mediocre, and I would have preferred a greater quantity of it compared to the other components. Despite its size, the sandwich was sufficient for our group. We didn't feel the need to order fries, but it was surprising to find them included in the sandwich. The fries could have been crisper, yet they were enjoyable, albeit too soft for my liking. In summary, I recommend visiting this place just once to savor the experience. The staff's attention is minimal due to the establishment's popularity. I don't plan to return. If you're yearning for the opportunity to dine there, seize it the next time you're in the vicinity, but it's not essential to make it a regular destination.

yelp:test:9310.orig:
Monday night.  Called our order in ...picked up 15 mins later.  Walked in to pick up and place wasnt packed.  

I ordered a fish sandwich.  NOT good at all!  The fish barely covers the bread!!!  They piled on the fries and slaw.  But hardly any fish!  

Next was my SMALL STREET FRIES.  For over $4.00 I EXPECT REAL BACON..NOT IMMATATION BACON BITS!!! OMG!  I had to feed these fries to my dog!  FRICKEN GROSS!!!!!  Along with the great big pieces of pinto beans.  :(  This is horrible.  I was so looking forward to this food!  

Thanks for letting me down!
yelp:test:9310.para:
Monday evening.  I placed my order and received it after a brief wait. Upon arrival, the area wasn't fully prepared.  

I had ordered a fish sandwich, but it was disappointing. The fish was scarcely on the bread, with excessive fries and coleslaw. The fish quantity was minimal.  

Next, my small street fries were overpriced at $4.00. I anticipated genuine bacon, but instead, I got mere imitation bacon bits. I was so dismayed that I ended up giving these fries to my dog. The overall experience was unpalatable.  

I appreciate your acknowledgment of my dissatisfaction.

yelp:test:9334.orig: I love this place.  The employees are awesome and the coffee is so good.  I love the blueberry muffin too.  All of them are so nice and there are plenty of places to sit and chill.  It is easy access if on foot or bike so that's a plus too.
yelp:test:9334.para: This location is fantastic. The staff members are exceptional and the coffee quality is top-notch. I also enjoy the blueberry muffin. Everyone is incredibly friendly and there are ample spots to relax. Plus, it's conveniently reachable by walking or cycling, which is an added advantage.

yelp:test:9354.orig: I had the California Burger. It was good but not excellent, and certainly not the best burger in Madison. I went with three other people and they agreed. We should have went to Five Guys.
yelp:test:9354.para: I savored the California Burger. It was satisfactory but not outstanding, and undoubtedly not the top-tier burger in Madison. Accompanied by three others, we concurred. A better choice would have been Five Guys.

yelp:test:9357.orig: Good jambalaya and ok chili (the cheese is a slice just plopped on top) and cornbread... Great beer... But that's all I could eat. I have a severe fish allergy and it was that or a few of their salads (nothing with any meat though). Very disappointing that they hadn't thought about cross contamination with allergies. I'll go back for the soup and definitely the beer but it'll only be with friends... Not by myself. And only if other people suggest it. Very disappointing.
yelp:test:9357.para: Excellent jambalaya and decent chili (with cheese simply placed on top) accompanied by cornbread, paired with excellent beer... However, due to a serious seafood allergy, I could only consume these items. It was disheartening to find no consideration for cross-contamination risks for allergies. I plan to revisit for the soup and beer, but only in the company of friends, and only if they recommend it. It was quite disheartening.

yelp:test:9394.orig: I've used this hotel for years through work and have always had a positive experience.  Free WiFi, great front desk staff, big rooms and easy access to the great city of Madison. \n  I tend to be very hard on hotels but this one always leaves me satisfied.
yelp:test:9394.para: Through my professional engagements, I've consistently stayed at this hotel and have been consistently pleased. The complimentary internet access, commendable front desk team, spacious accommodations, and convenient proximity to Madison's vibrant city life contribute to my unwavering satisfaction. Despite my generally stringent standards for hotels, this establishment consistently meets and exceeds them.

yelp:test:9400.orig: I always go for the scrambler,milk shakes, and coffee for Sunday brunch.  Really cozy diner which is unique to Madison.
yelp:test:9400.para: Every Sunday, I prefer to enjoy scramblers, milkshakes, and coffee at this distinctive cozy diner located in Madison.

yelp:test:9411.orig:
When I first moved to Madison I was really excited to come to this restaurant because the man had hyped it up as a great Thai eatery.  When I finally visited the restaurant it definitely did not live up to the hype.

On the plus side the place is really nice and is a great place for dates and groups as it is very large.  However the food, as this is a restaurant, should also be great and unfortunately it was not.  I ordered a red curry dish which sounded great but was disappointed at first bite.  It's not that it was bad because it certainly wasn't but it just wasn't great.  There seemed to be something missing that I was not able to put my finger on.  The man ordered the pad Thai which he actually loved.  I didn't try any of it so I don't have anything to say about it.

As far as the presentation of the food however that was spot on.  I would recommend this place to anyone trying to venture out and try something different as the flavors are not in your face.  Also the staff was great and very attentive.
yelp:test:9411.para:
Upon relocating to Madison, I was thrilled to dine at this establishment, lauded by a man as an exceptional Thai restaurant. However, upon my visit, it fell short of the anticipated excellence. 

Despite this, the venue itself is quite appealing and ideal for gatherings or romantic outings due to its spaciousness. Yet, the culinary experience did not meet expectations. I sampled a red curry dish that initially seemed promising but ultimately left me underwhelmed. It wasn't terrible, but it lacked the expected greatness. I couldn't identify a specific deficiency, but something was evidently amiss. The man enjoyed the pad Thai, but I refrained from tasting it, so I can't comment on it.

On a positive note, the food's presentation was impeccable. I would suggest this place to those seeking to explore new flavors, as the taste is subtle and not overpowering. Additionally, the staff demonstrated commendable attentiveness.

yelp:test:9422.orig:
These hacks couldn't make a cocktail if their lives depended on it.  They're arrogant and can't back it up.

The mojito was disgusting, with sad overworked mint.

The Sazerac was an abomination.  They shook it resulting in an over diluted drink, then added a squeeze of a lemon wedge instead of a twist of lemon peel.
yelp:test:9422.para:
The concoctions were flawed, lacking the finesse to even mix a proper cocktail. Their confidence was misplaced, devoid of substantiation.

The mojito was unappetizing, marred by overworked and wilted mint.

The Sazerac was a disgrace. The shaking process led to an excessively watered-down beverage, and a lemon wedge squeeze was used instead of a proper lemon peel twist.

yelp:test:9467.orig: So after 15 years having the best bloody marys around you changed your mix.  The watered down tomato juice out of the gun was horrible.  Drinks use to be good and over priced now they are horrible and over priced.  Won't be enjoying a cocktail here anymore.
yelp:test:9467.para: Following 15 years of serving top-notch bloody marys, your concoction alteration has led to disappointment. The diluted tomato base from the dispenser was dreadful. Previously, the beverages were of good quality but costly; now they're of poor quality and still overpriced. I'll no longer be savoring a drink here.

yelp:test:9470.orig: My 1st trip to Vegas I stayed at the palms and I have to say that it was the greatest experience and best decision made by my friends and I..  The crowd and the vibe was awesome.. You get to mingle with the young rich, grown & sexy.. oh and with celebrities as well..  The rooms were very spacious with a nice view and comfortable beds..  We stayed at the play pen suit and i have to say that the stripper pole came very well in handy... I can't see myself going back to Vegas and not staying anywhere else but the palms.. highly recommend it..
yelp:test:9470.para: My inaugural visit to Las Vegas was memorable, as I chose to stay at The Palms, which turned out to be an exceptional choice and a fantastic decision by my companions and me. The atmosphere and energy were electrifying, allowing us to interact with the youthful affluent, mature and alluring individuals, and even celebrities. The accommodations offered ample space, impressive views, and comfortable sleeping arrangements. I found the play pen suite particularly useful, especially the stripper pole feature. It's hard for me to imagine returning to Vegas without staying at The Palms, and I wholeheartedly endorse it.

yelp:test:9480.orig: I went to the Palms Casino thru Bookit.com.  My stay Oct 18-21 originally and it was for my 40th birthday.  First of all I only gave it 1 star for the actual room it self.  The room was clean, spacious with  a nice view of the strip.  The cons:   After I first initial night they came to clean our room at 6pm  I mean really...  but the second night we call them to come clean and they came right away and the third day we were there and extended our check out time  due to our flight leaving at 11pm that night, they never came at all!  We called them & asked for trash removal, towels & toilet paper & a guy that didn't speak any english or at least acted like he didn't brought towels up and kinda said someone would bring toilet paper he tired to leave but we ran & got the trash out our room & gave it to him to take with him.  Needless to say no one ever came to bring toilet paper or clean we used the kleenex in the bathroom.  At  check in I asked about the 2for1 drink specials that came with book.it.com the girl checking me in said they no longer did that and did not offer to accommodate me in any other way.    She did say we got free admission to the clubs in the hotel & we could  each
yelp:test:9480.para: I booked my stay at the Palms Casino via Bookit.com for my 40th birthday, originally scheduled from Oct 18-21. I rated the room just 1 star due to its cleanliness, spaciousness, and a pleasant strip view. However, I faced several issues: On our first night, cleaning staff arrived at 6pm, which was unexpected. The following night, they promptly responded to our call. Yet, on the third day, despite extending our check-out time because of a late flight, no cleaning was done. When we requested trash removal, towels, and toilet paper, we were met with a non-English speaking individual who failed to deliver the towels and only managed to take the trash. Consequently, we resorted to using tissues in the bathroom. Additionally, upon inquiry about the 2for1 drink specials advertised on Bookit.com, the check-in attendant informed us that they were no longer available and offered no alternative solutions. Despite this, we were granted complimentary access to the hotel's clubs and the option for each guest to enjoy them.

yelp:test:9489.orig: I went in for a tattoo during a vacation last week.  For a black and gray tattoo 3\"" x 3\"" to cost $400 with a non refundable deposit of $100 sight unseen of the drawing is not customer friendly.  You had artists sitting without appointments but would rather force me back out the door because I don't pay without knowing I will even like what you draw?  No thank you.  I had the money in my pocket in cash sweeties, but I left with it still there because I was unconvinced by your guy up front, inflated prices, and deposit policy.\nI have 20+ hours of ink and none from h&h.
yelp:test:9489.para: During my recent trip, I decided to get a black and gray tattoo measuring 3"x3", priced at $400, which required a non-refundable deposit of $100 without seeing the artwork firsthand. This approach was not appealing to me as a customer. Artists were available on a walk-in basis, yet they insisted on me leaving if I didn't commit immediately. Despite having the cash ready, I chose to retain it due to my doubts about the artist's credibility, the high costs, and the deposit terms. I ended up with no tattoo from this establishment, having invested over 20 hours in the process.

yelp:test:9495.orig: The Bellagio Pool Cafe is delicious but expensive... under a nice covered area, you can enjoy a wide variety of lunch options in your swimsuit and towel. By the time we sat down around 2:30 pm, I was starving so I ended up sampling everyone else's food in addition to my own.\n\nI had the teriyaki chicken lettuce wraps ($12.50) that came with cold noodles, pickled, veggies, and hoisen sauce. They were really yummy and a good amount of food. My uncle enjoyed the Cobb salad (about $14) that included fresh tomatoes (red and yellow), delicious avocado, etc. My brother and dad shared a tuna sandwich and a turkey sandwich with fries and cole slaw. Everyone appreciated their lunch selections and left the Cafe satisfied and happy.
yelp:test:9495.para: The Bellagio Pool Cafe offers delectable but costly dining options under a charming covered space, where you can savor an extensive range of lunch choices while dressed in your swimwear and towel. By 2:30 pm, I was famished and ended up trying out the dishes of others as well as my own.\n\nI relished the teriyaki chicken lettuce wraps ($12.50), which came with cold noodles, pickled vegetables, and hoisen sauce. They were truly scrumptious and provided ample food. My uncle savored the Cobb salad (around $14), which featured fresh red and yellow tomatoes, and delicious avocado among other ingredients. My brother and dad shared a tuna sandwich and a turkey sandwich with fries and coleslaw. Everyone was content with their lunch choices and departed the Cafe feeling satisfied and joyful.

yelp:test:9517.orig:
Awesome Buffet.  

We tried the Ballagio Buffet and the Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan.   The Bellagio Buffet was the winner, by far.  

King crab legs, Short Ribs, Prime Rib.... All amazing.   I am still trying to figure out how they make any money.  Plenty of options.
yelp:test:9517.para:
Exceptional Buffet Experience.  

We sampled the Ballagio Buffet and the Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan.   The Ballagio Buffet stood out significantly.  

Delicious offerings like King crab legs, Short Ribs, and Prime Rib left us in awe.   The abundance of choices still baffles us on their profitability.

yelp:test:9593.orig: This was my 7th time to Vegas and first time staying at the Paris. It will also be my last.... The service and the rooms are absolutely terrible!\n\nWe arrived around 11:30 am on a Weds. We knew it may be too early to check in but most hotels on the strip allow early check ins around noon. So we decided to give it a shot when we arrived. After waiting in line for nearly 20 mins (when there was only 4 people in front of us) we finally got to up to the counter. We gave our name and confirmation number and to our dismay the nice lady told us we only had reservations for one night instead of the four we booked and our name wasn't on any of the four rooms reserved for my wife's company. PLUS, there's now a $25 early check in fee!!! Our jaws dropped... We had to wait two hours for the wife's boss to arrive so he could sort out the confusion. AFTER all that was finally figured out, the nice lady proceeded to tell us that our rooms weren't ready. This being at 3:30 when regular check-in time usually is... yelp:test:9608.orig: This hotel has declined over the past years. We had a late check in and did not get the room we reserved. yelp:test:9608.para: Over the recent years, this accommodation has seen a drop in quality. We experienced a delayed arrival and were not provided with the room we had booked. yelp:test:9636.para:
During the Fourth of July weekend, I booked a cabana by the pool at Monte Carlo, opting for the jacuzzi suite. However, it required an intensive cleaning, akin to remodeling after a fire. I paid $300 for this cabana, but upon arrival, my girlfriend and I were given two lawn chairs just 2.5 feet away from the kids' wave pool, which infuriated me more than my girlfriend's deceptive invitation to an Andrew Lloyd Webber opera. I questioned the young woman in a bikini if this was our cabana, to which she nonchalantly replied, as if consulting her manager.

Feeling exasperated, I was more interested in getting drunk and indulging in food. The agreement was that the cabana was free for the day, but I had to spend at least $300 on food and drinks. I requested a few waters and cocktails due to the scorching heat. After waiting for over an hour, I was concerned about how I would justify spending $300 without even getting a drink. Another server passed by, adding to the frustration.

yelp:test:9644.para:
Monte Carlo, why did I opt to remain here? Possibly because it's centrally positioned amidst the strip, flanked by Aria and the City Center. This former favorite of my spouse in Las Vegas remains a mystery to me. The pool boasts a leisurely lazy river, shorter than those at MGM but adequate for unwinding and escaping the bustling casino sounds. Tube rentals are also available at the service desk. These are the main attractions of this hotel, unless you have a penchant for...

An affordable food court near the main elevators. I recall that it offers Starbucks, McDonald's, Manchu Wok, Rubio's, and Subway. These options are not typically found in other strip hotels. go to ANDRE'S, the upscale dining establishment of Monte Carlo. I haven't personally experienced it, but based on reviews from fellow yelpers, it's a traditional French restaurant.

yelp:test:9649.orig: This review will be mostly written regarding the staff.  Everyone we encountered was super friendly.   From the restaurants to the Bathrooms and pool.   Our house keeping staff greeted us every morning.  We had a broken lamp which she called maintenance to take care of before we even had a chance.  When they didn't get it fixed the first day she found us to apologize and tell us she had called again.  The pool servers, although there didn't seem to be very many of them, were very helpful with picking out the right drink and bringing buckets and ice to make sure the drinks didn't get too warm in the heat.   As far as the hotel itself - it needs work.  The rooms are pretty beat up and could use some TLC. For the most part the room was clean and sufficient.  Let's face it, who spends much time in their rooms in Vegas, but it could still use something.
yelp:test:9649.para: This feedback will primarily focus on the staff. Every individual we met displayed exceptional friendliness. From the dining areas to the restrooms and the pool, the housekeeping team welcomed us each morning. They addressed a malfunctioning lamp by alerting maintenance, ensuring it was resolved before we could complain. When the issue persisted, they reached out to us with an apology and a follow-up call. The pool attendants, though seemingly few, were incredibly attentive, assisting us in selecting the perfect beverage and providing buckets and ice to keep our drinks cool in the scorching heat. Regarding the hotel's condition, it requires improvement. The accommodations appear worn and could benefit from some attention. Despite this, the rooms were generally tidy and adequate. It's worth noting that even in Las Vegas, where guests typically spend minimal time in their rooms, there's still room for enhancement.

yelp:test:9660.orig: VERY SEXY SHOW! Very Vegas! Talented performances. A must see with your hubby, partner, or boyfriend. Its got something for everyone if you know what I mean, and it definitely gets you in the mood to have some dirty fun ;o)
yelp:test:9660.para: Extremely alluring showcase! Exquisite Vegas vibes! Exceptional talent on display. An essential experience to share with your significant other. It caters to a wide audience, ensuring a lively atmosphere, and it's guaranteed to ignite a sense of playful indulgence ;-)

yelp:test:9698.orig:
My brother got a comped room here, so I may be a bit bias...

Best part of the suite was the bathtub, large and deep enough to fit almost anyone.  Plus, three televisions and super comfy beds. We didn't pay the resort fee to get wifi in our room, but the main lobby and food court had free wifi so everything was okay.  Good location, in the middle of the strip and near shopping that's more reasonable like the Fashion Show and Caesar's Palace.  Oh, and Walgreens downstairs!  An overpriced Walgreens of course, but a Walgreens nonetheless.    

My only complaint was that the telephone line to the front desk was useless.  We tried calling on three occasions and never got to a real person despite 10-15 minutes of waiting.
yelp:test:9698.para: My sibling received a complimentary room here, which might influence my perspective...\n\nThe suite's standout feature was its spacious bathtub, capable of accommodating most individuals. Additionally, it boasted three TVs and plush beds. The pool was relatively shallow (under 4 feet) and bustling, a common occurrence during the summer season. Excellent opportunities for window shopping were available, including high-end stores like Barneys and DVF. We didn't opt for the resort fee to access wifi in our room, as the main lobby and dining area offered free internet service, making everything satisfactory. The location was prime, situated centrally on the strip and close to more affordable shopping venues such as the Fashion Show and Caesar's Palace. There was also a Walgreens located downstairs, albeit at a premium price. The sole grievance was the ineffective phone line to the front desk, which proved unresponsive despite multiple attempts and lengthy waits.

yelp:test:9704.orig: The Venetian is my favorite casino! It appears they shut off the water to the outside canal during the summer, but in the winter, it was beautiful. The canals inside ran during both seasons I went. We ate at an Italian restaurant overlooking the inside canals. It was pricey, but worth the food and service. We were also in awe of the mural on the ceiling at the entrance and how the inside makes you feel like it is always daytime. Simply amazing!
yelp:test:9704.para: My top choice for a casino is Venetian! They apparently turn off the water to the external canal in summer, yet in winter, it was stunning. The inner canals flowed throughout the visits I made. We dined at a restaurant with canal views, which was costly but the cuisine and service justified the expense. The entrance mural on the ceiling left us spellbound, and the interior gave off a perpetual daylight vibe. Truly remarkable!

yelp:test:9722.orig: This place is all about the hotel and the shops.  It's a great place to visit and have fun.  They are more expensive than a lot of the other casinos.  The Bourbon Room (bar) is a total rip off.  Don't order a beer or a drink there.  You'll pay more than you think.
yelp:test:9722.para: This location primarily focuses on its hotel and retail outlets. It's an excellent destination for enjoyment and exploration. However, it tends to be pricier compared to many other gambling establishments. yelp:test:9735.orig:
First time staying at the Mirage, and I was very happy with the experience.  Awesome pool, cabana at Bare on the first day, ridiculously fun bartenders at Kokomo's every night that kept our party going until (gulp!) 6 in the morning...not to mention Carnegie Deli *right there*.  The RhumBar is killer, and the spa will help you ""detox so you can retox"" right up there with the best of them...We literally had everything that we needed right inside the hotel, and we appreciated that there was no smell of smoke anywhere we went.  

Rooms were comfy, and soundproof! Did not hear any of the outside noise that other yelpers here have complained about.  

Pool service was great, though I docked one star for the non-hotel guests that seem to make it in.  Club promoters seem to have no problem, though we can't really complain about the club comps that they provided our group.   Still though, makes you wonder.  With the pool that packed, they would do good to make it a bit more exclusive...
yelp:test:9735.para:
Upon my initial visit to the Mirage, I was extremely pleased with the overall experience. The pool was exceptional, and we enjoyed a cabana at Bare on the first day, with bartenders at Kokomo's who consistently kept our celebration alive until 6 in the morning. The proximity to Carnegie Deli was a bonus. The RhumBar was outstanding, and the spa offered a detoxifying experience on par with the best. Everything we required was conveniently located within the hotel, and we were grateful for the absence of smoke odor. 

The rooms were cozy and soundproof, effectively blocking out any external noise, which was a relief compared to other reviews. The pool service was commendable, but I deducted one star due to the presence of non-hotel guests. Club promoters seemed to have no issue, and the club comps they provided for our group were satisfactory. However, it raised some questions about exclusivity, given the pool's popularity.

yelp:test:9746.orig:

A quick call to the Mlife counter and we were whisked away to another room with a king bed and a great view of the strip on one of the higher floors.
Gambling was fun at the Mirage and we spent almost 90 percent of our gambling time there. The dealers were friendly and people at the table were fun. This was our first time staying so far up north on the strip and we really liked it. Usually, we stay at Mandalay Bay which is on the southern tip of the strip or at the Aria, which is more centrally located.
We always make it a point to go BLT Burger regardless of where we stay on the strip and we have never been disappointed. This time was no exception either. Their burgers are awesome and I love their Knight Rider shake.

We tried out Stack for dinner one night and it was not bad at all. The ambiance is good and the food was pretty decent.

Oh, and the best part, Mlife comped off our entire stay when we checked out (except for my wife's spa bill), which was ve
yelp:test:9746.para:
In November, we opted to forgo our booking at the Aria and instead chose the Mirage. Upon arriving in Vegas on December 6th, we discovered that despite our request for a king-sized bed during booking, we were given a double. A swift communication with the Mlife desk resulted in an upgrade to a room with a king-sized bed and an impressive strip view on a higher floor.

Gambling at the Mirage was enjoyable, with us dedicating nearly 90% of our gambling time there. The dealers were amiable, and the atmosphere at the tables was lively. This was our inaugural experience staying so high up on the strip, and we found it quite pleasing. Typically, we prefer Mandalay Bay, located at the strip's southern end, or the Aria, which is centrally situated.

Regardless of our location on the strip, we make it a habit to visit BLT Burger and have never been let down. This time was no different, with their burgers being exceptional and their Knight Rider shake being a delight.

We also sampled Stack for dinner once and found it satisfactory. The ambiance was pleasant, and the food was commendable.

The highlight, however, was Mlife covering the entire cost of our stay (excluding my wife's spa expense), which was a significant saving for us.

yelp:test:9764.orig:

 I had the Pisco Sour as my cocktail, the petite lettuce wedges, filet and mash potatoes. All where freak'n delicious!

yelp:test:9764.para:

Another excellent venue at the Venetian is Bouchon.

yelp:test:9768.para:
I recently hosted guests at this location. I had booked through Open Table, initially for a group of 4, but then decided to include an additional person. However, they repeatedly informed me that accommodating another chair at the table was impossible. Alright.

Upon arrival, we discovered a private event taking place in the lobby/bar/wait area, which was somewhat unsettling. We were directed to the lounge area where we placed our drink orders, which were never delivered. When our designated table was finally set up, it turned out to be the end table in the lounge area. Consequently, we shifted to an adjacent table.

The wine selection was incredibly detailed and somewhat overwhelming. I preferred a simple red wine with my meat, but that wasn't the approach here. The beginning of our meal was marked by a crowded table, with excessive items and oversized service ware, making it challenging to dine comfortably.

Before our meal arrived, I took a detour to the restroom, which was quite a journey due to the restaurant's large size. As I passed by other tables, I noticed several larger tables with fewer occupants and unoccupied seats. This observation led me to question their inability to accommodate an extra guest or their lack of knowledge in managing seating arrangements.

yelp:test:9775.orig: Fantastic food, great service.  Much more expensive than what we usually spend on dinner, but so yummy and worth it!  We both had steak for dinner, with sides of salad in the sherry ving., garlic smashed potatoes, and the pecan pie.  I wish we had room to finish the pecan pie, but could only get through half.
yelp:test:9775.para: Exquisite cuisine and exceptional service. Prices are higher than our typical dining expenditure, yet the deliciousness justifies the cost. We both enjoyed steak dinners accompanied by sherry-infused salad, garlic-infused potatoes, and a half-finished pecan pie. The desire to savor the entire pecan pie remains, but we managed to indulge in half.

I have been to The Palm Restaurant in Downtown Los Angeles and I did not enjoy it that much.  We went for lunch and I had their steak frites and, unfortunately, they were using really poor quality beef (a New York Strip but not a good one).  You do have to use less expensive beef than dinner to serve steak but still achieve a reasonable lunch price, but most restaurants like Lucques do not settle for lower quality; instead, they just showcase a cheaper cut like hanger steak.

Since I went to the Downtown LA Palm for lunch, I did not get a chance to try their signature Prime steaks.  I could have tried them at my recent trip to the Las Vegas location (The Palm is located in the Forum Shops at Caesars Palace), but I opted for one of their other signature items instead--lobster.  I had their jumbo lobster tail and it was actually pretty good.  The lobster was huge--it was almost a pound--and the lobster meat was good--fresh, moist, lightly sweet, and fairly soft.  The seasoning of the lobster was also good--flavorful with a little bit of spice but not overpowering.

Almost everything
yelp:test:9782.para:
***Dining at The Palm Restaurant in Downtown Los Angeles left us with a less than satisfactory experience, particularly due to the subpar food and service during our visit***

I visited The Palm Restaurant in Downtown Los Angeles for lunch and found it less than enjoyable. I ordered their steak frites, but the beef quality was disappointing, even though it was a New York Strip. It's common for lunches to use less expensive beef to maintain a reasonable price, but most establishments like Lucques don't compromise on quality, opting for premium cuts like hanger steak instead. 

Since I dined at the Downtown LA Palm for lunch, I missed out on trying their prime steaks. I could have sampled them at my recent visit to the Las Vegas branch (The Palm is situated in the Forum Shops at Caesars Palace), but I chose a different signature dish--lobster. I enjoyed their jumbo lobster tail, which was quite substantial (almost a pound) and the lobster meat was fresh, moist, lightly sweet, and somewhat soft. The seasoning was also well-balanced, offering a hint of spice without being overpowering.

Almost everything

yelp:test:10116.para:
The pyramid-like design of the Luxor hotel disrupts the interior room layout, causing issues such as low ceilings, awkwardly angled windows that necessitate leaning back to view the outside, and consistently malfunctioning plumbing. Initially, we assumed our room was plagued by a non-functional toilet, but it turned out to be a common problem among past guests. The apparent significant design oversight in the pyramid structure is that the rooms are not stacked directly above each other, which likely disrupts the vertical alignment of pipes, leading to inefficient water flow. Although I'm not an expert in physics or engineering, this seems to be the most plausible explanation for the problem, as the casino's main floor bathrooms worked fine. 

The hotel's amenities were a mixed bag: limited dining choices, including a mini-food court with unappetizing fast food, several Starbucks, and a mediocre buffet; an average spa; and a decent pool. The management has systematically removed several elements.

yelp:test:10470.para:
Phoenix's Delux was among the initial dining establishments I frequented after relocating, and I've revisited it several times, predominantly for lunch during the workweek. It stands out as my preferred burger joint. 

The ambiance carries a touch of pretension, but the space is compact and somewhat constricted. Even during weekday lunch hours, it can feel tight at a table, with a significant likelihood of waiting in line for a while. I've experienced both indoor and outdoor seating and felt somewhat encroached upon by adjacent tables. Larger groups can add to the complexity. 

Despite this, the culinary offerings are exceptional. I consistently opt for the same Delux burger and sweet potato fries. Even if you're apprehensive about medium-rare, it's a must-try. It's one of the most extraordinary burgers I've tasted, and I often find myself unable to finish it. A mini version would be ideal. The accompanying fries are served in a charming metal mini cart. It's worth mentioning that you don't automatically receive ketchup with your fries. As for the beer selection, it's truly impressive. The option to order a

yelp:test:10501.orig: Better than Wynn, but not 30% better than Wynn, considering the 30% price increase.  Amazing seafood selection.  Pesto mashed taters and apricot mousse are to die for.
yelp:test:10501.para: Superior to Wynn, yet not exceeding Wynn's quality by 30%, given the 30% surge in cost. Exceptional variety of seafood. Delightful pesto-infused potatoes and delectable apricot mousse are unparalleled.

yelp:test:10509.orig:
Yum.  


That little 3 letter word sums it up.  I got here at 1045am.  The breakfast buffet closes at 11am.  I suggest you get there earlier to take full advantage of what this beast has to offer.  I couldn't get an omelette, as the line for it was like at a sizzler or waiting for crab legs, but man, they looked good.  Instead I just got the normal buffet fare.  There were 3 different kinds of potatoes (sliced thinly, cubed, and baked), the bacon was crispy but still had amazing taste, multiple sausages, waffles, french toast, pancakes, chorizo, etc.  It was all amazing, even though the scrambled eggs were a bit runny (I dislike runny eggs.  A lot.).  For $16 (this includes tax), I say it is well worth it.  If only I were hungrier (or was I too hungry from waiting too long??), I would've done more than $16 worth of damage.  Instead, I only probably did $13.  Sad.

Oh yea, the orange juice was amazing.  I highly recommend it.
yelp:test:10509.para:
That three-letter word encapsulates it all. I arrived at 10:45am. The breakfast buffet shuts down at 11am, so it's wise to arrive sooner to fully enjoy its offerings. Unfortunately, I couldn't secure an omelette due to the long queue, but the dishes on display were tempting. I opted for the standard buffet selection instead. There were three varieties of potatoes (thinly sliced, cubed, and baked), bacon that was crispy yet flavorful, a selection of sausages, waffles, french toast, pancakes, and chorizo. The entire spread was impressive, though I found the scrambled eggs slightly undercooked, which I don't particularly enjoy. At $16 (tax included), I believe it's a great value. However, I might have indulged more if I wasn't too famished from the wait or if I had more appetite. In reality, I probably spent around $13. It's a bit disappointing.

Also, the orange juice was exceptional. I highly suggest trying it.

yelp:test:10512.orig:
Let me preface this review with a couple of things:
1. I went on a Monday at 3pm, so probably not the most ideal time to see the freshest foods and most attentive staff, but less people to fight with to get to the food
2. I live in Manhattan so I am spoiled by knowing what good food and service are
3. I understand that a buffet, even an expensive buffet will never meet the quality of a decent restaurant

With all that said, the variety and quality of food was JUST BARELY OK, after seeing several reviews I guess my expectations got a little too high.

Also of note I found a HAIR in my gravy, when I mentioned it to the waitress her extremely caviler response was some thing to the effect of ""OK, I let them know"".  No ""I'm so sorry"" or ""I really apologize"", NOTHING.

All in all not a great experience, but if you want a large quantity of food you can't beat it for 20 bucks
yelp:test:10512.para:

1. My visit was on a Monday at 3pm, which may not be the prime time to sample the freshest dishes and most attentive service, but it did mean fewer people vying for the food.
2. As a resident of Manhattan, I am accustomed to high standards of cuisine and service.
3. I acknowledge that even an upscale buffet cannot match the quality of a reputable restaurant.

Despite these considerations, the assortment and caliber of food were barely satisfactory, perhaps due to elevated expectations based on numerous reviews.

Additionally, I discovered a strand of hair in my gravy. When I brought it to the waitress's attention, her response was curt and lacked any semblance of remorse, merely stating, "OK, I'll let them know."

In summary, the overall experience was less than stellar. However, if your priority is quantity over quality, it's hard to beat the value for money.

yelp:test:10535.para: April 12, 2012 - Thursday at 2 PM: The buffet I experienced in Vegas on this date was the most disappointing I've ever had. Despite the $48 price tag for two, the food seemed average but was actually quite disappointing in taste. The pasta was overdone and excessively salty, while the shrimp were old and lackluster. The seared salmon had an oily texture, and the ribs were undercooked and tough. Even the Caesar salad and cheesecake were subpar, with the cheesecake being particularly bland and pasty. I struggled to eat the meal, and I'm not one to be fussy about food. I considered complaining and asking for a refund immediately, but I regret not doing so as most of the food ended up being discarded. This experience has made me vow never to return to this buffet, as it was a complete waste of both money and time.

yelp:test:10546.orig: Decent price for a buffet in Vegas.  The line was not more than 30 minutes on a Thursday night.  The food was decent.  There was nothing incredibly delicious. yelp:test:10622.orig:
My goodness, I've basically grown-up (Club-wise) with Tao. I've probably been 10 or so times and I still believe it is one of the better clubs out there. BUT, it is not as amazing as it once was. 

Now, they close off the top-level on busy nights and that causes the other two levels to get ridiculously over-crowded (and alot of the crowdedness is just due to Tao's ever-increasing popularity). It also has a great mix of ethnicitiies...it has everything you could ever want in a club!

And the best part of all is this guy Taoboda! He can get your entire group past the line and in for free before 11 AND all the girls get free drinks from 10-11. What an awesome hook-up!

Taoboda alone keeps this place at a 4-star club for me despite its recent downfalls in other areas.
yelp:test:10622.para:
I've essentially matured (in terms of club experience) alongside Tao, having attended it around 10 times and maintaining my belief that it stands out as a top-notch club. However, it no longer matches its former glory. 

On peak nights, they limit access to the premium section, leading to the remaining two levels becoming excessively packed. This surge in density is partly due to Tao's growing popularity. Nonetheless, the interior design here is unparalleled, and the girls are consistently up for a good time (in stark contrast to the aloof crowd). The club also boasts a diverse range of ethnicities, offering a comprehensive club experience. 

The highlight for me is Taoboda. He efficiently manages to get your whole group through the queue and inside without charge before 11, and the girls receive complimentary drinks from 10-11. This impressive arrangement is what keeps this place in my 4-star club rating, despite some recent setbacks in other aspects.

yelp:test:10628.para: Avoid spending your cash on the bottle service in Tao's VIP area. I've observed superior booth seating at a Denny's for a fraction of the cost. If you decide to visit, consider paying the standard admission, purchasing a couple of drinks, and then taking advantage of the sophisticated individuals in their underwhelming VIP zones.

yelp:test:10680.para:
During a recent business trip to Las Vegas, my employer arranged a dinner at SW Steakhouse. The steaks were exceptional, but the overall dining experience fell short of our expectations.

The waiting area is notably compact, with merely six stools in the bar, which can be inconvenient for larger groups such as ours, consisting of seven individuals. This often results in prolonged periods of standing.

Once we were seated, the service was notably sluggish. We were ready to place our orders but were left unattended for at least fifteen minutes. The wine suggested to us was satisfactory but not remarkable, and the limited availability of only two bottles necessitated a mid-meal switch. In my experience, top-notch steakhouses always inform patrons of low stock before serving wine, particularly for groups of 5-7 people. While not a significant problem at SW, it does reflect a lack of sophistication, particularly when the cost of a steak is a minimum of $54.

Moving on to the food...

The steaks, as previously mentioned, are truly outstanding. The veal chop ordered by another guest also garnered high praise. I opted for the smallest steak available, a 9oz filet, cooked to medium rare perfection. Another diner had the same dish, and it was equally impressive.
