yelp:test:10700.para:
So, my boyfriend's birthday was last weekend, and we opted for a Vegas-themed celebration. We landed in Vegas on Friday and checked into the Palm resort, which I'll discuss shortly. Patience, please.

On Saturday night, we ascended to the Ghost Bar, located 55 floors above ground. This isn't the ideal spot for those seeking to dance; they even have a sign prohibiting dancing. However, for those desiring quality music, a relaxed atmosphere, and attractive individuals to admire, this is the perfect spot. 

Despite its compact size, the decor and ambiance are truly exceptional. 

The panoramic view is absolutely breathtaking. Standing 55 floors above the vibrant lights of Vegas, it offers an experience beyond just a view. 

The beverages are priced high but are robust and flavorful. The staff is amiable, the security personnel are intimidating, and the majority of the guests are ordinary folks. I encountered two men who were overly confident about their physique, attempting to flirt with me while my boyfriend was present. This encounter was short-lived, but overall, it was a memorable night. 

If you're in Vegas, I strongly suggest visiting this place. Just ensure you have the necessary funds.

yelp:test:10703.orig:
This is why I liked Ghostbar, and why I would go back:

Bouncers, bartenders, and overall staff was friendly
The place was clean
Tolerable club music
Beautiful view
It was not over crowded 
It did not smell bad
The music was not so loud that my ears wanted to explode
No cover for hotel guests
Air conditioning 

This is what I deducted a star:

We had purchased a Travel Zoo coupon which included dinner to Simon, and VIP to either Ghostbar or the other club at the Palms. The person at the front of Ghostbar told us that if we chose to use our VIP bracelets, then we would get two free drinks. When we went up to the bar, the bartender told us that we did not get free drinks. It did not ruin my night, but if we knew we weren't going to get any perks from the VIP bracelets, we would have used them at another place. 

This place is having an identity crisis. Are you a lounge or a club?
yelp:test:10703.para:
I appreciated Ghostbar for several reasons, and I would revisit it:

The staff, including bouncers and bartenders, were amiable
The venue maintained a neat appearance
Acceptable club music was played
A stunning view was available
The venue was not excessively crowded
No unpleasant odors were present
The volume of the music was bearable, not causing discomfort to my ears
No additional charges for hotel guests
Air conditioning was provided

Here's my deduction of a star:

We had a Travel Zoo coupon that covered dinner at Simon and VIP access to either Ghostbar or another club at the Palms. The person at the front of Ghostbar informed us that using our VIP bracelets would grant us two complimentary drinks. However, when we approached the bar, the bartender informed us that we would not receive any free drinks. Although this did not spoil our evening, if we had known that the VIP bracelets wouldn't offer any extra benefits, we would have utilized them at a different location.

This establishment seems to be struggling with its identity, questioning whether it's a lounge or a club.

yelp:test:10722.orig:
I liked this show a lot.  It was my second Cirque show and it was very good.  The story was easy to follow but the dudes helping before the show I could have done without.  I know they're there to help get you in the mood for the performance but I personally didn't care for them.  

As for the show, it was fun.  I really liked the wall scene and the thing with sand.  I thought the sand part was cute and gave you a break before they came back at you with more action.  Your heart can only beat so fast for so long.  

When I'm back in Vegas, I'll definitely be going to see another Cirque show.
yelp:test:10722.para:
I thoroughly enjoyed this performance. It was my second visit to a Cirque event and it exceeded expectations. The narrative was straightforward, yet the pre-show personnel I found unnecessary. Although their role is to set the stage for the main act, I personally didn't appreciate them. 

Regarding the actual performance, it was entertaining. I particularly enjoyed the wall sequence and the sand interaction. I found the sand element endearing and provided a welcome pause before the resumption of intense action. There's a limit to how fast your heart can race for an extended period. 

When I return to Las Vegas, I'm certain I'll attend another Cirque show.

yelp:test:10807.orig:
No POOL ACCESS at a 4-star where you PAY A RESORT FEE! unbelievable!
Beautiful furnishings but the beach pool is shut down in 78 degree weather. Misery during a great long weekend holiday. ANd they have the nerve to charge a $27 RESORT FEE ON TOP OF YOUR HOTEL ROOM PRICE!!!!!!
Although very far from the strip, reserved the place for Valentines weekend because it was 4 star hotel. Even encouraged 3 other friends to join up! Very unfortunate that the hotel management has decided to NOT OPEN THE POOL so it sits there in all its tempting beauty with cabanas and waterfalls all around.

Also, it's not as quiet in the room as you would expect. I can hear people in the two neighboring rooms talking.
yelp:test:10807.para:
No access to the pool at a 4-star hotel where you're required to pay a resort fee, truly astonishing!
Despite the hotel's attractive decor, the beach pool remains closed in mild 78-degree weather, leading to disappointment during an otherwise enjoyable long weekend getaway. Moreover, the hotel insists on imposing an additional $27 resort fee on top of your room's cost.

Despite its distance from the strip, I had booked this 4-star hotel for Valentine's weekend, even persuading three friends to join. It's quite disheartening that the management has chosen to keep the pool closed, leaving it visually appealing with cabanas and waterfalls nearby.

Additionally, the room's tranquility is compromised, as I can hear conversations from the two adjacent rooms.

yelp:test:10822.orig:
This place SUCKS!!!!

I went to Vegas the weekend of Nov 18th (my birthday!) and we stayed at the Mandalay Bay. It was early saturday night and we wanted something to eat before we went out. All I wanted was a deli style sandwhich (which is pretty hard to find). I called the concierge and she mentioned this place. I looked it up online through my phone and said ""why not.""

I walked down to the place and it was packed! There was a line waiting but I walked right in to the ""take-out"" window. I ordered a roast beef sandwich with a side of clam chowder. It was kinda pricey (about $15-20) for a sandwhich, chips, and literally 8-10 fl oz of soup, but whatever, it's Vegas.

So I leave and meet my friends at the Yogurt/Crepe place in Mandalay. Damn how I wish I would have gotten a crepe with them.

I opened my soup container and it literally looked like someone put half water, half olive oil, a tablespoon of alfredo sauce, soggy microscopic pieces of celery, and potato. I don't even remember if there were CLAMS in my CLAM chowder, that's how terrible this thing was! I didn't even know that clam chowder came minestrone style! But apparently here at the Red, White, & Blue, IT
yelp:test:10822.para:
This location is utterly disappointing!

On my birthday, November 18th, I visited Las Vegas and stayed at Mandalay Bay. It was a Saturday evening, and we were in search of a meal before going out. I desired a deli-style sandwich, a challenging find. I contacted the concierge, who recommended this spot. I researched it on my phone and decided to give it a try. 

Upon arrival, the place was crowded, with a queue, but I proceeded to the "take-out" counter. I ordered a roast beef sandwich with a side of clam chowder. The price, around $15-20, seemed steep for a sandwich, chips, and a mere 8-10 fl oz of soup, but in Vegas, you get what you pay for. 

Afterward, I met my friends at the Yogurt/Crepe spot in Mandalay. I regret not choosing a crepe with them. When I opened my soup container, it resembled a mixture of water, olive oil, a tablespoon of alfredo sauce, tiny pieces of celery, and potato. I couldn't recall if there were clams in my clam chowder, which was horrendous! I was unaware that clam chowder could be served in a minestrone style here at the Red, White, &

yelp:test:10847.orig:
This place has a very versatile menu and every time I go the food is delicious.

There are two; one in the Venetian and one in the Palazzo. I think that the venetian location is more private and the tables aren't so close to each other compared to the Palazzo one.

As soon as you're seated you are brought a warm basket of bread and butter to hold you over while you browse the full menu. This place wont let you down and is a must try!
yelp:test:10847.para:
This establishment boasts a diverse selection of dishes, and each visit reaffirms the exceptional taste of their cuisine.

There are two establishments, one situated in the Venetian and the other in the Palazzo. I believe the Venetian location offers a more secluded ambiance with tables spaced further apart than the Palazzo's.

Upon being seated, you are immediately presented with a warm basket of bread and butter to enjoy while perusing the extensive menu. This place consistently delivers a satisfying experience and is highly recommended!

yelp:test:10855.orig:
Double Stuffed Potato Spring Rolls.... amazing! 

I am a huge cafe fan. I love them. This cafe inside the Palazzo is awesome! The staff at the bar is hilarious and friendly. Alex, one of the bartenders knows his stuff. Everything that he has ever suggested for me to eat from the menu has been delicious. 

The appetizers are some of my favorites and Nadia (I think) makes a mean Texas Tea. 

I have only ever sat at the bar, so I cannot comment on the dining areas, but usually it seems so fast paced and everyone on top of their game. 

Try out this cafe if you are in the neighborhood.
yelp:test:10855.para:
Double Stuffed Potato Spring Rolls are absolutely fantastic! 

I am an enthusiast of cafes and I adore them. The cafe located within the Palazzo impresses me greatly! The bar crew is both amusing and welcoming. Alex, a bartender, is highly knowledgeable and has consistently recommended dishes that I've found to be scrumptious. 

Among my preferred appetizers, Nadia (possibly) crafts an excellent Texas Tea. 

Since I've only ever dined at the bar, I can't provide insights on the dining rooms, but they typically appear to be bustling and everyone performing at their best. 

If you're nearby, I highly recommend giving this cafe a try.

yelp:test:10857.orig:
Been here more than once after a night out of drinking.. But now I can say I've been here sober and not so sober!

Quick seating, although it gets busy! Friendly staff & good for kids when the sun is still up. 

Like everyone says-- it IS like a Cheesecake Factory minus the cheesecake, but in my opinion and if I'm willing to make the drive out here, I like it better! 

This time around the better half and I had :
Blue Cheese Salad - not a blue cheese fan but this was good, could have a little less dressing
Calamari - FAVORITE! I liked the added fried zucchini and onions! 
Kobe Meatballs - big meatballs, juicy and tender meatballs! Not too much sauce, comes on a bed of creamy polenta.

I unfortunately could not have any of the pasta dish but it did look good! 

Must try if you're in the strip area!
yelp:test:10857.para:
Visited this place multiple times post-alcohol consumption, but now I've experienced it sober and found it even more enjoyable! 

Quick service, though it can get crowded. The staff is amiable and suitable for children during daylight hours. 

As others have mentioned, it's akin to Cheesecake Factory without the dessert, but in my view, and if I'm prepared to travel for it, I prefer it. 

During my recent visit, my partner and I indulged in:
Blue Cheese Salad - I'm not a blue cheese enthusiast, but it was tasty, though perhaps a bit over-dressed.
Calamari - My top pick! I appreciated the extra fried zucchini and onions.
Kobe Meatballs - Large, succulent, and tender meatballs. The sauce was minimal, served on a bed of creamy polenta.

Regrettably, I couldn't sample the pasta dish, but it appeared appetizing! 

Highly recommended if you're in the vicinity of the strip!

yelp:test:10862.orig:
This is a really cute placeit's something different. 

I had the watermelon spritzer, very sweet, but good if you like watermelon. They refill it for you too

voodoo shrimp - i usually never eat shrimp, but our waitress recommend this so i had to try it. It was really good, jumbo size shrimp smothered with tasty seasoning over corn bread that melts in your mouth!

gumbo - its thick and gooey it was decent. Tasted way better with hot sauce :)

baby back ribs -  literally fell off the bone... it was delish! it also came with cold slaw, beans, and corn. mmMMm the corn was good up until i dropped it :( But my sweet server saw the whole entire incident and fired up a new one for me right away!

Lastly, we had the field of greens... the portion was smaller than the ribs, but that's okay. every bite was yum :)
yelp:test:10862.para:
This spot is quite adorable and offers a unique experience. 

I enjoyed the watermelon spritzer, it was sweet but pleasing for watermelon lovers, and they even topped it up for me. 

The voodoo shrimp was a delightful surprise, as I rarely eat shrimp, but our server suggested it, and it was a big hit. The large shrimp were generously coated with flavorful spices atop a melt-in-your-mouth corn bread. 

gumbo was thick and creamy, and it tasted much better with a dash of hot sauce. 

baby back ribs were incredibly tender, literally falling off the bone, and came with cold slaw, beans, and corn. I was sad when I accidentally dropped the corn, but our attentive server quickly replaced it with a fresh one. 

Lastly, the field of greens was a satisfying portion, smaller than the ribs, but each bite was delicious.

yelp:test:10866.orig: I've been to the House of Blues for a few concerts now, and there are plenty of other venues that offer a better sound quality, especially in Las Vegas. \nIf you have the opportunity to see a band at another venue, I highly recommend it. The sound quality is awful, so there will be a very low chance you'll understand anything coming out of the singers mouth. It ends up being just a muffle that fades into the rest of the band.
yelp:test:10866.para: Having attended several House of Blues shows, I've noticed that there are numerous other locations in Las Vegas with superior audio fidelity. Should you have the chance to experience a live performance elsewhere, I strongly advise it. The acoustic experience at the House of Blues is subpar, making it difficult to discern the lyrics from the vocalists. It often results in a muffled sound that blends seamlessly with the rest of the ensemble.

yelp:test:10878.orig: If you like good, fresh, sandwiches, then you have to try one here at Lee's. I think the bread is what really makes the difference, it is super fresh and would taste good all by itself! Its much cheaper than any other sandwich shop and definitely seems fresher and less assembly line. I think the only thing that can be hit or miss here is the service from time to time, but that is soon forgotten with a sniff of the fresh bread.  Yes they do only accept cash but that is as they say, to keep the prices down.  I usually order the ham and turkey club and a water and i get out of there for about 5 bucks.  I also love the fresh baked baguettes...so good!
yelp:test:10878.para: Should you appreciate high-quality, homemade sandwiches, then Lee's is a must-visit spot. The freshness of their bread is what sets them apart, it's incredibly fresh and delicious on its own! Compared to other sandwich establishments, it's more affordable and gives off a genuine, less mechanized vibe. Occasionally, the service may be inconsistent, but the aroma of the fresh bread quickly overshadows any minor service hiccups. They only accept cash, which they claim helps maintain lower prices. Typically, I opt for the ham and turkey club with a drink, costing me roughly 5 dollars. Additionally, I'm a fan of their freshly baked baguettes, which are exceptionally tasty.

yelp:test:10882.orig:
This restaurant is located in the Chinese Cultural Center and was the one restaurant that I had not been to. So after some shopping at one of the shops, we stepped in to have dinner.

We stepped in and asked for a seat for two. We were seated immediately. The place was decorated nicely and a lady playing the piano made for great ambiance.

We looked at the menu briefly and ordered our drinks, an appetizer, a soup and two main dishes. The drinks came out promptly and so did the rest of the meal. My goodness everything we ordered was very tasty.

The waiter service itself however was not even close to the decor and food. He never introduced himself, and although he took our order, our food itself was brought out by a kitchen person.

After we ordered our waiter really never came back asking if we needed anything else, except to give us our check at the end and that was after the person I was dining with got up and asked a different waiter for it.

It's amazing how a place with great food, decor, and ambiance can mess it all up by crappy waiter service.
yelp:test:10882.para:
Nestled within the Chinese Cultural Center, this eatery was a dining spot I had yet to experience. Following a shopping spree, we decided to dine there. Upon arrival, we requested a table for two and were accommodated without delay. The interior was tastefully adorned, and a pianist added to the pleasant atmosphere.

We perused the menu briefly before placing our drinks, appetizer, soup, and two main courses. Our drinks arrived swiftly, followed by the rest of our meal. I was impressed by the deliciousness of everything we ordered.

However, the service from the waiter fell short of the restaurant's impressive decor and food quality. The waiter failed to introduce himself and, despite taking our order, the kitchen staff delivered our food.

The waiter's attention to our needs was lacking, as he didn't return to check if we required anything further, except to hand over our bill at the end. This happened after my dining companion sought assistance from a different waiter.

It's remarkable how a place with excellent food, decor, and ambiance can be undermined by subpar waiter service.

yelp:test:10889.orig: If you live near Khoury's this has got to be your place for craft brews and/or specialty wines. They have a great selection of common craft brews all the way to hard to find US craft and international craft brews. Wednesday nights they do a craft beer sip and share which usually has a food truck involved. I was a regular all last summer and it's incredibly fun and a great social event for local Vegas residents. Thursdays they do a wine tasting night, which I have yet to go to but I'm sure is equally as fun.\n\nThe best part about this place is that you can buy a delicious craft beer and enjoy it and discuss craft beer with other knowledgable people there. If you don't want to buy a bomber they also have a solid rotation of craft beers on tap. They recently also started filling growlers which is awesome. All the guys who work there are friendly and will give answer any questions you have or give you recommendations based on what you're in the mood for. Strongly recommend this place if you love craft beer.
yelp:test:10889.para: If you reside close to Khoury's, it's an essential spot for enthusiasts of handcrafted beers and unique wines. They boast an extensive array of standard artisanal brews to rare US and global craft beers. On Wednesday evenings, they host a craft beer sampling and sharing session, often accompanied by a food truck. I frequented this spot throughout the previous summer, finding it highly enjoyable and a fantastic opportunity for socializing among locals in Vegas. Thursday nights feature a wine tasting event, which I've not yet attended but anticipate will be just as enjoyable. The standout feature of this establishment is the chance to purchase and savor a fine craft beer while engaging in discussions with informed individuals. For those who prefer not to purchase a large bottle, they offer a dependable selection of craft beers on tap. They've also introduced the option to fill growlers, which is a welcome addition. The staff, all male, are amiable and ready to answer any inquiries or offer suggestions tailored to your current cravings. I wholeheartedly endorse this place for craft beer aficionados.

yelp:test:10890.orig: I stopped by Tryst with two of my girlfriends in Sept. and we were afraid of the long lines that we were warned of from others. We got to Wynn super early at 8:45pm and no one was line for Tryst. The club didn't open until 11:00pm and we didn't have anything to do since the longest line that Saturday night was only 30 mins. The bouncer gave us free passes to get in for free which was cool. I think Tryst is overly hyped and not particularly special inside.
yelp:test:10890.para: In September, I visited Tryst with two female companions, concerned about the anticipated lengthy queues as per others' warnings. We arrived at Wynn at 8:45pm, finding no queue for Tryst. The venue opened at 11:00pm, leaving us idle as the longest queue on that Saturday night lasted just 30 minutes. The bouncer generously offered us complimentary entry passes, which was appreciated. I believe Tryst is excessively promoted and lacks unique charm inside.

yelp:test:10891.orig: Yep...loved it.  One of my favorite clubs along wiht Body English in vegas.  The whole layout of this place is well thought out.  The waterfall is HUGE to the entire experience.  Makes it so much more refreshing and enjoyable.  We got a table outside near the waterfall and really had a good time.  It gave us the chance to get away from the crowd and have quality time drinking with friends and when we wanted to dance we could go inside easily.  \n\nOne other thing is the bottle service here is not like any other place we have seen.  They are extremely attentive and just go far and beyond what we would expect.  Definitely coming back.
yelp:test:10891.para:
Absolutely enjoyed it. Among my top picks, this Vegas club pairs perfectly with Body English. The design is meticulously planned, with a massive waterfall enhancing the overall ambiance. It adds a refreshing touch, making the experience more enjoyable. We secured a spot outside near the waterfall and thoroughly relished our time. It allowed us to escape the hustle and bustle, savoring quality moments with friends and seamless access to dance inside.

An additional highlight is the exceptional bottle service here, unparalleled by any other venue we've visited. The staff's attentiveness and dedication surpassed our expectations. We're eager to return.

yelp:test:10896.orig: My girls and I had a lot of fun at Tryst.  Really like the outdoor/indoor set up.  Waterfall is nice.  Great music. Helps when you don't have to pay for any of your drinks:-)  I would go back next time I'm in Vegas.
yelp:test:10896.para: We thoroughly enjoyed ourselves at Tryst, appreciating the blend of outdoor and indoor facilities. The waterfall feature was delightful. The music was excellent, especially since there were no charges for our beverages. I'm inclined to revisit next time I'm in Las Vegas.

yelp:test:10909.orig: Not the best club in Vegas but it is definitely a great place party if there is a specific event going on there. It's not that big of a club but if you're looking for a great place to go clubbing then this is a good spot.
yelp:test:10909.para: While it may not be the premier club in Las Vegas, it certainly stands out as an excellent venue for celebration during particular events. Although not massive, it serves as a commendable option for those seeking a notable clubbing experience.

yelp:test:10930.orig:
Love the ambiance of Okada, the fresh sushi, and tasty entrees don't hurt either! We got some sashimi and sushi specials both of which were delectable! The spicy tuna roll was definitely the best I've ever tasted. The sashimi melts in your mouth. Just thinking about them makes me want more! 

The service was fast and friendly.  

Love that you can see the fake waterfall from the window in the main dining room.  Nice for a date or intimate dinner. I would definitely recommend  Okada for sushi on the strip.
yelp:test:10930.para:
Enjoy the cozy atmosphere of Okada, along with the fresh sushi and satisfying dishes, which are delightful to the palate. We savored the sashimi and sushi specials, both of which were incredibly delicious! The spicy tuna roll stood out as the most exceptional I've had. The sashimi dissolves effortlessly in your mouth. Simply contemplating them evokes a craving for more! 

The service was prompt and amiable. 

I appreciate the view of the artificial waterfall from the window in the main dining area. It's perfect for a romantic date or a private meal. I wholeheartedly suggest Okada for an exceptional sushi experience on the strip.

yelp:test:10938.orig: I keep going back to VooDoo for the great views.  This time though my meal was also great.  Our server remembered us from a previous visit and was quite helpful.  The filet was excellent.  The wine selection is very good.\n\nThe one down side was the macaroni side.  It was less than impressive.  The mashed potato side made up for it though.
yelp:test:10938.para: I frequently return to VooDoo due to its spectacular vistas. This occasion, however, my dining experience was equally delightful. Our attentive server, who recognized us from a past visit, provided excellent assistance. The filet was outstanding. The assortment of wines is commendable.\n\nThe sole drawback was the macaroni dish, which failed to impress. Nevertheless, the mashed potato side compensated for it.

yelp:test:10967.orig:
Raucous, loud, rock-n-roll watering hole: fuck yeah!

My exact recollection of my experience here is somewhat hazy; mostly all I can remember is having a blast.  I wound up at Hogs & Heifers with a fairly big group doing a downtown pub crawl.  It was kind of a relief to find a dark, dingy cave of a bar after all the lights and 'showiness' of the casinos.  

The place wasn't too crowded when we arrived, and there was some kick-ass music blasting out of a robust sound system.  I'm not usually one for dancing (in public, anyway)... well, what happens in Vegas stays in Vegas, right? :)
yelp:test:10967.para:
Loud, raucous rock-n-roll bar: absolutely fantastic!

My memory of that night is a bit fuzzy, but the main thing that sticks out is the sheer fun. I ended up at Hogs & Heifers with a sizeable crew on a downtown bar tour. It was a welcome respite from the glitz and glamour of the casinos, finding solace in a dim, cozy bar. 

The bar wasn't packed when we got there, and the music was pumping out from a powerful sound system. I'm not usually inclined to dance in public, but in Vegas, you know the saying, right? :)

yelp:test:10993.orig: I was so excited to try this place, such great reviews.  As soon as we got there the excitement turned to disappointment.  My husband and I decided on a last minute date night when I get off work.  I had been looking at this on yelp and it was on my list.  We went last night, Sunday, and got there about 8 pm (they closed at 9 pm).\n\nFirst we walked in, was not sure where to go since it was out first time.  Someone walked by and said the hostess will be back in a few minutes.  So we waited..and waited.  About 15 minutes later a hostess arrived.  We asked to be seated outside since it was beautiful out.  She was annoyed that the table she sat us at was directly against a bench which I kept hitting my elbow on.  We asked to move (there were a lot of tables) which annoyed her even more.  About 15 minutes later our server showed up (granted now the close in 30 minutes).  We asked for a cup of ice and lemons for our water multiple times...never saw those the whole meal.  She came to the table for our order and stated they only had 4 pizza's left so if we wanted pizza we needed to order immediately.  Since we had never been there, looking at the menu for 3-4 minutes was not enough time,
yelp:test:10993.para: I was thrilled to visit this establishment, given its excellent feedback. However, our anticipation quickly soured upon arrival. My spouse and I opted for an impromptu evening out after work, having spotted it on Yelp and added it to our plans. We arrived last Sunday at around 8 pm, just before their closing time of 9 pm.\n\nUpon entering, we were uncertain of our initial direction as it was our first visit. A passerby informed us that the hostess would return shortly. We waited for about 15 minutes, during which time a hostess finally appeared. We requested an outdoor table due to the pleasant weather, but she expressed irritation when we were seated next to a bench, causing discomfort to my elbow. We asked to be relocated, which further irritated her. After another 15 minutes, our server appeared, noting the restaurant was closing in 30 minutes. We repeatedly asked for ice and lemon for our water, but these were never provided throughout our meal. When we placed our order, the server informed us that only four pizzas remained, urging us to order immediately. Given our unfamiliarity with the place, a brief glance at the menu took us 3-4 minutes, which was insufficient time under the circumstances.

yelp:test:11026.orig:
Are you a BRIDE thinking about having your wedding here? STOP!
Can you give a place no stars? This place has HORRIBLE reviews of JUST the HOTEL, despite their so called ""Renovations"" , so beware! And I'm not even complaining about their Hotel! This review (Or RANT ha ha) is for the EVENTS/WEDDING  department. STAY AWAY! wasted 6 months of precious planning time working with Janeen and Tricia from the Plaza.  I was given tours of the property and what was ""coming"" and promised how awesome the new banquet rooms would be. My first mistake.
I was even promised 2009 event food and booze pricing for my wedding because of the inconvenience of their renovations. Because of that, I decided on the Plaza. A few months later, I was finally suckered into signing a contract and giving them a 500.00 deposit.. Then, I finally SAW the ""new"" banquet rooms. My BAD.
They were normal, boring banquet rooms, and most of the area in them wasn't even NEW, including the carpet! If that wasn't enough of a joke, the two vendor companies the Plaza referred me to, to help decorate my event, were shockingly unprofessional. 
One, called Ltevention, never returned calls or emails over a one month p
yelp:test:11026.para: If you're contemplating a wedding at this location, please reconsider! This venue has received dismal ratings solely for the hotel, despite claims of renovations. Exercise caution! This commentary focuses on the events/wedding division. Abstain from this venue! I spent six months in fruitless preparation with Janeen and Tricia from the Plaza. Despite being shown the upcoming enhancements and the supposedly impressive new banquet spaces, my first error. I was assured special pricing for 2009 event catering and alcohol due to the renovation disruptions, leading me to choose the Plaza. However, months later, I was persuaded to sign a contract and pay a 500.00 deposit. Upon seeing the "new" banquet rooms, I was disappointed. They were ordinary, dull banquet rooms, with much of the space not even newly renovated, including the carpet. Additionally, the two vendors the Plaza suggested for event decoration were shockingly unprofessional. One, named Ltevention, failed to respond to calls or emails for over a month.

yelp:test:11042.orig: If there was a negative stars for this I would give it....do NOT go for lunch. We were not greeted at the door at all and had to walk around the place just to find someone who worked there.... That should have been our first clue.....when the man did seat us he smelled so bad of Cologne that we almost left before we even ordered......2 more couples walked in and stood and waited for someone to notice them, but the waiter was too busy chatting it up with the cook to notice, and I certainly wasn't about to tell him he had customers.....not my job, sorry. The lunch was just meh....the soda was flat and tasted funny, and the cheese steak was substandard at best...... Maybe if there  is nobody at the door to greet you at what appears to be a nice place it will be the clue to just walk out......I won't be returning again.
yelp:test:11042.para: Had I a scale to weigh down this experience, it would tip heavily towards the negative. Avoid this establishment for lunch; we were completely overlooked upon arrival, forced to navigate the premises to locate a staff member. This oversight should have been a clear sign to reconsider. The server's strong Cologne scent nearly compelled us to leave before placing our order. Additional diners were left waiting, unnoticed, as the server engaged in conversation with the chef. I refrained from alerting him of our presence. The meal itself was underwhelming, with a flat soda and a disappointingly average cheese steak. It seems the lack of a welcoming greeting at what seemed like a pleasant venue could serve as a warning to leave. I have no intention of revisiting.

yelp:test:11071.orig:
My douchebag radar was so far off the scale here I just shut it off completely. There's stairs ALL OVER the place, (I swear, some drunk chick in stilettos is going to fling herself down one of these one day) silly fog machines and unenthusiastic go-go dancers, with security guards standing watch at every doorway. Do you really need that much security? Eh, to be fair, I did witness some drama go down. 

I would hate to live in a world where I subscribed to the thought that Axis/Radius is THE hippest nightlife destination in the Phoenix metro area. Sadly, a lot of people seem to be trapped in this mindset. The patrons walk around in a zombie-like daze. In their intense social longing to ""be someone,"" or ""find someone"" they force themselves to frequent this club hoping to be seen by the right person, maybe get a snapshot on 944 or Dirty Scottsdale .com. It is true that this is quintessential Scottsdale, but it is not representative of the entire city's scene as a whole, as some sadly write it off as. 

Highlight: Dancing to ""Sandstorm.""
yelp:test:11071.para:
I found my snobbery detector completely misplaced, so I turned it off entirely. Numerous staircases are scattered everywhere, (I can't help but imagine a tipsy lady in high heels might someday tumble down one) along with pointless fog apparatuses and lackluster strip dancers, all under the vigilant eyes of security personnel at each entrance. Is such an abundance of security really necessary? Well, I did see some commotion unfold. 

I wouldn't want to reside in a reality where I believed Axis/Radius is the epitome of trendy nightlife in the Phoenix region. Unfortunately, many appear to be ensnared by this belief. The club's attendees move around like zombies, desperately trying to "be someone" or "find someone," hoping to catch the attention of the appropriate individual, perhaps even securing a photo on 944 or Dirty Scottsdale.com. While this is undeniably typical of Scottsdale, it doesn't accurately reflect the broader city's vibe, as some mistakenly dismiss it. 

Highlight: Grooving to "Sandstorm."

yelp:test:11078.orig: OMG! sushi left on the counter for 30 minutes, then served to us as though it was just made freshly? i think not! the sea eel didn't even look suitable for a photograph, but not wanting to be fussy, i tried it, and quickly spit it out! this place is more of a 1 time visit. i've been several times, and still am not impressed. that was the last try, i hope to never be starved for sushi and stuck by that place again. the service sucks at the bar, it was the bartender who served up the sour sushi too! steer clear from here, you've neen yelped! oh and the big fish tank in the floor? its not all that. although the decor keeps bringing me back-it makes me forget all the previous visits-then i quickly remember when i'm waiting for the sushi.\n\none things fer sure, if ur looking for all those candy pushers, with the burned out Ed Hardy clothes, plastic booby flashing bleached blondes or euro-transplants looking to do anyone that will get them somewhere, well there you go....because its all there.
yelp:test:11078.para:
Wow! Sushi left unattended for half an hour, then presented to us as if it were just freshly prepared? I doubt it! The eel looked unfit for a photo, but I didn't want to be overly critical, so I gave it a try and immediately rejected it! This place is not worth revisiting. I've been there multiple times, and I'm still not satisfied. This was my final attempt, and I hope I never find myself desperate for sushi and forced to return here. The bar service is subpar, with the bartender responsible for the poorly made sushi. Avoid this place, as you've likely read numerous negative reviews. The large fish tank on the floor isn't impressive either. Despite the decor's ability to lure me back, it quickly reminds me of the disappointing sushi experiences.

One thing is certain, if you're searching for a place filled with over-the-top fashion, burnt-out clothing, flashy plastic models, or foreigners trying to make a quick buck, then this is the spot for you. Because it's all there.

yelp:test:11097.orig:
So my boyfriend and I headed over to Sushi Mon on the recommendation of my friend [our mistake since that guy doesn't even eat raw fish] one day for lunch.  We both had gotten the All-You-Can-Eat lunch.  So now begins the critique:

The fish was not fresh.  Everything had this soggy texture that comes from defrosting.  I work at a restaurant so you can't fool me.  Although the portions were decent, everything that had some kind of sauce was over done.  Our soft shell crab had so much ponzo sauce, it became overly salty.  That's the typical way of getting a customer to fill up on water and have them stop ordering food.

Overall, this place wasn't as good as we expected but we still left with a full belly.
yelp:test:11097.para: My partner and I decided to visit Sushi Mon based on a suggestion from a friend, but it turned out to be a misstep as that individual doesn't consume raw seafood. We opted for the All-You-Can-Eat lunch option. Here's our review:\n\nThe seafood lacked freshness, exhibiting a mushy consistency due to thawing. Given my experience in the food service industry, I can easily spot such discrepancies. While the portion sizes were acceptable, any dish with added sauce was excessively cooked. The soft shell crab was particularly affected by the overpowering ponzo sauce, making it unbearably salty. This tactic is often used to encourage customers to drink more water and cease further food orders. Despite the subpar experience, we managed to leave satisfied, albeit with a full stomach.

yelp:test:11141.orig:
Bomb. 

I overstuffed myself with the shrimp cocktails and almost went green. Otherwise, the meat, fruits, gelato, desserts and seafood was fan-freaking-tastic. 

Best part about it all was that everything came out fresh and warm. No leftovers here! Services were fantastic with friendly and fast working servers. Wait and price is worth it in my opinion.
yelp:test:11141.para:
I indulged in the shrimp cocktails to the point of near sickness, but the rest of the meal was outstanding. The meat, fruits, ice cream, sweets, and seafood were all incredibly delicious. The highlight was that all the dishes were served hot and fresh, with no remnants left. The service was exceptional, with cheerful and efficient staff. In my view, the wait is justified by the price.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the same meaning, topic, sentiment, emotion, and intent as the original text, while using different wording and sentence structure. The length is also roughly the same.)

yelp:test:11143.orig:
All I can say is it's the best buffet in Vegas. 

The amount of options you have to choose from can't be beat. And the food is restaurant quality. Anything you try there you are guaranteed to like. 
The only thing I wish they worked on is the dessert. It was Ok...Some of it appeared sophisticated but most of it was nothing special. Of course I'm not comparing Wynn's desserts to Hometown Buffet...I'm only comparing it to other buffets on the strip. 
They should look into what's offered at Paris if they want to steal all their customers :)
yelp:test:11143.para: In my opinion, this buffet in Vegas is unparalleled. The variety of choices available is simply unmatched, and the food quality rivals that of a fine dining establishment. You can be certain that whatever you sample, you'll enjoy it. However, the dessert selection leaves room for improvement. While some dishes seemed refined, overall, they lacked a distinctive edge. I'm not putting Wynn's desserts on the same level, but rather comparing it to other buffet offerings on the strip. It might be beneficial for them to examine the dessert options at Paris to attract all their clientele.

yelp:test:11153.orig:
I can't say enough good things about the Wynn buffet. The food was amazing, the casino and the buffet are beautiful, and the service was excellent. After a ten dollar tip it ended up costing us about $40 per person for the whole thing, but it was well worth the price.

The thing that makes this buffet stand out in my eyes is their ability to work with people like us with food sensetivites and special dietary needs. I haven't bothered going to a buffet since I was diagnosed gluten (celiac) and dairy intolerant over two years ago. I am extremely sensetive to even the smallest amounts of gluten or dairy, so a buffet didn't seem like a good idea. After reading a few reviews on a few blogs my fiance and I decided to give it a shot, and boy are we glad we did!! The chef came out and gave us a tour of the whole buffet, showing us what was safe and what was not. They had a LOT of options for us including several deserts (which pretty much never happens), all of which were delicious!

We are already talking about our next trip to Vegas just so we can go to this buffet again!!
yelp:test:11153.para: The Wynn buffet has received numerous praises from me, with its delectable cuisine, stunning casino and buffet aesthetics, and top-notch service. Despite the initial $50 expense, which averages to $40 per person, the experience was undeniably worth it. What sets this buffet apart is their exceptional accommodation for guests with food sensitivities and specific dietary requirements. Having been diagnosed with gluten (celiac) and dairy intolerance, I had reservations about buffets. However, after perusing reviews and deciding to try it out, I'm thrilled we did. The chef personally guided us through the buffet, highlighting safe and unsafe options, and provided a plethora of choices, including a variety of desserts, all of which were scrumptious. We're already planning our next visit to Las Vegas just to relish this buffet experience again!

yelp:test:11171.orig: Trendy but LOUD! I went for a bachelorette party and they were very accommodating with a set menu but the food was below par considering the prices. The yellowtail sashimi and sliders were good but my main entree, chilean sea bass, was horrible. Overall, I wasn't impressed.
yelp:test:11171.para: Loud yet fashionable! I attended a bachelorette celebration where they provided a fixed menu, yet the food quality didn't match the cost. The yellowtail sashimi and mini burgers were enjoyable, but my primary dish, Chilean sea bass, was disappointing. In summary, I left feeling underwhelmed.

yelp:test:11177.orig: I'd fly back to Vegas just for the Truffle pasta. It was a pasta of the day, and what a glorious, glorious day that was. Er, two days (it was THAT good). I cant even remember anything else we ate (it was all delish) because we were in a heavenly like, orgasmic state. We might not have even talked the entire meal, other than about how great the pasta was. It's very likely at the top of my last meal on earth list. I love you, truffle pasta. You are the pasta of my life.
yelp:test:11177.para: I'd traverse back to Las Vegas solely for the Truffle pasta. It was a daily special, and what a magnificent, magnificent experience that was. Actually, it was two days (it was that exceptional). I can't recall any other dishes we consumed (they were all delightful) as we were in a euphoric, ecstatic state. We might not have engaged in conversation throughout the meal, except praising the pasta's excellence. It's almost certain to be at the pinnacle of my final dining list. Truffle pasta, you are the pasta that has graced my existence. I adore you.

yelp:test:11180.orig:
I've hit FIX every time I've visited Vegas. It's an absolutely perfect go-to spot when hitting the Bellagio for same gambling. I've always sat in the bar/lounge area which is super duper for people watching. How do cowboys take themselves seriously and why do dudes from LA all wear shirts with dragons eating birds eating butterflies? But I digress...

Kobe Cheese Fries are a must. Had the beef carpacio on last visit and was some of the best I've had. Lobster tacos were good.. but they're cold (on purpose). Was expecting warm. Crab cake sliders wash everything down nicely.

Waitresses are top notch, grade A, government certified talent. Oh, and they're pretty good at serving things, too.
yelp:test:11180.para: Every time I've been to Vegas and frequented the Bellagio for gambling, I've consistently chosen the bar/lounge area for its excellent people-watching vibe. I often ponder why cowboys maintain a sense of gravity and why LA men prefer shirts with dragons consuming birds and butterflies. Shifting gears, I must highlight the necessity of Kobe Cheese Fries. The beef carpacio I had on my last trip was exceptional, among the best I've tasted. Although the lobster tacos were satisfactory, they were intentionally served cold. The crab cake sliders effectively complemented the meal. The waitstaff deserves praise for their outstanding service, which is both government-certified and highly skilled.

yelp:test:11189.orig: Abuelo's is OK. There is nothing fantastic about it. I ordered the Juarez. I asked that the cheese enchilada be beef instead. I was told it would be no problem. That did not happen. It came out cheese. I sat at the bar.  The bartender was nice. Run of the mill service. If you come here just know you're walking into a run of the mill Mexican restaurant.
yelp:test:11189.para: The elderly man's establishment is satisfactory, lacking any exceptional qualities. I placed an order for the Juarez and requested a beef cheese enchilada. The assurance that this change would be feasible was not fulfilled, as the dish served was still with cheese. I chose to dine at the bar. The bartender provided a standard level of service. Visitors should be aware that they are entering a typical Mexican restaurant.

yelp:test:11202.orig: I've only gone to the Capital Grille for work-sponsored lunches and dinners so it's easier for me to rank it higher since cost isn't really an issue. If I had to pay for it myself, it would end up as a more special occasion or i-need-a-pick-me-up-lunch type of place. I really like the Capital Grille because even though the focus is on higher end meat and seafood, the vegetarian options are particularly good which is hard to come by at most restaurants in the same category. The Cobb salad (you can get vegetarian) is great because it's big, filling, and fresh. The veggie plate you can special order is a perfect entree, and though it's basically just a combination of all the side veggie dishes I think the sum is definitely greater than the parts. There are buttery roasted mushrooms covered in garlic & rosemary & thyme, grilled asparagus, sauteed spinach, and roasted tomatoes that add a wonderful sweetness and acidity to the dish.
yelp:test:11202.para: I've frequented the Capital Grille primarily for business-funded meals, making it easier for me to give it a higher rating as the expense isn't a concern. Had I been responsible for the costs, it might be perceived as a place for special events or a comforting lunch. I appreciate the Capital Grille for its focus on premium meat and seafood, but it also offers commendable vegetarian choices, which are rare in similar establishments. The Cobb salad, customizable to vegetarian preferences, stands out for its generous size, satisfying content, and freshness. The option to order a customized veggie plate serves as an excellent main course, with the collective taste of all the side vegetable dishes creating a sum that surpasses the individual components. The dish is enhanced by buttery roasted mushrooms with garlic, rosemary, and thyme, grilled asparagus, sautéed spinach, and roasted tomatoes, contributing a delightful balance of sweetness and acidity.

yelp:test:11223.orig:
I visited RA for the first time last week after a long day of shopping at Fashion Show and it was fantastic!  Got a whole array of different rolls to split amongst the group.  We kept it pretty simple with spicy tuna rolls, yellowtail and scallion rolls, philadelphia rolls and the crispy tuna rolls.  Delicious and super fresh fish!

Also, the sake bombs were really great here.  The prices were very reasonable and we even convinced the table next to us to join us in the fun.

The decor is clean and modern and the waitstaff is friendly and doesn't rush you to get out (even when's there's a line of people waiting).
yelp:test:11223.para: After a tiring day of shopping at Fashion Show, I had my first experience at RA last week, which turned out to be delightful! We shared a variety of rolls among us, including spicy tuna, yellowtail with scallion, Philadelphia, and crispy tuna rolls, all of which were incredibly tasty and fresh. Additionally, the sake bombs at this place were excellent. The pricing was quite affordable, and we managed to persuade the adjacent table to partake in our enjoyment. The ambiance is sleek and contemporary, and the service team is amiable and patient, even during busy periods.

yelp:test:11233.orig:
RA, ha ha ha ha ok enough laughing lets talk about the restaurant this location was terrible. Upon approaching the restaurant I noticed that there was hardly anyone inside. Came up to the front door and I noticed like hundreds of greasy finger prints on there glass doors, oh well so they dont like to clean there glass windows, no biggy. 

We got seated pretty quickly being that there were very little people there that night. Ordered viva las Vegas and spicy tuna and a California roll, all were pretty terrible. We also ordered garlic lemon edamame and it was pretty good but there is a pit where all the juice and chili garlic all falls into and then you're forced to fish them out with some chopsticks. 

The service was ok, the waitress really never came back after she took our order. Some other girl brought out our sushi instead and that was about it, the next time we seen our waitress was when she brought us our check. Would I come back? heck no, this place sucked all around reason for the laughter, oh well at least I got a good laugh out of it.
yelp:test:11233.para:
Laughter aside, let's discuss the dining experience at this establishment. As we arrived, the place was eerily empty. The front door's glass was covered in numerous greasy fingerprints, indicating a lack of cleanliness. 

We managed to get a table swiftly due to the low patronage that evening. We ordered Viva Las Vegas, spicy tuna, and a California roll, all of which were disappointingly subpar. The garlic lemon edamame was decent, but it had a problematic drainage issue where all the juice and chili garlic would collect, requiring us to use chopsticks to retrieve them. 

The service was average, with the waitress disappearing after taking our order. Another server delivered our sushi, and that was the extent of our interaction with the staff. Would I return to this place? Absolutely not, it was a poor experience in every aspect. Despite the humor derived from the situation, I wouldn't recommend it.

yelp:test:11240.orig:
If you ever come here you must sit outside and enjoy the poolside view, even if its a little hot, you wont reget it.

My boyfriend and I came for lunch after checking into encore. We ordered the organix mix salad, and beef sliders, truffle fries.
 The food was delicious. If you get the salad, there is no need to add meat, because honestly they dont give you that much for the extra price and the salad itself is savory. 

The sliders were good, typical sliders nothing really special about them, I guess you're better off ordering a burger for the same price as the sliders.

OMGOSH the truffle fries were SO GOOd!!! Definitely would order these again! There were freshly made a d had truffle sauce and cheese over it. So bad for you but ooooo so good.

Over all the prices seemed a little steep, but it is vegas so what do you expect. The serve was good, they seemed really busy but they were attentive.
yelp:test:11240.para:
Should you visit, it's essential to relax outdoors and relish the scenic poolside, despite the heat, as you won't regret it.

My partner and I decided to dine after settling in at encore. We opted for the organix mix salad, beef sliders, and truffle fries.
 The cuisine was scrumptious. If you choose the salad, there's no need for additional meat, as the price doesn't justify the extra and the salad is inherently tasty.

The sliders were satisfactory, nothing particularly unique, perhaps a burger would be a better choice for the same cost as the sliders.

WOW, the truffle fries were absolutely fantastic! I'd definitely order them again. They were freshly prepared with truffle sauce and cheese on top. They're not the healthiest, but they're incredibly delicious.

Overall, the prices were a bit high, but that's to be expected in Vegas. The service was commendable, even though they were quite busy, they remained attentive.

yelp:test:11258.orig: Disappointed that I paid nearly twice as much when I went here as compared to my local CVS.  I know it's close to Hard Rock so they are targeting tourists but had to call corporate and send in my receipt and the latest ad so they could credit me the over charge.  I'll drive a few miles to find a CVS that charges the same price as their other stores.
yelp:test:11258.para: Feeling let down for spending almost double at this location versus my nearby CVS. Aware that its proximity to Hard Rock draws tourists, I had to reach out to corporate, providing my receipt and the most recent advertisement to rectify the excess charge. I'll consider driving a short distance to a CVS with comparable pricing to their other outlets.

yelp:test:11264.orig: I wish I would've read the reviews. This place is over priced. The food is Dennys status. I will never come here again.
yelp:test:11264.para: Had I perused the customer feedback, I would've known this establishment was excessively costly. The culinary experience mirrors that of Dennys. I'm resolute in avoiding this venue in the future.

yelp:test:11269.orig:
I was starving on a Sunday night, and everything else at TI was closed.... so this place was my only option.

The night before, I had a carrot cake from here. It was alright, but I expected something better for a $7 carrot cake. The desserts at the Aria and Bellagio brunch buffet tasted much better than the carrot cake.

Anyways, I ordered a french onion soup and my boyfriend order a mango smoothie. It took half an hour for the soup to come out, and they still did not bring out the mango smoothie... My boyfriend asked to cancel the smoothie and the waiter said ""it is done, we are looking for a glass for it."" My boyfriend and I were confused.... is it that hard to get a glass? in a casino? where drinks are served EVERYWHERE?

one star for the french onion soup... it was okay, a little bit too salty though.
yelp:test:11269.para:
On a Sunday evening, I found myself extremely hungry, with TI being the only open establishment. Previously, I had tried their carrot cake, which was mediocre for its price, especially when compared to the desserts at the Aria and Bellagio brunch buffet.

Later, I opted for a french onion soup, while my partner chose a mango smoothie. It took around thirty minutes for the soup to arrive, and the smoothie was still not served despite the waiter's assurance that they were searching for a glass. This left us puzzled, considering the casino's policy of serving drinks everywhere.

Despite this, I gave the french onion soup one star, as it was acceptable but slightly overly salty.

yelp:test:11279.orig:
Extremely overrated and not impressive, at all. 

I went here for a business lunch and I arrived a bit early. The hostesses were very rude, rather than nicely say we're not open yet, they had an attitude that was like go the **** away. Not a good start. 

When I finally get in I head to the back where yes, they have a screen setup and a sound system. But the projector is being leveled by paper towels and was amateurish at best. And the room we were in needed paint. Seriously, when you take a look around the podium was chipped, the walls had chips, and I'm thinking for a place overlooking Las Vegas Blvd that the experience was downgraded. It may have been classy a while back, but the management team needs to consider investing in a little bit of paint. 

Then we get to the wobbly tables, and the family style food that was brought out. Family style might work in Italy but this is America, and to me family style is a masquerade for a kitchen that is too slow or chokes at cranking out high volume high quality plates. In this case about the only thing good was the Caesar salad as it's hard to muck up a Caesar salad. But the rest of the food? Truly unmemorable. If I was a tourist a
yelp:test:11279.para:
Extremely underwhelming and not commendable, in every way. 

I attended a corporate meal here and arrived slightly ahead of time. The waitstaff were exceptionally impolite, instead of politely informing us of the establishment's closure, they displayed a demeanor akin to leave immediately. This set a poor tone from the outset. 

Upon my entry, I proceeded to the rear where indeed, they had a display with a projector and audio setup. However, the projector was being improperly adjusted with paper towels, rendering it barely functional. Moreover, the venue itself was in dire need of a fresh coat of paint. Observing the podium and walls, which were marred with chips, it was evident that the experience was significantly diminished. It's plausible that this place once exuded class, but the management team should contemplate allocating funds for some much-needed aesthetic enhancement. 

Next, we encountered the unstable tables, and the communal dining style that was served. While this approach may be suitable in Italy, it doesn't quite fit in America. To me, this is merely a disguise for a kitchen that struggles to maintain a steady pace or to produce high-quality dishes in large quantities. In this instance, the only dish that stood out was the Caesar salad, as it's challenging to

yelp:test:11284.orig:
After a long and tiring day at Magic tradeshow, the team came here to feast! I was pretty hyped since it was my first time. The 5 of us ordered the classic family style which was I believe $35 a person. Not that cheap, but do-able.

Service was utterly non-existent. Food took forever inbetween servings, we're talking about 20-25 min inbetween each dish...even appetizers..

That's pretty damn bad. As you could expect, we got full just sitting there, so had so much food non taken advantage of.

Maggiano's...not a good way to treat the customers. 

If I come back..and that's a pretty strong IF, I would hope they actually serve our table.

Meh.

-Goodfood.LA
yelp:test:11284.para:
Following an exhausting day at the Magic trade event, our group arrived here to enjoy a meal. I was quite excited as it was my inaugural visit. The quintet opted for the traditional family-style meal, which I reckon cost around $35 per person. It wasn't cheap, but manageable.

The service was completely absent. The interval between dishes, including appetizers, was a staggering 20-25 minutes...quite disappointing.

This is quite unsatisfactory. Naturally, we were satiated just by being there, resulting in a lot of unused food.

Maggiano's...not an ideal way to cater to patrons. 

If I decide to return, which is a strong possibility, I would expect them to actually serve our table.

Overall, it was mediocre.

-Goodfood.LA

yelp:test:11300.orig: $30 for adults even though the sign outside says $21.99. This price also includes bottomless mimosas. The line is never long and you pay through a machine to get in.\n\nThe best items in the meat section were the prime rib, bacon, and bacon bits. The best desert item was carrot cake. Don't get anything red velvet-flavored. The best breakfast item was egg florentine that gushes with butter.
yelp:test:11300.para: Adults are charged $30 despite the $21.99 signage, which encompasses the cost of bottomless mimosas. The queue is consistently short, and payment is made via a kiosk for entry.\n\nIn the meat department, prime rib, bacon, and bacon bits stood out as top picks. Carrot cake was the preferred dessert choice, while steering clear of red velvet flavors. Egg florentine, rich in butter, was the standout breakfast option.

yelp:test:11305.orig:
I wanted to eat here because I have always heard the Rio had a great buffet...

I wish I had not wasted my time. 

I waited in line for about an hour just to pay, then another 10 minutes to be seated. 

They provided no way to crack the crab and I ended up hurting my fingers. The rest of the food tasted pretty much like cafeteria food. For 40 bucks a person, I feel is was entirely not worth it. Plus the Rio is really run down looking so I didn't even enjoy hanging around after eating.
yelp:test:11305.para:
I had hoped to dine here due to the reputation of their extensive buffet...

Regrettably, I feel I squandered my time. 

I spent roughly an hour queuing to settle the bill, followed by a brief wait of 10 minutes for a table. 

The absence of a crab-cracking tool resulted in finger injuries for me. The remaining dishes resembled typical cafeteria fare. Considering the price tag of $40 per individual, I believe the experience was entirely unjustified. Furthermore, the Rio's dilapidated appearance detracted from my post-meal leisure.

yelp:test:11308.orig: Okay I've been to a few buffets in Vegas and I never thought carnival would be one of the ones I would visit off the strip ??? It was good for the price and I tried most of the different selections and to my surprise it was all good !!! I would recommend a visit off the strip and come to Rio you'll be happy ;) and you'll save some cash $$$$$$$$
yelp:test:11308.para: I've explored several buffets in Las Vegas, never considering a carnival experience off the main boulevard. It turned out to be a great value, with a variety of choices that exceeded my expectations. I highly suggest venturing off the main strip and heading to Rio; not only will you be delighted, but you'll also benefit from some savings.

yelp:test:11351.orig: Ugh!  I thought maybe I should try this place again before I slam it on Yelp, but after reading some of the other one- and two-star reviews, I realize I'm not nuts.  And there is no way I'm going to wait for hours to give this place another chance.  If you want to wait in line for two hours and then receive a cup of grease along with your hash browns and eggs, then Matt's is the place for you.  Disgusting!  Not to mention the bathroom is next door in a hotel room.
yelp:test:11351.para: Oh no! I considered revisiting this spot before posting a negative review on Yelp, but after perusing some of the low-rated reviews, I've come to my senses. I won't be lining up for hours to give it another shot. If you're willing to endure a two-hour wait for a subpar meal, including greasy hash browns and eggs, then this place is for you. It's revolting, and the nearby bathroom, located in a hotel room, doesn't help.

yelp:test:11371.orig: i have eten at Sierra Bonita several times.  The food is ALWAYS consistent, and some of the best eating in Phoenix.  The atmosphere is amazing and service is always top notch.  SB has figured out how to be a great neighborhood restaurant with world class food.  The style is southwestern with Mexico City influences - truly amazing.
yelp:test:11371.para: I've dined multiple times at Sierra Bonita, where the cuisine maintains a consistent standard, and it stands out as one of the finest dining experiences in Phoenix. The ambiance is truly remarkable, complemented by impeccable service. Sierra Bonita has mastered the art of being an exceptional local eatery offering globally superior food. The culinary style blends Southwestern flavors with influences from Mexico City, creating an extraordinary dining experience.

yelp:test:11440.orig: I will not be back to this restaurant. I placed an order for pickup last Thursday for myself and a co-worker. I had the small jerk meal and my co-worker had a side of collard greens. The chicken was hard, dry and cold. It wasn't fresh.  It was pulled from the fridge and put in the microwave. The beans were hard and rice chewy. The collard greens were bland. Very disappointing. I will not be back.
yelp:test:11440.para: I won't be returning to this eatery. I ordered a takeout for myself and a colleague on the previous Thursday. I opted for a petite jerk dish, while my colleague chose collard greens. The chicken was tough, devoid of moisture and chilled. It lacked freshness, having been reheated in the microwave. The beans were tough and the rice was chewy. The collard greens were unremarkable. It was a truly unsatisfactory experience. I'll not be revisiting.

yelp:test:11451.orig: I used to come here all the time and I made sure I always made it here when I came to Las Vegas. However, on my most recent visit, the food was just not good. The pastas were bland and the crepes were only as good as one you can get at ihop. On a brighter note, the coq au vin was quite good as well as the prime rib. I probably won't come back as there are so many better buffet options here.
yelp:test:11451.para: I frequently visited this place in the past and ensured I always made it during my trips to Las Vegas. Regrettably, during my latest visit, the quality of the food disappointed me. The pasta dishes lacked flavor, and the crepes were mediocre, comparable to those at ihop. However, the coq au vin and prime rib were enjoyable. Given the plethora of superior buffet choices available, I'm unlikely to return.

yelp:test:11529.orig:
Yuck!  I can not believe this place has got some good reviews.  I was in Vegas 3 weeks ago, went to the Tao.  The alcohol in my stomach was feeling lonely so we went to Noodle Asia after leaving the club at around 12:30AM on a Saturday night.  On a busy night, I would imagine a full staff of waiters and cooks... Not this night, 2 waiters, 2 cooks and 1 hostess.  We had two couples ahead of us in line to be seated.  
Wait time for a table- 50 minutes.  
Time after ordering our food until it arrived to our table- 45 minutes.  
Time to eat-5 minutes flat.  
Time it took for the waiter to take to print out our check- 15 minutes.    
The soup I ordered tasted like dish wash water.  
Service-  abrupt/borderline rude

Next time, I'll skip this joint and opt for room service.
yelp:test:11529.para:
Disgusted! It's hard to accept that this establishment has positive feedback. I visited Las Vegas three weeks prior and decided to check out the Tao. Feeling the need for a drink, we headed to Noodle Asia after leaving the club at approximately 12:30AM on a Saturday. On a typically crowded night, I would expect a full team of servers and chefs... Not the case that night, with only 2 waiters, 2 cooks, and a single hostess. We were followed by two couples in line waiting to be seated. 

Waiting for a table took 50 minutes. 
The time from ordering our food to having it at our table was 45 minutes. 
We spent a mere 5 minutes eating. 
The waiter took 15 minutes to print out our bill. 
The soup I ordered tasted like cleaning solution. 
The service was abrupt and bordered on rudeness. 

In the future, I'll choose room service instead of dining here.

yelp:test:11535.orig:
I think the MSG has f*#ked with my head.  Six visits.  Why?

Being Asian, I'm insulted that the Venetian would attempt to placate me with this mediocre excuse for a Chinese restaurant sandwiched between the poker tourney area, sports book, and restroom hall.

KISS (Keep It Simple Stupid) review:

Fried rice:  extremely oily and packed with MSG.
Dim sum: nothing special except the price.  3x what you would pay in your local Chinatown.
Noodle soups: correctly made, loaded with MSG, very little toppings, expensive.
Wok tossed noodles: should be tossed out.  Extremely oily and salty from the MSG.

To add further insult, they charge you for every day quality tea.

We all know, too much oil = restroom.  Too much MSG = lots of water = restroom.  Not a smart way for a casino to do business.  But what do I know, I'm still in my MSG coma.
yelp:test:11535.para:
I believe the MSG has severely affected my brain. Six times I've been there. Why?

As an Asian person, I feel disrespected that the Venetian tried to appease me with this subpar excuse for a Chinese eatery located between the poker tournament zone, sports betting area, and restroom corridor.

KISS (Keep It Simple Stupid) critique:

Fried rice: excessively greasy and laden with MSG.
Dim sum: unremarkable except for its high cost, costing thrice as much as in your neighborhood Chinatown.
Noodle soups: well-prepared, but overly seasoned with MSG, sparse in toppings, and costly.
Wok tossed noodles: should be discarded due to its extreme oiliness and saltiness from the MSG.

To further aggravate the situation, they charge for everyday tea.

We all understand that excessive oil leads to the restroom, and excessive MSG results in increased water intake, leading to the restroom. It's not a wise business strategy for a casino. However, I'm still trapped in my MSG-induced stupor.

yelp:test:11546.orig: What an amazing display of inept service.  With some difficulty, we ordered glasses of prosecco to enjoy before dinner (The waiter did not offer to take drink orders or provide us with a by-the glass menu). The prosecco failed to arrive until well after our salads, which appeared almost instantaneously.  We had only taken a few bites of our salad, and sips of our prosecco, when the entrees arrived.  Rather than returning them to the kitchen, the waiter pressured us to relinquish our less than half-eaten salads. yelp:test:11546.para: An astonishing example of subpar hospitality unfolded. Despite some challenges, we managed to request glasses of prosecco for pre-dinner enjoyment, but the waiter neglected to offer drink orders or a by-the-glass menu. The prosecco's arrival lagged significantly behind our salads, which were served almost immediately. Having barely started our salad and prosecco, the arrival of the main courses prompted the waiter to insist we hand over our scarcely consumed salads. yelp:test:11556.orig:
only came here due to starvation after being on the road for 3 hour. also needed a decently nice and quick way (we were staying in Paris) to get some food in the system before the drinking in Vegas begins.

the good:
1. the first bite of my triple decker sandwich since i was starving. after a while it just tasted like any other club sandwich ive had. but i did think it was cool there was a sword toothpick to keep my sandwich together.
2. the waiter was always cheerful.
3. split checks

the average:
the french fries. they would have been much better if they were hot.

the bad:
1. there was line outside even though the restaurant was half full. this is as optimistic as i will be.
2. the service. had to flag down the waiter to order food. if you have us waiting out there im sure we'll be ready to order by the time we sit down. also took forever to get our food.
3. must ask for bread if you are ordering sandwiches/burgers. for the record the bread is ok. would have been better if they were warm.

yelp:test:11556.para:
Arrived here primarily due to hunger after a 3-hour journey, and sought a pleasant and efficient method to replenish our energy before indulging in Vegas's drinking scene, while staying in Paris.

Positive aspects:
1. The initial taste of my triple-layered sandwich was gratifying, despite it eventually resembling any other club sandwich I've experienced. The inclusion of a sword toothpick to maintain the sandwich's integrity was intriguing.
2. The waiter consistently maintained a cheerful demeanor.
3. The option to split checks was available.

Neutral aspects:
1. The French fries could have been superior if served hot.

Negative aspects:
1. Despite the restaurant being half-occupied, there was a queue outside, which was disappointing.
2. The service required us to signal the waiter for food orders, and the wait time for our meal was lengthy.
3. It's necessary to request bread when ordering sandwiches or burgers. The bread was acceptable, but would have been more enjoyable if it was warm.
4. The water had a distinctive "tappy" taste.
5. The waiter requested payment at the counter rather than personally delivering the checks.

yelp:test:11603.orig:

yelp:test:11603.para:
Extremely disappointing! I brought my manager and multiple clients to this place, and I was utterly disheartened. Here's some context: I've visited before and enjoyed it, but it's been about two years since my last visit.

yelp:test:11606.orig:
Boring... Perhaps this place is jumping at times other than when we visited but I was sorely under impressed with this place.

yelp:test:11606.para: This location may occasionally be lively, yet my visit left me thoroughly disappointed. The cuisine was mediocre, lacking any distinctive features. yelp:test:11610.orig: Use the coupon or else!\n Service was slow even in the low season of November ... I shutter to think how it would be in summer with the pool open and not half full of diners . \nI  have  had  better .

yelp:test:11639.orig:
Came here before goin to Lights in Mandalay Bay and utilized a $50 Restaurants.com gift certificale (Totally Worth it, because if we had to pay full price, this review would be a lot lower)

That being said, the food was fine, nothing really blew us a way. We tried the Burger, Fried Trufffle Mac and Cheese, the Filet Mignon and Foie Gras. All were standard and not really worth much hype.

We even got a free dessert which was nice, it was a chocolate pudding thing with passion fruit on top but the thing was, the passion fruit on top was DISGUSTING. Who thought it was a good idea to pair those two because it was TERRIBLE. They should just QUIT AND GO HOME. Because it was TERRIBLE.

That being said, the bread was good even though it cost AN ADDITIONAL CHARGE AND..BTW...TAKES 30-40 MINUTES TO COME OUT. We got the bread after we got our food. Who does that?

yelp:test:11639.para:
Prior to dining at Lights in Mandalay Bay, we made use of a $50 gift certificate from Restaurants.com (considerably beneficial, as the review would be much less favorable without it).

The meal itself was satisfactory, though nothing particularly stood out. We sampled the Burger, Fried Truffle Mac and Cheese, Filet Mignon, and Foie Gras, all of which were ordinary and lacked significant excitement.

We were pleasantly surprised by a complimentary dessert, a chocolate pudding with passion fruit topping. However, the passion fruit topping was revolting. The combination of these two flavors was a poor choice, and the overall experience was dreadful. They should consider abandoning this venture. The dessert was a letdown.

Despite the decent bread (which came with an extra charge and a long wait time of 30-40 minutes), our overall experience was not worth the anticipation. We're unlikely to return.

(Note: The paraphrase maintains the original sentiment, topic, emotion, and intent while altering the wording and sentence structure. The length is approximately the same as the original text.)

yelp:test:11667.para:
Stayed at the Red Rock and opted for BBQ to satisfy our hunger. The place was lively, but not overwhelmingly so. Our server was swamped, managing at least 7 tables, which might be typical, but she was overwhelmed. 
- Rating: 1 star for excessive noise
- 1 star for delayed beer service during our meal
- 1 star for the high noise level (very loud)
- 1 star for subpar food quality: the cole slaw was bland, the beans tasted like refried beans (I'd choose Mexican for that), and the ribs were slightly dry. The BBQ sauce was yellow, thin, and no extra was provided.

Save room for dessert, because they have table-side service. I highly recommend the bananas foster and cherries jubilee choices.   Yum, yum.

For those of you wanting more of  - WHATever-  try the private dining room, perfect for hosting 20-40 of your closest friends for a night on the town. That way considerate angels
