yelp:test:11975.orig: Nice machines, not too packed, and at $10 month? Yah, I'm a fan.
yelp:test:11975.para: Pleasant devices, not overly crowded, and priced at $10 per month? Absolutely, I appreciate them.

yelp:test:11992.orig:
Scale of 1-10 (multiple visits):
5 Food
4 Service
5 Atmosphere
4 Value

An uninspired menu w/ average barfood at best.  This place obviously doesn't serve anything that appears local, organic, original, creative, pretty, tasty, or cheap - and is more obviously just making its money by forcing itself upon a captive airport audience with no other choices.  Come on, you have to offer at least ONE of those things!  Boring boring boring place.

But that doesn't mean the service is bad, right?  Well, when I order a bottled beer and the server doesn't tell me that it's a 20 oz bottle, I'm calling bullshit.  So I see this 20 oz bottle come to me and I just sit in confusion for a moment.  I recheck the menu, recheck the label: yup, no way I would have known (not even any prices on the alcohol).  Obviously a scam to try and get people to overbuy.  So i send it back.  ""would you like anything else instead?  we have it on draft too.""  no thanks; you'll probably give it to me in a two-gallon boot and then charge me $25 for it.  So i got my food and got the hell out of here.
yelp:test:11992.para:
Rating scale: 1-10 (multiple visits):
5 - Food
4 - Service
5 - Atmosphere
4 - Value

The menu lacks creativity and originality, offering only mediocre bar food. It's clear that the establishment doesn't prioritize local, organic, or unique offerings, instead relying on its location near an airport to attract customers with limited alternatives. It's disappointing and uninspiring. However, the service isn't entirely negative. For instance, when I ordered a bottled beer and the server failed to inform me of its size, I felt misled. Upon receiving the bottle, I was momentarily puzzled. I verified the menu and the label, confirming that I wouldn't have known the size or price of the alcohol. It seemed like a tactic to encourage excessive purchasing. Consequently, I returned the beer. The server offered an alternative, but I declined, suspecting an exorbitant price tag. I left after receiving my meal.

yelp:test:12023.orig: You can get better food at Denny's. And I don't even really like Denny's much.\n\nOnly good part of this buffet is the omlet guy. He's fun to watch, and the omlets are good.
yelp:test:12023.para: At Denny's, you might find superior culinary options. However, my fondness for Denny's isn't particularly strong.\n\nThe sole positive aspect of this buffet is the egg chef. His entertaining demeanor and the quality of his omelets stand out.

yelp:test:12029.para: The NY NY hotel's website claimed the buffet was located at their establishment. yelp:test:12085.orig:
What do you mean Social House is closed?!

That was my favorite sushi restaurant in Vegas! The food was great, the service was superb, the restaurant looks great and you can get a killer view of the Pirate show outside TI off the balcony. 

Where are you going Social House?! Please re-open before I head out in mid October!
yelp:test:12085.para:
Why is Social House shut down?

I adored this sushi spot in Las Vegas! The cuisine was excellent, the service impeccable, the ambiance stunning, and it offered an amazing vantage point to watch the Pirate show from the terrace of TI. 

Could you please reopen Social House? I'm planning to visit in the middle of October!

yelp:test:12096.orig:
Don't go here! Overpriced, overrated, and bad service. 

Environment:
I thought the cafe would be a nice dining experience overlooking the pools, but the tables are so close you might as well have a convo with your neighbor. Noisy! We had Debbie Downer for our waitress who never smiled and saw her only three times: once to take our order, another time to deliver food, and a final time to deliver the check. Um, can we get refills? She even messed up on the drink order: coffee. How do you forget coffee during brunch? 

Food:
I ordered lox and a bagel. Can't screw that up, but I will say that the bagel was small and they only gave my three rings of onion - not even a full slice of an onion! That lox and bagel was NOT worth $15. The cream cheese portion was not much...maybe a tablespoon. The tomato slice was a regular beef steak, not vine ripened and the tomato was pill-y. However, the lox was good. My bro ordered the corned beef hash which was good and meaty, and the hash browns were tasty and crunchy. Our meal came close to $70...for breakfast. 

Why two stars?
The service is bad as is the food. Avoid this place and hit the buffet or eat at another hotel. Definitely overpric
yelp:test:12096.para:
Avoid this location! It's costly, overhyped, and offers poor service. 

Atmosphere:
I anticipated a pleasant dining experience with a view of the pools, but the proximity of the tables made it feel like a bustling hallway. The noise level was high. Our server, Debbie Downer, was unenthusiastic, only interacting with us thrice: once for our order, once for food delivery, and once for the bill. Could we have some more refills? She also got our drink order wrong: coffee. Forgetfulness during brunch is unacceptable. 

Cuisine:
I chose lox and a bagel, which are simple dishes to get wrong. The bagel was disappointingly small, and we were only given three onion rings - not even a full slice. The lox was decent, but the cream cheese portion was negligible, perhaps just a tablespoon. The tomato slice was more like a regular beef steak, not a fresh vine-ripened tomato, and it was dry. However, the lox was satisfactory. My brother enjoyed the corned beef hash, which was hearty and flavorful, and the hash browns were delicious and crispy. Our breakfast bill nearly reached $70. 

Why two stars?
The service and food quality are subpar. It's best to

yelp:test:12102.orig:
Second time eating here in the span of 10 years and NOTHING has changed. Food once again is CRAP and service is terrible. Paid $22 for an Ahi tuna salad. Ahi looked bad. The color is one of that which fish should never be, a nice greyish tinge rather than bright red/purple. Served on a beautiful bed of shredded iceberg lettuce. What? Too cheap to buy mixed greens Bellagio? 7 very small pieces of Ahi was served on this ""salad"" so my friend and I each got a whopping 3.5. 

We also split the lobster mac & cheese which was served with a spinach salad that was simple, but decent with spinach, heirloom tomatoes, and a pesto dressing on the side. The lobster mac & cheese was certainly missing the main protein. It should have been called thick bacon/ham mac & cheese. There was hardly any lobster. We had to ask our server for our bread basket after our entrees came out 40 minutes later. A quick lunch ended up taking almost 2 hours. Even when the place emptied out, our server was still slow. 

This place is understaffed and the food is garbage. Definitely a tourist trap since it is located in the gardens & nobody will care about this review when they are starving and don't know where
yelp:test:12102.para:
After dining here twice within a decade, I've noticed no improvements. The quality of the food remains subpar, and the service is consistently poor. I paid $22 for an Ahi tuna salad, which appeared unappealing with a dull greyish hue instead of a vibrant red/purple. Served on a bed of shredded iceberg lettuce, it seemed like a cost-cutting measure to use mixed greens. We received only 7 small pieces of Ahi, resulting in each of us getting a mere 3.5. 

We also shared the lobster mac & cheese, which came with a simple spinach salad featuring spinach, heirloom tomatoes, and a pesto dressing. However, the dish lacked the expected lobster flavor, almost resembling a thick bacon/ham mac & cheese. Our bread basket request took 40 minutes after our meals, making our quick lunch stretch into almost two hours. Even as the venue cleared out, our server's pace didn't pick up. 

This establishment is severely understaffed, and the food quality is disappointing. It's a typical tourist trap, situated in the gardens, and this review may not be given much attention when people are hungry and unaware.

yelp:test:12108.orig: ok first of all... lets just start out by saying I am from LA... and lucky for me we have Chinatown and the entire San Gabriel Valley a.k.a. China! Now maybe Vegas just doesn't have too many authentic chinese restaurants but damn this was the worst dim sum I have ever had in my life! My friend took me there 2 weeks ago and well the name kinda threw me off to begin with but once I tried the shu mai... damn it was over! I didnt want to try anything else. The simplest dim sum and yet they couldnt even get it right. The beefballs were too overcooked too!  Even the tiny little pork buns were to run from. How does this place stay in business? But then again maybe they are catering to a different crowd. What really struck me as weird was the fact the place was full of asians! I mean, is this suppose to be as good as it gets in Vegas for dim sum? If so, I'd rather stop by a trader joes and pick up a pack of frozen shu mais. You will have much better luck going to the frozen food aisle at a supermarket for good dim sum. Oh one more thing.. horrible service. The employees are literally fresh off the boat! I guess thats the only thing authentic about this place, their workers! hahahaha Trust
yelp:test:12108.para: Starting with the fact that I hail from LA, where we're fortunate to have Chinatown and the San Gabriel Valley, also known as China! While it's possible that Vegas lacks numerous genuine Chinese eateries, I must express my utter disappointment with the dim sum I experienced there. My companion introduced me to this place two weeks prior, and the name initially confused me. However, the shu mai left me utterly dissatisfied, to the point where I didn't feel inclined to sample anything else. The simplest dim sum dish was executed poorly. The beefballs were excessively cooked, and even the petite pork buns were unappealing. It's puzzling how this establishment remains operational. Perhaps it's targeting a different demographic. The unusual sight of a predominantly Asian clientele also raised questions. If this is the pinnacle of dim sum in Vegas, I'd rather opt for a pack of frozen shu mai from Trader Joe's or a supermarket's frozen food section for superior quality. The service was also subpar, with staff seemingly just out of the boat. Ironically, the only authentic aspect of this place might be its employees. Haha, I trust you understand.

yelp:test:12113.orig:
This is the best dim sum in Las Vegas. 

1. Open kitchen. I like to watch people cook and check if they are sanitary. They're doing it right back there. Clean for a Chinese restaurant. 

2. The cart ladies can speak English. They don't just dump the dishes in my table when I point and ask, ""what is it?""

3. Food is fresh. They don't give me old food that's been around and rejected by other people. If I want the new batch, they'll give me just that. 

4. Rice is not free. Blahhh. I love rice. They come in a little portion bowl thingy. Their prices are typical for dim sum though. 

5. Food is not as great as LA dim sum, but it still has all of the items I want from a dim sum. 

I recommend you try.
yelp:test:12113.para:
Las Vegas boasts the finest dim sum experience. 

1. A transparent cooking area pleases me, as I observe hygiene practices and affirm their adherence to cleanliness standards. It's commendable for a Chinese eatery. 

2. The serving ladies are multilingual, ensuring I understand the dishes I'm inquiring about, rather than simply piling them on my table. 

3. Freshness is a priority here; I'm not served stale food that others have passed over. They're quick to provide the latest batch upon request. 

4. The rice comes in a small portioned bowl, and while I appreciate it, I find the pricing to be standard for dim sum fare. 

5. Although it may not match the quality of LA's dim sum, it still offers all the desired items. I highly suggest giving it a try.

yelp:test:12157.orig:
Talk about a special occasion.  At deseos prices, we won't be back unless we win the lottery.
The food and service were excellent. Another plus? When so many other restaurants have tv's to distract you, you won't find any distractions here.
We were recommended to try the shrimp chicharonnes. It was a textural wonderland. Crunchy sweet, but creamy spice with slivered jalapeños. 
Both my wife and I had the sea bass (not Chilean btw). Mine came with 2 large delicately cooked filets, skin on, and buttery delicious. 
We rounded out the meal with the cigar desert and it lived up to its status.

We left feeling extremely full and satisfied. This was definitely a splurge for us, as it is not amenable on a middle class budget to eat here regularly. But service, food, and ambiance was worth it for a special occasion.
yelp:test:12157.para:
Discussing an extraordinary event. At Deseos' affordable rates, we'll only return if we hit the jackpot.
The cuisine and customer service were top-notch. An additional advantage? Unlike other dining spots with TVs to divert attention, there are no such diversions here.
We were advised to sample the shrimp chicharonnes, which was a delightful mix of textures. Crispy sweetness, creamy heat, and finely chopped jalapeños. 
Both my spouse and I enjoyed the sea bass (not from Chile). My portion featured two large, tenderly prepared filets with skin, and it was utterly indulgent. 
We concluded our dining experience with the cigar dessert, which met its lofty expectations. 

We departed feeling incredibly satiated and content. This was a luxury for us, as it's not feasible on a typical budget to dine here often. However, the quality of service, food, and atmosphere was justified for a one-time event.

yelp:test:12164.orig: Excellent. Good staff, really welcoming and friendly. We had an awesome experience here. Drinks were fairly priced and poured. The piano players were quite good. Could not give it 5 stars because that is reserved for NY NY Piano Bar in Las Vegas and Andy's Pub (Piano Bar) in Oslo.
yelp:test:12164.para: Outstanding. The team was exceptionally welcoming and amiable. Our enjoyable time here was well-deserved. The drinks were reasonably priced and served well. The piano performers were impressive. However, we refrained from awarding a perfect 5 stars, as that distinction is held by NY NY Piano Bar in Las Vegas and Andy's Pub (Piano Bar) in Oslo.

yelp:test:12165.orig: I love the entertainment here and the drinks are always ice cold! This is a great place to take some coworkers and friends!\nBruce was very accommodating for special events!
yelp:test:12165.para: The enjoyment I find in this venue's entertainment and the perpetually chilled beverages make it an excellent spot for gathering with colleagues and pals. Bruce proved to be exceptionally welcoming and helpful during special occasions!

yelp:test:12166.orig:
The only reason I'm giving this place two stars is because our server did a really nice job.  

The food here is seriously overpriced and not very good in my opinion.  My pulled pork sandwich was $14.50 if I recall correctly.  

You can do much, much better.  I don't know whether BLT Burger (in the Mirage) has pulled pork sandwiches, but they do have killer gourmet hamburgers, and they don't cost $14.50.  Also, the service at BLT is very professional.  Pricing there (BLT) is a bargain given the quality of the food, the quality of the service, and the location.  

Do yourself a favor.  Skip Gilley's at TI and walk next door to the Mirage and have a much nicer dining experience for less money at BLT.
yelp:test:12166.para:
I'm rating this establishment two stars mainly due to the commendable service provided by our server.  

The cuisine here is excessively costly and falls short of my expectations.  I remember spending around $14.50 for a pulled pork sandwich.  

There's a significant room for improvement.  While I'm uncertain if the Mirage's BLT Burger offers pulled pork sandwiches, they certainly excel in delivering high-quality gourmet burgers at a more reasonable price. Moreover, the professionalism of the service at BLT is noteworthy. Considering the superior food quality, service, and prime location, the pricing at BLT is a smart deal.  

For a better dining experience at a lower cost, I recommend bypassing Gilley's at TI and opting for the Mirage's BLT instead.

yelp:test:12179.orig: I was there last week with some friends for happy hour. They have margaritas $1 off and 1/2 price appetizers. The blueberry margarita was delicious!
yelp:test:12179.para: Last week, I joined a group of pals for a convivial gathering where they offered margaritas at a discounted rate of $1 off and appetizers at half price. The blueberry margarita was exceptionally tasty!

yelp:test:12189.orig:
Eh.  I'm sorry Jim Gould's, I think you've changed and not for the better. 

Went for our anniversary dinner last night, and despite having a loud and obnoxious group of drunk out-of-town conference attendees trying to impress one another with their wit and cleavage seated right next to us, figured that the food, wine, and service would compensate.  It didn't.  At half-price, the glass of shiraz I had was overpriced, and slightly chilled. My kobe beef burger was bland and not particularly tender.  The brie on top was flavorless. So, neither the dish nor the price were ""special"".

yelp:test:12189.para:
I apologize, Jim Gould's, I believe you've evolved in a negative direction. 

We had our anniversary dinner last evening, amidst a boisterous and obnoxious crowd of inebriated conference guests from out of town, attempting to showcase their intellect and attractiveness next to us. I anticipated that the quality of the food, wine, and service would make up for it. Unfortunately, it didn't. The half-price shiraz I drank was still overpriced and slightly cool. The kobe beef burger I ordered was unremarkable and lacked tenderness. The brie on top was tasteless. The pommes frites were decent, but I'm certain they weren't "truffle oil infused" as advertised. Nevertheless, I'm glad about the pommes frites. My husband's beef medallion, which was supposed to be a "special", was minuscule and overdone. It was also listed on the standard menu at the price we paid, so it wasn't really a "special". 

This leads me to the peculiar service: when we commented on the unusual "one dollar wine shot" feature (really? a wine shot? served in a shot glass?), the waiter responded, "yes, well, we're trying to compete with KoFusions' $1 sushi. They're really busy over

yelp:test:12238.orig: Don't waste your money! My wife and I have always eaten there when visiting Vegas, but the price has gone way up and the food quality and selection way down. We arrived at 8pm on a Saturday night ... no line at all to get in, and the seating was only half full. That told us something right away. We went to Caesars Bacchanal buffet two nights later and it was absolutely unbelievable. I could spend a whole week just trying all the selections available, and the food quality is top notch. The price was only $2.00/ea more than the Village Seafood Buffet, and there is no comparison. Go to Bacchanal, wait 20 - 30 minutes in line, then enter heaven. We won't be back to the Village Seafood Buffet --- ever!
yelp:test:12238.para: Avoid spending your cash! My spouse and I frequently dined at this place during our trips to Las Vegas, but the cost has significantly increased while the food quality and variety have decreased. On a Saturday evening at 8pm, we found no queue to enter and only half the seats were occupied, indicating a potential issue. Two nights later, we tried Caesars Bacchanal buffet and it was astonishingly impressive. I could dedicate a week to sampling all the offerings, and the food quality is exceptional. The price is just $2.00 more per person than the Village Seafood Buffet, making it unbeatable. We'll never return to the Village Seafood Buffet again.

yelp:test:12254.orig: This place tries to be like the old Mick's chain in Atlanta - an Applebee's or Ruby Tuesday, but with fresh food, executed well. Unfortunately, the food's just not that good. The Italian meatloaf isn't awful, but it's nothing to write home about. The apps were decent, but not great. My GF loves their black bean burger, though (and it IS pretty good for a non-meat burger). It's a good place to watch a game,but not as a dining destination.
yelp:test:12254.para: This establishment aims to emulate the vibe of the former Mick's in Atlanta, akin to Applebee's or Ruby Tuesday, but with a twist of fresh cuisine. Regrettably, the culinary offerings fall short of excellence. The Italian meatloaf is passable, yet it lacks distinction. The appetizers are satisfactory but not outstanding. My partner enjoys their black bean burger, which is commendable for a vegetarian option. It serves as an ideal spot for game viewing, but it doesn't quite measure up as a prime dining spot.

yelp:test:12264.orig: Simple, Neopolitan-style pizza cooked to order in their brick oven. The crust is excellent, thin and soft.\n\nThey have an espresso machine, and if you like cappucino be sure to order one after you eat. It was one of the best i've ever had.
yelp:test:12264.para: Neapolitan-inspired pizza, prepared fresh in their brick oven, boasts a superbly thin and tender crust. They also offer an espresso machine, and for those who enjoy cappuccino, it's highly recommended to request one post-meal. This particular cappuccino was among the finest I've tasted.

yelp:test:12307.orig:
I was eating solo this night and was starving when I was perusing the Caesars mall. I decided to go for a known quantity since I have known CF for years. I ate at the bar and had my usual soda and small chopped salad and bread. It came out to $15 bucks with tip. That's CHEAP by Vegas standards. The small salads are a good deal b/c CF gives you a huge amount of food in the main entrees and so these are just the right generous portion and most hotel rooms have no place to refrigerate or heat up your doggy bag anyways.

Bar staff was great. I think it was Tim that helped me. Always made sure to keep my glass filled. Kudos to him and he's cute to boot.

Verdict: Okay so CF is a chain that is everywhere nowadays, but it's nice to find someplace that is a known quantity, fed me in less than an hour, and isn't charging 50% more than their normal outlets and has a nice bar staff.
yelp:test:12307.para: While dining alone at night and feeling famished, I found myself at the Caesars mall. Given my familiarity with CF for a long time, I opted for a familiar choice. I enjoyed a soda, a modestly sized chopped salad, and bread at the bar, which totaled $15, including tip. This price is quite reasonable compared to Vegas norms. The small salads are a smart pick as CF's main dishes are generous, making these portions just right. Plus, most hotel rooms lack facilities for refrigerating or warming your takeout. The bar team was commendable, with Tim being particularly attentive, ensuring my glass was always full. He's also quite appealing. In summary, CF, a widely recognized chain, offers a reliable dining experience. It served me quickly, without the steep price tag typical of other establishments, and boasts a friendly bar staff.

yelp:test:12321.para: It was incredibly annoying!!!! I had hoped to enjoy this location. The menu items appeared appealing. Upon entering, the ambiance was warm and luxurious. yelp:test:12358.orig: I don't get it. I ordered the chicken and waffles like everyone recommended but it was very tasteless and over cooked. Maybe I'll try it again. Just don't see it though. It was large enough for 2 people however. Maybe 3 since non of us cared for it.
yelp:test:12358.para: I'm puzzled. I followed the advice and chose chicken and waffles, but it lacked flavor and was excessively cooked. Perhaps I'll give it another shot. However, it wasn't appealing, even though it was ample for two, potentially three, as no one enjoyed it.

yelp:test:12360.para: Impressive size with substantial serving dishes!

yelp:test:12367.orig:
Came here on a Sunday afternoon. The place was packed and had to wait 10mins for a table. 
The waitress seemed a bit stressed (due to possible understaffing) and barely got a moment of her time. I had ordered the blt bloody Mary, nothing too special and a bit spicy for my taste. The slice of bread that comes with it - awesome idea...if there were a few more slices of bacon to go with it! 
I had ordered the fried chicken Benedict, my friend ordered the salmon scramble(I think). She had feared, after ordering, that what she'd ordered wouldn't be what's expected. As soon as the food came(ca. 15mins later), it wasn't what she'd expected and sent it back. Around 5mins. Later, her replacement meal was served. The kitchen was definitely on top of their game that day! 
I enjoyed my benedict, buuuut there was just a little too much chipotle for my taste.
yelp:test:12367.para: Arrived on a Sunday afternoon and found the venue crowded, resulting in a 10-minute wait for a table. The waitress appeared somewhat overwhelmed, likely due to a shortage of staff, and struggled to provide adequate attention. I opted for the blt bloody Mary, which was unremarkable and slightly too spicy for my preference. The accompanying bread slice was a clever addition, but it would have been better with additional bacon slices. \nMy friend chose the fried chicken Benedict, while I had the salmon scramble (I believe). She was apprehensive about her order, fearing it wouldn't meet expectations. When the food arrived approximately 15 minutes later, it didn't match her expectations, prompting her to send it back after about 5 minutes. Her substitute meal was promptly delivered later that day, showcasing the kitchen's exceptional performance. I appreciated my benedict, though the chipotle flavor was a bit overpowering for my liking.

yelp:test:12387.orig: celebrated our 30th wedding anniversary there-BIG mistake-the view was really the only good part.  Food was fair, prices outrageous, and overall, a very uneventful experience.  Told the manager, who offered to buy us a drink at the lounge-no thanks-couldn't wait to leave.
yelp:test:12387.para: Marked our 30th marriage milestone at that location, but it turned out to be a regrettable choice as the scenery was the sole positive aspect. The cuisine was mediocre, the costs exorbitant, and the entire visit was rather dull. We communicated our dissatisfaction to the staff, who suggested a complimentary beverage in the lounge, which we politely declined. Eager to depart.

yelp:test:12439.orig:
Hello all you foodies out there :)

Today I will give you our opinion of JOES BBQ.

And I do realize food is a preference and I am a very picky person.

I realize Joes has its local following, however from a girl who has tried many of the BBQ joynts here in the greater Phoenix area I have to say.... I DONT GET IT?

I was being fair in trying Joes twice.....just to make sure it wasent an off day.

We first went to Joes pick up window a few weeks ago and tried a slab of ribs and a combo plate with chicken, ribs and some bbq beef and bbq pork.

I enjoy some good ""fall off the bone"" ribs but what I got was a slab of ""pry off the bone"" ribs.

I must say the bbq sauce was ok but the meat was tough and chewy and I was extremely dissapointed.

On the combo place the chicken was dry as were the meats.

I would like to compliment the MAC and CHEESE which is better than most and the BBQ BEANS were also tasty.

I called  Joes to ask if I could bring back the ribs, of which I ate 2 bones, and get our money back and I was transfered to a very friendly manager who talked me into letting her send us a gift card so we can try again.

She insisted their ribs are normall
yelp:test:12439.para:
Greetings to all culinary enthusiasts:)

Today, we're sharing our perspective on JOES BBQ.

I acknowledge that taste is subjective and I'm known for my selective palate.

Despite Joes' local fan base, as a woman who has sampled numerous BBQ establishments in the Phoenix region, I must confess I'm puzzled.

I made an effort to visit Joes twice, ensuring it wasn't a bad day.

Our first visit was to Joes' pickup window a few weeks back, where we sampled a rib slab and a combo plate featuring chicken, ribs, and BBQ beef and pork.

I appreciate tender "fall off the bone" ribs, but what I received was a "pry off the bone" rib slab.

The BBQ sauce was passable, but the meat was tough and chewy, leaving me quite disillusioned.

The chicken and meats on the combo plate were equally dry.

I'd like to commend the MAC and CHEESE, which surpasses most, and the BBQ BEANS, which were enjoyable.

I reached out to Joes to request a refund for the ribs I consumed, but was instead directed to a very amiable manager.
\

yelp:test:12443.orig: Prices are a bit high but the food is great and the shows are fun!
yelp:test:12443.para: The cost is somewhat elevated, yet the quality of the cuisine is excellent and the entertainment is enjoyable!

yelp:test:12462.orig: I ate at the restaurant but the selection was a little disappointing and tasted pretty generic. Beer was excellent though.
yelp:test:12462.para: The restaurant's menu left me somewhat underwhelmed in terms of variety and flavor, but the beer selection was truly impressive.

yelp:test:12475.orig:
Having always been fascinated with human anatomy, I did toy with the idea of being a neurosurgeon.  My decision against pursuing that idea has and will continue to save(d) countless human lives (and pain and suffering caused by ensuing lawsuits and / or legal proceedings).  

Nonetheless, the subject never ceases to amaze me.  Which is why when BODIES... The Exhibition made its way to Silicon Valley, I was looking forward to perusing a variety of polymer-preserved body parts whilst recalling the materials from the Human Anatomy class that I took during my freshman year.

Allow two hours to go through the various sections (no pun intended) of the exhibition: skeletal, muscular, respiratory, circulatory, and nervous system.  Allow extra time in the circulatory system section - see what you would have looked like you are stripped off everything else but your heart, veins and arteries.  Look at what a blackened pair of lungs look like and wish that you had stuck to that new year's resolution of yours. yelp:test:12475.para:
My lifelong interest in human anatomy led me to consider a career as a neurosurgeon. However, choosing not to follow that path has consistently protected numerous individuals from the distress and legal complications that could arise. 

Despite this, the intricacies of the human body continue to captivate me. This fascination prompted my eagerness to explore a range of synthetic body components at the BODIES... The Exhibition in Silicon Valley, reminiscing about the anatomy lessons from my freshman year. 

Allocate about two hours to explore the different areas of the exhibition, including skeletal, muscular, respiratory, circulatory, and nervous system sections. Spend additional time in the circulatory system area to appreciate the heart, veins, and arteries as if they were the only elements remaining. Observe the darkened lungs and reflect on your commitment to your new year's resolution. Feel the donated organs (a heart and a liver) that are presented for public viewing, noting their somewhat artificial plastic-like texture - a humorous reference for those in the know.

yelp:test:12506.orig:
I hate this bar and grill.  Seriously.

We had some friends in town that had enjoyed Toby Keith's a few years ago and wanted to go back.  So we made the stop at Harrah's on a late Sunday afternoon.  On the way to the casino, I called ahead to make reservations.  You can't.  So I asked how busy they were, expecting the girl on the other end of the phone to tell me there would be a wait.  Instead, I was told ""We are the opposite of busy.""  Things weren't looking good already.

We were immediately seated and I enjoyed the feel of the place.  I'm not into country music but I don't mind it playing in the background.  It's pretty much an Applebee's or TGI Fridays feel, except with a country theme.  But you can only enjoy the scenery for so long....

We waited, and waited, and waited.  It took at least 15 minutes before our server even came over to greet us and get our drink orders.  Someone in my group wanted one of the specialty mixed drinks that are listed on the back of the menu (the ones that come in mason jars - 19 flipping dollars).  When my friend asked how much a 16-ounce version of the drink would be, she was told it was $12 but it would only come with a half a shot in
yelp:test:12506.para:
I strongly dislike this establishment that combines dining and gambling.  Truly.

Our acquaintances, who previously frequented Toby Keith's, desired to revisit.  Consequently, we decided to stop by Harrah's on a quiet Sunday afternoon.  Prior to our arrival, I attempted to secure a reservation but was informed that it was not possible.  I anticipated the representative to inform me of a potential wait time, but instead, I was told "We are not busy at all."  The situation seemed to be deteriorating from the start.

We were quickly seated, and I found the ambiance agreeable.  Although I don't typically appreciate country music, I don't object to it playing softly in the background.  The atmosphere resembled that of Applebee's or TGI Fridays, but with a distinct country twist.  However, the enjoyment of the surroundings was limited.

We experienced prolonged waiting times.  It took no less than 15 minutes for our server to approach and take our drink orders.  One of our companions wished to order a specialty mixed drink, which is featured on the menu's back (those served in mason jars - priced at $19).  When asked about the cost of a 16-ounce version, the server informed us it would be $12, but it would only include half a shot.

yelp:test:12507.orig: I love a good country song but I do not love this bar and grill.  The prices are very high for the portions you get.  Everything I have tried has been bland and overcooked.  The restaurant makes the big mistake made by many similar chains.  It tries to do too much.  There are far too many items on this menu for the staff to be able to get them all right. The real Toby Keith's in OK have smaller menus and better quality.  This is the PBR tourist trap and has almost no character.    Many better choices in town.
yelp:test:12507.para:
I have a fondness for heartfelt country tunes, yet this bar and grill fails to impress me. The cost is exorbitant relative to the portion sizes. The dishes I've sampled lack flavor and have been excessively cooked. This establishment falls into the common error of attempting to offer too much. The extensive menu hampers the staff's ability to deliver quality service. In contrast, the authentic Toby Keith's in OK boast more concise menus and superior dishes. This establishment is akin to a tourist trap, devoid of distinctive charm. There are numerous superior dining options within the city.

The Sriracha Beef came with an egg roll (that I ate) and fried rice that the wife substituted with white rice.  I'm a good sized guy and I did not finish my beef panang and rice.  A nice sized portion, and it tasted great.  On a 1-10 for spicy, I ordered an 8.  Yummmm.  The wife enjoyed the Sriracha Beef, a spicy dish with veggies and cooked in Sriracha chiles.  She could not finish her portions.  The service was brisk.  They gave a free refill on the Thai iced tea!  Two people ate for about $15.50.  A very good value, tasty food, and prompt service.
yelp:test:12538.para: During lunch with my spouse, I opted for beef panang with rice priced at $5.95, while she chose Sriracha Beef for $6.50. The Sriracha Beef was accompanied by an egg roll, which I consumed, and white rice instead of fried rice. As a larger individual, I didn't manage to finish my beef panang and rice, but the portion was generous and the flavor was excellent. I rated the spiciness level at 8 out of 10. The dish was delicious, and I expressed my approval with a hearty "Yummmm." My spouse also enjoyed the Sriracha Beef, a spicy dish with vegetables and cooked in Sriracha chiles, but she couldn't finish her share. The service was efficient, and we were offered a complimentary refill of Thai iced tea. The total cost for both of us was approximately $15.50, which we considered a great deal for the tasty food and quick service.

yelp:test:12595.orig:
As far as contemporary fine dining goes, Eleven sticks with the Big Burrito formula pretty closely. Nothing they serve is entirely challenging but for a lot of Pittsburghers, it probably appears that way.

Either way, there's no way to argue about the quality of the food. The ingredients are seasonal and local and the cooking is inspired. Eleven is probably the most upscale of the Big Burrito restaurants but the stuffiness that comes with that atmosphere is wholly missing.

I love being able to order food off a restaurant's menu and recognizing the name of the farms that supply their proteins.

The service at Eleven is exceptional and the food is great. A lot of people seem to have a problem with Big Burrito but I think they are wholly responsible for a lot of the fine dining scene in Pittsburgh. Mad Mex, as laid back and casual as it is, is a great way to introduce your palette to flavors that will lead you to bigger and much more challenging flavors. Eleven is Big Burrito's attempt at the prize at the end of that journey and I think for most people, it's sufficient.

For a more in-depth review you can read the article on my web site. http://eatinginpittsburgh.com/2011/02/
yelp:test:12595.para:
In the realm of modern upscale dining, Eleven adheres closely to the Big Burrito concept. While the offerings may not be particularly daunting, many residents of Pittsburgh might perceive them as such. However, the quality of the food is undeniable, with seasonal and local ingredients and cooking that is creatively inspired. Eleven stands out as the most refined among Big Burrito establishments, yet it lacks the formal atmosphere typically associated with such places.

I appreciate the opportunity to order from a restaurant's menu and identify the farms that provide their protein sources. The service at Eleven is outstanding, and the food is delicious. Although some individuals criticize Big Burrito, I believe they significantly contribute to the fine dining landscape in Pittsburgh. Mad Mex, despite its relaxed and informal nature, serves as an excellent introduction to flavors that pave the way for more complex and challenging tastes. Eleven represents Big Burrito's ambition to reach the culmination of this gastronomic journey, and I believe it meets the expectations of most people.

For a more comprehensive analysis, please refer to the article on my website. http://eatinginpittsburgh.com/2011/02/

yelp:test:12659.para:
Not content with the experience... The service and staff representation were subpar, with a noticeable lack of expertise. Requesting modifications such as "no spicy mayo" led to perceived offense. Additionally, the cost of $36 for four half portions of Maki Rolls was deemed unjustified. 

We ordered two of the seven-course tasting menus, priced at $59 each, which included three salads, two appetizers, and two entrees. However, all courses were combined onto a single plate, despite not being asked to separate them for our group of four. This oversight was seen as lazy.

Conversely, the spicy shrimp dish was commendable for its spice and flavor. The roasted flank steak was satisfactory, especially when served with fried spinach. Another complaint was the unsolicited choice offered in the tasting menu with entrees, where we were given wasabi mashed potatoes without being asked, despite our preference for fried rice. yelp:test:12679.para:
In August, I and four companions visited Las Vegas, where after an extensive excursion to the Grand Canyon, we felt famished. We browsed online and opted for Satay for our evening meal, influenced by the star-studded reviews on Yelp. The ambiance was pleasant and tastefully adorned, prompting us to request outdoor seating from the attentive waiter. 

The menu offered a substantial selection, and we chose Roti Canai and Vegetable curry Samosa, both Indian delicacies that were incredibly flavorful. The temptation was too strong, and we ordered an additional serving of Roti Canai. 

Nasi Lamak with curry chicken, served with coconut rice, was a delightful dish. The chicken was succulent, and we also enjoyed the half-boiled egg and cucumber. Nasi Goreng, a delightful fried rice with shrimp, squid, and half-cooked omelet, was equally enjoyable. The shrimp had a distinct flavor. 

Singapore fried noodles, a vegetarian dish without egg, was perfectly cooked and tasted excellent. The Green Curry, prepared with peppers, coconut milk, and eggplant, was satisfactory. The online menu was clear and informative, with most dishes accompanied by images. 

Al

yelp:test:12698.orig: I am usually not hugely into macarons, but these were excellent. I really loved the chocolate one, the frosting inside was dreamy and the texture was perfect. I also enjoyed my coffee and my meal - brioche French Toast. But I would have preferred real maple syrup instead of the caramel sauce it came with. But maybe that's just the northeasterner in me. Anyway, a good experience, with good service (although not the most pleasant atmosphere, being by a busy street/shopping center). I will be back for the macarons!
yelp:test:12698.para: Typically, I don't have a strong preference for macarons, yet these stood out as exceptional. The chocolate variant was particularly delightful, with its dreamy interior frosting and ideal consistency. I also savored my coffee and brioche French Toast. However, I would have opted for genuine maple syrup over the caramel sauce provided. Perhaps this preference stems from my northern roots. Nonetheless, it was a positive encounter, with service being commendable (though the ambiance was somewhat lacking due to the proximity to a bustling street and shopping hub). I'm inclined to return for the macarons.

yelp:test:12727.orig: CRAVINGS BUFFET\nThis is a decent buffet in the Mirage at Las Vegas. It's definitely improved over the years. I recall going there as a kid in the early 90's, where I met tennis star, Michael Chang, and got his autograph. Wide variety of foods here, but fast forward to 2008 and beyond, where the Cravings Buffet has expanded and vastly improved. There is quite an international feel to the buffet, ranging from Americano to Mexicano to Asian (Chinese, Japanese, Vietnamese). Lots of cut meats to choose from and plenty of soups to try! Desserts included cakes, tarts, bread pudding, and a gelato bar! Drinks are free, so drink up if you're into fruit juices: orange, cranberry, apple, etc. Service was great too, as they servers regularly cleaned our tables and refilled our drinks. The food is arrayed around the the dining area in a wide circular arc, making you walk a bit to find your favorite foods (a little exercise within the buffet compound). Not a bad buffet in Las Vegas. Not the best, but hey, it's not Bellagio!
yelp:test:12727.para: The Cravings Buffet at the Mirage in Las Vegas offers a commendable selection of dishes, showing significant enhancement over time. I remember visiting as a youngster in the early '90s and having the chance to meet tennis legend Michael Chang, where I secured his signature. The buffet boasts a diverse range of cuisines, from American to Mexican to Asian (Chinese, Japanese, Vietnamese). There's an abundance of sliced meats and various soups to sample! Desserts feature cakes, tarts, bread pudding, and a gelato station. Beverages are complimentary, encouraging those who enjoy fruit juices (like orange, cranberry, apple) to indulge. The service was exemplary, with attendants frequently tidying tables and refilling drinks. The food is spread out in a broad circular pattern around the dining area, prompting a bit of a trek to locate your preferred dishes (a touch of physical activity within the buffet zone). It's a solid buffet in Las Vegas, not quite the pinnacle, but certainly not lacking compared to Bellagio!

Drinks were served quickly enough, though there was some confusion as to who ordered what.

Price was reasonable for a buffet with the quality of food they had. But there is a lot of competition in this town. I seriously didn't need to be standing there that long, caffeine-less.
yelp:test:12735.para: I'll begin with a 4-star rating for the Bayside Buffet at Mandalay Bay, praising the food quality. They consistently provided fresh shrimp, exceptional steak, and ripe fruit. However, we were made to wait in the entry area for roughly 15 minutes as they struggled to seat our group of 10, despite prior assurances that we could be distributed among available tables. The situation was unclear, and by the time we were seated, some members had already consumed two plates of breakfast. Drinks were promptly delivered, though there was some mix-up regarding orders. The cost was fair considering the food quality, but the competition in this area was intense, and the wait without caffeine was unnecessary.

yelp:test:12789.para:
Starting with a quote from the official website of Caesar's Qua Baths and Spa:\n\n\"Utilizing its aquatic theme, cool blue hues, slate, and stone, the ambiance is set as you navigate through Qua's various facilities or relax in the Tea Room, where a Tea Sommelier is present.\"\n\nI consistently recommend my pals to avoid exaggerating in their thoughts, as the descent is significantly more challenging from the peaks we can construct in our minds. Regrettably, I failed to heed my own counsel in this instance. : ) I envisioned myself unwinding in the snow room, sipping tea prepared by the Tea Sommelier. Given my background in a region heavily influenced by Asian culture, and acknowledging both the health advantages and aesthetic appeal of a personally crafted cup of tea, overseen by a Sommelier, I was genuinely convinced by this feature. 

However, in reality, it only offers pre-packaged tea bags for self-service. When I inquired about the Tea Sommelier, the receptionist had to consult with management to clarify what a Sommelier is.

This situation alone was a significant setback, but in actuality, it was the final blow. I was also unhappy with the hair strands found in the brushes, illuminated by the blue lights.

yelp:test:12845.orig: The decor is sleek and modern and the food is pretty good too. The crowd is a little pretentious but very friendly. I always have a lot of fun here and it's my alternative to Scottsdale if I don't want to get all dressed up or if I want to do a Sunday Funday.
yelp:test:12845.para: The ambiance is stylish and contemporary, and the cuisine is commendable as well. The patrons exhibit a touch of pretension, yet they are notably warm. I consistently enjoy myself here, serving as my go-to option in lieu of Scottsdale, especially when I prefer casual attire or wish to indulge in a relaxed Sunday Funday.

yelp:test:12880.orig:
Mlife Black gave us a free room at The Mirage and a free meal here.  So who are we to turn down some free food?  Mr. W. and I just so happened to take my parents to Vegas for them to be tourists like good children one weekend and this offer pretty much just fell into our laps.  So let's eat some meat!!!

After having the best Brazilian BBQ in Vegas, I was hoping for a similar experience.  ""Disappointment"" seemed to be on the menu.  While the hostesses were rude and the waitress was no where to be seen majority of the time, the lovely servers with their sticks of grilled meats were always out and about between tables.  They kindly gave us these red-and-green colored things to let them know when they can bother us with more meat and when to give us a break.  They seemed pretty oblivious to this though and just kept wandering by.  I really don't mind since they're really just showing off all they had to offer and there was a pretty good variety but everything was so ridiculously dry.  

Bite after bite of beyond-well-done meats were piled onto our plates and something within the first ten bites made my stomach churn.  ""Where's the bathroom?"" I had asked politely to a snoot
yelp:test:12880.para:
Mlife Black provided us with complimentary accommodation and dining at The Mirage, prompting us to accept the generous offer. By chance, my parents and I were visiting Las Vegas, and this unexpected deal seemed to land in our favor. So, let's indulge in some grilled meat!

Despite savoring the finest Brazilian BBQ in Vegas, I anticipated a comparable delight. However, "disappointment" seemed to be the theme. The hostesses displayed rudeness, and the waitstaff was notably absent for most of the time. Yet, the attractive servers, equipped with skewers of grilled meats, were constantly roaming between tables. They politely handed us red-and-green tokens to signal their readiness to serve more meat or to grant us a respite. However, they appeared largely unaware of this system and continued their meandering. I don't mind this display of hospitality, as they were showcasing their extensive menu, which offered a diverse range. Nevertheless, the meat was excessively overcooked, making it unpalatable.

With each bite of overdone meat, my stomach revolted after just ten bites. I had politely inquired about the restroom, to which a haughty individual responded...

yelp:test:12884.orig: I've stayed here a few times already for business  and enjoy my stay each time. Havne't had a chance to use their spa yet but it looks really nice with the waterfall inside.  Have only tried eating at La Hacienda.  Margaritas there are good and the guacomole is made right there....but should save that review for La Hacienda.   Would love to bring the family here with me next time.    This hotel seems to be always busy.    Service and facilites overall were nice.
yelp:test:12884.para: I've visited this place multiple times for work and always find my visits enjoyable. I haven't utilized their spa yet, but it appears quite appealing with an indoor waterfall. I've only sampled food from La Hacienda, where the margaritas are excellent and the guacamole is freshly prepared. I'll reserve a review for La Hacienda. I'm eager to take my family to this hotel on my next visit. The hotel appears consistently occupied. Overall, the service and amenities have been pleasant.

yelp:test:12899.orig:
This is SUCH a lovely place to have breakfast!! They get 5 stars based on their vanilla yogurt alone. It's deliciously creamy and it's filled with real vanilla bean seeds. Oh.my.goodness. And for a cup of this, priced the same as a glass of iced tea, it's a steal..

My husband said he's never had fresher tasting fruit in his fruit plate. 

This place completely gets an A+ for their food. And while their prices are high, you are definitely getting your money's worth as far as quality of food and quality service. We went here a few times and really enjoyed ourselves.
yelp:test:12899.para:
This spot is absolutely delightful for a morning meal! Their vanilla yogurt alone has earned them a 5-star rating, boasting a richly creamy texture and genuine vanilla bean seeds. It's astonishing that for the cost of a glass of iced tea, you're getting such a fantastic deal. 

My spouse remarked that the fruit in their fruit plate tasted remarkably fresh. 

This establishment deserves an A+ for their culinary offerings. Despite the higher prices, the exceptional food quality and service make it a worthwhile investment. We visited multiple times and thoroughly relished our experiences.

yelp:test:12924.orig:
The two star ""I've experienced better"" rating is more than apt in this instance.

The decor of Settebello is very nice and the ovens are cool to look at. It's really easy to get all jazzed about the wood fired oven and unique toppings and flavor combinations. Hell, the website does enough boasting about how original and special the restaurant is. But it all comes down to the food and this pizza just was not good.

At the most basic level your margherita pizza should be the star. And it wasn't. The crust was flavorless and overcharred. Here's my unecessarily lengthy analogy: You know when you make grilled cheese (and c'mon, everyone makes 2 at a time, how could you eat just one?) and the first one comes out perfect but the second one comes out kinda messed up because the pan is probably too hot and there's not enough butter to help the bread brown correctly and the cheese doesn't fully melt because the thing is going to burn if you leave it on any longer? Well this is how my pizza was, it seemed hastily cooked over too high heat and lacked flavor. Not to mention the sauce was bland and the cheese was amorphous and too stringy. There was exactly one basil leaf on my pizza too
yelp:test:12924.para:
The "I've experienced better" two-star rating is well-deserved in this case.

Settebello's interior design is pleasing and the ovens are visually appealing. It's quite simple to become excited about the wood-fired oven and distinctive toppings and taste pairings. The website is quite boastful about the restaurant's uniqueness and specialty. However, the quality of the food is the ultimate decider, and this pizza fell short of expectations.

At its core, a margherita pizza should be the highlight. Unfortunately, it wasn't. The crust was tasteless and excessively charred. Here's a lengthy analogy: Imagine making grilled cheese (a common dish, right? Everyone makes two at a time, so why not just eat one?) and the first one is flawless, but the second one is slightly off because the pan might be too hot, there's not enough butter for the bread to brown properly, and the cheese doesn't melt completely as it's on the verge of burning. This pizza felt rushed, cooked at an excessively high temperature, and lacked flavor. Moreover, the sauce was unremarkable and the cheese was overly stringy and unappetizing. There was only a single basil leaf on my pizza.

yelp:test:12928.orig: I'm def a review kind of girl but I am not sure how this place got such great reviews.  This is some of the most expensive pizza I've ever eaten...  For about $13 a person then to add meats its like an extra $2 per meat...that is crazy.  The drinks were outrageous prices.  The servers were not the friendliest I've seen. My pizza was more or less just a dough mess.  I picked up a slice and everything fell off leaving nothing but flimsy dough.  They asked if I wanted it sliced and of course I said yes but they must have meant creased instead because there were just lines in the pizza... I actually had to cut it myself.  This is def not a place I will ever be going back to.  :(
yelp:test:12928.para: I identify as a reviewer, yet I'm puzzled by the high praise this establishment has received. Here, I encountered some of the priciest pizza I've ever tasted, costing roughly $13 per person, with additional $2 for each meat topping. The prices for beverages were exorbitant. The staff's demeanor was far from welcoming, and my pizza experience was disappointing, resembling a disorganized dough pile. When I requested slicing, it seemed they intended to crease it, as evidenced by the pizza's line marks. I had to slice it myself, and I'm certain I won't revisit this place. :(

yelp:test:12993.orig:
As you will see from my reviews I have eaten at high end steak places in NY, Philadelphia and DC.....this is definitely in the top 5 of all of them.   

We went here with a group and ate on a thursday night, we had no problem getting a table for 4 at 8pm with reservations.   

I had the lobster with bacon appetizer which was honestly the lowlight of my meal but still very good.   My wife had a beet salad which looked nice and a friend of mine split onion rings with the table.   The free fries were also amazing and we loved the different sauces.

Next came the main courses.   My wife ordered a filet done perfectly.   My friends GF had the halibut which was also excellent.   I had the regular rib eye and the king crap options as did my friend.   Let me just say this steak was seasoned and cooked PERFECTLY.   The king crap legs that were the side were amazing.   They were split and all of the good parts were left.   A great addition! 

We got the mashed potato sides  as well as a mushroom that was part of a forrest fire.   

I think that this is a great steakhouse and a great place to eat.   I would highly recommend this place in LV.
yelp:test:12993.para:
From my dining critiques, I've sampled premium steak establishments in NYC, Philly, and Washington, and this ranks among the top five.  

We dined here with a group on a Thursday evening, securing a reservation for four at 8pm without any hassle.  

I sampled the lobster with bacon starter, which, despite being the least impressive dish of the night, was still commendable.  

My spouse enjoyed a beet salad that appeared appetizing, while a companion shared onion rings with the group.  

The complimentary fries were exceptional, and we appreciated the variety of sauces.  

The main courses were noteworthy.  

My spouse's filet was cooked to perfection.  

My companion's gluten-free halibut was also delicious.  

I opted for the standard rib eye and my friend chose the king crab sides, which were outstanding.  

The steak was expertly seasoned and cooked to perfection, and the king crab legs, served as a side, were equally impressive.  

We also enjoyed the mashed potatoes and a forest fire mushroom.  

In my opinion, this is an excellent steakhouse and a top choice for dining.  

I would highly recommend this establishment in Las Veg

yelp:test:13033.orig:
This is a hotel that could be great & maybe it was in times gone by. First Staff is great doing all they can with what they have to work with... It's still being renovated but any standard Holiday Inn would be a better deal. 

Rooms look nice but lamps don't work... They forgot the business traveler when they did the renovation... The desk in my room is by the window so can't see the TV & no plugs within 8 feet of the thing... Plus they have the nerve to charge $9.99 for internet...

The bar/restaurant is by the pool & is a giant cavern... Ordered a steak came with a case knife to cut it... Bartender is a nice fellow but the place closes at 9pm... Really!

All in all whoever owns this place or is in charge of the renovation needs to go back to Hospitality school & learn what the public wants in a hotel...
yelp:test:13033.para:
This establishment once had the potential to be excellent, but currently, it may not meet expectations. The initial team is commendable, making the most of their available resources during ongoing renovations. However, a typical Holiday Inn would offer a more advantageous option. 

The rooms appear attractive, but the lighting is non-functional. The renovation seems to have overlooked the needs of business travelers, as evidenced by the desk's placement in my room, which obstructs the view of the TV and lacks nearby power outlets. Additionally, they impose a $9.99 fee for internet access. 

The bar/restaurant, situated near the pool, resembles a large cave. When I ordered a steak, it came with a case knife for cutting. The bartender is amiable, but the establishment shuts down at 9pm, which is quite early. Overall, the current management or renovation supervisor should consider revisiting Hospitality school to understand public preferences for a hotel.

yelp:test:13043.orig: Are you bored? Do you want to kill about 2 hours of your time looking at random stuff and end up walking out with things you weren't expecting to buy? Cost Plus World is for you! I don't remember how I heard about this place, but I remember my first time here. I spent about 2 hours just browsing. And now I'm a fan and still spend a good amount of time here during each visit. \n\nThis store has so much stuff. They have, picture frames, jewelry, furniture, food kitchen stuff and so much more! Everything is so colorful that my attention span is really short. I'll look at something and another thing will catch my eye and I'll completely forget what I was looking at in the first place. My favorite sections in the whole store are the food and the kitchenware. There are so many different snacks to choose from, like vegetable chips to chocolate covered waffles. And I love looking at the candy and spices from all around the world. It's a bit pricier, but you'll find some unique items if you look hard enough. On my last visit, I found a bunch of different flavored Kit Kat. I also love looking at all the mini kitchen stuff! Mini measuring cups, mini whisks, mini bowls...LOVE ALL THE MINIS!!!
yelp:test:13043.para: Do you feel restless and wish to pass approximately 2 hours exploring various items, possibly acquiring unexpected purchases? Cost Plus World is your destination! I can't recall the source of my discovery, but my initial visit is vivid in my memory. I dedicated roughly 2 hours to leisurely perusing. yelp:test:13066.orig:
Don't go here. The food came out cold and was way overpriced. Cheaper and tastier meals are everywhere in Vegas, so don't give this place another thought. I would suggest going to Panda Express for a more authentic experience. Yes, Panda Express = More Authentic Experience.

For a city filled with Asian gamblers, it was odd to see no other Asian person dinning at an Asian restaurant (always a big negative in my book). Maybe their frequent game play has given then enough comps to dine elsewhere, so I'll give this place the benefit of the doubt as far a demographically biased portion of my rating goes.

I ordered the prix fixe menu where the main course was braised sea bass. The sea bass was more boiled than braised. It was texturally unappealing and had no flavor. The greens that accompanied it were overcooked and essentially dead. 

I really should have just gone to the food court....
yelp:test:13066.para:
Avoid this location. The meals served were both chilly and excessively costly. In Las Vegas, where affordable and delicious food options abound, it's best to disregard this place. I recommend trying Panda Express for a genuine dining experience. Panda Express = Authentic Dining Experience.

In a city teeming with Asian gamblers, it was strange to find no Asian diners at an Asian restaurant, which I consider a significant downside. Perhaps their regular gambling has earned them enough complimentary meals to dine elsewhere, so I'll consider this place with a demographic-biased perspective in my rating.

I opted for the prix fixe menu, which featured braised sea bass as the main dish. However, the sea bass was more akin to boiled than braised, lacking in both texture and taste. The accompanying greens were overcooked to the point of being lifeless. 

I would have been better off choosing the food court...

yelp:test:13093.orig:

yelp:test:13093.para:
Achieving 300 reviews! 

We were aware of only positive feedback about this establishment, both from Yelp and personal recommendations from acquaintances and colleagues. Upon arrival, the blackout curtains instantly created a nighttime ambiance. We chose a bar seat and examined the menu, contemplating our choices. 

I selected the Shepherd's Pie (Cottage Pie) Pasty and he chose the The Oggie. We agreed to share a side of "chips" (i.e. fries). The unique aspect of dining at any bar is observing the staff in action. This venue excelled in this regard, as we could watch bartenders crafting beverages and the kitchen was prominently displayed, allowing us to witness the entire food preparation process! 

The food took some time to arrive, but each dish is prepared fresh, and the fries are baked, not deep-fried, making the wait worthwhile. Both our Pasties were scrumptious and satisfyingly filling! The fries were cooked to perfection, providing a delightful break from the usual fried food scene, while still savoring a delicious stuffed pasty and fries. 

The staff was incredibly amiable and frequently checked in on us. Due to our fullness, we didn't indulge in dessert on this occasion.

yelp:test:13095.orig: Oh how I love Coffee Bean!  There are none where I live, so I made my co-worker come here for coffee two days in a row. I got my coffee fix with a great white chocolate mocha. Something about their drinks are better - creamier maybe? The service was decent - not exceptional fast, but fine.  They are also located conveniently above the Bouchon kiosk, so we went downstairs to grab pastries after getting coffee.
yelp:test:13095.para: I adore Coffee Bean! Unfortunately, it's not available near me, so I persuaded my colleague to visit twice for coffee. I satisfied my caffeine craving with a delightful white chocolate mocha. I believe their beverages have a creamier texture - perhaps? The service was satisfactory - not particularly swift, but acceptable. Plus, they're conveniently situated above the Bouchon kiosk, prompting us to descend and pick up some pastries post-coffee.

yelp:test:13173.orig: only two stars cuz the food tasted good. i had the bonzai, which is ok. i think the carls jr. teriyaki burger tastes better though. my bf got a royal red robin and it was ok for him too. we also had some coleslaw and mac n' cheese but they never brought out napkins and utensils. we asked for some and we got napkins but the guy said the utensils were being washed. we thought that was weird but w/e. halfway through our meal and we still didnt get it. when we finished, we sat around for probably 10 minutes before we were noticed. they gave us to go boxes for our stuff and asked if we needed our check but we waited another while before we got it... maybe the staff has memory issues or something... our server came by and asked us how we were doing and i mentioned that we never got our utensils so she apologized and told her manager. the manager ended up comping the whole meal so we didn't have to pay at all. i'd prolly go to red robin again, just not this location...
yelp:test:13173.para: The food was satisfactory, with only two stars awarded due to its good taste. I sampled the bonzai, which was acceptable. However, I believe the carls jr. teriyaki burger surpasses it in flavor. My partner enjoyed the royal red robin, which was also acceptable. We also consumed coleslaw and mac n' cheese, but we faced an issue as napkins and utensils were not provided. We requested them and received napkins, but the staff informed us that the utensils were currently being cleaned. This seemed odd, but we didn't dwell on it. We waited for about 10 minutes before being acknowledged. Upon completion, we were given takeout containers and asked if we required a bill. We delayed receiving it, speculating if the staff might have memory problems. Eventually, our server inquired about our experience and I brought up the unresolved utensil issue. The manager intervened and decided to cover the entire meal cost, sparing us from payment. Despite the hiccup, I'd consider revisiting Red Robin, but not at this specific branch.

yelp:test:13214.orig:
Gotta love historic theaters playing off beat, artistic, foreign, documentary, etc films. Don't expect Transformers 18 to be on the marquee here. Check Harkins website for shows, show times and upcoming films. Films usually have a short run (1-2 weeks tops) so if you see one you like make sure you jump on it while it's still playing. 

Parking for theater or anywhere on Mill: the Lot behind the condos off Ash in between 5th and 3rd, near Macayo's, the lot behind Z-Tejas off Maple, pay parking in the garage of Brickyard, east passed Urban Outfitters, more pay parking (not on weekends past a certain time - check City of Tempe for hours - off 5th and Forest Avenue - also close to lightrail station). Street parking with meters in front of House of Tricks and a mega lot that's new off University and College. 

Overall: Great alternative to your typical dinner and a movie - try a movie here, and dinner at one of the great Mill Ave dining locales (La Bocca, House of Tricks, Cafe Boa, Canteen, Rula Bula, Z-Tejas etc)
yelp:test:13214.para:
Enjoy the unique charm of historic cinemas screening unconventional, artistic, and documentary films. Don't anticipate seeing Transformers 18 here. For show schedules and future films, visit Harkins' website. Films typically have a brief run, so if you find one you enjoy, make sure to catch it while it's still showing. 

Parking options for the cinema or Mill area include the lot behind the condos on Ash between 5th and 3rd, near Macayo's, the lot behind Z-Tejas on Maple, and pay parking in the Brickyard garage. East of Urban Outfitters, there's more pay parking, but it's not available on weekends past a certain time - check the City of Tempe for specifics. Street parking with meters is available in front of House of Tricks, and there's a new, large parking lot off University and College. 

Overall: A fantastic alternative to the usual dinner and movie outing - watch a film here and then enjoy a meal at one of the excellent Mill Avenue dining establishments (La Bocca, House of Tricks, Cafe Boa, Canteen, Rula Bula, Z-Tejas, etc).

yelp:test:13226.orig:

5 stars for service. 4 stars because food quality has been inconsistent. Never bad, but one of their chefs is hands down better than the others.
yelp:test:13226.para:

I rate the service as 5 stars. I've given it 4 stars due to the fluctuating quality of the food. It's never been terrible, but one chef stands out significantly above the rest.

yelp:test:13268.orig:

yelp:test:13268.para:
I recently relocated to Las Vegas from California and have visited three hair salons. Jeff at Mosaic has undoubtedly excelled in my hair care, standing out among the others. 

Before settling for Mosaic, I had experiences at Tonic II and Kelly Cardenas. Both Tonic and Kelly Cardenas offer a more appealing and fashionable environment compared to Mosaic, which somewhat resembles a row of hair salons. 

At Mosaic, I didn't receive a drink, and the waiting area felt confined. They've incorporated a clothing store within the lobby, which seemed unnecessary as my primary reason for visiting was hair care. If you prioritize customer service or atmosphere, the other two salons would be a better choice.

Regarding the haircut, Jeff demonstrated exceptional professionalism. He thoroughly discussed his qualifications with me, which are indeed impressive. He listened to my hair preferences, reasons for dissatisfaction with my previous haircuts, and explained why the previous stylists couldn't deliver the desired look. Throughout the process, he maintained a friendly demeanor and engaged in conversation with me. Overall, I am quite content with the service. However, he trimmed a bit more length than I had initially intended.

yelp:test:13330.para: JD performed my VCH piercing today, and I was extremely anxious, but he was incredibly empathetic and assisted me in relaxing. He executed the piercing flawlessly! The location was immaculate and the team was exceptionally welcoming. :)

yelp:test:13334.orig: I was in for lunch yesterday and had a great experience! The food was really good and the service was even better! My server Melanie was very personable and helpful. Couldn't of asked for a better lunch!
yelp:test:13334.para: Yesterday, I enjoyed a delightful lunch where the meal quality was exceptional and the service surpassed expectations. The attentive and friendly server, Melanie, contributed to an unparalleled dining experience. It was truly a lunch I couldn't have wished for any better.

yelp:test:13347.orig:
Having stayed 4 nights with an initial problem described in my first review, I have to say that there are definitely some pluses but the customer service at the front desk is still abysmal. Checking out, not one person smiled at any customer, there were no ""I hope you enjoyed your stay"" or ""Please come back soon"" type of comments to be heard. These are, IMO, essential service points at any hotel. 

On the plus side, the service when calling through the room operator is good, hangers brought up quickly, electrical issues resolved smoothly. Also, the movie theater and food court come in very handy for good entertainment and quick snacks. Valet parking attendants are courteous.

Improving front desk service, fixing the slow elevators, and adding coffee/water in rooms would bring this hotel up to the level of other hotels I've used in Las Vegas like the Signature MGM and The Venetian.
yelp:test:13347.para:
After spending four nights and initially noting issues in my first review, I must acknowledge there are some positive aspects, yet the front desk's customer service remains extremely poor. No cheerful greetings or welcoming remarks were heard during checkout, which I believe are crucial elements of hotel service. 

On the brighter side, the room service via the room operator is commendable, with swift delivery of hangers and efficient resolution of electrical problems. Additionally, the availability of a movie theater and food court provides excellent entertainment and convenient snack options. The valet parking attendants also display good manners. 

Enhancing the front desk service, addressing the issue of slow elevators, and providing coffee/water in rooms could elevate this hotel to the standard of other Las Vegas hotels such as the Signature MGM and The Venetian.
